items.title: Retention forestry practices in India for biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, and sustainable forest management across diverse forest zones
items.abstract: Retention forestry is an ecologically informed forest management approach in which selected trees, deadwood, habitat patches, keystone species, old-growth individuals, riparian corridors, and microhabitats are deliberately retained during forest management interventions to maintain biodiversity, ecological continuity, and ecosystem services. Although widely developed in boreal and temperate forests of Europe, North America, and Australia, its relevance is highly significant in India, where forestry traditionally emphasizes ecological security, biodiversity conservation, and community dependence. India’s diverse ecosystems, including Himalayan alpine forests, tropical evergreen forests, mangroves, dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and island ecosystems, support high endemism, climate-sensitive habitats, and culturally important species. This review synthesizes the concept of retention forestry within Indian forestry systems and evaluates its applicability across major agroclimatic zones and forest types. It examines policy frameworks such as the National Forest Policy (1988), National Working Plan Code (2014 and 2023), Joint Forest Management, Forest Rights Act (2006), CAMPA mechanisms, and the Biological Diversity Act (2002). Region-specific examples from the Himalayas, Western and Eastern Ghats, Northeastern forests, arid ecosystems, Sundarbans mangroves, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands are also discussed. The review concludes that India already possesses strong ecological and institutional foundations for formal retention forestry, but effective implementation requires region-specific guidelines, biodiversity-sensitive management plans, monitoring frameworks, and integration with climate adaptation strategies.

items.title: The environmental aspect of eco-design in an urbanised area
items.abstract: The article outlines the background to the emergence of design and one of its promising areas – eco-design. The preconditions for the emergence of eco-design and the components on which it is based are examined. The paludarium, as a tool for shaping the contemporary physical and spatial environment within urbanised areas, can be regarded as one example of the application of eco-design in design practice. Based on the classical view of the relationship between humans and the environment, contemporary approaches and innovative technologies, the paludarium is capable of addressing a number of humanity’s priority issues, whilst performing a variety of functions – ranging from general social to educational and environmental conservation. The article focuses on the requirements for constructing a modern paludarium, its interior design and innovative approaches to its use. Recommendations are provided regarding the selection of species for its animal and plant populations. The use of paludariums in secondary and higher education institutions further enhances the importance of eco-design in educational activities. In secondary schools, paludariums will adorn corridors and classrooms, whilst fulfilling an educational and nature conservation role. In school laboratories, paludariums provide the opportunity to house plants and animals, which can subsequently be used as living teaching aids for long-term use in biology lessons. Paludariums are also suitable for use in higher education institutions. A paludarium can be considered one of the most striking examples of applying ecosystem-based approaches to eco-design. The creation of the paludarium’s emergent (above-water) biotopes follows the same principles, utilizing various forms of plant and animal life. When establishing terrestrial biotopes, preference is given to tropical plants; the most popular choices include «Caladium», «Cordyline», «Dracaena», «Fittonia», «Cyperus», «Syngonium», «Ophiopogon», and others. Particular attention is paid to the potential for using paludariums in addressing socio- environmental issues. The potential for utilising the paludarium in the comprehensive resolution of humanity’s general environmental problems is outlined. The prospects for using eco-design in the rehabilitation of people injured during hostilities on the territory of Ukraine are examined

items.title: Potential distribution of the cashew tree (Anacardium occidentale) in the Caatinga under CMIP6 climate projections from EC-Earth3-Veg and MIROC6
items.abstract: Introduction Cashew ( Anacardium occidentale ) is one of the most economically and socially important perennial crops in the Brazilian semiarid region, supporting rural livelihoods while also representing a native species adapted to tropical drylands. Understanding how climate change may alter the environmental suitability of native species is critical for conservation planning and sustainable land use in dryland ecosystems. Methods Here, we modeled the current and future potential distribution of Anacardium occidentale (cashew tree) across the Caatinga biome using MaxEnt (v.3.4.4) and bioclimatic predictors derived from two CMIP6 Earth System Models (EC-Earth3-Veg and MIROC6) under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 emission scenarios for the baseline period and future projections (2050 and 2070). Occurrence records were compiled from GBIF, SpeciesLink, and Embrapa databases and refined through ecological filtering and pedoclimatic zoning. Results The current model showed high predictive performance (AUC ≈ 0.88), with approximately 25% of the biome classified as highly suitable (≥ 0.5), mainly concentrated in the northern Caatinga. Suitability patterns were primarily driven by precipitation seasonality, annual rainfall, elevation (altitude), and vegetation cover, indicating strong dependence on water availability and habitat structure. Future projections revealed substantial contractions of suitable areas, particularly under SSP5-8.5, with losses ranging from 68% (EC-Earth3-Veg) to 76% (MIROC6). Both climate models consistently indicated that increasing temperatures and reduced seasonal precipitation will intensify aridification, leading to a spatial retreat of the species niche toward coastal and sub-humid zones—areas that correspond to the historical origin and current climatic refugia of the species. Discussion These results demonstrate the high vulnerability of Anacardium occidentale to ongoing climate change and highlight the importance of conserving coastal and sub-humid microrefugia, as well as implementing climate-adaptive management strategies to support rural livelihoods and extractive systems dependent on cashew production in the Brazilian semi-arid region.

items.title: Caspian Sea Regression and Climatic Aridisation as Factors in the Transformation of Coastal Landscapes of the Russian Caspian Region
items.abstract: Aim. To identify the spatiotemporal patterns and main directions of transformation of coastal landscapes in the Russian Caspian region under the combined influence of modern Caspian Sea regression and climatic aridisation. A comparative regional analysis was conducted for the Volga delta, Kalmyk and Dagestan sectors of the western Caspian coast, with detailed studies concentrated in the Dagestan sector. The study used Landsat imagery for 1984–2025, Sentinel‐2 imagery for 2015–2025, SRTM and ALOS digital elevation models, weather‐station series for 1985–2025, cartographic materials, field observations from 2023–2026 and GIS analysis. Rising air temperature and a declining hydrothermal coefficient intensify the drying and deflation reworking of surfaces formed during sea retreat. A sequence of transitions from shallow‐water areas to littoral, solonchak, halophytic, reed‐marsh or deflation‐aeolian complexes was identified. Chechen Island shows decreasing isolation and incorporation into the Agrakhan‐Chechen accumulative massif, whereas Tyuleniy Island retains its insular position while displaying pronounced seasonal variability in area and shoreline configuration. The combined effect of Caspian Sea regression and climatic aridiation drives rapid transformation of low‐lying coasts in areas of the Russian Caspian region dominated by semi‐desert landscapes. Degradation of some shallow‐water and wetland complexes occurs simultaneously with the formation of young littoral, halophytic, reed‐marsh, and aeolian geosystems. These complexes should be incorporated into multilevel monitoring of coastal dynamics and potential organic matter accumulation.

items.title: Diet behavior of whitefish Coregonus lavaretus Linnaeus, 1758 in Lake Sevan (Armenia)
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the diet and behavior of the whitefish. Studies of the Lake Sevan whitefish Coregonus lavaretus Linnaeus, 1758 population were conducted in 2023–2024. A total of 300 whitefish were collected during the three seasons, reaching 100 specimens per season. Whitefish of various ages were used for the analysis. The whitefish ranged in age from 1+ to 6+. Analysis of the trophic structure revealed a significant shift in the whitefish's diet. While zooplankton, primarily Daphnia magna , constituted the bulk of the whitefish's diet (up to 95–100 %) in 2016–2017, its share decreased to 66–69 % in 2023–2024. Against the backdrop of declining zooplankton biomass, whitefish increasingly feed on macroinvertebrates – snail and gammarid. The condition factor decreased from 1.42 (2016–2017) to 1.22 (2023–2024) and the mass of fish of the same length decreased. The stomach fullness index in the autumn of 2024 decreased by 3–4 times compared to the same period in 2016–2017, which confirms the deterioration of food availability. An additional sign of structural changes in the population was a reduction in the number of gill rakers to an average value of 34.8, which may indicate a predominance of individuals with few rakers in reproduction.

items.title: Forest reclamation framework of the Steppe Pre‐Urals, Russia: Classification of elements and assessment of environmental and recreational potential
items.abstract: Aim. Creation of a brief description of the elements of forest reclamation framework of the model area of the Steppe Pre‐Urals (Belyaevsky district), Russia and allocation of ecologically and recreationally valuable forest terrain. The research was carried out using the cartographic method (mapping of forest vegetation using remote sensing data (ESRI, Google Earth), a digital model of the earth's surface (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission) and maps of the forest management system of the Federal State Information System of the Forestry Complex). Field studies were conducted to assess the recreational potential and environmental value. The forested area of the research area is 121 km and the forest cover is 3.2%. The classification of forests of natural origin (according to the conditions of formation) and forest plantations (according to their purpose) of the Steppe Pre‐Urals and a brief description of forests of various types are given. The most ecologically valuable forests are marked. The forest terrain with the greatest recreational potential and the main problems of their recreational use have been identified. Despite the low forest cover, forested areas play an important role in the formation of the nature conservation and recreational land fund. They are of great importance for the functioning of a network of protected areas and hunting grounds; many of them are used or can be used as places of recreation and tourism.

items.title: Assessment of biogeocenotic representativeness of specially protected natural areas of the Western Caucasus orobiomes (Russia)
items.abstract: Aim. To assess the degree of representativeness of specially protected natural areas and to show how zonally representative the existing network of protected areas of the Western Caucasus within the Krasnodar Territory is. Among the possible approaches to regional analysis of protected areas, the concept of biomes was chosen. The biota of these biomes most effectively utilises abiotic components of the environment due to the historical adaptation of both individual elements and the entire ecosystem to them. Research methods: analysis and synthesis of the obtained materials, analysis of published scientific literature on the physicalgeographical and biogeographical characteristics of the Krasnodar Territory and author's data on sozological studies of specially protected natural areas. The natural and climatic characteristics of three orobiomes of the Western Caucasus are presented, serving as the foundation upon which floristic complexes, endemism, altitudinal zonation and vegetation cover developed. The established network of specially protected natural areas is demonstrated and its effectiveness in preserving the entire ecosystem and species diversity in each orobiome is determined. It has been established that only the Sochi orobiome has a high level of ecosystem conservation – 78 % of the territory is protected. The Northwest Caucasus orobiome has the lowest level of conservation (12 % of the territory). Foothill oak forests, sub‐Mediterranean woodlands and shiblyak forests at the northwestern boundary of the habitat are not protected. The Otradnensky District is one of the areas where ecosystems remain virtually untouched by economic activity but they are poorly covered by the protected area system. The research conducted will help strengthen conservation efforts to establish protected areas in certain municipalities.

items.title: Taxonomic and functional responses of benthic diatoms to river modification by small hydropower plants
items.abstract: Abstract Small hydropower plants are increasingly recognised as important drivers of hydromorphological alteration in river ecosystems, yet their effects on benthic diatoms remain insufficiently understood. We investigated the taxonomic and functional responses of benthic diatom assemblages to two operational-channel hydropower plants along the Hernád River (Hungary). Twenty-five benthic samples were collected from the main channel, operational channels, and hydromorphologically modified river sections. Taxonomic composition differed markedly among habitat types, whereas functional trait composition showed weaker differentiation, indicating functional redundancy despite pronounced taxonomic turnover. Species richness, effective Shannon diversity, and evenness did not differ significantly among habitat categories; however, functional richness and functional divergence revealed significant differences, highlighting functional reorganisation associated with hydromorphological modification. Significant distance–decay relationships were detected within both operational channels and modified river sections, suggesting that spatial structuring persisted despite river fragmentation. Fifteen threatened taxa and several non-native species were recorded, but neither habitat-specific segregation of threatened taxa nor invasion hotspots were identified. Our results demonstrate that small hydropower plants can substantially modify the taxonomic and functional organisation of benthic diatom assemblages without necessarily reducing local taxonomic diversity. The observed responses suggest community reorganisation rather than biodiversity loss and highlight the importance of maintaining longitudinal connectivity in regulated rivers.

items.title: The ethological mirror and the olfactorily disconnected and disinhibited hypothesis: reclaiming human social efficacy and empathy through interspecies sensory alignment
items.abstract: When we encounter extreme human violence, the cultural instinct is to label it “bestial”—a defensive projection that ignores the adaptive logic of animal behavior. Yet, ethological observation reveals that intraspecific violence in animals is typically mediated by stable, regulatory feedback systems. In contrast, modern human pathology represents a profound “sensory loneliness” caused by the decoupling of our species from ancient bio-behavioral scaffolds. This paper introduces an ethological framework for reclaiming social efficacy, proposing that modern systemic pathology is not a regression to an animalistic nature, but a consequence of environmental disruption to our evolved bio-behavioral requirements. Applying a neuro-ethological lens, we propose the Olfactorily Disconnected and Disinhibited (ODD) hypothesis, arguing that the “deodorized” landscape of industrial life leaves the human orbitofrontal cortex starved of its ancestral sensory anchors, leading to a structural bio-behavioral discordance. We utilize domesticated species and comparative non-human models (such as disrupted social structures in translocated wildlife) as biological “sentinels” whose lives remain governed by the chemical honesty and multisensory feedback that humans have systematically suppressed. By synthesizing comparative ethology with neurobiological findings, we demonstrate that the human capacity for empathy is not lost, but dormant, obscured by the cultural mandates of modern, disconnected environments. We conclude that restoring social health requires a conscious realignment with the bio-behavioral rhythms and interspecies connections that remain the hallmark of a healthy, functioning society.

items.title: Shipboard microcosm simulations of eddy-driven water mass mixing reveal distinct strategies of prokaryotic and eukaryotic microbiomes
items.abstract: Abstract. Mesoscale eddies strongly influence marine microbiomes, but their effects on microbiome association and stability remain unclear. We conducted 16-day shipboard microcosm experiments using surface water, DCM water, and 1:1 mixed seawater from eddy-influenced and non-eddy-influenced sites in the Kuroshio Extension. We hypothesized that eddy enhanced nutrients and light would alleviate resource competition, promoting diversity and deterministic assembly by shifting taxa from stress tolerant to growth adapted strategies. Prokaryotes and microeukaryotes responded divergently. Eddy associated conditions increased prokaryotic richness and evenness but reduced microeukaryotic richness. Microeukaryotes showed narrower niche breadth in surface and mixed treatments and stronger heterogeneous selection, especially in the DCM. Assembly was strongly depth dependent. Surface communities were restructured more than DCM communities. In surface and mixed layers, prokaryotes showed increased dispersal limitation and decreased homogeneous selection under eddy associated conditions, whereas the DCM showed the opposite. Microeukaryotes generally exhibited opposite depth dependent patterns. Co occurrence networks were more complex and robust under eddy associated conditions, mainly driven by prokaryotes. DCM networks had higher robustness and lower vulnerability. Weakened correlations between prokaryotic composition and environmental variables suggest a shift from top down environmental filtering to bottom up biotic control. These results reveal distinct adaptive strategies of prokaryotic and eukaryotic microbiomes and highlight the role of eddies in sustaining microbial resilience and ecosystem functioning in the open ocean.

items.title: Multi-Criteria Environmental Assessment of Protected Areas: Ecosystem Services and Use by Visitors
items.abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are currently the planet's primary tool for conserving biodiversity and sustaining the ecosystem services upon which human well-being depends. Despite this, their environmental valuation remains methodologically fragmented, particularly in Latin America, a region where frameworks capable of integrating ecological, economic, and tourism dimensions are scarce. To address this gap, this study proposes a multi-criteria environmental valuation framework for the Sumaco Biosphere Reserve (RBS) in Ecuador, a UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)-recognized territory covering 931,930 ha that combines exceptional biodiversity gradients with a well-established community-based ecotourism sector. The framework articulates twelve ecosystem services, classified according to the Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services (CICES v5.1), with four visitor usage metrics, using the combined AHP-VIKOR (Analytic Hierarchy Process-VIšeKriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Rešenje) model. Using secondary institutional sources and input from a panel of twelve experts in protected area management and ecosystem services, a standardized indicator matrix was developed to obtain compromise indices for each management zone. The results show that the core zone achieves the most favorable environmental index (Q = 0.000), followed by the buffer zone (Q = 0.612) and the transition zone (Q = 1.000). Cultural services proved to be the dimension with the greatest weight (w = 0.444), driven by recreation, ecotourism, and aesthetic experience, in line with the ecotourism profile of the Biosphere Reserve. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that the classification remains stable in 78% of the disturbance scenarios evaluated. The proposed framework bridges the gap between ecosystem services science and visitor management, offering a replicable and transferable tool for protected areas facing conservation-tourism tensions in the Global South.

items.title: Larger lakes are hit harder and longer by Dreissena invasion
items.abstract: Abstract Invasive quagga mussels are swiftly spreading across Europe and North America, causing major ecological and economic impacts even in lakes already invaded by zebra mussels. A key challenge is to understand the magnitude and timing of mussel impacts across a wide range of freshwater ecosystems, to predict potential impacts on uninvaded systems. We assembled high-resolution data sets spanning 18 North American and European invaded lakes and five key ecosystem variables (Secchi depth, phosphorus and chlorophyll concentration, phytoplankton and zooplankton biomass). We then address the questions: How have the pace and magnitude of dreissenid impacts varied with lake morphometry (area, depth, volume)? How have impacts differed between polymictic and stratified lakes? Which lakes have exhibited recovery following zebra and quagga mussel invasions? We found that impacts manifest earlier in polymictic than in stratified lakes. After the initial impacts, lakes invaded by zebra mussels usually exhibited signs of partial ecosystem recovery, which was interrupted in lakes that experienced a secondary invasion by quagga mussels. In the Laurentian Great Lakes, mussel populations reached maximum biomass later, and ecosystem impacts manifested more slowly but culminated at a higher overall impact level. Furthermore, no ecosystem recovery in the Great Lakes has been observed to date, even 30 years after mussel invasions, though recovery may be delayed in large lakes. Our results indicated that lake size is more important than other parameters in determining Dreissena impact, and findings from smaller inland lakes cannot be directly applied to larger systems (e.g., the Great Lakes) and vice versa.

items.title: How do cultural and creative industries contribute to sustainable development? A systematic review and bibliometric analysis
items.abstract: Introduction Unlike most previous studies that synthesized the literature using a single major technique, we used a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of the literature on cultural and creative industries in the developing-country context. Moreover, we integrated the PRISMA literature selection protocol. Methods We conducted a comprehensive search of the Scopus and Web of Science databases covering January 2007 to December 2025; after screening and reapplying the developing-country eligibility criteria using the World Bank FY2026 income classification, we retained 151 articles for analysis. Results The major findings suggest rapid growth in CCI publications after 2020 (annual growth rate 26.1%; 88% of the corpus published since 2020), with research output concentrated in China (41% of corresponding authors). Keyword clustering identifies six thematic clusters: (1) sustainable development, China and the creative and cultural industries; (2) cultural industries, tourism and regional/rural planning; (3) economic development, environment and urbanization; (4) SDGs, tourism industry and conservation; (5) cultural policy and creative ecosystems; and (6) creative city, entrepreneurship and design. SDG mapping reveals an imbalance: economic and urban goals (SDGs 8, 11, 9) dominate, while social (SDGs 1, 5, 10) and climate and environmental goals (SDGs 13–15) remain significantly underrepresented. Regarding research methods, quantitative approaches dominate (44%), while longitudinal and experimental designs are largely absent in CCIs and sustainable development. Discussion Because the evidence base is concentrated in China and East Asia and drawn from two English-language databases, the findings characterize the indexed literature rather than all developing countries. The identified thematic, geographic, and methodological gaps inform a future research agenda.

items.title: Neuroptera diversity, seasonality, and habitat distribution in the arid landscapes of the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) represents an arid environment that supports a diverse insect fauna adapted to extreme climatic conditions. This study provides the first comprehensive assessment of the Neuropteran fauna of the UAE, based on extensive field surveys and an analysis of three decades of specimen records from the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi’s Invertebrate Inventory Project and published literature. The objectives were to document species diversity, analyse habitat associations, and assess seasonal activity patterns across eight major habitat types. A total of 97 species were recorded, representing 40 genera and seven families. At the regional scale, 250 species from 45 genera and nine families are documented across the Arabian Peninsula. The results indicate that 25% of Neuroptera families are associated with mountainous, rocky, and wadi habitats, while sand sheets and dunes support the highest diversity (85% of species). Gravel plains and inland standing water habitats exhibited lower richness, with intertidal habitats showing minimal abundance. Seasonal activity peaked among antlions (Myrmeleontidae) during April and May, with a marked decline in January. These findings provide new insights into the ecology, distribution, and habitat specialization of Neuroptera in arid environments, supporting ongoing biodiversity monitoring and conservation planning in the UAE.

items.title: Cover crop management influences soil properties and grapevine performance across three growing seasons in a subtropical vineyard
items.abstract: Cover crop management can modify soil conditions and grapevine performance, but these responses may depend on the vegetation-management strategy and growing season. This study evaluated the effects of different cover crop management systems on soil, physiological, yield, and fruit technological variables of Vitis vinifera L. cv. Viognier cultivated in Campo Largo, Paraná, Brazil, for three growing seasons (2023–2026; 2023/24, 2024/25, and 2025/26). The treatments were: T1, spontaneous vegetation (white clover in winter and Cynodon spp in summer) with herbicide application in the vine row; T2, spontaneous vegetation without herbicide; T3, black oat in winter and predominantly white clover + angola grass in summer; T4, common vetch in winter and mombaça grass in summer; and T5, multispecies cover crop mixtures in winter (black oat + rye + vetch + forage radish) and summer ( Cynodon ssp + buckwheat + mombaça grass). Cover crop biomass and macronutrient accumulation, soil chemical and physical properties, soil water content, and grapevine nutritional, physiological, vegetative, yield, and technological variables were evaluated. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models accounting for repeated measurements across growing seasons, complemented by multivariate analyses. T4 (vetch and mombaça) and T5 (oats + rye + vetch + forage radish; and Cynodon ssp + buckwheat + mombaça) generally showed greater biomass production and accumulation of N, P, K, Ca, and Mg than systems based on spontaneous vegetation. Vegetation management also affected selected surface-soil properties, particularly available P, total organic carbon, total N, cation exchange capacity, bulk density, and soil water content, although responses varied among growing seasons. Grapevine leaf area (LA) and the Yield/LA ratio did not differ among treatments, whereas physiological responses were treatment- and season-dependent. The clearest yield response occurred in 2025/26, when T2 and T4 reached 11.06 and 11.12 Mg ha −1 , respectively, approximately 20% greater than T1 (9.21 Mg ha −1 ). Soluble solids and pH were unaffected by vegetation management, and differences in titratable acidity occurred only in 2023/24. Global multivariate profiles differed among treatments but were strongly season-dependent. Overall, sown cover crops increased biomass production, nutrient accumulation, and selected surface-soil attributes, but these responses did not consistently translate into greater grapevine yield or fruit technological maturity within the 3-year experimental period.

items.title: Chrysolina americana L. – a dangerous pest of rosemary
items.abstract: The purpose of the research was to identify Chrysolina americana (Linnaeus, 1758) on the Black Sea coast of Sochi and select effective modern insecticides against the rosemary leaf beetle ( C. americana L.). The increase in the number of C. americana pests on the Black Sea coast of Sochi since 2018 and the locations of its foci justify the need to develop a methodology for protective measures. Insecticides of the chemical group pyrethroids, Spray Bona forte and Tabu, exhibit high toxicity against rosemary leaf beetle ( C. americana L.). The best results were shown by an insecticide with the active ingredient Acetamiprid – Spray Bona Forte, BA for imago – 99.5 %, for larvae – 100 % on average. The biological insecticides Bitoxibacillin had the least effect on both beetles and larvae (8.2 % and 64.9 % on imago and larvae, respectively) and Phytoverm (29.4 % and 53.3 % on average). To develop a comprehensive biological protection system against the invasive pest C. americana L. in economically significant crops, and in order to eliminate resistance to the effective bioinsecticide identified, research on both the biology and phenology of the development of C. americana L. should be continued. During the entire growing season, the forage plants identified included rosemary, lavender, sage, etc.

items.title: Genomes of Argia emma (Odonata: Coenagrionidae) and Epeorus albertae (Ephemeroptera: Heptageniidae) as novel resources for evolution, ecology, and conservation research
items.abstract: Paleopteran insects (Odonata and Ephemeroptera) occupy a crucial position in insect evolution and are ecologically significant indicators of freshwater ecosystem health. Recent improvement in the number of publicly available genomes and transcriptomes have advanced understanding of genome size evolution, morphological innovation, and ecological responses in these orders. Here we present genome assemblies for the damselfly Argia emma (Zygoptera: Coenagrionidae) and the mayfly Epeorus albertae (Ephemeroptera: Heptageniidae), two ecologically and culturally significant species from the Salmon River, Idaho, USA. Both species play essential roles in regional aquatic food webs, including supporting salmon populations central to Nez Perce cultural lifeways. These genomes provide valuable comparative resources for approximating genetic diversity and reconstructing historical demographic change. Both genomes represent high-quality assemblies as measured by contiguity and completeness. Demographic models built from both assemblies show how the populations of these two species have generally trended in similar directions through time, consistent with the hypothesis that these species respond similarly to environmental change and may be useful complementary bioindicators. The genome assembly of A. emma further suggests that similar genome sizes in the family Coenagrionidae are not correlated with similar profiles of repetitive elements. These genomes provide a timely baseline for future study of how proposed land-use change in the Salmon River watershed may affect aquatic insects, are an important resource for navigating freshwater biodiversity conservation efforts in the American West, and, by filling taxonomic gaps, will be important tools for further study into the evolution of Paleoptera.

items.title: Beyond Riverbeds: Environmental Impacts of Sand Mining on Riverine Ecosystems and Traditional Water Bodies in Karnataka, India
items.abstract: Sand is a finite natural resource and crucial for maintaining environmental equilibrium.However, despite its strategic importance, it is being extracted at an unprecedented rate worldwide to meet the surging demand driven by population growth, rapid urbanization and increasing global infrastructure investments.This rampant extraction from diverse ecosystems is causing severe environmental repercussions leading to ecosystem degradation and the disruption of natural processes.The far-reaching impacts threaten biodiversity, destabilize landscapes and intensify global environmental challenges, including climate change and global warming.Rampant sand mining has emerged as a nationwide issue in India, leading to severe socio-economic and ecological repercussions.Despite existing regulatory mechanisms, the over-exploitation of this minor mineral continues at an alarming rate, including in Karnataka, where it has caused significant environmental damage.To investigate the ecological impacts of sand mining, this study was conducted across four river basins in Karnataka known for intensive sand mining activities.Data was gathered through Focused Group Discussions (FGDs) with various stakeholders, particularly farmers residing along the riverbanks.The study reveals that sand mining operations contribute to numerous adverse effects, including soil erosion, land degradation, altered water flow patterns, shrinking of traditional water bodies and grazing lands and a decline in local biodiversity.Additionally, filtering activities prevalent in the river basins of southern Karnataka have inflicted irreversible damage on riverbeds, lakebeds, streams, channels, grazing lands, forests, government fallow lands and native vegetation

items.title: Effects of Urban Blue–Green Landscape Patterns on Carbon Sequestration in Chongqing’s Central Urban Area: An XGBoost–SHAP Analysis
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of the "Dual Carbon" goals, this study focused on the main urban area in Chongqing. With remote sensing, land use, meteorological data from 2000, 2010, and 2020 -- we used the CASA model to estimate vegetation net primary productivity, or NPP, which we compared to MODIS NPP products. By combining optimal scale analysis, landscape pattern indices, the XGBoost model and SHAP (the Shapley Additive exPlanations) interpretation methods, our study showed that the space relationship between the blue and green landscapes and how they help to reduce the amount of vegetation carbon sinks are associated with one another, not just by the space that the areas are in, but by these other ways. The results indicate that from 2000 to 2020, NPP in the study area showed an overall upward trend. High-value areas were primarily distributed in the peripheral mountains and continuous ecological spaces, while blue-green spaces in the central urban area and densely built river valleys exhibited greater fragmentation. Compared to the baseline model (M0) containing only elevation and slope, the extended model (M1) incorporating landscape pattern indices significantly improved cross-validation R² values: from 0.5954, 0.6248, and 0.5735 to 0.7996, 0.8031, and 0.7311 for the years 2000, 2010, and 2020, respectively.SHAP analysis revealed that among the selected predictors, elevation contributed the most. PLAND (Percentage of Landscape) demonstrated a significant predictive contribution across all three years, whereas the roles of ED (Edge Density), SPLIT (Splitting Index), and AI (Aggregation Index) varied interannually. Nonlinear responses and reference thresholds were identified for elevation, slope, PLAND, LPI (Largest Patch Index), and their contributions to NPP prediction; however, SHAP contributions do not imply direct causal effects. The study concludes that topographic backgrounds, combined with the area, fragmentation, and connectivity of blue-green spaces, collectively correlate with spatial variations in NPP within mountainous cities. These findings provide a reference for optimizing ecological spaces and enhancing vegetation carbon sink potential in the main urban area of Chongqing.

items.title: Biotechnological potential of aquatic hyphomycetes: a review
items.abstract: Aquatic hyphomycetes are an ecological group of anamorphic fungi that play an essential role in decomposing plant substrates in lotic environments. This narrative review compiled studies highlighting the biotechnological potential of this group, contributing to the understanding of its applications and perspectives. The analysis emphasizes aquatic hyphomycetes as significant producers of metabolites with applications across various sectors, including industrial, agricultural, environmental, and health sectors. Notably, these organisms degrade lignocellulosic compounds and produce antimicrobial compounds. Several studies also highlight their bioremediation potential, particularly their ability to tolerate and transform environmental pollutants, including synthetic dyes, toxic elements, and endocrine-disrupting compounds. None of the studies considered in this review were conducted in tropical or subtropical countries, with most of the research concentrated in North America and Europe. These findings suggest that a substantial number of chemical compounds with biotechnological potential remain unexplored, underscoring the importance of expanding research efforts, particularly in under-investigated ecosystems.

items.title: Technological, Nature-Based Adaptation and Mitigation for Planetary Sustainability Collaborations
items.abstract: This chapter examines the Pacific Island state of Tuvalu, where severe climate risks, climate shocks and sea-level rise threaten the livelihoods of 11,810 residents across 26 km2 of land. As IPCC projections suggest Tuvalu could become uninhabitable, this study explores the critical adaptation and mitigation challenges posed by Tuvaluan climate risk, examining whether migration is the sole option or whether sustainable solutions can safeguard the nation. Integrating literature reviews and GIS applications, the research evaluates the vulnerability of coastal and oceanic ecosystems. It proposes a three-pronged framework: (1) technological solutions, including the conceptual “Funafuti Atoll's Osmotic, Triple-layered Protection Belt”; (2) nature-based strategies protecting unique biodiversity; and (3) global collaboration networks to sustain local socio-economic, cultural, and agricultural systems. Ultimately, this study aims to balance engineering, ecology, and international partnerships to ensure long-term resilience for Tuvalu's people and cultural landscapes.

items.title: Nonthermal particle acceleration by magnetic pumping in pulsating plasmas
items.abstract: We present a new "pulsating box" setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression-expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results are relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.

items.title: Onsite Calibration of the Shear-Shear Correlation
items.abstract: Abstract Calibration of the cosmic shear bias is crucial for justifying the cosmological results. However, it is still unclear to what extent calibrations based on simulated galaxy images, as what is commonly done in the weak lensing community, can capture the real shear bias, especially given the complicated instrumental effects. On the other hand, selections of the source galaxies (magnitude cut, redshift binning, etc.) made in real measurement, as well as stochastic but possibly correlated shear biases, may introduce errors to the shear-shear correlations that are hard to calibrate apriori. In our previous few papers, we have shown that the field-distortion signal associated with each galaxy image can be saved in the shear catalog to provide onsite calibrations of shear bias for both galaxy-galaxy lensing and shear-shear correlation. In this paper, we apply this method to the HSCpdr3 shear catalog generated by the Fourier\_Quad shear measurement method. Using our onsite calibration method, we find that the shear biases vary with the selections of photo-z bins, SNR cuts, optical bands, as well as alternative forms of the shear estimators. Nevertheless, after calibrations, the shear-shear correlation functions and cosmological parameter constraints show consistent results in all the cases considered. The fiducial results from the r/i/z bands shear catalog with $\mathrm{SNR}>10$ cut yield: $S_8=0.740^{+0.030}_{-0.030}$ and $\Omega_m=0.383^{+0.129}_{-0.132}$.

items.title: Transonic Solutions for Recombination-driven Stellar Winds
items.abstract: Abstract We present an analytical stationary isentropic solution of the spherically symmetric Euler equations in the gravitational field of a star using an equation of state of ionizable monatomic gas. The solution consists of a fully ionized hydrostatic inner region, followed by a thick hydrostatic recombination region where the density decreases by orders of magnitude, the radius increases by about an order of magnitude, and the temperature decreases by a factor of 2. Within this recombination region, a large portion of the recombination energy is used for lifting the gas subsonically. This region ends at a critical point, located roughly at 10−100 au, where the gas is mostly recombined, beyond which it flows supersonically as a wind. We find the position and the quantities of the gas at the critical point and derive the mass-loss rate of the solution. We apply our solution to evolved stars, with a compact core surrounded by a high-entropy envelope. We derive the mass-loss rate as a function of time. As the star is losing mass, it goes through a sequence of our solutions, in a runaway manner which ends once most of the high-entropy envelope is lost. Recombination-driven winds are initiated once the star expands to a radius of about 1 au M / M ⊙ and are terminated on a timescale of 10 1 –10 4 yr. We discuss the implications for common envelope evolution.

items.title: A Possible High-redshift Origin for the Short GRB 061201: Implications of a Compact Binary Merger beyond Cosmic Noon
items.abstract: Abstract Short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) at redshift z ≳ 2 remain exceptionally rare, yet they are crucial for tracing compact binary mergers in the early Universe and understanding their role in the production of r -process elements. GRB 061201 is an unusual and still debated event: although its optical afterglow was accurately localized, no secure coincident host galaxy was identified, and the proposed associations with nearby galaxies all require a large separation between the GRB and its birth site. In this work, we revisit GRB 061201 and argue that the observations are more naturally explained if the burst occurred within a faint F322W2 ∼ 28.4 AB mag galaxy at z ≳2. By combining constraints from the afterglow and deep near-infrared imaging from JWST, we show that a distant origin ( z ≈ 3–4) provides a coherent explanation of the burst phenomenology. If confirmed, GRB 061201 would represent one of the most distant short GRBs known, extending the observed compact merger population to an epoch when the Universe was only about two billion years old.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for the Lyα Forest: CNN-Based Absorber Detection and Characterization
items.abstract: Abstract The Lyα forest is a powerful probe of the intergalactic medium and small-scale matter distribution, but deriving absorber properties traditionally requires computationally expensive Voigt-profile fitting. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN) that identifies and characterizes H i Lyα absorbers directly from quasar spectra. The model is trained on synthetic spectra generated from the IllustrisTNG simulation and fitted with the viper Voigt-profile fitting code to provide training labels. The network simultaneously predicts absorber presence, column density (NHI), Doppler parameter (bHI), and line centroid. On simulated spectra, the CNN reproduces the viper reference catalogue with an F1 score of ∼0.8, with mean absolute errors of ∼0.18 in log NHI and ∼0.10 in log bHI. It reproduces the H i column density distribution function (CDDF) and the bHI–NHI relation obtained from viper, recovering similar CDDF slopes and a lower-envelope relation with an RMS difference of only 0.36 km s−1. Applied to high-resolution UVES spectra, performance decreases to an F1 score of ∼0.5, with mean absolute errors of ∼0.35 in log NHI and ∼0.22 in log bHI. Latent-space analysis reveals a significant domain shift between the simulated and observational spectra, contributing to the reduced performance. Nevertheless, the CNN reproduces the observed CDDF and bHI–NHI distributions obtained from the viper reference catalogue, yielding CDDF slopes consistent with viper and a lower-envelope RMS difference of 3.20 km s−1 relative to viper. Monte Carlo dropout is implemented during inference to quantify predictive uncertainties. Together with its computational efficiency, the method provides a scalable and uncertainty-aware framework for Lyα forest analysis in upcoming spectroscopic surveys.

items.title: The stability of radially anisotropic rotating stellar systems with a central density cusp
items.abstract: We investigated the interplay between radial velocity anisotropy and internal rotation in self-gravitating systems characterised by initial spherical symmetry and a moderate density cusp. We studied the stability properties of such configurations to disentangle the impact of anisotropy, rotation, and density structure on the formation of triaxial stellar systems. We performed a set of collisionless N-body simulations starting from initial equilibria with a phase space distribution function of the class introduced by Osipkov and Merritt, modified to impose a net global angular momentum with the Lynden-Bell daemon protocol. We analysed the growth of the density and phase space distribution modes, as well as the axial ratios and triaxiality index of the final configurations. We find that internal rotation has a mitigating effect on the strength of the radial orbit instability in radially anisotropic models with a anisotropy index close to the consistency limit, while it slightly hastens the onset of the instability in marginally stable models. From the analysis of the growth rate of the density modes, we also find that an inner bar, which for maximally rotating initial conditions declines after its initial growth, is formed even in systems with initial profiles with a central density cusp. items.title: Black hole-neutron star binaries with high spins and large mass asymmetries. III. Properties of the ejected material and its electromagnetic signatures
items.abstract: Compact binary systems consisting of a black hole (BH) and a neutron star (NS) are expected to provide detectable signals both in the gravitational-wave and in the electromagnetic channels, thus representing excellent sources for multimessenger astronomy. In this third paper in a series, we report on the geometric and thermodynamic properties of the purely dynamical ejecta component modeled in our general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamical simulations of BHNS systems over a comprehensive binary parameter space consisting of large mass ratio and high BH spin. The tidal disruption and dynamical mass ejection is studied by monitoring the transfer of energy and angular momentum to matter for the particular case of a highly unequal-mass binary with large BH spin, extending known results for low-mass-ratio, irrotational BHNS binaries. By varying the binary parameters, we investigate their influence on the geometric, thermodynamic, and kinematic properties of the ejected matter. Furthermore, we employ the nuclear-reaction network kyet to obtain the elemental abundances resulting from the r process active in the ejecta and study how they depend on the properties of the progenitor objects. Finally, using the radiative-transfer code , we compute the kilonova light curves from the results of our simulations, discuss their bolometric and optical/near-infrared evolution, and compare them with the AT2017gfo data and upper limits for S190814bv, finding overall consistency.

items.title: Sea Ice as an Origin of Life Location for Hycean and Ocean Worlds
items.abstract: Abstract Water worlds with potential deep oceans are at the forefront of currently observable exoplanetary habitability. The standard requirements for habitability are the presence of an energy source, a source of nutrients, and a solvent, all of which can be met in exoplanets with deep liquid water oceans. Such planets may be numerous, ranging from hycean worlds and ocean worlds to terrestrial-size planets with enhanced water content. However, abiogenesis requires additional conditions, namely a mechanism to accumulate nutrients to the high concentrations required for prebiotic chemistry, and an energy source to drive the chemistry. A deep ocean, and in some cases the high-pressure ice layers underneath, has traditionally been thought to prevent the required concentrations. Here we outline a location where nutrients could be concentrated in sufficiently high quantities to make abiogenesis possible – at the interface between the open ocean and the surface ice shelf. Using a 3D General Circulation Model, we explore cases corresponding to several candidate habitable exoplanets which might have dayside sea ice. We discuss how the planet’s climate influences the nature and behaviour of the sea ice. We investigate the ability of small-scale ice formation and melting processes to concentrate nutrients to prebiotically useful levels, and also explore the potential for meteoritic impactor fragments to provide a platform for prebiotic chemistry. We find that both of these mechanisms may plausibly provide concentrated chemical feedstock for prebiotic chemistry, which adds an important new perspective when evaluating the prospects of habitability in planets with deep oceans.

items.title: Two sides of the same spin: Tracking optical and radio pulsations of SAX J1808.4-3658 from outburst to quiescence
items.abstract: High-time resolution optical and UV observations have recently revealed unexpectedly bright coherent pulsations from accreting millisecond X-ray pulsars. Their luminosity exceeds that expected from thermal emission from neutron-star hotspots or X-ray reflection by the accretion disk. Characterizing optical pulsations over a wide range of accretion rates through coordinated multiwavelength observations is expected to shed light on their origin. We present a timing study of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 during its 2022 outburst and quiescent state, using high-time-resolution optical observations with TNG/SiFAP2, simultaneous NICER X-ray data, optical monitoring from LCO, and MeerKAT radio observations in quiescence. During the outburst, we detect coherent optical pulsations, with pulsed luminosities of sim1.3 , . Combined with previous detections, our results suggest that the optical pulsed amplitude increases as the X-ray flux decreases. The X-ray and optical pulsed luminosities appear to show opposite trends with X-ray luminosity, suggesting different responses of the two pulsed components to changes in the accretion rate. We also measure X-ray-to-optical delays of 0.88 ± 0.04, and 0.51 ± 0.03, on two different outburst observations, indicating that the relative timing between the two signals is not constant. Together with the spectral energy distribution, these results support different emission mechanisms for the pulsed radiation in the two bands, with nonthermal emission from relativistic particles producing optical pulsations and channeled accretion onto the neutron-star surface powering X-ray pulsations. During quiescence, we detect no coherent optical pulsations, obtaining a 95% confidence upper limit of L^ 30 -1 ms ms V, UL _ pulsed <2.2 , on the optical pulsed luminosity, corresponding to an optical efficiency comparable to those of spider radio millisecond pulsars. Simultaneous MeerKAT observations reveal no radio pulsations down to 10^ 29 -1 significantly improving previous constraints, but not excluding the presence of an active rotation-powered pulsar whose radio emission may be absorbed by intra-binary material.

items.title: Neutrino production at the extreme vicinity of the supermassive black hole in NGC 1068
items.abstract: The identification of NGC~1068 as an extragalactic high-energy neutrino source raises the question of the physical conditions required for neutrino production. Motivated by the newly updated IceCube data (down to $\sim 0.2 \,\rm TeV$) for NGC 1068, we present a statistical, model-independent inference primarily constrained by the multi-messenger observations. We calculate neutrino production from hadronic channels (including hadronuclear and photomeson processes) and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, and then employ the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method to explore the parameter space comprehensively, constrained by observational data. According to our results, the emission region is tightly limited: $R \gtrsim 10\,R_{\rm s}$ is excluded at $\sim 5σ$, and $R \gtrsim 6\,R_{\rm s}$ at $\sim 3σ$, where $R_{\rm s}$ is Schwarzschild radius of supermassive black hole (SMBH). Furthermore, reproducing $\gtrsim 80\%$ of the observed neutrino flux further restricts the emission to $R \lesssim 3R_{\rm s}$. Finally, we explore the possible particle acceleration mechanisms and find that stochastic acceleration naturally satisfies all constraints, whereas alternative mechanisms require extreme, fine-tuning parameters. We therefore identify stochastic acceleration as the most viable origin of the neutrino emission from NGC~1068.

items.title: Perceptions and recommendations: exploring the ethics of using satellite data to understand, monitor, and publish research on international geohazards
items.abstract: Abstract. Over the last ten years, open-access earth observation satellite data volumes have grown exponentially. Through use of this data, geohazard remote sensing scientists' abilities to impact policy and reduce societal vulnerability to geohazards has become increasingly tangible. However, much of this open-access data is acquired, stored, and disseminated by the Global North, whilst most disasters take place in the Global South. Furthermore, many societies are imaged by these earth observation satellites perhaps without knowing these satellites exist. There exists little ethical guidance for remote sensing researchers in navigating ethical risks that may arise during geohazard research which uses satellite data. We explore these ethical considerations with UK based geohazard remote sensing scientists through thirteen interviews and three focus group discussions. We discuss with scientists their thoughts on ethical review systems for geohazard remote sensing; the importance of visiting study regions; how data should be handled which images people and societies; the desired impact these scientists want to achieve; and the ethical risks of open data. We find among remote sensing researchers in industry, government organisations, and academia a deep desire to contribute to the reduction of societal vulnerabilities to geohazards. In accordance with geoethical practice, all participants are driven to produce world-leading research outputs to contribute to disaster risk reduction. However, we find among the academic geohazard remote sensing community a misunderstanding around the purpose and need to consider research ethics, focusing mainly on personal privacy rather than ethical risks associated with their own research. This community additionally struggles to balance their desire of meaningfully reducing societal vulnerability to geohazards with the demands of academic expectations and national excellence frameworks. Resultingly, despite best intentions, time, funding, and academic pressures sometimes drive researchers to seek and publish data and results without consultation with in-country communities, particularly post disaster. We recommend geohazard remote sensing researchers receive training to promote the need and ability to reduce ethical risks in their research through five main topics, including practices for decolonisation of geohazard research. We propose a light-touch ethical review system at project design stage would allow ethical risk identification and mitigation. Our findings and recommendations are in accordance with geoethical practice and build on the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.

items.title: Thermodynamic uncertainty relation for generalized time-reversal observables
items.abstract: Time-reversal symmetry plays an essential role in the thermodynamic uncertainty relations, which bound the fluctuations of observables in terms of the associated dissipation. In fact, thermodynamic uncertainty relations are typically derived under the assumption that the observable of interest is antisymmetric under time reversal. This also suggests that existing thermodynamic uncertainty relations are restricted to a limited class of observables. In this paper, we mitigate this restriction by introducing a new class of observables that do not exhibit the exact antisymmetry but change the sign under time reversal. We call it generalized time reversal and derive a broadly applicable thermodynamic uncertainty relation for observables with this condition. The generalization is achieved by direct statistical arguments on the observable distributions and holds for both deterministic and stochastic dynamics. We demonstrate the derived thermodynamic uncertainty relation with observables subjected to rectifications, showing that the precision of generalized observables remains expressible in terms of the dissipative cost. The result extends the scope of thermodynamic uncertainty relations beyond the reach of previous frameworks relying on the exact antisymmetry.

items.title: Toward Scalable Audio Description Quality Control: A Workflow for Evaluating Human and VLM Raters
items.abstract: Digital video is central to communication, education, and entertainment, but without audio description (AD), blind and low-vision users are excluded. While crowdsourced platforms and vision-language models (VLMs) expand AD production, quality is rarely checked systematically. Existing evaluations rely on n-gram overlap metrics and short-clip guidelines, leaving open the question of how to assess long-form AD quality at scale. To address this, we developed a methodological workflow using Item Response Theory to evaluate VLM and human rater proficiency against expert-established ground truth. Evaluations were based on a six-dimensional framework, grounded in professional guidelines and shaped by insights from our accessibility experts and blind consultants. Findings suggest that top-performing VLMs can approximate ground-truth ratings at levels comparable to human raters. However, qualitative analysis reveals that VLM reasoning is less reliable and actionable than that of human respondents. These insights underscore the potential of hybrid evaluation systems that leverage VLMs alongside human oversight, offering a path toward scalable AD quality control.

items.title: Me, Myself, and My Voice: Exploring Cultural and Linguistic Identity in AAC AI-generated Voices
items.abstract: Voice is a central element of identity. We recognize people by their voice, and we uniquely express who we are with it. For people who rely on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, such as speech-generating devices (SGD), the device’s voice becomes an identity marker others associate with them. Yet, it is hard to find a voice that truly aligns with one’s identity both linguistically and culturally. Although modern AI-generated voices can reproduce diverse accents and speaking styles, AAC users still lack accessible ways to articulate how they want an identity-aligned voice to sound like. We first conducted a survey of AAC users (across eight countries) to characterize current voice representation, finding that non-binary, transgender, and non-US-born respondents rated their current voice support identity alignment consistently lower than other respondents. To examine how AAC users respond to voices designed to reflect their cultural identity, we built a tool that elicits cultural markers through guided questions and generates personalized voice candidates for participants to hear and reflect on. After participants heard the voices, we interviewed them to examine what it means for a voice to feel culturally representative, how they interpreted voices with cultural connotations, and how these voices shaped their sense of identity and agency. Our findings show that cultural voice alignment runs deeper than accent or language alone; it touches on belonging, self-recognition, and what it means to be heard as who you are.

items.title: Intraoperative electrocorticography-guided resection of epileptogenic cavernomas: our strategy and literature review.
items.abstract: Objective Intraoperative electrocorticography (ECoG) in the resection of cavernomas associated with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) has traditionally been performed with strip/grid electrodes for superficial cortical recording. However, there is no evidence demonstrating a better epileptological outcome for ECoG-guided corticectomy beyond the hemosiderin ring compared with resection limited to the hemosiderin ring. The authors describe a new surgical strategy for intraoperative ECoG recording that combines surface strip ECoG (sECoG) with the intraoperative use of a stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) electrode to enable recording of deep areas, such as mesial temporal regions, during resection. Methods The authors conducted a retrospective study of a prospectively collected surgical series of cavernoma-related epilepsy (CRE) cases resistant to antiseizure medications treated surgically at their center. They evaluated the seizure outcome after ECoG-guided tailored resection for the treatment of CRE, and they performed multivariate analysis and proportion comparisons to assess which techniques were associated with better seizure outcomes. A systematic literature review of intraoperative ECoG-guided resection for treating CRE was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Results Twenty-three patients with supratentorial cavernomas associated with DRE who underwent surgery at their center between September 2020 and May 2024 were selected. The postoperative follow-up was conducted at least 12 months after the procedure. Engel class IA outcomes were achieved in 100% of patients who underwent extension of the lesionectomy to areas identified with the SEEG electrode and sECoG. In the multivariate analysis, SEEG electrode application was the only variable statistically associated with better seizure outcomes (Engel class IA). The authors included 12 studies in the systematic review. Conclusions Based on the authors' preliminary experience, the combined SEEG electrode/sECoG technique enables a good seizure outcome for the treatment of CRE. Moreover, compared with sECoG, the use of SEEG electrodes was found to be associated with improved seizure outcomes.

items.title: Blood-Based Biomarkers as Predictors of All-Cause Dementia: A 13-Year Follow-Up in the Whitehall II Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers are strongly correlated with amyloid positivity in research settings, but their long-term performance in heterogeneous populations remains unclear. Our aim was to determine their long-term prediction accuracy for incident all-cause dementia on their own and when used alongside known risk factors in community-dwelling older adults. Methods This was a retrospective study based on the UK Whitehall II longitudinal, population-based cohort study established in 1985 among civil servants that includes a clinical examination every 4-5 years. Blood samples stored at the 2013-2013 wave were assayed in 2024 for measures of amyloid-beta (Aβ) 42 and 40, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light (NfL), and phosphorylated tau protein 217 (p-tau217). Incident all-cause dementia, from 2012 to 2013 to 2025, was ascertained from linked medical records, and Cox regression was used to examine associations of biomarkers with dementia, followed by estimation of prediction statistics. Results Of the 5,225 (27.2% female) participants (mean age in 2012-2013, 69.4 ± 5.7 years), 516 (30.0% female) had a dementia diagnosis over a 12.2-year median follow-up. Participants with values in the worst quartile of amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ42)/40 ratio (hazard ratio [HR] 1.88; 95% CI 1.57-2.24), p-tau217 (HR 3.74; 95% CI 3.12-4.50), NfL (HR 1.88; 95% CI 1.56-2.28), and GFAP (HR 2.25; 95% CI 1.87-2.72) had higher risk of dementia. The C-index for predicting dementia was highest for p-tau217 (0.693; 95% CI 0.672-0.714), lowest for Aβ42/40 ratio (0.587; 95% CI 0.566-0.608), and was 0.760 (0.738, 0.781) for all biomarkers together. Sensitivity (between 41.7% and 59.5%) and positive predictive value (between 16.4% and 23.5%) of all biomarkers were modest, but specificity (between 76.8% and 78.8%) and negative predictive value (92.3%-94.7%) were good. A second approach to prediction modeling showed a model containing sociodemographic, behavioral, and health-related risk factors to have a C-index of 0.765 (95% CI 0.746-0.785); adding all biomarkers to this model led to a C-index of 0.813 (95% CI 0.795-0.830). Discussion The long-term predictive ability of blood-based biomarkers for incident dementia in community-dwelling older adults was modest due to poor sensitivity and similar to that of a model containing known risk factors.

items.title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains.
items.abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662 , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

items.title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs.
items.abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 "FADDosome" complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor-driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor-initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor-driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

items.title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection.
items.abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor ( Ifnar1 -/- ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors ( Ifnar1 -/- Ifnlr1 -/- ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1 -/- dams compared to Ifnar1 -/- Ifnlr1 -/- dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1 -/- Ifnlr1 -/- dams compared to Ifnar1 -/- dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ-responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

items.title: Susumu Tonegawa (1939-2026): A molecular biologist who transformed immunology and neuroscience.
items.abstract: Susumu Tonegawa transformed two fields of biology. His discovery of the genetic mechanism generating antibody diversity established the foundations of modern immunology and earned him the 1987 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Remarkably, he then began a second scientific career in neuroscience, pioneering genetic approaches to dissect the molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory and, ultimately, the neuronal ensembles that store specific memories. He was also an ambitious institution builder whose leadership shaped neuroscience at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and RIKEN. As former trainees from his immunology and neuroscience labs, we remember a scientist of extraordinary curiosity, intensity, and intellectual courage, who was never afraid to leave familiar territory in pursuit of a fundamental question.

items.abstract: Plasma membrane sheets provide direct access to the cytosolic face of the cellular membrane while retaining membrane-associated proteins and lipids. This platform is readily adaptable to investigate diverse membrane proteins, lipid-dependent mechanisms, and vesicle tethering events across cellular systems.

items.title: Mapping the topographic organization of the human zona incerta using diffusion MRI.
items.abstract: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an 'immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said'. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral-caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.

items.title: Morphology and ultrastructure of pharyngeal sense organs of Drosophila larvae.
items.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.

items.title: Ataxia Therapeutics: A Comprehensive Overview of the Clinical Development Pipeline.
items.abstract: Ataxias are a heterogeneous group of rare neurological disorders characterized by progressive impairment of motor coordination and balance, caused by a broad range of genetic, immune-mediated, and degenerative mechanisms. Despite significant advances in molecular diagnostics and disease characterization, effective disease-targeted treatments remain limited, with omaveloxolone currently representing the only approved therapy for Friedreich's ataxia. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of the clinical drug development pipeline for ataxias, based on a systematic analysis of international clinical trial registries up to April 2026. One hundred and fifty-four interventional pharmacological trials investigating 66 therapeutic agents across phases 1-3 were identified. The majority of ongoing clinical efforts focus on symptomatic and supportive therapies, which together constitute more than half of the pipeline and include the most developmentally advanced programs. Neuroprotective therapies represent a substantial portion of trials but have shown mixed efficacy to date. In contrast, disease-targeted approaches, including gene therapies, antisense oligonucleotides, cell-based therapies, and protein replacement strategies, account for a smaller share of the pipeline and remain largely confined to early-phase development. More than half of investigational agents are repurposed compounds, reflecting a pragmatic strategy to accelerate therapeutic progress in rare disorders. Overall, the ataxia therapeutic landscape is expanding but remains fragmented, underscoring the need for improved patient stratification, validated biomarkers, harmonized registries, and international collaboration to enable the successful translation of emerging therapies into clinical practice.

items.title: The 'good mobile': a mobile launcher for children to facilitate human interactions.
items.abstract: Children today grow up in a hybrid physical and digital environment, engaging with mobile devices from an early age, which poses a risk of negatively impacting their development. This usage often replaces social interactions and physical activities, potentially deteriorating relationships, socio-cognitive skills, and mental health. Banning device use is unrealistic, but the way children use mobiles can be altered through responsible technology. In the present study we (1) explored parental expectations regarding children's mobile applications, (2) directlyincorporated these expectations into the design of a specific application (Alphie), and (3) examined its reception through UX testing. Alphie is a child-focused application (launcher) that promotes social interaction, real-world activities, and reduces solitary screen time. Its design is informed by parental expectations and scientific data, emphasizing educational, age-appropriate, and moderately stimulating content, with parental control features. A user study with parent-child dyads showed positive experiences. Notably, the games requiring active parental involvement were also well-received, suggesting that they are effective tools for facilitating joint activities within the family. This research highlights how responsible technology can support the mental and physical health of the new generation. By linking parental expectations, application design, and user experience within a single framework, the present studyprovides a more integrative perspective on the development and evaluation of child-focused digital applications.
