items.title: Memory-Based Learning Disabilities: A Syndrome without a Pigeonhole-Towards a Mechanism-First Assessment Framework.
items.abstract: Memory-based learning disabilities represent a distinct and underrecognized clinical entity that current diagnostic classification systems fail to capture. This theoretical synthesis argues that these difficulties constitute an identifiable syndrome defined by neuropsychological vulnerabilities in declarative memory systems, particularly those dependent on hippocampal function. Evidence from cognitive neuroscience, developmental neuropsychology, and educational psychology converges to identify a distinctive phenotypic profile that differentiates memory-based learning disabilities from other developmental learning disorders. Five etiologic pathways are identified, including hypoxic ischemic, toxic metabolic, epileptic electrical, genetic congenital, and perinatal traumatic pathways, which converge on hippocampal and related medial temporal networks to produce an identifiable phenotype. Classification systems organized by academic domain systematically overlook children whose primary difficulty lies in memory-based learning rather than phonological processing, attention, or general intellectual ability. Comprehensive assessment of declarative memory function may improve the identification and characterization of children whose learning difficulties are not adequately captured by current academic domain based classifications. Memory-based learning disabilities should be recognized as a distinct syndrome, with important implications for assessment, intervention, and future research.

items.title: Loneliness relates to smaller hippocampal subfield volumes in individuals with elevated plasma pTau217: results from IGNITE.
items.abstract: Loneliness is associated with cognitive decline and dementia risk, but the role of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology in its associations with medial temporal lobe (MTL) morphology remains unclear. We examined whether loneliness was related to total hippocampal volume, hippocampal subfields, and entorhinal cortex (ERC) volumes, and whether plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) moderated these relationships. We analyzed baseline data from cognitively unimpaired older adults aged 65-80 years enrolled in IGNITE. Loneliness was assessed using the revised UCLA Loneliness Scale. Structural 3 T MRI included a high-resolution T2-weighted hippocampal sequence. Hippocampal subfields and ERC volumes were extracted using ASHS, and FreeSurfer estimated total hippocampal volume and intracranial volume. Participants were classified as pTau217-positive or negative using an Aβ-PET-calibrated threshold (> 0.46 pg/mL). Covariate-adjusted linear regression models tested loneliness associations and loneliness×pTau217 interactions. We included 601 participants (69.8 ± 3.7 years; 72.2% female; 76.4% White); 582 had usable pTau217 data, of whom 28.9% were pTau217-positive. pTau217 moderated associations with CA3 (β = - 0.215, 95% CI - 0.381 to - 0.048) and ERC (β = - 0.167, 95% CI - 0.318 to - 0.016), with negative associations observed among pTau217-positive but not pTau217-negative participants. Greater loneliness was associated with smaller total hippocampal volume (β = - 0.077, 95% CI, - 0.147 to - 0.007, p = 0.031), but not with individual subfields. Loneliness showed biomarker-dependent associations with MTL subfields, suggesting that pTau217-defined biological risk may modify links between psychosocial factors and neuroanatomical vulnerability. This biomarker-informed framework may help explain heterogeneity in prior loneliness-neuroimaging findings.Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02875301.

items.title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
items.abstract: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF). This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory. Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively. Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Is Narrative Enhancement Possible in Healthy Aging? A Preliminary Investigation into the Effects of Advanced Training Activities.
items.abstract: Over the past two decades, age-related declines have been documented in both the micro- and macrolinguistic aspects of language processing, adversely affecting discourse production in older adults. The present study investigated the potential for enhancing narrative abilities in healthy aging through the Advanced Cognitive Pragmatic Treatment (Advanced-CPT), an intervention designed to improve narrative and communicative abilities by targeting multiple aspects of social interaction. Nineteen healthy Italian-speaking adults aged 65-86 years participated in the program, which consisted of nine sessions lasting approximately 90 min each. Narrative assessments were conducted before training (T0), immediately after training (T1), and at a three-month follow-up (T2) using standardized tasks based on two single‑scene pictures and two cartoon‑sequence stories, administered individually to each participant. Oral productions were transcribed and analyzed using multilevel discourse analysis. The results revealed significant improvements in both microlinguistic and macrolinguistic skills, particularly through reductions in morphological and local coherence errors. Participants also produced more complete sentences and demonstrated greater lexical informativeness following training. Although total word production decreased at follow-up, this pattern was interpreted as reflecting more efficient communication rather than reduced productivity. Overall, the findings suggest that targeted intervention can enhance narrative abilities in healthy aging and support the potential of structured narrative training to promote communicative competence. These results provide new avenues for enhancing quality of life through structured narrative training interventions.

items.title: NMN Ameliorates STXBP1-R292C Variant-mediated Developmental and Motor Dysfunction: Molecular Docking and Functional Studies.
items.abstract: STXBP1-related disorders (STXBP1-RD) are severe neurodevelopmental conditions associated with synaptic dysfunction, presenting an unmet medical need. P.Arg292Cys (R292C) variant is predicted to alter protein stability and affect interactions involved in synaptic vesicle fusion. This study aimed to screen for interactions between STXBP1-R292C and FDA-approved drugs and natural compounds using in silico and in vivo methods to better understand STXBP1-RD molecular defects. We employed computational structural modeling of STXBP1-R292C, screening and ranking transiently interacting drugs, followed by in vivo phenotypic assessment in a humanized STXBP1-R292C Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) model, and longitudinal clinical observation in a single individual carrying the R292C variant. STXBP1-interacting FDA-approved drugs and natural compounds were identified using in silico analysis based on predicted structural effects. C. elegans locomotion features were quantified using standardized assays. Clinical outcomes were assessed using Vineland-III over 25 months. Computational modeling identified β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) as one of the lead compounds predicted to transiently stabilize the STXBP1-R292C. We further discovered that NMN was unstable in the R292C mutant STXBP1 pocket and diffused from it, whereas its metabolite the essential coenzyme, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) remained stable at the binding site throughout the structural simulation. In the C. elegans model, NMN exposure partially, but significantly, modulated locomotion phenotypes toward a wild-type (WT) profile. Vineland-III assessment of a child (2-4 years old) with STXBP1-RD and motor delays showed improved motor domain scores, while other developmental domains displayed limited changes. Our study revealed an association between STXBP1-R292C/STXBP1 and NMN/NAD+ as a lead molecule. At the organismal level, NMN treatment ameliorated motor defects in humanized STXBP1-R292C C. elegans. Lastly, 2-year observations in a child carrying the same mutation suggested an NMN effect on the motor domain, toward a future well-designed clinical trial.

items.title: Tau A152T risk variant drives distinct cell type transcriptional signatures in AD and PSP.
items.abstract: The A152T point mutation is a rare genetic variant in the tau gene (MAPT) that is linked to risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia spectrum disorders, including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD). To uncover mechanisms through which the A152T variant contributes to risk of tauopathy, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on postmortem brain tissue collected from A152T carriers and pathology-matched non-carriers with either AD or PSP, along with age-matched controls. These efforts revealed that despite similar cell type composition across groups, A152T carriers exhibited distinct cell type-specific transcriptional changes in both AD and PSP. Differential expression analysis identified excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes as the most affected cell populations in AD and PSP, and these same cell types showed the strongest A152T-specific changes. These findings identify transcriptional alterations that differentiate sporadic AD and sporadic PSP from AD-A152T and PSP-A152T, as well as shared molecular signatures unique to A152T carriers in both PSP and AD. Donor-level pseudo-bulk analyses showed broad directional support with the single-nucleus findings although the proportion of donor-supported genes varied across cell type and comparison. Importantly, merging sporadic and A152T cases into a single disease group was found to mask transcriptional differences in several cell types in both AD and PSP, indicating divergence in transcriptional signature and highlighting the importance of screening for genetic risk variants like A152T in snRNA-seq data from human cohorts.

items.title: The Dutch Mini-Linguistic State Examination (MLSE-NL): findings in Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA).
items.abstract: State of the art Changes in speech and language occur as the first symptoms of Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA). The Mini-Linguistic State Examination (MLSE) is a short speech and language screening test used in the diagnostic process of PPA in English-speaking patients. We adapted the MLSE into Dutch (MLSE-NL) and validated this new version as a diagnostic screening tool in Dutch-speaking patients. Methodology We assessed the MLSE-NL in 90 Dutch-speaking patients with PPA (nonfluent variant PPA (nfvPPA) n = 23, logopenic variant PPA (lvPPA) n = 24, semantic variant PPA (svPPA) n = 32, PPA Not Otherwise Specified (PPA-NOS) n = 11) (mean age: 68.3, 47.8% male) and 276 healthy volunteers (mean age: 56.3, 38.8% male). The MLSE-NL includes subscores in motor speech, phonological structure, semantic knowledge, syntax, and working memory. Group differences were assessed using Kruskal-Wallis tests, with linear models controlling for covariates as confirmatory analyses. Results The MLSE-NL shows significantly lower scores for all PPA variants for total score, ranging from 30 to 96/100 in patients and 83 to 100/100 in controls. The AUC for total score was 0.99 (subdomain AUCs ranged from 0.80 to 0.92). nfvPPA had more motor speech errors than controls, svPPA had more semantic errors, while lvPPA had the most working memory deficits. Syntax errors were frequent in all variants, while phonological deficits were greater in lvPPA and nfvPPA. PPA-NOS had deficits in all domains aside from motor speech. Conclusions The MLSE-NL can successfully discriminate the three canonical variants of PPA and PPA-NOS from controls and captures domain-specific neurolinguistic profiles.

items.title: Divergent Trends in Relapse Activity and Relapse-Independent Progression Over Two Decades in Multiple Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) management has increasingly favored earlier high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy (DMT). We examined diagnosis-era changes in relapse activity and disability accrual alongside evolving DMT use. We retrospectively analyzed two Italian cohorts of adults with MS onset in 2001-2024 across four diagnosis eras. Annualized relapse rate (ARR) was modeled by Poisson regression; confirmed disability accrual (CDA), relapse-associated worsening (RAW), and progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) by Andersen-Gill Cox models. CDA was classified as RAW when relapse onset occurred from 90 days before through 30 days after the event, otherwise as PIRA. Treatment was time-varying: untreated, low-/moderate-efficacy therapy (LET/MET), or high-efficacy therapy (HET). Inverse probability-weighted models included residual adjustment. Sensitivity analyses examined a strict common 2-year horizon, MRI restriction/adjustment, relapsing-onset MS, first-event analyses, 90-day DMT lag, early-HET exclusion, pre-treatment versus never-treated person-time, visit frequency, and center stratification. Among 1096 patients (228, 214, 292, and 362 across eras 1-4), first-line HET use reached 45.9% in era 4. Each later diagnosis year was associated with lower ARR (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99; p < 0.001), with steeper calendar-time declines during LET/MET and HET than untreated person-time (joint interaction p < 0.001). Later diagnosis year was also associated with lower RAW (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.97; p < 0.001) and modestly lower CDA over full follow-up (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-1.00; p = 0.026), although CDA attenuated in weighted and common-horizon analyses. PIRA was not associated with diagnosis year (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.99-1.04; p = 0.262). Lower ARR and RAW persisted across sensitivities, whereas the strict 2-year analysis suggested higher early PIRA in more recent eras. Later diagnosis-era cohorts had lower relapse activity and relapse-associated disability accrual, whereas overall disability accrual was less consistent and PIRA did not decline. Improvements in relapse-related disease activity were not accompanied by a comparable reduction in relapse-independent disability accrual.

items.title: Clinimetrics of the Shortened Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB15) in Neurodegenerative Disorders.
items.abstract: Introduction This study aimed to provide a clinimetric evaluation of the shortened Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB15) in a large cohort of patients with neurodegenerative disorders. Methods FAB15 scores were retrospectively retrieved from 379 patients with neurocognitive disorders and 260 healthy controls (HCs). The clinical cohort included patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD; n = 147), AD with mixed etiology (n = 26), frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD; n = 52), and Lewy body disease (LBD; n = 32). First, we tested the discriminatory power of FAB15 across etiologies and disease severity. Then, optimal cutoffs were derived, and available normative thresholds were tested for their diagnostic performance. Within the clinical sample, factorial structure, internal consistency, construct validity, and ecological validity were also examined. Results After demographic adjustment, a FAB15 cutoff around 11 optimally discriminated HCs from patients with neurodegenerative disease. Importantly, discrimination was stronger for dementia than MCI and remained consistent across etiologies, with the best performance observed in LBD. Overall, normative cutoffs were highly specific but poorly sensitive, with their screening utility being largely prevalence-dependent. Psychometrically, the FAB15 showed a unidimensional factor structure, strong convergence with executive measures, and weaker associations with episodic memory tasks, as well as functional autonomies. Conclusion The FAB15 is a clinimetrically and psychometrically sound screener for detecting executive dysfunction in neurodegenerative disorders.

items.title: Effect of Pain Science Education and Behavioral Graded Activity on Pain in Survivors of Breast Cancer: A Study Protocol for a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Pain affects up to half of survivors of breast cancer and is one of the most common long-term consequences of cancer treatment, yet it remains under-recognized and undertreated. Pharmacological options often provide limited relief and may cause adverse effects. Evidence from other pain populations supports a biopsychosocial approach combining pain education and physical activity. The objective is to evaluate whether pain science education (PSE) with behavioral graded activity (BGA) versus usual care (UC), reduces pain intensity and interference in survivors of breast cancer with pain. Secondary aims include assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and central pain modulation. This study is a multicenter, two-arm, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized controlled superiority trial. The trial will be conducted in Belgium, with interventions delivered in hospital and academic research settings. Two hundred women with a history of breast cancer and persistent pain will be recruited. Participants will be randomized to either (1) PSE (1 session) plus 5 BGA sessions delivered by a trained physical therapist, or (2) usual care with a standardized biomedical pain information leaflet, over a 12-week period. The primary outcome will be pain intensity and interference (Brief Pain Inventory). Secondary outcomes will include HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30) and central pain modulation (Quantitative Sensory Testing). Exploratory outcomes include sleep, fatigue, pain-related cognitions, and health care utilization. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and at 3-month (primary endpoint), 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups. This trial will determine whether a structured PSE+BGA program improves pain and HRQoL in survivors of breast cancer, offering a potential scalable non-pharmacological treatment. These findings may guide targeted rehabilitation strategies and strengthen the role of physical therapists in managing post-cancer pain, particularly in light of the growing population of survivors of breast cancer and the increasing prevalence of persistent symptoms.

items.title: CuS-Cu<sub>2</sub>S/γ-Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> for efficient Cr(VI) elimination from electroplating wastewater: The role of surface-active Cu-based sulfide phase regulation.
items.abstract: Conventional adsorbents for Cr(VI) elimination from electroplating wastewater are constrained by limited uptake capacity, poor recyclability, and inadequate management of retained chromium. To tackle these issues, a magnetically recoverable CuS/γ-Fe 2 O 3 composite was developed as a reusable adsorbent. Upon thermal annealing, a partial phase transformation from CuS to Cu 2 S occurred, yielding a mixed CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 hybrid. This hybrid exhibited enhanced Cr(VI) capture, achieving 87.2 mg g -1 at pH 4.0, 25 °C, 0.5 g L -1 adsorbent dosage, and 50 mg L -1 initial Cr(VI). Elimination process proceeded via the adsorption-reduction route, governed by surface reductant availability and affinity aqueous Cr(VI) and H + . Although the CuS-to-Cu 2 S transformation reduced total reductant sites, it improved Cr(VI) and H + adsorption, likely due to the unique surface properties of Cu 2 S; hence, the CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 composite outperformed its single-phase counterpart. Moreover, this composite also showed good stability and reusability, maintaining 100% Cr(VI) removal over fifteen cycles while retaining magnetic recoverability. Furthermore, repeated adsorption enabled efficient Cr(VI) enrichment from electroplating wastewater onto CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 , allowing the spent adsorbent to serve as a potential substitute for chromium ore. In summary, these findings highlighted CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 as a highly promising adsorbent for treating Cr(VI)-bearing electroplating wastewater.

items.title: Convergent Biogenic Magnetite Formation from Diverse Iron (Oxyhydr)oxide Precursors Drives Cr(VI) Reduction via an Environmental Battery Mechanism.
items.abstract: Iron (oxyhydr)oxides mediate electron flux across coupled biogeochemical cycles in anoxic environments, yet whether their biogenic transformation feeds back to reshape interfacial electron transfer efficiency remains unresolved. Here, five structurally distinct iron (oxyhydr)oxide precursors (ferrihydrite, goethite, magnetite, wüstite, and hematite) were exposed to anaerobic sulfur-oxidizing bioreactors under Cr(VI) stress, and their transformation trajectories were tracked using synchrotron EXAFS spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, DFT calculations, and metagenomic profiling. Mineral bioavailability decreased in the order ferrihydrite > goethite > magnetite > wüstite > hematite, a hierarchy governed by lattice iron-leaching energetics quantified via DFT (Efev from -8.96 eV for ferrihydrite to 5.76 eV for hematite). Despite this wide disparity in precursor lability, all biotransformation trajectories converged on magnetite as the thermodynamically stable end point. In the ferrihydrite system, biogenic magnetite reached 60% of the final solid phase and operated as an in situ "environmental battery" (storing and releasing electrons through reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) lattice cycling), lowering interfacial charge transfer resistance and producing a 4.77-fold higher pseudo-first-order Cr(VI) reduction rate constant than the mineral-free biotic control (C-S). Metagenomic analysis revealed mineral-specific restructuring of the microbial community toward a tightly coupled sulfur-iron redox network. These results reframe precursor mineralogy from a determinant of intrinsic reactivity to a kinetic regulator of biogenic electron-buffer formation, providing a mechanistic basis for mineral-informed bioremediation design.

items.title: Model-based multilocus, genomic, and phenotypic integration reveals species assignment inconsistencies and sampling blind spots across Asian ecozones in Dicroglossidae.
items.abstract: Widespread amphibians often show inconsistent species assignments in public databases, complicating accurate range-wide biodiversity mapping and obscuring gaps in taxonomic resolution. We assessed three widespread cryptic Asian Dicroglossid genera (Fejervarya, Hoplobatrachus, Quasipaa) across Indomalayan and Palearctic ecozones, where diffuse boundaries, taxonomic uncertainty, and exotic introduction impact biodiversity patterns. Using a hierarchical, scenario-based species delimitation framework based on publicly available molecular datasets and targeted new data, we evaluated 18 species-delimitation scenarios across 14 nominal taxa, with GenBank-based assignment as a control model. All scenarios were based on shared multilocus Dicroglossidae datasets (up to 517 sequence entries), integrating GenBank data with targeted sampling across two ecozones. The best-supported scenario was further refined using genome-derived SNPs from heterogeneous data sources (GBS, RNA-seq, and WGS/WCS), together with a binary morphological trait. Across analyses, the best-supported Model A1 showed a lower MLE than GenBank-based assignments, indicating non-random taxonomic mismatches between updated local classifications and public database entries. The model delineated 17 dicroglossid clades, including a single Hoplobatrachus lineage in East Asia. Diverging over 19 Mya, Fejervarya showed pronounced cryptic structure, with two deeply divergent clades recovered within the F. limnocharis, F. kawamurai, and F. multistriata species complexes, while Quasipaa displayed deep divergences. Integration of ecological niche modelling and bioacoustic analyses for a selected sympatric pair at the ecozone boundary further showed differences in predicted habitat associations and selected acoustic traits between F. kawamurai [Clade II] and F. multistriata [Clade I], despite substantial range overlap. Fejervarya multistriata was associated with coastal lowlands, whereas F. kawamurai was more widely distributed inland. Our integrative framework highlights regions with high mismatch under dense sampling (e.g., the Yangtze-Huai transition and East Asian mainland), and regions with mismatch under limited sampling, particularly insular systems (e.g., Taiwan and Hainan), defining priorities for future genomic surveys.

items.title: Integrating ecology with genetics to explain gene reuse during repeated evolution.
items.abstract: The role of determinism and chance in the evolutionary history of life is often analyzed through the lens of the repeatability of evolution. Although it is now clear that evolution often repeats itself, we are only beginning to understand why this varies in degree. For example, the probability of gene reuse during repeated bouts of adaptation often declines with time since divergence, but the causes of this pattern remain unclear. Here, we explore two core hypotheses for time-dependent variation in the repeatability of gene reuse during adaptation. Specifically, gene reuse depends on the extent to which lineages have 1) similar genomes such that they have similar genetic architectures, mutations, and mutational effects (i.e., a fairly well-appreciated "shared genetics" hypothesis), and 2) similar ecologies such that they have similar environments and patterns of natural selection (i.e., a mostly unexplored "shared ecology" hypothesis). The latter hypothesis emphasizes ecology's role in gene reuse and has received little explicit attention. In particular, testing the shared ecology hypothesis requires moving beyond a simple dichotomous characterization of ecology to embracing ecological divergence as a multivariate and continuous phenomenon. Although such tests are only beginning to emerge, they already illustrate how integration of ecological factors can help explain variation in gene reuse. Here, we advocate a framework that integrates the influence of both genetic and ecological factors in the repeatability of evolution and can be applied to a range of organisms to better understand the role of determinism and chance in biological diversification.

items.title: Instructor Development of Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) Self-Efficacy within a PoP-CURE Professional Development Community of Practice.
items.abstract: This case study investigates changes in technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) self-efficacy in a group of instructors engaged in a Power of Place Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experience (PoP-CURE) Professional Development (PD) Community of Practice. We hypothesized that mentored and iterative PD would create a community of practice in which instructors become confident adopters of evidence-based technological PoP-CURE practices, promoting the overall development of instructor TPACK self-efficacy. Previous work on PD personas helped to inform our work by guiding observations of how interactions and individual choices contributed to TPACK self-efficacy. Within this case, the multiple embedded units of analysis were the five personas identified from the previous work. We found increases in various components of TPACK across all personas, but different TPACK components were emphasized for different personas. In-person PD retreats and group meetings offered opportunities for mastery, vicarious learning, and verbal persuasion to increase self-efficacy in TPACK building blocks (content knowledge, technological knowledge, and pedagogical knowledge). Mastery experiences during implementation, followed by reflection during the community of practice, were the sources of more complex forms of TPACK self-efficacy.

items.title: Three-spined sticklebacks do not respond behaviorally to environmentally relevant concentrations of the toxic explosive 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene.
items.abstract: Approximately 1.6 million tons of conventional munitions were dumped in German coastal waters. Corrosion of munition shells facilitates the leakage of explosives, such as the toxic and carcinogenic 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT), into the marine environment. Consequently, TNT contamination was detected in seawater, sediments, and marine organisms near munition dump sites, and is known to cause adverse effects in marine organisms. Accordingly, avoidance of contaminated areas would be advantageous for fish. We therefore hypothesized that fish respond to dissolved TNT and exhibit an avoidance reaction. To test this, we exposed three-spined sticklebacks (Gasterosteus aculeatus) to environmentally relevant TNT concentrations and evaluated their behavioral response. Individual fish were placed in a behavioral test tank equipped with two hideout zones composed of artificial plants. The hideout zone occupied by the stickleback was infused with either TNT solution (100 µg/L) or control water. Behavioral readouts included the time stickleback spent in the infused hideout zone, time until the exposed hideout zone was first left, and number of transitions between hideout zones. Sticklebacks did not exhibit significant behavioral responses to environmentally relevant TNT exposure. Consequently, fish inhabiting munition dump sites may experience chronic TNT exposure, potentially increasing long-term toxicological risks.

items.title: Detection, characterization, and evolutionary inferences regarding a novel virus identified in Amblyomma dissimile Koch, 1844 (Acari: Ixodidae) from the Amazon, Pará, Brazil.
items.abstract: Ticks are among the primary vectors of infectious agents of medical and veterinary importance, second only to mosquitoes in the number of pathogens transmitted to humans. These arthropods are capable of transmitting a wide diversity of microorganisms, including protozoa, bacteria, and viruses. Notable among tick-borne viruses are those associated with viral encephalitis, which cause severe acute and chronic neurological infections in humans. This study aimed to characterize the RNA virome of an Amblyomma dissimile specimen collected from a Boa constrictor rescued in the municipality of Ananindeua, Pará state, in the Brazilian Amazon, using an RNA metagenomic sequencing approach. A total of eleven viral sequences were identified, distributed across five families: Chuviridae (n = 2), Rhabdoviridae (n = 2), Orthomyxoviridae (n = 5), Nodaviridae (n = 1), and Orthototiviridae (n = 1). A key finding was the identification of Dissimile tick rhabdovirus a potential new member of the Rhabdoviridae family described here for the first time, with no prior records in the scientific literature. Additionally, segments of Granville quaranjavirus were detected in Brazil for the first time, expanding the known geographic distribution of this virus. These results highlight the underrepresentation of viral diversity associated with Brazilian ticks in reference databases, underscoring the need to expand metagenomic surveillance and virological characterization efforts in the country, particularly given the potential impacts of climate change on tick distribution and virus circulation dynamics.

items.title: Source-related patterns and ecological risk prioritization of antibiotics in a large lake-river system: insights from the Poyang Lake Basin.
items.abstract: Antibiotic mixtures in large floodplain lake basins are shaped by overlapping anthropogenic inputs, environmental mixing, and compound-specific toxicity, complicating source interpretation and risk prioritization. We measured 10 antibiotics in 158 samples collected during a high-water-period campaign from 26 to 30 August 2023 in the Poyang Lake basin, including 42 lake-water samples and 116 wastewater samples from sewage treatment plants, hospitals, livestock and aquaculture facilities, and pharmaceutical industries. Mean total antibiotic concentration in lake water was 73.9 ng L -1 , dominated by oxytetracycline, chlortetracycline, and tetracycline. Exploratory socio-economic correlation analyses showed category-dependent patterns with economic activity, production intensity, and sector-related antibiotic use. Receptor-side positive matrix factorization resolved three compositional patterns accounting for 46.0%, 11.8%, and 42.1% of modeled antibiotic mass: an oxytetracycline-rich mixed pattern, a sulfamethazine-chlortetracycline-doxycycline mixed pattern, and a chlortetracycline-dominated tetracycline-rich pattern. Source-profile comparison and non-negative least squares fitting indicated mixed and spatially variable compositional consistency with the four wastewater categories rather than evidence for a single dominant source. In the primary Monte Carlo analysis, oxytetracycline, chlortetracycline, and enrofloxacin had the highest probabilities of exceeding a risk quotient of 1 (16.3%, 16.3%, and 14.8%, respectively), while mixture-level summed risk quotients exceeded 1 in 65.1% of simulations. Weighting by predicted no-effect concentrations further increased the relative priority of ciprofloxacin in wastewater profiles and shifted lake-water priorities from oxytetracycline toward enrofloxacin and ofloxacin. These results show that concentration-based composition does not directly represent ecological-risk priority and support source-sensitive, risk-oriented management of antibiotic mixtures in large floodplain lake basins.

items.title: Expanding the geographic and host range of moss-nostocacean symbioses in central Europe.
items.abstract: Since their re-discovery, Moss-cyanobacterial symbioses are of increasing interest, especially Nostoc-feather moss symbioses. Efforts to document Nostoc-feather moss symbioses have historically been centered in Scandinavia and the North American Boreal forest zone. Herein we report the results of several opportunistic surveys investigating the occurrence of Nostocaceae-moss symbioses in the region of Franconia (Germany), from Hylocomium splendens of the forest floor and four moss species (Orthotrichum lyellii, Zygodon dentatus, Homalia trichomanoides, Pseudoamblystegium subtile) located on three tree species (Fagus sylvatica, Fraxinus excelsior, and Sorbus schuwerkiorum). Using culture- and microscopy-based methods, we confirm the occurrence of such symbioses in our region. Four new moss host species for the symbiosis are documented, from the epiphytic family Orthotrichaceae (Orthotrichum sp. and Zygodon sp.), and also Neckeraceae (Homalia trichomanoides) and Amblystegiaceae (Pseudoambylstegium subtile). This further extends the range of known moss hosts for Nostoc and Nostoc-related organisms outside the traditional feather moss (Hypnales) and Sphagnum clades. 16S rRNA gene sequence alignments placed the moss-associated Nostoc and Nostoc-related organisms throughout our Nostocaceae phylogeny, with no obvious single symbiotic clade. We note the presence of multiple alternate nifH genes within the genomes of our cultured Nostoc and Nostoc-related organisms, possibly enabling diazotrophy under variable ecological conditions. We also present evidence for possible endophytic colonization by cyanobacteria of stems of mosses.

items.title: Cordyceps as a multitarget therapeutic platform: biology, bioactive metabolites, and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Cordyceps-related fungi have garnered global attention as multifunctional therapeutic resources owing to their exclusive entomopathogenic biology, remarkable metabolic diversity, and expanding pharmaceutical bearing. Recent taxonomic revisions determined by molecular phylogenetics have redefined the traditional notion of Cordyceps, revealing distinct evolutionary lineages with species-specific metabolite profiles and biological functions. This review provides a complete and evidence-based synthesis of the taxonomy, ecology, host interactions, chemical composition, biosynthetic pathways, pharmacological activities, and translational prospects of chief medicinal species, including Ophiocordyceps sinensis, Cordyceps militaris, Cordyceps cicadae, and related taxa. Particular emphasis is placed on cordycepin, the signature bioactive nucleoside, and its integration with broader metabolite networks encompassing polysaccharides, sterols, peptides, and secondary metabolites. Current evidence demonstrates that Cordyceps-derived compounds influence multiple interconnected signaling pathways, including AMPK, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, NF-κB, MAPK, and oxidative stress-response networks, thereby contributing to immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotective, and metabolic regulatory effects. The review further reviews recent advances in genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, biosynthetic gene-cluster analysis, synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, and exactness fermentation technologies that are redesigning Cordyceps research and industrial production. Critical challenges including species authentication, chemical standardization, pharmacokinetic limitations, product reproducibility, safety evaluation, regulatory requirements, and inadequate clinical validation are also discussed. By integrating biological identity, metabolite biosynthesis, molecular mechanisms, and technological innovation within a translational framework, this review positions Cordyceps as a promising systems-level platform for future therapeutics, functional foods, and precision mycotherapy.

items.title: Ecological impact of steeplebush (Spiraea tomentosa L.) invasion on mite communities (Acari, Mesostigmata) in wet meadow ecosystems.
items.abstract: Invasive plants are species introduced outside their natural range and often cause ecological or economic harm. By modifying litter quality, root architecture, and soil chemistry, invasive plants can alter many soil processes, including nutrient cycling and edaphic activity. The main aim of our study was to provide the first assessment in Poland of the ecological impact of Spiraea tomentosa L. invasion on the abundance, diversity, and species richness of soil Mesotigmata (Gamasida; Gamasina and Uropodnia) mite communities in wet meadow ecosystems, thereby offering novel insights into the belowground ecological consequences of this invasive species. The research was carried out in a wet meadow complex located in the Lower Silesian Forests in south-western Poland. A total of 104 soil samples were collected from 26 experimental plots (13 invaded by Spiraea tomentosa and 13 uninvaded) in May and October 2024. In total, we identified 2,502 mesostigmatid mites belonging to 71 taxa. The three most abundant mite species across the entire study were Paragamasus vagabundus (Karg) (409 ind.), Zercon gurensis Mihelčič (228), and Trachytes aegrota (C. L. Koch) (216). Mite abundance was negatively associated with soil Fe, while litter pH and litter Pb showed positive but non-significant trends. Species richness was positively associated with soil Mn and litter Pb, and negatively associated with soil Fe and litter Cu. Mite diversity showed a significant overall effect of collection time and site type, although Tukey HSD post hoc tests did not detect significant pairwise differences among treatment combinations. Moreover, Mesostigmata diversity increased with soil Mn and K and decreased with soil Fe, Na, and soil moisture. However, diversity was lower at uninvaded sites than at invaded sites. Overall, our findings show that microhabitat alteration associated with the biological invasion of Spiraea tomentosa has a complex impact on the diversity and composition of mite communities.

items.title: Context-dependent sublethal hazard of glyphosate to non-target predators revealed by functional response analysis.
items.abstract: Glyphosate, one of the most widely used herbicides globally, is a significant environmental contaminant that may affect non-target organisms crucial to ecosystem services, including biological pest control. While glyphosate targets the shikimate pathway in plants, which is absent in animals, there is increasing evidence that glyphosate induces sublethal effects on arthropod predators. However, the factors modulating these effects remain unclear. Here, we investigated how physiological context, specifically pre-treatment with the broad-spectrum antibiotic tetracycline, commonly used to experimentally alter host associated microbial communities, modulates the sublethal hazard of glyphosate-based herbicide (GBH) on the predatory behavior of adult female Pardosa wolf spiders. Predation efficiency was measured using functional response assays across varying prey densities. Our results showed that GBH significantly reduced the spiders' predation rates, confirming its sublethal toxicity. However, spiders pre-treated with antibiotics exhibited higher capture rates following GBH exposure compared to the GBH only group. These findings demonstrate that the sublethal hazard of GBH on predators is context-dependent and can be altered by antibiotic-sensitive processes (such as host-symbiont interactions). This study highlights the complexity of pesticide effects on ecosystem services and suggests that the functional response of non-target predators depends strongly on their physiological background.

items.title: Low variability in the capsid gene of a generalist densovirus across lepidopteran hosts and geographic regions.
items.abstract: Viruses are ubiquitous in all ecosystems, and insects can serve as model host systems for understanding their geographic range and host specificity. Lepidoptera are relatively easy to collect and rear and are known to harbor diverse groups of viral pathogens. Much of the research on viruses in Lepidoptera has focused on baculoviruses, but this is beginning to change with better sequencing techniques. In this study, we use genetic tools to characterize the host and geographical range of the Junonia coenia densovirus (JcDV) (Family Parvoviridae, subfamily Densovirinae, genus Protoambidensovirus, specific epithet lepidopteran1). Using host tissue and larval frass, we screened 25 lepidopteran families from 11 locations across North and Central and South America for JcDV. We detected JcDV in the frass from 11 families of Lepidoptera, originating from both Neotropical and Nearctic biogeographic realms. To characterize genetic variation in the viruses detected, we conducted Sanger sequencing of a segment of the viral capsid gene in ten frass samples and from an additional 56 individual lepidopteran cadavers from three families in the Papilionoidea superfamily. Across all sequences obtained, the average sequence identity to the Oxford reference genome sequence was 99.85% and within our samples 99.77%. Compared to the reference, we found 18 nucleotide changes which were characterized into ten JcDV haplotype variants. These differences conferred seven amino acid substitutions and were not predicted by sample type (frass or cadaver tissue), geographic location, or lepidopteran host family. Ultimately, we conclude that JcDV is a widespread virus to which many lepidopteran families are exposed in their natural environment, and the capsid gene of JcDV is genetically well-conserved across geographic space and lepidopteran host species.

items.title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision.
items.abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

items.title: The effects of affect: Working memory, rumination and emotion reactivity - Insights from an affective n-back task.
items.abstract: Objective Internalizing disorders are associated with emotion regulation characterized by repetitive negative thinking. There is a proposed relationship between rumination and working memory and there are gaps in understanding how emotions impact this association. In the present study, we investigated differences in negative (hot) and neutral (cold) working memory processing in relation to measures of rumination and emotion reactivity. Our aim was to address hot working memory as a potential clinically relevant mechanism in challenges with emotion regulation. Emotion reactivity was hypothesized to mediate the relationship between rumination and working memory. Method Participants were undergraduate students (N = 120). Working memory was assessed using the Memory Affective Flexibility Task (MAFT), an affective experimental paradigm based on the n-back task that incorporates neutral and valenced visual stimuli. Facets of maladaptive emotion regulation were measured through self-report questionnaires for rumination and emotion reactivity. Associations were examined using multiple linear regression with rumination as the outcome variable. Results There were small relationships between working memory performance in both neutral and negative conditions of the MAFT with measures of rumination and emotion reactivity. There was a significant moderate correlation between emotion reactivity and rumination. Conclusion Despite correlations among self-report measures of emotion reactivity and rumination, we observed limited support for the links of task-based hot or cold working memory performance with self-rated emotion measures. This aligns with previous reports of modest correlations between task-based and self-report measures. The findings add to a growing literature on the challenges of capturing the interplay between emotion processes, affect and cognition in neuroscientific research.

items.title: Anthropocentric Thinking about Antibiotic Resistance and Ecosystems: Relations between Explanations and Misconceptions in American Undergraduates from Urban and Rural Backgrounds.
items.abstract: Intuitive conceptual frameworks can shape students' reasoning for biology concepts, sometimes forming misconceptions. Anthropocentric thinking-reasoning that centers humans-often relates to misconceptions about antibiotic resistance and ecosystem change. Cultural influences, such as lifestyles with greater exposure to nature, have been associated with reduced anthropocentric reasoning. The backgrounds of rural and urban children vary in opportunities for experiences with nature-rural children have greater exposure and urban children less exposure to outdoor settings. The relationship between students with rural and urban backgrounds and anthropogenic thinking highlights potential differences in students' biology misconceptions. Here, we compare students' rural and urban backgrounds and institutions to their use of anthropocentric reasoning and its relatedness with misconceptions in biology. Students from rural and urban backgrounds were recruited to complete a survey with written and categorical agreement ratings for misconceptions in biology. All students-regardless of hometown population and institution densities-showed similar rates of anthropocentric reasoning. However, the use of anthropocentric language was highly correlated with biological misconceptions. Our research suggests that anthropocentric thinking is pervasive in undergraduate students and influences biological misconceptions.

items.title: Emotional inertia in daily life: a dynamic structural equation modelling analysis of the role of emotion regulation strategy use.
items.abstract: High negative affect inertia refers to negative emotional states that show strong carryover from moment to moment and has been linked to maladjustment and poor mental health. Recent ecological momentary assessment (EMA) research has suggested that emotion regulation strategy use in daily life may contribute to emotional inertia. We build on this by examining the roles of rumination, suppression, reappraisal and acceptance in negative affect inertia for seven affective states in a sample of n = 451 emerging adults (mean age 27) who completed a 2-week EMA protocol. Using two-level dynamic structural modelling with within-person cross-lagged effects, rumination showed significant mediating effects with four negative affective states, implying a role in perpetuating negative affect; however, no other significant mediation effects were identified. Results point to rumination as the most promising intervention target among the emotion regulation strategies examined for reducing negative affect inertia, though the effects were modest.

items.title: Not everything can be counted: how awe enhances perceptions of immeasurability.
items.abstract: Awe arises in reaction to events or objects that exceed our expectancies, such as vast landscapes, breathtaking sunsets, or mind-blowing ideas (Gocłowska, M. A., Elliot, A. J., van Elk, M., Bulska, D., Thorstenson, C. A., & Baas, M. (2023). Awe arises in reaction to exceeded rather than disconfirmed expectancies. Emotion , 23 (1), 15-29.; Keltner, D., & Haidt, J. (2003). Approaching awe, a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion. Cognition and Emotion, 17(2), 297-314.Keltner, D., & Haidt, J. (2003). Approaching awe, a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion. Cognition and Emotion , 17 (2), 297-314.). Little psychological research has investigated how experiencing awe influences people's epistemic beliefs (e.g. beliefs about the nature of knowledge and the process of knowing). To achieve this, we tested how awe affects people's subjective sense of immeasurability , defined as a perception that conventional measures, such as words or numbers, are inadequate to describe aspects of the world around us (e.g. the beauty of nature). Across one correlational study and three experiments ( N = 596, collected between 2024 and 2025), we investigated the relationship between awe and immeasurability. We found that manipulated awe increased people's sense of immeasurability of the beauty of nature. In the final experiment, this effect was explained by the extent to which the awe experience was seen as exceeding (but not disconfirming) expectancies. These findings provide new insights into how awe affects people's epistemic beliefs.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Proposed Cut-Off Values of the ASRS-R for Screening ADHD in Chinese Children and Adolescents: A Case-Control Study.
items.abstract: Building on the prior validation of the Revised Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-R), this case-control study aimed to derive proposed cut-off scores for screening ADHD in Chinese children and adolescents aged 8-14 years. The study included 457 children and adolescents (106 with DSM-5 diagnosed ADHD, 351 controls) from a Shenzhen hospital. Reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.929) and validity (GFI = 0.954; rs = 0.604 with SNAP-IV) were good. ROC analysis was used to determine proposed cut-offs. For the total score, the proposed cut-off was 27.5 (AUC = 0.881, 95% CI: 0.847-0.915), with sensitivity 89.6% and specificity 77.8%. Adjusted for population prevalence, positive and negative predictive values were 21.6% and 99.1%. For inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity subscales, proposed cut-offs were 19.5 (AUC = 0.846) and 17.5 (AUC = 0.853), respectively. The ASRS-R demonstrates satisfactory screening efficacy for Chinese children and adolescents aged 8-14 years. These preliminary cut-offs, characterized by exceptional ability to rule out non-ADHD cases, provide evidence-based support for early ADHD screening in school, community, and clinical settings. However, these cut-offs require external validation, ideally in consecutively recruited and community-based samples.

items.title: School-based prevention of anabolic-androgenic steroid use: mapping the evidence from adolescent prevention programs.
items.abstract: Adolescents are vulnerable to sociocultural influences related to body image and appearance, which may increase the risk of anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) and other image- and performance-enhancing drug (IPED) use and subsequent adverse health outcomes. School-based prevention initiatives targeting AAS use and its associated health risks may prevent the initiation and use of these substances among adolescents by educating them about the dangers, adverse effects, and risks of AAS use while promoting healthier choices. This scoping review aimed to map the characteristics, intervention components, and reported outcomes of school-based prevention programs targeting AAS and other IPED use among adolescents. Peer-reviewed English-language studies evaluating school-based prevention programs addressing AAS and IPEDs among adolescents were included. Searches were conducted through Scopus, Embase (Elsevier), CINAHL (EBSCOhost), Web of Science, ProQuest, MEDLINE (Ovid), and PsycINFO, covering all eligible records published up to September 2025. Data were charted to map study characteristics, intervention types and delivery features, populations, and outcome domains assessed, with findings synthesised descriptively in line with scoping review methodology. Seventeen studies were included. Interventions mostly involved classroom-based education (70.6%) and sport- or exercise-integrated components (52.9%). Outcomes were predominantly evaluated by study-specific questionnaires (58.8%). Most studies examined knowledge, attitudes, intentions, and psychosocial outcomes, whereas fewer studies assessed behavioural outcomes, particularly actual AAS use (≤ 20%). Considerable variation was identified in intervention content, outcome measures, and follow-up periods. The available literature is heterogeneous and primarily focuses on knowledge, attitudinal, intentional, and psychosocial outcomes rather than behavioural outcomes. Future research should include more consistent outcome measures, longer follow-up periods, and greater attention to behavioural outcomes and psychosocial determinants of AAS and IPED use.

items.title: Assessing physical activity using Fitbit trackers and the association with quality of life among newly diagnosed patients with hematologic cancer.
items.abstract: We investigated associations between real-world activity data based on daily steps and heart rate, measured by wearable activity trackers, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in newly diagnosed patients with hematologic cancers. In this observational cohort study, 314 patients completed HRQoL questionnaires at diagnosis, 3, 6, and 12 months. Of these, 130 patients wore Fitbit Inspire HR trackers. HRQoL was measured using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and disease-specific modules. Mixed models assessed associations between daily steps (physical activity), heart rate (general fitness/health status) and HRQoL over time. Outcomes were presented based on quartiles of daily steps. The median number of daily steps per quartile at diagnosis was approximately 3,000, 6,000, 8,000 and 11,000, respectively. Patients in the first quartile were older, more likely to be male, overweight, current smokers, report ≥2 comorbidities and/or have multiple myeloma diagnosis, and less likely to have higher education or income, compared to the fourth quartile. Clinically relevant better HRQoL increased with step count, but plateaued at high activity (±8,000 steps/day). Higher heart rate was associated with greater symptom burden. For every 1,000 additional steps per day, physical (β=1.0 p<0.001) and role (β=1.1 p=0.03) functioning, global health status/QoL (β=1.0 p<0.001), fatigue (β=-0.9 p=0.03) and dyspnea (β=-1.1 p=0.01) improved significantly. Physical activity and general fitness/health status at diagnosis may be important predictors of maintaining HRQoL in the first year after diagnosis. These findings underscore the potential of wearable technology to inform supportive care and empower self-management. Even small increases in daily steps may contribute to maintaining HRQoL after diagnosis.

items.title: Performance psychology workshops for surgical trainees: A prospective pilot study on anxiety and mental toughness.
items.abstract: Background Performance anxiety and resilience are critical determinants of surgical trainee performance. Aims To evaluate the feasibility and preliminary impact of a brief performance psychology intervention, combining individual self-regulation with team-based performance strategies, on performance anxiety and mental toughness in surgical trainees. Methods In a prospective single-arm pilot and feasibility study in a university teaching hospital, nine surgical trainees from various subspecialities enrolled, with eight completing follow-up assessments. The intervention comprised two immersive workshops over two weeks, integrating individual and team-based psychological skills grounded in the biopsychosocial model of stress, challenge-threat appraisal, and high performance principles. Participants completed the Sport Anxiety Scale-2 and the Mental Toughness Evaluation Questionnaire-2 (MTE-2) at baseline (T0), three weeks (T1), and three months (T2). Results Eight of nine trainees (89%) completed all follow-up assessments, and the programme was delivered as planned. Mental toughness (MTE-2) improved over time (p = 0.002), and a median improvement of 580 points (95% CI 200 to 880) was sustained at three months. Most marked improvement seen in pre-performance distraction control. Anxiety (SAS-2) showed a short-term reduction, clearest for the worry subscale, though returned to baseline at three months. Frequency of technique use did not correlate with outcomes. Conclusions This brief high-performance psychology intervention was feasible and acceptable and was associated with short-term reductions in performance anxiety and sustained improvements in mental toughness in surgical trainees. These findings support the feasibility of integrating time-efficient psychological training in surgical education. Larger, controlled studies are required to confirm efficacy and mechanisms.

items.title: Boundaries and Bridges: The Complex Alliance Between Counselling and Learning Theories.
items.abstract: Counselling theories have traditionally been conceptualised within psychological, therapeutic, and developmental frameworks while learning theories have largely evolved as a separate field of inquiry. Although both domains are concerned with personal change, adaptation, and the development of new understandings, explicit theoretical integration between counselling and learning remains relatively limited. This article explores whether counselling may be usefully understood through the lens of learning theory and examines the extent to which key learning concepts can illuminate processes commonly associated with counselling. Drawing on major traditions in learning theory, including behaviourist, cognitive, constructivist, social, experiential, transformative, and humanistic perspectives, the paper develops a conceptual framework for analysing counselling as a context in which intensive personal learning frequently occurs. Rather than proposing an equivalence between counselling and learning, the analysis identifies significant areas of conceptual overlap and highlights how counselling may facilitate changes in knowledge, self-understanding, behaviour, meaning making, and identity. Attention is given to the roles of reflection, experience, dialogue, agency, and relational processes in supporting learning-oriented forms of personal development. The article concludes that a learning perspective offers a valuable complementary lens for understanding counselling processes and provides a basis for strengthening interdisciplinary dialogue between counselling theory and learning theory. Implications for theory development, research, and professional practice are discussed, alongside the limitations of the present conceptual analysis.

items.title: Emotion regulation difficulties are selectively associated with executive and behavioural apathy in Huntington's disease.
items.abstract: Objective Apathy occurs frequently in psychiatric and neurological disorders and is associated with functional impairment, reduced quality of life, and caregiver burden. Its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood, but recent studies indicate that apathy is multidimensional and has heterogeneous manifestations across disorders. Self-regulatory processes, such as emotion regulation, may contribute to these manifestations, but this relationship has received little attention. Huntington's disease (HD) provides a clinical model for examining whether emotion regulation difficulties are associated with global and multidimensional apathy. Methods Eighty-nine HD gene expansion carriers (HDGECs) completed the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale, Lille Apathy Rating Scale, and Dimensional Apathy Scale. Cognitive screening included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Hierarchical regressions examined associations between emotion regulation difficulties and apathy, adjusting for depressive symptoms. Results Greater emotion regulation difficulties were associated with global, Executive, and Behaviour/Initiation apathy, but not Emotional apathy. After accounting for depressive symptoms, Executive and Behaviour/Initiation apathy explained an additional 24.2% of variance in emotion regulation difficulties, whereas global apathy explained an additional 5.8%. Exploratory subgroup analyses found an independent association between Executive apathy and emotion regulation difficulties in premanifest but not manifest HDGECs. Conclusions Emotion regulation difficulties were associated with global apathy and showed the strongest associations with Executive and Behaviour/Initiation apathy, independent of depressive symptoms. These findings suggest that self-regulatory processes may be relevant to the heterogeneous manifestations of apathy and highlight the importance of examining specific apathy dimensions when investigating its underlying mechanisms and informing potential treatment approaches.

items.title: Developing a Measure of the Double-Edged Health-Related Consequences of Lottery Participation (DEHC-LP) Among Chinese Lottery Participants and Examining Their Psychological Correlates: The Roles of Lottery Beliefs and Passion.
items.abstract: Lottery participation may be associated with both beneficial and detrimental consequences relevant to individuals' health, well-being, and daily functioning, reflecting a double-edged phenomenon. Understanding the psychological factors associated with these divergent consequences is important for promoting responsible lottery participation. This study developed the Double-Edged Health-Related Consequences of Lottery Participation scale (DEHC-LP) and examined how lottery beliefs and passion were associated with these consequences among legal lottery participants in mainland China. Two independent samples comprising 588 lottery players were used for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, followed by a third sample of 918 lottery players who completed measures of luck beliefs, strategy beliefs, lottery passion, and the DEHC-LP. Results supported a two-factor second-order structure comprising lottery-related benefits and harms, with satisfactory reliability and validity. Structural equation modeling indicated that luck beliefs were indirectly associated with lottery-related benefits through harmonious passion. Strategy beliefs showed a more complex pattern: they were indirectly associated with lottery-related benefits through harmonious passion and were associated with both lottery-related harms and benefits through obsessive passion. These findings suggest that lottery participation should not be evaluated solely from a risk perspective, as psychological factors such as lottery beliefs and passion may be associated with divergent health-related consequences. The DEHC-LP provides a multidimensional measure of participants' perceived lottery-related consequences across domains relevant to health, well-being, and daily functioning. The findings underscore the importance of considering individuals' beliefs and passion when developing responsible lottery participation initiatives aimed at enhancing potential benefits while reducing harms.

items.title: An updated conceptual framework on physical performance and training in soccer: a narrative review.
items.abstract: Soccer practitioners routinely use external load (EL), internal load (IL) and fitness measures to monitor players; however, the same monitoring variable may be interpreted as training load (TL), performance, or athlete capacity depending on its purpose and reference. The conceptual problem addressed in this review is therefore not the absence of definitions for EL, IL, or fitness status, but rather the lack of an integrated interpretative structure explaining how these established constructs should be differentiated when evaluating soccer physical performance. This conceptually focused narrative review therefore aims to clarify the distinction between TL, physical performance output, physiological response, and athlete fitness capacity, and to integrate these established concepts within an interpretative framework for soccer training and monitoring. The framework does not propose match demands, physiological responses, or fitness status as replacements for the established concepts of EL, IL, and fitness. Rather, it organizes their interpretation according to three related questions: what external output did the athlete produce, what physiological response accompanied that output, and what does the relationship between output and response indicate about the athlete's capacity to perform?. By separating the purpose for which monitoring variables are interpreted, the framework aims to support practitioners in selecting appropriate measures and aligning training prescription with either physiological adaptation targets or the external performance demands that players are required to reproduce in competition.

items.title: Episodic memory in immersive virtual reality environments: the role of affective context and navigation control.
items.abstract: Memory in immersive virtual reality (VR) may depend on the encoding context and on users' control over virtual exploration. We examined memory for a single immersive episode in 234 young adults using a 2 × 3 between-subjects design crossing navigation control (self-directed vs. automated movement) with affective audiovisual context (pleasant, unpleasant, neutral). Memory was assessed through free recall, visual-feature memory, spatial-location memory, and complementary error indices. One effect held up under Holm correction across the three non-derived memory-performance outcomes. Free recall differed across affective contexts, F(2, 228) = 4.75, p = .010, ω² = 0.031, Holm-adjusted p = .030, with lower recall in the unpleasant than in the neutral condition, and the difference remained evident after adjustment for age, gender, and prior VR experience. Navigation control showed no robust general association with the principal memory-performance outcomes. A localized navigation-control × affective-context pattern emerged for spatial false object reports (raw p = .032), but the interaction did not survive correction across the corresponding family of memory-error tests (Holm-adjusted p = .192) and is treated as exploratory. The unpleasant-neutral contrast cannot be attributed uniquely to emotional valence, because the neutral condition lacked the concurrent audiovisual stream present in the affective conditions and may therefore differ in attentional or other stimulus properties. The results yield one multiplicity-robust performance effect and a set of exploratory error patterns; together they argue for tighter control of audiovisual and attentional features in immersive-memory research.

items.title: Ketamine Beyond Anaesthesia: Analgesic, Psychiatric, Antitumour, and Immunomodulatory Actions and Their Signalling Mechanisms.
items.abstract: To synthesize current evidence on ketamine for cancer-related pain and its intersecting psychiatric, anti-tumor, and immunomodulatory actions, emphasizing mechanisms, clinical relevance, and uncertainties relevant to oncology. Ketamine provides analgesia primarily through non-competitive antagonism of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and additional effects on excitatory, inhibitory, and opioid-related signaling. In patients with refractory cancer pain, it may be a useful adjunct to opioid-based multimodal analgesia and may reduce opioid requirements; however, clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Its rapid antidepressant effects may be relevant to the reciprocal burden of pain and depressive symptoms in cancer. Preclinical studies report antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, and ferroptosis-associated effects across several tumor models, involving phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin, extracellular signal-regulated kinase, and non-coding RNA-associated pathways. These findings are not uniform: breast cancer models have suggested potentially pro-metastatic effects. Immune effects are likewise dose-, context-, and perioperative-setting dependent, with reports of anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, and neutral effects. Ketamine is a potentially valuable opioid-sparing adjunct for selected patients with cancer-related pain and may also address comorbid depressive symptoms. Its putative direct anti-tumor and immunomodulatory actions remain predominantly preclinical and context dependent and should not currently guide oncologic treatment decisions. Appropriately powered clinical studies should define patient selection, dose and route, duration, safety, immune consequences, and long-term oncologic outcomes.

items.title: Clinical cutoffs for plasma biomarkers to identify intracranial pathology in traumatic brain injury patients with Glasgow Coma Scale scores 13 to 15: a TRACK-TBI study.
items.abstract: Objective The authors sought to identify plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase-L1 (UCH-L1) cutoffs corresponding to a range of high positive predictive values (PPVs) for detecting intracranial pathology on CT and detecting pathology on MRI (when CT is negative) in patients who present to a level I trauma center for TBI evaluation with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores of 13-15. Methods This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data from the Transforming Research and Clinical Knowledge in Traumatic Brain Injury (TRACK-TBI) study, which is a longitudinal, observational study of patients with TBI who presented to one of 18 US level I trauma centers within 24 hours of injury. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours. Plasma samples were analyzed for GFAP (pg/mL) and UCH-L1 (pg/mL). The CT or MRI scan was considered positive (CT+, MRI+) if there was evidence of acute intracranial pathology related to TBI. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis (AUC) was performed to evaluate the ability of day-1 GFAP and UCH-L1 to discriminate CT+ versus CT-, and CT-/MRI+ versus CT-/MRI-. A K-fold cross-validation procedure was used to identify GFAP cutoffs for predicting CT+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and for predicting MRI+ among patients with GCS scores of 13-15 and CT- subjects, based on the adjusted PPV thresholds. Results Among the 1718 TBI participants with GCS scores 13-15, 633 (37%) had CT+ findings. Of the 1085 CT- participants, 608 underwent MRI at 2 weeks postinjury, of whom 154 (25%) had MRI+ findings. Day-1 GFAP had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 (95% CI 0.80-0.84), and UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.57-0.63) for discriminating CT+ from CT-. Day-1 GFAP had an AUC of 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) while UCH-L1 had an AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.55-0.65) for discriminating CT-/MRI+ from CT-/MRI-. For CT+ prediction, assuming a prevalence of 0.36 (from our data) and 0.1 (from the literature), the median GFAP cutoffs to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 were 2879 (95% CI 2195-4704) and 5191 (95% CI 3779-5426), respectively. For MRI+ prediction among GCS 13-15 CT- patients, the median GFAP cutoffs were 1382 (95% CI 1145-2424) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.9 and 2317 pg/mL (95% CI 1262-2551 pg/mL) to achieve an adjusted PPV of 0.98. Conclusions These threshold values can be used as an aid-in-diagnosis tool and assist in appropriate triaging of patients who have sustained TBI to urgent neuroimaging, potential escalation in care, and interventions as clinically indicated.

items.title: Open Surgery in the Robotic Era: National Trends and Training Implications from Two Decades of American Board of Urology Case Logs.
items.abstract: Purpose Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) has rapidly transformed the surgical management of urologic diseases, with robotic-assisted techniques increasingly replacing open approaches (OA). We aimed to characterize trends in OA versus MIS across major urologic oncologic procedures and evaluate surgeon-specific factors associated with surgical approach. Material and methods Operative logs from American Board of Urology examinees from 2000-2023 were examined for radical nephrectomy (RN), partial nephrectomy (PN), radical nephroureterectomy (RNU), radical prostatectomy (RP), and radical adrenalectomy (RA) and categorized by surgical approach. Approach proportions were assessed over time and stratified by individual procedure, surgeon gender, geographic region, certification status, and fellowship training. Results A total of 54,972 procedures were analyzed, of which 23% were OA and 77% were MIS. While surgical volume increased more than tenfold from 2003-2005 to 2021-2023, the proportion of OA declined from 75% to 9.9%. Declines in OA were observed across all procedures. Surgeon factors including age, sex, and fellowship training were associated with OA. Regional variation in the United States was identified, with the Southeast demonstrating the highest proportion of OA. Conclusions Open surgery in urologic oncology has declined dramatically over the past two decades and now represents a minority of cases. While this transition reflects advances in surgical technology and patient care, it raises important concerns regarding declining exposure to OA during training. As robotic surgery continues to dominate contemporary practice, targeted efforts may be necessary to ensure adequate training and competency in open surgical techniques.
