items.title: Impact of a Simulation-Based Training Program on Cup Detachment During Vacuum-Assisted Vaginal Birth: Protocol for a Multicenter Quasi-Experimental Before-and-After Study.
items.abstract: Safe vacuum-assisted vaginal birth depends on appropriate case selection, accurate cup placement, controlled traction, recognition of technical difficulty, and timely abandonment of an unsuccessful attempt. Simulation-based education can improve procedural performance, but evidence that vacuum-specific simulation changes patient-level clinical practice remains limited. This study aims to estimate the change in the occurrence of cup detachment (known as "pop off") following implementation of a standardized simulation-based training program for vacuum-assisted vaginal birth. Cup detachment was designated as the single primary outcome after evaluation of the preintervention cohort but before any postintervention versus preintervention comparative analysis. This multicenter quasi-experimental before-and-after study is being conducted in 19 Spanish maternity hospitals participating in the Registro Español de Morbimortalidad Materna y Perinatal. The implemented preintervention observation period ran from November 28, 2024, through February 28, 2026. The training and washout phase was conducted during March and April 2026, followed by postintervention data collection from May through October 2026. Preintervention clinical variables are ascertained retrospectively from medical records, whereas postintervention data collection is prospective. The intervention combines preparatory theoretical material, a 1-hour face-to-face simulation workshop using a PROMPT FLEX obstetric simulator and vacuum devices, checklist-based assessment, supervised practice, feedback, and debriefing. The primary outcome will be analyzed using modified Poisson regression to estimate risk ratios and 95% CIs, accounting for hospital and protocol-defined calendar time trends. Sequential instrumentation and conversion to cesarean birth will be analyzed separately as key secondary clinical outcomes. Ethical approval was granted by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee of Girona (code 2024.070) on August 5, 2024. This study was funded in November 2024. During the preintervention phase, 1155 cases were recorded in 19 hospitals; 12 were excluded according to the selection criteria, leaving 1143 eligible cases. At the verified July 2026 project update, 144 postintervention cases had been collected. Postintervention data collection is scheduled to close in October 2026; the protocol-defined comparative analysis will be performed after database lock, with publication of the main results planned for summer 2027. The current analysis plan was fixed before database lock and before any formal comparative postintervention versus preintervention effectiveness analysis. The protocol also defines assessment of contamination, intervention fidelity, secular trends, and the limitations inherent to a nonrandomized before-and-after evaluation.

items.title: Digital Archiving of Direct-to-Consumer Marketing Claims Made by Businesses Selling Unproven Stem Cell Interventions.
items.abstract: Over the last 2 decades, a large global marketplace has emerged in which businesses use direct-to-consumer advertising to sell putative stem cell treatments that are unsupported by convincing scientific evidence of safety and efficacy. It is common for such purported stem cell therapies not to have been reviewed and approved by national regulatory authorities, even though they are supposed to undergo rigorous premarketing review by regulatory bodies responsible for evaluating such medical products and determining whether they are backed by sufficient evidence to warrant approval. The marketing claims, commercial activities, and clinical practices of such businesses have resulted in patients experiencing serious harms, including loss of life, physical injuries, financial losses, and avoidable delays in accessing evidence-based treatments. Such businesses are also responsible for collective harms, including diverting patients from participating in legitimate stem cell clinical studies, damaging the field of credible stem cell research, and contributing to public confusion and misunderstandings about how to distinguish evidence-based stem cell therapies from stem cell interventions that are not backed by robust data. Researchers in bioethics, health law, the social sciences, and other academic fields have made important contributions to the critical analysis of direct-to-consumer digital marketing claims made by businesses selling unproven and unapproved stem cell interventions. Scholars studying such marketing representations have documented the use of persuasive "tokens of legitimacy" to make advertised stem cell interventions seem credible, trustworthy, and backed by current scientific evidence. Acknowledging the value of such scholarship, there is a growing need for the development of best practices in research methods and data-archiving practices. In particular, there is a need for increased digital archiving of online marketing claims made by businesses selling supposed stem cell treatments. Numerous parties can benefit from increased digital archiving of such problematic marketing representations. However, analyzing, archiving, and critiquing the marketing claims, business operations, and clinical practices of such businesses must be done in a careful, rigorous, and evidence-based manner that is attentive to the intimidating tactics some of these businesses use when responding to public criticism. Researchers need to document the marketing representations made by businesses selling unapproved and unproven stem cell interventions in ways that minimize exposure to legal threats and other efforts to suppress critical analysis. Using the Wayback Machine or other comparable archiving tools to create digital repositories of such marketing representations is one way to mitigate such threats, by capturing the exact claims such businesses make when promoting putative stem cell therapies. Archiving such digital marketing representations is important for academic research and can play a valuable role in other contexts, such as in legal actions taken against businesses using purportedly deceptive marketing claims to sell unproven and unapproved stem cell-based interventions.

items.title: Word Retrieval in the Wild: The Feasibility of an Audio-Based Ecological Momentary Naming Protocol Completed by Adults With and Without Poststroke Aphasia.
items.abstract: Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) involves collecting data regarding behaviors or states of interest repeatedly in individuals' natural environments, typically from a smart device. The feasibility of EMA protocols with people with aphasia (PWA) remains relatively unexplored, particularly for objective assessments of language ability. We assessed the feasibility of a novel, smartwatch-delivered, audio-based ecological momentary naming protocol. Fourteen PWA and 13 healthy controls completed a 3-week EMA protocol in which they attempted to name pictured objects delivered via smartwatch prompts while going about daily routines. Participants were pseudorandomly assigned to either a single-item (36 prompts per day, one image each) or nine-item (four prompts per day, nine images each) condition. Feasibility metrics were compliance (number of naming attempts/number of scheduled prompts), completion (number of naming attempts/number of delivered prompts), and perceived ease and burden of completing EMAs (captured via weekly surveys). Average compliance for both PWA and controls was 77%, with completion at 83% and 84% for controls and PWA, respectively. Participants in the one-item condition trended toward higher compliance (at 83.3%) than individuals in the nine-item condition (at 71.9%). Perceptions of EMA ease and burden did not change over time or vary by group or EMA condition. Higher compliance was associated with temporal variables (day of protocol, time of day, day of week), older age, and better inhibitory control. Higher completion was associated with being unemployed and higher perceived burden. Qualitative analysis of exit interviews indicated that 89% of participants had a generally positive impression of the protocol. This novel EMA was feasible for adults with and without aphasia. Although EMA research with PWA is still in its infancy, mobile health methodologies provide several promising avenues for improving the accuracy of long-term, in situ surveillance of aphasia symptoms.

items.title: Developing a Health App Quality Report for CEN-ISO/TS 82304-2 to Satisfy Health Care Professionals' Information Needs on the Quality of Health Apps: Participatory Design Study.
items.abstract: Health apps, which comprise medical and wellness apps, hold potential to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and management of disease. Yet, recommendation and prescription rates by health care professionals (HCPs) are low. Trusted standardized health app quality reports providing the information HCPs need to recommend or prescribe a specific app for an individual patient and guidelines from medical societies are considered crucial to enable this digital transformation of medicine. The CEN-ISO 82304-2 (hereinafter "82304-2") Technical Specification, an initiative of the European Commission, includes a research-based health app quality assessment framework comprising 81 quality requirements. Results of 82304-2 app assessments are summarized in an intuitive "health app quality label." The 82304-2 quality label's potential to increase HCP willingness to recommend health apps was recently confirmed. To adequately enable decision-making and thus app recommendations, 82304-2 proposes a more detailed "health app quality report" to complement the 82304-2 quality label. This study aimed to design the 82304-2 health app quality report that satisfies the information needs of individual HCPs in decision-making on an individual health app for an individual patient. A participatory design approach was applied. In an 18-month process of participatory prototyping with 9 HCPs with digital health expertise, the 82304-2 quality report was iteratively designed. A convenience sample of 31 HCPs indicated the priority 82304-2 quality requirements they considered useful in decision-making on recommending an app, and thus needed detailed quality information. Final feedback meetings with the 9 HCPs and 8 medical societies were used to finalize the 82304-2 quality report design. Web-based questions in these meetings, feedback from the Dutch Patient Federation, and a comparative content analysis and the Health Education Materials Assessment Tool were used to evolve to and evaluate the final 82304-2 quality report design. In total, 37% (30/81) of the 82304-2 quality requirements were prioritized by >50% of the HCPs. The final 82304-2 quality report design provides detailed information for 90% (27/30) of the prioritized quality requirements. The reporting detail for 2 quality requirements requires more research. The final feedback meetings, the Patient Federation feedback, comparative content analysis, and Health Education Materials Assessment Tool provide indicative proof of the usefulness and usability of the quality report design. We succeeded in our aim to design the 82304-2 health app quality report and found promising potential for its distinctive usefulness for HCPs and patients in recommending and considering a health app, respectively, and for medical societies in creating guidance. Further efforts are needed to test its effectiveness, fine-tune multistakeholder and intercontinental usefulness and usability, support medical societies in providing guidance and potentially training on recommending health apps, and advance from the current design to a scalable fully functional version of the quality report and associated open access database.

items.title: Balancing protection and progress: is New Zealand's ethical review framework appropriate for low-risk research?
items.abstract: Clinical audits, observational studies and patient registries are essential for evaluating healthcare quality, identifying inequities and improving patient outcomes. New Zealand's ethics system plays an essential role in protecting participants and maintaining public trust and includes pathways for expedited review of low-risk research. However, New Zealand already has proportionate review mechanisms. The difficulty is that, in practice, studies requiring temporary access to identifiable information often receive the same level of scrutiny regardless of their actual participant risk, creating barriers that can prevent valuable studies from proceeding. The cost of these barriers is overlooked. When low-risk research is delayed or abandoned, opportunities to improve care are lost. Important questions affecting Māori and Pacific communities may remain unanswered, inequities may persist and New Zealand risks contributing less to international research efforts. The burden also falls on clinicians, particularly early-career doctors, who may become discouraged from undertaking research altogether. We argue that more consistent application of existing principles of proportionate review would maintain appropriate ethical oversight while supporting a health system that learns from everyday practice and continually improves care for all New Zealanders.

items.title: Health complexity, metabolic health and service use in a high need primary care population in Aotearoa New Zealand: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to understand the characteristics, health complexity and intensity of service provision for patients aged 16 years or older enrolled in a high-need practice. This cross-sectional study used routinely collected data from an urban Very Low Cost Access practice serving a high-need population in Cannons Creek, Porirua, Aotearoa New Zealand. All patients aged ≥16 years enrolled for a 12-month period were included. Demographic, clinical, biological, medication and service use variables were extracted, and individuals were categorised into normoglycaemia, prediabetes and diabetes groups. Analyses used descriptive statistics, age-standardised rates and comparative assessments of health complexity and service utilisation. The population (n=4,715) was predominantly Pacific, with most living in areas of high socio-economic deprivation and 25% classified with prediabetes or diabetes. Younger adults with diabetes had disproportionately high HbA1c and elevated albuminuria. Long-term conditions (LTCs), particularly obesity-related conditions, increased progressively across the glycaemic spectrum, with twofold to fourfold higher rates in dysglycaemia. Prediabetes and diabetes groups had similar LTC profiles. Service use increased with worsening dysglycaemia, with individuals with diabetes having nearly double the consultation rates, triple the prescription counts and markedly higher emergency department and ambulatory sensitive hospitalisation rates. Dysglycaemia and multiple LTCs are common and resource-intensive in this population. Together, these data highlight the urgent need for proactive, well-resourced, equity-focussed primary care models to address metabolic risk, LTCs and high service demand.

items.title: Epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of a large-scale upsurge of dengue in the rohingya refugee camps and host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, 2021 to 2024: A retrospective study.
items.abstract: Dengue emerged as a new public health threat in the Rohingya refugee camps in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, in 2021 and expanded into large-scale upsurges in subsequent years. Evidence on dengue epidemiology and clinical presentation in protracted refugee settings remains limited, despite the need for stronger outbreak preparedness and case management in these contexts. To describe the epidemiological, clinical, and diagnostic characteristics of the dengue upsurge among Rohingya refugees and surrounding host communities in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, and to identify predictors of inpatient admission and diagnostic positivity patterns. This retrospective observational study used anonymized surveillance data from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) dengue patient database. Rapid diagnostic test (RDT)-confirmed dengue cases identified across 36 IOM-supported health facilities in Ukhiya and Teknaf between 1 October 2021 and 31 December 2024 were included. Demographic, epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory variables were summarized using descriptive statistics. Weekly case counts were aggregated by epidemiological week and calendar year, and epidemic growth and decay phases were modelled using phase-specific Poisson regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with inpatient admission, while separate models examined associations between delay in presentation and RDT positivity patterns, adjusting for age and sex. A total of 35,581 RDT-confirmed dengue cases were reported, of which 90.2% occurred among Rohingya refugees. The median age was 17 years (IQR 7-30), and 46.0% of cases were among children aged 0-14 years. Annual caseload increased from 1,011 in 2021-11,752 in 2022, 10,669 in 2023 and 12,149 in 2024, with seasonal peaks during the monsoon period and progressively later peaks and longer epidemic tails over time. Poisson models showed decreasing growth rates across years (r = 0.449 in 2021 to r = 0.091 in 2024) with increasing doubling times, while decay rates remained broadly comparable (halving time ~4.4-6.0 weeks). Overall, 8.0% of cases required inpatient admission, 1.3% were referred, and four deaths were reported (case fatality <0.1%). In multivariable analysis, inpatient admission was associated with older age (≥60 vs 0-14: aOR 2.48), delayed presentation (aOR 1.06 per day), refugee status (aOR 1.43), fever ≥38°C at presentation (aOR 1.13), presence of any WHO warning sign (aOR 28.87), and chronic co-morbidity (aOR 6.63). Males had lower odds of admission than females (aOR 0.87). Sustained dengue preparedness is required in Cox's Bazar, including strengthened surveillance, community-based early referral, targeted monitoring of high-risk groups, environmental vector control, and phase-appropriate use of NS1 and IgM/IgG diagnostics to reduce missed diagnoses and prevent progression to severe disease. These findings highlight the need for a policy shift from episodic outbreak response toward sustained dengue preparedness in humanitarian settings, including strengthened surveillance systems, integrated diagnostic strategies, community-based early referral, and coordinated vector control interventions.

items.title: Temporal Patterns of Multimorbidity Progression Among Inpatients With a Recorded Hypertension Diagnosis Across Three Counties in Rural Henan, China: Retrospective Cohort Study Using Temporal Network Analysis.
items.abstract: Hypertension is a key driver of multimorbidity; however, its role in shaping dynamic disease progression, especially in rural populations, remains underexplored. This study aimed to characterize temporal patterns of multimorbidity progression among inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis and to examine whether these patterns differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. We analyzed electronic health record data from 34,099 inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis across 3 rural counties in Henan, China (2019-2023), constructing a temporal comorbidity network of 250 disease nodes and 1512 disease transitions. Statistical validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, case-dropping, and permutation tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, insurance type, and county. The temporal comorbidity network revealed a densely interconnected core involving hypertension, atherosclerotic heart disease, and cerebral infarction, with type 2 diabetes occupying a bridging position between cardiovascular and multisystem disease clusters. The ordering of dominant recorded pathways differed by sex (earlier coronary involvement among female inpatients vs more direct progression to stroke among male inpatients), was more complex in inpatients older than 70 years of age, and was more diffuse among those covered by urban-rural resident insurance compared with urban employee insurance. Multimorbidity among inpatients with recorded hypertension followed structured and heterogeneous temporal patterns that differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions formed the principal recorded progression pathways, while type 2 diabetes connected cardiovascular pathways with broader multisystem complications. These findings support further evaluation of risk-stratified and locally adapted approaches to chronic disease prevention and longitudinal care.

items.title: Schistosomiasis as an urban disease: 13 years of studies in the neighborhoods of Salvador, BA, Brazil.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization in Brazil has shifted the epidemiological landscape of parasitic diseases, such as schistosomiasis and malaria. Although typically considered a rural infection, Schistosoma mansoni transmission persists in urban settings where sanitation and water access remain uneven. This study investigates the persistence and dynamics of urban schistosomiasis across neighborhoods of Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. Between 2011 and 2024 cross-sectional surveys were conducted to identify neighborhoods with the highest prevalence in the major metropolitan area of Salvador, Bahia. A total of 6,863 residents provided demographic information and Kato-Katz examination of at least one stool sample. We conducted demographic surveys and stool examination on 3,964 individuals who were re-examined on up to three occasions at intervals ranging from 1-5 years. The overall prevalence of initial examination was 7%. Regardless of treatment intervals, the community-wide prevalence declined by more than half and did not rebound. Apparent Incidence decreased to <0.5%/year following a second period of treatment. In nearly all communities, most infections occurred among individuals born in Salvador with no travel history outside the city. Overall, the study provides one of the first individual-level longitudinal assessments of schistosomiasis persistence in an urban Brazilian setting, combining repeated parasitological surveys with demographic and environmental data across multiple neighborhoods. These findings indicate that schistosomiasis transmission in Salvador is largely local rather than imported. The decline in prevalence coincides with observed community-level improvements in sanitation and reduced contact with surface water. f prevalence rates were applied across the population of Salvador, this city could be considered one of the state's most important endemic areas.

items.title: Precancerous cervical lesions and associated factors among HIV-positive women in Southern and Eastern African countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) face a sixfold increased risk of cervical cancer compared to HIV-negative women. Most WLHIV residing in the Southern and Eastern African regions have a substantial HIV-related cervical cancer burden. Studies on precancerous cervical lesions (PCCL) and associated factors in WLHIV from these regions have inconsistent and inconclusive findings. Therefore, we aimed to synthesize the pooled prevalence of PCCL and associated factors among WLHIV in Southern and Eastern Africa. This study was registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251123583) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 standards. Primary studies published from inception to 2025 in Southern and Eastern Africa were included. The methodological quality of studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Data extraction and statistical analyses were done in Microsoft Excel and STATA 17, respectively. Pooled prevalence, publication bias, subgroup, and sensitivity analysis were conducted. Associations were expressed as odds ratios (OR), and a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. 44 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a sample size of 47,009. The pooled prevalence of PCCL was 22.25% (95% CI: 19.57, 24.93). Age at first sexual intercourse (< 18 years) (OR = 2.99, (2.34, 3.82)), multiparity (OR = 4.97, (3.21, 7.69)), having multiple sexual partners (OR = 3.06 (2.45, 3.83)), having a history of sexually transmitted infections (STI) (OR = 3.93 (3.23, 4.78)), smoking (OR = 7.01, (3.39, 14.49)), ever taking oral contraceptive pills (OR = 2.69, (1.85, 3.90)), low CD4 count (OR = 1.79, (1.56, 2.05)), and having not initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) (OR = 2.02, (1.56, 2.62)) were significantly associated with an increased risk of PCCL. The pooled prevalence of PCCL was high. Additionally, early first sexual intercourse, parity, STIs, multiple sexual partners, smoking, oral contraceptive use, CD4 count, and ART were positively associated with the occurrence of PCCL. Therefore, stakeholders shall implement interventions to avert future incidents of PCCL and address the identified factors.

items.title: Common mental health problems experienced by adolescents living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
items.abstract: Adolescents living with HIV (ALWH) carry a substantial burden of mental health problems, yet summary data remain limited. Previous reviews, particularly systematic reviews, have focused mainly on diagnosed disorders among adults or broader populations of young people living with HIV, while substance use and emotional and behavioural symptoms remain understudied and often underreported. This scoping review synthesized existing evidence on common mental health problems among ALWH aged 10-19 years in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). We searched five electronic databases (PubMed, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Embase, and Open Access for Africa) and Google Scholar, and screened the bibliographic references of selected articles for additional studies. Search terms were combined using Boolean operators and organized into four concept categories: HIV, age, mental health, and region. Eligible studies were original, peer-reviewed research published in English between 2020 and 2026, conducted in SSA, and reporting on mental health among ALWH aged 10-19 years. The search yielded 427 records, of which 29 duplicates were removed. Of the 398 articles screened, 317 were excluded at the abstract stage and a further 57 after full-text review, leaving 24 articles for inclusion. The review identified six common mental health problems among ALWH in SSA: depressive disorders and symptoms, generalized anxiety, suicidality, emotional and behavioural problems, posttraumatic stress, and substance use problems. Depression and suicidality were the most frequently reported, whereas substance use, generalized anxiety, posttraumatic stress, and emotional and behavioural problems were less frequently reported. ALWH in SSA experience a range of mental health problems that may affect their well-being and engagement in HIV care. Routine mental health screening, prevention, and psychosocial support should be integrated into HIV care for this population. Strengthening integrated mental health and HIV services may help address unmet needs and improve health outcomes among ALWH in SSA.

items.title: Gut virome remodeling after fecal microbiota transplantation is associated with virus-bacteria co-variation and metabolic response in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
items.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) modifies gut bacterial composition and improves metabolic outcomes in subjects with obesity and type 2 diabetes (ObT2), but bacterial changes alone do not fully explain the heterogeneity in clinical response. We performed virus-like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing coupled with bulk-DNA metagenomic sequencing on longitudinal fecal samples from a randomized controlled FMT trial in ObT2. Using random forest classification, post-FMT virome changes showed accuracy comparable to bacteriome changes (84.8% vs 81.4%) in distinguishing LDL responders from non-responders. Donor-derived viral contig engraftment was detected in 64.7% (11/17) of recipients receiving FMT alone and 58.8% (10/17) receiving FMT with lifestyle intervention (LSI), versus 5.6% (1/18) in the sham with LSI group. FMT was associated with increased virome diversity, compositional shifts toward the donor virome, and coordinated virus-bacteria associations, with most responsive viral contigs classified as Caudoviricetes. FMT-responsive viral contigs that were shared between the two FMT groups were predicted to infect Roseburia and Bifidobacterium, while contigs associated with clinical responses were predicted to infect Escherichia, Roseburia, Blautia, and Enterococcus. These findings suggest that the gut virome is a complementary ecological component associated with FMT responses and metabolic outcomes in ObT2.

items.title: Impact of a phased transition model on Advanced HIV Disease outcomes: A pre- and post-implementation evaluation study in Malawi.
items.abstract: To promote sustainability and strengthen national ownership of Advanced HIV Disease (AHD) services, a transition was implemented across 22 health facilities in Central Malawi. This transition involved shifting responsibility for key AHD program elements from partner-led implementation to full Ministry of Health (MoH) leadership. This evaluation assessed the impact of this transition on diagnostic coverage, TB preventive therapy (TPT) uptake, and 12-month survival outcomes. A retrospective cohort study included all children and adults enrolled in AHD care during the pre-MoH transition (January 2020-December 2021) and post-MoH transition (January 2023-December 2024) periods. Eligibility was defined by national AHD criteria: CD4 count <200 cells/mm³, WHO stage 3 or 4 disease, or age < 5 years. Data were abstracted from clinical records and routine facility registers. Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox proportional hazards, and Fine and Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate 6 and 12-month mortality and retention as primary outcomes. A total of 1,044 AHD clients were included (553 pre-transition; 491 post-transition). Median age increased post-transition (35.9 to 38.5 years, p < 0.001). CD4 testing uptake declined (80.7% to 46.0%, p < 0.001), while WHO staging and TB diagnostic coverage improved. TB diagnoses decreased (44.5% to 31.2%, p = 0.002). TPT uptake dropped from 46.4% to 31.6% (p < 0.001). Twelve-month mortality declined significantly from 9.4% to 5.5% (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.37-0.94, p = 0.026). Retention in care remained stable (HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.62-1.20, p = 0.384). Transitioning AHD services to MoH leadership was associated with sustained key program outcomes and a significant reduction in mortality. Continued mentorship and government ownership appeared to support these outcomes, although the pre-post design precludes causal inference. Declines in CD4 testing and TPT coverage highlight the need to strengthen diagnostics and integrate preventive care. These findings support scaling nationally led AHD models in high-burden HIV settings.

items.title: Abdominal circumference and its relationship with the incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024.
items.abstract: Background Hypotension is a common complication in pregnant mothers during cesarean section after spinal anesthesia. Identifying the association between abdominal circumference and the likelihood of developing hypotension following a cesarean delivery while under spinal anesthesia can facilitate preventing hypotension. Objectives This study aims to assess the relationship between the abdominal circumference of pregnant women and the occurrence of hypotension during cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024. Method A prospective observational study through a simple systematic random sampling technique was conducted on 360 pregnant mothers who underwent elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia from January 7, 2024, to March 30, 2024. Data was collected using a data collection questionnaire and checklist. The data was entered using Epi Info 7.2 and exported into SPSS 26. The Patients were categorized by their median abdominal circumference, Result Among 360 study subjects, the incidence of post-spinal hypotension was 76.67% with 95%CI [71.9-80.9]. items.title: The hidden burden of viral meningitis in ethiopia: Etiology and clinical outcomes.
items.abstract: Viral meningitis remains a significant global public health problem, particularly in resource-limited settings where the diagnosis of viral etiology is mainly based on clinical assessment. This study aimed to identify the common viral etiologies of meningitis, describe their associated clinical features, and assess patient outcomes among individuals suspected of meningitis without evidence of bacterial meningitis. We conducted a multicenter study involving 430 patients clinically suspected of meningitis. Clinical data and cerebrospinal fluid samples (CSF) were collected following standard procedures. Viral nucleic acids were extracted from CSF specimens. Complementary DNA was prepared from viral RNA using reverse transcription. Viral nucleic acids were amplified and detected using qualitative conventional polymerase chain reactions. Patient outcomes were evaluated using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS). Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with unfavorable patient outcomes, with statistical significance set at a p-value < 0.05 at a 95% confidence level. The prevalence of viral meningitis was 52.8% (227/430). Enteroviruses were the most common, 47.9% (206/430), followed by herpes simplex virus-1, 2.8% (12/430), herpes simplex virus-2, 1.4% (6/430), and Epstein-Barr virus, 0.7% (3/430). Overall, 6.7% (29/430) of study participants experienced unfavorable outcomes (GOS = 1-4). Factors independently associated with unfavorable outcomes included sex (AOR = 2.684, 95% CI = 1.177-6.119), duration from disease onset to hospital visit (AOR = 1.433, 95% CI = 1.043-1.967), and history of antibiotic intake before hospital visit (AOR = 2.784, 95% CI = 1.270-6.104). In this predominantly pediatric study, enteroviruses are the leading cause of viral meningitis in Ethiopia. Most study participants experienced favorable outcomes. Unfavorable outcomes were independently associated with sex, duration from disease onset to hospital visit, and history of antibiotic use before hospital visit. Further identification and characterization of Enteroviruses are warranted.

items.title: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk.
items.abstract: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.

items.title: The science of child and adolescent mental health in Mozambique: A systematic review of prevalence estimates, measurement tools, and interventions.
items.abstract: Mozambique is home to 18 million children and adolescents largely underrepresented in mental health research. We conducted a systematic review of evidence-based resources (prevalence estimates, assessment instruments, and interventions) on mental health-related outcomes addressing individuals aged 0-19 years in Mozambique. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, CINAHL, Google Scholar, African Index Medicus, and local catalogues. Extraction followed COSMIN and Cochrane manuals (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251016208). The search yielded 81 unique publications, including 61 reports presenting prevalence estimates from 25 studies, 29 reports providing data on 42 assessment instruments, and 9 intervention reports describing 8 intervention trials. The clinical prevalence of mental disorders were estimated in two surveys, conducted in Nampula (ADHD: 13·4%; N = 748, 6-18 years) and Maputo (any mental diagnosis: 23%, anxiety disorders: 17·5%; major depression episode: 8·5%; disruptive behavior disorder: 6·6%; substance use disorders: 4·5%; ADHD: 3·3%; PTSD: 1·2%; N = 486, 12-19 years). Most research focused on psychosocial adversities, with nationally representative adolescent surveys reporting significant exposure to violence (physical/emotional violence annually: 24·86%; girls suffering intimate partner violence: 21·11%; lifetime sexual abuse: 16·55%). National suicide rates were highest among 15-19-year-olds (1·53 per 100,000). Only four instruments were cross-culturally adapted and showed reliable psychometrics (MINI-KID, GAD-7, PHQ-A, and SDQ), whilst unadapted tools performed poorly. There was a single randomized clinical trial which reported a cost-effective intervention for neurodevelopment among high-poverty preschoolers. Children and adolescents in Mozambique face significant psychosocial adversity, and available evidence suggests a substantial burden of mental disorders according to limited clinical data. There are few available instruments assessing mental conditions, and culturally sensitive approaches are warranted for strengthening local research.

items.title: "Carrying the burden silently": A mixed-methods analysis of common mental health disorders among women caregivers living with HIV in Enugu, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Women caregivers living with HIV (WCLHIV) face a dual burden of managing their own health while caring for their families, increasing their vulnerability to mental health disorders. This study aimed to ascertain the prevalence and factors associated with common mental health disorders among WCLHIV in Enugu, Nigeria. A cross-sectional study employing a mixed method approach was conducted among 1,011 WCLHIV accessing anti-retroviral therapy in four tertiary health facilities in Enugu State, Nigeria. Quantitative data were obtained face-to-face using pre-tested, validated tools to assess the prevalence of depression, anxiety, stigma, and other psychological characteristics. Multivariate logistic regression identified significant risk factors of mental health disorders at a 95% confidence interval and p < 0.05. Four focus group discussions involving 35 WCLHIV explored factors impacting their mental well-being. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically using an inductive approach. Participants had a mean age of 44.3 (SD ± 8.44) years. The prevalence of depression and anxiety was 25.7% and 19.2%, respectively, while 79.0% reported high perceived stigma. Having primary education (AOR = 1.53; 95% CI: 1.06 -2.22), and low social support (AOR = 2.32; 95% CI: 1.11-5.07) were risk factors while low income (AOR = 0.42; 95% CI: 0.21-0.85), and low perceived stress (AOR = 0.05; 95% CI: 0.02-0.15) were protective of depression. Low perceived stress was protective of anxiety (AOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.02-0.22). Qualitative findings converged with quantitative data, highlighting the impact of stigma, poor social support, pill burden, fear of status disclosure, and financial strain on the mental health of WCLHIV.The prevalence of common mental health disorders was high among WCLHIV with a substantial proportion experiencing depression and anxiety, reflecting the significant impact of stigma, low social support, and stress. Targeted multi-level psychosocial interventions and community empowerment programs are needed to strengthen social support and reduce stigma among WCLHIV.

items.title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and control measures on type 2 diabetes care among South Asians: the perspective of healthcare providers in British Columbia, Canada.
items.abstract: British Columbia is one of the most ethnically diverse provinces in Canada, with South Asians emerging as one of the fastest-growing ethnic minority groups, burdened by a high incidence of type 2 diabetes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many healthcare services shifted to virtual care to minimize infection transmission. Given the limited understanding of how primary care physicians in BC adapted their diabetes care approaches and the consequent impact on patient experience, this qualitative study aims to explore the effects of pandemic-related control measures on primary care diabetes services in BC from the perspectives of general practitioners, focusing particularly on their South Asian patients. We conducted semi-structured interviews with ten primary care physicians serving large South Asian patient populations. Interviews explored the pandemic's effects on care delivery, provider adaptations, and consequences for South Asian patients with diabetes. Sessions were held in person or via Zoom/Teams and transcribed verbatim. Transcripts underwent thematic content analysis to identify recurring themes and insights regarding barriers, adaptations, and recommendations to improve diabetes care. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted diabetes care, shifting services to virtual care and interrupting routine monitoring. This transition impacted specific aspect of diabetes care that can best be provided in-person (e.g., foot examinations, blood pressure checks and lifestyle counselling). The pandemic compounded existing issues, e.g., cost, concerns with side effects, and medication compliance among South Asian patients. Physicians also observed a general rise in anxiety and depression during the pandemic among their patients. Older South Asian patients faced additional cultural, language, and digital barriers; physicians struggled to obtain timely Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) tests. For many patients, a significant reliance on pharmacists embedded within certain physician's clinics, ensured an uninterrupted access to diabetes medication and supplies. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted diabetes care, with some groups facing additional cultural, language, and digital barriers. Our findings highlight the need for primary care reforms: improved telemedicine and EMR infrastructure, and policies to support virtual care. Bridging the digital divide and implementing targeted supports are essential to minimize care disruption for vulnerable populations during future pandemics or similar crises and ensure equity.

items.title: Analysing the implementation and transferability of an enhanced care pathway integrating systematic supportive cancer care and patient-partner support for people living with anal cancer: Protocol for a mixed-methods study in two French cancer centres.
items.abstract: Background Supportive cancer care (SCC) is essential for comprehensive oncology care. It addresses treatment-related adverse effects, reduces long-term sequelae and improves patients' quality of life. Patient-partner (PP) programmes positively impact psychological well-being, patient empowerment and supportive care. Nevertheless, access to SCC remains inconsistent, fragmented and unequally distributed, while PPs are rarely integrated into routine cancer care pathways. Anal cancer is a predominantly localised cancer with high survival rates. Treatment is associated with acute toxicity and often severe long-term sequelae. This interventional public health research study aims to implement and evaluate an innovative enhanced care pathway combining systematic SCC and structured PP support for all individuals diagnosed with anal cancer living in France. The study will assess the intervention's clinical, organisational, and social effects, and will identify the conditions required for its long-term sustainability and transferability. Methods and design This is a longitudinal mixed-methods case study conducted in two French Comprehensive Cancer Centres. The intervention entails introducing a systematic, coordinated, and repeated SCC offer together with a structured PP support programme for all patients diagnosed with anal cancer and over 12 months following diagnosis. One centre will implement the enhanced care pathway, while the other will initially provide standard care before progressively adopting the intervention during the transferability phase. Quantitative data will include patient-reported outcomes, clinical information and implementation indicators. Qualitative data exploring implementation processes, organisational changes and contextual determinants, will be collected through observations, semi-structured interviews, focus groups and PP activity logs. Discussion The study's results will provide essential scientific knowledge on the implementation of programmes providing equitable SCC and PP support access to people living with anal cancer. Specifically, by combining implementation research, participatory approaches and mixed-methods evaluation, the project aims to identify the organisational conditions for the sustainable implementation of such programmes for this population, and their successful transferability to other populations living with cancer and to other healthcare settings.

items.title: Changes in the acceptance of artificial intelligence in medicine among physicians and the general public in Japan: A repeated cross-sectional comparison of 2018 and 2025.
items.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced rapidly, yet whether growing societal familiarity with AI is accompanied by greater willingness to receive relatively autonomous AI-led care remains unclear. We conducted repeated cross-sectional online surveys in Japan in 2018 and 2025 using the same questionnaire and compared self-identified physicians and members of the general public (2018: 399 physicians and 600 members of the public; 2025: 300 physicians and 300 members of the public). Mean responses to the item assessing intention to use medical AI did not differ significantly between survey years in either group, despite consistently favorable evaluations of its usefulness and future necessity. Among physicians, the unadjusted mean response regarding the potential of medical AI to improve clinical efficiency was higher in 2025, but this difference was not significant after adjustment for age and sex. Among members of the public, self-rated knowledge of medical AI was higher in 2025, while expectations that medical AI would increase healthcare costs were also greater. These findings suggest that increased self-rated knowledge may not necessarily be accompanied by greater intention to use relatively autonomous medical AI. Implementation strategies should therefore address concerns regarding responsibility, safety, data protection, and healthcare costs alongside efforts to improve public understanding.

items.title: Longitudinal blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients: A Bayesian multivariate joint modeling study in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Stroke is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hypertension being its most important modifiable risk factor. Although the association between elevated blood pressure and stroke is well established, the extent to which longitudinal blood pressure patterns influence the timing of stroke remains poorly understood, particularly in low-resource settings. We investigated the association between longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 494 newly diagnosed hypertensive patients receiving follow-up care at two general hospitals in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia, between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2024. Time to stroke was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model, while repeated systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements were modelled using linear mixed-effects models. The longitudinal and survival processes were jointly estimated using a Bayesian multivariate joint modelling framework. Posterior adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. The incidence of stroke was 2.19 per 100 person-years (95% CI: 1.60-2.64). Higher current underlying systolic and diastolic blood pressure levels were associated with increased stroke risk, with posterior AHRs of 3.25 (95% CrI: 1.85-5.83) and 2.32 (95% CrI: 1.35-4.27), respectively. Older age (≥65 years; AHR: 6.18; 95% CrI: 2.32-18.05), comorbidity (AHR: 4.00; 95% CrI: 1.72-10.25), and stage II hypertension (AHR: 4.06; 95% CrI: 1.49-16.36) were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. Rural residence was associated with a lower hazard of stroke (AHR: 0.16; 95% CrI: 0.05-0.40). Higher longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. These findings support regular blood pressure monitoring and targeted prevention strategies among older adults and patients with comorbidities in similar resource-limited settings.

items.title: Spatial and multilevel determinants of delayed healthcare access following occupational accidents in Brazil.
items.abstract: Delayed healthcare-seeking following occupational accidents increases the risk of complications, disability, and mortality. Although occupational injuries remain a major public health concern in Brazil, national evidence on the spatial distribution and multilevel determinants of Delayed healthcare-seeking is limited. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, geographic distribution, and individual and municipal-level determinants of Delayed healthcare-seeking following occupational accidents in Brazil. A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted using 2024 data from the Brazilian Notifiable Diseases Information System. A total of 477,276 Occupational accident cases were included in the analysis. Delayed healthcare-seeking was defined as accessing healthcare services more than 24 hours after injury occurrence. A two-level mixed-effects logistic regression model was used to identify individual and municipal-level determinants, while spatial clustering techniques were applied to assess spatial clustering patterns. The prevalence of Delayed healthcare-seeking was 12.2%. Significant spatial clustering was observed across Brazilian municipalities, with hotspots concentrated in the North and Midwest regions. Compared with White individuals, Black (AOR = 1.11; 95% CI: 1.06-1.15) and Brown individuals (AOR = 1.13; 95% CI: 1.10-1.16) had higher odds of Delayed healthcare-seeking. Agricultural workers were more likely to delay care (AOR = 1.20; 95% CI: 1.14-1.25). Injuries occurring in the evening showed the strongest association with delay (AOR = 3.62; 95% CI: 3.51-3.75). Higher odds of delay were also observed among individuals with lower limb injuries (AOR = 1.51), trunk/back injuries (AOR = 2.05), and multiple injuries (AOR = 1.90). Living in municipalities with lower health facility density was associated with an increased likelihood of Delayed healthcare-seeking. More than one in ten workers in Brazil experience Delayed healthcare-seeking following occupational injuries. Delays are associated with both social vulnerability and structural inequalities in healthcare access and exhibit significant geographic clustering. Strengthening healthcare accessibility, extending service availability, and implementing geographically targeted interventions in high-risk municipalities may improve timely care and reduce adverse occupational health outcomes. Findings highlight urgent need for geographically targeted occupational health interventions.

items.title: Exploring barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in low- and middle-income countries: Perspectives from international experts.
items.abstract: Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Although various interventions have been implemented to address this issue, many have failed to achieve positive outcomes due to numerous barriers. To explore the barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in LMICs. This qualitative exploratory study involved 19 adolescent pregnancy prevention program implementers across 24 LMICs. Data were collected through virtual in-depth individual interviews, organized using Dedoose software, and analyzed thematically. Findings highlighted seven interrelated challenges shaping programme reach, acceptability, and sustainability. Experts reported that adolescents' engagement depended on perceived usefulness and, at times, material or social benefits of attendance, while stigma made participation social risky and encouraged private information-seeking. Prevention efforts were further constrained by gendered allocation and unequal decision-making power, which limited boys' participation and girls' agency. Separately, poverty, household material insecurity, and transactional marriage practices such as bride price contributed to early unions and subsequent childbearing, while programme legitimacy is challenged by taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and the normalization of violence. Finally, implementation was hindered by administrative delays, weak institutional backing, school-level resistance, and unstable or poorly enforced policy environments, limiting continuity and scale-up of interventions. Effective teenage pregnancy prevention in LMICs requires more than delivering sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information; programmes must be designed to feel relevant to adolescents while reducing stigma and protecting confidentiality to support genuine engagement. Interventions also need to address gendered power dynamics and gatekeeper control, alongside community-level legitimacy barriers such as taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and normalized violence. Sustainable impact will depend on enabling implementation conditions, including reduced bureaucratic delays, stronger institutional and school support, coherent policies, reliable financing beyond donor cycles, and better data to guide targeted action.

items.title: Smart Paper Technology for maternal and newborn health data in The Gambia: A qualitative study of early implementation.
items.abstract: Many low- and middle-income countries rely on paper-based maternal and child health records that are often incomplete, fragmented, and difficult to use for continuity of care and decision-making. Smart Paper Technology (SPT), a hybrid paper-digital documentation system, has been proposed as a practical alternative to fully electronic medical records in resource-constrained settings. This study explored the early implementation of SPT in maternal and infant health services in The Gambia, focusing on feasibility and acceptability. We conducted a qualitative descriptive implementation evaluation guided by Rapid Assessment Procedures (RAP) in two pilot facilities in the Western Region of The Gambia between September and December 2024. Data were collected through 30 semi-structured interviews; four focus group discussions with 30 participants spanning facility-level clinical, management, and administrative staff, Ministry of Health staff, and technical and implementing partners; and non-participant observations across key service delivery areas. Data were analysed thematically using NVivo 14. Participants described SPT as feasible and broadly acceptable because it built on familiar paper-based workflows, was introduced through a participatory process, and offered advantages in reporting, information retrieval, and maternal-infant record linkage. However, these benefits were contingent on the implementation context. Key challenges included uneven training coverage, dual documentation, limited internet connectivity, scanning and data capture errors, storage constraints, and concerns about data governance. Staff adapted through peer mentoring, remote troubleshooting, and local workarounds. Participants emphasised that successful scale-up would require sustained training, clear governance arrangements, adequate human and technical resources, and a phased transition to government ownership. SPT offers a practical pathway towards digitisation in maternal and infant health services in LMICs, but its success depends on strong organisational systems, workforce support, and implementation processes that are responsive to routine service realities.

items.title: The intention to use Kangaroo Mother Care among first-time mothers 15-24 years in Kinshasa, DRC: An application of the integrated behavioral model.
items.abstract: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) is a low-cost, safe, and simple method that has proven efficacious at improving neonatal health outcomes, including mortality, in low-income countries. While beneficial for all newborns, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends KMC specifically for low birthweight (LBW) and premature infants. This study examined the applicability of a modified Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) framework for predicting KMC intentions among first-time mothers (FTMs) 15-24 years old in Kinshasa, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This study used secondary cross-sectional data from the 2020 Momentum Project endline survey, a quasi-experimental study in three intervention and three comparison health zones in Kinshasa, DRC. The association between IBM components and KMC intentions was tested using multivariate logistic regression. The total sample consisted of 1,918 adolescent and young first-time mothers (FTMs). About half of the respondents stated that they were "very likely" to practice KMC if they had a LBW or preterm baby. Approval of KMC, normative expectations, descriptive norms, self-efficacy, and autonomy were all positively associated with the intent to practice KMC. Age was also found to be a significant predictor; the odds of KMC intentions were 90% higher (95% CI= (1.11-3.24)) for FTMs 20-24 years compared to FTMs 15-19 years. The association between autonomy and KMC intentions was moderated by age. Marginal effects of the interaction found that the probability of intending to practice KMC for respondents 20-24 years was constant regardless of autonomy level, while autonomy significantly increased the probability of KMC intentions for younger women aged 15-19 years. Results suggest that KMC intentions among first-time mothers 15-24 years are associated with multiple factors simultaneously. Programs seeking to improve KMC intentions among this population should consider implementing age-specific empowering and norms-based strategies.

items.title: Risky sexual behaviors and associated factors among adolescent girls and young women in the context of HIV prevention pre-exposure prophylaxis in Tanzania: Analysis of the Tanzania HIV Impact Survey 2022-2023.
items.abstract: Risky sexual behavior contributes to HIV acquisition among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), including Tanzania. However, nationally representative evidence on its prevalence and associated factors remains limited. This study examines the prevalence and associated factors of risky sexual behavior among AGYW aged 15-24 years in Tanzania, in the context of the expanding Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) provision. A secondary analysis of nationally representative data from the 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey (THIS) was conducted among 3,669 sexually active AGYW aged 15-24 who answered PrEP-related questions. Survey-weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were carried out. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.The survey-weighted prevalence of risky sexual behaviors was 38.29%, higher among those aged 15-17 years than 18-24 years (61.57% versus 35.63%). Not being in a union was associated with increased odds of risky sexual behaviors among participants aged 15-17 years (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI: 4.33-17.55; p < 0.001) and 18-24 years (AOR = 15.13, 95% CI: 11.40-20.08; p < 0.001). Alcohol use was also associated with increased odds in both age groups (15-17 years: AOR = 13.38, 95% CI: 1.53-116.64; p = 0.019; 18-24 years: AOR = 2.47, 95% CI: 1.57-3.89; p < 0.001). Among young women aged 18-24 years, health facility attendance, family planning use and willingness to use PrEP were associated with higher odds, whereas secondary or higher education, parent or guardian communication about sex or HIV, and prior HIV testing were associated with lower odds. Risky sexual behavior remains common among Tanzanian AGYW, particularly those aged 15-17 years. Age-responsive prevention programmes need to integrate behavioral and biomedical interventions, prioritizing AGYW who are not in a union and who use alcohol or have limited access to PrEP.

items.title: Butyrate enhances the obesity reduction effect of Semaglutide.
items.abstract: Obesity represents a global public health burden with continuously increasing prevalence over recent decades. Combination regimens pairing semaglutide (Sema) with additional therapeutic agents have emerged as a major focus for anti-obesity research. In diet-induced obese (DIO) mice, we evaluated whether oxytocin (Oxt, 3 and 5 mg·kg-1), long-acting oxytocin (la‑Oxt), caffeine, or butyrate could potentiate the anti-obesity efficacy of Sema. We further compared hypothalamic neuronal activity and plasma metabolomic profiles following Sema treatment against dietary restriction (DR), an established intervention for weight loss and metabolic improvement. Whereas Oxt, la‑Oxt, and caffeine did not augment Sema-mediated body weight reduction, butyrate produced significant potentiation of Sema's anti-obesity effects. Either Sema monotherapy or Sema-butyrate co-administration elevated the number of c-Fos-positive cells in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of the hypothalamus. By contrast, DR decreased PVN c-Fos-positive cell number. Butyrate amplified Sema-elicited activation of PVN neuronal activity. Plasma metabolomics revealed limited overlap between the pharmacological interventions and DR, demonstrating orthogonal metabolic responses. These findings identify the Sema-butyrate combination as a promising anti-obesity strategy, and demonstrate that Sema and DR exert divergent effects on both hypothalamic neuronal activity and plasma metabolite levels.

items.title: Changes in attitudes toward the HPV vaccine in Kenya.
items.abstract: Globally, attitudes about vaccines and vaccination are changing rapidly, but few studies have examined within-person shifts over time. We use a longitudinal survey in Kenya to assess how respondents' attitudes about the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine changed between 2022 and 2024. In 2022, we conducted a random digit-dialed phone survey of 1405 Kenyan parents/caregivers of girls age-eligible for the HPV vaccine; respondents were re-contacted in 2024, and 1093 people (78%) were successfully re-surveyed. Each survey included identical questions about HPV vaccine and vaccination attitudes (adapted from the Vaccine Hesitancy Scale-HPV). We estimate direction and degree of each person's change in attitude, overall and by construct/question, and explore associations between these changes and respondent demographics, and baseline knowledge about HPV and HPV vaccination. Attitudes about the HPV vaccine changed substantially from 2022 to 2024. Although perceptions of the vaccine's importance and effectiveness were relatively stable (only 25% of respondents reported any attitude change), there were significantly more changes among respondents with lower educational attainment and who were unemployed. Safety perceptions changed substantially over this period: two-thirds of respondents changed their beliefs around the vaccine's side effects and riskiness. Approximately one-quarter of respondents developed a worse safety attitudes, while 18.9% of respondents improved their safety attitude. Among individuals with lower socioeconomic status, attitudes about following a clinician's HPV vaccination recommendation and riskiness of the HPV vaccine significantly worsened over this period. We found that, in this population of Kenyan adults and over a two-year period, attitudes about the HPV vaccine have changed both positively and negatively. Targeted interventions may be needed, particularly with less socioeconomically-advantaged groups, to reinforce messages about the vaccine's importance, effectiveness, and safety. Further research is needed about reasons for the large changes in safety perceptions, both toward more and less favorable views.

items.title: Microscopically detectable maternal schistosomiasis at delivery in Eastern Uganda: Prevalence, microscopy-based species distribution and associated household WASH characteristics in a hospital-based cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Schistosomiasis remains an important but neglected public health problem in Uganda. We estimated its prevalence, microscopy-based species distribution and associated factors among women delivering at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital. A hospital-based analytical cross-sectional study included 392 women from 1 September to 30 December 2025. One stool and one urine specimen per participant were examined microscopically for Schistosoma mansoni and S. haematobium, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associated factors; parsimonious conventional and Firth penalized models were used in sensitivity analyses. Microscopically detectable schistosomiasis was present in 44/392 women (11.2%; 95% CI: 8.5-14.8). Among microscopy-positive women, S. haematobium accounted for 63.6% of infections (95% CI: 48.2-76.7), S. mansoni for 29.5% (95% CI: 17.7-45.0), and mixed infection for 6.8% (95% CI: 2.1-19.6). Unimproved main water source (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.11; 95% CI: 1.46-6.64; p = 0.003), unimproved toilet facility (aOR = 4.40; 95% CI: 2.01-9.67; p < 0.001) and absence of a handwashing facility (aOR = 2.12; 95% CI: 1.02-4.41; p = 0.043) remained associated with microscopy-detected infection after adjustment. Women reporting fewer than four antenatal care contacts had higher adjusted odds than those reporting four to seven contacts (aOR = 8.43; 95% CI: 3.21-22.18; p < 0.001). The principal WASH associations remained consistent in sensitivity analyses. S. haematobium predominated among microscopy-classified infections. Household WASH characteristics remained associated with microscopy-detected infection, while the antenatal care association requires cautious interpretation. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causality but support further evaluation of context-appropriate schistosomiasis risk assessment within maternal health services and coordinated WASH and schistosomiasis-control strategies in endemic settings.

items.title: Health, workforce, and cost trade-offs of HIV programme prioritization strategies in Malawi.
items.abstract: Malawi has achieved substantial progress towards HIV epidemic control, reaching the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. However, declining external financing and health-workforce constraints threaten sustainability. Programme reconfiguration is being considered to reduce resource use. We used the Thanzi La Onse (TLO) individual-based health system simulation model to evaluate HIV programme changes in Malawi from 2025 to 2050. HIV testing, treatment monitoring, prevention interventions, and tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) were assessed individually and in combination, and compared against a Status Quo scenario with service delivery fixed at end-2024 levels. Changes that weakened diagnosis or treatment monitoring produced the largest adverse effects. Reducing HIV testing by 50% increased HIV/AIDS deaths by 55 200 (95% uncertainty interval 35 100-78 000) and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) by 3.28 million (2.41-4.54 million), while releasing 26.45 million healthcare-worker-hours and reducing total programme costs, including human resources for health and consumables, by USD 538.9 million. Removing viral load monitoring increased HIV/AIDS deaths by 21 460 (12 400-31 700) and DALYs by 1.17 million (0.58-1.69 million), with little change in workforce requirements but cost savings of USD 108.9 million. Reducing prevention services produced smaller savings with uncertain effects on mortality or DALYs. Combining reductions in testing, monitoring and prevention generated the largest cost savings (USD 812.0 million) but increased HIV infections by 1070 (990-1160), HIV/AIDS DALYs by 4.56 million (3.67-5.37 million) and AIDS deaths by 80 960 (66 240-93 640). Reducing HIV diagnosis or treatment monitoring risks undermining epidemic control. These services should be maintained if HIV programmes are reconfigured.

items.title: Therapeutic patient education upon oral emergency hospital discharge: Which skills should be prioritized?
items.abstract: Oral health inequalities remain a major public health concern, particularly among vulnerable populations who experience reduced access to dental care and increased reliance on emergency services. In France, emergency dental consultations are more frequent than in other European countries, reflecting persistent barriers to preventive and routine oral healthcare. Existing educational interventions in emergency settings are often limited to information delivery and rarely rely on structured pedagogical frameworks. Although therapeutic patient education adapted to hospital discharge contexts (TPE-HD) has demonstrated effectiveness in improving self-care skills in acute settings, no structured oral health intervention based on this model has yet been developed. This study aimed to identify the priority educational needs of patients attending a hospital-based oral medicine emergency department in order to define the competencies targeted by a brief educational intervention. A Knowledge-Attitudes-Practices survey was conducted toward patients consulting for oral emergencies. Identified educational needs were then translated into operational competencies integrated into the educational intervention design. This work demonstrates how observed gaps (insufficient knowledge, inappropriate beliefs, and inadequate practices) can be transformed into actionable capabilities that patients may use to manage their oral health. Drawing on the principles of discharge education and the structured framework of therapeutic patient education, it highlights the relevance of using emergency visits as opportunities for health learning and behavioral change. It contributes to the literature by supporting the needed integration of structured educational care into oral emergency pathways to reduce inappropriate emergency utilization, improve continuity of dental care, and address oral health inequalities.

items.title: Cross-sectional analysis of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine immunity in infants from the community.
items.abstract: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) reduce invasive disease and routine pediatric infections, yet subtherapeutic antibody responses have been reported in children with refractory otolaryngologic disease. This study evaluated pneumococcal antibody responses in a community cohort of vaccinated children and compared findings with prior specialty cohorts and prelicensure trial data. Serum from children aged 15-36 months with a documented four-dose PCV series was analysed for IgG concentrations to 14 serotypes. Protective thresholds were defined for invasive disease (≥0.35 μg/ml) and noninvasive disease (≥1.3 and ≥ 2.0 μg/ml). Results were compared with published pediatric cohorts and prelicensure trial data. Overall, 77.1% of children met the invasive disease threshold. Only 31.3% and 18.8% met the ≥1.3 and ≥ 2.0 μg/ml thresholds, respectively. Antibody levels were consistently lower than those reported in prior cohorts and prelicensure trials across most serotypes. These findings suggest that real-world immunogenicity following routine PCV may differ from that observed in strictly defined and controlled clinical trial populations, particularly at higher antibody thresholds associated with noninvasive disease. Larger-scale, prospective studies are needed to determine if trends hold across broader cohorts.

items.title: Readability and Citation Sources of ChatGPT-Generated Responses to Lymphoma-Related Health Questions: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Lymphoma is one of the most prevalent groups of cancers among people aged 15 to 29 years. Increasingly, patients with lymphoma and their caregivers use generative AI systems, supported by large language models (LLMs), to seek cancer-related online health information. Despite the need for plain and clear health information for clinical decision-making, there is a dearth of research on the readability and citation source classification of LLM-supported online health information. The objective of this study was to assess the reading level and reading ease of lymphoma-related health information using OpenAI's GPT-5.2 model, as well as the citation sourcing of LLM-generated results. Questions were submitted to the LLM through an automated pipeline. The application code was written with Claude and run and hosted on Vercel. Standardized instructions were submitted to the LLM, asking for evidence-based sources with URLs to enable citation analysis. The final dataset included 392 citations garnered from 96 standardized lymphoma-related questions. Readability was assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Flesch Reading Ease scores. Citation sources were classified into 9 predefined organization types, and topics included Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma and clinical trials. Differences in readability were tested using linear models fitted to all 392 citations, with standard errors clustered by question. Estimated marginal means (EMMs) were used to summarize model-adjusted readability scores by citation source and topic. When the omnibus test was statistically significant, pairwise comparisons were performed using the Tukey-Kramer adjustment for multiple comparisons. The Flesch-Kincaid reading levels of the ChatGPT responses by citation source and topic type were determined to be at the college or university level, well above the recommended sixth-grade level. Grade level did not differ by citation source (P=.58). The reading grade level of responses for Hodgkin lymphoma responses was statistically higher than that of clinical trial responses (mean 16.2, SD 3.4 vs 13.6, SD 2.5; P=.005). Flesch Reading Ease scores across source and topic were found to be very difficult at the university graduate academic level and did not differ by source (P=.27) or topic (P=.17). Although LLMs frequently produce responses that include cited information, the readability of these outputs may limit accessibility for many patients and caregivers. These findings highlight the need for improved readability standards in AI-generated health information and reinforce that LLM outputs should complement, not replace, professional medical guidance.

items.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
items.abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.
