items.title: Characterization of the complete mitochondrial genome of Haemaphysalis hystricis and its phylogenetic implications.
items.abstract: Haemaphysalis hystricis is a medically important tick vector, and three complete mitochondrial genomes derived from specimens collected from different geographic regions and hosts have previously been reported. In this study, we sequenced and analyzed the complete mitochondrial genome derived from H. hystricis specimens collected from a human host in Shaoguan, Guangdong Province, China, and systematically compared it with previously published H. hystricis mitogenomes. The complete mitogenome is 14,714 bp in length and contains 13 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, 2 ribosomal RNA genes, and two non-coding control regions. The overall gene order and composition are highly conserved and consistent with those reported for other Haemaphysalis species. The genome exhibits a strong A + T nucleotide bias, which is a typical feature of hard tick mitogenomes. Most tRNAs fold into typical cloverleaf secondary structures, whereas several exhibit truncated structures, reflecting a common pattern of mitochondrial tRNA structural simplification in arthropods. Selective pressure analysis indicated that all 13 PCGs are under purifying selection. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis showed that H. hystricis was most closely related to H. longicornis, consistent with previous studies. This study provides an additional H. hystricis mitogenome and compares it with the three previously published conspecific mitogenomes. The comparison revealed differences in genome length, the structure of non-coding regions, and tRNA secondary structures and provided estimates of gene-specific selective pressures. These findings provide valuable data for comparative mitogenomics and studies of intraspecific genetic variation in ticks.

items.title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
items.abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies. To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis. This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026. Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%. Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality. Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0. Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

items.title: A systematic review and probabilistic meta-analysis of health risks and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) associated with heavy metals in global drinking water: a continental comparison.
items.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in drinking water is a public health issue. This study conducted a probabilistic meta-analysis of health risk assessment for six commonly reported heavy metals (arsenic [As], lead [Pb], mercury [Hg], cadmium [Cd], chromium [Cr] and nickel [Ni]) in drinking water across six continents (Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America and Oceania) using the data from 2000 to 2024. Human exposure and risks were quantified in terms of cancer risks (CRs) and loss of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Monte Carlo simulation was employed to generate 5,000 random scenarios to incorporate uncertainty in risk assessment. Africa exhibited the average concentrations of As, Pb, Hg, Cd, Cr and Ni in drinking water of 176.7, 123.3, 93.7, 80.2, 91.0 and 35.1 μg/L respectively. The overall averages of CRs in Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Africa and Oceania were predicted to be 3.25 × 10-4, 1.34 × 10-4, 2.26 × 10-4, 1.18 × 10-3, 4.1 × 10-3 and 5.83 × 10-5 respectively while the DALYs were 1.48 × 105, 7.14 × 103, 1.20 × 104, 5.51 × 104, 8.63 × 105 and 2.68 × 102 respectively. Across six continents, inorganic fraction of arsenic (iAs) was the dominant carcinogen, contributing (45-91) % to total cancer risks in Asia, contributions of iAs and Cd were almost similar. The loss of DALYs were highest in Africa (8.63 × 105), due mainly to arsenic-induced bladder and cadmium-induced lung cancers. The global economic burden was USD 29 billion, with Africa accounting for almost 52 %. Sensitivity analysis identified iAs as the key parameter. The heavy metal contamination is a public health issue that requires decisive actions in Africa, South America and Asia.

items.title: Anti-Bacterial and Anti-Biofilm Activities of Cell-Free Supernatant of Lactobacillus johnsonii Against Salmonella Typhimurium.
items.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a predominant foodborne pathogen whose robust biofilm-forming capacity poses a persistent challenge to food safety and public health. This study investigated the inhibitory effects of cell-free supernatant (CFS) derived from Lactobacillus johnsonii on biofilms and characterized the transcriptional responses associated with CFS exposure using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). L.johnsonii CFS retarded bacterial growth at high concentrations. Moreover, CFS at various concentrations significantly inhibited biofilm formation in both S. Typhimurium strains, SL1344 and 14028, with maximum inhibition rates of 88.22% and 79.32%, respectively. CFS treatment markedly reduced metabolic activity, surface hydrophobicity, and auto-aggregation, meanwhile impaired bacterial motility and disrupted the architectural integrity of the biofilms. Furthermore, the CFS effectively prevented biofilm formation on various food and food-contact surfaces. RNA-seq analysis revealed that CFS treatment significantly altered the transcriptional profiles of Salmonella, with differentially expressed genes mainly enriched in ribosome, carbon metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, and microbial metabolism in diverse environments. These findings demonstrate the antibiofilm potential of L. johnsonii CFS under laboratory conditions and indicate its potential in controlling Salmonella contamination in food industry.

items.title: Mapping the debate on the role of national ethics councils in democratic reasoning. A narrative literature review.
items.abstract: Developments in science and society are moving fast. Emerging technologies give rise to ethical questions about manipulability of life and the ethical limits of biomedical science. To foster legitimate and justified policymaking on bio-ethical issues, governments seek expert guidance from bioethics advisory bodies such as national ethics councils. This raises questions about how they fulfil their advisory role within the democratic context. In what way can national ethics councils best contribute to democratic reasoning and decision-making regarding complex bioethics issues? We performed a narrative review of academic literature that concerns the role and legitimacy of national ethics councils. We searched literature databases PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar. The goal was to identify key themes that emerge as common threads across the literature. We identified five themes. We examined the discussions on the conceptualization of advice and the forms deemed appropriate for a national ethics council in relation to democratic decision-making, on the role of consensus, on the dimensions of expertise and council composition, on the dual tasks of formulating policy advice and stimulating public debate, and on the normative frameworks underpinning the work of national ethics councils. Our results indicate that in the context of complex policy issues, national ethics councils can make important contributions to democratic reasoning, though this involvement is shaped by several underlying dynamics. This narrative review urges national ethics councils to increase (self-) awareness as well as transparency about how they interpret their role within the democratic system.

items.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
items.abstract: Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation. The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report. On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions. This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

items.title: Perceived Discrimination, Preparation for Bias, and Associations with Physical and Mental Health of Racially/Ethnically Marginalized Children.
items.abstract: Prior studies suggest that perceived discrimination and preparation for bias are associated with children's mental health, yet few studies have examined relationships with children's physical health. The current study expands on prior literature by examining associations between perceived discrimination and preparation for bias parenting practices on the physical and mental health of racially/ethnically marginalized children. Children (n = 227, ages 7-13 years, 58% female; 28% Non-Hispanic Black, 26% Hispanic, 15% Hmong, 15% Native American, 10% multiracial/ethnic with White and 6% multiracial/ethnic without White) completed an in-clinic assessment of cardiometabolic health and self-reported perceived discrimination. Parents completed survey measures of their child's mental health (self-efficacy, inhibitory control, depression) and their use of preparation for bias parenting practices. Physical health measures (BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, pulse rate, hair cortisol) were taken at a lab visit. In adjusted regression analyses, children who self-reported any experiences of perceived discrimination had significantly lower levels of self-efficacy (p < 0.05) and inhibitory control (p < 0.05) than those who did not report experiences of discrimination. Preparation for bias parenting practices differed significantly by race/ethnicity and higher levels were associated with higher hair cortisol concentrations in children, reflecting elevated activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary adrenal (HPA) axis (p < 0.05). There were otherwise no statistically significant differences in children's mental or physical health outcomes as a function of perceived discrimination or preparation for bias parenting practices. Our findings highlight the potential importance of interventions that reduce interpersonal discrimination and the need for further research on parenting practices that may influence children's health.

items.title: The medical and surgery outcomes of pulmonary hydatid cyst disease: A 12-year multidisciplinary experience.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hydatid cyst disease (PHCD) remains a significant public health problem in endemic regions. To evaluate the demographic, serological, radiological, and surgical characteristics of patients with PHCD and to identify factors associated with hepatic involvement and postoperative outcomes. This retrospective study included 515 consecutive patients who underwent surgical treatment for PHCD at Dicle University Faculty of Medicine between 2013 and 2025. Demographic characteristics, cyst features, indirect fluorescent antibody (IFA) test results, concomitant hepatic involvement, surgical procedures, postoperative outcomes, and complications were analyzed. Among 515 patients, 275 (53.4%) were male and 240 (46.6%) were female. Female patients were significantly older than male patients (28.0 ± 18.0 vs. 23.8 ± 18.4 years, p = 0.002). Hepatic involvement was significantly associated with positive IFA test results (p < 0.001), bilateral pulmonary disease (p < 0.001), multiple pulmonary cysts (p < 0.001), female sex (p = 0.045), and left-sided pulmonary involvement (p = 0.019). Blood group distribution was not associated with hepatic involvement (p = 0.773), although IFA positivity differed significantly among ABO blood groups (p = 0.006). Larger cyst size was associated with longer hospital stay (r = 0.130, p = 0.003) and prolonged drainage duration (r = 0.094, p = 0.034). Perforated cysts were associated with increased hospital stay (r = 0.180, p < 0.001) and drainage duration (r = 0.139, p = 0.002). Pediatric patients had significantly larger cysts than adults (p = 0.007). Positive IFA results, multiple pulmonary cysts, and bilateral lung involvement are associated with concomitant hepatic hydatid disease. Cyst size and perforation status significantly influence postoperative recovery, particularly hospital stay and drainage duration. Surgical treatment provides excellent outcomes with low reoperation rates and no disease-related mortality in experienced centers.

items.title: Brief Report: User Participation in the Iterative Co-Design of Public Child Mental Health Services.
items.abstract: Service planning should necessarily involve the community. This brief report presents parental feedback collected after a psychoeducational group for parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and places these observations within recent literature on participatory co-design. Collected feedback illustrates how parental input can guide iterative, user-centered improvements in public ASD services. items.title: Heat Exposure Definitions in Temperature-Mortality Studies: Towards a Harmonisation Framework.
items.abstract: We reviewed how heat exposure is defined using thresholds and reference temperatures derived from the temperature-mortality exposure-response curve in time-series and case-crossover studies using distributed lag non-linear models and propose a harmonisation framework relevant to climate change research and heat disaster preparedness. The rapid review identified variation across studies in heat thresholds and reference temperatures, affecting the comparability of estimates. A case study in Spain illustrates how the minimum mortality temperature (MMT) approach estimates overall heat-related mortality and its contributions from moderate and extreme heat, whereas the percentile-based approach estimates excessive heat mortality that could potentially be prevented by protective measures operating above the heat threshold. Differences in heat thresholds and reference temperatures make findings harder to compare across studies and complicate risk communication. Explicit reporting of these two components and their relevance to the research question and intended application would improve interpretation and translation to public health action.

items.title: Genotypic and phylogenetic characterization of Salmonella Minnesota ST548 strains with potential risk to public health.
items.abstract: Salmonella Minnesota ST548 has emerged as an important serovar in the poultry industry and has been detected in food products. Five nonclonal S. Minnesota isolates from poultry in southeastern Brazil were characterized using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and 263 database sequences were analyzed for virulence genes, antimicrobial resistance genes, and phylogenetic relationships. Among the analyzed sequences, 191 multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains carried antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) conferring resistance to aminoglycosides (aac(6')-Iaa, aph(3')-Ia and aadA1), quinolones (qnrB19), tetracycline (tetA), sulfonamides (sul2), and beta-lactams (blaCMY-2, blaCTX-M-8, blaCTX-M-55 and blaTEM-126). Furthermore, several genes associated with virulence factors were identified, including adherence (faeC, faeE, and fimB), fimbrial adherence determinants (pegA, staA, fimA, and csgD), magnesium uptake (mgtB and mgtC), macrophage inducible genes (mig-14), toxin (cdtB) and secretion system (ssaM, sseE and sseJ). Twenty-five plasmid replicons and 53 distinct prophages were identified in the analyzed sequences. Phylogenetic analysis showed close relationships between nonclonal S. Minnesota poultry isolates from southeastern Brazil and S. Minnesota sequences associated with human outbreaks from other sources and countries. These findings highlight the need for surveillance of this serovar in both public and veterinary health.

items.title: Change in alcohol consumption and all-cause mortality among postmenopausal women diagnosed with breast cancer.
items.abstract: Evidence is inconsistent regarding an association between alcohol consumption and survival following a breast cancer diagnosis; therefore, we examined how change in alcohol consumption affects all-cause mortality (ACM) in a population of breast cancer survivors. We prospectively assessed pre-diagnosis, pre- to post-diagnosis, and post-diagnosis change in alcohol consumption among 1,558 postmenopausal women (mean age-at-diagnosis: 71 years) diagnosed with non-metastatic invasive breast cancer from the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort (baseline: 1992-1993). Five categories of alcohol intake were determined at each assessment; change in alcohol consumption was categorized as stable, quit, reduced, and increased. Change occurred at a median of two years before (pre-diagnosis) and two years after (post-diagnosis) diagnosis. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the associations between change groups and ACM. Over a median follow-up of 12.6 years, 750 women died (130 breast cancer deaths). Compared to stable consumption, the association between cessation and ACM varied by change interval: pre-diagnosis (HR:0.91, CI:0.69-1.21), pre- to post-diagnosis: (HR:1.39, CI:1.12-1.73), post-diagnosis: (HR:0.98, CI:0.70-1.35). Alcohol reduction was not associated with ACM. Among women consuming ≥ 1 drink/day pre-diagnosis, increasing consumption elevated ACM risk (HR:1.83, 95%CI:1.02-3.31). Alcohol reduction or cessation was not associated with a decrease in ACM among older breast cancer survivors. Among those drinking ≥ 1 drink/day, an increase in consumption pre-diagnosis was associated with higher mortality. Findings may be limited by uncontrolled confounding, a low prevalence of heavy drinking, or an insufficient duration of sustained change.

items.title: Methodological challenges and uncertainties in human health risk assessment of nitrate exposure.
items.abstract: Safe and clean water is a fundamental requirement for human health and well-being. Both the quantity and quality of drinking water directly affect population health, which makes the investigation of contaminants and their associated health risks a matter of growing scientific and public concern. Among the many waterborne contaminants, nitrate is of particular importance. It is a recalcitrant compound found in most water bodies, originating from both natural sources and anthropogenic activities such as agriculture and wastewater discharge. Numerous studies have attempted to evaluate the health risks of nitrate exposure across different age groups, including infants, children, and adults. However, in reviewing the literature, we have identified recurring methodological inconsistencies that may compromise the reliability of risk estimates. In this discussion paper, we examine key methodological issues in nitrate-related human health risk assessment, including the misapplication of nitrate reference dose (RfD) values across different population groups, inconsistencies in chemical units and nomenclature, and uncertainties arising from the conversion of nitrate to nitrite during exposure and risk assessment. Examples from published research will be used to illustrate and critically analyse these common methodological pitfalls.

items.title: Prospecting for efflux pump and repressor genes in rivers of the Amazon region of Brazil.
items.abstract: The spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria in water bodies poses a significant public health concern. Efflux pumps represent critical mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, regulated by genetic repressors that aid bacterial adaptation to environmental stress. This study profiles the diversity of efflux pump genes and genetic repressors in the surface waters of the Cereja (Bragança) and Uraim (Paragominas) rivers in the Amazon region of Brazil. Surface water samples were collected along a gradient of anthropogenic impact, and environmental DNA was sequenced on the Illumina platform. The resulting sequencing data were subsequently subjected to metagenomic analysis, which identified a higher abundance of efflux pump genes in the Cereja River compared to the Uraim River, dominated by the RND and SMR families. Additionally, two-component system (TCS) repressor genes, particularly cbrB, were successfully recovered and modeled using Swiss-Model homology modeling. The higher coverage of the cbrB repressor gene in anthropogenically impacted sites underscores its regulatory role in bacterial stress responses, suggesting its potential application as a novel biomarker of environmental pollution and antibiotic resistance spread in aquatic ecosystems.

items.title: Association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan.
items.abstract: Few studies have explored the adverse health effects of nighttime heat exposure. This study examined the association between nighttime heat exposure and emergency hospitalization for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in Japan. Hospitalizations were identified from a nationwide administrative database covering the period from May to September between 2011 and 2021. Days with minimum temperatures higher than region-specific 92.5th percentile temperatures were considered as exposed to nighttime heat. Daily maximum temperature was adjusted for as a proxy for daytime heat exposure. First, a time-stratified case-crossover study using conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was conducted to estimate location-specific heat-related relative risks (RRs) of emergency hospitalization for OHCA over lag 0-6 days. Second, a random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled RRs. The analysis was further stratified by age, sex, and region. Third, in an attempt to account for the geographical heterogeneity in RRs, the location-specific penetration rate of air conditioners (ACs) was included as a meta-regressor. A total of 135,898 hospitalizations for OHCA were identified. Nighttime heat exposure was associated with increased emergency hospitalizations for OHCA (RR: 1.090 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.047-1.135). Higher RRs were observed among people aged ≥ 75 years and females living in northern areas (1.295 (95%CI: 1.117-1.500) and 1.352 (95%CI: 1.145-1.596), respectively). In locations with a lower penetration rate of ACs, females and those aged ≥ 75 years were at higher RRs.

items.title: Immediate vs delayed extubation after pediatric liver transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Immediate extubation (IE) in the operating room following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is increasingly adopted in adults but pediatric evidence remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify factors associated with IE and compare outcomes between IE and delayed extubation (DE) after pediatric OLT. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 30, 2025. Studies comparing IE and DE in pediatric OLT recipients were included. Outcomes included reintubation, mortality, thrombosis, reoperation, tracheostomy, PICU, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Random-effects meta-analysis was pre-specified for all outcomes; sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Twelve retrospective single-center studies comprising 1323 patients (1158 unique children after accounting for two center-level cohort overlaps) were included. IE was associated with lower odds of reintubation (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59) and mortality (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18-0.68); both estimates were confirmed by a correction-free Peto odds ratio (0.29 and 0.31, respectively). No significant differences were observed for thrombosis or reoperation. IE was associated with shorter PICU LOS (SMD - 0.88, 95% CI - 1.39 to - 0.37), hospital LOS (SMD - 1.16, 95% CI - 2.00 to - 0.31). Donor-type subgroup analyses showed effect sizes in the same direction as the overall analysis for PICU and hospital LOS, but none of the within-subgroup estimates reached statistical significance. Meta-regression identified intraoperative transfusion differences as predictor of hospital LOS (β = - 0.045, p = 0.006, R2 = 57.1%), a pattern more consistent with confounding by indication than with a beneficial mechanism of transfusion itself. IE was associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter LOS in pediatric OLT, but these findings derive exclusively from retrospective studies at high risk of selection bias, and causality cannot be established. Children undergoing IE were likely older and in better preoperative condition; hospital LOS findings are particularly susceptible to confounding. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these outcomes benefit. • Delayed extubation with prolonged mechanical ventilation has been standard after pediatric orthotopic liver transplantation. • Immediate extubation in the operating room is increasingly used after adult liver transplantation experiences. • Pediatric evidence on immediate extubation comes from single-center retrospective studies. • This meta-analysis of 12 studies found immediate extubation associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter length of stay. • These associations likely reflect selection bias rather than a proven causal benefit. • Immediate extubation appears feasible and safe in selected children, but prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine patients benefiting from this approach.

items.title: Maternal Anxiety Surrounding Fetal Cardiac Evaluation: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Fetal echocardiography has transformed prenatal cardiac diagnosis, yet the emotional burden of referral and evaluation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify maternal anxiety before and after fetal cardiac evaluation (FCE), identify clinical predictors of anxiety, and assess whether anxiety changes following evaluation and consultation regardless of outcome. In this prospective cohort study, 117 pregnant women undergoing initial or follow-up FCE completed pre- and post-consultation assessments using a seven-item symptom inventory adapted from the Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SASRQ; score range 7-42). Participants were classified as anxious or non-anxious by direct self-report. Scores were compared with paired t-tests; exploratory multivariable models adjusted for clinical, demographic, and referral covariates, including prior pregnancy loss, psychiatric history, and diagnostic outcome. 80% of participants (94/117) reported anxiety about the FCE before evaluation; prior pregnancy loss was associated with anxious state (p = 0.049). Following FCE and consultation, mean symptom scores in the anxious group fell from 15.07 to 9.03, a 6.04-point (40.1%) reduction (p < 0.001), with reductions across symptom domains regardless of diagnostic outcome. Scores in the non-anxious group did not change significantly (8.48 to 7.87; p = 0.27). Most women referred for FCE report anxiety before evaluation. FCE with consultation was associated with a substantial reduction in anxiety symptoms in these women, irrespective of whether a cardiac abnormality was found. Although the uncontrolled pre-post design cannot establish causation, these findings suggest that diagnostic clarity and expert consultation may themselves be anxiety-reducing and support evaluation of integrated psychosocial care models in fetal cardiology.

items.title: Rise of Lower Respiratory Tract Infections Other than Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the Emergency Room: Results from the Season (2024/25) of the RISE Study.
items.abstract: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) are a major cause of pediatric emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations. Although respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and rhinovirus (RV) are common etiological agents, pathogen-specific data from pediatric emergency settings remain limited. This prospective surveillance study quantified ARI-related ED visits, described pathogen-specific epidemiology, and assessed attendance and hospitalization rates as well as the distribution of lower versus upper respiratory tract infections (LRTI/URTI) in children younger than 60 months in two pediatric EDs in Berlin between November 1, 2024 and May 31, 2025. Respiratory pathogens were identified using nasopharyngeal swab samples tested by multiplex real-time RT-PCR (QIAstat-Dx® Respiratory Panel Plus). Within the study period 4042 ARI-related ED visits occurred. A total of 310 children were enrolled in our study (median age 18 months); 115 (37.1%) had LRTI and 195 (62.9%) URTI. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 271 children (87.4%). The attendance rate for RSV was 24.4% (66 cases), for FLU 25.8% (70 cases), and for RV 29.5% (80 cases). Overall, 93 children (30.0%) were hospitalized, including 65 with LRTI and 28 with URTI. Hospitalization rates were highest for RSV infections (26/65, 40.0%) and RV infections (28/65, 43.1%), and lower for FLU infections (13/69, 18.8%). Hospitalization due to LRTI predominated among children with RSV (24/26, 92.3%) and RV infections (20/28, 71.4%), whereas FLU infections were less frequently observed (7/13, 53.9%). Furthermore, younger age, a history of pneumonia, a history of bronchiolitis, and the absence of breastfeeding were associated with hospitalization. In contrast to the previous season, in which RSV was associated with the highest attendance and hospitalization rate, we observed a high burden of RV infections in the 2024/2025 season. These findings may impact surveillance strategies, clinical management, and future public health strategies.

items.title: Examining the role of patients' socioeconomic status in the appraisal stage of health technology assessment in the Netherlands.
items.abstract: Socioeconomic health inequalities remain a persistent public health concern, and there is growing recognition of the potential role of health technology assessment (HTA) in addressing them. In the Netherlands, the National Health Care Institute (ZIN) does not formally consider socioeconomic status (SES) in the assessment stage of HTA. This study examined whether SES is considered in the appraisal stage. We reviewed all publicly accessible meeting minutes of the appraisal committee published between 2013 and 2024. Minutes were screened for SES-related search terms, and contextual information was extracted on how SES was discussed. For minutes with more extensive SES-related discussions, it was examined whether SES considerations were reflected in final recommendations. SES-related terms were identified in 18 of the 86 meeting minutes. Most references were brief and not followed by further discussion. More extensive discussion occurred in the context of four topics that were discussed in several meetings. Three of these topics concerned reimbursement decisions involving potential additional patient costs. The fourth concerned the updated assessment framework 'Necessity of insurance', in which health inequalities were included as a consideration. Across these four topics, SES was discussed in relation to financial vulnerability, affordability, and access to care for groups with limited resources. SES does not appear to be systematically considered in the appraisal stage of the HTA process at ZIN. Further research on deliberation and decision making is needed to assess whether and how SES should be incorporated into the decision-making framework and to explore methods allowing integrating SES-related considerations in both assessment and appraisal stages.

items.title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China.
items.abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. In this study, we report the co-circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and H5N6 HPAIVs associated with mortality events in Anseriformes and Charadriiformes at a coastal wintering site in Fujian Province, China. H5N1 and H5N6 viruses were identified in four species of waterfowl (Bean Goose, Eastern Spot-billed Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, and Eurasian Curlew). Phylogenetic analysis indicated that these H5N1 and H5N6 isolates were clade 2.3.4.4b strains circulating within Eurasia and lacked known mammalian adaptation markers in key proteins. The infected birds exhibited severe systemic multi-organ pathology, with the most pronounced damage observed in the lungs. H5N6 and H5N1 viruses caused lethal injury in BALB/c mice, with H5N1 leading to systemic infection. Environmental sampling also revealed the presence of H5N1 HPAIVs alongside low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) such as H3N1 and H6N1. Our findings highlight the complex and dynamic transmission patterns of H5 HPAIV in wild bird populations and the substantial threat they pose to mammals, underscoring the critical importance of sustained surveillance for high pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds.

items.title: Altered GABA<sub>B</sub> receptor sensitivity in heavy drinkers indexed using a TMS-based biomarker: a randomized controlled experimental medicine trial.
items.abstract: Metabotropic γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptors (GABA B Rs) are implicated in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and represent a promising therapeutic target. However, robust biomarkers of GABA B Rs target engagement and sensitivity in humans are lacking. We examined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-derived cortical inhibition and growth hormone (GH) release as measures of GABA B R function, and whether heavy alcohol use is associated with altered responses to pharmacological GABA B R activation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 31 healthy volunteers (16 heavy drinkers, 15 light drinkers) received baclofen 30 mg, baclofen 60 mg, or placebo across three sessions. Long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), short-interval intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation were assessed with paired-pulse TMS at baseline and ~60 min post-dose. Baclofen blood concentrations and plasma GH levels were measured. Baclofen produced dose-dependent increases in GH release, confirming neuroendocrine GABA B R engagement. The LICI response to baclofen differed between groups: In light drinkers, baclofen at 30 mg potentiated LICI, and a similar potentiation was seen at 60 mg, indicating that a plateau may have been reached. In contrast, in heavy drinkers, a potentiation of LICI similar to that in light drinkers was seen at 30 mg baclofen, but was absent at the 60 mg dose despite comparable pharmacokinetics, suggesting altered GABA B R function. Effects were selective for GABA B R-mediated inhibition, with no consistent modulation of short-interval intracortical inhibition or corticospinal excitability. Acute baclofen administration reveals altered GABA B R sensitivity in heavy drinkers, with preserved responses at lower doses but reduced response under stronger agonist stimulation. LICI and GH release provide complementary biomarkers of central and peripheral GABA B Rs engagement and may support translational development of mechanism-based treatments for AUD.

items.title: Circuit architecture and regulation of the Drosophila brain neuroendocrine system.
items.abstract: Insect neurosecretory cells (NSCs), located in distinct regions of the brain and the ventral nerve cord (VNC), are a major source of neuropeptides and peptide hormones (NPHs) that facilitate communication between the nervous system and peripheral tissues. NPHs, in turn, regulate growth and development, and modulate diverse behaviors and physiological processes including feeding, locomotion, social behaviors, metabolism, and reproduction. Given their central role in regulating systemic homeostasis, NSCs are tightly regulated. Recent advances in connectomics and single-cell transcriptomics have enabled comprehensive identification of NSCs in the Drosophila melanogaster brain and identified factors that modulate their activity. Here, we review the current state-of-the-art on insect NSCs and the inputs regulating them, predominantly focusing on adult Drosophila. We highlight: 1) major synaptic inputs, 2) neuromodulatory inputs, 3) gut-derived NPHs, and 4) cell-autonomous internal sensors that influence NSC activity. Finally, we discuss open questions in the field and how advances in omics approaches can bridge the gap in our understanding of NSC regulation between Drosophila and other insects.

items.title: Mechanisms of Seizure Generation and SUDEP in Cortical Dysplasia: A Role for Cortical Up and Down States.
items.abstract: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) remains the primary cause of epilepsy-related mortality, yet the preictal brain dynamics that distinguish fatal from nonfatal seizures are not well understood. Identifying the network mechanisms determining these outcomes is critical for developing SUDEP risk biomarkers. Using a neuron-specific PTEN knockout mouse model of cortical dysplasia-which exhibits spontaneous seizures and SUDEP-like events-we employed long-term video-EEG monitoring to analyze cortical state transitions and network signatures. We found that nonfatal seizures are preceded by a progressive "ramp-up" of cortical up and down states, characterized by alternating neuronal depolarization and hyperpolarization, which appears to facilitate seizure initiation. In sharp contrast, sudden death is preceded by a marked suppression of these state transitions and the emergence of infraslow EEG activity, suggestive of spreading depolarizations. This pattern differed from the sustained spike-wave complexes and preserved state transitions observed during status epilepticus. These physiological differences are mirrored behaviorally: nonfatal events typically feature forelimb clonus and spike-wave discharges, whereas fatal seizures are characterized by kicking, tonic hindlimb extension, and diffuse EEG attenuation. Together, these findings suggest that cortical up and down states support seizure initiation, while their disruption and failure to recover postictally predisposes neocortical networks to spreading depression episodes that very likely propagate to brainstem circuits, ultimately triggering SUDEP. By delineating these divergent peri-ictal signatures, this study identifies candidate neurophysiological markers for SUDEP risk stratification.

items.title: Drosophila Models of Human Neurodegenerative Diseases.
items.abstract: In his book Insects and the Life of Man: Collected Essays on Pure Science and Applied Biology, Sir V. B. Wigglesworth examined how a fundamental understanding of insect physiology and biology can be applied to some of society's greatest challenges, including human health. Here we reflect on how, in the 50 years since his book's publication, Drosophila melanogaster have played a critical role in advancing our understanding of human neurodegenerative diseases. Focusing on Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and the frontotemporal dementia / amyotrophic lateral sclerosis spectrum, we examine the role Drosophila have played in elucidating fundamental mechanisms of neurodegeneration, identifying therapeutic targets, and dissecting the complex interplay that exists between genetics and environmental factors. Together these studies highlight how Drosophila models continue to provide critical insight into the molecular mechanisms underpinning neurodegeneration and provide a fundamental pre-clinical model in which we can accelerate research into human neurodegenerative conditions.

items.title: Cross-species evaluation of commercial primary antibodies by Western blotting for immunohistochemical protein detection in mouse, rat, and human brain tissue.
items.abstract: Background Commercial antibodies show variable specificity and performance, limiting reproducibility of immunohistochemical studies. We systematically evaluated antibodies used to detect brain proteins across species. New method Established Western blotting (WB) and immunofluorescence (IF) validation approaches were applied systematically and in parallel to mouse, rat, and human brain tissue. The distinctive scope of the study was the comparative evaluation of 23 antibodies targeting 17 proteins, with WB results interpreted in the context of expected molecular weights, isoforms, post-translational modifications, and published evidence concerning each target. Antibody performance was further compared with publicly available validation information, and logistic regression was used to assess whether antibody citation count and manufacturer-provided validation information predicted successful experimental validation. Results Ten antibodies (43%) showed supportive WB results, and eight (35%) were validated by both WB and IF. Several antibodies produced unexplained or non-specific bands, while others showed speciesdependent performance. Validated antibodies displayed appropriate neuroanatomical and subcellular staining patterns. Antibody citation count was moderately associated with successful validation, whereas manufacturer-provided validation information did not improve predictive performance. Comparison with existing methods The overall validation rate was comparable to previously published antibody validation studies and Human Protein Atlas results. The present study extends existing work through its broader antibody panel, parallel cross-species evaluation, detailed target-protein assessment, and quantitative analysis of antibody metadata. Conclusions Commercial antibodies require independent validation before use in cross-species immunohistochemical studies. Our results provide a practical resource for antibody selection and highlight limitations of manufacturer claims and citation counts as indicators of antibody performance.

items.title: Baseline Adjustment and Normalisation in Neurite Outgrowth Assays: A Simulation-Based Comparison of Analytical Methods.
items.abstract: Background When baseline neurite lengths differ between experimental groups, analytical methods may detect, miss or overstate treatment effects. We assessed how commonly used methods recover a baseline-adjusted treatment effect. New method We developed a simulation framework comparing endpoint comparison, change score, percentage change, percent-of-control normalisation and ANCOVA. A known 8 μm treatment effect was simulated under varying baseline imbalances and baseline-growth relationships, with additional analyses of sample size and baseline measurement error. Results In the worked example, endpoint comparison and percent-of-control normalisation did not recover the true adjusted effect, whereas change score overestimated it by 55%. Across 20 parameter combinations, ANCOVA maintained nominal Type I error (3.8-5.8%) and remained essentially unbiased (mean absolute bias: 0.02 μm) when baseline was measured without error. Small-sample analyses showed that systematic bias persisted while error rates varied with sample size. Substantial baseline measurement error reduced ANCOVA's bias advantage and could inflate its Type I error. Comparison with existing methods Endpoint and percent-of-control approaches estimate unadjusted endpoint differences. Change scores can be distorted when baseline predicts subsequent growth, while percentage change additionally introduces denominator-related distortion when baselines differ. ANCOVA directly estimates the treatment effect at a common baseline under its standard assumptions. Conclusions When the target is a baseline-adjusted effect and baseline is measured reliably, ANCOVA provides the most appropriate analysis under the conditions examined. Baseline values, the target estimand and assumption checks should be reported explicitly.

items.title: A study protocol of fasting to provide energy needed to help adults in need of cognitive enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE).
items.abstract: Background Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is defined as a self-perceived reduction in cognitive function and is associated with future cognitive impairment. However, few clinical trials have explored the impact of nonpharmacological interventions in older adults with SCD. Time-restricted eating (TRE) restricts food intake to a daily eating window and has shown improvements in cardiometabolic markers associated with cognitive impairment. Objective The Fasting to provide Energy Needed to Help Adults in Need of Cognitive Enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE) study is a rater-blinded, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial, designed to evaluate the effects of TRE on cognitive function in overweight older adults with SCD. Methods The study aims to enroll older adults (aged ≥65 years) who are overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m 2 ) and have SCD without objective impairment. Participants are randomized to either a 6-month TRE or Successful Aging (SA) group. The TRE group is instructed to restrict eating to an 8-h window, and the SA group to maintain current lifestyle behaviors. The primary outcome is change in cognitive function, assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status and Montreal Cognitive Assessment at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Secondary outcomes include physical function, blood biomarkers, and self-reported mood, sleep, and quality of life. Conclusion The Fasting ENHANCE study protocol outlines the methodology for evaluating the effect of TRE on cognitive and metabolic health in older adults with SCD. Results will inform future nonpharmacological interventions aimed at attenuating cognitive decline. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05732935.

items.title: Zinc activates autophagy by regulating HDAC6 expression following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.
items.abstract: Intracellular zinc accumulation and excessive autophagy have been reported to contribute to neuronal death following cerebral ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6), which contains a zinc-dependent active site, is closely associated with autophagy. However, the relationship between zinc, HDAC6 and autophagy following cerebral I/R remains unclear. In this study, we aim to investigate whether ischemia-induced zinc accumulation activates autophagy through HDAC6. Rats were treated with zinc chelator, autophagy activator/inhibitor or HDAC6 inhibitor during a 90-minute middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume, neurological deficits, protein expression, and the colocalization of HDAC6, Beclin1, and zinc in neurons were evaluated. Our results demonstrate that beclin1 expression was significantly increased after cerebral I/R and this elevation was markedly attenuated by zinc chelation. Notably, reactivation of autophagy with rapamycin significantly, though not completely, diminished TPEN-mediated neuroprotection, suggesting that zinc-induced autophagy is an important contributor to neuronal injury following cerebral I/R. Moreover, immunofluorescence revealed that HDAC6 was colocalized with Beclin1 in the penumbra of ischemic rats, and inhibition of HDAC6 reduced Beclin1 expression and alleviated brain injury. Molecular docking analysis suggested a potential interaction between HDAC6 and α-tubulin, which may influence autophagy by regulating microtubule stability and autophagosome transport. Furthermore, chelating zinc decreased HDAC6 expression, while HDAC6 inhibition did not influence zinc levels, demonstrating that zinc acts upstream of HDAC6. In conclusion, our findings identify a novel zinc-HDAC6-autophagy signaling axis underlying neuronal injury following cerebral I/R, suggesting that targeting zinc homeostasis or HDAC6 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.

items.title: Behavioral and motor deficits following traumatic brain injury: implications for post-traumatic epilepsy.
items.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a severe complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Patients with PTE often experience comorbid neurobehavioral deficits, which further reduce the quality of life and impede the recovery of patients. This review examines behavioral and motor deficits associated with PTE across clinical and preclinical studies, with an emphasis on the need to identify PTE-specific phenotypes that may serve as biomarkers of disease development and progression, as well as distinguish PTE from other forms of epilepsy. Despite growing evidence of post-TBI behavioral and motor abnormalities, their relationship with PTE remains unclear, particularly in preclinical models where direct comparisons are limited between animals that do and do not develop PTE. We further evaluate the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for characterizing these phenotypes throughout post-traumatic epileptogenesis, highlighting its potential to provide automated, objective, and sensitive measures of functional outcomes.

items.title: Brain-State-Resolved Consistency of Corticospinal Responses to TMS.
items.abstract: Background An important feature of motor-evoked potential (MEP) responses to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over the primary motor cortex (M1) is their substantial trial-to-trial variability. Ongoing brain activity at the time of TMS, such as the power and phase of the sensorimotor mu rhythm, influences MEP amplitude. It is unclear to what extent these endogenous brain states also shape the consistency of MEP amplitude across trials. Objectives We investigated trial-to-trial variability of MEP amplitude as a function of pre-stimulus mu dynamics. Methods Twenty-nine healthy participants received 1200 single TMS pulses over the left M1 during simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) recording; 10 participants completed two sessions to assess inter-session reproducibility. Trials were stratified based on pre-stimulus mu power, phase, and interhemispheric M1-M1 functional connectivity. Brain-state-resolved MEP variability was quantified using the coefficient of variation (CV) within subsets of trials defined by similar pre-stimulus mu dynamics. Results Trial subsets characterized by high mu power were associated with reduced MEP variability, indicating more consistent corticospinal output. In contrast, mu phase did not significantly influence MEP variability at the group level. Mu power group-level effects were reproducible across sessions in an exploratory test-retest analysis and across experimental sites. Conclusions We show that inter-trial consistency of MEP amplitude reflects a structured, brain-state-dependent feature of the sensorimotor network. These findings contribute to our mechanistic understanding of trial-to-trial variability in TMS-evoked responses. This may provide a basis for future TMS approaches aimed at reducing response variability and improving the consistency of neuromodulatory effects.

items.title: Systemic D1-like receptor activation during song exposure biases the emergence of song selectivity in the juvenile zebra finch NCM.
items.abstract: Vocal learning requires juveniles to form auditory representations of adult vocal models that guide vocal practice. The caudomedial nidopallium (NCM), a higher-order auditory pallial region in songbirds, has been implicated in tutor-song memory and receives dopaminergic input, but whether dopamine receptor activation biases the emergence of song-specific selectivity during development remains unclear. We recorded NCM single-unit activity in juvenile male zebra finches with limited tutor-song exposure. One adult song was repeatedly presented after systemic administration of the D1-like receptor agonist SKF-38393, the D2-like receptor agonist quinpirole, or saline, and neural selectivity was assessed before and after pairing. Pairing did not produce a uniform population-wide shift in average selectivity. However, a linear mixed-effects model accounting for pre-pairing selectivity and multiple units per bird revealed significantly higher post-pairing selectivity in SKF-treated units than in saline-treated units. SKF-treated units also differed from quinpirole-treated units, whereas quinpirole and saline did not differ. Among initially non-selective units, threshold-defined gains occurred in 31.3% of SKF, 15.4% of saline, and 10.8% of quinpirole units, with SKF showing the highest gained fraction across all tested thresholds. Although the exact bird-label permutation test was not significant, continuous and threshold-based analyses provided convergent unit-level evidence for an SKF-associated enhancement of paired-song selectivity. These findings support neuromodulatory gating as a potential mechanism by which developmental auditory experience shapes stimulus-specific sensory representations.

items.title: An MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for linking behavioral neurophysiology and stimulation-evoked fMRI in non-human primates.
items.abstract: Local electrophysiology and microstimulation reveal site-specific neural activity and physiological effects but do not directly link these local effects to whole-brain responses from the same target site. We developed an MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for macaques that enables CT/MRI-based localization, postoperative depth adjustment, neural recording, microstimulation during behavioral testing, and subsequent electrical microstimulation combined with functional MRI (EM-fMRI) using the same implanted electrode. The system supported local field potential recording, a stimulation-induced reduction in pupil size, and distributed stimulation-evoked blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) responses. This approach provides a practical framework for linking local neural activity and stimulation-induced physiological responses with whole-brain responses at the same target site.

items.title: Frustration Induction Alters Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Pediatric Irritability.
items.abstract: Background Irritability is a prevalent, impairing, transdiagnostic affective symptom domain in youth associated with elevated risk for adverse outcomes. Theoretical models of irritability implicate disruptions in reward learning and frustrative nonreward. This is the first study to investigate reward prediction error (RPE) signaling before and after frustration as a neural correlate of irritability. Methods We used reinforcement learning modeling to derive individualized trial-by-trial RPEs from behavior during a child-friendly, fMRI-based probabilistic reward learning task in 88 youth (M age =14.43 years, 48.86% female). Irritability severity varied across participants and was characterized dimensionally. Neural encoding of RPEs was examined across prefrontal, ventral striatal/pallidal, and insular regions of interest (ROIs). To test the impact of frustration, RPE-modulated BOLD activity was assessed before and after an acute frustration induction. Results Prior to frustration induction, higher irritability was associated with enhanced positive coupling between trial-by-trial RPEs and BOLD activity in the ventral striatal/pallidal ROI. Following frustration, this pattern reversed, such that higher irritability was associated with attenuated positive coupling between RPEs and BOLD activity in ventral striatal/pallidal and right insular areas, indicating decreased neural encoding of reward outcomes. Irritability was not associated with RPE-modulated orbitofrontal or left insular activity. Conclusion Findings provide computationally-grounded evidence linking youth irritability to altered neural RPE encoding during learning and a reversal following task-induced frustration. This emotional state-dependent change in RPE-BOLD coupling suggests that frustration disrupts the neural encoding of reward outcomes during reward learning in youth with elevated irritability and highlights a candidate target for interventions addressing frustration reactivity.

items.title: Infant Negative Affect During Mother-Infant Interaction Is Associated with Neonatal Limbic-Prefrontal Connectivity in the First Month of Life.
items.abstract: Background Early caregiving may shape neonatal limbic circuit organization, yet whether microanalytically coded interaction quality relates to neonatal limbic-prefrontal connectivity is unknown. We tested associations between infant and maternal affect during mother-infant interaction and neonatal limbic-prefrontal cortex (PFC) connectivity. Methods At approximately 30 days postnatal, 143 mother-infant dyads from the Healthy MiNDS cohort (São Paulo, Brazil) completed a video-recorded interaction coded with the Coding Interactive Behavior (CIB) system; infant negative affect was the percentage of interaction time in distress. Neonates underwent resting-state fMRI; limbic-PFC connectivity was quantified by principal component analysis of amygdala and hippocampus seed-to-ROI maps. Covariate-adjusted regressions tested associations. Results Infant negative affect was associated with right amygdala-PFC (β = -0.247, p = .003) and right hippocampus-PFC connectivity (β = -0.202, p = .021), both surviving FDR correction and robust across multiple analytic approaches. The amygdala association was limited to infant distress-related behaviors, whereas maternal positive expressiveness showed an independent, opposing association (β = 0.202, p = .019); no other CIB measure was significant. Exploratorily, connectivity was associated with sleep problems at 18-24 months in females (r = -.324, p = .030). Conclusions The emotional quality of early caregiving is associated with neonatal limbic circuit organization: infant distress is selectively associated with weaker amygdala-PFC connectivity, whereas maternal positive affect shows an independent opposing association. These findings identify the mother-infant relationship as a modifiable input to neonatal brain development.

items.title: Decoding individual differences in mental information from human brain responses predicted by deep neural networks.
items.abstract: Brain decoding using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has high potential for evaluating unobservable mental information that varies across individuals in everyday situations. Although estimating individual differences in mental information using brain decoding could be effective for social applications, especially in neuromarketing, the physical constraints and high costs of fMRI limit the practical application in real-world settings. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework to estimate individual differences in decodable mental information using brain responses predicted by deep neural networks (DNNs). In this framework, DNN-based models are trained to predict fMRI responses to natural movie scenes. Then, additional fMRI measurements are no longer required because mental information for new movie scenes can be decoded from the predicted responses instead of the measured ones. A large-scale analysis revealed that the proposed predicted-response decoding captures individual difference patterns consistent with those derived from conventional measured-response decoding across various cognitive domains. Of the 88 cognitive labels associated with movie scenes, individual difference patterns could be captured for more than 70% of the labels. This framework offers a promising approach for evaluating personal mental information with substantially reduced reliance on fMRI, thereby expanding the potential for social applications of brain decoding.

items.title: Neurodegeneration in Sub-Saharan Africa: Intersections of Biological Ageing, Genomic Diversity and the Lifetime Exposome.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are emerging as an important consequence of population ageing in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), but their scientific relevance extends beyond a projected rise in case numbers. SSA combines exceptional human genomic diversity with marked heterogeneity in vascular and metabolic risk, infection, nutrition, occupational exposures, air pollution, and access to health care. This combination creates an underused setting in which to study why biological ageing produces neurodegeneration in some individuals but relative resilience in others. This review critically synthesises evidence on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis/frontotemporal degeneration, Huntington's disease and related disorders, focusing on the intersection between hallmarks of ageing, disease-specific proteinopathies, ancestry and the lifetime exposome. Age-associated loss of proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired autophagy, chronic inflammation, neurovascular injury and genomic/epigenomic instability provide a mechanistic scaffold on which genetic susceptibility and cumulative exposures may act. Yet African evidence remains dominated by cross-sectional clinical phenotyping; neuropathology, longitudinal biomarkers, multi-omics and measured environmental exposures remain sparse. Recent African-ancestry Parkinson's disease genomics and emerging plasma biomarker studies demonstrate that ancestry-inclusive molecular neuroscience is feasible and can generate findings not predictable from European-ancestry datasets. The next phase should therefore move beyond documenting underdiagnosis toward longitudinal, biologically anchored cohorts that integrate phenotype, genomics, blood biomarkers, neuroimaging, exposomics, digital measures and health-system outcomes. This review proposes a research framework centred on biological ageing, gene-environment interaction and resilience. Such work would improve the validity of prevention, diagnosis and therapeutic translation in African populations while contributing globally to a more complete biology of neurodegenerative ageing.

items.title: Redefining chronic pain models: what should we model?
items.abstract: Chronic pain is generally defined as pain that persists or recurs for more than 3 months. However, its pathogenesis cannot be fully explained solely by ongoing tissue injury or inflammation. Conventional inflammatory and neuropathic pain models have greatly advanced our understanding of pain hypersensitivity and its underlying mechanisms. Clinically, many patients experience persistent pain despite minimal peripheral pathology. These observations underscore the need for experimental models that better reflect the mechanisms of pain chronification and recurrence. Recent advances in research on central sensitization, hyperalgesic priming, and latent sensitization support the view that chronic pain involves persistent neuroplastic changes. In some chronic pain conditions, these changes may persist even after the initial injury or inflammation has resolved, suggesting that chronic pain may involve a form of "pain memory" encoded within the nervous system. This review outlines the limitations of conventional pain models and focuses on persistent sensitization models, particularly hyperalgesic priming and latent sensitization. Considering chronic pain as a manifestation of persistent neuroplastic changes, we summarize the experimental features and pathophysiological significance and discuss their relevance to chronic pain conditions that are difficult to explain solely by ongoing inflammation or nerve injury, including nociplastic pain-related conditions. Finally, we argue that future chronic pain models should aim to reproduce persistent neural states that drive pain chronification, maintenance, and recurrence rather than pain hypersensitivity alone. This approach may help bridge the translational gap between preclinical and clinical pain research and facilitate the development of more effective therapies.

items.title: Dynamic Thresholds and Spatial Boundaries Coordinate Memory Association and Discrimination Across Scales.
items.abstract: The ability to connect related experiences while preserving their individual identities is a central requirement of adaptive behavior. Engram overlap offers a cellular substrate for memory linking, but overlap must be regulated: too little prevents integration, whereas too much promotes generalization, interference, and confusion. Here, we organize evidence across molecular, cellular, glial, circuit, and systems levels around a common association-discrimination problem. We distinguish prospective linking, in which temporally adjacent experiences are biased toward shared neuronal allocation during a transient excitability window, from retrospective linking, in which memories separated in time are integrated through replay and cross-regional coordination. Within this framework, CREB- and CCR5-associated excitability states and inhibitory microcircuits set dynamic thresholds that regulate the timing and extent of neuronal recruitment; dendritic compartmentalization and branch-specific plasticity help preserve event-specific information within shared neurons; and representational drift may provide temporal decorrelation across repeated experiences. We further evaluate emerging evidence that learning-associated astrocyte ensembles, perisynaptic processes, calcium dynamics, and metabolic coupling help set the spatial boundaries of plasticity, while emphasizing that a direct role in defining engram boundaries remains a testable hypothesis. Together, these mechanisms form a Memory Engram Association Network that links neural organization to behavioral outcomes including integration, discrimination, generalization, and interference. This framework identifies experimentally separable mechanisms and shows how their disruption may contribute to age- and disease-related cognitive dysfunction. As this evidence is predominantly rodent-derived, we review the human literature on generalization, interference, and integration separately and frame the clinical extensions, including neurorehabilitation, as predictions awaiting human test.

items.title: Long-term cervical sagittal balance after single-level anterior cervical discectomy with or without fusion or arthroplasty: sex-specific changes in cervical alignment over 5 years.
items.abstract: Background context Cervical sagittal balance influences spinal biomechanics and may be affected by anterior cervical discectomy (ACD), potentially affecting clinical outcomes. Purpose To evaluate longitudinal changes in cervical sagittal alignment over 5 years following single-level ACD with or without fusion or arthroplasty and assess associations with clinical outcomes. Study design Post hoc analysis of the Netherlands Cervical Kinematics (NECK) trial (NTR1289). Patient sample Patients undergoing single-level ACD with or without fusion or arthroplasty for cervical radiculopathy were evaluated at baseline, 1-, 2-, and 5-years follow-up. Outcome measures C0-C2 angle, C2-C7 Cobb angle, segmental Cobb angle, C7 angle, T1 angle, T1-CL (T1 angle minus C2-C7 lordosis) and C2-C7 sagittal vertical axis (SVA) were measured on lateral radiographs. Clinical outcomes included the Neck Disability Index (NDI) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for arm and neck pain. Methods Linear mixed models assessed longitudinal changes, corrected for potential confounders. Linear regression evaluated associations between alignment and clinical outcomes. Results Out of 109 enrolled patients, 81 patients had a lateral X-ray available at baseline. C2-C7 Cobb angle increased from 9.0° at baseline to 13.8°, 12.3°, and 13.6° at 1-, 2-, and 5-year follow-up (p Conclusions Single-level ACD with or without fusion or arthroplasty is associated with long-term increases in cervical lordosis with sex-specific compensatory patterns. Alignment-outcome cross-sectional associations were limited to early follow-up, suggesting that restoring adequate segmental lordosis at surgery may reduce early postoperative arm pain.

items.title: Circulating immune cells phenotypes discriminate bipolar disorder from major depressive disorder during a depressive episode: A machine learning elastic-net approach.
items.abstract: MDD and BD are characterized by differences in peripheral immune markers, in frequencies of T helper, T cytotoxic, Natural Killer (NK) and T regulatory cells that may contribute to the development of mood disorders. However, few studies have used immune cells populations to discriminate MDD from BD with inconsistent findings. We applied an elastic-net machine learning pipeline predictive model using 5-fold nested cross-validation based on a wide panel of immune cell populations to discriminate between MDD and BD. The sample included 124 MDD and 89 BD hospitalised for depressive episode, and 40 healthy controls (HC). The predictive model achieved an accuracy of 78%, with 76% sensitivity, 80% specificity. The model performed significantly better than chance (p + IFN-γ, CD4 + IL-17, CD4 + TNF-α, CD8 + TNF-α, NK cells/TNF-α), and regulatory cells (FOXP3), whereas MDD diagnosis was associated with elevated frequencies of early activating memory cells both T helper and cytotoxic (i.e. CD4 + CM/CD69 + , CD4 + EM/CD69 + , CD8 + CM/CD69 + ), and cytotoxic effector cells producing apoptotic proteins (CD8 + EM/Perf + GrzB + , NK cells/Perf + GrzB + ). Excluding patients in lithium only early activated and cytotoxic cells differentiated the two diagnoses. Limitations include possible residual instrument-related effects and cryopreservation effects, lack of generalization to other phases of the illness, lack of external validation. Our data confirm that MDD and BD show different immune signatures and suggest a more pronounced alteration of immune cell populations in MDD especially in cytotoxic CD8+ cells. Future studies should address these differences to develop more effective therapies for mood disorders.

items.title: An accidental ultrasonic noise source in the mouse facility activating a band of neurons in the inferior colliculus.
items.abstract: Experimental animals are housed under tightly regulated conditions to standardize experiments and minimize the number of animals per experiment. Ultrasonic noise pollution is a potential problem in housing as it is inaudible for humans, and may thus remain undetected, whereas most laboratory animals can hear ultrasound. Compared with sounds audible to humans, ultrasonic noise has received much less attention, yet it can likewise induce physiological and behavioral effects in animals, including deleterious effects on welfare and on experimental reproducibility. In this study, we accidentally discovered that our mouse stable was polluted by an ultrasonic beep emitted by a radio. To investigate the impact of this beep, we tested under which conditions this beep would activate neurons in the inferior colliculus (IC) using the c-fos promotor in TRAP2 mice as a marker for activation. Exposure to the beep of the radio activated a band of neurons. A similar band was observed in the TRAP2 mice following exposure to a beep with the same frequency as the radio beep, and the location of the bands in both cases agreed with the tonotopic organization of the IC. A similar ultrasonic tone was observed in more than half of commercially available radios, indicating that the presence of a radio is likely to expose animals to a continuous tone that is inaudible to humans. Based on our findings, we therefore recommend that animal facilities routinely check for ultrasonic noise contamination to increase animal welfare and enhance study reproducibility.

items.title: Dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal graph fusion for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
items.abstract: Multi-modal fusion methods have demonstrated potential in integrating complementary information from different data modalities. However, existing methods often rely on static fusion strategies, failing to capture the heterogeneous interactions across modalities. To address this challenge, we propose the dynamic multi-scale topology learning and cross-modal interaction graph fusion network (DMTL-Net) for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) diagnosis. The model is designed to extract distinctive and complementary features from brain functional and structural networks while capturing their dynamic topological organization. Specifically, the structural radiomics similarity network (RSN) and functional connectivity network (FCN) are constructed from structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), respectively. Multi-modal graph initialization is performed by the cross-modal inclusive integration and consensus filtering to balance sensitivity and specificity. Then we propose the dynamic topology learning mechanism that integrates multi-scale feature extraction with adaptive channel-wise and spatial-wise fusion, effectively capturing complex inter-modal interactions. Additionally, focal loss is used to reduce the contribution of easy-to-classify samples and emphasize hard examples during optimization. Evaluated on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange dataset, the proposed DMTL-Net demonstrates superior performance and consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: State transitions in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: mechanistic convergence and biomarker-guided stratification.
items.abstract: Background Biological heterogeneity is a major obstacle to therapeutic development in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Cross-sectional pathway labels do not show whether a mechanism is active or treatment-relevant in an individual patient. Methods We conducted a structured critical narrative review informed by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and CENTRAL were searched for English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 to 7 August 2026; seminal earlier studies were identified by citation tracking. Human genetic, pathological, longitudinal biomarker, multi-omic, imaging, neurophysiological, and interventional evidence was prioritized. Evidence was appraised by human proximity, temporality, replication, mechanistic specificity, and treatment relevance. Results Evidence supports interacting RNA/proteostasis, nucleocytoplasmic-transport, glial-inflammatory, and energetic-metabolic processes, but current evidence does not yet support the use of any candidate state for individual treatment assignment. The most mature temporal example is loss of TDP-43 splicing repression before neurofilament elevation in genetically at-risk individuals. Nucleocytoplasmic-transport evidence is strongest in C9orf72 disease; inflammatory and metabolic signals are confounded by disease burden and systemic illness; and the gut-brain axis remains a context-dependent amplifier. We propose prespecified transition rules, evidence grades, and biomarker-by-treatment interaction tests. Conclusions A state-transition model becomes clinically useful when longitudinal measurements add value beyond clinical predictors and injury markers and prospectively identify differential treatment benefit.
