items.title: On-Site, Highly Sensitive, and Multisignal Detection of Cucumber Bacteria via CRISPR/Cas12a Coupled with Duplex Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.
items.abstract: Pseudomonas amygdali pv. lachrymans (Pal) and Pectobacterium brasiliense (Pb) are highly destructive bacterial pathogens that cause severe oozy diseases in cucumber crops, often resulting in significant yield losses. Rapid and accurate detection is essential for effective disease management, yet current molecular detection methods are limited by their reliance on sophisticated instrumentation, time-consuming procedures, and laboratory-dependent operations, significantly limiting their practicality in field settings. To address these limitations, we developed a portable detection platform that integrates dual recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a technology. This system demonstrated exceptional sensitivity with a detection limit of 10 -5 ng/μl for both Pal and Pb while exhibiting high specificity and enabling multisignal output capabilities. For rapid on-site detection, we further developed a portable device integrating a heating unit and a blue light-excited fluorescence detection system, coupled with a smartphone-based readout for high-throughput field testing. The entire process was completed within 1 h. This platform not only provides a powerful tool for rapid field detection of plant pathogens but also pioneers a novel universal nucleic acid detection strategy with broad application prospects in point-of-care molecular diagnostics across healthcare, agriculture, and other fields. By bridging the gap between laboratory precision and field practicality, this technology opens new avenues for decentralized diagnostics in crop protection, microbial ecology, and public health.

items.title: Aggression in children and adolescents: A practical approach to assessment and treatment.
items.abstract: Aggression is a common and challenging presentation in pediatric practice and may arise from a wide variety of developmental, medical, psychiatric, relational, and environmental factors. Although immediate safety must be addressed when aggressive behavior creates a risk of harm, aggression is a symptom rather than a diagnosis. Effective treatment depends on understanding what is contributing to and maintaining the behavior in an individual child. This review provides a practical approach to the assessment and treatment of aggression in children and adolescents. Assessment begins by characterizing the behavior, evaluating safety, considering the child's developmental capacities, and identifying biological, psychological, and social contributors. These factors can be integrated into a working formulation that considers what predisposed the child to aggression, what precipitated it now, what may be perpetuating it, and what protective factors can support treatment. Treatment should address the factors identified by this assessment, including modifiable environmental and developmental factors, caregiver needs, underlying medical, neurodevelopmental, and psychiatric conditions, and indications for evidence-based behavioral and psychotherapeutic interventions. Medication should likewise target identified conditions whenever possible; medication directed more specifically toward persistent aggression requires careful consideration of expected benefit and potential harm. Treatment intensity should be matched to safety, functional impairment, caregiver capacity, developmental needs, and available supports. The pediatrician can remain central to care by coordinating appropriate consultation, monitoring transitions across levels of care, and revisiting the child's needs as development and circumstances change.

items.title: Daily Adherence and Barriers to Physical Exercise in Esports Athletes: A 30-Day Diary Study.
items.abstract: Background/objectives Regular physical exercise (PE) may enhance health and performance in competitive gaming and esports, yet sustained engagement remains challenging. This study examined adherence patterns and factors associated with PE behaviour over time, with a specific focus on barriers and prospective confidence. Methods Eighteen club-affiliated competitive players completed a 30-day diary protocol. Participants were instructed to perform structured high-intensity interval sessions at least three times per week. Daily entries captured planned exercise, completion (full/partial vs. none), barriers (multiple selections possible), confidence for the next session (0-10), and additional PEs. Analyses were conducted on days with planned sessions using generalised linear mixed models with a binary adherence outcome (completed vs. not completed), accounting for repeated measures within individuals. Results Across 239 planned sessions, 47.7% were completed and adherence showed substantial within- and between-person variability. Higher prospective confidence was positively associated with completion. Time constraints emerged as the most frequently reported barrier and showed negative associations with adherence. Engagement in additional PE on the same day showed no consistent association with adherence. Descriptive findings indicated moderate-to-high variability in perceived PE benefits and responses to exercise. Discussion Adherence to structured PE in competitive gaming contexts is highly dynamic and associated with both self-regulatory (confidence) and situational (barriers) factors. The findings suggest that barrier management and self-regulatory processes may represent relevant targets for future interventions. The findings highlight the importance of within-person approaches when evaluating PE behaviour in this population.

items.title: The Visual Cortex and Beyond: Investigating Long-Term Cortical Plasticity Following Monocular Deprivation.
items.abstract: Aim To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. Methods In this single-arm longitudinal study, 21 healthy adults underwent five structural MRI sessions: at baseline, during MD on days 1, 3 and 5, and after a seven-day recovery period (day 12). MD was induced by occluding the right eye with a translucent eye patch for five consecutive days. Grey matter volume (GMV) changes were analysed using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain effects and generalised estimating equations (GEE) to model temporal trajectories in predefined cortical and subcortical regions. Results Ultra-long MD induced dynamic GMV changes in primary and higher visual cortices, with exploratory changes also in subcortical and cerebellar structures. VBM showed cumulative volume increases in bilateral occipital cortex, including calcarine, lateral occipital and fusiform regions, and adjacent cerebellar lobules, peaking between days 3 and 5. Region-wise modelling resolved the temporal build-up of these changes across visual, subcortical and sensorimotor regions; after correction for multiple comparisons, a time-dependent effect remained in occipital and ventral occipito-temporal cortex (occipital pole, fusiform and calcarine cortex), converging with the voxel-wise result. Following binocular restoration, an exploratory GMV decrease was observed selectively in the left middle occipital gyrus, while an exploratory increase was observed in the left hippocampus, compatible with persistent plasticity in associative memory networks. Conclusion Prolonged sensory imbalance via ultra-long MD induces rapid, region-specific and possibly persistent GMV plasticity in the adult brain. These changes follow temporally stratified trajectories across visual, subcortical and integrative systems, consistent with models of homeostatic and hierarchical plasticity. Corrected evidence supports cumulative occipital plasticity during deprivation; whether the exploratory extra-visual and post-recovery changes reflect persistent adaptation requires confirmation. MD-based paradigms thus offer a controlled window on structural plasticity in both healthy individuals and clinical populations.

items.title: Sequential accumulation of independent cultural traits: A Gaussian limit for the popularity spectrum.
items.abstract: Cultural traits, unlike genes, are acquired sequentially across and within individuals' lifetimes through repeated learning, innovation, and loss. While many tractable neutral models of cultural evolution assume one-shot acquisition, in which an individual's repertoire is fixed when it enters the population, we study a neutral model in which long-lived individuals in a fixed population repeatedly copy traits from one another and occasionally forget them, so that cultural turnover is driven by learning and forgetting within lifetimes rather than by births and deaths. The process admits a unique limiting distribution, with a stationary trait popularity spectrum in closed form. When the social learning efficiency is subcritical, the spectrum is monotone and total cultural diversity grows linearly with population size. Above the critical value the spectrum concentrates around an intermediate frequency and diversity grows exponentially with population size. Our main result concerns this supercritical regime: we prove that the spectrum is asymptotically Gaussian, with explicit mean, width, height and error bounds, and from this we derive the asymptotic behaviour of cultural diversity at the population and individual levels and of the time to stationarity. The same spectrum arises in the group-level model of Nakamura et al. (2020), so the shape of a spectrum does not by itself identify the mechanism behind it. Because the supercritical regime arises whenever individuals get more than one chance to acquire a trait, intermediate-peaked popularity distributions and abundant shared culture need not by themselves be read as evidence of biased or selective transmission.

items.title: The Spectrum within the Spectrum: Neural Heterogeneity in Autism.
items.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) encompasses diverse behavioral, cognitive, and neural profiles that vary widely across individuals. Because diagnosis remains predominantly behavior-based, clinically meaningful within-spectrum differences are often missed. Recent advances in neuroimaging analysis have created opportunities for the identification of distinct neural profiles within ASD. These new avenues provide ways to examine intra-ASD heterogeneity directly, identifying person-specific brain-behavior patterns that group-level comparisons fail to capture. The present systematic review focused on neuroimaging methods (i.e., resting-state fMRI; rs-fMRI, cortical morphology) that emphasized heterogeneity-informed outcomes based on normative modeling, data-driven subtyping, clustering analysis and similar analytic choices. For rs-fMRI, findings showed that differences in connectivity within the default mode and salience networks were linked to social-communication and language impairments, with subtype-specific patterns emerging across samples. In cortical thickness and surface area, studies identified distinct developmental trajectories and individual deviation profiles, with prefrontal and temporal regions often tied to repetitive behaviors and social-communication difficulties. Voxel-based analyses revealed subgroup-specific gray matter alterations, including cerebellar and cortical differences, that aligned with variation in repetitive behaviors and social difficulties. Collectively, this emerging evidence supports the notion that neural heterogeneity in autism is a core feature rather than a limitation. Embracing individual variability can provide crucial insight into the inconsistencies and contradictions of earlier case-control and group-level findings. Moving forward, autism research must prioritize heterogeneity-based methods to establish reproducible subtypes and individualized brain-behavior links.

items.title: When emotion meets conflict: Additive but not synergistic effects in neural oscillatory activity.
items.abstract: Cognitive control allows individuals to regulate their behavior in the face of conflicting or distracting information. Growing evidence suggests that emotional states-particularly self-related emotions-can modulate these control processes. This study explored neural mechanisms underlying amplification of the conflict-adaptation effect (CAE) by self-related emotions, replicating Landman and van Steenbergen (2020). Electroencephalogram (EEG) data were analyzed during two successive trials (Trial N-1 and Trial N) in a prime-probe task. Corrugator muscle activity was also measured as an index of emotional valence. Orthogonal to conflict, word emotion (unpleasant and neutral) and its social context (self- and sender-related) were manipulated. We hypothesized that the emotional facilitation of conflict adaptation by self-related emotional words in Trial N-1 is driven by an affective amplification of conflict-related brain signals. Our behavioral results revealed that emotional words tended to increase CAE, but this effect was threshold-dependent and we failed to replicate the moderation by social context. At the neural level, we replicated earlier results related to conflict and cognitive control; conflict induced early theta synchronization in fronto-central areas and late alpha desynchronization in centro-parietal areas during Trial N-1. Those oscillations showed CAE patterns mirroring the behavioral effect in Trial N. Incongruence increased corrugator activity, indicating that conflict induced unpleasant emotion. Emotion induced neural modulation overlapping with the conflict processing observed in the theta and alpha frequency ranges, suggesting additive but not synergistic effects. Our results reveal neural modulation by conflict and emotional words that might provide input for downstream processes that integrate these signals to drive emotional modulation of behavioral adaptation.

items.title: Person-oriented and context-oriented goals in job coaching at the workplace.
items.abstract: Purpose The aim of this job coaching study was to explore and describe goals of coachees (employees with a severe disability) and the companies they were employed in by examining goals, whether these changed from beginning to end, and if these were reached or skipped. Methods Sixty-two case files of job coaching were analysed qualitatively. Job coaching is an intervention on the job for employees with severe disabilities. The intervention had a duration of several months, and included training of the person as well as adjustment of the workplace. Goals were formulated by the coach in the beginning, during the intervention and at the end of job coaching. A deductive-inductive analysis based on Mayring was conducted to classify and quantify the expressed goals. Results A total of 370 goals were classified into 13 categories, within two overarching dimensions: context-oriented and person (i.e. coachee)-oriented goals. These goals covered a wide range of topics, with most goals focusing on mastering work (task) (24.55%), followed by workplace & task adaption (12,42%). Conclusions Despite the fact that job coaching is person-focused, especially on work tasks, context aspects such as work environment and team communication need to be addressed, in order to ensure work integration.

items.title: "Aging-out" of the out-of-home care system: What young people and carers say helps and hinders this transition.
items.abstract: Background The transition from the formal out-of-home care system at 18 years old can be a time of significant upheaval for young people, with well-documented consequences for their wellbeing. Yet, few studies have captured young people and caregivers' perspectives on what might help or hinder this transition, particularly drawing on views both before and after this change. Objective To explore young people's and caregivers' views on what helped and hindered over this leaving-care transition. Participants and setting At baseline, participants were 25 17-year-olds, all in formal out-of-home care in England or Wales. For 13 of these participants, their caregiver also participated. Method Semi-structured interviews were conducted approximately 12 months apart, before and soon after young people turned 18 years old and thus transitioned out of the formal care system. Framework analysis was used to identify risk and protective factors at the systemic, social, and individual levels. Results Eight themes were grouped into three overarching areas: 1. Resourced, consistent, and accurate information-sharing and professional support systems; 2. Social networks and relational stability; and 3. Young people's sense of agency and coping. Interactions across systemic, relational, and individual factors were reported to influence young people's wellbeing across the transition. Conclusion Findings underscore the importance of timely, accurate guidance, early and consistent professional involvement, and policies that prioritise relational continuity into early adulthood. As UK policy increasingly emphasises relationship-based practice, this study provides insights into how out-of-care transitions at 18 can be better supported to promote the wellbeing of these young people.

items.title: The association between self-compassion and self-control: Parallel indirect roles of resilience and narcissism.
items.abstract: Although self-compassion has been linked to self-control, little is known about the psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship. This cross-sectional study examined whether resilience and pathological narcissism statistically mediate the association between self-compassion and self-control in a sample of 3766 Chinese undergraduates (Mage = 18.74, SD = 1.42). Parallel mediation analyses revealed significant indirect effects via resilience (indirect effect = 0.05, 95% CI = [0.04, 0.06], accounting for 11.2% of the total effect) and via pathological narcissism (indirect effect = 0.09, 95% CI = [0.07, 0.10], accounting for 20.2%). Specifically, self-compassion was positively associated with resilience, which in turn predicted higher self-control. For the narcissism pathway, self-compassion was negatively associated with narcissism, which, in turn, negatively predicts self-control. These findings suggest that resilience and pathological narcissism may help explain how self-compassion relates to self-control.

items.title: Artificial intelligence adoption and employee well-being: A job demands-resources perspective from academia and practice (scoping review).
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into workplaces is reshaping work design by augmenting, automating, and reconfiguring human work, with important implications for employee engagement and experience. While Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory provides a robust psychological framework for understanding how work characteristics influence wellbeing, insights into how AI alters demands, resources, and organisational dynamics remain fragmented across academic research and organisational practice. This scoping review synthesises academic and practitioner literature to examine how AI adoption is associated with employee engagement and wellbeing through a JD-R lens and to identify convergences and gaps between these perspectives. Guided by established scoping review approaches, academic and grey literature published since 2001 were systematically identified, screened, and synthesised. Forty-eight sources from 2019 to 2025 were included, comprising 35 academic studies and 13 practitioner publications. The literature predominantly emphasised strain-related outcomes such as stress and burnout, whereas work engagement received comparatively limited attention. Research addressing personal resources, work design factors, and proactive employee behaviours, particularly job crafting, was scarce. Integrating evidence across domains, the review conceptualises AI-enabled work as a dynamic and ambivalent work characteristic that may simultaneously generate demands and resources. The review frames job crafting as an emerging and theoretically promising mechanism through which employees may shape AI-enabled work to balance demands and resources and sustain engagement. Advancing psychologically sustainable AI-enabled work therefore requires closer and more purposeful scholar-practitioner collaboration, ensuring that theoretical insight and organisational experience jointly inform the design, implementation, and governance of AI-related work systems.

items.title: Emergency department use disparities in schizophrenia: Mediating role of antipsychotic availability and administration.
items.abstract: Racial disparities in emergency department (ED) use among patients with schizophrenia may reflect differences in treatment access and continuity after antipsychotic initiation. We examined whether oral antipsychotic availability or administering long-acting injectable antipsychotics, measured by proportion of days covered (PDC) using claims data, mediated the association between race and ED use and whether mediation differed by antipsychotic class and route of administration. Using South Carolina Medicaid claims from 2004 to 2019, we identified 1666 adults with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder initiating antipsychotic treatment with 12-month washout period. PDC was measured during the first 6 months after treatment initiation. The outcome was any ED visit during the subsequent 6 months. Mediation analysis was conducted overall and by antipsychotic subgroup. Black beneficiaries had higher ED use than White beneficiaries (33% vs. 27%, p = 0.03) and lower PDC (mean 0.45 vs. 0.55, p < 0.0001). In unadjusted analyses, PDC mediated 23% of the association between race and ED use (95% CI 8%-94%, p = 0.03). After covariate adjustment, PDC mediated 25% of the association (95% CI 10%-95%, p = 0.006). Significant mediation was observed among oral antipsychotic users (28%, p = 0.02), second-generation antipsychotic users (29%, p = 0.008), and most prominently in oral second-generation antipsychotic users (30%, p = 0.006). No significant mediation was observed among first-generation antipsychotic or long-acting injectable users. These findings suggest that antipsychotic availability and administration may be one pathway contributing to racial disparities in acute psychiatric care.

items.title: Wound problems and infections after major joint arthroplasty : national survey results from primary and secondary care in the UK.
items.abstract: Aims Early postoperative wound problems following major joint arthroplasty (MJA) are common, yet comprehensive guidelines for superficial surgical site infections (SSIs) are lacking. This study aimed to explore healthcare professionals' views and management strategies for early wound problems after MJA. Methods A national cross-sectional online survey was distributed to orthopaedic surgeons, microbiologists, general practitioners, physiotherapists, and nursing staff involved in MJA care. The survey explored perceptions of wound problems, along with diagnostic and management approaches, and sought to identify any evidence gaps. Results were reported with descriptive statistics. Results Of 111 respondents (51% orthopaedic surgeons), 90% were involved in managing early MJA wound problems. Most (94.6%) considered early wound problems serious. Skin reactions (32.4%) and superficial wound infections (28.8%) were the most frequently cited causes. Respondents generally believed superficial infections could not be clinically distinguished from deep infections, but could be managed with oral antibiotics in primary care. However, a need for further evidence was expressed, particularly regarding diagnostic utility, intervention thresholds, and clear guidelines to differentiate superficial from deep infections. Common superficial infection signs included red skin and localized swelling, while deep infections were thought to present with fever and deep pain. Conclusion Healthcare professionals recognize the seriousness of early postoperative wound problems, frequently encountering skin reactions and superficial SSIs. While superficial infections are often managed nonoperatively, there is a clear demand for high-level evidence and comprehensive guidelines to improve differentiation and management. This should ultimately enhance patient outcomes, reduce the time to correct diagnosis and management, and limit the need for unnecessary treatments and associated complications.

items.title: Feasibility of a Co-Designed Personalized Cognitive Reablement Program Delivered via Digital Voice Assistants for Older Adults Living With Early-Stage Dementia or Mild Cognitive Impairment: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Background Home-based reablement programs have improved everyday functioning for people living with early-stage dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the substantial time commitment required for delivery by health professionals has created a barrier to widespread implementation. Digital technology could facilitate delivery, but traditional devices such as smartphones and tablets present usability challenges for this population. We have co-designed a cognitive reablement program, VOICE-COG, that can deliver personalized interventions broadcast via voice-controlled digital voice assistants (DVAs). Objective This pilot nonblinded randomized controlled trial examined the feasibility and potential effectiveness of VOICE-COG for older adults living with dementia or MCI to guide the design of a full-scale trial. Methods Older adults (aged 60-85 years) with a self-reported diagnosis of dementia or MCI (N=30) were recruited via Facebook or the StepUp-for Dementia Research database and randomized to either a DVA intervention (n=15) or control (n=15) group for 12 weeks. Each participant randomized to the intervention group and their care partner met with a psychologist via Zoom to select 2 or 3 personalized goals from the VOICE-COG program. The personalized program was input into the software (BuddyLink) by researchers for broadcast via a DVA (Amazon Alexa Show 8). Participants in the control group received enhanced usual care, consisting of treatment as usual, plus weekly informational emails. Primary feasibility outcomes were recruitment, retention, device-recorded adherence, and the System Usability Scale (SUS). Secondary outcomes were self-reported by the participant and care partner via web-based Qualtrics forms and included the Goal Attainment Scale-Light (GAS), changes in participant mood, cognition, and everyday functioning, and carer burden. Results The recruitment rate was 86% (30/35) and the retention rate was 97% (29/30), with 1 participant in the intervention group lost to follow-up. Adherence to the VOICE-COG program ranged from 29% to 100% (mean 70%, SD 17%). The VOICE-COG program was rated as marginally acceptable (mean SUS score 56.3, SD 18.1). After 12 weeks, 60% (9/15) of the intervention group reported having met or exceeded their goals (GAS-Light t-score ≥50; mean 57.6, SD 15.4). The intervention group had a significantly higher increase in Multifactorial Memory Questionnaire-Strategy subscale score compared with control, mean difference 5.0 (95% CI 0.03-10.1, P =.049), representing a medium effect size ( d =0.55). There were no other significant differences between groups. Conclusions This co-designed VOICE-COG program, delivered via DVAs, was feasible for older adults living with early-stage dementia or MCI, resulting in most participants meeting their reablement goals and increases in the use of memory strategies. System usability issues should be addressed in future adequately powered trials.

items.title: Vaping and smoking as risk factors for arthritis: Evidence from double machine learning.
items.abstract: Smoking is a well-documented risk factor for chronic diseases, including arthritis. Vaping, often marketed as a safer alternative, has risen sharply, yet its implications for musculoskeletal health remain unclear. We examine the associations of vaping and smoking with arthritis using Double Machine Learning (DML), and present illustrative economic scenarios projecting the potential cost implications of arthritis cases associated with these behaviors. Data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), collected in the United States, for adults aged 18-64 years (N = 36,768) is used. Arthritis is the outcome variable; vaping and smoking are the exposure variables, with estimates conditioned on twenty-seven demographic, behavioral, and health-related covariates (See Table 1). Results show that vaping is associated with a 2.12 percentage point higher prevalence of arthritis than among non-vapers, while smoking is associated with a 2.22 percentage points increase compared with non-smokers. When accounting for concurrent nicotine behaviors, the estimated associations remain largely stable, with smoking exhibiting a slightly larger estimate of 2.14 percentage points while vaping attenuated to 1.91 percentage points. Vaping was estimated to be associated with approximately 190,581-254,109 arthritis cases annually, corresponding to a potential economic cost projection of $133.4--$177.9 million. Smoking was statistically associated with approximately 518,886-687,413 cases, corresponding to $363.2 -$481.2 million. Combined, the projected economic burden associated with vaping and smoking was approximately $496.6-$659.1 million annually under conservative assumptions. Relative to published estimates of the total U.S. arthritis burden, these projections represent approximately 0.09%-0.22% of arthritis-related expenditures under direct healthcare cost assumptions and up to 9.23% when broader indirect and societal costs are considered. Our findings suggest that vaping is associated with musculoskeletal risk comparable to, or potentially exceeding, that of smoking, and do not support the perception of vaping as a risk-free alternative. The illustrative projections may inform policy discussions on vaping and smoking in relation to the broader arthritis-related health and economic burden.

items.title: The composition of energy flow in the upper extremity under different lower extremity mechanics in baseball pitching.
items.abstract: Generating high ball speed is crucial for achieving competitive baseball pitching performance. The lower extremity mechanics play a key role in generating high ball speed during a baseball pitch. However, some previous studies have reported no significant difference in ball speeds despite differences in lower extremity mechanics, highlighting the need to examine how energy is transferred through the upper extremity to the ball under these conditions. This study examined how upper extremity energy flow differed across stride-length conditions in relation to the observed differences in ball speed. Twenty college baseball pitchers pitched with under-stride length (US) and over-stride length (OS) in addition to normal-stride length (NS). We analyzed the mechanical energy of the upper extremity segments at key events during pitching, and the energy flow through each joint between events. The mechanical energy in the proximal segments at the stride foot contact increased as the stride length extended. In contrast, the mechanical energy in the distal segments at maximum external rotation in the shoulder joint was greater in the NS than in the US and OS, consistent with ball speed differences. During this phase, the energy flow to the upper arm through the shoulder joint was greater in the NS than in the US and OS, and the same condition pattern was observed for energy transfer through the elbow and wrist joints and for ball speed. Additionally, although no statistically significant difference in ball speed was observed between the US and OS, the JFP and STP components of shoulder energy flow showed different condition patterns, suggesting that shoulder energy flow composition may differ even when no statistically significant difference is observed in total energy flow into the upper arm.

items.title: Factors influencing elderly people's intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps: Quantitative research.
items.abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people's intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users' data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users' perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users' intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = -0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users' intentions to adopt mHealth apps.

items.title: Histological and ultrastructural examination of immune cells in the gill epithelium of the silver carp (Hypophtalmichthys molitrix).
items.abstract: Fish use their mucosal barriers to interact with their surroundings while maintaining homeostasis. Gill-associated lymphoid tissue (GIALT) provides an important initial line of defense against waterborne infections. We examined the morphology and ultrastructural characteristics of immune cells in the branchial epithelium of silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix) using histology and transmission electron microscopy. We processed samples from silver carp (n = 10) for semi-thin sectioning and transmission electron microscopy. We stained semi-thin sections with toluidine blue and methylene blue and ultrathin sections with uranyl acetate and lead citrate. We identified several immune cell types in the gill mucosa, including polymorphonuclear leukocytes with multilobed nuclei and three granule types: eosinophilic granular cells with crystalloid cores in their specific granules, and rodlet cells at granular and mature developmental stages. We identified mononuclear phagocytes (macrophages) in the lamina propria and gill lumen. In the basal and intermediate layers of the branchial epithelium, we observed cells with abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum and endo-lysosomal systems. We also observed apoptotic characteristics in the surface layer, including chromatin condensation and the expansion of rough endoplasmic reticulum. Our findings illustrate the complex cellular architecture of the branchial mucosal immune barrier in silver carp and establish a morphological basis for understanding the cellular components that influence gill-associated immunity.

items.title: Fish intake and mortality in Japan, a high fish-consuming country: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies.
items.abstract: Fish consumption has been linked to decreased mortality risk in several prospective studies. However, most existing evidence is based on multi-regional analyses, and the dose-response relationship in populations with high habitual fish intake remains insufficiently characterised. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies among Japanese adults to assess the associations between fish consumption and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to investigate potential dose-response relationships in a high-fish-intake population. We systematically searched the MEDLINE and Ichushi-Web databases. Prospective cohort studies conducted in Japan that reported hazard ratios or relative risks for fish intake and mortality outcomes were included. The protocol was registered a priori in the PROSPERO database (CRD42025635066). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled estimates by comparing the highest and lowest intake categories. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using generalised least-squares trend estimation and restricted cubic spline models. A total of 113 articles were assessed for eligibility, and 16 studies met the inclusion criteria, and nine were eligible for meta-analysis. Higher fish intake was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.98) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.80-0.91), with low heterogeneity. According to the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence was rated low. Visual inspection suggested that mortality risk reduced with increasing fish intake up to approximately 100 g/day, after which the decline slowed, implying a plateau effect at higher intake levels. Among Japanese adults, high fish consumption was associated with a lower risk of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality. Further research is required to clarify the dose-response relationship in populations with high fish consumption.

items.title: First evidence of measles virus detected from exhaled breath in humans.
items.abstract: Objectives Measles is among the most transmissible human infections, yet direct capture of measles virus from an infected person's exhaled breath has not been described. We assessed whether measles virus RNA can be detected from exhaled breath using facemask sampling (FMS). Methods We studied a 23-year-old unvaccinated woman with laboratory-confirmed measles (throat-swab RT-qPCR positive on day 5 post symptom onset). From day 10 post symptom onset, longitudinal sampling was performed for six consecutive days with duplicate specimens collected at each timepoint from the throat, face, cutaneous lesions and exhaled breath using a surgical mask fitted with polyvinyl alcohol sampling strips (FMS). Dissolved mask strips and swab eluates underwent RNA extraction followed by RT-qPCR targeting measles nucleoprotein and haemagglutinin genes, with human RNase P as a sample adequacy control. Quantification was derived from nucleoprotein-gene standards and normalised per strip or per 100 μL of swab eluate. Results Measles virus RNA was consistently detected in exhaled breath captured by FMS and remained >10ˆ4 genome copies per sampling strip despite sampling beginning 10 days after symptom onset. During FMS collection, the participant reported no respiratory symptoms and did not vocalise. RNA kinetics differed by sampling site: throat and facial swabs increased even after complete rash resolution, whereas cutaneous-lesion swabs yielded comparatively low RNA levels. FMS kinetics diverged from throat swabs over time, suggesting distinct patterns of virus emission across compartments. Conclusions This study provides the first empirical evidence that measles virus RNA can be captured directly from the exhaled breath of an individual with measles. Although RNA detection does not confirm infectious virus, persistent high-level exhaled RNA supports FMS as a practical, non-invasive tool to study measles respiratory emission and may inform understanding of transmission and the duration of potential contagiousness. Empirical sampling of different respiratory compartments may help refine infection-prevention guidance during resurgent outbreaks.

items.title: Unexpected enrichment of chlorinated-iodinated carbazoles in deep-sea sediments from the Haima cold-seep area: occurrence, compositional patterns and possible sources.
items.abstract: Polyhalogenated carbazoles (PHCZs) are emerging organohalogen contaminants, yet their molecular diversity, sources, and controlling processes in deep-sea cold seep environments remain poorly understood. In this study, known PHCZs and previously unknown PHCZs (UPHCZs) were investigated in sediment cores from the Haima cold seep area of the South China Sea, including a mature seep site (HMS18), an early-stage seep site (HMW07E), a non-seep site (HMW07N), and coastal sediments. Target analysis showed that Σ 12 PHCZ concentrations ranged from 0.16 to 3.8 ng g -1 (median, 1.6 ng g -1 ), with higher levels at HMW07N than at HMS18 and HMW07E. Orbitrap HRMS-based non-target screening further yielded 47 candidate UPHCZs, all tentatively annotated at Level 3, with diverse halogen substitution patterns, including Cl-, I-, Cl/Br-, Cl/I-, Br/I-, and Cl/Br/I-substituted carbazole-like compounds. Σ 47 UPHCZ concentrations ranged from 3.7 to 170 ng g -1 , with a median value of 24 ng g -1 , exceeding those of target PHCZs by more than one order of magnitude. These results indicate that conventional target analysis substantially underestimates both the abundance and molecular diversity of halogenated carbazole-like compounds in cold seep sediments. Five-halogenated and Cl/I-substituted congeners dominated the cold seep sediment pool, revealing a distinct halogenation signature. Core-specific correlation analyses showed covariation between PHCZ/UPHCZ compositions and local geochemical gradients, whereas the relationships varied among the three cores. Exploratory comparisons further showed differences in UPHCZ composition between HMS18 and HMW07E, including higher estimated concentrations of more highly halogenated mixed-halogen features at HMS18. The Cl/I-rich and highly halogenated PHCZ/UPHCZ profiles may reflect several unresolved processes, including precursor inputs, halide availability, transformation, transport, and differential preservation. Overall, these findings document diverse halogenated carbazole-like features in sediments from the Haima cold seep area and provide a basis for further investigation of their sources, transformation, and environmental fate.

items.title: Risk Factors for Admission to the Intensive Care Unit and Mortality in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
items.abstract: Background Adults with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are at risk of requiring intensive care unit (ICU)-level care following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Risk factors for admission to the ICU and outcomes are, however, poorly defined. Objective To assess risk factors associated with ICU admission in such patients, identify variables associated with ICU mortality, and analyze the outcome of ICU survivors in comparison to HCT recipients not admitted to the ICU. Study design Here, we retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 1,265 adults with MDS/AML or AML who received an allograft while in first or second remission between 2006 and 2023. Results The cumulative incidence of ICU admission was 9.2% on day +100 after HCT. HCT-comorbidity index (hazard ratio [HR]=1.15, P=0.005), treatment-related mortality (TRM) score (HR=1.07, P=0.004), and graft from an HLA-mismatched donor (HR=2.19, P=0.018) were independently associated with ICU admission. Within 100 days of ICU admission, 50 patients (43%) died; poor performance status (odds ratio [OR]=5.45, P=0.005), higher TRM score (OR per one unit increase=1.14, P=0.035), and secondary AML (OR=2.71 P=0.035) were associated with increased day +100 mortality after ICU admission. In a landmark analysis, patients admitted to the ICU during the first 100 days after HCT and alive at day +150 had significantly higher NRM (HR=2.36, P Conclusion Together, these results highlight that ICU admission is common after allografting in adults with AML and is associated with high mortality. Identification of patients at increased risk may, ultimately, help develop possible preventive strategies and allow testing in particularly vulnerable individuals.

items.title: Effect of 0.01%, 0.02% and 0.04% Atropine eyedrops vs Placebo on myopia incidence in pre-myopic children: A randomized clinical trial.
items.abstract: Purpose To investigate the dose-response relationship and individual efficacy of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops for preventing myopia onset in pre-myopic children. Design Twelve-month randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial conducted in Shanghai primary schools (March 2023-December 2024). Methods Children aged 6-10 years with cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction of -0.50 to +0.75 diopters (D) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo or 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine once daily. Primary outcome was 12-month cumulative myopia incidence (SER ≤ -0.50 D in the worse eye); secondary outcomes were changes in SER and axial length of the worse eye. Children with ocular or systemic diseases, prior orthokeratology use, or other myopia control interventions were excluded. Results Among the 428 randomized children, 395 (92.3%) were included in the final primary analysis. Cumulative myopia incidence was 39.0%, 29.4%, 26.9%, and 25.8% in the control, 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% groups, respectively (P trend = 0.044). SER changes showed a significant dose-response relationship (P trend trend = 0.418). Compared with control, the 0.04% atropine group showed a significantly lower mean change in SER (P Conclusions Low-concentration atropine demonstrated a dose-response relationship for reducing cumulative myopia incidence and slowing refractive progression in pre-myopic children, but no such relationship on axial length. This preliminary evidence suggests potential for early myopia prevention, but larger, longer-term trials are needed before recommending an optimal clinical concentration.

items.title: Survival Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Decade of Treatment in a Western Tertiary Referral Center.
items.abstract: Background & aims Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a challenging malignancy with various available treatments. This retrospective study provides clinical outcomes on staging, treatment, and overall survival (OS) of HCC patients. Methods All included patients were diagnosed between 2013 and 2022. OS was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, stratified by BCLC stage and diagnosis period. Results A total of 1,306 patients were analyzed: 9.1% BCLC-0, 44.3% BCLC-A, 19.1% BCLC-B, 17% BCLC-C, and 10.4% BCLC-D. Median OS (mOS) for the cohort was 19.7 months (95% CI 16.9-23.0), ranging from 86.1 months (95% CI 47.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.4 months (95% CI 1.7-3.4) for BCLC-D. Poor survival was associated with Child-Pugh (CP) classification (CP-B: HR1.49, 95% CI 1.17-1.89, CP-C: HR2.45, 95% CI 1.57-3.81), and portal vein tumor thrombosis (HR1.75, 95% CI 1.19-2.58). In 2013-2017, 609 patients (46.6%) were diagnosed with mOS of 21.7 months (95% CI 18.4-25.1), while 697 patients (53.4%) in 2018-2022 had mOS of 18.9 months (95% CI 14.8-22.7). Stratified by BCLC stage, mOS in 2013-2017 ranged from 86.1 months (95% CI 41.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.9 months (95% CI 2.2-5.7) for BCLC-D. In 2018-2022, mOS was 59.8 months (95%CI 44.2-not reached) for BCLC-0, and 1.8 months (95% CI 1.4-3.1) for BCLC-D. Conclusions Our clinical data from a consecutive decade-long HCC cohort support the evolution of staging and survival data in HCC management, with CP classification, portal vein tumor thrombosis, and treatment modality as key survival predictors.

items.title: Rethinking Inhalation Risk Assessment: Integrating Respiratory Cell Models with Air-Liquid Interface Exposure?
items.abstract: Air-liquid-interface (ALI) exposure systems, combined with respiratory cell models, have been increasingly used for the past decades to assess the hazard of substances and for drug safety and efficacy testing. Further, these are being used for exploring disease mechanisms. Currently, on a global scale, there is a critical mass of scientific researchers conducting such experiments and using the technologies for ALI exposure. The methodology is already paramount within the training of the next generation of researchers, due to the concomitant necessity to develop alternative, human relevant models for regulatory risk assessment and accelerating drug development. There are many different ALI respiratory cell models and exposure systems available, but there is a lack of widely accepted standard operating procedures and pre-validation efforts for increasing confidence and acceptance by different stakeholders. However, how do we get there? The herein commentary intends to discuss the current situation of ALI-based experimentation, as well as consider the future challenges that must be overcome to establish these next-level testing strategies to be accepted in the regulatory arena.

items.title: Mycobacterium smegmatis MSMEG_6906 modulates IL-1β via NF-κB pathway to benefit intracellular survival.
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), instigated by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), exerts a detrimental impact on public health worldwide. Mtb features unique and abundant lipids components and genes involved in lipogenesis, which are believed to provide the pathogen an advantage in the host, but the underlying mechanisms remain inconclusive. In the present study we show that Mycobacterium smegmatis (M. smegmatis) MSMEG_6906, annotated as a hydrolase that probably involved in lipid biosynthesis, functions in affecting bacterial morphology, and plays a role in modulating IL-1β expression in macrophages. The absence of MSMEG_6906 results in significantly attenuated survival of M. smegmatis in macrophages. Mechanistically, MSMEG_6906 suppresses the expression of IL-1β through nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway, thus benefiting the survival of M. smegmatis in macrophages. Exogenously added IL-1β neutralizing antibody could partially rescue the bacterial load of MSMEG_6906 deficient strain to the level of wild type M. smegmatis in macrophages. Our findings broaden understanding on the interplay between mycobacterium and host immune response, provide an alternative for TB treatment or drug development in the future.

items.title: Being a child while seriously ill: parental and physician perspectives on suffering and adaptation.
items.abstract: Context Suffering is central to the care of children with life-threatening conditions, yet it can be difficult to recognize and assess, and its role in treatment decisions remains contested. Objectives To explore how parents and physicians interpret suffering in children aged 1-12 years with life-threatening conditions, and how adaptation and opportunities for ordinary childhood shape these judgments. Methods Qualitative interview study based on grounded theory principles. We interviewed 64 parents of 44 children with life-threatening conditions and 34 physicians in the Netherlands, recruited using maximum-variation sampling. Interviews were conducted from November 2016 to October 2018; coding and analysis were completed in 2020. Perceived sources, domains, and modifiers of suffering were identified through iterative coding and constant comparison. Results Participants described 3 overlapping domains of suffering: physical, psychological, and existential. Assessments reflected not only symptoms and functional limitations but also their effects on the child's enjoyment, relationships, participation, agency, and continuity of ordinary childhood. Apparent adaptation could mitigate perceived suffering, whereas limited communication or consciousness made it harder to judge whether and how much the child was suffering. Conclusion Parents and physicians understood suffering in seriously ill children as multidimensional, context-dependent, and not directly inferable from symptoms or functional limitations alone. Assessment should distinguish observations from interpretations, incorporate the child's perspective whenever possible, draw on multiple perspectives, and remain open to revision. A proposed reflective framework may support such assessment without quantifying suffering or determining decisions on its own.

items.title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO).
items.abstract: Background The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. Methods From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. Results A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P Conclusions Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

items.title: Collateral Sensitivity in Bacteria: Phenomenon, Mechanisms, Modulators and Therapeutic Prospects.
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation and infection of multidrug-resistant bacteria pose a significant threat to global public health. The gradual increase in drug resistance, primarily driven by the inappropriate use of antibiotics, underscores the urgent need for developing novel therapeutic approaches for drug-resistant bacterial infections. Collateral sensitivity (CS) describes the phenomenon whereby bacteria resistance to a specific antibiotic increases susceptibility to other antibiotics. In some cases of antibiotic resistance, CS can provide rapid and effective guidance for clinical drug use by detecting the lowest drug sensitivity concentration of resistant bacteria. In order to prevent or mitigate the emergence of drug-resistant bacteria, it is crucial to thoroughly investigate the underlying mechanisms of CS. This article discusses recent research progress on the CS phenomenon, its mechanisms, influencing factors, and the therapeutic potential of CS in bacteria.

items.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Parasitology: A holistic perspective from diagnosis to therapeutics.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being investigated to address challenges in parasite detection, disease surveillance, and therapeutic development. This narrative review examines current and emerging AI applications in parasitology across diagnostics, drug discovery, genomics, epidemiology, education, and public health decision-making, with particular emphasis on diagnostic applications. Machine learning and deep learning methods support automated parasite detection, classification, and quantification in microscopic images, alongside medical image analysis and arthropod identification. Applications are discussed for malaria, leishmaniasis, schistosomiasis, cystic echinococcosis, soil-transmitted helminth infections, and intestinal protozoal infections. Beyond diagnosis, AI-assisted approaches support compound screening, drug repurposing, toxicity prediction, and prioritization of potential therapeutic targets. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses also offer opportunities to investigate parasite biology and predict drug resistance. Surveillance models may inform outbreak forecasting and targeted control, although their operational value requires evaluation in the intended settings. Educational applications remain emerging, and the benefits of digital learning should be distinguished from those attributable specifically to AI. Across these domains, performance on curated datasets does not establish clinical utility or generalizability. Major barriers include limited representative datasets, insufficient external and prospective validation, infrastructure constraints, and concerns regarding privacy, bias, and accountability. Future progress requires reproducible evaluation, experimental validation of therapeutic candidates, and assessment of clinical and public health benefits. AI is therefore best positioned as a complementary tool that supports parasitological expertise, with responsible implementation guided by transparency, equitable access, and human oversight.

items.title: Pharmacological Targeting of Fc Receptor and FcRn Pathways: Therapeutic Antibody Engineering in Immune-Mediated Disorders.
items.abstract: The Fc domain of therapeutic antibodies is a major pharmacological determinant of efficacy, safety, and disposition because it governs interactions with Fc receptors and the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). Advances in Fc engineering have enabled the rational modulation of antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis, complement activation, and IgG recycling, thereby improving the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic profiles of antibody-based biologics. In this review, we discuss the structural basis of Fc-mediated signaling and summarize how FcγR- and FcRn-directed engineering strategies are being applied across cancer, autoimmune disease, allergy, and selected chronic inflammatory conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on the pharmacological consequences of Fc glycoengineering, Fc silencing or enhancement, and FcRn antagonism, as well as on clinically advanced agents that illustrate these principles in practice. We also address translational challenges, including receptor polymorphism, tissue-specific response variability, immunogenicity, and developability. Overall, Fc engineering has emerged as a central pharmacological strategy for optimizing next-generation antibody therapeutics.

items.title: 1-Octen-3-ol from Bamboo Leaves Suppresses Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the PI3K/AKT Pathway and Activating p53/Caspase-3-Dependent Apoptosis.
items.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, presents substantial therapeutic challenges due to limited targeted therapy options and prevalent drug resistance. In this study, we characterised 1-octen-3-ol, an active compound derived from bamboo leaves, as a bioactive natural compound with anti-LUSC activity. In vitro, 1-octen-3-ol significantly suppressed LUSC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis. Network pharmacology predicted the PI3K/AKT pathway as a central mediator of its activity. Mechanistic studies confirmed that 1-octen-3-ol inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, accompanied by increased expression of p53 and cleaved-caspase3. The PI3K agonist 740Y-P and AKT agonist SC79 partially reversed the effects of 1-octen-3-ol on LUSC cell migration, invasion, colony formation, and protein expression, underscoring the critical role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, 1-octen-3-ol markedly suppressed LUSC xenograft growth, and its tumor-suppressive effect was abrogated by co-administration of either the PI3K or AKT agonist. This study is the first to demonstrate that 1-octen-3-ol exerts potent inhibition of LUSC progression via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, thereby activating p53 and initiating caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-LUSC activity of 1-octen-3-ol, a natural volatile small-molecule, and support further lead-discovery efforts based on natural-product sources.

items.title: Neighborhood and Individual Socioeconomic Predictors of 5-Year Pain Trajectories After Burn Injury.
items.abstract: This study identified 5-year pain trajectories in adult burn survivors and examined whether neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage was associated with adverse trajectory membership. Using the Burn Model System National Database (2015-2025), Growth Mixture Modeling identified pain intensity trajectory classes in 1,354 adults assessed at 6, 12, 24, and 60 months. In the geocoded subsample (n=909), multinomial regression with multiple imputation (m=100) estimated associations between the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) and trajectory membership, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and site characteristics and then additionally for individual socioeconomic characteristics. Three trajectories emerged: Low Pain (56%), Moderate Pain (30%), and High Pain (14%). Each 1-SD increase in ADI was associated with estimated relative risk ratios of 1.19 for Moderate Pain (95% CI 0.996-1.43, p=0.056) and 1.27 for High Pain (95% CI 0.99-1.63, p=0.058) versus Low Pain; both intervals included the null. Using Neighborhood Atlas ADI, disadvantage was associated with Moderate Pain (RRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.03-1.55) but not High Pain membership. Estimates were attenuated after additional socioeconomic adjustment. After correction for multiple comparisons, pre-injury unemployment and other public insurance (vs. private) were associated with higher High Pain risk, and household income of $50,000-$99,999 (vs. <$50,000) with lower Moderate Pain risk. Evidence was most consistent for persistent Moderate Pain, though estimates varied in precision across ADI measures. Individual socioeconomic characteristics were also associated with trajectory membership.

items.title: Machine learning-based computerized adaptive testing of PHQ-8 and GAD-7 in psychiatric outpatients.
items.abstract: Background Scalable, accurate and efficient monitoring tools are urgently needed to support psychiatric assessment in routine care. This study aimed to evaluate a machine learning-based computerized adaptive testing (ML-CAT) model for the PHQ-8 and GAD-7 in psychiatric outpatient settings. Methods Data were obtained from a longitudinal cohort study of patients with depression or anxiety diagnoses. ML-CAT models were developed using the M5P algorithm. Model performance was evaluated via 10-fold cross-validation. Concurrent validity was assessed with Pearson's r, R 2 , and mean absolute error (MAE). Longitudinal change detection used paired t-tests and Cohen's d. Diagnostic classification agreement (based on ≥10 cutoff between assessments) was examined using percentage agreement and Cohen's κ. Results The ML-CAT administered a median of 2 items per instrument (66-71% item reduction) while achieving near-perfect concurrent validity with full-scale scores (r = 0.996-0.997; R 2 = 0.986-0.991; MAE Conclusions The ML-CAT model reproduced PHQ-8 and GAD-7 scores with high accuracy and detected meaningful clinical change across two follow-up waves. The resulting adaptive questionnaire can be presented as a flowchart and administered both online and offline, providing real-world clinical evidence for scalable ML-CAT-based psychiatric assessment.

items.title: Socioeconomic and circumstance differences in means of suicide among U.S. adults: Evidence from the National Violent Death Reporting System.
items.abstract: Background Suicide is a major public health problem. To our knowledge, few studies have examined how multiple sociodemographic and circumstance factors are associated with a comprehensive set of International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-defined suicide means; therefore, we evaluated these associations in a national sample of U.S. adults. Methods Data were obtained from the U.S. National Violent Death Reporting System from 2003 to 2023. Adults aged ≥18 years who were assigned an ICD-10 cause of death code that corresponds to a suicide means were included (N = 391,250). Suicide means were categorized as firearm, asphyxiation, medication poisoning, non-medication poisoning, non-firearm weapon, jumping, and motor vehicle. Multinomial logistic regression was used to regress suicide means by socioeconomic and circumstance factors, using firearm suicide as the reference outcome. Results Firearms were the most common suicide method (52.6%), followed by asphyxiation (26.9%) and medication poisoning (11.1%). In general, suicide by firearm was relatively less likely among those in older age groups, higher education levels, racial-ethnic minorities, females, and those with mental health and substance abuse history. In contrast, suicide by firearm was generally more likely among those who were married, military history, employed in the workforce, financial hardship, and those with physical health and relationship problems. Conclusions We identified sociodemographic and circumstance factors that may be at higher risk of suicide via different means of suicide. These results may identify high risk individuals and guide clinical practice, screening guidelines, and policies based on which suicide means may be more likely.

items.title: Monkeypox on a disc: Portable centrifugal microfluidic platform for multi-assay colorimetric LAMP.
items.abstract: Monkeypox is currently the most important orthopoxvirus infection in humans. The increase in the number of cases, combined with its potential social impact and international spread, led the World Health Organization (WHO) to classify it as the most recent Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Although mainly endemic in resource-limited countries, quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) remains the gold standard for detection but is challenging due to the need for specialized instrumentation. To address this, we propose an instrument-friendly molecular assay based on colorimetric Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP), performed on a multi-assay polystyrene-toner (PST) centrifugal device. The new analytical device was designed to include chambers for loading the LAMP mixture and samples, interconnected channels for mixing them, and separate chambers for simultaneous LAMP amplification and visual detection of each sample. When evaluated in a panel of real clinical samples, compared to qPCR, the assay based on visual detection demonstrated 100.00% specificity, 91.67% sensitivity, and 95.83% accuracy, which increased to 100% accuracy when digital image analysis was employed, with a total analysis time of approximately 60 min. The relative simplicity of the assay may facilitate its implementation in resource-limited settings and contribute to expanding access to molecular detection of monkeypox.

items.title: Value-based care contracting for pharmacy drugs: opportunity for the United States.
items.abstract: The onset of improved data interoperability required as a result of the 21st Century Cures Act, 92% Health Information Exchange coverage, and lessons learned from European pharmaceutical risk-sharing models present innovative and timely opportunities for the U.S. to adopt pharmaceutical value-based contracting (VBC), which uses drug-level performance to allocate financial risk between payers and manufacturers based on clinical and economic metrics. Having been piloted in Italy, Spain, and the UK, this analysis explores different contracting options and paths for organizations like CMS and integrated payer-provider networks to draw on these lessons to adapt VBC frameworks to the U.S. pharmaceutical landscape. While advances have been seen in other areas of VBC and rising net drug costs year-over-year, only 2.3% of publicly available pharmaceutical VBC contracts have been deployed in the U.S. as compared to 77.9% in Europe. As such, we present a path forward for the expansion of VBC to promote orphan drug development, expand access to pharmaceuticals, and improve patient safety.

items.title: Epidemiological modeling and optimal intervention strategies for seasonal scrub typhus infection in human population mediated by mites and rodents.
items.abstract: Scrub typhus is a re-emerging vector-borne disease of significant public health concern, particularly in endemic regions where seasonal factors strongly influence transmission dynamics. Individuals engaged in agricultural and field-based activities are particularly vulnerable to increased exposure to infected mites, especially during the monsoon season, thereby underscoring the importance of adopting appropriate preventive measures to reduce transmission risk. Motivated by this, we developed a mathematical model with optimal control to describe the transmission dynamics of scrub typhus in humans, incorporating a seasonally varying transmission rate in the human population. The proposed model ensures positivity and boundedness of solutions, with disease persistence characterized by the basic reproduction number and equilibrium stability examined analytically. The scrub typhus incidence data from Mizoram, India, spanning January 2021 to December 2022 is utilized for data fitting and estimation. It is found that the proposed full model outperforms the sub-models in terms of goodness-of-fit statistics, with AIC (234.71), AICc (251.63), and BIC (246.49) and Akaike weight (0.84505), thereby providing stronger support for its selection. It is found that scrub typhus infection dynamics are highly sensitive to the β 2 and β 3 transmission rates, where the infection peak is observed during the monsoon season. This study may provide valuable information to guide policymakers in implementing evidence-based approaches for the prevention and control of scrub typhus infection.

items.title: International Regulatory Status and Reimbursement Recommendations of Haematological Malignancy Drugs Withdrawn from the FDA Accelerated Approval Pathway.
items.abstract: Background The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) can grant earlier access to promising therapies through its accelerated approval pathway, conditional on post-authorisation trials confirming clinical benefit. Between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2024, the FDA granted accelerated approval to 59 haematological malignancy drug indications, 13 of which were subsequently withdrawn because of unconfirmed clinical benefit or safety concerns. Methods We assessed the regulatory status and reimbursement recommendations for these 13 FDA-withdrawn drug indications in Australia, Canada, and England using publicly available regulatory and health technology assessment (HTA) data. Results Eight of the 13 FDA-withdrawn drug indications were approved in at least one comparison jurisdiction, resulting in 14 marketing authorisations overall. Three of 14 were subsequently withdrawn. As of June 2025, 11 authorisations remained active, of which only five had received positive reimbursement recommendations. Conclusion Many haematological malignancy drug indications withdrawn from FDA accelerated approval remain authorised in other jurisdictions, with a minority continuing to receive positive reimbursement recommendations. Differences in regulatory and reimbursement decisions across jurisdictions may reflect variation in pathway use, post-authorisation evidence requirements, authorised indications, and interpretation of evidence. Policy summary The continued authorisation of haematological malignancy drug indications in Australia, Canada, and England following FDA withdrawal of comparable indications has important implications for patients and health systems. Continued approval for the indication may facilitate use of the drug in patients with refractory disease and few alternatives, but may also expose patients to treatments with no clear evidence of clinical benefit or for which safety concerns altered the benefit-risk assessment. Continued public reimbursement under such conditions could also lead to unnecessary spending for health systems. Major new evidence or regulatory action in a comparable jurisdiction should prompt proportionate reassessment of local authorisation and reimbursement decisions, with consideration of differences in the authorised indication and applicable evidence.

items.title: PPARγ Activation Rescues High‑Fat Diet‑Induced Obesity Exacerbated Food Allergy by Maintaining Intestinal Homeostasis.
items.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity has been suggested to be a potential risk factor for the increasing incidence of food allergies, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, we investigated the causal role of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) in HFD-induced obesity exacerbated food allergy using both in vitro and in vivo approaches. In bone marrow‑derived mast cells (BMMCs), pharmacological inhibition of PPARγ enhanced IgE‑mediated degranulation and IL‑4 secretion without affecting IgE‑FcεRI binding, indicating that PPARγ negatively regulates mast cell activation independently of the initial receptor engagement. In HFD‑fed mice with ovalbumin‑induced food allergy, oral administration of the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone alleviated allergic reactions by reducing mucosal mast cell activation, without significantly altering IgE levels. Mechanistically, PPARγ activation restored intestinal barrier integrity, expanded RORγt⁺ regulatory T cells in mesenteric lymph nodes, and reversed gut dysbiosis, particularly by restoring Ligilactobacillus abundance. Collectively, these findings establish that PPARγ suppression is a causal mediator of obesity‑exacerbated food allergy and highlight PPARγ as a potential target for preventive strategies against allergic disease in the context of obesogenic dietary patterns.

items.title: Physical and psychological burden in RRMS: depression and fatigue beyond disease duration.
items.abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, autoimmune, demyelinating and neurodegenerative disease. Accumulation of physical and psychological disabilities adversely affects patients' health-related quality of life. The 29-item Multiple Sclerosis Impact Scale (MSIS-29) is a self-reported measure of the physical and psychological burden. Objective To evaluate the physical and psychological impact levels in patients with MS and to examine their relationship with disease duration. Methods We enrolled 100 consecutive adults aged 18 to 55 years with relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS). The Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), annual relapse rate (ARR), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), MSIS-29, and Timed 25-Foot Walk Test (25-FWT) were applied. Results A total of 57 participants (57%) were female patients. The mean age was 38.5 ± 8.0 years, and the mean disease duration, 9.8 ± 6.8 years. The mean MSIS-29 physical and psychological scores were 36.7 ± 15.7 and 45.3 ± 20.4 respectively. No significant differences were found between patients with disease duration ≤ 10 and > 10 years in terms of the physical ( p = 0.263) or psychological ( p = 0.551) subscales. Physical impact was significantly associated with the female sex ( p = 0.021) and the scpres on the EDSS ( p = 0.030), BDI ( p p p = 0.005), ARR ( p = 0.020), and the scores on the BDI ( p p Conclusion Disease duration did not predict physical or psychological impact in RRMS. Depression severity, lower-extremity function, and the female sex were the independent determinants of disease-related impact in the multivariate analysis. The association of fatigue with disease impact, significant at the bivariate level, was attenuated by depression in the multivariate analysis. Routine assessment of these modifiable factors should be accompanied by disease-modifying treatments in MS care.

items.title: No Sensorization without Representation: Co-designing Tailored Sensorization Plans with Nursing Home Leadership, Direct Care Staff, Residents, and Resident Family Members.
items.abstract: Objective : Although interest in using sensors in long-term care (LTC) settings is growing, little guidance exists on how to engage stakeholders in planning. This study aimed to (1) develop a systematic, community-engaged process for co-designing sensorization plans - defining goals and parameters (e.g., data collection, sharing) to support decision making prior to sensor deployment, (2) apply this process with LTC stakeholders, and (3) examine stakeholder perspectives across sensor approaches. Methods : We conducted a multi-phase, multi-method study in a single nursing home that included observations and engaging nursing home leadership, direct care staff, residents, and resident family members through surveys and interviews. Results : Most participants (72%, N=25) identified improving staff mental health as a top priority, citing high workloads driven by staffing shortages. Two sensorization plans were developed: (1) an individual-level plan to detect and address direct care staff stress and (2) a workplace-focused plan using automation to reduce documentation burden. A majority of the 22 interview participants (59%) preferred the workplace-focused plan due to its broader benefits for direct care staff and resident care. Participants identified trade-offs across the plans, including tensions between perceived usefulness of direct stress detection versus workload reductions, privacy concerns, unintended sensor data uses, and questions about feasibility of sensor placement and staff buy-in. Additionally, we identified two practical lessons learned to improve the co-design process - the importance of: balancing meaningful stakeholder engagement with participant burden and creatively communicating complex sensorization plans to diverse stakeholders. Conclusions : These findings demonstrate both the feasibility of a structured, multi-stakeholder sensorization planning process and the value of engaging stakeholders early to identify community priorities, compare alternative sensorization strategies, and surface implementation trade-offs. Future work should continue to refine the co-design process and explore scalable approaches that integrate stakeholder engagement with computational tools to support efficient and democratic planning.
