items.title: CochleaNet: deep learning-based image analysis for cochlear connectomics and gene therapy.
items.abstract: With the emergence of gene and optogenetic therapies targeting deafness, the comprehensive analysis of the molecular anatomy and physiology of the cochlea has become ever more important. Here, we introduce CochleaNet, a deep learning-based framework to analyze volumetric imaging data obtained by light-sheet microscopy of decalcified, cleared and fluorescently labeled cochleae. CochleaNet covers the workflow from reconstruction of the cochlea to segmentation of inner hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons and their afferent synapses, to the analysis of tonotopy and specific fluorescent expression patterns. We validated CochleaNet by comparison to manual image analysis, also demonstrating its superiority to prior segmentation methods. We then analyzed different spiral ganglion neuron types and validated different gene therapy products with CochleaNet. Trained on high isotropic resolution mouse data, CochleaNet was also applicable to the cochlea of the gerbil, another relevant animal model, and lower-resolution mouse and marmoset data from a commercially available microscope. We conclude that the combination of light-sheet microscopy and image analysis with CochleaNet paves the way for rapid and reliable quantification of cochlear molecular anatomy and preclinical gene therapy outcomes.

items.title: Antithetical roles of tau in hippocampal long-term synaptic depression in rats versus mice.
items.abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is a primary feature of tauopathies, a group of major neurodegenerative diseases that includes Alzheimer's disease. However, the normal synaptic functions of tau are poorly understood. Since rats provide advantages over mice for understanding human tau, such as expressing six tau isoforms and showing more robust signs of tau pathology, as well as offering a richer behavioural repertoire, we developed a tau knockout (Mapt KO) rat line. We primarily investigated the impact of tau elimination on long-term synaptic depression (LTD)-a form of synaptic weakening that tau mediates in mice. Low-frequency stimulation of hippocampal Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses revealed a robust enhancement of LTD in Mapt KO rats relative to WT littermates. In contrast, in interleaved experiments, Mapt KO mice exhibited reduced LTD compared to WT littermates, in line with previous reports. Together, our findings demonstrate a species-dependent role for endogenous tau in regulating hippocampal LTD, promoting it in mice yet constraining it in rats. Therefore, the functions of tau are not necessarily conserved in rodents, underscoring the importance of animal model choice.

items.title: SLC20A2 Intragenic Structural Variants as a Cause of Primary Brain Calcification.
items.abstract: Background Intragenic structural variants of SLC20A2 remain poorly characterized in primary brain calcification (PBC). Objectives The aim was to identify and characterize intragenic SLC20A2 structural variants in PBC. Methods One familial PBC pedigree and two sporadic patients underwent whole-genome sequencing and copy-number analysis, followed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and Sanger validation. Long-read sequencing (LRS) resolved complex architecture. Transcript and protein effects were assessed by reverse transcription (RT)-PCR, RT-quantitative PCR, and western blotting. Results We identified three intragenic SLC20A2 structural variants: exon 2-3 and exon 5 tandem duplications in F1 and F3, respectively, and a complex exon 2-3 inverted insertion in F2. F1 and F3 showed aberrant, frameshift-generating transcripts, and F3 showed reduced SLC20A2 mRNA and protein. Accordingly, the F1 and F3 variants were classified as pathogenic, whereas the F2 variant remained of uncertain significance. Conclusions Our study expands the spectrum of intragenic SLC20A2 structural variation in PBC and highlights the value of copy number variation analysis and LRS in genetically unresolved individuals. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

items.title: Remote Versus In-Person Follow-up Programming After Subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation for Parkinson's Disease: A Multicenter Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
items.abstract: Background Remote programming of deep brain stimulation may improve access to specialized postoperative care for people with Parkinson's disease, but prospective randomized evidence remains limited. Objective We aimed to determine whether remote follow-up programming after standardized inpatient initiation is noninferior to conventional in-person follow-up programming for motor outcomes during the early postoperative period. Methods In this prospective, randomized, open-label, multicenter noninferiority trial, adults with idiopathic Parkinson's disease who recently underwent bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation implantation at six German centers were randomly assigned 1:1 to conventional in-person follow-up programming or remote follow-up programming through a secure telemedicine platform during the first 90 days after surgery. All participants underwent initial in-person postoperative programming before randomization. The primary outcome was the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part III score at 90 days in the medication on and stimulation ON state. The prespecified noninferiority margin was 5 points. Results Fifty-two participants were randomly assigned. The per-protocol population included 26 participants in the conventional care group and 22 in the remote programming group. The between-group median difference of the primary endpoint was -2.5 points (95% confidence interval, -9.0 to 2.0), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion. Secondary clinical outcomes and patient-reported outcomes were broadly comparable between groups. Serious adverse events occurred at similar frequencies in both groups, and no deaths occurred. Conclusions Remote follow-up programming after standardized inpatient initiation achieved motor outcomes noninferior to conventional in-person follow-up during the first 3 months, with no clear short-term safety signal. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Spatiotemporal Resolution for Neurodegenerative Diseases: Linking Proteinopathy, Cellular Vulnerability, and Disease Trajectories.
items.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by selective and progressive degeneration of specific neuronal populations, often accompanied by glial dysfunction. Despite extensive investigation, proposed pathogenic models remain insufficient to fully explain selective vulnerability and stereotyped spatiotemporal patterns of neurodegeneration across diseases. Spatial omics technologies preserve anatomical context and enable interrogation of cell-type composition, molecular heterogeneity, and intercellular interactions within neural systems. In this review, we synthesize current concepts and technological advances in spatial omics and discuss how these approaches are reshaping our understanding of NDs. Spatial omics provides an integrative framework for linking pathological protein aggregation with selective cellular vulnerability, microenvironment-dependent interactions, and disease progression across molecular, cellular, and anatomical scales. We highlight emerging insights into pathology-associated gene modules, neuron-glia interactions, and mechanisms underlying regional vulnerability. Finally, we discuss multimodal data integration and future directions for translating spatially resolved molecular maps into mechanistic understanding.

items.title: Dimensional and categorical emotional ratings of Russian nouns: The ENRuN-2 database.
items.abstract: Databases with emotional ratings of words are essential for studying emotional information processing in psychology, psycholinguistics, neuroscience, and related disciplines. The emotional content of stimuli is traditionally described within two approaches: dimensional (rating words on continuous scales such as valence and arousal) and categorical (rating associations of words with discrete emotion categories). Databases with emotional ratings of words have been developed for various languages, but only a few integrate both approaches. The present study introduces the first large database with emotional ratings of Russian words, ENRuN-2, which includes 6,708 nouns rated by valence, arousal, and relatedness to five discrete emotion categories: happiness, sadness, fear, anger, and disgust. Ratings were collected from 3,902 native speakers, with data quality procedures yielding a final sample of 2,681 participants. Reliability analyses demonstrated high inter-rater consistency across parameters (mean ICCs = .84-.96) and strong intra-rater stability of ratings. High correlations with existing Russian affective norms (rs = .50-.98) demonstrate the convergent validity of the ratings. Analysis of relationships among emotional parameters revealed that they are mostly nonlinear and consistent with findings from similar databases in other languages, further supporting validity. Gender differences in ratings are negligible, and correlations between them are high; however, male and female ratings diverge substantially for some words. The ENRuN-2 database can be used in a wide array of emotion studies and is freely available on the Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/sv9mh ).

items.title: Distinct Contributions and Sensorimotor Encoding of PV and FoxP2 Neurons in the External Globus Pallidus during Perceptual Decision-making.
items.abstract: The external globus pallidus (GPe), the central nucleus of the basal ganglia, comprises diverse cell types, including parvalbumin (PV) and forkhead box protein P2 (FoxP2) neurons. Their roles in movement regulation and sensory processing are well established; however, their contribution to perceptual decision-making remains unclear. Using a Go/No-Go visual task in mice, we found that optogenetic activation of either population impaired performance, whereas PV inhibition, but not FoxP2 inhibition, disrupted behavioral accuracy. Electrophysiological recordings showed that PV and FoxP2 neurons differentially encoded visual stimuli, licking movements, and trial outcomes. FoxP2 inhibition produced minimal changes in the spontaneous firing of substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr) neurons. PV inhibition altered spontaneous SNr firing and, together with PV activation, altered task-evoked SNr activity, reducing the preference for reward-predicting stimuli in one subpopulation and unrewarded outcomes in another. These findings reveal the distinct roles of GPe PV and FoxP2 neurons in shaping perceptual decisions and modulating basal ganglia output.

items.title: Neuroplastin Suppresses Seizures by Downregulating Endophilin A1 to Promote Internalization of GluA1-AMPA Receptors: Therapeutic Implications of Arbutin.
items.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a critical neurological disorder characterized by an imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission. α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission, whereas internalization of GluA1-containing AMPARs regulates neuronal excitability. Although neuroplastin (Np) modulates neuronal excitability, its role in GluA1-AMPAR internalization in epilepsy remains unclear. Using single-cell transcriptomics, virtual knockout, in vitro and in vivo epilepsy models, patch-clamp, biochemistry, and behavioral tests, we identified Endophilin A1 (EndoA1) as a key target through which Np regulates GluA1 internalization. In epilepsy models, EndoA1 was upregulated, surface GluA1 levels increased, and receptor internalization was reduced. EndoA1 knockdown decreased the amplitude and frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs), promoted GluA1 internalization, prolonged seizure latency, and shortened seizure duration. Np overexpression reduced EndoA1 expression, facilitated GluA1 internalization, and suppressed hyperexcitability, whereas EndoA1 knockdown rescued the Np knockdown-induced phenotype. Network pharmacology and molecular docking studies identified arbutin as an EndoA1-targeting compound that reduced hyperexcitability, mEPSC amplitude, and surface GluA1 in a concentration-dependent manner. These findings establish the Np-EndoA1-GluA1 axis as a key epileptic pathway, whereby Np negatively regulates EndoA1 to promote GluA1-AMPAR internalization and suppress excitability. Arbutin, which targets EndoA1, exerts anti-epileptic effects by modulating excitatory transmission.

items.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in neurology: biomarkers and clinical implications.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a shared downstream pathogenic mechanism across a wide spectrum of neurological disorders, ranging from primary mitochondrial diseases to conditions including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, hereditary ataxias and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. This Review examines the role of mitochondrial biomarkers in improving diagnostic accuracy, patient stratification and monitoring of disease progression and therapeutic response. Primary mitochondrial diseases are presented as proof-of-concept models of impaired oxidative phosphorylation, providing a framework for biomarker identification and validation with translational relevance to other neurological diseases. Mitochondrial biomarkers can be broadly categorized into four domains: fluid biomarkers, reflecting metabolic alterations and stress signalling; genetic biomarkers, capturing mitochondrial DNA integrity and dynamics; multi-omics approaches, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic signatures; and imaging biomarkers, enabling in vivo assessment of structural and functional consequences of mitochondrial dysfunction. Across disorders, these biomarkers reveal shared disturbances in bioenergetics, redox homeostasis, mitochondrial genome maintenance and inflammatory signalling. However, clinical implementation remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, biological variability and reduced disease specificity. Integrated, multimodal biomarker strategies, combined with longitudinal validation, will be essential for supporting precision medicine and guiding the development of therapies to target mitochondrial pathways in neurology.

items.title: Privileged representational axes in biological and artificial neural networks.
items.abstract: How do neurons code information? Recent work emphasizes the geometry and information content of population codes, using measures that are blind to the native tunings (or 'axes') of neural responses. But might these representational axes matter, with some privileged systematically over others? We developed methods to test for alignment of neural tuning across brains and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Across both vision and audition, both brains and DCNNs consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world. Moreover, the representational axes of DCNNs trained on natural inputs were aligned to those in perceptual cortices, such that axis-sensitive model-brain similarity metrics better differentiated competing models of biological sensory systems. We further show that coding schemes that privilege certain axes can facilitate task performance, reduce downstream wiring costs and improve generalization. These results motivate a new framework for understanding neural tuning in biological and artificial networks and its computational benefits.

items.title: Interneurons and network activity in the cerebral cortex: a developmental dialogue.
items.abstract: The mammalian cerebral cortex undergoes profound functional changes during early postnatal development. During this period, neurons generate spontaneous electrical activity long before sensory experience, coordinating into distinct patterns of synchronous activity. Traditionally, neuronal activity has been viewed as instructing interneuron development by modulating transcriptional programmes, morphology and connectivity. However, accumulating evidence in rodents reveals that this relationship is bidirectional: cortical interneurons are not merely passive recipients of activity-dependent signals but also active architects of developing network dynamics. They regulate spontaneous activity transitions from gap-junction-mediated synchronous events to large, synaptically driven bursts, and later to sparse firing characteristic of mature circuits. Critically, different interneuron subtypes mature at distinct timelines and orchestrate transitions in network activity. Activity-dependent mechanisms, in turn, regulate interneuron wiring, programmed cell death, diversification and terminal differentiation. This reciprocal dialogue between interneurons and network activity is essential for establishing functional cortical circuits.

items.title: Registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia, 2015-2024: a Bayesian spatiotemporal mapping study.
items.abstract: Purpose To describe temporal and geographic variation in registered adolescent suicide mortality in Colombia and its ecological association with multidimensional poverty. Methods This nationwide ecological study analyzed 4,234 presumed suicide deaths at ages 10-19 during 2015-2024 from the national forensic register (INMLCF). Bayesian Poisson models smoothed rates across neighboring departments and years. Aggregate rates combined four sex-age strata. Separate national vital-statistics (DANE) analyses compared suicide-coded deaths with two scenarios including undetermined intent. Results Male-to-female rate ratios (RRs) were 2.00 (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.86-2.15) at ages 15-19 and 1.05 (0.93-1.18) at ages 10-14. Total posterior rates were 4.54 (4.22-4.87) per 100,000 in 2015 and 5.23 (4.86-5.60) in 2024; no adjacent-year change had a 95% CrI excluding zero. Putumayo, Arauca and Amazonas exceeded 10 per 100,000 in 2024. Fifteen INMLCF departments had a probability > 0.95 of rates above the national comparator in all ten years. The pooled Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) RR per standard deviation was 0.84 (0.74-0.94). Including usable DANE undetermined-intent deaths increased the strict count by 22.18%; the expanded pooled MPI RR was 1.04 (0.93-1.17). Conclusion Registered mortality varied by age, sex and department. MPI associations and geographic classifications depended on registration source and case definition. The findings do not establish protection from poverty and support strengthening adolescent surveillance and death classification.

items.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT<sub>2A</sub>R-β-arrestin signaling.
items.abstract: Psychedelics produce long-lasting antidepressant effects, but their hallucinogenic properties limit clinical use. Using structure-guided design of 5-HT 2A R-β-arrestin-biased agonists, we identified β-arrestin signaling as a critical driver of prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. Here we show that the slow-dissociation kinetics of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) enable progressive accumulation of 5-HT 2A R engagement during repeated low-dose administration, approaching the receptor occupancy achieved by an acute high dose while avoiding its high peak concentration. This kinetic separation sustains β-arrestin signaling while limiting robust Gα q -mediated Ca 2+ responses. Consistent with this framework, repeated low-dose LSD and repeated low-dose psilocybin pretreatment followed by a high-dose psychedelic challenge produced sustained antidepressant-like behavioral effects in mice. In parallel, these regimens produced no detectable psychedelic-associated behavioral disruption in mice and cynomolgus macaques. Together, these findings uncover the signaling basis of sustained psychedelic efficacy and provide a rational framework for developing nonhallucinogenic psychedelic therapies for psychiatric disorders.

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles.
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. Here we introduce an approach to immuno-isolate EVs from neurons and glia based on protein surface markers. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

items.title: Blood pressure control before and after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage: a stroke service audit and strategies for improvement.
items.abstract: In a retrospective audit of 89 adults with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) at a tertiary neuroscience centre, fewer than 60% met the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) blood pressure (BP) target in the year before their haemorrhage, despite most carrying a known diagnosis of hypertension. Blood pressure control and antihypertensive prescribing improved after ICH, yet most survivors remained above the European Stroke Organisation (ESO) secondary-prevention target, and the first documented community BP check occurred a median of 62 days after discharge. These findings expose primary- and secondary-prevention gaps spanning the whole care pathway and lend support to a structured, protocolised uptitration pathway after discharge, combining remote BP monitoring with pharmacist- or nurse-led dose escalation.

items.title: Psychological and Neurodevelopmental Correlates of Extreme Demand Avoidance in a Clinical Sample, an Exploratory Study.
items.abstract: Extreme/pathological demand avoidance (EDA) is a behavioral profile characterized by the avoidance of everyday demands, with significant impact on the individuals and those around them. Little is understood regarding the correlates and drivers of EDA; understanding these better may lead to targeted interventions and support strategies. Cross-sectional data from parent-rated measures were analyzed for 63 children referred to a specialist neurodevelopmental clinic in the United Kingdom. The relationship between EDA traits and a number of psychological (intolerance of uncertainty, anxiety, emotional dysregulation [reactivity and dysphoria], cognitive inflexibility, alexithymia [i.e., difficulty identifying emotions]), and neurodevelopmental (autistic and ADHD) traits was tested. No differences in EDA traits were found by diagnostic group (autistic vs. not-autistic) or gender (male and female). Across the whole sample, EDA traits were negatively correlated with age and positively correlated with emotional dysregulation reactivity, ADHD traits, cognitive inflexibility, intolerance of uncertainty and alexithymia. EDA was not associated with autistic traits or anxiety. Path models were used to identify which cognitive and behavioral features predicted EDA scores, once inter-correlations among predictors were controlled for. Only emotional dysregulation, ADHD traits and age predicted EDA-Q scores. Further research is needed to assess how these variables contribute to EDA in larger more diverse samples, capturing potentially unmeasured variables, and exploring possible mediation pathways.

items.title: Nonlinear absorber device to treat essential tremor: The TREM-AB open-label pilot study.
items.abstract: Background Essential tremor (ET) is the most common movement disorder. Medical treatments are not always effective and can have side effects. Surgical interventions are not an option for all patients and can also have debilitating side effects. Objectives This project aims to develop a passive nonlinear vibration absorber namely, Nonlinear Energy Sink (NES), to reduce tremors in ET patients. Methods Five ET patients were enrolled. Tremor was assessed clinically using the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) rating scale and electrophysiological recording before and after short-duration device use. Results The NES bracelet led to a reduction of the FTM score of 32.1% (±19%) while tremor power was reduced by 49.2% (±23.4%) compared to baseline for the arm treated. No side effect was noted. items.title: Closed-Loop Targeted Memory Reactivation During Sleep Spindles Enhances Motor Memory Consolidation.
items.abstract: Sleep spindles are thought to facilitate motor memory consolidation by reactivating recently acquired memory traces during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, yet most human evidence is correlational. Using a closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (CL-TMR) protocol, this study tested whether auditory cueing time-locked to spindles enhances the consolidation of a newly acquired motor sequence. Twenty-six young adults practiced two eight-element, explicitly known, sequences of finger movements, each paired with a distinct auditory cue. During subsequent NREM Stage 2 and 3 nighttime sleep, a portable deep-learning-based EEG device (Portiloop) detected spindles online and selectively replayed the cue associated with one sequence (TMR condition), while the other served as a within-subject non-reactivated control (non-TMR) condition. Behavioural performance was assessed before and after sleep. Greater overnight improvements in performance were observed for the reactivated as compared to the non-reactivated condition, hence demonstrating enhanced consolidation following spindle-locked CL-TMR. The magnitude of this TMR benefit was positively correlated with the percentage of stimulations delivered during true spindles. Furthermore, a higher percentage of stimulations occurring during spindle trains (i.e., two or more spindles separated by 6 s apart) was associated with reduced gains. These findings provide further evidence that spindle-timed reactivation supports motor memory consolidation in humans and suggest that spindle trains may represent a favourable physiological window for closed-loop interventions.

items.title: Elucidation and reconstitution of the poplar salicortin biosynthetic pathway.
items.abstract: Salicinoids are specialized benzenoid (C 6 -C 1 ) metabolites characteristic of the Salicaceae family. Although salicinoids have long been recognized as effective defense compounds and pharmacologically active constituents in willows and poplars, the biosynthetic pathway underlying their formation remains largely unresolved. Through integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses of black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) roots, we identified candidate genes involved in salicinoid biosynthesis belonging to the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase family 92 (CYP92) and the progesterone 5β-reductase/iridoid synthase-like enzyme (PRISE) family of short-chain dehydrogenases/reductases. Co-expression of all identified candidate genes, together with the previously characterized glycosyltransferase gene PtUGT71L1, acyltransferase gene PtACT47, and cinnamic acid-CoA ligase gene PtCNL5, in Nicotiana benthamiana resulted in the production of salicortin, the most abundant salicinoid in poplar. Further characterization of the P450 candidates revealed that two enzymes catalyze ortho-hydroxylation of both aromatic rings of the proposed salicortin precursor, benzyl benzoate, while two other P450s catalyze the subsequent oxidative dearomatization of the benzoic acid-derived ring of benzyl benzoate. The resulting dieneone intermediate is converted by PRISE enzymes via a 1,4-reduction to form the characteristic 1-hydroxy-6-oxocyclohex-2-en-1-carboxylic ester moiety of salicortin. Functional redundancy among the identified CYP92 and PRISE enzymes may reflect the central role of these compounds in plant defense.

items.title: The uncinate fasciculus in frontotemporal dementia subtypes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of diffusion-tensor imaging studies.
items.abstract: BackgroundFrontotemporal dementia (FTD) is a leading cause of early-onset neurodegeneration with selective frontal and temporal lobe degeneration. Despite well-characterized gray and white matter atrophy patterns across FTD subtypes, the extent of degeneration of the uncinate fasciculus (UF) tract has not been systematically quantified across FTD subtypes.ObjectiveTo compare uncinate fasciculus fractional anisotropy, mean diffusivity, radial diffusivity, and axial diffusivity between frontotemporal dementia subtypes and healthy controls.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science and performed a random-effects meta-analysis of diffusion tensor imaging studies published between 2011 and October 2025 according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines.ResultsWe systematically reviewed 11 studies and performed a meta-analysis of 540 participants across 10 studies. We found that all FTD subtypes demonstrated significant degeneration of the UF compared to controls. The greatest effect sizes were observed when comparing the left UF between the semantic variant primary progressive aphasia (svPPA) and controls (FA: SMD = -2.5396, 95% CI: -3.7914, -1.2878, p < 0.0001; RD: SMD = 2.2414, 95% CI:1.7972, 2.6855, p < 0.0001; AD: SMD = 1.9831, 95% CI: 1.1434, 2.8227, p < 0.0001; MD: SMD = 2.5268, 95% CI: 1.9993, 3.0542, p < 0.0001), while the behavioral variant (bvFTD) showed the largest reduction in right UF fractional anisotropy. Within-group analyses revealed significant left-right asymmetry in svPPA and non-fluent aphasia (nfvPPA), with greater left UF involvement, while bvFTD and controls showed no hemispheric differences.ConclusionsWe highlight the UF as a promising tract for understanding disease mechanisms and developing imaging biomarkers in FTD.

items.title: Ten rules for identifying horizontal gene transfers in deep plant phylogenies.
items.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is one of the most intriguing aspects of genome evolution, challenging classical views of vertical inheritance. Growing genome availability across the tree of life offers opportunities to discover HGT, yet recent reanalyses suggest many reported cases may not withstand scrutiny. Detecting ancient transfers is especially difficult, as phylogenetic signal erodes over time and analytical choices strongly shape conclusions. Here we propose 10 practical rules for evaluating HGT in deep plant phylogenies, organised around three themes: genomic foundation, rigorous analytical framework, and biological interpretation. A reliable genomic foundation requires excluding contamination, verifying genomic integration, and avoiding biased taxon sampling. Rigorous phylogenetics is essential, as deep phylogenies are sensitive to alignment parameters, substitution model, rooting strategy, and branch support. We illustrate this with three glycosyl hydrolase families: for GH9 and GH32, analytical choices can eliminate apparent HGT signals entirely, while GH18 shows why complex, multi-domain families resist confident inference. Finally, HGT signatures demand cautious, biologically plausible interpretation. Recurrent gene duplication, loss, and domain shuffling commonly produce HGT-like patterns and should always be considered as alternatives. Our rules offer a pragmatic checklist helping authors and reviewers distinguish robust HGT from artefacts, fostering more reliable evidence on HGT in plants.

items.title: Histological description and bone compactness analysis of fossil (Aldabrachelys sp.) and extant Aldabra giant tortoise (Aldabrachelys gigantea) shell bone fragments.
items.abstract: Aldabra Atoll, north of Madagascar and part of the Seychelles Outer Islands, is home to the Aldabra giant tortoise, Aldabrachelys gigantea, the only survivor of several species of giant tortoises that were once widespread on islands across the Western Indian Ocean. Aldabra Atoll preserves an extensive fossil record of giant tortoises, providing a unique opportunity to compare the shell bone microanatomy of extinct and extant forms. This study presents the first detailed histological investigation of fossil Aldabrachelys sp. shell fragments and a preliminary comparison with extant A. gigantea. Additionally, bone compactness is determined. Most fossil specimens exhibit the typical diploe structure of tortoise shell bones, comprising external and internal cortices surrounding cancellous bone, although considerable variation in cortical thickness, vascularization, remodeling, the presence and abundance of Sharpey's fibers, and preservation was observed. In contrast, extant specimens generally display a more homogeneous microanatomy with less distinct regions. This variation is also reflected in the bone compactness. Fossil Aldabrachelys sp. fragments range between 45.1% and 84.9%, and those of extant A. gigantea fragments between 45.8% and 86.1%. The substantial intra- and interfragment variability observed in both histology and compactness complicates the identification of general microanatomical patterns and highlights the importance of considering regional shell variation. Our study establishes a baseline for future investigations of giant tortoise evolution, ecology, and insular adaptation via histological characterization of shell bones.

items.title: Engineering adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials: integrated biotechnology framework for regenerative medicine.
items.abstract: Natural polysaccharides are versatile building blocks for regenerative biomaterials because of their structural diversity, generally favorable biocompatibility and biodegradability, chemical tunability, and capacity for biologically relevant interactions. Advances in biotechnology and materials engineering have expanded their role from primarily structural matrices to multifunctional platforms that can influence cellular, immune, and biochemical processes during tissue repair. This review presents an integrated biological engineering framework linking polysaccharide source and molecular architecture with extraction and purification, chemical functionalization, crosslinking, advanced fabrication, biological recognition, and translational performance. Particular emphasis is placed on structure-function relationships, stereospecific glycan-receptor interactions, immune-instructive biomaterials, protein-mediated cell-material interactions, microbiome-responsive systems, and emerging artificial intelligence-assisted approaches for biomaterial design. The importance of material purity is also critically considered, particularly the potential for residual endotoxin contamination to confound interpretation of immunomodulatory responses and compromise reproducibility. Representative applications in skin, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, neural, and other regenerative systems illustrate how material composition, scaffold architecture, biofunctionalization, and manufacturing strategy collectively influence biological performance. Finally, challenges associated with scalable manufacturing, batch-to-batch reproducibility, sterilization, storage stability, quality control, regulatory translation, and clinical implementation are examined. By integrating molecular design, biological mechanisms, fabrication, and translational requirements, this review provides engineering principles for the development of adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials and identifies priorities for advancing reproducible and clinically translatable regenerative technologies.

items.title: Coupling irrigation technology upgrades with targeted expansion enables water-efficient and climate-resilient cereal production in China.
items.abstract: Irrigation expansion and water-saving technologies are essential for future water and food security, yet approaches that jointly improve resource conservation, yield stability and investment efficiency remain elusive. Here we integrate 42,190 county-level agricultural records, a nationally representative farmer survey comprising 3,576 observations and 2,230 controlled field experiments on maize, wheat and rice. We show that China's shift towards more efficient irrigation reduced water use by 6.6-13.4% since 2010, but the continuation of historical trends is insufficient to meet national targets or protect yields under future climate change. We identify an optimized investment pathway that combines upgrades in existing irrigated areas with targeted expansion. This crop- and region-specific approach could raise yields by 0.1-10.9% while reducing water use by at least 25.5%, with rice offering the greatest savings potential. This framework provides actionable guidance for strategic irrigation investment in China to support sustainable agricultural intensification.

items.title: Hormesis as a universal cellular strategy for growth.
items.abstract: Our review synthesizes a vast and dispersed literature to demonstrate that subtoxic doses of structurally diverse chemicals can induce a conserved growth-stimulatory (hormetic) response across bacterial, microalgal, plant, and mammalian cells. Stimulation is concentration- and exposure-time-dependent, with higher concentrations inhibiting growth. In eukaryotic models, moderate ROS signaling and activation of DNA-PKcs/Akt, ERK1/2, PI3K/AKT, mTOR, or AURKA accompany growth stimulation, with Cyclin D-CDK4 promoting G1/S transition in mammalian cells. The proliferative DNA-PKcs/Akt response is observed in human hepatic cells, while bacterial examples involve LuxR-dependent signaling and fatty acid β-oxidation. Metabolism rewires, with some microalgae enhancing glycolysis and Krebs cycling, whereas other photosynthetic microorganisms reroute photosynthetic carbon toward lipid or starch storage while downregulating selected carbohydrate-catabolic proteins. Nrf2-driven antioxidants in mammalian cells, carotenoids, and detoxifying enzymes are upregulated, establishing a preconditioned state that can attenuate apoptosis upon subsequent challenge. Within the Catabolic-Anabolic Cycling Hormesis (CACH) model, some time-dependent responses are consistent with an anabolic overshoot following a transient catabolic decline (ATP depletion). This anabolic reprogramming accompanies biofilm formation, altered motility, and, in neoplastic cells, anchorage-independent growth. Thus, cell proliferation is a metabolic strategy shaped by adversity, with functional consequences that depend on cellular context and the endpoint assessed.

items.title: Population-specific transcriptomic bioactivity assessment of perfluorooctanoic acid using human liver spheroids and physiologically based toxicokinetic modeling.
items.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) has been widely used in industrial and consumer products and was recently classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer. However, uncertainties remain regarding transcriptomic bioactivity thresholds associated with liver effects and their variability across clinically relevant populations. In this study, previously published transcriptomic data obtained following 24-h and 10-day exposure of primary human liver spheroids (LS) to PFOA were integrated into a physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK), population-specific framework to estimate transcriptomic human equivalent doses (HEDs). In addition, exploratory concordance analysis was performed between PFOA-responsive genes and liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC)-associated transcriptomic profiles. Median transcriptomic HEDs ranged from 283 to 412 µg/kg body weight (bw)/week and were substantially higher than the estimated HEDs corresponding to the 95th percentile serum PFOA concentration in the U.S. population (0.0099 µg/kg bw/week) and the mean PFOA concentrations reported in human liver tissue samples (0.035 µg/kg bw/week). Obesity class III, cirrhosis Child-Pugh classes A and B, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease reduced transcriptomic HEDs by approximately 31-41% compared with the healthy population, although HEDs remained substantially above reference values. Gene-level analysis identified only a limited number of genes within the bioactivity exposure ratio range of 1-100. More than 50% of PFOA-responsive genes exhibited concordant expression patterns with LIHC-associated transcriptomic profiles. Although the biological significance of these overlaps remains uncertain, concordance significantly exceeded that expected by chance from a background gene set and was driven mainly by down-regulated genes. Overall, this study provides a population-informed framework for integrating transcriptomic bioactivity data with PBTK modeling in human-relevant assessment of PFOA-associated liver effects.

items.title: The mediating roles of depression and demoralization daily hassles and behavioral inhibition as predictors of post-MI self-care: the distinct pathways of depression and demoralization.
items.abstract: Effective self-care after myocardial infarction (MI) is essential for secondary prevention, yet many individuals struggle to maintain recommended health behaviors. Daily hassles and psychological distress may interfere with self-care, but the roles of depressive symptoms and demoralization have not been sufficiently examined simultaneously. Although these forms of distress may co-occur, they reflect distinct psychological experiences. Depression is characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, and related cognitive and motivational symptoms, whereas demoralization centers on perceived inability to cope, helplessness, and loss of meaning or purpose. This cross-sectional study examined the associations of daily hassles and behavioral inhibition (BI) with self-care behaviors after MI and tested whether depressive symptoms and demoralization statistically mediated these associations. Participants were 175 individuals who had experienced MI (mean age = 54.42 years, SD = 12.03; 58% male; 79% married) completed self-report questionnaires assessing self-care behaviors, daily hassles, BI, depressive symptoms, and demoralization. The mean time since MI was 12.08 months (SD = 4.26; range = 6-19 months). Structural equation modeling examined the hypothesized associations and indirect effects. Self-care behaviors were negatively associated with daily hassles, BI, depressive symptoms, and demoralization. Participants generally reported adequate dietary adherence and medication management but lower levels of physical activity. The model showed good fit to the data (CFI = .98, TLI = .95, RMSEA = .08). Depressive symptoms significantly mediated the associations of daily hassles and BI with self-care behaviors (indirect βs = -.09 to -.10, p p < .05). Overall, depressive symptoms and demoralization showed distinct indirect associations with poorer post-MI self-care. The findings highlight the relevance of considering multiple dimensions of psychological distress in psychosocial approaches to secondary prevention.

items.title: Mindfulness-based perioperative care, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, and early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a prospective observational cohort study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between perioperative care by mindfulness and sleep quality, autonomic regulation, inflammatory activity, and early recurrence of atrial tachyarrhythmia (AT) following radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) for atrial fibrillation (AF). This was a prospective assessor-blinded observational cohort study involving 124 patients with AF who underwent their initial radiofrequency catheter ablation from April 2023 to December 2025. Conventional perioperative care was provided to one group (n=62), while the other group (n=62) received mindfulness-based perioperative care. To reduce baseline imbalance, propensity score overlap weighting was implemented. Objective sleep architecture was assessed by overnight polysomnography and autonomic function was examined by HRV analysis. hs-CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and MCP-1 were analyzed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Health related quality of life was determined based on the SF-36 questionnaire. Compared with conventional care, mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with greater observed changes in total sleep time (389.4 ± 43.8 vs. 365.7 ± 45.2 min, P=0.012), sleep efficiency (77.4 ± 7.2% vs. 71.2 ± 7.8%, P=0.004), sleep onset latency (27.1 ± 8.8 vs. 34.8 ± 10.5 min, P=0.009), and PSQI scores (7.2 ± 2.5 vs. 9.3 ± 2.9, P=0.006). The mindfulness group also showed lower inflammatory biomarker levels and differences in short-term autonomic indices, including a lower LF/HF ratio (1.39 ± 0.41 vs. 1.66 ± 0.54, P=0.005). Early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence occurred in 6 patients (9.7%) in the mindfulness-based perioperative care group and in 11 patients (17.7%) in the conventional care group, corresponding to a crude risk ratio of 0.55 (95% CI: 0.22-1.38). Mindfulness-based perioperative care was associated with improved objective and subjective sleep quality, more favorable autonomic and inflammatory biomarker profiles, better postoperative quality of life, and a lower observed rate of early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for AF.

items.title: Decision-making in biospecimen and biomarker research among African American participants: Procedure-specific perspectives including on the uniqueness of brain donation.
items.abstract: BackgroundAfrican Americans are disproportionately affected by Alzheimer's disease (AD) but remain significantly underrepresented in research. While previous studies often assess these barriers to such research engagement using hypothetical scenarios, there is a need to focus on in vivo decision-making processesObjectiveTo identify the specific facilitators and barriers influencing African American participants' decisions to engage in or decline four types of biospecimen data collection: biomarker collection via MRI, PET, or lumbar puncture (LP), and brain donation.MethodsSemi-structured interviews were conducted with 41 participants (68.2% female; age range 58-84; average 68) recruited from the African Americans Fighting Alzheimer's in Midlife Study who had made the decision for or against these four types of research. items.title: The Kessler 6 psychological distress scale (K6) in swedish: a psychometric study of reliability, factor structure and measurement invariance in a large population-based sample.
items.abstract: Background Psychological distress is a major public health concern, and brief, reliable screening instruments are essential for early detection and monitoring. The six-item Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6) is widely used internationally; however, evidence regarding its psychometric properties in Sweden remains limited. This study examined the reliability, factor structure, and measurement invariance of the Swedish version of the K6 in a large population-based sample. Methods Data were obtained from the Life and Health Survey (2022), conducted in five regions in Mid-Sweden. The study included 31,759 adults aged 18-102 years. Internal consistency was assessed using McDonald's omega total. Structural validity was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis, comparing a one-factor model, a two-factor model representing depression and anxiety, and a bifactor model comprising a general psychological distress factor and two specific factors representing depression and anxiety. Measurement invariance of one-factor model was examined across age groups and by gender using multigroup CFA, testing configural and metric invariance. Results Internal consistency was high across all demographic groups (McDonald's omega total 0.883-0.899). The one-factor model demonstrated best fit, with acceptable values according to CFI, TLI, and SRMR, but unacceptable according to RMSEA (CFI = 0.996, TLI=0.993, RMSEA=0.069, SRMR=0.020), with standardized loadings ranging from 0.70 to 0.91. The two-factor model showed acceptable fit according to CFI, TLI and SRMR, but unacceptable fit according to RMSEA (CFI=0.989, TLI=0.982, RMSEA=0.109, SRMR=0.040). Standardized factor loadings were high for both factors (Factor 1: 0.78; Factor 2: 0.78-0.91). The correlation between the two latent factors was extremely strong (r=.99). The bifactor model did not converge and therefore could not be evaluated or interpreted further. Configural and metric invariance were supported across the age groups and between men and women. Conclusions The Swedish version of the K6 demonstrates strong reliability and supports a unidimensional structure. Measurement invariance testing supported comparable measurement of psychological distress across age and gender. The scale is suitable for monitoring psychological distress in public health surveys and may also be useful as a brief screening tool in clinical practice. Further research should establish clinically relevant threshold values in a Swedish context. Trial registration Not applicable.

items.title: Can large language models code meaning-making? A multi-model validation of automated autobiographical reasoning scoring in Chinese adolescent narratives.
items.abstract: Autobiographical reasoning (AR) involves drawing self-relevant meaning from personal experiences. It is central to narrative identity research, but manual coding requires substantial time and trained coders. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automating other narrative coding tasks, but their capacity for meaning-making judgments that may depend on implicit event-self connections remains untested. We collected autobiographical narratives from 437 Chinese high school students and evaluated three LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-Max) across four prompting strategies (zero-shot, chain-of-thought, 3-shot, 5-shot) using three scoring granularities (binary, ordinal, continuous). The best-performing condition (DeepSeek-V3, zero-shot) achieved Run 1 Cohen's κ = .416; three-run majority-vote accuracy rose from 54.9% for AR-absent texts to 94.4% for moderate-to-high-AR texts, revealing strongly condition-dependent performance. In the fully crossed subset, paired-bootstrap confidence intervals for CoT-minus-zero-shot differences included zero for all three models. Error analysis identified two bias patterns: false negatives concentrated in low-AR texts (OR = 3.99, p < .001) and false positives consistent with over-interpretation of emotional expression. Under the models, prompts, corpus, and scoring rules tested here, general-purpose LLMs cannot replace formal manual AR coding.

items.title: A web-based spot-the-difference paradigm for studying social information processing in naturalistic visual scenes.
items.abstract: This pilot study introduced and assessed a novel web-based spot-the-difference paradigm for investigating social information processing in naturalistic visual scenes. The task systematically manipulated both the presence versus absence of social elements (i.e., social figures) and the location of the target difference (social vs. nonsocial regions). Participants identified differences via mouse clicks while their eye movements and mouse trajectories were recorded simultaneously throughout the task. In Study 1, behavioral and eye-tracking data supported the task's sensitivity to social salience, as evidenced by differences in accuracy and reaction times for social versus nonsocial target differences, along with consistently greater gaze fixation on social regions regardless of where the target difference appeared. In comparison, mouse-tracking data reflected more goal-oriented behavior, with cursor trajectories more frequently falling within regions containing the target difference. Study 2 further showed that this paradigm was sensitive to individual differences in autistic traits. Participants with higher autistic trait scores exhibited slower responses specifically in social contexts, irrespective of the location of the target difference, suggesting increased cognitive demands during social information processing. However, their gaze and mouse movement patterns remained comparable to those with lower autistic trait scores. Collectively, these findings suggest that this paradigm may provide a scalable and flexible approach for studying social cognition beyond traditional laboratory settings and may help capture the dynamic unfolding of social information processing through integrated multimodal data.

items.title: Spatial-numerical associations survive spatial frequency equalization in an adult unimanual SNARC task.
items.abstract: The origins of spatial-numerical associations (SNAs), such as the SNARC (Spatial-Numerical Association of Response Codes) effect, remain debated. The Brain's Asymmetric Frequency Tuning (BAFT) hypothesis recently proposed that non-symbolic SNAs may arise from hemispheric asymmetries in spatial frequency (SF) processing, rather than reflecting a genuine spatial representation of number. Here we examined whether SNAs persist even in adult human cognition when both SF cues and, crucially, bimanual response confounds are eliminated. Participants performed a Go/No-Go non-symbolic magnitude comparison task, in which lateralized dot-arrays were compared to a central reference. Critically, all stimuli were controlled for low-level visual properties, including luminance and the SF power spectrum, thereby neutralizing potential SF hemispheric asymmetries. In addition, responses were executed using a single central key, removing any contribution of bimanual spatial coding. Results revealed a robust ratio effect, consistent with Weberian numerosity processing. Crucially, a significant SNARC congruency effect emerged in both accuracy and reaction times: relatively smaller numerosities were processed more efficiently when presented in the left visual space, whereas larger numerosities showed a right visual space advantage. Converging evidence from continuous regression analyses further supported this spatial-numerical mapping, showing an asymmetrical advantage for smaller magnitudes in left visual space and larger magnitudes in right visual space. This pattern persisted despite lacking SF asymmetries and bimanual response mappings. Together, these findings weaken the BAFT hypothesis, but only in adulthood, by showing that non-symbolic SNAs cannot be reduced to low-level visual or response-related confounds. Instead, they support a higher-order representation of numerical magnitude likely mapped onto space.

items.title: The SPOT Grid: Naturalistic images with predefined settings, patterns, objects, and textures.
items.abstract: In the natural world, higher-level visual features (e.g., scenes and objects) systematically covary with specific lower-level constituent features (e.g., textures and patterns). This natural covariation makes it difficult to isolate aspects of behavior or brain activity that are specific to a single level of the feature hierarchy. For example, a particular neural or behavioral response may reflect recognition of a "jungle" scene, or it may reflect sensitivity to the lower-level features - leaf textures, dense vertical lines, etc. - that constitute jungle scenes. To address this challenge, we developed a novel approach for partially decoupling higher- and lower-level features in naturalistic images. We employed a Stable Diffusion image generation framework to create a naturalistic image set in which setting-object pairings and texture-pattern pairings are factorially combined, enabling systematic manipulation of higher-level and lower-level image content. To validate our approach, we used state-of-the-art image-processing models to confirm that higher-level features are represented similarly regardless of their lower-level constituents and, conversely, that lower-level features are represented similarly regardless of the higher-level objects/settings they constitute. We then confirmed that human participants can readily and rapidly categorize these features in our generated images. We present the image generation framework and introduce the SPOT (Settings, Patterns, Objects, Textures) Grid, a publicly available stimulus set accompanied by image-specific metrics (upon request: forms.gle/X2HpzRYUGigFS1S27). This resource provides new opportunities for investigating hierarchical visual representations, feature binding, and abstraction across perception, behavior, and the brain.

items.title: Morphological analysis when morphemes are hard to detect: Evidence from infixation and reduplication.
items.abstract: There is substantial psycholinguistic evidence that skilled reading involves morphological analysis, whereby morphologically complex words like teacher are recognised via constituent morphemes {teach}+{-er}. The ability to recognise morphemes is vital as it allows readers to interpret both familiar and unfamiliar words. However, over 50% of the evidence for this claim comes from studies of suffixation in English, where morphemes typically have a relatively consistent surface form across exemplars (clean in cleaner, cleanliness; -ed in walked, jumped). It remains unclear whether morphological analysis is also robust when morphemes lack a consistent surface form. Using the morpheme interference paradigm in Tagalog, we test whether infixes and reduplicants are detected during prelexical processing. Infixes are inserted within a stem and therefore reduce the consistency of its surface realisation (e.g., tawag → t-in-awag 'called'), while reduplicants involve partial or full copying of a stem and therefore lack a consistent surface realisation (e.g., tawag and lundag become tatawag 'will call' and lulundag 'will jump', where ta- and lu- are instances of the same reduplicant morpheme). We found robust morpheme interference effects in both accuracy and RTs. Specifically, nonwords with morphological structure induced significantly lower accuracy and longer RTs than nonwords without. Our findings show skilled readers' acquired sensitivity to these sophisticated morphological structures and motivate refinements to theories of morpheme learning.

items.title: Stimulation uncertainty reveals distinct mechanisms of sensation seeking and impulsivity.
items.abstract: Sensation-seeking is often described as a tendency to pursue novel and stimulating experiences, yet such options are often uncertain as well. This creates a central ambiguity where choices that appear to reflect attraction to stimulation may instead reflect tolerance of uncertain outcomes, or an interaction between the two. Across two experiments, we tested how expected stimulation and stimulation uncertainty shape reward-guided choice. A reanalysis of a previous operant sensation-seeking dataset suggests that stimulation uncertainty explained behaviour better than expected stimulation. Subsequently, we conducted a preregistered online experiment to investigate the joint effects of expected stimulation and stimulation uncertainty and to compare their respective associations with sensation-seeking and impulsivity. Our results indicate that higher sensation-seeking was associated with broader stochastic sampling and lower reward performance, but this was not reducible to random choice or uncertainty tolerance alone. Instead, uncertainty weighting depended on the value assigned to expected stimulation. This profile differed from impulsivity, suggesting that the two traits shape choice through distinct computational routes. By separating expected stimulation from uncertainty, these findings refine accounts of exploratory choice by showing that sensation-seeking shapes not only how much people sample uncertain options, but how stimulation value and uncertainty are jointly weighted during choice.

items.title: Lymphoedema in Head and Neck Cancer Survivors: Healthcare Professionals' Perspectives.
items.abstract: Introduction Improvements in head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment have increased survival rates, resulting in survivors living with side effects, such as head and neck lymphoedema (HNL). We aimed to document healthcare professionals' perceptions of HNL, approaches to managing HNL, and integration of HNL management into routine practice in Australia and New Zealand. Methods We conducted an online, 51-item survey between February and October 2024. The survey comprised two main sections: (i) all healthcare professionals working with HNC and HNL; and (ii) only HNL therapists. Results Participants included in the analysis of the (i) HNC healthcare professionals section (n = 73/113), and (ii) HNL therapists section (n = 40/46). 45% (n = 33/73) of the participants reported not having access to a specialized multidisciplinary team for HNL management. 55% (n = 22/40) of HNL therapists reported not having standardized institutional lymphoedema management protocols. Conclusions Findings highlight the need for system-level guidelines, clearer pathways, improved education resources, and coordinated MDTs to improve HNL management.

items.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment.
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant potential to support diagnostic decision making; however, the collaboration between clinicians and AI systems often does not surpass the performance of unaided humans or standalone AI. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI advice on diagnostic decision making among experts and novices, focusing on the occurrence of AI over-reliance and under-reliance and the potential mitigating effect of explainable AI. Methods We used a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experimental design. Participants (50 task experts [radiologists] and 75 novices [non-radiologist physicians and medical trainees]) were randomly assigned in equal proportions to one of six groups, which determined the order in which the three conditions were presented across the three sessions. In each session, participants read 50 head CT scans with or without the presence of an intracranial haemorrhage, under one of three experimental conditions: control, no AI prediction; basic AI advice, AI prediction without annotations; and explainable AI advice, AI prediction with scan annotations. 80% of cases with basic or explainable AI advice received correct advice, and 20% received incorrect advice. The main outcomes were diagnostic performance (the correct identification of intracranial haemorrhage), confidence in the diagnosis, case reading time, and AI advice usefulness ratings. We defined under-reliance as a final decision that did not align with correct AI advice, and over-reliance as a final decision that aligned with incorrect AI advice. All elements of the project were preregistered and are available on the project's Open Science Framework repository. Findings Data were collected between Feb 16, 2023, and Aug 10, 2023. Both over-reliance on incorrect advice and under-reliance on correct advice occurred. Under-reliance was associated with high uncertainty and, in absolute terms, had a more detrimental effect on diagnostic performance than over-reliance. Correct explainable AI advice reduced under-reliance and improved performance (OR=1·84, p Interpretation The occurrence of both under-reliance and over-reliance highlights the need for efficient counterstrategies beyond classic explainable AI methods to foster appropriate reliance and synergy in AI-supported clinical decision-making. Funding Volkswagen Foundation, Forum for Interdisciplinary Research, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.

items.title: Inclusion of a multi-ancestry polygenic risk score into a machine learning weight gain prediction model: an observational analysis from the NIH All of Us Research Program.
items.abstract: Objective Obesity is a public health crisis with few effective preventative treatments limited by challenges in identifying who is at high risk of weight gain. To address this gap, our group has developed machine learning weight gain prediction models with modest predictive power. In this study, we aimed to build upon our prior work by incorporating a multi-ancestry polygenic risk score (MAPRS) into a machine learning model and hypothesized that its inclusion would improve weight gain prediction performance. Materials and methods Adults aged 18-70 years with weight measurements 2 years apart were identified within the NIH All of Us Research Program. Participants with a history of cancer, bariatric surgery, or pregnancy were excluded. XGBoost machine learning models were developed using demographics, vitals, laboratory data, obesity-related comorbidities, and MAPRS. The primary outcome was total body weight (TBW) gain of ≥10% over 2 years. Performance was compared using the area under the curves (AUCs). Results The cohort consisted of 40 205 individuals (mean [SD] age 51.1[13.5] years; 56.1% female; 48.5% White, non-Hispanic), 3806 (9.5%) of whom gained ≥10% TBW over 2 years. Model performance with and without MAPRS was similar, with AUCs of 0.705 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.692-0.718) and 0.697 (0.683-0.710), respectively. Baseline age and MAPRS had the highest variable importance. The best net reclassification index was 0.7%, indicating marginal improvements in risk classification with MAPRS. Discussion Despite the known hereditary components of obesity and the strong association between the MAPRS and weight gain, incorporating a MAPRS did not substantially enhance model performance. Conclusion Further optimization of integrating polygenic risk scores into machine learning weight gain prediction models is needed before they can be applied in the clinical setting.

items.title: Lightweight open-source reasoning large language model for evidence synthesis screening.
items.abstract: Objectives To evaluate performance and efficiency of a lightweight open-source reasoning large language model (LLM) against an expert-derived reference standard for screening scientific publication databases. Materials and methods Two expert reviewers screened subsets of database records across 3 stages: (1) base eligibility ( n = 200), (2) obesity focus ( n = 200), and (3) women of reproductive age focus ( n = 150). The LLM (gpt-oss-20b) screened all records ( n = 20 118). Performance (F1-score and sensitivity [recall]) and efficiency (average screening rate) were assessed. Results Interreader agreement was near-perfect ( κ : 0.99-1.00; all P .001). LLM performance was high: F1-score, 0.83-0.94; sensitivity, 90%-95%; specificity, 86%-99%; accuracy, 89%-94%; precision, 77%-99%; and negative predictive value (NPV), 89%-96%. LLM screening was faster than reviewers (19.4 vs ∼1.0 records/min). Discussion The LLM achieved high performance and efficiency relative to an expert-derived reference standard for screening. Conclusion The use of lightweight open-source reasoning LLMs shows promise to support screening in evidence synthesis workflows.

items.title: Building sustainable resilient health systems: The Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists statement on desflurane.
items.abstract: Climate change is recognised as a public health emergency requiring urgent and decisive action. The adverse effects on the environment from delivering healthcare are well established, and identifying areas for positive change that are under our direct control as anaesthetists is imperative. Desflurane, a volatile anaesthetic gas, has significantly greater negative environmental and financial impacts, with little benefit to patient safety or quality of care, compared with clinically equivalent alternatives. In this context, the Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists released a statement on desflurane in 2024 to provide balanced guidance for reducing desflurane consumption based on current evidence and expert consensus opinion. This article summarises the background for the statement and presents the 'ANZCA Statement on Desflurane' verbatim.

items.title: Advancing women's health in Egypt: an economic evaluation of the presidential initiative for nationwide breast cancer early detection and treatment.
items.abstract: Background Breast cancer (BC) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide and poses a major public health and economic challenge in Egypt, where late-stage diagnosis remains high. Egypt launched the Presidential Initiative for Women's Health, a nationwide, publicly funded program providing free early detection, diagnostic, and treatment services. This study presents a model-based economic evaluation of the initiative. Methods A hybrid decision tree and Markov model compared the Presidential Initiative pathway with opportunistic case detection, from a societal perspective over a lifetime horizon. Outcomes were quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), life years, net societal cost, and return on investment (ROI); health outcomes were not monetized. Model structure was assessed using face, internal, and cross-validation following the ISPOR-SMDM taxonomy with structured review by 16 clinical and program co-authors. Uncertainty was examined using Monte Carlo probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA) with 5000 iterations. Inputs were national program data for July 2019 to September 2024. Results Approximately 23.8 million unique women generated 53,453,745 recorded screening and service encounters. Among confirmed cases, the observed stage I to II proportion was 61.3% in the initiative data versus 41.6% in the comparator. The model estimated 32,576 incremental QALYs and 63,448 additional discounted life years, with total societal costs of EGP 11.68 billion (USD 258 million) versus EGP 18.07 billion (USD 398 million), a net societal saving of EGP 6.39 billion (USD 141 million) and an ROI of 54.7%. In the PSA, at the Egyptian threshold of EGP 164,588 per QALY, the initiative was cost-effective in all 5,000 simulations (100%), and dominant in 4,988 (99.76%), with a base-case net monetary benefit of EGP 11.75 billion (USD 259 million). Conclusions Under the observed program stage distribution, the Presidential Initiative was projected to provide greater modeled health outcomes at lower societal cost than opportunistic case detection, dominant in the base-case and cost-effective at the Egyptian threshold in every simulation. These are model-based estimates conditional on transferred survival and utility inputs. The findings support continued program evaluation and investment alongside collection of Egyptian long-term outcome data.

items.title: The accumulation of adverse life events across the life course and their association with mental health and well-being: exploring gender heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Background Most individuals experience multiple adverse life events across their life course, accumulating into cumulative disadvantage with lasting consequences for mental health and well-being. Evidence suggests that women's mental health and well-being is more vulnerable to the negative consequences of single adverse life events, due to gender differences in event perception, available resources, and preferred coping strategies. Until now it's unclear whether these gendered patterns hold when looking at the accumulation of adverse events over a life course. The aim of this study is to examine if the accumulation of adverse life events is associated with depressive symptomatology, life satisfaction, and quality of life with a central focus on gender differences in these relationships. Methods A secondary data analysis was conducted using Wave 3 of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). Accumulation of adverse life events was operationalized as the number of different adverse events experienced during the life course, covering 22 life events. Three accumulation scores were calculated: a total score (TCALE) including all adverse events and two separate scores for self-oriented (SOCALE) and other-oriented (OOCALE) adverse events. Associations with depressive symptomatology, life satisfaction, and quality of life were analyzed using logistic and linear regression models. Interaction terms between accumulation scores and gender were included to examine gender differences in these associations. Results Greater accumulation of adverse life events is associated with higher likelihood of depressive symptomatology, lower life satisfaction, and reduced quality of life. Gender moderates the relationships for TCALE, with women being more vulnerable to the accumulation of adverse life events. Although no consistent gender interactions could be found for SOCALE and OOCALE, non-significant trends, for OOCALE, aligned with the patterns observed for the total accumulation score. Conclusion Cumulative life course adversity is a significant risk factor for poorer mental health and well-being, with women showing heightened vulnerability.

items.title: Jail-based opioid treatment implementation, outcomes, and costs: lessons learned from the Massachusetts Justice Community Opioid Innovation Network (MassJCOIN).
items.abstract: Limited access to medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) is a major driver of the opioid overdose crisis. Jails have been slow to implement MOUD treatment, especially agonist medications (methadone, buprenorphine). Massachusetts mandated certain county jails pilot-test delivery of all FDA-approved MOUD treatments, stipulating jails continue MOUD, or initiate it prior to release, and facilitate MOUD continuation in the community post-release. The Massachusetts Justice Community Opioid Innovation Network (MassJCOIN) partnered with seven pilot jails, the Massachusetts Department of Public Health, and community treatment providers to conduct a Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study of this carceral MOUD program. Drawing from selected MassJCOIN evidence on MOUD treatment program implementation, outcomes, and costs, we consider how findings can inform more effective, humane public health and clinical responses to treating incarcerated individuals. MOUD treatment in jail improves treatment engagement, reduces recidivism, and saves lives. MOUD program implementation facilitators included: policies and processes to offer universal MOUD access; transformative and adaptive leadership; appropriate staffing capacity and capabilities; proactive prevention of MOUD diversion; and consideration of patient preferences for MOUD treatment and co-occurring mental health conditions. MOUD program success was influenced by the legislative mandate and other major statewide changes and a community-based treatment system conducive to MOUD implementation. MOUD treatment continuity post-release was facilitated by re-entry planning and preparing individuals for post-release risk environments. Site-specific costs of implementing and sustaining MOUD programming provide information for decisions about program design, budgetary needs, and resource allocation. Carceral MOUD programming is a compelling strategy to advance public safety and public health. Lessons learned provide a playbook for broader diffusion of carceral MOUD programs and can help carceral leadership, healthcare providers, and policymakers make carceral healthcare improvements. Within a harm reduction framework, carceral MOUD treatment can provide substantial opportunities to fill gaps in public health prevention efforts and clinical care to reduce opioid overdose and other concomitant risks. Carceral MOUD programming offers ways for carceral systems to work for the common good, garner trust in public institutions, and increase their legitimacy and value as public institutions.

items.title: Plan for Scale Out: Adapting a Diabetes Prevention Program for Implementation in Rural and Remote British Columbia.
items.abstract: Background Rural and remote communities in Canada face a higher incidence and risk of developing type 2 diabetes (T2D) compared to urban populations (Government of Canada SC, 2022). Small Steps for Big Changes is an evidence-based diabetes prevention program designed to support individuals at risk of T2D in adopting and maintaining sustainable changes to their diet and exercise through the application of behavior change techniques. To expand the reach of Small Steps for Big Changes and address the significant gap in T2D prevention resources in rural and remote communities, the program was scaled out to rural and remote community organizations across British Columbia. The aim of this study was to describe the process used to scale out Small Steps for Big Changes and to identify the program and implementation strategy (IS) adaptations made during the pre-implementation phase to support delivery. Method Adoption rates were analyzed and reported according to the adoption dimension of the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) framework (Glasgow et al., Am J Public Health 89(9):1322-1327, 1999 Sep) to describe the proportion of settings willing to deliver Small Steps for Big Changes. Data on adaptations were extracted from meeting notes and email correspondence. Adaptations to IS were identified by comparing these data to IS used in a previous Small Steps for Big Changes implementation project. All adaptations were deductively coded by two independent coders using the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications to Evidence-Based Interventions (S, Wiltsey Stirman et al., Implement Sci 14(1):58, 2019 Jun 6) and the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications to Implementation Strategies (CJ Miller et al., Implement Sci 16(1):36, 2021 Apr 7). Results Three organizations in the Interior and two in the Northern region of British Columbia adopted Small Steps for Big Changes, representing adoption rates of 23% and 22%, respectively. Twenty-seven program adaptations were made with a primary goal of improving program oversight and quality improvement. 15 implementation strategy adaptations were identified and an additional 15 implementation strategies were added to support scale-out in attempts to improve reach, adoption, acceptability, or fidelity of the program. Conclusion These findings can inform targeted implementation efforts and guide decisions about scaling diabetes prevention programs, such as Small Steps for Big Changes, into diverse community settings.
