items.title: Structural brain correlates of symptom severity in stress-induced exhaustion.
items.abstract: Exhaustion due to chronic stress, a hallmark feature of burnout, represents a substantial and growing public health burden, yet its structural brain correlates remain poorly understood. We used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to examine associations between regional gray matter volume and symptom severity in a cohort of 300 individuals on self-reported sick leave due to the Swedish medical condition stress-induced exhaustion disorder (ED), characterized by debilitating fatigue following prolonged stress exposure. Symptom severity was assessed using the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire (SMBQ-18) and its subscales. Overall symptom severity (SMBQ-18 total score) and Physical Exhaustion (PE) were negatively associated with gray matter volume in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a region implicated in stress regulation and affective control, which remained significant when adjusting for depressive symptoms. An exploratory finding was that Listlessness was negatively associated with gray matter volume in the bilateral hippocampi and right middle temporal gyrus after adjustment for depressive symptoms. These results provide evidence from a large cohort for brain-symptom associations in chronic stress and highlight the value of dimensional approaches for capturing heterogeneity in stress-related conditions.

items.title: Natural Products as Protective Modulators of Environmental Pollutant Toxicity Through the Gut-X Axis.
items.abstract: Environmental pollutants, including heavy metals, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, particulate matter, persistent organic pollutants, pesticides, and micro/nanoplastics, perturb the gut microbiome and intestinal barrier and propagate oxidative, inflammatory, metabolic, and epigenetic injury through interconnected gut-organ axes. This narrative review reframes the gut-X axis as a mechanistic platform for evaluating natural products as protective agents against pollutant toxicity. We summarize pollutant-induced dysbiosis, barrier dysfunction, microbial-metabolite disruption, and immunometabolic reprogramming, then examine evidence for natural products and microbiota-active interventions, including polyphenols, flavonoids, triterpenoids, medicinal-plant constituents, polysaccharides, dietary fibers, and probiotic-derived strategies. Particular attention is given to antioxidant and anti-inflammatory signaling, restoration of epithelial integrity, modulation of short-chain fatty acids and bile acids, suppression of TLR4/NF-κB and NLRP3 signaling, and regulation of immune-cell metabolism. The available literature contains stronger mechanistic evidence than direct pollutant-specific intervention studies; therefore, established protective mechanisms are distinguished from evidence that remains indirect or preclinical. The review identifies the gut-X axis as a promising route through which natural products may reduce systemic consequences of environmental exposure and highlights priorities for pollutant-specific animal studies, human cohorts, pharmacokinetic characterization, combination strategies, and integrated multi-omics and in silico approaches.

items.title: Brief Social Gameplay Accelerates Attentional Reorienting and Enhances Sensorimotor Learning in Preschool Children.
items.abstract: A large body of research in developmental science and comparative biology identifies social play as a fundamental driver of learning and experience-dependent plasticity in some species. Rather than rehearsing stereotyped behaviors, social play is thought to promote adaptive responses to uncertainty through dynamic, reciprocal interactions. However, whether these functional properties produce immediate cognitive benefits during early childhood remains unknown. Here, we tested whether a brief session of socio-competitive gameplay (Mario Kart™ 8 Deluxe), implementing key functional properties of social play, could transiently modulate attentional reorienting and sensorimotor learning in preschool children. Using a within-subject crossover design (n = 33), including no-play and an active object-play control (Tangram), we found that only 30minutes of socio-competitive gameplay play accelerated the emergence of inhibition of return and selectively enhanced dominant-hand sensorimotor learning. Importantly, cross-SOA attentional modulation following socio-competitive gameplay was associated with late-phase dominant-hand advantage in manual dexterity. These findings show that brief exposure to a socially contingent digital environment can rapidly modify attentional dynamics and facilitate online sensorimotor learning in five-year-old children. Although digital gameplay cannot fully reproduce the embodied nature of physical social play, our results suggest that videogames implementing key functional properties of social play may transiently engage evolved mechanisms supporting behavioral flexibility and surprise-driven learning. More broadly, the immediate cognitive benefits of play may depend less on its physical form than on the computational demands it places on the developing brain.

items.title: Selective control of course correction over long timescales in the Drosophila central complex.
items.abstract: The insect central complex governs intricate navigational behaviors. One key region of the central complex, the fan-shaped body (FB), is where movement decisions are computed during goal-directed behaviors. However, our knowledge of when FB circuits are deployed is limited, and the FB has only been directly implicated in a few, narrowly defined behaviors. Here, we demonstrate that FB circuits affect course-correcting movements that, over long timescales, align the fly's heading with the perceived direction of optic flow. Silencing a major input neuronal population to the FB, the PFNd neurons, abolishes this behavior while leaving certain reflexive turning behaviors intact. Further, introduction of a fictive error signal in either the PFNd or PFNa neurons via optogenetic activation reveals that they are sufficient to affect the forward movement of the fly while slightly biasing its heading direction. We propose a model whereby the fly recruits the circuitry of the central complex to selectively influence features of movement that emerge over long timescales.

items.title: Association of Altered Anteriorization of Electroencephalographic Alpha Oscillation During Transition to Unconsciousness With Postoperative Delirium: A Prospective Observational Study.
items.abstract: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium. This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review. Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency. Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

items.title: Apathy and decision-making in non-clinical individuals: A computational model of effort, reward and probability.
items.abstract: Apathy, a transdiagnostic syndrome characterized by diminished motivation, is increasingly observed in non-clinical individuals, yet its cognitive mechanisms in non-clinical populations remain poorly understood. This study investigated the association between trait apathy and effort-based decision-making (EBDM), focusing on the critical roles of reward, probability and frame (gain vs. loss), and aimed to uncover the underlying computational processes of subjective value (SV) calculation. Participants included 84 non-clinical young adults (45 females, aged 18-25). They completed a key-pressing task where they decided to accept or reject offers that combined varying levels of effort demand, potential gain/loss frame, and probability. We analyzed behavioral measures including task accept rate and response time. Computational modeling was further employed to fit and compare different SV discounting models to participants' choices, estimating key parameters such as effort sensitivity and probability sensitivity. Compared to participants with low trait apathy, those with high trait apathy showed a significantly lower accept rate. Computational modeling indicated that this deficit was driven by the increased effort sensitivity in the gain frame and heightened probability sensitivity in the loss frame. These findings revealed that trait apathy is associated with altered effort-based decision-making, likely driven by an imbalance in how effort costs and probability-related risks are integrated into SV computation. Computational modeling provided an integrated perspective to jointly evaluate effort, reward, and probability, highlighting that apathetic individuals may require higher rewards or lower effort to act.

items.title: Approach and avoidance in schizophrenia: The influence of comorbid social anxiety disorder and of social anxiety symptoms severity.
items.abstract: People with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD) frequently present with a comorbid social anxiety disorder (SAD), which is associated with increased functional impairment, potentially due to heightened social avoidance. Individual differences in approach and avoidance can be conceptualized using Gray's revised Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory (RST), which describes three interacting motivation systems: the Behavioral Approach System (BAS), the Behavioral Inhibition System (BIS), and the Fight-Flight-Freeze System (FFFS). This case-control study examined approach and avoidance in people with SSD and the impact of SAD in 42 individuals with SSD and 42 community controls (CO). Social anxiety was assessed using the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale (LSAS) and the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 (SCID-5). Approach and avoidance motivations were assessed using the Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory Personality Questionnaire (RST-PQ). Fifteen participants with SSD and six CO met the diagnostic criteria for SAD. A significant group effect (SSD > CO) was observed for both the BIS (p = 0.003) and the FFFS (p no SAD across groups) emerged only for the BIS (p < 0.001). No significant effect emerged for the four BAS scales. Social anxiety symptom severity was positively correlated with BIS scores for both groups (ps < 0.001) and negatively correlated with BAS-Reward Interest scores only for the SSD group (p < 0.001). These findings emphasize the role of social anxiety in shaping approach and avoidance motivations, a factor particularly relevant given its high prevalence in SSD.

items.title: Is psychomotor retardation a sixth domain of negative symptoms?
items.abstract: The five canonical domains of negative symptoms in schizophrenia - blunted affect, alogia, asociality, anhedonia, and avolition - were established by a consensus process. Meta-analyses have placed psychomotor retardation (PMR) rating scale items in negative symptom factors, suggesting it may be a sixth negative symptom domain. We pooled data from two cross-sectional, multicenter, international studies of schizophrenia (N = 271) and used PANSS item G7 (Motor Retardation) as a measure of PMR. In multivariate analyses we examined G7 as a predictor of cognitive function, personal and social function, and negative symptoms other than PMR. We also examined whether G7 mediated the association between extrapyramidal symptoms and negative symptoms. In some analyses the G7 factor had relationships characteristic of the five canonical domains: correlations with those negative symptoms and negative correlations with function and cognition. However, other findings were consistent with its classification as a motor symptom: significant correlations with the PANSS Mannerism and Posturing item and with extrapyramidal symptoms, and mediation of the relationship between extrapyramidal symptoms and the canonical negative symptoms. There was no significant relationship with self-reported hours of sleep. PMR showed associations with negative symptoms, cognitive impairment, and functional outcome, consistent with status as a sixth negative symptom domain. However, other findings leave unclear whether it should be considered a negative symptom, a motor symptom, or something more complex. Problems in the G7 item definition and description contribute to this uncertainty.

items.title: Expert consensus on the clinical and organizational use of VNS therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy in the United Arab Emirates: a single-round modified Delphi study.
items.abstract: Epilepsy affects over 50 million people worldwide, and approximately one third of patients develop drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), a major driver of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulatory treatment option for DRE, but local guidance on its use in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) remains limited. This study aimed to establish an expert consensus to define best practices for the effective and efficient use of the VNS in the UAE setting. A multidisciplinary Task Force conducted a literature review and developed 25 evidence- and experience-informed statements, which were refined during an in-person expert meeting to ensure clinical relevance for the UAE context. Statements were rated through a single-round modified Delphi process involving UAE neurologists and neurosurgeons. Participants rated their agreement with each statement using a 7-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement, corresponding to ratings of 6-7. Statements with 60-69% agreement were classified as moderate agreement but were not considered to have reached consensus. Fifty-six experts completed the Delphi round, corresponding to a 75.7% response rate. Item-level denominators varied across statements. Eighteen of 25 statements reached consensus, six demonstrated moderate agreement, and one did not reach consensus. Strong agreement was observed for patient selection, safety, structured parameter optimization, and multidisciplinary care pathways. Moderate agreement emerged for presurgical evaluation, timing of implantation, and selected clinical scenarios. Building on existing international guidance and previous Delphi work in other settings, this study provides a UAE-specific description of expert agreement and variability on the clinical and organizational use of VNS for DRE. The findings may inform future local pathway development and identify areas requiring clearer definitions, prospective data collection, and further evidence generation. This study asked expert clinicians in the United Arab Emirates to rate 25 statements on the clinical and organizational use of vagus nerve stimulation for drug-resistant epilepsy. Vagus nerve stimulation is an adjunctive treatment that aims to reduce seizure burden and improve patient-centred outcomes; it should not be interpreted primarily as a treatment intended to achieve complete seizure freedom. Eighteen statements reached the prespecified consensus threshold, while six showed moderate agreement and one did not reach consensus. Experts showed agreement on several areas, including multidisciplinary care, safety considerations, MRI compatibility, structured follow-up, and individualized programming. However, agreement was more limited for some topics, including expected responder rates after one year, timing of implantation, selected programming criteria, and quality-of-life effects independent of seizure reduction. These findings identify areas where expert views are aligned and areas where practice remains variable. They may support the development of more consistent local care pathways, while highlighting topics that require further clinical evidence and local guidance.

items.title: Clear Positive MOG Antibodies in Adults With Multiple Sclerosis Features: Diagnostic Challenges.
items.abstract: Distinguishing multiple sclerosis (MS) from myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) can be challenging because of some shared clinical and radiologic features. We aimed to describe adults with clear positive serum MOG antibodies (MOG-Abs) presenting with MS features and rethink their nosological framework. We conducted a retrospective longitudinal study within the French NOMADMUS cohort and included adults from 2015 to 2025 tested clear positive for MOG-Ab in the serum with at least 1 MS-suggestive feature: (1) biological (CSF-specific oligoclonal bands [OCBs] and/or kappa free light chain index [KFLCi] ≥5.7) or (2) radiologic (≥1 lesion among juxtacortical lesion, Dawson finger, or inferior temporal lobe lesion). All MRI scans were reviewed blindly by an expert neuroradiologist. Minimum clinical and radiologic follow-up was 6 months. We classified patients as (1) typical MS when fulfilling 2024 McDonald criteria, with OCB and/or KFLCi ≥5.7 and showing no MOGAD supporting features, or (2) equivocal in all other situations. Among the 78 included patients (65% female, median age: 35 years), 23% were classified as typical MS and 77% as equivocal; all met MOGAD criteria, and 76% met 2024 McDonald criteria, without using central veinous sign or paramagnetic rim lesion, which have been rarely assessed. Myelitis followed by optic neuritis constituted the predominant clinical presentations in the whole cohort (45% and 32%, respectively) and in both groups. For typical MS cases, half of the patients did not receive maintenance therapy after the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 28% relapsed, 55% developed new silent lesions, and none showed lesion resolution (median follow-up: 1.9 years). For equivocal patients, 84% had OCB and 88% had ≥1 MOGAD supporting feature. After the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 72% initiated a maintenance therapy-mostly rituximab-15% relapsed, 46% developed silent new lesions, and 23% showed complete resolution of ≥1 lesion (median follow-up: 3 years). Clear positive MOG-Ab may occur in patients with genuine MS, and their presence may lead to therapeutic inertia. The substantial proportion of equivocal cases highlights current diagnostic limitations and underscores the need for longitudinal clinical and radiologic reassessment.

items.title: MOG Antibody Status Is Associated With Distinct Clinical Profiles and Treatment Responses in Chronic Relapsing Inflammatory Optic Neuropathy.
items.abstract: Chronic relapsing inflammatory optic neuropathy (CRION) is a steroid-dependent form of optic neuritis with incompletely understood pathophysiology. The identification of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies (MOG-IgG) in a substantial patient subset has challenged the diagnostic and therapeutic management. The aim of this study was to investigate clinical profiles and treatment outcomes of patients with CRION, comparing MOG-IgG-positive (MOG+) and seronegative (MOG-) subgroups. Patients from 6 European tertiary centers fulfilling diagnostic criteria for CRION were included. All underwent cell-based autoantibody testing. Clinical outcomes (visual acuity and annualized relapse rate), laboratory and imaging findings (MRI, OCT), and treatment responses were retrospectively analyzed. Sixty patients were included (median age 33 years; 70% female); 27 (45%) were MOG+. MOG+ CRION was associated with later onset, higher annualized relapse rate (ARR) before treatment (median [IQR] 2 [1-3] vs 1 [1-2], p = 0.023), and a trend toward shorter interrelapse intervals. Additional distinguishing features included higher frequencies of antinuclear antibody positivity, elevated CSF interleukin-6, and extensive enhancement of the optic nerve on MRI. Relapse burden correlated with visual acuity decline and retinal thinning. In MOG+ patients, monoclonal antibody therapy reduced the ARR (n = 21; 2 [1-3] vs 0 [0-2], p = 0.024), primarily driven by tocilizumab (n = 11; 2 [1-3] vs 0 [0-1], p = 0.023). In MOG- patients, rituximab and azathioprine showed a trend toward ARR reduction. CRION represents a heterogeneous syndrome encompassing distinct subgroups. Although MOG+ patients demonstrate higher disease activity, tocilizumab might represent a therapeutic option, though further validation is needed. Serologic testing is critical for treatment stratification and preventing relapses.

items.title: Feasibility of a machine learning model for predicting weight gain after kidney transplantation machine learning and weight gain after kidney transplantation.
items.abstract: Excessive weight gain after kidney transplantation adversely affects patient and graft outcomes. Machine Learning has been increasingly used to improve risk prediction across a range of transplant-related outcomes, yet its application to post-transplant weight trajectories remains unexplored. This study is the first to evaluate the feasibility of using Machine Learning algorithms to identify predictors of weight gain after kidney transplantation. This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. We developed an Elastic Net regression model with 10-fold cross-validation to predict body weight variation at 12 months post-transplant. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. This pioneering study establishes an analytical benchmark and reveals the informational limits of standard clinical datasets for predicting post-transplant weight gain. While Machine Learning application is feasible, current demographic and clinical variables are insufficient for precise individual prediction. Future models must integrate more granular behavioral and pharmacological data to achieve clinically actionable risk stratification.

items.title: Measuring audience experience across 20 showings of the same theatre performance using customer feedback kiosks and a questionnaire.
items.abstract: Audience experiences can vary both between performances and among spectators, but little is known about how different methods capture this variation across repeated showings of the same production. We therefore examined audience experience across twenty live performances of the same music theatre production. We combined two complementary methods: immediate audience ratings collected through customer feedback kiosks and more detailed post-performance questionnaires. The kiosks recorded 1,887 responses, corresponding to 67% of total attendance, and 458 audience members (16%) completed questionnaires. Overall, the reception was positive, but kiosk ratings varied significantly across performances, indicating that audience-level enjoyment ratings differed from one showing to another. Kiosk and questionnaire responses to the same enjoyment question did not differ significantly at the aggregate level, suggesting that brief kiosk feedback may provide a practical, low-burden measure of audience-level enjoyment. Cluster analysis of questionnaire data identified three descriptive response profiles that differed primarily in overall engagement and ratings of specific artistic elements. These profiles illustrate heterogeneity within the audience of a single production. Qualitative responses from participants whose quantitative ratings were closest to each cluster centroid provided illustrative accounts of the experiences associated with these profiles. These narratives added context to the quantitative findings by showing differences in emotional tone, interpretive emphasis, and personal connection to the performance. Supplementary interviews with the director, artistic director, and an external playwright illustrated both interest in and reservations about incorporating audience data into creative work. Their comments emphasised the potential of empirical findings to support artistic reflection, while also underscoring the importance of how and when feedback is communicated within production teams.

items.title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface.
items.abstract: Brain activation to verbal commands can be detected by EEG in clinically unresponsive patients. These patients with cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) are unable to communicate with the environment despite preserved consciousness. Advanced brain-computer interfaces (BCI) are promising to support motor function in patients with motor neuron disease or spinal cord injury. Our primary objective was to determine if clinically unresponsive patients can control a self-paced, one-way BCI early after acute brain injury. Secondarily, we assessed the association of BCI control with short- and long-term outcomes. We conducted a prospective single-centre cohort study in 41 clinically unresponsive, critically ill and acutely brain injured patients, as well as in a convenience sample of 8 healthy volunteers and 22 conscious critically ill patients. The self-paced BCI analysed EEG in real time and modulated frequency and pitch of a tone that patients controlled by attempting a motor task: patients were provided with instructions 'to make the beep sound faster, keep opening and closing your right hand' alternating with 'to make the beep sound slower, stop opening and closing your right hand'. CMD was detected by applying machine learning to EEG recorded while patients listened to motor commands. Clinical outcomes were recovery of consciousness by hospital discharge, assessed with the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised, and recovery of functional independence at 12 months, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score of 4 or higher (denoting the ability to function independently for 8 h or more). Additionally, we invited conscious patients as well as family members of conscious and clinically unresponsive patients to complete a survey on perceived utility and challenges associated with the BCI. In this study, 13 clinically unresponsive patients (32%) achieved BCI control and 8 of 41 (20%) were CMD-positive. All healthy volunteers and nine conscious patients (41%) were able to control the BCI. Median signal delay for BCI control was 49.8 [interquartile range (IQR) 39.9-75.6] seconds for clinically unresponsive patients, 17.1 (IQR 7.8-19.9) for conscious patients and 15.5 (IQR 12.9-21.2) for healthy volunteers. In the group of 41 clinically unresponsive patients, 4 of 13 patients with (31%) and 1 of 28 without BCI control (4%) recovered clinical consciousness at hospital discharge [odds ratio (OR) 21.2; 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.3-930.7]. At 12 months, 6 of 13 patients with (46%) and 2 of 28 without BCI control (7%) recovered functional independence (OR 9.9; 95% CI 1.8-81.6). None of the patients that were unable to control the BCI and were CMD-negative recovered. Patients with BCI control had shorter times to recovery of functional independence by 12 months than those who did not (hazards ratio 6.0; 95% CI 1.2-30.6). All respondents of the BCI survey (n = 37) expressed strong support for the potential future use of BCI devices. These results suggest that BCI control is a strong predictor of outcomes following acute brain injury and provide initial evidence that a bedside, EEG-based BCI system might permit bidirectional communication in critically ill unresponsive patients.

items.title: TIA1 is required for microglial activation in tauopathy.
items.abstract: The RNA-binding protein T cell intracellular antigen-1 (TIA1) regulates cellular stress responses and tau pathology, key contributors to the pathophysiology of tauopathies, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). TIA1 acts in peripheral monocytes to inhibit inflammation, but its function in central microglia, critical to neuroinflammation and disease progression, remains unknown. Here, we crossed TIA1 microglial conditional knockout (cKO) mice (using a Cx3cr1-driven Cre element) with the PS19 P301S MAPT mouse model of tauopathy and demonstrated that TIA1 promotes microglial activation, with a corresponding suppression of microglia activation upon TIA1cKO. We observe striking reductions in cytokine (Tnf-α and Il-1β) and sensome markers (Clec7a, Trem2, and Itgax); importantly, these reductions were accompanied by decreases in tau pathology. Proteomic analyses show TIA1 interaction with the microglial proteins C1Q, previously implicated in microglial activation. These results position TIA1 as a regulator of neuroinflammation and tauopathy in CX3CR1-expressing myeloid cells, including microglia, with potentially divergent functions in central versus peripheral immune compartments.

items.title: Programmed DNA breaks drive chromatin reconfiguration and facilitate transcriptional potentiation at neuronal early response genes.
items.abstract: Neuronal activity causes topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4. TOP2B-mediated DSBs facilitate ERG transcription, yet how this occurs is unclear. Using circular chromosome conformation capture (4C-seq), we report here that DSB formation is sufficient to emulate contact profiles observed at the promoters of Fos and Npas4 following neuronal stimulation, including elevated interactions with their cognate enhancers. Despite their purported risk, recurrent DSB cycles progressively potentiate ERG induction in mouse cortical neurons and HEK293T cells, evoking the effects of transcriptional memory. Potentiated ERG inducibility following recurrent DSBs persists through intervening cell cycles, occurs even when DNA repair is likely mutagenic, and correlates with a substantial loss of cis- and a gain of trans-, chromosomal interactions with ERG promoters. Together, these results reveal how activity-induced DSBs impact transcription by regulating chromatin dynamics at ERG promoters.

items.title: Dopamine signaling in the medial accumbens shell constrains the duration of reinforced actions.
items.abstract: Dopamine regulates the frequency of motor actions, but it is unclear whether it similarly regulates the duration of discrete behaviors. Here, we show that dopamine signaling within the medial accumbens shell reinforces actions while simultaneously constraining their duration. When mice hold down a lever to continuously self-stimulate dopamine axons in the medial accumbens shell, hold-downs are rarely longer than 5 s, and higher stimulation frequencies elicit shorter, but more numerous, lever hold-downs. This disengaging property of medial accumbens shell dopamine also applies to consummatory behavior, as mice are quicker to both terminate and reinitiate bouts of licking paired with high-frequency dopamine axon stimulation. Dopamine D1 receptors underpin this disengaging property of dopamine signaling, as we demonstrate a D1 agonist shortens both self-stimulation hold-downs and bouts of consummatory behavior. Altogether, we uncover an anatomically defined role of dopamine, which is to disengage its own reinforcing properties through D1 receptor signaling.

items.title: Neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulation: A systematic review of task-based neuroimaging studies.
items.abstract: Adequate sleep is essential for physiological, cognitive, and mental functioning. While epidemiological and behavioral studies show that sleep restriction or sleep deprivation is associated with altered responses to food stimuli, the neural mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. The preregistered systematic review synthesized evidence from task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging studies examining neural responses to food-related stimuli following experimental sleep manipulations, including sleep deprivation or sleep restriction. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and American Psychological Association PsycInfo, yielding 11 eligible studies, including nine with adult samples and two with adolescent samples. We extracted the data, assessed the risk of bias, and conducted a qualitative synthesis. Across studies with adult samples, six visual food-cue studies generally reported stronger brain activity following sleep deprivation or sleep restriction, particularly in the striatum, insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and inferior frontal gyrus. Two food valuation studies, including a willingness-to-pay and food-desire task, showed enhanced neural activity in the amygdala and hypothalamus during food valuation. Moreover, one study using a food odor perception paradigm showed that sleep deprivation altered chemosensory and interoceptive processing by enhancing food odor encoding in the piriform cortex. Two adolescent studies reported distinct neural findings. Together, these findings highlight that experimentally induced sleep deprivation or sleep restriction does not uniformly enhance reward-related brain activity; rather, it is associated with task-dependent changes in neural responses to food-related stimuli. However, the limited and heterogeneous evidence limits conclusions regarding common neural mechanisms. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Dopamine signaling via astrocytic D1 receptors regulates nucleus accumbens synaptic remodeling and cocaine seeking.
items.abstract: D1-type receptor (D1R)-mediated dopaminergic signaling within the nucleus accumbens shell (NAcSh) is essential for forming adaptive circuit changes that embed persistent memories associated with drug seeking and craving. While D1R is expressed in both NAcSh neurons and astrocytes, the specific contribution of astrocytic D1R to drug-related circuit plasticity remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated in mouse NAcSh slices that D1R agonists increased astrocytic Ca2+ activity, an effect that was attenuated by astrocyte-specific D1R knockdown. Furthermore, selective knockdown of astrocytic D1R in the NAcSh prior to cocaine self-administration inhibited cocaine-induced generation of silent synapses, thereby hampering the associated remodeling of NAcSh circuits. Behaviorally, knockdown of NAcSh astrocytic D1R expedited the extinction of cocaine seeking and reduced cue-induced reinstatement. These results identified astrocytic D1R as a fundamental component of NAcSh dopamine signaling during cocaine experience that remodeled synaptic connections and neural networks underlying drug seeking and relapse.

items.title: Updates in the treatment of eating disorders in 2025: a year in review in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention .
items.abstract: A broad range of relevant and diverse studies on the treatment of eating disorders were published in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention in 2025. We review novel treatment approaches, including interventions for individuals with complex clinical presentations, integrated primary care models, brief psychological treatments, peer support, and virtually delivered interventions. We also examine clinical, psychological, family, and treatment-related factors associated with treatment outcomes and barriers and facilitators to the implementation of Family-Based Treatment. Moreover, we highlight recent developments in caregiver-focused interventions designed to support and strengthen caregiver skills throughout treatment. With regard to binge-eating disorder, we review evidence supporting guided self-help, together with methodological considerations for strengthening future treatment research. Finally, we synthesize articles addressing adaptation needs for underserved populations, including autistic individuals, racially and ethnically minoritized groups, sexual and gender minority populations, and military-affiliated youth. Overall, the articles published in Eating Disorders: The Journal of Treatment & Prevention in 2025 highlight the growing emphasis on personalized, accessible, and implementation-focused models of care, while underscoring the need for further research to strengthen the evidence base and optimize treatment delivery across diverse clinical settings and populations.

items.title: Clobazam Use in Epilepsy: An Old Story with a New Twist. A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: Clobazam (CLB), a 1,5-benzodiazepine, widely used and now available in an oral liquid formulation with a registered indication as adjunctive antiseizure medication for drug-resistant epilepsy, is characterized by a distinctive pharmacological profile. It is rapidly absorbed and extensively metabolised via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 to its active metabolite, N-desmethylclobazam, with marked interindividual variability driven by pharmacokinetic interactions, genetic polymorphisms, and patient-specific factors. Its antiseizure effects are mediated through modulation of γ-aminobutyric acidA receptor subunits and associated with a lower propensity for sedation compared with classical 1,4-benzodiazepines. There is solid evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of CLB, particularly in Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes, while its role in other epilepsy syndromes relies on an expanding, albeit heterogeneous, body of evidence. The drug is increasingly incorporated into combination regimens where pharmacokinetic interactions-most notably CYP2C19 inhibition by cannabidiol, stiripentol, and cenobamate-may enhance antiseizure efficacy but it needs appropriate dose individualisation to reduce the risk of sedation, especially in vulnerable populations. The recent approval of an oral solution as adjunctive therapy in epilepsy in adults or children can facilitate appropriate dosage adjustments regarding the clinical target, weight, and concomitant medications. Overall, CLB represents a versatile and clinically valuable therapeutic option, with its optimal use increasingly guided by precision medicine principles and rational polytherapy strategies.

items.title: Greater and Lesser Occipital Nerve Blocks for Frequent and Severe Headaches in Children and Adolescents: A Protocolized Repetitive Intervention Study.
items.abstract: Headache management in children and adolescents remains challenging, particularly in patients with high headache-related disability, medication overuse, and comorbid conditions, for whom evidence-based preventive treatment options are limited and often ineffective. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes and safety of a protocolized, repetitive bilateral greater and lesser occipital nerve block (GONB/LONB) strategy in pediatric patients with frequent and severe headaches. This retrospective study included adolescents aged 11-18 years who underwent bilateral GONB and LONB for headache between 2018 and 2025. At each treatment session, 1 mL of 2% lidocaine was administered at each of four injection sites (bilateral GON and LON), corresponding to a total volume of 4 mL (80 mg) per session. Blocks were administered weekly for 4 weeks, followed by additional applications at 1 and 3 months. Headache severity and disability were evaluated using the visual analog scale (VAS) and the Pediatric Migraine Disability Assessment (PedMIDAS) before and after completion of the block protocol. Forty-five patients (91.1% female) received a total of 258 bilateral GONB/LONB procedures. The mean number of headache days per month was 20.8 ± 7.9, and the mean headache duration was 11.6 ± 10.7 months. Significant reductions were observed in both VAS and PedMIDAS disability grades following treatment (p < 0.001). At the patient level, 41 of 45 patients (91.1%) met the predefined criteria for clinical response. No serious adverse events occurred. Protocolized repetitive bilateral GONB/LONB was well tolerated and was associated with reductions in headache severity and headache-related disability in this predominantly adolescent cohort. However, the uncontrolled retrospective design precludes attribution of these improvements specifically to the intervention. Prospective sham-controlled studies are needed to establish treatment-specific efficacy.

items.title: Intracranial EEG for Detecting Epileptic Activity in Acute Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) has been increasingly explored as part of multimodal neuromonitoring in acute brain injury, yet its diagnostic benefit compared with continuous surface EEG (suEEG) remains uncertain. We have performed a meta-analysis to quantify seizure and rhythmic and periodic pattern detection rates and concordance with suEEG. Secondary objectives were the assessment of correlations with brain injury, safety, and techniques. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched for studies reporting iEEG monitoring in adults with acute brain injury. Epileptic patterns were harmonized to the American Clinical Neurophysiology Society Standardized EEG Nomenclature for Critically Ill Patients (ACNS) 2021 terminology, classifying events as seizures/status epilepticus (SZ/SE) or rhythmic and periodic/ictal-interictal continuum patterns (RPP/IIC). Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and custom bias domains. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted for (i) pooled proportions and (ii) pooled paired within-patient comparisons. Twelve cohorts (n = 864 participants) with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (n = 343), traumatic brain injury (n = 351), and mixed etiologies (n = 170) were included. Six studies provided paired iEEG-suEEG data (n = 273). Techniques were based on a strip or depth electrode. No severe adverse events were reported. Pooled iEEG versus suEEG incidence rates were respectively: 26% vs. 15% for SZ/SE, 47% vs. 34% for RPP/IIC, and 57% vs. 37% for clinically relevant epileptic activity. Pooled paired analysis demonstrated that iEEG additionally detected SZ/SE in 16.5% of patients [pooled McNemar odds ratio (OR) 3.46 (0.51-23.6); I2 = 63%; p = 0.158] and RPP/IIC in 26% [pooled OR 4.25 (0.19-96.1); I2 = 73%; p = 0.236], while suEEG was negative. Sensitivity analyses for high-risk studies or cohort overlap did not alter the results. Invasive EEG monitoring substantially increased the detection of seizures and RPP/IIC patterns compared with suEEG alone in patients with acute brain injury, serving as a promising monitoring adjunct.

items.title: When to Start Oral Anticoagulant Therapy Post-Stroke: From Common to Rare Conundrums.
items.abstract: This review summarizes recent evidence on when to start oral anticoagulant therapy following stroke, including both common and rare clinical conundrums. While previous recommendations based on Diener's rule suggested waiting up to 12 days based on stroke severity and neuroradiological findings, newer data support earlier initiation or resumption of anticoagulation, particularly for mild and moderate ischemic strokes, generally within 4 days. In patients with a history of intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation resumption involves weighing thromboembolic risk against recurrent hemorrhage risk, requiring individualized decisions regarding whether and when anticoagulation should be resumed. Clinical recommendations for post-stroke anticoagulation emphasize early, individualized initiation of direct oral anticoagulants for mild-to-moderate ischemic strokes based on neuroimaging. After intracerebral hemorrhage, anticoagulation is generally restarted within 4 to 8 weeks for atrial fibrillation, with earlier resumption potentially warranted in selected high-thromboembolic-risk patients, particularly those with mechanical heart valves.

items.title: Urgent versus scheduled resection in high-grade glioma: patient selection and healthcare utilization in a single-center cohort.
items.abstract: Patients with high-grade glioma reach surgery during the initial, index hospitalization (urgent), or through scheduled/outpatient pathways. There is a paucity of literature examining what patients require expedited versus elective surgery. This single-center retrospective study describes complications, utilization, and survival by pathway. Adults with WHO grade 3-4 gliomas undergoing primary resection (2021-2026) were classified as urgent (admitted without a planned resection date) or scheduled (discharged and readmitted for planned surgery, or managed exclusively as an outpatient). Primary outcomes were 30-day complications and days alive at home within 30 days of admission for resection (DAH-30). Secondary outcomes were progression free and overall survival. Survival was analyzed with propensity-score overlap weighting and Cox regression. Of 166 patients, 122 underwent urgent resection and 44 scheduled resections; 40 of 44 (91%) proceeded as planned. Urgent patients more often had midline shift (62% vs. 32%), less often seizure (15% vs. 39%), and lower Karnofsky scores (70 vs. 80); all p ≤ 0.002. They had longer index hospitalizations (median 8 vs. 3 days, p < 0.001) and fewer days at home (median 15 vs. 27; adjusted difference - 8.9 days, 95% CI - 12.9 to - 4.8). Complication rates (36% vs. 30%; adjusted OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.52-2.62) and overall survival (median 15.4 vs. 19.0 months, p = 0.758) did not differ detectably. Scheduled resection identified a distinct population, recognizable at initial evaluation by preserved performance status and the absence of midline shift. These patients spent more days at home and required shorter hospitalizations; no harm signal was observed. These data suggest that a substantial proportion of patients with newly diagnosed presumed high grade gliomas can be managed effectively in an expedited, outpatient basis.

items.title: Feedstock-dependent biochar properties shape short-term soil CO<sub>2</sub> emissions through microbial enzyme-associated processes beyond the effect of soil pH in black soil.
items.abstract: Black soils represent globally important reservoirs of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the mechanisms regulating short-term carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions following biochar amendment remain poorly understood. Although biochar-induced alkalization has been widely proposed as a key mechanism influencing soil carbon mineralization, whether increased soil pH alone can explain feedstock-dependent CO 2 responses remain unresolved. Here, we investigated the effects of biochars derived from six feedstocks on CO 2 emissions, soil chemical properties, microbial functional traits, and extracellular enzyme activities in a short-term incubation experiment using black soil. Biochar application increased cumulative CO 2 emissions by 9.1%-44.6%, with substantial variation among feedstocks. Biochars increased soil pH, nutrient availability, and the activities of carbon-, nitrogen-, and phosphorus-acquiring enzymes, but the magnitude of these responses varied substantially with feedstock-dependent biochar properties. Cumulative CO 2 emissions were positively associated with β-glucosidase (BG), leucine aminopeptidase (LAP), and acid phosphatase (ACP) activities. Random forest and regression analyses identified soil pH and extracellular enzyme activities as major predictors of CO 2 emissions, with extracellular enzyme activities collectively contributing 52.9% of the relative importance and exhibiting stronger relationships with CO 2 emissions (R = 0.68-0.72) than soil chemical properties alone. Importantly, pH manipulation using NaOH in the absence of biochar failed to reproduce the enhanced enzyme activities and CO 2 emissions observed following biochar amendment, demonstrating that alkalization alone was insufficient to explain the contrasting CO 2 responses among different biochar treatments. These findings indicate that short-term CO 2 emissions following biochar application are shaped by feedstock-dependent biochar properties in association with microbial enzyme-mediated carbon turnover beyond the effect of soil pH. Our results highlight the importance of integrating biochar properties and microbial functional responses when evaluating short-term soil carbon mineralization and the environmental implications of biochar amendment.

items.title: Daphnia magna bioconverts eicosapentaenoic acid continuously and independently of dietary supply.
items.abstract: Freshwater food webs are increasingly exposed to eutrophication and warming, which can shift phytoplankton community composition and reduce the availability of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids to higher trophic levels. We investigated whether the model freshwater crustacean Daphnia magna can compensate for a dietary lack of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) through endogenous EPA synthesis from its precursors, and whether this response depends on food quality, temperature, and genetic background. Two D. magna strains, isolated from contrasting temperate regions, were exposed to four diets ranging from edible cyanobacteria-dominated to cryptophyte-enriched communities at 15, 20, and 25 °C. Using deuterium labelling, compound-specific hydrogen isotope analysis, fatty acid quantification and fitness measurements, we assessed EPA bioconversion and its consequences for consumer performance. Cyanobacteria-rich food reduced biomass accrual, delayed reproduction, decreased body size, and lowered offspring production. Despite these pronounced fitness effects, endogenous EPA production remained stable across all dietary treatments. Instead, bioconversion was primarily governed by water temperature, reaching a maximum at approximately 20 °C, and was slightly higher in the cold-adapted strain, consistent with underlying biochemical constraints on metabolic processes. Slight differences between the two strains suggest an important contribution of genetic background in determining EPA biosynthesis. These results indicate that endogenous EPA synthesis in D. magna was not actively regulated but was constantly active and potentially buffered against low dietary EPA levels, but did not fully compensate for poor food quality.

items.title: Healthy default beverage policies: A comprehensive inventory and comparative analysis of enacted and proposed policies across U.S. state and local jurisdictions.
items.abstract: Background Previous evaluations of healthy default beverage (HDB) policies showed inconsistent implementation and enforcement. No study has described and compared implementation and enforcement provisions in enacted and proposed policies to identify gaps impacting policy success. Objective To identify and examine trends in enacted and proposed U.S. local and state HDB policies; compare implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions across policy status and jurisdictional levels; evaluate alignment with Healthy Drinks Healthy Kids (HDHK) recommendations; and illustrate how enacted policies changed during committee review. Design This study identified enacted and proposed local and state policies through systematic searches of policy databases (American Legal Publishing Code Library, Municode, NexisUni, Westlaw), websites, and literature in September 2024. Policies were reviewed for inclusion, and a jurisdiction's final policy version coded for key characteristics. Enacted policy's legislative websites were separately searched for accompanying documents (e.g., committee reports). Main outcome measures The outcomes were number of enacted and proposed policies; frequency of implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions; HDHK recommendations alignment; and committee-required changes to enacted policies. Statistical analyses performed Intercoder agreement was calculated with Cohen's kappa, and descriptive statistics summarized policy contents. As a case-study, accompanying documents from state-level enacted Hawaii and Illinois policies were qualitatively reviewed. Results This inventory included 86 policies (28 local, 58 state) from 2015-2024. After excluding duplicate state-level bicameral policies and counting each re-introduction of a policy across legislative sessions as an additional policy, there were 65 unique policies. Policies were enacted in 28 local jurisdictions and 4 states, and proposed (not enacted) in 14 states. Implementation, evaluation, and enforcement provisions were uncommon across jurisdictions and statuses. Equity provisions appeared only in local policies. No policies completely met HDHK recommendations. Accompanying documents illustrated how the legislative process strengthened or weakened policy provisions in Hawaii and Illinois. Conclusions HDB policies are increasingly enacted across U.S. jurisdictions. Strengthening implementation, enforcement, and equity provisions may enhance policy effectiveness in reducing children's restaurant sweetened beverage intake.

items.title: Intermittent illumination enables reversible carbon buffering by Rhodopseudomonas palustris for enhanced methane recovery from food waste anaerobic digestion.
items.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) of food waste (FW) is vulnerable to acidification when fermentation outpaces syntrophic oxidation and methanogenesis. To address this temporal imbalance, we introduced Rhodopseudomonas palustris (R. palustris), which can assimilate fermentation-derived volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and store carbon as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs). Intermittent illumination reduced VFA accumulation and end-cycle H 2 partial pressure, while yielding the highest mean daily methane production (589.0 mL d -1 ) and fraction of carbon recovered as methane (37.2 %). A pure-culture assay showed that PHA accumulated during illumination and declined in darkness, indicating reversible intracellular carbon storage and remobilization. The PHA turnover pattern paralleled reactor methane dynamics, which was consistent with a temporal association between carbon storage and downstream methanogenesis. Intermittent illumination yielded the lowest NADH/NAD + ratio while maintaining high ATP availability. Community analysis revealed a more balanced distribution of functional guilds between the liquid and reactor-wall fractions, while metagenomic analysis indicated functional potential for PHA turnover and methanogenesis. Together, these findings support a carbon-buffering model in which light-dark cycling is associated with transient carbon storage and subsequent remobilization, potentially improving the temporal coupling between acidogenesis and methane formation and enhancing AD stability and methane recovery.

items.title: Metal-organic frameworks-enabled lignocellulose valorization toward medium-chain fatty acids: From sustainable synthesis to integrated catalysis, bioconversion, and separation‬‬‬‬.
items.abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is a renewable carbon source for medium-chain fatty acid (MCFA) production, but conversion from solid feedstock to recoverable C6-C8 products is limited by biomass recalcitrance, enzyme deactivation, microbial inhibition, and downstream separation. This review critically evaluates metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as stage-specific materials rather than a universal platform, linking manufacture and stability to biomass conversion, enzyme immobilization, carbohydrate upgrading, chain elongation, product recovery, regeneration, and process economics. Direct studies are distinguished from related-system evidence, mechanistic interpretations, and proposed integrations, with comparisons constrained by material identity, process matrix, and reported endpoints. Key trade-offs concern activity and stability, enzyme protection and substrate access, and adsorption affinity and release. Initial direct studies report enhanced caproate production with MOF-assisted chain elongation, whereas selective and repeated C6-C8 recovery from real chain-elongation broth remains insufficiently demonstrated. The most defensible near-term route is modular, stream-matched use of MOFs rather than a single multifunctional material spanning the biorefinery.

items.title: Oscillatory Regimes in a Game-Theoretic Model for Mosquito Population Dynamics under Breeding Site Control.
items.abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a major public health threat, and the control of mosquito populations depends on sustained household participation in removing breeding sites. While environmental drivers of mosquito oscillations have been extensively studied, the influence of spontaneous household decision-making on mosquito dynamics remains poorly understood. We introduce a game-theoretic model in which the proportion of households performing breeding site control evolves through imitation dynamics, driven by perceived risks that can depend on mosquito prevalence. We assume that household behavior regulates the carrying capacity of the aquatic mosquito stage, creating a feedback between control actions and mosquito population growth. For a simplified model with constant payoffs, we characterize four locally stable equilibria, corresponding to full or no household control and the presence or absence of mosquito populations. When the perceived risk of not controlling breeding sites depends on mosquito prevalence, the system admits an additional equilibrium with partial household engagement. We derive conditions under which this equilibrium undergoes a Hopf bifurcation, yielding sustained oscillations arising solely from the interaction between mosquito abundance and household behavior. Numerical simulations confirm our analytical results by delineating the parametric regions of local stability for each steady state. Parameter explorations of the oscillatory regime further reveal that larger basic offspring numbers produce oscillations of higher amplitude and shorter period, while the perceived risk ratio modulates these trends and drives the amplitude to vanish near the Hopf boundaries. Our study demonstrates that spontaneous household decision-making alone can generate nontrivial dynamics in mosquito populations, offering insights into the interplay between risk perception and vector ecology. From a public health perspective, recurrent peaks in mosquito abundance may translate into periodic surges in cases, and effective interventions may therefore target the perceived risks that drive household participation in controlling breeding sites.

items.title: Spatial patterns, source apportionment, and environmental correlates of soil potentially toxic elements in an arid high-altitude mining area of Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China.
items.abstract: Disentangling mining-related inputs from heterogeneous geological backgrounds remains difficult in arid mining regions. We analyzed eight potentially toxic elements (PTEs; As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in 155 surface-soil samples from an arid, high-altitude mining area in Wuqia County, Xinjiang, China. A staged framework combined a self-organizing map (SOM), improved absolute principal component scores-multiple linear regression (APCS-MLR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify multielement patterns, estimate potential-source contributions, and characterize nonlinear environmental associations. SOM resolved localized Cd-Pb-Zn co-enrichment, with class C3 concentrated near the waste-rock dump and processing plant. APCS-MLR separated five potential-source signals: mining-traffic Cd-Zn, mixed Hg-As deposition/agricultural, Ni parent-material, mixed Cr-Cu parent-material/industrial, and Pb traffic-deposition. In the 105 robust samples used for the final Huber-regression branch, F1 and F4 accounted for mean contributions of 29.7% and 27.5%, respectively. Spatial out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation of downstream LightGBM models identified F1 as the most stable factor (pooled OOF R 2 = 0.36; positive R 2 in all five folds), and its estimated contribution decreased with distance from the mining area. A full-sample, uncertainty-weighted, five-factor positive matrix factorization (PMF) sensitivity analysis recovered one-to-one correspondence with the APCS-MLR structure (cosine similarities, 0.724-0.977); all five profiles matched at cosine similarity ≥ 0.80 in 93% of bootstrap resamples. SHAP associations for F2-F5 remained exploratory because their spatial stability was weak. By separating pattern identification, statistical source apportionment, and association interpretation, the staged evidence chain supports targeted monitoring and improves the robustness of source-oriented environmental assessment in arid mining regions.

items.title: Females shape hunting of vertebrates in wild bonobos.
items.abstract: Hunting and meat consumption are widely considered key drivers of human evolution, and hypotheses about their origins draw on comparisons with our closest living relatives, chimpanzees and bonobos. These comparisons typically set up a behavioral dichotomy in which chimpanzees are characterized by cooperative hunting of arboreal primates by male-dominated parties, whereas bonobo hunts are thought to involve the opportunistic targeting of terrestrial ungulates, primarily by individual females. 1 , 2 , 3 Observations from two habituated bonobo communities at LuiKotale covering 10 years challenge this dichotomy. LuiKotale bonobos hunted both terrestrial ungulates (42%) and arboreal primates (43% of vertebrate prey), with red colobus monkeys comprising the majority of primate prey (77%). Males and females hunted arboreal primates at similar rates, and females accounted for most non-primate captures. Female age affected the hunting frequency of primates and ungulates, with the former being biased to younger and the latter to older females. The prominent role of female bonobos in hunting supports predictions that relate hunting activity to intersexual dominance relations rather than risk aversion, with the dominant sex being more active. Comparing data from neighboring communities revealed differences and suggests that social and environmental parameters affect prey choice by each community in different ways. Together, these findings challenge the assumption that chimpanzee-like, male-biased hunting represents the ancestral condition. They highlight the contribution of females to obtaining vertebrate prey, call for a reassessment of the role of females in hunting and meat sharing, and by extension, the framing of models of early hominin subsistence and social organization.

items.title: Spawning strategy drives divergent stock trends of walleye pollock and Pacific cod under ocean warming in the northwestern Pacific.
items.abstract: Walleye pollock and Pacific cod are cold-water semi-demersal species with similar life histories; however, their long-term catch trends have diverged since the late 1980s along their southern distribution limits in Korea and Japan. This study examined how warming-driven water-column changes differentially affect these species with contrasting spawning strategies (pelagic eggs: pollock; demersal eggs: cod). Using data from 1982 to 2023, spawning-season water-column structure, early life-stage thermal habitat suitability index (HSI), and habitat suitable depth (HSD; HSI ≥ 0.6) were compared with catches across three regional groups (A: Korean East/Japan Sea coast; B: Japanese East/Japan Sea coast; C: Japanese Pacific coast), and lead-lag relationships were assessed by cross-correlation function (CCF) analysis of detrended time series. Surface temperatures increased in all groups under Kuroshio-origin warm currents (A: East Korea Warm Current; B: Tsushima Warm Current; C: Kuroshio Extension), whereas bottom thermal conditions differed depending on regional cold-water masses. Pollock catches declined sharply in all groups after the late 1980s without recovery, even where surface HSI remained suitable. In Group A, pollock HSI declined or remained low in sub-regions, whereas suitable cod habitat persisted and catches increased. In parts of Groups B and C, cod catches declined after the early 2010s; HSD deepened in Group B and was negatively associated with catch five years later in B-1 (r = -0.72, p < 0.001), whereas HSD-catch relationships varied among Group C sub-regions. Contrasting spawning strategies therefore expose early life stages to different water-column layers, whereas catch responses depend on regional oceanographic conditions.

items.title: Dam-induced reshuffling of functional traits in fish communities across the Lower Mekong Basin.
items.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems in the Lower Mekong Basin (LMB) are increasingly affected by anthropogenic pressures such as hydropower development, altered flow regimes, and habitat degradation. While taxonomic declines are documented, the functional reshuffling of fish communities remains poorly understood. To address this gap and assess the temporal shifts in fish traits and identify those most sensitive to environmental change, we applied a trait-based approach using long-term monitoring data from four sites spanning from the upper LMB to the delta. Post-dam, we observed reduced temporal variability at most sites along with strong site-specific patterns in trait dynamics. Notably, migratory species were replaced by non-natives at the upstream site (LPB) and marine-related guilds emerged in Tonle Sap Lake (TLS) but disappeared from the delta. Community-weighted mean (CWM) values decreased for key functional groups, including rhithron residents (G1) at LPB and floodplain-related guilds at TLS. CWM-redundancy analysis identified water level, temperature, dissolved oxygen, total suspended solids (TSS), and total nitrite and nitrate (NO32) as key drivers. Upstream communities (G1 and migratory species, particularly at LPB) were correlated with high water level, dissolved oxygen, and NO32, but low temperature and TSS. Conversely, downstream communities, such as floodplain and marine related guilds, showed the opposite pattern. These findings reveal that post-dam environmental changes reshape the functional organization of the Mekong fish communities. Identifying traits sensitive to long-term environmental variation improves our understanding of how hydrological changes influence the functional composition of fish communities and can guide conservation efforts and environmental flow strategies to sustain functional fish diversity.

items.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet.
items.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

items.title: The evolutionary accessibility of cultural fitness landscapes.
items.abstract: Many human cultural and technological traits have a complex and peculiar structure. They are often characterized by multiple closely interacting parts that can form modules, and change as a result of innovation, collaboration, and social learning. A full understanding of the ways in which such cultural traits evolve requires a model that accounts for the close epistatic interaction of the constituent parts, and for the uniquely cultural processes that act on them. Here, we generalize the concept of 'adaptive landscapes', where populations search a landscape for optimal combinations of components. This generalization accounts for epistatic interactions, and includes processes such as modularization, communication, and collaboration, that are not features of genetic systems but may be quite common features of cultural systems. We show that modularization in combination with collaborative communication of search results is more successful, but sometimes more costly, than searching a full adaptive landscape. However, in many of the circumstances under which technology evolves, a full search of many thousands of possible modules may not be feasible since time, financial, energetic, and environmental constraints are likely to be strong. Under these conditions, our models suggest that there is a critical value for the number of modules to search below which the global optimum is more likely to be reached by searching the full landscape. The value of this threshold depends on the complexity of the technology. Overall, we suggest that analysis of cultural fitness landscapes is likely to be a fruitful avenue for research into technological change especially when combined with elements of human learning and interaction known to be important features of cultural evolution.

items.title: Host-virus interactions dominate fitness and conceal additive genetic variation.
items.abstract: Host-parasite coevolution is expected to generate strong selection for resistance and infectivity that has the potential to erode genetic variation. Despite this, natural populations often retain extensive genetic variation in these traits. Genotype-by-genotype interactions on fitness can generate negative frequency-dependent selection, which helps maintain this variation by preventing any host or pathogen genotype from retaining a permanent advantage. Because these interactions place genetic variance in the interaction term rather than in additive differences among hosts or pathogens, that variance is masked from directional selection and can remain 'cryptic'. Here we combine coevolutionary modelling with large‑scale experimental infection assays to quantify how host-pathogen interactions structure fitness variance in a vertically transmitted virus system, Drosophila melanogaster and sigma virus. Simulations show that coevolution typically erodes additive genetic variance in host and pathogen fitness, concentrating variance in host-virus interaction terms. Consistent with these predictions, experiments spanning 90 host-virus genotype combinations reveal that transmission, viral load, and virulence are overwhelmingly governed by host-virus genetic interactions rather than host or virus main effects. As a result, neither host resistance alleles nor viral genotypes confer consistently higher fitness across genetic backgrounds. Interactions tend to be sex‑specific, further limiting heritable fitness variation. Our results demonstrate that coevolution can substantially mask heritable genetic variation from directional selection by rendering fitness context-dependent. This extensive cryptic genetic variation may be revealed either when ecological or evolutionary conditions shift, or when the process of coevolution itself alters the direction of selection. This demonstrates the need to account for genotype-specific interactions when forecasting evolutionary responses.

items.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides.
items.abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

items.title: Innovative Standards for Using Nature-Based Solutions in Water Reuse Projects.
items.abstract: Water reuse is increasingly recognized as a key element in sustainable water resource management, yet its implementation faces technical, economic, and social challenges. The Can Cabanyes project in Granollers (Catalonia, Spain) offers a pioneering example of a hybrid water reuse system that combines nature-based solutions with a technical reclamation plant and a distribution network. Over two decades of operation, the system has demonstrated reliable removal of conventional pollutants, pathogens, and certain emerging contaminants while also revealing seasonal patterns linked to temperature-dependent nitrification. Beyond water quality improvements, the project has generated significant ecological and social benefits, including habitat restoration, biodiversity enhancement, and recreational opportunities, all of which contribute measurable positive externalities that outweigh private costs.Drawing from this long-term experience, a set of innovative standards is proposed to guide the replication of hybrid systems. These include integrating green and grey infrastructure, adopting adaptive management practices, implementing rigorous performance monitoring, valuing externalities in economic assessments, and ensuring transparent stakeholder engagement. Together, these principles establish a robust framework for designing resilient and socially accepted water reuse projects. The Can Cabanyes case illustrates how nature-based solutions can be strategically embedded within peri-urban contexts, advancing both environmental sustainability and water security.

items.title: Clonal integration drives divergent assembly of rhizosphere bacteria and fungi in Hydrocotyle vulgaris under cadmium heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Clonal plants enhance their fitness in heterogeneous environments through clonal integration, which enables resource sharing among interconnected ramets. However, how clonal integration shapes rhizosphere microbiome assembly and function remains poorly understood. In this study, we constructed patchy heterogeneous soils with cadmium-polluted and unpolluted substrates to simulate fragmented polluted habitats. Apical ramets were grown in cadmium-polluted soil and basal positions were cultivated in unpolluted soil, with stolons left either intact or severed. Rhizosphere and root-zone soils were sampled, and bacterial and fungal communities were characterized via 16 S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Our results demonstrated that stolon integration significantly altered rhizosphere microbial composition, with elevated relative abundances of Acidobacteriota, Actinobacteriota and Ascomycota and a reduction in Firmicutes. Beneficial genera Streptomyces and Savoryella were enriched under intact stolon treatments. Bacterial α-richness (Chao1) was significantly higher in the rhizosphere of stolon-intact plants, especially at the basal positions, whereas fungal α- richness showed no significant difference among treatments. Beta-diversity analysis revealed that bacterial communities were more sensitive to stolon integration than fungal communities, with fungal community structural shifts observed only in the basal rhizosphere. Amplicon sequence variant (ASV) analysis showed that intact stolons increased unique bacterial ASVs but reduced unique fungal ASVs in the basal rhizosphere. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that clonal integration differentially regulates the assembly of bacterial and fungal communities in the rhizosphere. This study highlights the distinct ecological roles of bacteria and fungi in plant-soil feedback and emphasizes multi-kingdom assessments of clonal integration under heterogeneous Cd condition.
