items.title: First report of odontoma in Petroscirtes breviceps (Valenciennes, 1836) from Rameswaram Island, India.
items.abstract: Odontogenic tumours are rarely reported in teleost fishes, and detailed histopathological descriptions of these lesions remain limited. This study describes a rare case of compound odontoma in the striped poison-fang blenny mimic, Petroscirtes breviceps (Valenciennes, 1836). Among 30 examined individuals, one male specimen measuring 13 cm in total length and weighing 12 g presented with a distinct tumour-like growth in the oral cavity. Gross examination revealed a localized, pale pink, fleshy odontogenic lesion attached to the left side of the lower jaw. The mass contained numerous toothlet-like structures of varying sizes, suggesting progressive tumour-associated odontogenic differentiation. Histopathological analysis showed a well-circumscribed, non-invasive mass composed of multiple irregular denticle-like structures embedded within a moderately cellular fibrovascular stroma. These denticles exhibited features consistent with dental tissue organisation, including eosinophilic dentine-like mineralised matrices surrounding central pulp-like cores, with enamel-like caps observed in some areas. The lesion also contained proliferating fibroblasts, mesenchymal cells resembling dental papilla, and scattered nests of odontogenic epithelium. No evidence of cytological atypia, necrosis, vascular invasion, inflammatory infiltration, or significant mitotic activity was observed, confirming the benign nature of the tumour. The presence of well-differentiated tooth-like structures composed of dentine-, cementum-, and enamel-like materials supported a definitive diagnosis of compound odontoma. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the first documented report of odontoma in P. breviceps from Rameswaram Island, India.

items.title: Electron transfer to nitrogenase in Paenibacillus polymyxa .
items.abstract: Nitrogenase requires low-potential electrons to reduce N2 to produce ammonia. The direct electron donors to nitrogenase are reduced ferredoxin (Fd) and flavodoxin (Fld). The enzymes that reduce Fd or Fld for N2 fixation mainly include pyruvate-flavodoxin (ferredoxin) oxidoreductase (PFOR), ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase (FNR), Rhodobacter nitrogen fixation protein complex (Rnf), and bifurcating electron transfer flavoprotein complex (Fix). Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model for studies of nitrogen fixation, but the pathways of electron transport to nitrogenase are unknown. In this study, we characterized the electron transport pathway to nitrogenase in P. polymyxa. Deletion analysis showed that among 15 genes encoding Fds, Fld, and Fd-/Fld-reducing enzymes, only cbiW gene and pfoAB operon decreased nitrogenase activity (31% and 37% relative to wild type, respectively). Triple deletion of cbiW and pfoAB led to a reduction of nitrogenase activity by 61%. Elemental analysis and ultraviolet-visible absorption spectroscopy revealed that the purified Fd protein encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd. The purified Fd protein was able to substitute for Klebsiella NifF (Fld) to transfer electrons from pyruvate to Klebsiella nitrogenase in vitro. The pfoAB operon encodes PFOR, which is composed of two subunits. Klebsiella oxytoca NifJ (PFOR) was able to support nitrogen fixation in the ΔpfoAB mutant. These findings suggest that [2Fe-2S] Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. Gram-positive and facultatively anaerobic Paenibacillus polymyxa is a model diazotroph whose nif (nitrogen fixation) genes encoding nitrogenase have been used for engineering yeast and plants. However, the pathway of electron transfer to Paenibacillus nitrogenase is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that Fd encoded by cbiW and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon constitute an electron transport pathway to Paenibacillus nitrogenase. Fd encoded by cbiW is a [2Fe-2S] Fd, and PFOR encoded by the pfoAB operon is a heterodimer. In contrast, in many gram-negative diazotrophs, [4Fe-4S] Fds are widely used as electron donors to nitrogenase, and PFORs (NifJs) are homodimers. These results suggest that there may be some differences in the mechanisms of electron transfer to nitrogenase between gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria. The identified electron transport components in P. polymyxa will have great potential for use in engineering eukaryotes.

items.title: Expanding the Orchidaceae virome through analysis of public-domain sequencing data.
items.abstract: Orchidaceae is one of the largest plant families and includes species of major ornamental, economic, and ecological importance. Despite this diversity, the viruses associated with orchids remain poorly characterized. The growing availability of high-throughput sequencing data offers new opportunities to explore plant virus diversity across broad taxonomic scales. Here, we conducted a large-scale meta-analysis of orchid-associated viruses by reanalyzing 2,789 publicly available RNA-seq data sets representing 41 genera across 18 subtribes and five subfamilies. We identified sequences corresponding to 163 viruses, including 13 new associations with orchids. Notably, 117 sequences likely represent putative novel species, including tentative new genera within the families Benyviridae, Betaflexiviridae, Phenuiviridae, and Tymoviridae. This analysis also reveals patterns of virus co-occurrence within the orchid virome and uncovers links between viral taxa and orchid life forms. Overall, these findings greatly broaden the known diversity of orchid-associated viruses and offer a comprehensive global framework for understanding their composition, ecological interactions, and potential scope.IMPORTANCEOrchids are among the most diverse plant families, yet little is known about the viruses associated with them. Plant viruses pose significant risks to agriculture and may also threaten orchid conservation, particularly when infected plant material is moved through trade or cultivation. A comprehensive understanding of the orchid virome is therefore essential for improving virus detection, managing diseases, and producing virus-free planting material. In this study, we used large-scale analysis of publicly available RNA-seq data to identify viral sequences associated with orchid-derived transcriptomic data sets and to characterize the diversity of orchid-associated viruses. Our results substantially expand the catalog of viruses associated with Orchidaceae, revealing numerous previously undescribed viruses and candidate virus-orchid associations. By providing a global perspective on the Orchidaceae virome, this work highlights the power of data mining approaches for virus discovery and establishes a foundation for future studies on plant virus ecology, evolution, and surveillance.

items.title: Local Adaptation to the Sex Environment: Reciprocal Sex-Limited Selection in Different Thermal Regimes.
items.abstract: The shared genome prevents independent responses to sex differences in selection. Each sex does not evolve in response to its own sex-specific selection but is influenced by selection on the other sex via the shared genome. We used experimental evolution in Drosophila melanogaster to create separate pools of Chromosome 3s for males (male-limited "ML" chromosomes) and females (female-limited "FL" chromosomes), thereby separating the gene pool, for 15 generations. Viewing each sex as a separate environment, this separation of the genome allows sex-specific adaptation to each sex environment. We performed a reciprocal transplant between the sexes to quantify the strength of local adaptation to each sex. We found each chromosome type was more beneficial in the sex it had been selected for (i.e., local adaptation to sex). Because it has been postulated that sex-differences in selection may depend on how well adapted a population is to the abiotic environment, we performed experimental evolution at two thermal regimes (3 replicate populations each): one benign temperature to which the populations were well-adapted and one novel temperature. Female-specific adaptation was stronger at the benign temperature whereas male-specific adaptation was stronger in the novel temperature. Within chromosome pools, male and female fitness were more positively correlated in the novel compared to the benign conditions. Though males carrying ML chromosomes were typically more fit than males carrying FL chromosomes, they were also more harmful to their female mating partners.

items.title: How metapopulation dynamics shape evolutionary inferences from resurrection ecology.
items.abstract: In the context of global change, such as climate change, resurrection ecology-where ancestors and descendants are phenotyped in a common environment-has recently emerged as a powerful method for characterizing evolution. This approach has been applied across diverse organisms, provided they possess a dormant stage in their life cycle. While limitations have been raised (e.g., the impact of propagule storage on phenotypes), methodological solutions have also been developed. Here, we identify metapopulation dynamics and within-population selection as a potential drivers of evolutionary change in resurrection ecology studies. Using a simple population genetic model, we show how allele frequencies can change with population age. Second, we propose a method to disentangle the evolutionary effects of metapopulation dynamics from those driven by external factors such as climate change. The method is based on the analysis of a set of populations at the initial sampling time and a new, independent set of populations after a given period, moving beyond from the classical "ancestor-descendant" paired approach.

items.title: Duplication, Loss, and Feeding Ecology of Lysozyme Gene Copy Number in Insects.
items.abstract: Lysozymes are ubiquitous enzymes traditionally associated with immune defense via bacterial cell wall degradation. In some insect lineages, particularly Diptera with bacteria-rich diets, these enzymes have been secondarily recruited for digestion, but how widespread this shift is across other insect groups remains unclear. Here we investigate the evolutionary dynamics and functional roles of C-type and I-type lysozymes across 275 insect genomes, inferring patterns of gene duplication and loss and testing associations between lysozyme copy number and dietary habits. Phylogenetic Generalized Least Squares (PGLS) method revealed few significant associations: a weak link between larval detritivory and C-type copy number, and a more consistent one between an omnivorous diet and I-type copy number across life stages. Duplication analysis revealed multiple independent expansions of C-type lysozymes within Brachycera. In Muscoidea, C-type lysozymes were highly expressed in the Musca domestica larval midgut, consistent with digestion, whereas in Blattodea, moderate C-type copy numbers and salivary gland-biased expression in Periplaneta americana adults instead suggest a primarily antiseptic role. I-type lysozymes lack the catalytic residues required for canonical muramidase activity, yet remain conserved throughout Insecta, including in lineages that lost C-type lysozymes, suggesting alternative, non-canonical functions. Together, these findings are more consistent with a predominantly lineage-specific pattern of gene family evolution, largely uncoupled from a single ecological driver, than with a broad, diet-driven adaptive signal. Digestive recruitment of C-type lysozymes may extend beyond the well-characterized cases of Musca domestica and Drosophila melanogaster to additional expanded lineages across Brachycera, although direct functional evidence remains lacking.

items.title: To buzz or to sip: Asymmetric pollination effectiveness hints at the evolutionary transition of floral rewards.
items.abstract: Evolutionary transitions between floral reward types, such as the repeated loss of nectar, are common across angiosperms, yet the ecological mechanisms driving these shifts remain poorly understood. In Pedicularis, the evolutionary loss of nectar is hypothesized to be associated with shifts to buzz pollination. However, empirical comparisons of pollination effectiveness between nectar- and pollen-foraging behaviours within a single transitional system are largely lacking. We investigated Pedicularis alaschanica and its principal pollinator, Bombus friseanus, in the Hengduan Mountains. This plant represents a transitional evolutionary state, as it possesses a beak for specialized pollen delivery but still secretes copious nectar. This novel and unique system allows for a direct comparison of two distinct intraspecific foraging behaviours performed by the same bee species: upright nectar feeding (dorsal contact) versus vibratile pollen collection (ventral contact/buzz pollination). We quantified floral traits, nectar dynamics, single-visit pollen removal and deposition, and assessed the plant's breeding system and natural pollen limitation. We confirmed and quantified the nectar properties of this transitional species, revealing distinct nectar secretion dynamics. While single-visit pollen removal did not differ significantly between the two foraging behaviours, buzz-pollinating visits were significantly more time-efficient and deposited on average more than twice as many pollen grains on stigmas compared to nectar-foraging visits. Breeding system experiments revealed that P. alaschanica is a partially self-incompatible outcrosser, and its natural seed set is not pollen-limited. Our study revealed a marked functional asymmetry in pollen transfer driven by intraspecific behavioral variation among pollinators. In a non-pollen-limited system, the superior per-visit pollen deposition achieved by buzz-pollinating bees likely enhances male siring success. This high effectiveness likely relaxes the selective pressure to maintain metabolically costly nectar. Our findings provide a compelling mechanistic explanation for the repeated evolutionary loss of floral nectar.

items.title: Auditory Biofeedback Gait Training in Individuals With Chronic Ankle Instability: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) develops in a large majority of patients with lateral ankle sprain (LAS), who often experience recurring injuries, residual feelings of instability, and abnormal neuromuscular patterns. Specifically, gait alterations are common in those with CAI and considered a contributing factor to poor long-term ankle joint health. Yet, there are no evidence-based gait-training protocols targeted to improve biomechanics, which may improve long-term outcomes related to ankle joint health and patient satisfaction. This study protocol introduces a progressive auditory biofeedback (ABF) gait-training program aimed to improve short- and long-term lower extremity biomechanics and talar cartilage outcomes and reduce the frequency of ankle-giving-way episodes and recurring injuries. This study is a multisite randomized controlled trial (RCT) with a target enrollment of 100 patients with CAI into a control group (n=50, 50%) or an ABF gait-training program (n=50, 50%). Both groups will complete a progressive 6-week (12-session) protocol comprising walking, ruck marching, and running on a treadmill. Lower extremity kinematics and kinetics, talar cartilage characteristics (via ultrasonography), self-perceived dysfunction and instability, and number of recurring sprains will be assessed prior to intervention, immediately after intervention, and 6 and 12 months postintervention. Finally, the frequency of ankle-giving-way episodes in the 6 months prior to intervention will be compared to the frequency of episodes at the 6- and 12-month time points to determine a longitudinal difference in ankle-giving-way episodes. The study was funded in September 2024 and prospectively registered through ClinicalTrials.gov on March 10, 2025. The first participant was enrolled in May 2025. As of August 2026, 118 individuals had been recruited and 19 participants enrolled. Recruitment will remain open until September 2027, and study completion is expected in September 2028. Data processing is projected to continue through September 2028, with the final report published in June 2029. This study will be the first RCT of ABF gait training to assess the immediate and long-term effects on lower extremity biomechanics, ankle joint health, and patient-reported outcomes in patients with CAI. Results from this study will advance the knowledge of long-term joint health that may be associated with poor outcomes post-LAS. items.title: Nocturnal road traffic noise and Sleep during Mid-Adulthood in Urban Settings: Examining Sex and Socioeconomic Differences within the DAS-EP Project.
items.abstract: Sleep is essential for physical and mental health but tends to deteriorate from mid adulthood, particularly among women. Nocturnal road traffic noise is a major environmental stressor that can disrupt sleep. This study aimed to examine the association between nocturnal road traffic noise and sleep health during mid-adulthood and explore potential sex-based differences. We conducted a cross sectional analysis using data from population health surveys (2021-2023) including 1,898 adults aged 40-60 living in urban areas of the Basque Autonomous Community, the Valencian Community, and Barcelona. Nocturnal road traffic noise was assessed using Lnight indicator, defined as the long-term average noise level during the night-time period (23:00-07:00), and estimated using official noise maps. Sleep health was assessed through self-reported measures of sleep duration, overall sleep satisfaction, and sleep quality using the SATED scale, a multidimensional measure of sleep health (Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, and Duration). A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) was used to identify covariate adjustment sets and associations were estimated using linear models accounting for the complex survey design. Women generally reported poorer sleep health than men, with lower sleep satisfaction and poorer sleep quality, and sleep quality increased with area-level household income. Noise exposure increased with income at lower levels, while different patterns were observed across regions after €50,000. The association between noise exposure and sleep health varied across regions and sleep health dimensions. In Barcelona, higher noise exposure was associated with greater sleep satisfaction, but this association was not significant in pooled meta analyses. In contrast, higher noise exposure was associated with poorer sleep quality in the Basque Country, with the pooled meta-analysis showing a similar overall pattern. These findings highlight the context-dependent nature of noise-sleep relationships and support the need for targeted public health strategies.

items.title: Altered white matter functional activity and connectivity in pretreatment breast cancer: exploratory associations with affective symptoms.
items.abstract: Resting-state fMRI studies in breast cancer have predominantly focused on gray matter, with limited attention to white matter functional organization. This study investigated white matter functional activity and connectivity before treatment and their associations with anxiety and depressive symptoms. Female patients with breast cancer (BC) were recruited from Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital from November 2023 to December 2025. Amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) were used to compare local white matter functional activity between the BC and healthy control (HC) groups. Seed-based functional connectivity (FC) analysis was then performed to investigate whole-brain white matter FC alterations. Correlations between clinical scale scores and rs-fMRI indices were analyzed. Compared with HCs, patients with BC showed altered ALFF/fALFF in the anterior and posterior corona radiata, internal capsule, posterior thalamic radiation, body of the corpus callosum, pontine crossing tract, left superior cerebellar peduncle, and left superior longitudinal fasciculus. Seed-based analysis revealed decreased FC within the bilateral anterior corona radiata and between the body of the corpus callosum and right anterior corona radiata, and increased FC between the left superior cerebellar peduncle and left posterior thalamic radiation. Higher ALFF in the body of the corpus callosum and reduced FC between this region and the right anterior corona radiata were associated with higher Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale scores at an uncorrected threshold. Neither association survived FDR correction. Patients with BC showed altered white matter functional activity and connectivity before cancer-related treatment, suggesting that pretreatment brain functional alterations may also involve white matter functional organization. The relationship between these white matter changes and anxiety or depressive symptoms remains exploratory.

items.title: Structural constraints and psychosocial eating behaviours associated with dietary quality among reproductive-aged mothers in urban slums of Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Dietary quality among women in urban slums may reflect structural constraints and eating behaviours, yet evidence examining both is limited. This cross-sectional study examined associations of food insecurity, work-time burden, and eating behaviours with dietary quality among 400 mothers aged 15-49 years in 20 urban slums of Dhaka, Bangladesh (two-stage stratified cluster sampling), and explored whether food insecurity moderated the emotional eating-dietary quality association. Dietary quality was assessed using the Bangladesh Healthy Eating Index (BD-HEI; 0-90) from a single 24-h recall, and food insecurity using the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES; 0-8). Multilevel models with slum random intercepts included linear and quadratic food insecurity terms (quadratic term improved fit, p < .001). Mean BD-HEI was 61.5 (SD 15.7), lowest for fruits and milk products. Predicted BD-HEI was 17.3 (95% CI: -24.2 to -10.5) and 18.6 points (-26.7 to -10.4) lower at FIES = 4 and 8, respectively, than at FIES = 0, mostly at low scores, with no statistically significant difference between FIES 6 and 8. Age (β = 0.375) was positively, and emotional eating (β = -0.872 per scale point; 95% CI: -1.696 to -0.048) negatively, associated with BD-HEI; work-time burden and residence duration were not significant after adjustment. The apparent food insecurity × emotional eating interaction was not supported with a quadratic term (joint test χ2(2) = 1.89, p = .389). Findings were similar including implausible energy reporters (n = 427); associations are cross-sectional and the nonlinear analyses data-driven.

items.title: Psychometric Validation of PROMIS Measures in Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis.
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures are essential for evaluating symptom burden and quality of life (QoL) in acute and chronic pancreatitis (AP/CP), yet many instruments used in this patient population lack robust psychometric evidence. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) offers standardized measures designed for comparability across populations, but their suitability for AP/CP has not been comprehensively evaluated. The objective of this study was to assess the psychometric properties of PROMIS-29, PROMIS-Global Health, and PROMIS Pain Quality scales in individuals with AP/CP and provide an overview of psychometric standards that facilitate selection of PROs for use in clinical research and patient care. Data were drawn from 1,927 participants enrolled in PROCEED, a multi-site longitudinal study across the pancreatitis spectrum, including healthy controls, chronic abdominal pain, acute/recurrent acute pancreatitis and definite CP. Factor models and regressions were used to psychometrically evaluate univariate construct validity, known-groups validity, convergent validity, reliability, structural validity and population invariance. PROMIS measures exceeded all psychometric benchmarks tested. Scores were approximately normally distributed and comprehensively covered the range of each symptom domain. Correlations with other commonly used QoL measures supported convergent validity. PROMIS scores discriminated effectively among diagnostic subgroups and exhibited excellent structural validity and internal consistency reliability. Population invariance assessments indicated that scores are comparable across age, sex, race, and diagnostic subgroups. This study provides strong preliminary evidence that PROMIS measures meet rigorous psychometric standards that supports their use in patient research and care in AP/CP. Their adoption may enhance measurement consistency and support core outcome sets in clinical research and trials of AP/CP.

items.title: A two-layer model of technology lay beliefs and their societal and political consequences: The case of AI.
items.abstract: Modern technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to economic and societal prosperity. Yet, independent of their actual effects, consumers, workers, and the public often hold negative beliefs about these technologies, which can contribute to aversion to AI and technological change more broadly. This article examines technology lay beliefs, with AI as the focal case, and proposes an interconnected two-layer model to explain their societal impact. Layer 1 captures general psychological predispositions to technological change that provide a baseline for why technology lay beliefs often emphasize potential losses. Layer 2 captures specific contextual interpretations of AI that amplify or attenuate this baseline. We use this model to organize existing research and discuss the societal and political consequences of technology lay beliefs in the age of AI.

items.title: The psychology behind knowledge hiding: Exploring resource preservation motives and their impact on employee well-being and performance.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the phenomenon of knowledge hiding in organizational settings by examining its antecedents and consequences at the employee level. Specifically, the study seeks to uncover the underlying factors that drive individuals to engage in knowledge hiding behavior and to understand the subsequent effects this behavior has on employees. This study employs an exploratory qualitative design. Data were collected through open-ended essays administered via an online research platform, with responses obtained from 50 full-time employees across varied industries. The essays were analyzed using thematic analysis, following open, axial, and selective coding, allowing for the identification of both the antecedents and outcomes of knowledge hiding. The study highlights that personal antecedents such as indispensability, moral disengagement, and concerns over career prospects were associated with knowledge hiding behavior. Similarly, contextual antecedents including task interdependence and the presence (or absence) of ethical leadership were perceived by participants to shape knowledge-hiding behaviors within organizations. Further, the findings suggest that overall knowledge hiding was associated with adverse effects on critical employee outcomes, leading to reduced creative and innovative performance, diminished psychological well-being, and compromised task performance. This study advances the knowledge hiding literature by simultaneously uncovering its personal and contextual antecedents and linking them to multiple employee outcomes. This study also enhances theoretical understanding and offers a more nuanced foundation for future research in organizational behavior and knowledge management. It also advances the conservation of resources theory by examining how resource preservation motivations drive knowledge hiding behaviors in organizational settings.

items.title: Differentiating predictors of physical and cognitive effort expenditure in early psychosis: A study of reinforcement environment, negative symptoms, and cognitive control.
items.abstract: Schizophrenia patients compared to controls show reduced physical and cognitive effort allocation despite higher rewards offered. Negative symptoms, cognitive control deficits, and functional impairments are all implicated in reduced effort allocation, suggesting compromised cognitive-reward systems drive patient outcomes. However, patterns and predictors of decisions to expend different types of effort remain underexplored in early psychosis (EP). This study investigated predictors of effort allocation in 34 EP outpatients. We used Generalized Estimating Equations to evaluate the following as predictors of decisions to expend effort: (1) changes in reinforcement environment (reward, probability, expected value), and (2) patient characteristics (expressive and motivation/pleasure symptoms, cognitive control). Assessments included the Effort Expenditure for Rewards Task (physical), a parallel cognitive effort task adapted by our team, AX-Continuous Performance Test, and clinical symptom interviews (e.g., Brief Negative Symptom Scale). Patients modulated physical effort based on integrated assessments of reward and probability. Cognitive control, measured as the proactive maintenance of goal-relevant information and resources, predicted physical effort expenditure, but only at low expressive symptom severity. In contrast, patients showed inefficient effort modulation and a risk-aversive probabilistic assessment on the cognitive effort task. By early psychosis, patients exhibit conservative cognitive effort allocation, disregarding high-value rewards, despite intact capacity. Our findings indicated that negative symptoms and cognitive control had a minimal direct influence on effort decisions in early psychosis. This suggests that the illness burden in early stages may be less pronounced than in chronic psychotic illness, potentially leading to different mechanistic pathways for effort allocation.

items.title: Network analysis reveals specific patterns of relationships between connected speech features in subjective cognitive decline.
items.abstract: Subtle language changes occur early in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Early detection of these changes therefore represents a potential tool for the early detection of individuals who could develop the disease. Knowledge on connected speech (CS) in Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD, a preclinical stage of AD for at least some individuals, characterized by cognitive complaints without objective cognitive deficits), remains limited. In this study, we used network analysis to examine the relationships between CS features extracted with Natural Language Processing techniques. This method allowed us to determine whether the patterns emerging from the SCD CS network (i.e., a network modelling the relationships between CS features) differed from those observed in similar networks constructed for controls and individuals with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI, a prodromal stage of AD for many individuals, characterized by objective cognitive deficits but preserved daily functioning). We found minimal differences between individuals with SCD and controls and individuals with MCI in raw CS features. Nevertheless, our network analysis revealed a stronger relative subdivision of the SCD network into different dimensions (representing linguistic domains), as well as relative reductions in within-dimension density and between-dimension strength compared to the Control and MCI networks. There were also relative differences in how the CS features forming the Semantic conciseness and Lexical and syntactic complexity dimensions associated with other features in the SCD network. Results suggest that network analysis might be more sensitive than other methods to subtle CS differences in SCD and that this population might use distinct CS production mechanisms.

items.title: A failure of food-specific inhibitory control training to affect food choices via a hypothetical food delivery platform.
items.abstract: Inhibitory control training (ICT) is a computerised intervention which requires individuals to repeatedly inhibit a pre-potent motor response to unhealthy food-related cues. In doing so the cues are devalued, which may in turn reduce the choice and/or consumption behaviour towards unhealthy foods. Whilst single-session laboratory evidence suggests ICT may be a promising intervention, online studies show equivocal results. In this pre-registered randomised controlled trial, we administered ICT online (vs a control group) to 512 individuals (47.6% female, mean age = 41.68). Immediately following training participants were asked to make a hypothetical food order from a mock pizza delivery website based on a popular UK chain. Devaluation of pizza, salad, and unhealthy but untrained images was also measured pre- and post-training. Our results demonstrated that ICT (mean = 1270 kcal) did not lead to fewer calories ordered vs the control group (mean = 1287 kcal: t(503.74) = 0.381, p = .703, d = 0.03 [95% CI: -0.14 to 0.21]: BF10 = 0.105), or fewer number of individuals ordering pizza-dishes (X2(1) = 1.93, p = .165; OR = 0.72 [95% CI: 0.47 to 1.11]: BF10 = 0.272). Overall, the findings of this study suggest ICT delivered online is unlikely to be an effective stand-alone intervention for changing food-ordering behaviours, however replication with real world outcomes is necessary.

items.title: Determining the Needs of Spanish-speaking Families That Receive Ambulatory Services in the Division of Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrics (DDBP): The Family Viewpoint.
items.abstract: Previous satisfaction surveys in a Midwestern developmental-behavioral pediatrics clinic showed suboptimal experiences among Spanish-speaking caregivers, particularly regarding visit length and feeling unsafe during encounters. This study sought to gather detailed information about Spanish-speaking families' experiences with ambulatory developmental-behavioral services and to address a gap in the literature on inequitable health care experiences among caregivers of children with developmental-behavioral disorders. We collected descriptive, qualitative data on Spanish-speaking families' experiences with developmental-behavioral ambulatory care using Group Level Assessment (GLA) and Participatory Action Research (PAR) methods. Fifteen Spanish-speaking caregivers participated. Although interpreter services were consistently available and often described as excellent, families reported concerns about interpretation accuracy and consistency. Caregivers also noted that providers sometimes appeared rushed, particularly when language barriers led to delays or shortened encounters with non‑Spanish-speaking clinicians. Families proposed several improvements, including expanding bilingual staffing to enhance comfort and communication, strengthening oversight and training for interpreter services-especially in telehealth-and ensuring interpreters actively engage children during therapeutic sessions. Addressing these concerns through expanded bilingual staffing, improved interpreter quality, and more culturally responsive communication practices may substantially enhance the care experience for Spanish-speaking families and promote more equitable developmental-behavioral services.

items.title: Effectiveness of the internet-based unified protocol transdiagnostic intervention for the treatment of depression, anxiety, and related disorders in a routine primary care setting in Ireland: a pilot pragmatic randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: The Unified Protocol (UP) is an empirically supported transdiagnostic therapy for emotional disorders. To improve scalability, alternative delivery methods are being developed such as an internet-based version of the UP (iUP) with minimal support. The study examined the effectiveness of iUP and explored users' experiences of the intervention within a primary care setting in Ireland. The study employed a randomised controlled trial design. Participants were assigned to: (a) the iUP or (b) an enhanced waiting list control (eWLC). Randomization followed a 2:1 allocation ratio (iUP n = 60; eWLC n = 29). Depression/anxiety symptoms were assessed at baseline, 4-weeks, 8-weeks and 12-weeks. Participants in the iUP condition also completed a follow-up assessment. Qualitative data regarding participants' experience were also collected. Participants receiving iUP showed statistically significant improvements over the course of treatment, with gains largely retained at follow-up. Although effect sizes suggested a trend for superiority of the iUP, the differences were not statistically significant relative to the eWLC group. Qualitative analyses indicated that participants appreciated the supporters' guidance and the theoretical framework of the intervention, and suggested increased personalization. Benefits included improvements in emotion regulation and awareness.Trial registration ISRCTN18056450 https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN18056450.

items.title: The association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Introduction: Parental health numeracy is relevant to pediatric asthma management because caregivers often interpret medication quantities, risk information, and peak-flow thresholds. Objective: This study examined the adjusted association between parental health numeracy and medication adherence among children with asthma in Jordan. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 400 parents or legal guardians of children with physician-diagnosed asthma at the University of Jordan Hospital between May and August 2024. The children had a median age of 6 years (IQR: 3-11). Parental numeracy was assessed using the Arabic version of the Asthma Numeracy Questionnaire (Ar-ANQ), and adherence was assessed using the Arabic version of the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5). Results: The median Ar-ANQ score was 3 (IQR: 1-4), and 178 children (44.5%) were classified as having high medication adherence. In adjusted logistic regression, each one-point increase in the Ar-ANQ score was associated with greater odds of high adherence (adjusted OR = 1.404, 95% CI: 1.179-1.672, p < 0.001). Parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence. Conclusion: Higher parental health numeracy was associated with greater odds of high medication adherence, whereas parental education and household income were not significantly associated with adherence.

items.title: Say Less! Backchanneling and HPA-axis Attunement, But Not Semantic Synchrony, Relate to Couples' Relationship Quality Across the Transition to Parenthood.
items.abstract: Language and physiology each carry information about how couples attune, yet are rarely studied together, especially during vulnerable periods such as the transition to parenthood. Semantic synchrony, or shared meaning across partners' speaking turns, is a potential marker of relational functioning that may reflect couples' use of active listening and reflection to validate one another's concerns. Semantic synchrony may also intersect with other dimensions of health-relevant synchrony such as covariation in partners' hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. The present study examined semantic and HPA-axis/cortisol synchrony in 100 expectant parent dyads during lab-based discussions in pregnancy and at six months postpartum. Results: Semantic synchrony was present across all conversations and was strongest during discussions of conflict. Positive HPA-axis synchrony emerged at both timepoints, but semantic and HPA-axis synchrony were unrelated. Semantic synchrony during discussions about relationship conflict was negatively associated with partners' validation of one another (i.e., communicating sincere understanding), but this association was primarily attributable to couples' backchanneling (e.g., "mmhm," "uh-huh") - brief verbal expressions that communicate understanding without interrupting the speaker. Neither form of synchrony predicted relationship quality at either visit, with one exception: postpartum HPA-axis synchrony marginally predicted couples' relationship quality (P=.04). Moreover, partners' backchanneling during discussions of conflict was positively associated with participants' relationship quality. Together, these findings suggest that it is backchanneling, not semantic synchrony, that is associated with greater validation and relationship quality and may therefore serve as a potential linguistic marker of relational functioning.

items.title: Blinks are strategically coupled with head movements in unconstrained natural gaze behavior.
items.abstract: Blinks are a ubiquitous yet largely unnoticed aspect of human vision, despite causing frequent interruptions of visual input that can amount to up to 10% of waking time. By leveraging a large dataset of unconstrained gaze behavior during two natural tasks, we found a behavioral strategy to limit the impact of blinks: blinks were strategically coupled with head movements, which minimizes information loss due to unreliable visual input during head movements. Specifically, blink probability increased with higher head velocities and showed strong temporal modulation relative to head movement onset: Blink probability was reduced before head movement initiation and then peaked during the head movement. The strength of this coupling was tailored to the individual needs of participants, with participants with higher baseline blink rates showing stronger synchronization. This indicates that blinks are a part of an individually coordinated strategy when orchestrating eye and head movements during unconstrained natural behavior.

items.title: Intrapersonal and interpersonal predictors of posttraumatic growth following the February 6, 2023, Türkiye earthquakes.
items.abstract: The present study examined intrapersonal and interpersonal predictors of posttraumatic growth (PTG) among survivors of the February 6, 2023, Türkiye (Turkey) earthquakes. Specifically, the study focused on loneliness, forms of self-criticism (inadequate self and hated self), self-reassurance, shame, and guilt as potential psychological correlates of PTG. A total of 300 adult earthquake survivors (61.8% women) participated in a face-to-face assessment approximately 2 years after the disaster. Participants completed self-report measures assessing PTG, loneliness, self-criticism, self-reassurance, shame, and guilt. Bayesian correlation and regression analyses were conducted to identify the most parsimonious psychological model of PTG. Results indicated strong evidence for a negative association between loneliness and PTG and very strong evidence for a positive association between self-reassurance and PTG. Associations between PTG and self-critical forms, shame, and guilt were weak or inconclusive. Model comparison demonstrated that a minimal model including loneliness and self-reassurance provided substantially stronger evidential support than more complex models (BF₁₀ = 1,671.34, R² = .086). In the final model, loneliness was negatively associated with PTG (b = -0.13, 95% credible interval [-0.24, -0.02]), whereas self-reassurance was positively associated with PTG (b = 0.36, 95% credible interval [0.16, 0.56]). These findings suggest that posttraumatic growth following large-scale disasters may be most closely tied to the restoration of interpersonal connectedness and the cultivation of affiliative self-regulation, with important implications for community-based and compassion-focused postdisaster mental health interventions. items.title: Enhanced cognitive flexibility with self-determined task choice.
items.abstract: Cognitive control-the ability to regulate one's behavior in accordance with internal goals-is fundamental to adaptive behavior. Despite substantial progress in our understanding of different cognitive control functions supporting goal-directed behavior, most studies rely on externally instructed tasks, whereas in real-world contexts, people often have the autonomy to choose which task to perform. Although research suggests that having the opportunity to choose can enhance a variety of psychological processes (e.g., motivation or learning), it remains unclear whether and how cognitive control differs between instructed and voluntarily chosen tasks. The present study addresses this question using a novel paradigm to investigate how one core function of cognitive control-the flexibility to switch between tasks-differs between self-determined (free-choice) and externally determined (forced-choice) tasks. We reasoned that self-determined task choice may enable individuals to optimize control more effectively (e.g., by switching when control demands are relatively low) and/or may motivate individuals to invest more effort in flexibility-related control processes. Consistent with performance optimization and motivational accounts, switch costs in task performance (in particular, reaction times) were reduced under free-choice compared to forced-choice tasks across multiple experiments. This reduction was driven specifically by shorter reaction times on switch trials in free-choice tasks, suggesting that voluntary task choice takes advantage of control processes that promote cognitive flexibility, such as disengaging from a previous task or reconfiguring a new one. Overall, the present study provides new evidence linking self-determined task choice to improvements in higher order cognitive control functions-specifically, cognitive flexibility. items.title: Correcting for publication bias in multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis: A multivariate step function selection model approach.
items.abstract: Univariate meta-analysis models assume that all effect sizes are independent. This assumption is violated if, for example, two outcomes are reported in a study of interest to the meta-analyst or a study reports multiple experiments administered by the same researchers. The multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis models allow modeling dependent effect sizes. These two models have recently gained in popularity among meta-analysts in psychology, where one of the largest threats to validity of meta-analysis is publication bias where a selective subset of studies remain unpublished. We extend the univariate step function selection model approach, for modeling publication bias, to multivariate and multilevel meta-analyses. We propose strict and relaxed selection models that assign a different publication probability to studies that have only statistically significant outcomes or at least one significant outcome. These two selection models are straightforward approaches for modeling publication bias. Our method can also accommodate more sophisticated alternative selection models, and we discuss possibilities for this. We primarily focus on the method's implementation as a sensitivity analysis where publication probabilities in the selection model are assumed as known but also show how these can be estimated. Simulation studies tailored to two applications show that the proposed method as a sensitivity analysis outperforms the multivariate and multilevel meta-analysis models that do not correct for publication bias. The simulations also show that the publication probability is imprecisely estimated. We offer guidance for applying the proposed method in practice and share R code to facilitate the application of our proposed methodology. items.title: How to design a panel study for investigating bivariate dynamics using continuous-time modeling.
items.abstract: Designing effective longitudinal panel studies to capture bivariate dynamics requires making informed decisions about how many measurements to collect and when to collect them. This study examines how sample size, number of repeated measures, and various aspects of the temporal sampling schedule influence the recovery of bivariate dynamic parameters in panel data analyzed using a continuous-time random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (CT-RI-CLPM). Through a Monte Carlo simulation, we tested a range of population generating conditions. We also proposed a novel approach for planning sampling schedules: the short-and-long-lags design (SHALL), which deliberately combines closely spaced and widely spaced intervals. SHALL schedules are simple to implement, require no prior knowledge of the system dynamics, and take advantage of the capacity of continuous-time models to accommodate unequal time intervals. Our findings indicate that the number of measurement occasions and sample size, rather than the temporal distribution of the measures, are the primary determinants of parameter recovery. Cross-effects proved particularly difficult to recover, exhibiting low estimation efficiency and statistical power even under the most favorable conditions. We provide actionable recommendations for researchers planning panel data studies, along with open-source R code to facilitate the design of SHALL sampling schedules and for fitting the CT-RI-CLPM to new data sets. An empirical example illustrates the application of such model to data from an empirical panel study relating self-esteem and depression. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Plastic consumption and waste generation in China: Pathways toward full chain governance under policy interventions.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution has emerged as a central challenge in global environmental governance, placing production limits and upstream mitigation at the heart of the negotiation under the ongoing UN global plastics treaty process. Effective governance requires robust, forward-looking assessments of plastic demand. This study develops an integrated forecasting framework that couples S-curve dynamics with multiple linear regression to capture both long-term economic convergence and short-term socioeconomic drivers. Using historical data from 1980 to 2020 across 68 countries and regions, the model projects China's plastic consumption and waste generation to 2040 and evaluates the outcomes of alternative policy pathways. Results identify three representative S-curve development trajectories. In the absence of further mitigation measures, extrapolation from comparable medium-to-high economies suggests that China's annual per capita plastic consumption could reach 132-182 kg by 2040, with annual plastic waste generation rising to approximately 208 Mt, largely driven by short-lived applications. However, scenario analysis demonstrates that an integrated circular economy strategy-combining source reduction, material substitution, and enhanced recycling-could curb total plastic demand by up to 24 % and reduce mismanaged waste by nearly 90 % compared to a business-as-usual baseline, with packaging and textiles presenting the highest mitigation potential. By linking demand-side drivers with sector-specific waste fate and policy levers, this analysis provides a quantitative, full-chain evidence base to support China's transition to a circular plastics economy and to inform ambitious national targets under a future global plastics agreement.

items.title: Differentially Expressed Infection-Associated Genes in a Shewanella algae isolate From a Deceased Northern Bottlenose Whale.
items.abstract: Diseases are an important but poorly understood influence on marine ecosystems. However, many pathogens of wild marine organisms remain poorly characterized, limiting our understanding of their ecology and potential impacts. This study investigates the potential virulence mechanisms of a Shewanella algae strain isolated from the brain tissue of a deceased northern bottlenose whale (Hyperoodon ampullatus). Using long-read Oxford Nanopore RNA Sequencing, differential gene expression analysis (DGEA) was conducted comparing growth in standard media, Tryptic Soy Broth (TSB) and TSB supplemented with 5% brain homogenate (BH) to stimulate expression of genes potentially associated with virulence. Twenty-eight significantly differentially expressed genes (23 identified using the assembled genome and five additional non-overlapping genes detected using a closely related reference genome) were identified out of 7,213 genes with at least two primary mapped reads. These genes were associated with processes that have been linked to bacterial virulence in previous studies, including protein translocation (e.g., small signal recognition particle), flagellar motility, chemotaxis, and iron acquisition. Functional analysis indicated an increased expression of pathways related to amino acid metabolism and motility, whereas carbohydrate and inorganic ion transport were downregulated. These results suggest that environmental cues, potentially including factors related to iron metabolism, may influence bacterial virulence, obtained using Oxford Nanopore RNA sequencing for pathogen transcriptomics.

items.title: Conflict with industrial fleets undermines the contributions of small-scale fisheries to sustainable development in vulnerable regions.
items.abstract: Equitable and sustainable governance of small-scale fisheries (SSFs) is essential for achieving food security and conservation in coastal areas. Yet in increasingly industrialized oceans, competition and conflict with large-scale fisheries (LSFs) threaten the contributions of SSFs to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Here we have developed a small-scale and industrial fisheries interaction index and applied it to 126 countries using 2 recent global datasets. Vulnerability to conflict is highest in countries where SSFs are vital for nutrition, but governance is weak, especially in Africa, Oceania and Asia. We also identify low-exposure outlier countries with unexpectedly low risk of SSF-LSF interactions, providing insights for proactive policy. Preferential access areas granting spatial rights to SSFs are common in both low- and high-vulnerability countries, suggesting such policies are often reactive and may be insufficient alone without strong enforcement. As ocean industries expand, it will be necessary to strengthen SSF access rights and limit LSF overcapacity to reduce conflict and advance sustainable development.

items.title: Steroid hormones produced by coral-associated Endozoicomonas influence coral immune response during thermal stress.
items.abstract: The coral microbiome is believed to play a crucial role in sustaining corals and enabling adaptation to perturbations. A ubiquitous group of coral-associated bacteria, known as Endozoicomonas, are hypothesized to provide essential metabolites to corals, although detailed dynamics of the interactions between host and microbe are poorly understood. Here multi-omics and laboratory validation experiments reveal that Endozoicomonas encodes genes for the metabolism of coral-derived testosterone and converts ubiquitous cholesterol into testosterone and progesterone, both important steroids that accumulate within the coral holobiont during thermal stress. Field sampling along a natural temperature gradient showed general suppression of coral steroid hormones under thermal stress and during white syndrome manifestation. Provision of testosterone or progesterone to corals during laboratory thermal stress induced transcriptional reprogramming of the coral innate immune response, suggesting microbial involvement in host immune modulation. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized potential mechanism of microbial contribution to coral resilience.

items.title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity.
items.abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO 2 effects on the chemistry of the world's ecosystems remains nascent. CO 2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO 2 ) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO 2 , implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

items.title: Hidden potential for mixotrophy in soil protists.
items.abstract: Mixotrophy, the ability of a single protist to combine phototrophy and phagotrophy, is widely recognized as an important functional strategy in aquatic ecosystems, where it shapes food-web structure and carbon cycling. In soil, however, mixotrophy remains largely overlooked despite increasing evidence for trophic flexibility among protists. Here, we argue that this neglect may reflect conceptual and methodological limitations rather than ecological absence. We highlight inconsistencies in trait-based classifications, delineate feeding traits that enable certain forms of mixotrophy, and evaluate soil microhabitats that support mixotrophic activity. Recognizing mixotrophy in soil challenges traditional views of distinct trophic categories and reveals its potential contributions to soil carbon fluxes. Incorporating mixotrophy into soil ecology is therefore essential for developing mechanistic and predictive models of terrestrial ecosystem functioning.

items.title: Comparison of Giemsa and Hemacolor Staining Reveals Systematic Differences in Avian Leukocyte Profiles.
items.abstract: Accurate identification of avian leukocyte fractions from blood smears depends strongly on the staining method. This study provides a comparative evaluation of Giemsa and Hemacolor staining, integrating qualitative and quantitative assessments based on paired samples from 39 Great Tits Parus major . Leukocyte profiles derived from Hemacolor-stained smears showed significantly higher heterophil counts and approximately 40% higher H:L ratios, whereas Giemsa-stained smears yielded higher lymphocyte proportions; eosinophil counts did not differ significantly between methods. These quantitative differences were consistent with microscopic characteristics: Hemacolor generated a lighter field with distinctly defined heterophilic granules, while Giemsa provided stronger nuclear contrast and facilitated lymphocyte identification. The consistent directional differences observed between staining methods indicate a systematic bias in leukocyte assessment. Because the two methods emphasize different cellular features, they produce non-interchangeable leukocyte profiles with implications for ecological and physiological interpretation. Accordingly, staining protocols should be explicitly reported, and a single method should be applied consistently within a dataset.

items.title: Host-Associated School Integration and Behaviour Among Juvenile Caranx crysos and Sarpa salpa in a Shallow Mediterranean Habitat.
items.abstract: Interspecific associations between fishes can generate complex behavioural interactions, yet their occurrence and functional significance in temperate marine systems remain poorly documented. Here we describe a previously unreported case of host-associated behaviour involving juvenile Caranx crysos and schools of juvenile Sarpa salpa in coastal Mediterranean habitats. Associations were recorded exclusively in C. crysos individuals ≤ 15 cm TL, suggesting a size- and context-dependent pattern of association with the host schools. Juvenile C. crysos integrated into S. salpa schools by adopting spatial positioning and behavioural patterns consistent with social mimicry. This association may provide antipredator advantages through group integration, while also allowing opportunistic foraging on benthic organisms and resuspended organic particles generated during host grazing activity. In rare cases, multiple individuals of C. crysos co-occurred within the same school, producing aggressive interactions and indicating intraspecific competition for access to the host aggregation. From the host perspective, S. salpa exhibited only brief and limited behavioural responses, with no evidence of persistent exclusion or disruption of schooling behaviour, suggesting a low-cost, largely tolerated interaction. Overall, our observations suggest the occurrence of a host-related behavioural strategy in juvenile C. crysos that combines group integration, commensalistic and opportunistic feeding and intraspecific competition, likely shaped by ontogenetic constraints. These results highlight a previously overlooked level of behavioural complexity in temperate fish assemblages and suggest that fine-scale interspecific interactions in Mediterranean coastal ecosystems may be more widespread than currently recognised.

items.title: Co-Infection of Aeromonas veronii and Citrobacter braakii in Yellow Catfish (Tachysurus fulvidraco).
items.abstract: Recently, a disease outbreak was observed in farmed yellow catfish (Tachysurus fulvidraco) in Tianjin, China. Naturally infected fish exhibited surface haemorrhages, abdominal distension, anal redness, and hemorrhagic ascites. Histopathological examination revealed systemic lesions in the stomach, intestine, liver, and spleen. Two Gram-negative bacterial isolates, designated PFL and PFS, were isolated from the liver and spleen of diseased fish, respectively. The isolates were identified as Aeromonas veronii and Citrobacter braakii by morphological and biochemical characterisation combined with 16S rRNA and gyrB gene sequence analyses. Experimental infection with single or combined isolates demonstrated that both A. veronii and C. braakii were pathogenic to yellow catfish, with A. veronii showing higher virulence. Fish infected with A. veronii or co-infected with the two isolates displayed similar external clinical signs with the naturally diseased fish. Hemolytic assays revealed β-hemolysis in A. veronii and γ-hemolysis in C. braakii. These findings indicate that both A. veronii and C. braakii contribute to disease outbreaks in yellow catfish.

items.title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.
items.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

items.title: The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
items.abstract: Objective To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). Methods We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Results Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). Conclusions PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.

items.title: Metagenomic analysis of oral microbiota in Chinese children with obesity.
items.abstract: Childhood obesity represents an increasingly severe global public‑health concern, whose precise etiology remains incompletely elucidated and is likely multifactorial. In addition to genetic and lifestyle factors, mounting evidence indicates that the microbes in the digestive tract play a crucial role in the development and progression of obesity. Among them, the oral microbiota may contribute to obesity through mechanisms such as inducing systemic chronic inflammation and promoting gut microbiota dysbiosis. In the present study, saliva samples were collected from 9 obese children and 9 normal-weight children. Using metagenomic sequencing, we aimed to analyze the structural characteristics and functional profiles of the oral microbiota in Chinese school‑age children with obesity, so as to comprehensively dissect the oral microbiome ecology of this population from structural and functional perspectives. The results revealed that the microbiota diversity was similar between the two groups. At the species level, Dialister invisus, Treponema porcinum, Moraxella sp., Moraxella sp. VT 16 12, Moraxella lacunata, and Moraxella caprae were significantly enriched in the normal-weight group. Conversely, Campylobacter concisus, Veillonella sp. oral taxon 158, Veillonella rogosae, Veillonella sp. S13053 19, Streptococcus ilei, and Streptococcus australis were significantly enriched in the obese group. Functional annotation analysis demonstrated significant enrichment of functional genes associated with the hypoxia-inducible factor-1 (HIF-1) signaling pathway, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway, beta-alanine metabolism, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling pathway, and apoptosis in the normal-weight group. In contrast, functional genes related to biofilm formation-Vibrio cholerae, selenocompound metabolism, RNA polymerase, xylene degradation, and dioxin degradation were significantly enriched in the obese group. Correlation analysis further revealed strong positive correlations between Veillonella sp. oral taxon 158, Veillonella sp. S13053 19, Streptococcus ilei, Streptococcus australis and the functional pathways of biofilm formation-Vibrio cholerae, selenocompound metabolism, xylene degradation, and dioxin degradation. These observations suggest that the oral microbiome undergoes compositional and functional alterations in children with obesity, implying a potential role of oral microbiota in the etiology of childhood obesity.

items.title: Thresholds for clinical importance to improve interpretation of the EORTC QLQ-COMU26 communication questionnaire.
items.abstract: Purpose This study defined thresholds for clinical importance (TCIs) for the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Communication Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-COMU26). TCIs support the clinical evaluation of individual patients' communication with professionals. Methods In this cross-sectional study, an international sample of cancer patients with mixed diagnoses and treatments completed the EORTC QLQ-COMU26, which comprises six scales and four individual items. Item 26, which evaluates patients' satisfaction with communication with professionals, served as the anchor for detecting a negative event (unsatisfactory communication). Diagnostic accuracy for each domain was determined using ROC analysis, and the sensitivity of the TCIs was evaluated. Sensitivity analyses using multivariate binary logistic regression explored potential variability in TCIs across patient groups. Results A total of 988 patients from 13 countries participated (mean age, 60.7; 50.0% female). TCIs ranged from 80.3 to 92.5 on the 0-100 metric of the QLQ-COMU26 scales. All TCIs demonstrated sensitivity of at least 0.75, and ROC AUC values ranged from 0.80 to 0.90. Separate TCIs were identified for communication with nurses and doctors, with thresholds > 4 points higher for nurses in five QLQ-COMU26 domains. No evidence supported separate thresholds by age, gender, or treatment intention. Conclusion This study established TCIs with high diagnostic accuracy for the EORTC QLQ-COMU26, supporting its use in clinical practice and research. The findings suggest that the questionnaire can identify patients who report low communication for specific domains and help improve communication in clinical settings.

items.title: Leveraging whole-genome sequencing to manage a Streptococcus agalactiae outbreak in a neonatal intensive care unit.
items.abstract: Objectives To investigate late-onset Group B Streptococcus (GBS) transmission dynamics in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). Setting A 57-bed level III NICU in Toronto, Canada. Patients Neonates with late-onset GBS (LOGBS) identified, July 2023-February 2024. Methods An outbreak management team oversaw the investigation, hygiene audits, and stakeholder communications. Canada's National Microbiology Laboratory performed WGS (Illumina) on outbreak and prior isolates. Core single nucleotide variant (SNV) phylogeny used SNVPhyl. Clinical data included age, infection type, maternal GBS status and outcome were reviewed. Three consecutive weekly point-prevalence surveys (PPS) were conducted using rectal and throat swabs. Results In August 2023, two LOGBS cases (bacteremia and meningitis) triggered the investigation. Two more LOGBS bacteremias occurred pending WGS results. Three of the 4 isolates matched a prior early-onset (day-1) case (0 SNVs; cluster 1, serotype Ia). The fourth was 1 SNV different from a conjunctivitis case detected a week later (cluster 2, serotype V). PPS revealed 5 asymptomatic cases genomically unrelated to either cluster. In February 2024, two further LOGBS cases (bacteremia; asymptomatic bacteruria) emerged. The first matched the mother's antepartum isolate with transmission to the second infant (0 SNVs; cluster 3, serotype IV). Hygiene audits identified gaps in hand and environmental safety; room proximity was the primary commonality. Following reinforcement of infection prevention measures, no further nosocomial GBS infections occurred through October 2025. Conclusions This prolonged NICU outbreak involved multiple serotypes. WGS was critical in distinguishing horizontal transmission from independent introductions, directly guiding targeted infection control interventions.

items.title: How to tackle inequities in bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities: a national qualitative study using experience-based co-design.
items.abstract: Background High-income countries globally are becoming increasingly diverse. People from ethnically diverse communities experience inequities in accessing bereavement support, but evidence to inform equitable provision remains limited. We aimed to determine how formal bereavement support services can better serve ethnically diverse communities by identifying barriers to and facilitators of equitable access, defining key components of culturally safe and appropriate bereavement care, and developing a logic model and recommendations for equitable bereavement support. Methods Multi-phase national qualitative study, drawing on experience-based co-design principles. We conducted interviews (n = 53) and focus groups (n = 9) with 121 bereaved people from 13 ethnically diverse backgrounds, interviews with 23 bereavement support providers across 12 services, four online co-design workshops with bereaved people and stakeholders (n = 53), and a hybrid workshop to refine recommendations (n = 29 stakeholders). Recruitment and data collection prioritised cultural safety and an asset-based approach. Directed thematic analysis was informed by Levesque et al.'s access to healthcare framework. Results Barriers to equitable bereavement support arose across the access pathway but were concentrated mainly within bereavement support organisations and the wider bereavement support system. Racism and intersectionality were cross-cutting themes, influencing whether bereaved people could identify, trust, reach and engage with support. Key barriers included poor signposting and referral, long waiting lists, limited staff diversity, language barriers, weak organisational commitment to equity, precarious funding, and white-centred, individualised models of grief support. Participants identified culturally safe and equitable care as requiring anti-racist practice, sustained community partnership, provision of support in trusted settings and community languages, holistic and flexible provision, and greater investment in grassroots services designed and delivered by ethnically diverse communities. The logic model and recommendations identify system-wide actions needed to address barriers and support equitable access. Conclusions Inequitable access to bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities is rooted primarily in the design, organisation and cultural orientation of services and the wider bereavement support system. Improving equity will require sustained investment in community-led provision, accountability mechanisms, and genuine partnership with ethnically diverse communities. Findings from this robust multi-perspective study provide actionable recommendations to reform bereavement support across high- and middle-income settings.

items.title: Suicide among children and adolescents in India as a public mental health priority.
items.abstract: Background Suicide among children and adolescents (≤ 18 years old) is a growing public health concern in India, contributing to an alarming 6% of total suicides reported in 2022. Despite policy efforts, systemic gaps in prevention, reporting, and mental health infrastructure persist. Methods/approach This paper uses secondary data from the Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI) reports (2014-2023) published by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) to map the key trends and key drivers of suicide among youth in India. Descriptive report estimates on suicide data among individuals aged 0-18 years were categorised by gender, cause, and year. To interpret the underlying drivers of suicide, we applied the Socio-Ecological Model (SEM), which organises risk factors across four levels: individual, interpersonal, community, and societal. Results Between 2014 and 2023, a total of 100,787 children died by suicide in India, with female children consistently outnumbering males. The most frequently reported causes were family-related problems (25,049), followed by academic failure (12,988), love affairs (12,988), and mental illness (6143). Nearly 29% of suicides were attributed to unknown or "other" causes, indicating gaps in documentation. Conclusion Suicide among Indian children and adolescents is driven by multifaceted structural and psychosocial factors. A Bronfenbrenner's socio-ecological approach reveals multiple points of intervention, including school-based mental health services, family support programs, anti-stigma initiatives, and community-level capacity building. A coordinated public health response tailored to each SEM level is essential to reverse current trends and safeguard child mental health.
