items.title: Robot Generalization Beyond Volume: The Diversity Path via Zero-Shot Capabilities
items.abstract: General-purpose robots must handle tasks, objects and environments they were never trained on, yet zero-shot generalization remains one of the least solved problems in physical AI. In digital AI, zero-shot capability grew with the volume and, above all, the diversity of training data, much of it sourced from the crowd. Robotics instead relies on paid collection by a few well-funded teams, which yields volume without diversity. We formulate zero-shot generalization in physical AI as coverage of the deployment distribution, and show that more samples from the same collectors shrink the unseen region only slowly, while each new contributor can extend it. Building on this and on zero-shot learning, we propose a shared latent space for robot actions that combines multi-modal alignment, generative augmentation, and noisy-label learning. As a scalable source of diverse data, we propose a community of developers building applications on one standard, approachable robot, Origami. We close with a testable hypothesis and an evaluation protocol relating real-robot zero-shot success to the diversity of contributed data.

items.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
items.abstract: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. This is a short empirical study, with one conversation and one run per cell. Agent memory is a costly patch for a weak model: Mem0 beats full context only with GPT-4o-mini, and its build alone costs more than a whole full-context rollout. Agent memory also has a ceiling, set by the model that writes it: a stronger reader does not recover what a weaker writer left out. With Claude Opus 5.5, Pi tops the cost-accuracy frontier, scoring 99% for less than half the cost of full context; its one miss is a wrong answer key. Part of that lead comes from photo captions that only the agents could read: on the 88 questions whose evidence has no photo, Pi and full context differ by one answer.

items.title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient inference through sparse, event-driven computation, yet remain constrained on continuous, context-dependent tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR). A key bottleneck is the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, whose membrane decay erases information across pauses and phonetic boundaries while it must both extract features and retain long-range context. Inspired by cortical separation of nonlinear filtering and somatic integration, we introduce the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU): a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit performs temporal filtering, while downstream Resonate-and-Fire (RF) neurons generate the binary spike stream driving the next block's event pathway. This makes binary event transmission a native training constraint rather than a separate deployment-time activation quantization step; together with ternary weights, learned projections avoid dense floating-point matrix MACs. Trained end-to-end on LibriSpeech-960, Small, Medium, and Large stGRUs reach 8.09%, 7.04%, and $6.44 \pm 0.17\%$ WER on test-clean without an external language model. To our knowledge, these are the first matrix-MAC-free spiking networks without a learned ANN sequence decoder to achieve single-digit WER on LibriSpeech. The architecture also achieves 10.88% test CER on Aishell-1 (9.28% on dev) when trained from scratch. Internally, trained networks develop a depth-graded hierarchy: shallow layers act as fast acoustic filters, while deep layers form slower semantic integrators whose latent representations segregate into part-of-speech manifolds and word-level spike events. Deep-layer firing rates follow lognormal distributions with a sparsity gradient, mirroring hierarchical processing observed in human cortex in vivo. Our biologically grounded architecture combines competitive ASR with favorable modeled compute and memory cost.

items.title: Vagus nerve stimulation strengthens beta- and gamma-rate auditory steady-state responses in rat cortex
items.abstract: Background: Gamma entrainment using sensory stimulation (GENUS) is under study as a treatment for neurological disease, but cortical engagement is variable. Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) modulates cortical state and sound-evoked beta-gamma activity, suggesting that it may strengthen responses to rhythmic sensory input. Objective: To determine whether VNS strengthens auditory steady-state responses across beta and gamma rates and whether the effect depends on cortical region and sensory drive. Methods: Electrocorticography (ECoG) was recorded from core and belt auditory cortex, insular auditory field (IAF), and anterior insular cortex (AIC) in seven isoflurane-anesthetized rats before and 90 min after initiation of 30-Hz cervical VNS. Responses to 500-ms click trains at 20 and 40 Hz were quantified using inter-trial phase clustering (ITPC), event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP), and debiased weighted phase-lag index (WPLI). Results: VNS increased click-evoked P1-N1 amplitude. During 40-Hz trains, 40-Hz ITPC and ERSP increased only in auditory core. During 20-Hz trains, 20-Hz ITPC increased in core, belt, and IAF, whereas ERSP increased only in core; 40-Hz harmonic responses increased only in core. AIC showed no change. Within auditory cortex, WPLI increased selectively at frequencies present in each click train and not in the alpha band. Conclusions: VNS strengthened beta- and gamma-rate stimulus-locked responses in auditory-driven cortex without globally increasing synchrony. VNS may therefore enhance auditory cortical target engagement during GENUS, although effects on disease pathology or clinical outcomes remain untested.

items.title: Predictions for an unseen third planet in the WISPIT 2 system
items.abstract: We predict the mass and semi-major axis of a currently unseen but hypothesised planet in the WISPIT 2 system based on the location of the ring observed by ALMA at 144.4 au. Using findings from previous hydrodynamical models, we predict that a ~0.2-1 $M_{Jup}$ planet may exist at ~ 100-120 au. We also demonstrate that the ring seen in VLT/SPHERE observations at 96.7 au is consistent with the mass and semi-major axis of WISPIT 2b and confirm that WISPIT 2b cannot be the cause of the ALMA ring. We also discuss how future observations of the system's gas component may help constrain these predictions better, and note that this third planet in WISPIT 2 may be discoverable using upcoming JWST/NIRCam observations or Gaia data release 4 (DR4).

items.title: The Pandora SmallSat: Target Selection and Early Science
items.abstract: The Pandora spacecraft is a smallsat selected in NASA's inaugural class of Pioneers missions. The aim of the Pandora mission is to disentangle stellar activity signals from exoplanet atmospheric transmission spectroscopy measurements. Pandora accomplishes this goal with its combined visible photometry and NIR spectroscopy that observe each target in the prime mission for 10 separate transit observations, each spanning 24 hours at a time. Targets were carefully selected for the Pandora prime mission. Pandora is specifically studying planets around low-mass stellar hosts (K and M dwarf stars) spanning a range of rotation periods and activity levels. The planets range in size from 1.5 - 15 Earth radii and orbital periods ranging from 1.7 - 11.5 days. In addition to the 10 transit visits planned for each of the 20 prime mission targets, Pandora is observing a number of auxiliary targets encompassing a variety of science topics. This includes topics such as stellar activity and young systems, transit timing variations of exoplanets, brown dwarf compositions, exoplanet phase curves, etc. We will discuss the selection of these targets, how they have been scheduled to fill in gaps in prime mission operations, and early science results. If the mission is extended, there is further opportunity for accomplishing additional science. Here we will discuss the possible options for extended mission operations and science.

items.title: Topographically Forced Stationary Waves Can Explain the Near-Surface Zonal Winds Observed by Huygens on Titan
items.abstract: Titan's equatorial superrotation is associated with climatological retrograde (westward) near-surface winds at low latitudes, as consistently simulated by Titan general circulation models. However, the Huygens probe measured prograde (eastward) near-surface winds, contrary to the expected circulation. We investigate whether these observations reflect localized forcing by large-scale topography, using paired three-dimensional dry simulations with and without topography in the Titan Atmospheric Model. We find that topography generates longitude-locked, vertically structured zonal wind anomalies that reproduce key features of the Huygens wind profile in the lowest few kilometers. Helmholtz and spectral analyses show that this structure arises from the superposition of several vertically varying low wavenumber modes. A predominantly rotational, topographically forced stationary zonal wavenumber s=1 response provides a major eastward anomaly throughout the lowest 2 km, whereas a locally divergent s=4 response consistent with a gravity wave, opposes it near the surface. Weaker s=2 and s=3 responses also vary vertically and contribute eastward anomalies near the surface. Combined with the retrograde zonal-mean circulation, these modes produce a Huygens-like profile characterized by prograde flow within the lowest 1 km and shear toward retrograde flow aloft. The paired simulations establish their topographic origin, while coherence with the corresponding terrain-forcing components demonstrates that the responses remain phase locked to the forcing. Similar but weaker stationary responses are simulated near the planned Dragonfly landing site, providing baseline expectations for interpreting its future atmospheric measurements. This study demonstrates how large-scale topography can generate localized departures from Titan's zonal-mean circulation and highlights the importance of stationary waves.

items.title: The morphology of contact binary objects in the Solar System
items.abstract: Contact binaries, appearing as two objects stuck together, are prevalent throughout the Solar System, making up between 30- 50% of asteroids and comets. Despite this, detailed shape models of contact binaries are hard to obtain remotely, requiring rare occultation events or close approaches to Earth (< 0.1 au) to observe with ground-based radar systems. Despite only 16 contact binary models being published, there already exists a wide variety of different arrangements of the two lobes relative to one another. At the same time, simulations of contact binary object formation are increasing in scale, producing 10s to 1000s of contact binary candidates per simulation. It is therefore necessary to begin the process of characterising the different shapes observed, and to further investigate any emerging trends. We analyse the size, period, neck prominence, volume distribution, ratio between the sizes and volumes of the individual lobes, and the alignment between them to summarise the extent of the currently modelled asteroids.

items.title: Condensation and optimal targeting of repeated forcing in heterogeneous networks
items.abstract: Many networks receive repeated external forcing through a subset of entry nodes, for example infections imported from another population, information seeded by a campaign, or invasive species arriving through ports. We study how concentrating such forcing on important entry nodes, with seeding probability $π_i\propto w_i^γ$, changes the size of the resulting cascades in a stochastic SIR model on bipartite networks. The response to one seeding event is linear in the degree of the seeded node, so the relative gain from targeting does not depend on transmissibility. The targeting distribution is a Gibbs measure. For importance tails $p(w)\sim w^{-a}$ and responses growing as $w^η$, the targeted response diverges at $γ_1=a-1-η$ and the forcing condenses on a few nodes at $γ_2=a-1$. Under repeated forcing, the burden-maximizing exponent $γ^*$ is strictly positive, and in large populations depletion of nodes already reached bounds it by the condensation point, $γ^*\leγ_2$. The optimum decays as $γ^*\simeq K/x$ for intense forcing, where $x$ is the expected number of seeding events per entry node, and approaches the condensation point as $γ_2-γ^*\simeq(a-1)/\ln(1/x)$ for sparse forcing. A cut-off of the importance distribution rounds the transitions in populations smaller than a crossover size $n_c$ and removes them in larger ones. Networks calibrated to survey data on sexual partnerships have between $0.08\,n_c$ and $0.8\,n_c$ entry nodes, which places them in the finite-size regime, where the asymptotic results hold only qualitatively.

items.title: OGLE-2013-BLG-1125/MOA-2013-BLG-584: Discovery of a gas giant orbiting an M dwarf
items.abstract: We report the discovery and characterization of a planetary system in the microlensing event OGLE-2013-BLG-1125/MOA-2013-BLG-584. We analyze photometric data from OGLE and MOA surveys, as well as LCO, $μ$FUN, and Mindstep follow-up telescopes to model the microlensing light curve. We also used data from the Keck II telescope collected in 2018 to obtain additional constraints on the lensing system. We found a Saturn-mass planet of mass $M_{\rm p}=105\pm13 \ M_\oplus$ orbiting a low-mass host star $M_{\rm L}=0.139\pm0.011 \ M_\odot$ at $1.00\pm0.08$ kpc from Earth. This discovery adds to the small sample of giant planets orbiting low-mass stars and provides constraints on planet formation theories.

items.title: Radio and high-energy variable emission from a multi-wavelength follow-up of the infant planet-hosting star V1298 Tau
items.abstract: V1298 Tau is a very young and magnetically active K1V star which hosts a benchmark multi-planetary system to study planet formation and evolutionary history at the earliest stages. Between 2025 and 2026, we conducted a campaign to monitor the variability of V1298 Tau in radio (band C), X-ray, and NUV bands, with the support of publicly available contemporary optical light curve, and to investigate multi-band correlations to link the emission with stellar activity. Radio observations were carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) in band C (4.5--6.5 GHz). X-ray and NUV observations were carried out with the Swift satellite over 20 days, ending one month before the begin of the radio campaign. We analysed the temporal variability of peak (integrated) fluxes in the C-band and of X-ray (NUV) luminosities on various timescales, comparing it with the variability observed in the high-cadence optical light curve collected by the ASAS-SN survey. We observed both radio and high-energy time variable emission. JVLA detected emission in 90\% of the visits, switching between high ($\geq$0.1 mJy/beam) and low flux states in matter of days or hours. The fluxes show moderate correlation with the optical light curve, suggesting modulation with the stellar rotation period. Except for one visit, dynamic spectral analysis does not reveal short-term (minutes) variability, nor is there any evidence of circularly polarised emissions. Overall, the radio observations can be explained as gyrosynchrotron and/or cyclotron emission from the corona, and linked to stellar magnetic activity. At high-energy, we detected significant variability in X-ray luminosity (within the range ~1.2--2.5x10$^{+30}$ erg/s), the decay phase of a stellar flare, and evidence of correlation with the optical flux. Our data confirm that V1298\,Tau follows the near-linear Güdel-Benz relation.

items.title: Urban climate regressions require representative monitoring networks
items.abstract: Land use regression models relate intra-urban air temperature to spatial predictors such as building volume, tree canopy cover and topography, and are increasingly used to produce fine-scale temperature maps. However, the accuracy of these estimates can be compromised by unrepresentative monitoring networks. Here we show that reference weather station networks, designed for regional rather than intra-urban monitoring, sample only a narrow portion of a city's spatial heterogeneity, missing both the densely built core and the cool, vegetated periphery that set the two ends of the urban temperature range. As a result, city-wide predictions underestimate temperature differences, in ways that cross-validation against the station measurements does not detect. Using Zurich, Switzerland, as a case study, we compare multiple linear regression, generalized additive models and random forests as up to 117 low-cost temperature sensors are added to the four reference weather stations. When trained on reference stations alone, all three models achieve comparable cross-validated performance. As low-cost sensors broaden the sampled spatial heterogeneity, multiple linear regression scores lower on both metrics, whereas the non-linear models remain at their reference-only level. Although a third of the low-cost sensors already recovers nearly the full predicted temperature range, which predictors are identified, and with which sign, is determined by the station sample rather than the model class. At full coverage, only multiple linear regression leaves significant residual spatial autocorrelation, suggesting a linear form unable to capture non-linear responses of air temperature to urban form. Drawing on landscape ecology research on focal site study design, we provide a transferable framework for diagnosing station network representativeness and improving the reliability of city-wide environmental maps.

items.title: Surface regolith model of near-Earth asteroid (3200) Phaethon
items.abstract: The near-Earth asteroid (3200) Phaethon displays activity as it comes close to the Sun and is presumed to be the progenitor of the Geminids meteor shower. Both CM- and CY-meteorites have been suggested as possible meteorite analogues for Phaethon. Previous spectral and polarization measurements of Phaethon indicate possible surface heterogeneity in the regolith properties. By combining mineral components and their size fractions, we present a regolith model for Phaethon that reproduces the spectral, polarization, and geometric albedo measurements presented in various studies, with the aim of quantitatively characterizing the surface material and structure, as well as the regolith heterogeneity. The best fit model able to produce the measurements is constructed from large olivine particles with troilite inclusions and small scale surface roughness, mixed with smaller, porous troilite aggregates comprised of monomers resembling interplanetary dust. Our model suggests that the different spectral and polarization responses of the regolith are caused by changes in the size and amount of the small dark troilite particles. Based on the amount of troilite in the regolith model, we propose that CM-meteorites are the preferable meteorite analogue for Phaethon.

items.title: An Eco-Friendly Tourism Trip Planner Driven by Z-Number Uncertainty: Evidence from Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul
items.abstract: Deployed tourism trip planners ingest travel times and ratings as exact numbers, although routing services return travel times that vary with the hour of departure and a platform rating may rest on a handful of reviews or on tens of thousands. We present an eco-friendly trip planner that represents both quantities as Z-numbers, which pair a fuzzy restriction on a value with a fuzzy reliability on the evidence behind it, and that constructs them directly from routing-service observations at six departure hours and from platform review counts rather than from linguistic elicitation. A hybrid loss combines score, carbon, travel-time, and reliability terms, and an adaptive large neighborhood search returns single-day itineraries with per-leg reliability annotations through a conversational front end. We compare the planner with a crisp-mean baseline under an identical optimizer in Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul, with fifteen points of interest and thirty seeds per city, and we evaluate the selected itineraries on their trip carbon and their total travel time. Pooled over 150 seed-paired runs, the planner lowers trip carbon from 3.24 to 2.61 kg (19.3%, Wilcoxon p = 0.017; city-clustered bootstrap interval 6.4% to 26.7%) and travel time from 123 to 109 minutes per trip (11.5%, p = 2.8e-10; interval 5.0% to 18.2%). The travel-time reductions survive a Holm correction in Baku, Istanbul, and Abu Dhabi, the carbon reduction is significant in Baku and large but uncertain in the dispersed catalogs of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and neither metric changes in Tashkent. Review counts were measured for Baku and estimated for the other four cities, and the comparison involves a single baseline, so the results establish feasibility and direction rather than a general advantage. Code, routing caches, frozen routing tables, and per-seed results are openly released.

items.title: Hollow homes: Roost selection and role of roost morphometrics in the cavity-roosting Bamboo Bat (Genus Tylonycteris) from the Western Ghats, southern India
items.abstract: Bat species occupy diverse day-roosting habitats, ranging from rock-based to plant-based substrates. Depending on the properties of roosting substrates and the ability of bats to adapt to them, roosts can be stable or ephemeral over time. Bamboo bats (genus Tylonycteris) occupy bamboo cavities and possess adaptations such as a flattened skull, thickened thumb pads and modified soles of the feet, making them specialised for roosting within often ephemeral bamboo internodes. The Western Ghats host a bamboo bat species that has traditionally been considered a subspecies of Southeast Asia's Tylonycteris pachypus. However, its precise taxonomic status is unresolved, and recent analyses suggest this population could be a potential new species. Nevertheless, their roosting ecology and the role of bamboo properties in occupancy remain unexplored. By comparing properties of used and unused cavities by the bamboo bats in the Western Ghats, we investigated how physical roost characteristics are associated with cavity occupancy and how the roost properties and space available differed between solitary and non-solitary roosts. We found that only the area of the cavity mouth was associated with occupancy, and all tested properties, including roost volume, were similar for solitary and non-solitary roosts. Our findings are similar to patterns reported from other Tylonycteris species, but these findings contribute to the comparative understanding of bamboo bat roost selection across the tropics. It also opens up future avenues to investigate the understudied ecological continuum in the Indian tropics that involves bats, bamboo, pest insects, cavity-dwelling taxa and bamboo harvesters in further detail.

items.title: The ontogeny of repeatability: measurement choices shape individuality estimates in a clonal fish
items.abstract: Consistent among-individual differences in behavior across time and contexts ("individuality", "animal personality") are increasingly recognized as playing an important role in both the ecology and evolution of species. Such individuality is not static: individual differences emerge, shift, and crystallize across ontogeny, shaped by developmental plasticity, stochastic processes, and gene-environment interactions. Despite growing awareness of this developmental dimension, the field has relied predominantly on snapshot designs with few repeated measures, raising the question of how much reported repeatability estimates reflect biology versus methodological choices. Here, we leverage high-resolution tracking data from 45 clonal Amazon mollies (Poecilia formosa) recorded at 5 frames per second across the first 28 days of life to systematically examine how temporal aggregation, sampling rate, frame rate, and the number and placement of measurement days affect repeatability estimates and their underlying variance components. We find that repeatability increases with higher temporal aggregation, decreases with lower sampling rates, and varies substantially depending on the developmental stage sampled. These results demonstrate that commonly used measurement practices can substantially distort repeatability estimates, and that conclusions about behavioral consistency may be as much a product of study design as of biology. We close with practical recommendations for researchers studying individuality across development.

items.title: A million orthopteran singers from a year of continuously operating field recorders detected, tracked and organized by song
items.abstract: Continuous acoustic monitoring has become an invaluable tool in ecology and conservation biology, with hundreds of thousands of automated recording units deployed worldwide. While semi-manual annotation is adequate for some uses, fully automated methods to segregate and identify the source of animal sounds are essential to utilize these data to their full extent. Significant progress has been made for birds, whose calls are generally discrete and structured, and where large annotated reference libraries are available. However these methods do not extend neatly to insects, whose choruses dominate nighttime, and often daytime, soundscapes across most of the world. While many approaches have been proposed to fill this gap, an efficient end-to-end system for annotating insect calls that can operate at the scale of available data has not emerged. Here we describe an unsupervised method that uses the intrinsic, highly repetitive structure of the songs of many insects, especially orthopterans, to identify and separate distinct songs in narrow (minute) time windows, connect them across windows for as long as entire nights as their carrier frequencies and syllable repeat rates vary with time, temperature and other factors, and assemble them across days and locations into a catalog of singers and song types across time, space and conditions. We apply this method to thirteen months (November 2024 to November 2025) of recordings from 27 autonomous recording units in different microhabitats at a field site in southwestern Arkansas, 175,896 recorder-hours in all. We detected 10.9 million singers in five-minute windows and linked them, within each night or day, into 911,005 tracks, of which 103,802 lasted two hours or more (71,770 at night, 32,032 by day), a total of 335,882 hours of song. In the plane of carrier frequency against syllable repeat rate these singers fall on discrete lines along which each slides with temperature, and we use this organization to define 45 song types, 37 trilling and 8 chirping, each composed of dozens to thousands of singer-nights. Within singers, syllable rate rises by about 3 percent per degree and carrier frequency by about 1.5 percent in nearly every type, recapitulating and extending classical observations on the temperature dependence of orthopteran song. Published and reference recordings placed on the same plane fall on these lines, and species of Anaxipha recorded by Walker and Funk land on single types at the right temperatures. More generally, this method and the data it produces provide a robust means of studying changes in insect song over time and space, and of understanding the behavioral and physical forces that shape its production.

items.title: Bionomics aspects of major arbovirus vectors, Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus in different ecoclimatic environments of Cameroon
items.abstract: Abstract Background Aedes mosquitoes transmit dengue, Zika and chikungunya viruses, which remain major public health concerns globally and in Africa. Effective prevention and control rely on a sound understanding of vector bio-ecology. In Cameroon, little is known about the bio-ecology and behaviour of Aedes vectors. This study aimed to update the geographical distribution, resting behaviour, host-seeking behaviour and natural infections by arboviruses in Aedes spp. vectors in Cameroon. Methods Sampling was carried out in eight locations across the country. Immature stages of Aedes were collected in seven localities, transported to the insectary, reared to adult, identified, counted, and grouped by species to determine their distribution. Resting behaviour was assessed through inside houses and outdoor aspirations using Prokopack and CDC backpack aspirators. Host-seeking activity was evaluated with BG-Sentinel traps. Natural infections with dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses were determined by real-time quantitative Multiplex PCR and RT-PCR. Chi-squared test was used to compare abundances Results 17,040 adults identified from the immature stages of Aedes spp. collected. We noted 51.05% Ae. albopictus , 48.93% Ae. aegypti , and 0.02% Ae. vittatus . We noted the first identification of Aedes albopictus in Meiganga since its introduction in Cameroon. Aedes aegypti was present in all the localities surveyed, while Ae. albopictus had a distribution limited to the southern part of the country below latitude 6.4°N. Resting and biting behaviours have shown that both species are essentially exophilic and exophagous. Aedes aegypti preferred to rest in used tyres, while Ae. albopictus had a wide range of preferred resting sites (natural vegetation, used tyres, banana plants, mixed resting places). Both species of mosquito bite throughout the day between 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., with essentially unimodal host-seeking activity, with a major peak of activity in the afternoon between 1 p.m. and 6 p.m. Natural infections by dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses showed one positive pool of Ae. aegypti for serotype 3 of dengue virus (DENV-3). Conclusion These results provide an important knowledge base on the bionomics of Aedes mosquitoes in different localities in Cameroon and also establish evidence base essential for designing and implementing targeted arboviral diseases surveillance and vector control strategies.

items.title: Habitat use patterns and diet of Lontra longicaudis (Olfers 1818) in urban streams of southern Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract The Neotropical otter ( Lontra longicaudis ) is a semiaquatic mammal widely distributed throughout Latin America and is considered an important indicator of aquatic ecosystem integrity. This study evaluated the habitat use and feeding ecology of the species in three coastal streams in the municipality of Rio Grande, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, representing different levels of urbanization and landscape modification. Sampling was conducted monthly from August 2024 to July 2025 in three streams along an urbanization gradient. Indirect signs of the species were recorded, the microhabitats used were characterized, and land use and land cover surrounding the watercourses were analyzed using imagery obtained from an unmanned aerial vehicle and processed through supervised classification. Diet was determined through fecal analysis. Habitat-use intensity was estimated based on sign encounter rates, while spatial and seasonal differences were assessed using non-parametric tests and multivariate analysis (PERMANOVA). A total of 175 signs were recorded, most of them in the intermediate-urbanization stream (133), followed by the most urbanized (29), and the least urbanized (13). Encounter rates differed significantly among streams and were highest in the intermediate-urbanization stream, with no significant seasonal variation. Sandbanks accounted for 95.1% of all records, highlighting their importance both as marking sites and for sign detectability. Diet was predominantly composed of fish, followed by crustaceans and birds, with no significant differences in diet composition among streams or seasons. The results indicate that habitat-use intensity was more closely associated with the availability of favorable microhabitats, landscape connectivity, and anthropogenic disturbance than with riparian vegetation extent alone. We conclude that the conservation of Neotropical otter in anthropized coastal landscapes depends on maintaining functional connectivity among aquatic environments and mitigating the impacts of urbanization.

items.title: From Microsatellites to SNPs: Improving hybridization rate estimation in non-invasive monitoring
items.abstract: Abstract The transition from traditional microsatellites to single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) markers is a major objective in modern DNA-based wildlife monitoring. However, empirical comparisons evaluating their relative performance on degraded, non-invasively collected DNA remain scarce. Using the European wildcat ( Felis silvestris ) as a biological model for hybridization with the domestic cat ( Felis catus ), we directly compared results obtained with a traditional 16-microsatellite panel to those obtained with a customized 96-SNP array on the exact same set of 133 wild individuals sampled via non-invasive hair traps. Our results reveal profound methodological divergences in resolution and assignment of hybrid category. While microsatellites indicated an homogeneous wild population, suggesting limited sensitivity for detecting advanced backcrosses, SNPs revealed greater genetic heterogeneity, assigning several individuals to first-generation hybrid or backcross classes. These misclassifications could explain why the overall hybridization rate appeared nearly three times higher with SNPs, a metric also affected by strict assignment thresholds. Furthermore, when considering individuals assigned as pure wildcats, microsatellite data indicated a higher inbreeding coefficient (Fis = 0.28) than SNPs data. These findings offer important insights for molecular ecology. While microsatellites remain cost-effective for assessing broad-scale population genetic structure, this study demonstrates how marker choice can influence hybridization diagnostics and estimates of genetic diversity, underscoring the need for careful calibration when assessing introgression in non-invasive samples.

items.title: Rethinking Ecosystems, Climate Change and Insecurity Through Indigenous Knowledge Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change has aggravated environmental degradation, resource competition and human insecurity across Nigeria, threatening livelihoods and weakening ecosystem resilience. Although contemporary responses have largely relied on scientific and technological interventions, comparatively little attention has been given to Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS), which historically informed environmental conservation and community adaptation. This paper rethinks the relationship between ecosystem governance, climate change and insecurity by examining the significance of indigenous ecological knowledge to contemporary environmental and security challenges. It argues that indigenous practices such as sacred forest conservation, traditional weather forecasting, customary land-use regulation and community-based natural resource management provided sustainable mechanisms for ecological preservation, climate adaptation and conflict mitigation. The study adopts a qualitative historical methodology, drawing on historical literature, ethnographic studies, policy documents and documented case studies from Nigeria. Guided by Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Political Ecology perspectives, it analyses how indigenous environmental practices have shaped ecosystem governance and community resilience across time. The findings reveal that despite the erosion of many indigenous institutions through colonialism, urbanisation and changing socio-economic conditions, indigenous ecological knowledge remains a valuable resource for strengthening climate adaptation, environmental sustainability and local security. The study further contends that the marginalisation of indigenous knowledge in environmental governance has limited community participation and reduced the effectiveness of climate response initiatives. The paper concludes that sustainable responses to climate-induced insecurity require the integration of Indigenous Knowledge Systems with contemporary environmental policies and scientific innovations. It recommends the documentation and preservation of indigenous ecological practices, their incorporation into climate adaptation and environmental governance frameworks, and stronger collaboration among local communities, researchers and policymakers. Such an integrated approach offers a more possible pathway to ecosystem sustainability, climate resilience and community security in Nigeria.

items.title: Producción científica estudiantil y Agenda 2030: análisis lexicométrico asistido por inteligencia artificial en pregrado
items.abstract: Objective: To characterize the scientific production and thematic trends of health sciences students at Lamar University (2024-2025), evaluating their alignment with the 2030 Agenda to determine the social relevance of undergraduate research. Methodology:A mixed-methods, descriptive, and longitudinal study. A corpus of 393 abstracts presented at the CIARTEC conference (200 in 2024 and 193 in 2025) from the degree programs of Medicine, Psychology, Nutrition, Nursing, and Physical Therapy was analyzed. The analysis was conducted using the Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Qualitative Analysis (ACAIA) model, employing NotebookLM for lexicometric systematization and cross-mapping with the official ECLAC document on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The process integrated three phases: semantic co-occurrence analysis, alignment mapping with the 17 SDGs, and identification of regional epistemological silences. Results:A discursive transition was identified in Medicine: from a personal-narrative approach (autoethnography) in 2024 to a clinical-epidemiological and technological one in 2025, where Artificial Intelligence emerged as a key topic. Although a robust link with SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being, 92.1%) exists, critical "epistemological silences" were detected in priority targets for Latin America: neonatal health (2%), reproductive rights (0.5%), and total omission (0%) regarding neglected tropical diseases (Chagas/Leprosy) and international migration. Psychology showed a massive shift toward netnography, while Nursing and Nutrition maintained stable preventive and educational approaches. Conclusions:Student research reflects technical and scientific maturation, but a "technical blindness" toward structural problems and social determinants of global health persists. The high concentration on individual and urban pathologies, contrasted with silence on issues of social justice and regional vulnerability, suggests the need to reorient undergraduate research lines. The ACAIA model proved to be a disruptive tool for managing large volumes of data in medical education, enabling informed decision-making to enhance the social relevance of the curriculum in the face of 2030 Agenda challenges.

items.title: Conceptualizing Cognitive Growth and Release: Integrating Adult Development into Contemplative Science
items.abstract: Adult developmental theory has the potential to contribute across many fields. This paper, authored by two developmentalists and a neuroscientist studying meditators, argues that developmental models are increasingly needed as contemplative science enters a “third wave” concerned with advanced meditation including highly skilled practitioners, deep meditative states, and enduring transformations. This leading edge also overlaps with wisdom studies, spiritual and transpersonal inquiry, and trauma theory, exposing important conceptual tensions. We argue that these arise from a common assumption that cognitive complexity and spiritual clarity or psychological wholeness necessarily develop together along a single vertical axis of developmental “altitude.” To clarify and resolve these tensions, we propose a framework distinguishing two quasi-independent developmental movements: ascending structural growth, the cumulative and hierarchical construction of cognitive capacities, and descending structural release, the loosening, deconstruction, or seeing-through of cognitive structures. Release exposes constrained or inaccessible cognitive resources, enabling deconditioning, reintegration, healing, and/or insight. We apply this framework to problems including the fallibility of spiritual adepts; relationships among states, stages, and stable “vantage points”; requisite complexity and adverse effects of intensive contemplative practice; disputes over maps of contemplative attainment; and the legitimization of traditional and Indigenous knowledge. The framework offers a heuristic bridge among contemplative science, developmental psychology, and adjacent fields, while generating theoretically and empirically testable hypotheses about increasingly deep possibilities for human development.

items.title: Tutorbot pilot study: learning support, feedback and assessment in a crisis intervention module
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence has recently emerged as a major contender in higher education practice. There are limited studies on the value in a crisis intervention module psychology training in multilingual South Africa. This pilot study investigated how postgraduate students used the tutorbot at a single South African higher education institution. An exploratory learning analytics approach, supported by qualitative content analysis, was used to examine 1,546 anonymised chat messages with three error rows excluded. The cleaned data set consisted of 571 student messages and 975 tutorbot responses in 405 chat-threads from 46 unique student interactions. The analysis focused mainly on how students used the tutorbot, what pedagogical functions the tutorbot performed, and what tensions arose in the learning interaction. The findings indicated that the tutorbot was mainly used for module content-related learning, concept clarification, assessment preparation, and multilingual support. The tutorbot functioned as a formative scaffolding by explaining concepts, asking Socratic questions, giving feedback, and encouraging students to revise their thinking. However, the intentional Socratic style of the tutorbot sometimes frustrated students who required a direct explanation rather than further questioning. Multilingual exchanges suggested potential for expanding epistemological access in South African psychology education. The article argues that tutorbots can support postgraduate psychology teaching when they are used as bounded formative tools within a supervised academic environment. The findings support the use of AI for structured rehearsal, feedback and conceptual consolidation, but not as a replacement for lecturers, clinical supervision, or professional judgement.

items.title: Towards Early Warning Systems for Shigellosis in Africa: Multi-Horizon Forecasting of Incidence in Rural Western Kenya Using Statistical State-Space and Machine Learning Models
items.abstract: Introduction: Despite the significant burden of Shigellosis, routine surveillance systems in resource-limited settings lack predictive capabilities to guide proactive public health responses. Consequently, we developed and evaluated the accuracy, uncertainty and computational cost of multi-horizon forecasting models for Shigella incidence among children <5 years in rural western Kenya using 16-year longitudinal incidence time-series. Methods We estimated monthly Shigella incidence using data from three pediatric enteric studies (2008–2024), supplemented with Kenya Health Information System during inter-study gaps. Incidence estimates incorporated sampling, healthcare-seeking, stool-testing, and pathogen-specific weights, with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Predictors included Google Trends health-related indicators, climate, temporal trends, and seasonality. Forecasts at 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons were evaluated using rolling-origin validation. Following horizon-specific predictor selection using Boruta, 14 state-space, machine-learning, and hybrid models were compared using point-forecast and probabilistic metrics, bootstrap confidence intervals, and Model Confidence Sets. Adaptive conformal prediction recalibrated prediction intervals, while Shapley Additive exPlanations assessed predictor contributions. Results Mean monthly Shigella incidence was 2.51 per 100 child-years (standard deviation=1.85). Shigella dynamics in Kenya can be forecast beyond seasonal persistence alone for up to six months reducing absolute errors by ~ 33%. However, optimal model architectures and predictor sets shift systematically across forecasting horizons. Temporal trend and recent incidence were the dominant predictors, while predictor importance shifted with forecast horizon toward syndromic, pharmaceutical, seasonal, and lagged environmental signals. Extreme Gradient Boosting performed best at 1 month (Root mean squared error [RMSE]=1.86), remained competitive at 3 months (RMSE=1.89), whereas exponential smoothing (ETS) performed best at 6 months (RMSE=2.05). Forecast accuracy declined with increasing horizon. ETS and TBATS provided the best-calibrated prediction intervals, whereas machine-learning models generally under-covered. Model Confidence Sets demonstrated horizon-dependent model distinguishability. Conclusion Horizon-specific model selection balancing predictive accuracy, uncertainty calibration, and computational feasibility could strengthen operational early warning systems for shigellosis.

items.title: Detection and Characterization of Human Bocavirus in Stool Samples from an Acute Gastroenteritis Outbreak in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, in 2024.
items.abstract: Introduction: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a global public health problem and a major cause of mortality in low- and lower-middle-income countries. Human bocavirus (HBoV) is among the viral agents associated with this condition. Therefore, investigating the presence of HBoV in cases of AGE in Salvador, Bahia, as well as its prevalence and circulating strains, is important. Objective: To investigate the occurrence of HBoV infection during an AGE outbreak in Salvador. Methods: A total of 178 samples were analyzed for HBoV using nested polymerase chain reaction (nested PCR), and the amplification products were visualized by agarose gel electrophoresis. HBoV was detected in 5.7% of the samples analyzed. Conclusion: This study contributes to the understanding of HBoV epidemiology as a secondary agent associated with acute gastroenteritis during a norovirus outbreak in Salvador. Continued investigation and identification of the etiological agents involved in outbreaks are essential for evaluating the causes of AGE. These findings also highlight the need for broader diagnostic approaches and the importance of phylogenetic analysis for monitoring and controlling viral infections.

items.title: Design and Technical Evaluation of a Standards-Based System That Delivers Enclave-Derived Case-Finding Models to Patients and Clinicians
items.abstract: Background: Research data enclaves such as the All of Us Research Program do not allow participant-level data, or models fitted to them, to leave, which makes it hard to deliver case-finding models, which flag patients with possibly uncoded conditions for clinician review, to patients and clinicians. Objectives. We describe and technically evaluate a system that fits models outside an enclave from released summary counts and delivers them through standard health information technology interfaces. Methods. We exported dissemination-compliant summary counts from the All of Us Researcher Workbench and, outside the enclave, fitted versioned models for Long COVID, chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, endometriosis, Lyme disease, lupus, migraine, depression, and anxiety. A model contract (a model file and a written specification), a Python reference implementation, and synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) test patients define the expected outputs. One JavaScript scorer runs in a patient demonstration, a SMART on FHIR clinician application, and a CDS Hooks service. An atlas displays aggregate results. We evaluated the system on synthetic records with automated tests, cross-implementation output comparison, launches through the public SMART sandbox, and a counterexample review of the scoring and display rules. Results. The deployed Long COVID model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.67 in a random validation split. The eight self-report models reached 0.61 to 0.82 in identifying self-reporters without a code. The JavaScript scorer reproduced all 162 reference outputs exactly, and all 437 automated tests passed. A counterexample review found 5 classes of failure, including scoring ineligible patients and treating unavailable data as absent, all fixed and added as tests. Conclusions. Models fitted from released summary counts can be delivered through FHIR, SMART on FHIR, and CDS Hooks with reproducible scoring on synthetic records. Real-record interoperability, usability, and prospective clinical performance remain to be evaluated.

items.title: Echoes of neglect: modeling the consequences of delayed HIV/AIDS treatment in Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) established the country as a global reference in HIV/AIDS control, largely due to the timely implementation of universal access to combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) in 1996. However, recent policy setbacks—including service disruptions, testing shortages, and governance failures during the COVID-19 pandemic—highlight how institutional delays and neglect can yield severe health outcomes . Methods: In this retrospective ecological time-series study, we used counterfactual modeling to estimate the potential long-term consequences of delaying key public health interventions, simulating alternative cART implementation scenarios. Annual HIV/AIDS mortality data from 1980 to 2023 were obtained from Brazil's Mortality Information System (SIM/DATASUS) , and we employed the Prophet time-series framework to simulate delays of one year (1997) or two years (1998). Results : The historical introduction of cART in 1996 coincided with a marked decline in HIV/AIDS mortality. Counterfactual simulations indicated that a one-year delay could have resulted in 73,493 additional deaths by 2023, whereas a two-year delay could have resulted in 106,035 additional deaths. The effects were non-linear and extended well beyond the delay period, with mortality remaining elevated for decades. Conclusions : These findings demonstrate that delays and disruptions in HIV care generate persistent excess mortality. Counterfactual modeling underscores the critical need to safeguard institutional capacity, ensure continuity in testing and prevention, and prevent political or administrative setbacks in public health programmes.

items.title: Integrating Interpolated Weather Data into National Clinical Data Warehouse to Support Health Services
items.abstract: Abstract Bangladesh is increasingly vulnerable to climate-sensitive infectious diseases, including dengue, cholera, malaria, and other diarrheal diseases, influenced by dynamic transmission patterns driven by meteorological variables such as temperature, humidity, and precipitation. Spatially unevenly distributed ground observation weather stations across the country create a fundamental barrier to using meteorological data for public health preparedness. Moreover, the absence of a systematic framework incorporating clinical and weather data, as well as a disease-specific data mart, points to a significant challenge in supporting preventive public health decision-making. In response, this study integrates interpolated weather data with the National Clinical Data Warehouse (NCDW) to facilitate preparedness for epidemic and pandemic outbreaks. We applied machine learning techniques to interpolate weather data across all 516 upazilla (sub-district)s in Bangladesh from 42 weather stations and found that Random Forest outperformed other models for interpolating min temperature (R²=0.9658, MSE=0.9931), max temperature (R²=0.9173, MSE=1.2525), rainfall (R²=0.3929, MSE=184.3544), and humidity (R²=0.8109, MSE=13.7712). A snowflake-schema-based architecture, introduced as Climate-NCDW, integrated the interpolated data to map clinical data in real time and established a nationwide disease-specific data mart to support advanced analytical infrastructure. Through interpolation, 82,727 records of weather data provide a comprehensive view of the weather patterns during the 2019-2024 time period. We found rainfall has the highest association with dengue disease involvement (Corr=0.87) during the nationwide post-monsoon period (August-October) in 2019 and 2021. Overall, our findings demonstrate that the Climate-NCDW framework can provide a robust, multidimensional big data infrastructure for real-time assessments of disease risk to support public health policy and decision-making and optimize resource allocation, marking a significant step toward integrating environmental and health informatics for proactive disease control.

items.title: Integrated multi-pathogen serosurveillance in children from East New Britain, Papua New Guinea using multiplex bead assays
items.abstract: Abstract Children in Papua New Guinea experience a high burden of infectious diseases, including neglected tropical diseases, arboviral infections, enteric pathogens, and soil-transmitted helminths. Multi-pathogen serological surveillance provides a powerful approach for simultaneously characterising population-level exposure and susceptibility to multiple pathogens, complementing other forms of surveillance and to guide public health decision-making. We collected blood samples from 379 children aged 10 to 24 months (median 16 months) living in East New Britian Papua New Guinea, to assess antibodies to 11 priority pathogens. Seropositivity was highest for Cryptosporidium (52.8%), followed by dengue (30.9%), chikungunya (25.3%), Giardia (13.5%) and malaria parasites (Plasmodium vivax 11.1%; Plasmodium falciparum 5.0%). Males were significantly more likely to be positive for trachoma (10.5% vs 2.2%, p = 0.001). Co-exposure to multiple pathogen groups was common, with approximately 45% of children seropositive for antibodies from two or more different pathogens. While prevalence varied markedly across pathogen groups, these results confirm substantial early-life exposure to multiple endemic pathogens in East New Britain, Papua New Guinea. Simultaneous assessment of multiple pathogens from a single sample demonstrates the value of multiplex serological surveillance and can inform targeted public health interventions.

items.title: Development and validation of an RPA-CRISPR-Cas12b assay for rapid visual detection of Solanum rostratum
items.abstract: Abstract Solanum rostratum is a noxious invasive weed posing risks to crop production and public health. Its seeds are easily concealed in bulk grain commodities, serving as the primary pathway for long-distance dispersal. However, existing PCR-based detection methods require laboratory equipment and lengthy turnaround, and their suitability for rapid on-site seed quarantine remains limited. In this study, we developed and laboratory-validated an RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay for detection of S. rostratum using leaf DNA and plasmid templates. A reference sequence dataset was constructed from 148 newly generated DNA barcode sequences and publicly available sequences from NCBI and BOLD, covering five marker regions (rbcL, matk, ITS, ITS2, and trnH-psbA). Using the best-performing sgRNA (SR-sgRNA-1) and RPA primer pair (SR-RPA-F1/R1), selected according to fluorescence increase rates, a two-step fluorescence assay was developed. A visual FAM (6-carboxyfluorescein) readout format was also established. Both detection formats were systematically evaluated using plasmid templates and 30 actual samples (14 S. rostratum accessions collected across eight Chinese provinces/autonomous regions and 16 non-target Solanum species). Both formats detected plasmid DNA down to 10 copies/test. In the tested panel, the assay identified 14/14 S. rostratum accessions and 16/16 non-target Solanum accessions, with complete concordance between the two formats. This RPA-CRISPR/Cas12b assay provides a rapid and highly specific detection workflow, effectively addressing the technical bottleneck in seed quarantine and offering a practical solution for source interception of S. rostratum .

items.title: Frequency and factors associated with the offering of gifts or favors in access to health care in Guinea: a cross-sectional study based on Afrobarometer 2022 data
items.abstract: Abstract Background Despite being legally prohibited, offering gifts or favors to access medical care remains common in Guinea. We sought to measure the frequency of this practice and identify the factors associated with it among users of public health facilities. Methods We conducted an analytical cross-sectional study using data from the ninth round of the Afrobarometer survey carried out in Guinea in 2022. The dependent variable was offering a gift or favor to a health worker to obtain needed care. Results Of the 869 respondents, 331 (38.1%) reported having offered a gift or favor at least once to obtain care, and these individuals were on average younger (41.1 ± 15.2 years versus 43.6 ± 16.1 years ; p = 0.027). items.title: Effectiveness of an experiential on-site education intervention on food safety knowledge, attitude and practices among street food vendors in Nairobi’s informal settlements

However, unsafe food handling and poor sanitation pose significant health risks, as street food vendors (SFVs) often lack adequate training and infrastructure. Despite their role in local food systems and livelihoods, support for improving food safety is limited. The study aimed to assess the effectiveness of a context-specific education and support supervision intervention on food safety knowledge, attitudes, and practices with regard to the causes of food-borne illnesses and their symptoms, food contaminants and hygiene practices in food handling and storage, food preparation, and preservation among SFVs in Nairobi’s informal settlements. items.title: From student voice to visible influence: A mixed-methods needs analysis of medical student partnership engagement across Türkiye
items.abstract: Abstract Background Student engagement through partnership positions students as collaborators in educational design, research, governance, quality assurance, and community engagement. Although increasingly promoted in health professions education, less is known about how students experience partnership across national contexts or why some participation mechanisms produce influence while others remain symbolic. This study examined how medical students in Türkiye perceived and experienced engagement through partnership. Methods We conducted a nationwide, multiphase mixed-methods needs analysis. An online survey included five-point items, a five-level engagement continuum, and open-ended questions on facilitating and hindering factors. Medical education departments or units across Türkiye’s seven geographical regions were asked to distribute the survey. Survey findings informed two student-only online focus groups. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively in R. Open-ended responses and focus-group transcripts were analysed using an iterative, team-based codebook thematic approach and integrated during theme development and interpretation. Results A total of 144 students completed the survey; 130 (90.3%) attended public universities, and 80 (55.6%) reported no role in student representation or organisations. Partnership was rated at least moderately important by 82.6%, and 90.9% perceived at least a moderate contribution to educational quality; 59.0% rated institutional support at the scale midpoint or above. Across four domains, 89.5%–92.3% rated partnership at least moderately important, whereas 59.7%–70.1% reported engagement at involvement or higher. The integrated qualitative dataset comprised 639 meaning units and generated five higher-order themes: from student voice to visible influence; from goodwill to institutionalised partnership; building safe, respectful, and fair relationships; protected capacity for sustainable partnership; and enacting partnership through shared practice. Representation, feedback, and formal structures could facilitate or hinder partnership depending on their enactment. Conclusions Students valued partnership but perceived an implementation gap between its educational importance and institutional practice. Meaningful partnership requires student voice to have visible influence through institutionalised processes, psychologically safe and equitable relationships, adequate capacity, and shared practice. Medical schools should prioritise feedback accountability, inclusive representation, role clarity, partnership literacy, psychological safety, and protected capacity rather than simply increasing opportunities to speak.

items.title: Comparative Burden and Attributable Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in China versus G20 Nations from 1990 to 2040: A Joinpoint Regression and Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort Modeling Study
items.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a principal contributor to cancer-related deaths globally, presenting significant public health and economic challenges. This investigation presents a detailed examination of the spatial and temporal progression, associated risk factors, and projected trajectories of HCC burden in China and G20 nations spanning the period from 1990 to 2040. Leveraging data from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study, we applied descriptive statistical methods, Joinpoint regression analysis, Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) modeling, ARIMA forecasting techniques, and risk factor decomposition. Findings revealed that while the absolute count of HCC cases rose, largely attributable to demographic aging, the age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) exhibited a downward trend from 1990 to 2023. This reduction was more pronounced in China compared to the G20 average, despite China’s rates continuing to exceed the group mean. Notable inequalities were identified, with higher burdens observed among males, older populations, and G20 countries with lower socioeconomic status. A transition in the etiological profile was evident: the proportion of cases attributable to hepatitis B virus (HBV) declined, whereas the fraction linked to metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) rose significantly. Projections for 2040, generated through integrated BAPC-ARIMA models, anticipate a persistent decrease in age-standardized rates. Scenario modeling indicated that enhanced control of primary risk factors—including HBV, HCV, alcohol use, tobacco consumption, and MAFLD—could markedly hasten this decline. In summary, despite advancements, the HCC burden remains substantial, with a growing contribution from metabolic risks. These results highlight the necessity for precise, resource-adapted preventive measures, with particular emphasis on addressing MAFLD and existing inequalities, to effectively reduce the future impact of HCC.

items.title: High seroprevalence of Brucella spp. antibodies in small-ruminant milk and poor brucellosis-related awareness among herders in Maiduguri, northeastern Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Brucellosis is an important bacterial zoonosis affecting livestock production and public health, particularly in resource-limited settings where contact between humans and infected animals and consumption of unpasteurized animal products are common. In Nigeria, information on Brucella exposure among small ruminants and the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAPs) of their handler’s remains limited. This study assessed the seroprevalence of anti- Brucella antibodies in milk from sheep and goats and evaluated brucellosis-related KAPs among small-ruminant herders in Maiduguri, northeastern Nigeria. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among small-ruminant flocks and herders in Maiduguri. A total of 184 fresh, unpasteurized milk samples, comprising 92 from sheep and 92 from goats, were collected from 14 purposively selected flocks using simple random sampling within flocks. Samples were screened for anti- Brucella antibodies using a commercial indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (iELISA). Because the iELISA does not differentiate among Brucella species, species-specific molecular confirmation was undertaken on 14 randomly selected ELISA-positive samples using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), owing to financial constraints. A separate KAP survey was conducted among 360 randomly selected small-ruminant herders drawn from a broader operational sampling frame comprising herders associated with the 60 identified flocks and additional larger flocks. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary and multivariable logistic regression. Results: Anti- Brucella antibodies were detected in 32.1% (95% CI: 25.4–39.3) of the 184 milk samples, with significantly higher seroprevalence among goats (54.4%; 95% CI: 43.6–64.8) than sheep (10.0%; 95% CI: 4.6–17.8). At the flock level, 71.4% (95% CI: 41.9–91.6) of the 14 sampled flocks had at least one ELISA-positive animal. Seropositivity was significantly associated with species, source of animals, parity, history of abortion, body condition score, and reported flock-level antibiotic use. However, these associations should be interpreted cautiously because the study was cross-sectional, antibiotic use was assessed at flock level based on herder recall, and the animal-level regression analysis did not explicitly account for clustering within flocks. Of the 14 ELISA-positive samples tested by PCR, four (28.6%) were positive for B. melitensis DNA, all from sheep, while 10 were PCR-negative. Thus, molecular evidence of B. melitensis was restricted to the tested subset and was not used to estimate population-level B. melitensis prevalence. The KAP assessment revealed generally poor levels, with only 20.8%, 17.2%, and 16.9% of herders demonstrating good knowledge, positive attitudes, and appropriate practices, respectively. Breeding system, years of experience, economic status, educational level, and farming system were independently associated with KAP outcomes. Conclusions: The high seroprevalence of anti- Brucella antibodies indicates substantial Brucella exposure among small ruminants in the study area, while detection of B. melitensis DNA in a limited subset provides species-specific molecular evidence of B. melitensis among some tested animals. The combination of substantial serological evidence and poor brucellosis-related KAPs highlights an important One Health concern, particularly in relation to raw milk consumption and unsafe handling of potentially infectious materials. Strengthening veterinary extension and surveillance services, improving herder awareness, promoting milk pasteurization and safer handling of abortion materials, and strengthening collaboration between veterinary and public health services are warranted to reduce the potential risk of brucellosis transmission in the study area.

items.title: Implication of the Perception of Newborn Screening, Premarital Screening, and Genetic Counseling on Sickle Cell Anemia a Study of Patients in Eastern Nigeria
items.abstract: Sickle Cell Disease remains a major public health challenge across Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Nigeria and its eastern regions, where cultural practices and healthcare system constraints significantly influence disease prevention strategies. This study investigates how patients’ perceptions of newborn screening, premarital genotype testing, and genetic counseling affect the prevention and management of sickle cell anemia. Employing a cross-sectional research design, data were collected from patients and caregivers in selected healthcare facilities across Eastern Nigeria. The findings reveal that although awareness of premarital screening is relatively high, misconceptions, social stigma, financial constraints, and cultural beliefs continue to hinder the acceptance and utilization of screening and counseling services. Positive perceptions were associated with increased screening uptake, earlier diagnosis, and improved disease management, whereas negative perceptions contributed to delayed diagnosis, poor treatment adherence, and the sustained burden of the disease. The results highlight the need for culturally appropriate health education, active community participation, and enhanced newborn and premarital screening programs supported by comprehensive genetic counseling to strengthen prevention efforts. Incorporating community perceptions and beliefs into public health strategies has the potential to substantially decrease the incidence of sickle cell anemia and lessen its associated health complications in Nigeria.

items.title: Testing capacity-constrained learning
items.abstract: Abstract We introduce a general test of capacity-constrained learning models. Learning has capacity constraints when the set of possible ways to learn is exogenously fixed, as in the widely used fixed-capacity versions of rational inattention (Sims, 2003) and efficient coding (Woodford, 2012). With such models, changes in incentives do not alter the extent of attention, only how individuals decide to allocate their scarce attention. We show that choice data are consistent with capacity-constrained learning if and only if they satisfy a No Improving (Action or Attention) Switches (NIS) condition. Based on existing experiments in which the incentives for being correct are varied, we find strong evidence that participants fail NIS for a wide range of standard perceptual tasks: identifying the proportion of ball colors, recognizing shapes, and counting the number of balls. We further show that violations of NIS occur systematically in response to higher incentives, suggesting that incentives often expand attention beyond what capacity-constrained models allow. However, we find that this is not true for all existing perceptual tasks in the literature, which offers insights into settings where we do or do not expect incentives to impact the extent of attention.

items.title: Strong mnemonic prediction errors increase cognitive control, attention, and arousal
items.abstract: Ongoing experience is continuously processed in the context of past events. Divergence between current experience and memory-based predictions (i.e., a mnemonic prediction error; MPE) is theorized to be a signal for the hippocampus that encoding, as opposed to retrieval, should be prioritized. We asked how MPEs place demands on cognitive and neural resources beyond the hippocampus, and whether these demands differ as a function of prediction strength. We investigated these questions across two experiments, wherein we recorded scalp electroencephalography and/or pupillometry as 101 young human adults performed an associative memory task. Strong MPEs, more so than weak MPEs, increased physiological indices of cognitive control (frontal theta), attention (posterior alpha and pupil size), and arousal (pupil size). Trial-level pupil-linked MPE responses scaled with the amount of attention (posterior alpha) allocated during prediction generation. Finally, greater cognitive control (frontal theta) during strong MPEs promoted better learning of prediction violating (i.e., unexpected) stimuli. Collectively, these findings reveal how the mind and brain respond adaptively to violations of strong mnemonic predictions.

items.title: Language usage shapes neural mechanisms of code-switching
items.abstract: Linguistic environments play an important role in shaping the mechanisms of language processing. The current study examined how neural responses to bilingual code-switching vary as a function of ongoing language usage, and which control processes may underlie these differences. Forty highly proficient English-French bilinguals listened to continuous spoken narratives containing inter-sentential switches. Participants were matched for proficiency and language background but differed in their current L2 usage (Active vs. Inactive). Narratives alternated either between their first and second languages, or between language and an acoustically matched non-linguistic signal, providing a means to probe language disengagement and re-engagement. While comprehension and cortical speech tracking were comparable across groups, oscillatory analyses revealed a usage-dependent modulation of alpha-band activity. Active bilinguals showed comparable alpha responses to switch and non-switch sentences, whereas Inactive bilinguals showed reduced alpha power following language switches, emerging from 650 ms over parieto-occipital regions. The direction, timing, and location of this effect are consistent with later attention control processes rather than early perceptual responses to the switch. Further analyses suggested that group differences were more closely associated with language disengagement than re-engagement. Together, these findings demonstrate an association between current L2 usage and alpha-band responses during language switching, suggesting that ongoing language experience may be modulating the neural mechanisms of language control.

items.title: Social chatbots and character: Mind-modelling, mimetics, and postdigital misperception
items.abstract: This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

items.title: The Depth of Problem Definition: Evaluating Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers’ Initial PCK through Post-Case Study Diagnosis
items.abstract: This qualitative embedded single-case study examined how pre-service mathematics teachers in Eastern Indonesia define pedagogical problems after school-based case studies and how the depth of those definitions differs across initial pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) categories. Six purposively selected sixth-semester students, two each in low, moderate, and high initial-PCK groups, were selected from 44 questionnaire respondents. Data comprised post-case-study reports, an initial-PCK questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed through a reflexive thematic procedure involving data condensation, coding, theme development, and cross-category comparison, with triangulation, peer debriefing, member checking, and an audit trail. All participants identified conceptual and procedural difficulties, prerequisite gaps, and modeling obstacles. However, low-PCK participants predominantly described surface symptoms; moderate-PCK participants mapped error patterns and prerequisite weaknesses using evidence; and high-PCK participants constructed precise, evidence-based, multidimensional diagnoses spanning cognitive, affective, and metacognitive dimensions. Topic complexity was treated as an analytic condition rather than a basis for causal inference by comparing the structure and evidential quality of definitions within each case and then across PCK categories. The findings position problem definition as an observable expression of pedagogical reasoning and support explicit, scaffolded diagnostic-competence learning in mathematics teacher education, especially in resource-constrained and diverse educational settings. Keywords: pre-service mathematics teachers, problem definition, initial pedagogical content knowledge, eastern indonesia.

items.title: Feminist Metaphors of Force and Obstacle: Constructing Empowerment and Inhibition in American and Chinese Magazines
items.abstract: Cross-cultural analyses of feminist issues in magazines remain scarce. Metaphorical use influences societal attitudes toward gender equality and resistance. This study investigates the feminist metaphors of force and obstacle in American magazines Ms. and Bust (1,617 articles; 2.13 million words) and Chinese magazines Women of China and Marriage and Family (5,182 articles; 3.63 million words), using corpus tools, the Metaphor Identification Procedure, and an inter-coder reliability check, revealing how cultural and ideological contexts construct narratives of empowerment and inhibition. Results show that, after normalization per 100,000 words, force metaphors are nearly three times more frequent in the Chinese corpus (194.8 per 100,000 words) than in the American corpus (69.8 per 100,000 words), whereas obstacle metaphors show the reverse pattern (35.0 versus 3.6 per 100,000 words). American discourse pairs force with repeated, adversarial talk of barriers to be broken, removed, or dismantled, reflecting liberal individualism and often critiquing structural inequities. Chinese discourse is saturated with collective force metaphors of solidarity and institutional coordination, yet rarely frames women's progress as obstructed, instead emphasizing coordinated agency and top-down synergy. These distinctions illustrate how sociopolitical ideologies shape the conceptualization of gender equality, positioning feminism as both a transformative force and a movement constrained by cultural narratives.
