items.title: Putative Transcriptomic Endotypes Reveal Neuronal, Immune, and Metabolic Heterogeneity in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy with Hippocampal Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS) is a biologically heterogeneous disorder in which neuronal loss, gliosis, neuroinflammation, and metabolic stress may coexist but are unlikely to be uniformly represented across all patients. To investigate this heterogeneity at the molecular level, we analysed publicly available hippocampal transcriptomic data from individuals with TLE-HS. Our analyses identified three transcriptomically defined putative endotypes within this shared neuropathological diagnosis. These states were associated with distinct molecular programs, including a neuronal/synaptic signalling-dominant profile, an immune- and glia-associated inflammatory state marked by cytokine and complement pathway activity, and a metabolically shifted state characterised by oxidative phosphorylation, reactive oxygen species signalling, and stress-response pathways. Cell-type-associated transcriptional signatures analysis and co-expression network organisation further characterised these transcriptomic endotypes, indicating that glial activation, inflammatory signalling, and mitochondrial/metabolic remodelling are differentially weighted across TLE-HS rather than uniformly present. These findings suggest that TLE-HS comprises partially distinct molecular contexts that may converge on a common histopathological endpoint. By characterising transcriptomically defined states within TLE-HS, this study highlights molecular heterogeneity within a shared histopathological diagnosis.

items.title: Parent-child discrepancies in health-related quality of life in pediatric celiac disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To evaluate differences in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) between child self-reports and parent-proxy assessments in children and adolescents with celiac disease (CeD) using the CeD Dutch Questionnaire (CDDUX), and to describe disease-specific HRQoL patterns across the included populations. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies assessing HRQoL in pediatric CeD using the CDDUX questionnaire were identified through PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library databases. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models and expressed as ratios of means (RoM). Twenty-one studies from 14 countries, including 2,453 children with CeD and 2,257 parents, were included. Children consistently reported better HRQoL than perceived by their parents, with self-reported scores 7% higher overall. Differences were observed across all domains, particularly for "Diet". Overall, CDDUX scores indicated neutral HRQoL. Across studies, domain scores followed a consistent hierarchical pattern, with "Having CD" showing the lowest scores and "Communication" the highest. Marked geographic differences emerged, with the highest HRQoL scores reported in South America and the lowest in the Middle East and North Africa. Children with CeD reported higher HRQoL than their parents perceived, although the clinical importance of the pooled difference remains uncertain. The emotional burden of living with CeD represents the most affected dimension of HRQoL, while communication-related aspects are relatively preserved. Geographic variation emerged, however should be interpreted cautiously because comparability across language versions and cultural settings was not established. • Generic health-related quality of life questionnaires may underestimate the psychosocial burden associated with celiac disease; parent and child perceptions of disease burden frequently differ. • Parents consistently report lower health-related quality of life scores than children themselves, particularly in the "Diet" domain, while the"Having celiac disease" domain represents the greatest psychosocial burden worldwide.

items.title: Bioactivity profiling of linear venom peptides from Italian small wood-scorpion (Euscorpius italicus).
items.abstract: Background Rising host-expansion and the global spread of pest insects, confront agricultural sectors with substantial concerns. A promising source of potential lead compounds to target these growing challenges are animal venoms which abound with a huge diversity of bioactive peptides suited for both pest control and drug discovery. Arachnids in particular contribute substantially to the extreme diversity of highly adapted venom compounds, and for some of these, translational potential in pest control has already been demonstrated. Members of the Euscorpiidae family of scorpions are among the most successful groups of scorpions in Europe. Although they use their venom for hunting, none of their toxins has thus far been functionally evaluated as their low toxicity to humans has kept them out of the spotlight of venom research. We hypothesize that their venom peptides exert insecticidal activity which might be harnessed for pest control applications. Results Based on our hypothesis, we conducted bioactivity profiling of linear venom peptides derived from Euscorpius italicus, one of the most common euscorpiid species. In silico analyses revealed them as neutral to cationaic alpha helical peptides with high hydrophobicity. Functionally, our established profiling pipeline that combines in vivo and in vitro bioassays, reveals that one of the tested linear venom peptides, Ei1, causes mortality in Drosophila suzukii postinjection, as well as signs of neuroparalysis. Furthermore, Ei1 exhibits inhibitory effects on Staphylococcus aureus, while also affecting MDCK II cells and equine erythrocytes, implying functions in host defense. Conclusion This study reveals insights on properties of Euscorpiidae venom, their ecological values for predation and defensive function against microbial colonization of the venom glands - revealing further knowledge to the growing biodiscovery of animal venoms and potential agricultural functions as a biological insecticide. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Metagenomic detection and characterization of RNA viruses associated with Rhipicephalus linnaei (Audouin, 1826) ticks from the Amazon, Pará, Brazil.
items.abstract: In recent years, tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have gained significant prominence in public and veterinary health due to reports of fatal cases associated with vertebrates and the identification of a wide diversity of viruses in ixodid ticks through molecular techniques, particularly high-throughput sequencing. This study aims to investigate RNA viruses in Rhipicephalus linnaei ticks from two distinct regions of the state of Pará, in the Amazon, using a metagenomic approach. Specimens of Rhipicephalus linnaei were confirmed based on the COXI gene of their mitochondrial genome. We report the first record of Brown dog tick mivirus 1 (Mivirus rhipicephali; Family Chuviridae) and Brown dog tick phlebovirus 2 (Uukuvirus tobagoense; Family Phenuiviridae) in Brazil, as well as partial fragments of Uukuvirus tobagoense, Castanhal tick orthomyxovirus (Family Orthomyxoviridae), Guangdong tick quaranjavirus (Family Orthomyxoviridae), Alpharicinrhavirus taishun (Family Rhabdoviridae) and Zhangye Rhabd tick virus 1 (Family Rhabdoviridae). This research identified viruses with potential relevance to public and animal health and expands knowledge about the geographic distribution of viruses in tick populations, especially species of vector importance. In this context, studies on ixodid populations are essential to elucidate viral ecology, identify potential emerging agents and assess risks to public and animal health, contributing to the improvement of disease surveillance and prevention strategies.

items.title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant- and fungal-derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems.
items.abstract: Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. Spatiotemporal variation in the transfer of plant- versus microbial-derived energy to higher trophic levels is poorly understood but can affect bottom-up and top-down processes. For example, seasonal shifts in herbivore versus microbivore availability (bottom-up) may alter prey choice by generalist-feeding predators and lead to changes in top-down predator control on primary production and decomposition. We tested how spatiotemporal variation in primary production influences the use of different energy channels by a widely distributed generalist invertebrate predator in the Arctic tundra. We sampled wolf spiders across four sites spanning a productivity gradient in the Alaskan Arctic during peak summer and on a weekly basis at one focal site throughout the growing season. Using essential amino acid (EAA) carbon isotope (δ 13 C) fingerprinting, we traced the flow of plant-, bacterial- and fungal-derived EAAs to spiders and quantified the use of plant- versus microbe-based energy channels between sites and across summer. Wolf spiders were associated with more plant- and less fungal-derived carbon assimilation when larger or collected from sites with higher normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Across the growing season, spiders shifted from primarily assimilating fungal-based resources in early summer to plant-derived resources in late summer, aligning with seasonal increases in NDVI. These patterns demonstrate spatiotemporal variation in carbon flow through different energy channels and suggest subsequent top-down predator effects may also vary with basal resource availability. Our findings also suggest wolf spider body size may predict whether predation indirectly influences primary production or decomposition. As climate change alters seasonality, resource dynamics and invertebrate body sizes, these insights provide a basis for predicting spatiotemporal variation in predator impacts on ecosystem processes. Finally, our work demonstrates the utility of compound-specific stable isotope analysis for integrating ecological and biogeochemical theory through the conceptual lens of zoogeochemistry.

items.title: Blood, ink, and flies: A case report on the house fly (Musca domestica) feeding on active tattooing wounds.
items.abstract: Cases of adventitious feeding on humans by non-hematophagous insects hold significant medical relevance, yet their occurrence during active body art procedures remains undocumented. This case report describes a persistent instance of opportunistic exsudatophagy by the house fly, Musca domestica Linnaeus, 1758 (Diptera: Muscidae), during a tattooing session on a healthy 32-year-old male client in Germany. Over a four-hour timeframe, four adult house flies entered the ground-floor studio through doors and windows opened for summer cross-ventilation. The insects exhibited highly persistent landing and feeding attempts directly on the freshly wounded tissue of the right lower leg, actively drinking a matrix of blood, plasma, and tattoo ink. Attraction intensified significantly once large-scale shading expanded the exuding epidermal surface area. Effective mechanical repulsion was heavily restricted by the client's enforced immobility required to ensure precise tattoo application. Following a routine aftercare protocol, the lesion healed completely without secondary bacterial infection. This report highlights a neglected hygienic hazard where the saprophagous and coprophilic ecology of synanthropic filth flies poses a mechanical vector risk for dermal pathogen inoculation, emphasizing the necessity of simple vector control strategies in tattooing facilities.

items.title: Plant-based meat alternatives can support reductions in agricultural land expansion and greenhouse gas emissions but entail micronutrient trade-offs.
items.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs), designed to mimic the sensory properties of meat, may help reduce animal-sourced protein consumption and support a shift towards plant-based diets. Here we integrated PBMAs into a land-use model to assess their effects on nutrition, greenhouse gas emissions and food system sustainability. PBMA adoption not only substantially reduced agricultural land expansion and greenhouse gas emissions from the agriculture, forestry and other land use sector but also increased risks of micronutrient inadequacy. Across regions, PBMA diets exhibited diminishing marginal returns. Replacing ruminant meat alone achieved nearly half of the potential emission reductions while incurring relatively small nutritional costs. By contrast, broader substitution of livestock products delivered additional environmental benefits but markedly increased micronutrient deficiencies. Targeted policy support, sustainable land management and improved PBMA formulations will be essential to ensure equitable dietary transitions and progress towards global climate and sustainability goals.

items.title: Soil viruses as key regulators of the microbial carbon pump in deep soils.
items.abstract: Deep soils store over half of terrestrial organic carbon, yet the viral mechanisms governing carbon persistence in subsurface contexts remain unclear. Here, by conducting a soil profile survey (0-700 cm) across four agroecosystems and a global synthesis of subsurface metagenomes, we established the Deep Soil Viral Resources Database, comprising 50,949 viral operational taxonomic units and 3,902 auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs). Viral richness increased significantly with depth, accompanied by a shift towards lysogeny driven by declining carbon availability. The deep-soil virome carried AMGs and lysozymes involved in polymer degradation and cell endolysis. Viral endolysin significantly promoted necromass carbon accumulation, which contributed to increases in mineral-associated organic carbon. A synthesis of 138 global soil profiles further revealed a positive effect of viral abundance on soil organic carbon. Our findings establish a framework where viruses strengthen the microbial carbon pump in deep soils by facilitating host carbon scavenging via AMGs and promoting necromass formation via endolysin activity.

items.title: Drift, selection and recombination bias drive the evolution of a non-ribosomal peptide.
items.abstract: Non-ribosomal peptides play important roles in microbial ecology and medicine, for example as toxins and antibiotics such as penicillin. Like ordinary proteins, non-ribosomal peptides are subject to evolutionary change, which is driven by rampant recombinations of their synthetases. The evolutionary dynamics and causes of non-ribosomal peptide diversification are not well understood, because recombinations complicate phylogenetic analysis and statistical tests for natural selection and drift. Here we study the non-ribosomal GameXPeptides, which entomopathogenic bacteria use to kill their insect prey. We use recombination-aware phylogenetics, ancestral sequence reconstruction and statistical analysis of historical recombination patterns to retrace the evolution of GameXPeptides. This uncovers dozens of new GameXPeptides, including striking patterns of structural convergence. We provide statistical and experimental evidence that this diversity is shaped by selection, but also that GameXPeptides experience substantial genetic drift and biased recombination rates that limit the space of accessible peptide variants. Our work illuminates the complex interplay of adaptive and non-adaptive evolutionary forces acting on some of the most versatile chemical weapons in nature.

items.title: A rare deletion of IhUF3GT1 in the Ivy-leaf morning glory eliminates anthocyanin-based pigmentation.
items.abstract: Anthocyanin biosynthesis is a highly branched network with upstream mutations leading to the loss of many other branches beyond just anthocyanins like flavonols, isoflavonoids, and proanthocyanidins. Consequently, disentangling the specific effects of anthocyanins on plant fitness from those of other branches is difficult unless a mutant impacting the terminal step of anthocyanin biosynthesis can be found. We discovered an Ipomoea hederacea plant (Ivy-leaf morning glory) lacking anthocyanins due to a genetic deletion in the terminal step of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Anthocyanin loss follows a recessive, Mendelian inheritance pattern. Anthocyanin loss is perfectly correlated with a lack of expression of the anthocyanin biosynthesis gene IhUF3GT1 (anthocyanidin-3-O-glucosyltransferase). IhUF3GT1 is the gene most strongly and consistently differentially expressed between unpigmented and pigmented flowers in F 2 siblings. A deletion of half of the IhUF3GT1 gene, which includes the start codon is the genetic basis underlying a loss of IhUF3GT1 expression and, consequently, anthocyanins in unpigmented plants. The IhUF3GT1 deletion is rare and unique to the unpigmented line. Genome coverage analyses demonstrate that no other pigmented I. hederacea line (of 123 screened) has a loss-of-function mutation in IhUF3GT1. Furthermore, we confirm cosegregation of the IhUF3GT1 deletion with the unpigmented phenotype in F 3 progeny from a cross where all unpigmented plants are homozygous for the IhUF3GT1 deletion. Taken together, we describe the genetic basis of a novel unpigmented mutant in I. hederacea, creating a potentially important model for studying the fitness effects of anthocyanin loss.

items.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts.
items.abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation 1-5 , rising tree mortality 6-8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest 9-11 . Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions 1-4,11,12 . Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable 1,9,13 . Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts 9,14-17 . Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO 2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr -1 , with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr -1 ) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011-2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr -1 ) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019-2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr -1 ) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr -1 ) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

items.title: Parasites in the meta-ecosystem landscape: hidden connectors and disruptors.
items.abstract: The meta-ecosystem framework explains spatial flows of organisms, materials, and energy across ecosystem boundaries. Parasites play crucial roles in these processes, yet they remain absent from meta-ecosystem models. Using examples from terrestrial and aquatic environments, we illustrate how parasitic organisms act as central connectors or disruptors of the flow of organisms, nutrients, and energy across ecosystem boundaries via four key mechanisms: parasite-induced host movement, behavioural changes that increase cross-ecosystem predation, host mortality, and parasite avoidance behaviour. These examples highlight the central role of parasites in driving and regulating nutrient and energy flow from catchment-to-coast, and we outline a pathway for improved integration of these parasite-mediated processes into the meta-ecosystem framework.

items.title: Hidden carbon: uncovering the diversity and function of polyhydroxyalkanoates.
items.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are a widespread family of microbial carbon-storage polymers. Ecological studies often focus on polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), obscuring the broader chemical diversity. We argue that PHA monomer composition should be treated as a microbial trait and propose a multiscale framework, from the single cell to the ecosystem level, to reveal hidden carbon dynamics.

items.title: Microbial resistance from genotype to metabolic phenotype.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses an escalating global threat, yet surveillance and mechanistic understanding remain anchored in individual resistance genes, an approach that is inadequate for capturing the ecological, genomic, and metabolic complexity through which resistance emerges and spreads. In this opinion article, we argue that genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) offer a principled framework for advancing AMR research beyond this gene-centric paradigm. Strain-resolved GEMs embed resistance determinants within metabolic networks, with the potential to generate quantitative, context-dependent phenotypic predictions, including minimum inhibitory concentrations and environment-conditional resistance, that sequence-based tools do not provide. Expanded GEM frameworks incorporating mobile genetic elements, horizontal gene transfer, and community-level interactions support ecology-aware resistance profiling. At the therapeutic level, whole-network modelling can identify metabolic vulnerabilities, synthetic lethal interactions, and microbiome-targeted strategies. Integrating GEMs with multiomics and data-driven approaches represents a critical step toward a mechanism-aware AMR platform connecting surveillance, diagnosis, and drug discovery.

items.title: Effect of visual and electrosensory deterrents on captive elasmobranchs.
items.abstract: Commercial gillnet fisheries interact with a wide range of elasmobranch species, many of which are incidentally captured as bycatch. Deterrent technologies have emerged as a potential approach for reducing interactions with threatened elasmobranchs. In this exploratory study, captive Giant Shovelnose Rays (Glaucostegus typus) and Brownbanded Bamboo Sharks (Chiloscyllium punctatum) were exposed to a static green LED light and a pulsed electrosensory deterrent attached to an experimental gillnet. The light deterrent initially reduced interactions by Giant Shovelnose Rays; however, this response diminished over time. Over a 10-min period, deterred Giant Shovelnose Rays showed a significantly greater distance of deterrence in both treatments compared to the control. There was also a significant difference in mean eye distance between the control and light treatments, but not in nose distance. In contrast, Brownbanded Bamboo Sharks exhibited no significant response to either deterrent. These contrasting responses may reflect differences in the sensory ecology of the two species, underscoring the importance of species-specific considerations in developing elasmobranch bycatch mitigation technologies. Given the promising outcomes reported for these deterrents in other studies, and the apparent variability in responses among elasmobranch taxa, further evaluation across a broader range of bycatch species is warranted.

items.title: A hypothesis-generating study of collateral reactivation: a reanalysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes from 119 recurrent tuberculosis cases.
items.abstract: Recurrent tuberculosis is traditionally classified as exogenous reinfection or endogenous reactivation. We previously proposed "collateral reactivation," in which distinct Mycobacterium tuberculosis subclones derived from a hypothetical original clone are involved in separate disease episodes, in contrast to traditional endogenous ("direct-descent") reactivation. To explore whether collateral reactivation occurs beyond the single case we previously reported, we reanalyzed publicly available whole-genome sequencing data from 123 recurrent tuberculosis cases. After curation, 119 cases (pairwise single-nucleotide variant [SNV] distance, 0-18) were classified as cases of collateral or direct-descent reactivation. In 21 cases (17.6%), a hypothetical original clone could be inferred, and these cases were classified as collateral reactivation. These cases showed a higher rate of SNVs/genome/year (median 3 vs. 0.4, p < 0.0001) and a higher proportion of drug resistance-associated SNVs (23.8% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.009) than direct-descent reactivation cases. These observations support the view that collateral reactivation is not restricted to the single case we previously reported, although mixed infection or exogenous reinfection caused by closely related strains cannot be excluded as alternative explanations. To determine whether collateral reactivation should be recognized as a concept distinct from direct-descent reactivation, future studies integrating whole-genome sequencing of single colonies, lesion-specific sampling, longitudinal sampling, deep sequencing, imaging, clinical follow-up, and epidemiological exposure information will be required.

items.title: Cold-season grazing better sustains ecosystem multifunctionality than warm-season grazing in Tibetan alpine steppe.
items.abstract: Grazing season profoundly shapes vegetation and soil properties in alpine grasslands, yet its effects on ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) remain poorly understood. Here, we compared grazing exclusion (GE), moderate-intensity warm-season grazing (WG), and herder-managed cold-season grazing (CG) in a cold-season pasture of the alpine steppe on the Tibetan Plateau to evaluate how seasonal grazing influences species diversity, community biomass, soil physicochemical properties, and EMF. Relative to GE, WG reduced grass dominance but increased sedge and forb proportion, while also decreasing plant height and aboveground biomass (AGB), and lowered EMF. By contrast, CG was associated with higher plant diversity and significantly elevated soil total carbon (TC) while maintaining AGB at levels comparable to GE. Effect-size analysis showed that WG significantly reduced EMF relative to GE whereas the reduction under CG did not reach significance. Correlation and path analyses further indicated that, under WG, multifunctionality was chiefly associated with the biomass pathway, which was positive but insufficient to counterbalance the direct negative effect of grazing, whereas no significant plant diversity or soil nutrient pathway was detected. Under CG, EMF was jointly associated with plant biomass, plant diversity and soil nutrients. These findings highlight the critical role of grazing season in maintaining ecosystem multifunctionality in alpine steppe, suggesting that, in cold-season pastures of the central Tibetan Plateau, cold-season grazing represents a more sustainable strategy than warm-season grazing for balancing forage production and ecological conservation.

items.title: Occurrence of lipophilic marine algal toxins in surface sediments from representative polar seas and implications for toxigenic microalgae.
items.abstract: Phytotoxins produced by harmful algal blooms threaten marine organisms and human health, yet research on algal toxins in polar marine system remains extremely limited. In this study, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to systematically characterize the composition, concentration, spatial distribution, and potential sources of lipophilic marine algal toxins (LMATs) in surface sediments from Antarctic Prydz Bay and the Arctic Bering-Chukchi Seas. Only low levels of pectenotoxin-2 (PTX2) were detected in Prydz Bay sediments (mean ± SD: 6.649 ± 3.669 ng/kg; n = 8), providing evidence of sedimentary PTX2 occurrence. In contrast, eleven LMATs were detected in sediments from the Bering-Chukchi Seas, reflecting markedly higher LMAT chemical diversity. Notably, azaspiracids, PTX2-SA, and gymnodimine were recorded for the first time in this Arctic region. The mean ± SD concentration of ΣLMATs was 6313 ± 2842 ng/kg (n = 10), dominated by yessotoxin (YTX) and okadaic acid. ΣLMATs displayed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with elevated levels concentrated in the southwestern portion of the study region near the Chukchi Peninsula, whereas the Bering Strait region showed low concentrations. Considering the observed LMAT diversity, documented YTX-producing taxa in the northwestern Pacific, and high-latitude records of Dinophysis and Azadinium/Amphidoma, the sedimentary LMAT assemblage may reflect contributions from multiple toxigenic microalgal sources. Because the vastness and harsh environmental conditions of polar oceans make comprehensive mapping of toxigenic microalgae difficult, sediment-derived LMATs provide baseline evidence of LMAT occurrence in high-latitude polar environments.

items.title: Review on algae-derived biopolymers to remove radionuclides from aquatic systems: sorption mechanisms, kinetics and stability.
items.abstract: The carboxyl, sulfate, phosphate and hydroxyl groups on algal biomass and its polysaccharides bind uranium, caesium, strontium and radium. The reported uranium capacities for brown macroalgae vary greatly depending on pH and pretreatment, ranging from roughly 150 to 560 mg/g. Green macroalgae and immobilized microalgae report much smaller uranium capacities, typically in the range of 75-290 mg/g. Certain microalgae remove 88-95% of dissolved 137 Cs within 48 h. However, these values mostly stem from acidic, single-solute batch experiments. When the same material is used to test actual effluents, removal rates drop, often dramatically. This review evaluates algae as a feedstock for functional polymers, combines capture mechanisms with the aqueous chemistry that governs them, and re-evaluates how isotherm, kinetic, and thermodynamic models are interpreted. The review then compares the quantitative and qualitative data regarding engineered hydrogels and composites, including their stability, regeneration, and response to competition from other ions. Finally, the loaded sorbent is viewed as secondary radioactive waste, and column operation, life-cycle burden, and traditional alternative options are placed within this context. Maximum capacity is less important than selectivity in real water and safe end-of-life management as critical evaluation criteria.

items.title: Phospholipid analogs and beyond: pleiotropic roles of betaine lipids in phycology, ecology, and biomedicine.
items.abstract: Betaine lipids (BLs) are a class of non-phosphorus glycerolipids widely found in microalgae, fungi, bacteria, mosses, and ferns. For decades, the central paradigm regarding the biological function of BLs has been their role in substituting for phospholipids under phosphate starvation-a crucial adaptive mechanism for survival in oligotrophic environments. However, accumulating evidence indicates that the functional diversity of BLs is far more extensive. Recent studies have demonstrated their distinct roles in fatty acid metabolism, adaptation to various environmental stresses, and ecological interactions such as symbiosis and predation. This review summarizes current insights into the pleiotropic roles of BLs in microalgal physiology and ecology, moving beyond their role as mere phospholipid surrogates. Furthermore, we highlight the recently discovered bioactive function of BL derivative in mammals.

items.title: A Qualitative Pragmatic Evaluation of Statewide Efforts to Promote Digital Access for Migrant and Seasonal Farmworkers in North Carolina.
items.abstract: Objectives Migrant and seasonal farmworkers face barriers to internet access, which impacts health. We sought to draw lessons and practitioner experiences from three digital accessibility programs for farmworkers in North Carolina (NC): (1) a project that provided technology and training to farmworker-serving community health workers and tablets to students from farmworker families; (2) a project that provided laptops to children of farmworkers; and (3) a state health department emergency pandemic response that provided internet access to farmworkers and community health workers. Methods We conducted 52 in-person, virtual, or phone interviews in English or Spanish with migrant and seasonal farmworkers ( n = 29), farmworker service providers ( n = 21), and employers or farm owners/managers ( n = 2) between August 2020 and February 2022. A team of four analysts used deductive and inductive thematic coding in NVivo 12. Results Our findings were captured in four themes: (1) pre-project challenges regarding internet accessibility and quality as well as access to technology and resources; (2) project-related experiences including recruitment, trainings, resources, and challenges; (3) benefits of the projects, including improved access to care and health information, communication, and self-efficacy; and (4) recommendations for training, resources, and relationship building, as well as persisting challenges. Conclusion Based on these findings, interventions to promote digital accessibility through internet access and education can benefit the health of farmworkers. Future program planners should consider lessons learned across three real-world implementation efforts in NC, addressing participants' recommendations for pairing training with internet access and seeking sustainable options for internet access through partnerships.

items.title: Diapause in Forest Insects: From Eco-Physiological Adaptations to Management Applications.
items.abstract: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.

items.title: Contrasting resistance and recovery of co-occurring conifers to larch caterpillar defoliation in a Northeast China temperate forest.
items.abstract: Climate change has been linked to the intensification of forest pest outbreaks, posing a serious threat to non-coevolved tree species because of their potentially weak defensive capabilities. However, unlike broad-scale climatic disturbances such as drought and heatwaves, insect outbreaks are highly heterogeneous in space and among host species, and the response of occurring conifers to such outbreaks remains poorly understood. The core area of the Changbai Mountain Nature Reserve in northeastern China was severely defoliated in 2019 by larch caterpillars (Dendrolimus superans Butler)-a conifer-feeding defoliator that prefers larch but also attacks other conifers. In this region, a vegetation transition zone between the broadleaf-Korean pine and spruce-fir forests hosts multiple conifer species co-existing within short distances under similar defoliation intensities. We monitored 1,837 trees in 2019 (pre-disturbance), 2021 and 2024, and sampled needles of healthy individuals of each species in 2024 to obtain species-level proxies of intrinsic foliar traits. Results revealed that: (i) mortality of attacked Korean pine peaked within 2 years, with little subsequent increase, resulting in a cumulative mortality rate of 31.3%; in contrast, mortality of spruce and fir continued to increase until the fifth year, reaching a combined cumulative rate of 78.6%, while larch exhibited nearly 100% survival. (ii) a deciduous habit, low needle biomass allocation and low carbohydrate concentrations enhanced survival by reducing canopy regeneration costs. (iii) regarding radial growth responses, spruce showed stronger compensatory growth but weaker recovery ability than fir and Korean pine, likely due to its limited carbon and nutrient reserves. Considering these findings, prioritizing the protection of non-coevolved conifers is recommended to minimize biomass loss during pest outbreaks. This study also provides important insights for temperate and boreal conifer forest conservation, highlighting the high vulnerability of spruce-fir forests to larch caterpillar outbreaks.

items.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation.
items.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

items.title: Perinatal health outcomes in relation to principal applicant and live-in caregiver status among economic class immigrants to Canada: A retrospective analysis of births from 1993 to 2017.
items.abstract: Objectives Economic class immigrants to Canada tend to have better health outcomes than other immigrant groups. However, variation may exist even within this population. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of data from the Migrant Maternal and Infant Morbidity and Mortality (MMIMM) dataset, which linked Canadian birth and infant death records (1993-2017) with maternal immigration records (1952-2017). All singleton births to economic class immigrant women at least 18 years of age at immigration were analyzed. Women were classified as principal applicants (PA), non-principal applicants (NPA), or former live-in caregivers (LIC); all analyses were stratified by marital status at landing. Outcomes examined included preterm birth (PTB), small- and large-for-gestational-age birth (SGA and LGA, respectively), stillbirth, and infant mortality. Risk ratios for adverse outcomes by PA and former LIC status were estimated with adjustment for parental, birth, and immigration characteristics. Results The cohort included 490,310 births (165,850 births to PAs, 267,200 to NPAs, 57,160 to former LICs). In adjusted analyses, among women who were single at landing, NPA had slightly lower rates of LGA (fully adjusted risk ratio (aRR) = 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.98) and stillbirth (aRR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.53-0.97) compared to PA, and former LICs had slightly elevated rates of PTB (aRR 1.05, 95% CI 1.00-1.11) and SGA (1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10). Conclusion These findings add to existing literature highlighting the vulnerability of live-in caregivers in Canada while shedding light on possible differences between principal and non-principal applicants.

items.title: Ontogenetic Variation in Plant-to-Plant Signaling Effects on Direct and Indirect Defenses in Wild Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum).
items.abstract: Various plant-related factors have been shown to influence volatile organic compound (VOC)-mediated plant-to-plant interactions, but effects of plant ontogeny have been rarely considered. Here, we tested if these interactions differ between two ontogenetic stages in wild cotton, Gossypium hirsutum. We used 2.5- and 4.5-month-old plants (seedlings and juveniles, respectively), arranged in triplets where one plant acted as an emitter and two as receivers (all plants within a cage were of the same developmental stage). Half of the emitters were subjected to herbivory by Alabama argillacea caterpillars, while the emitters of the other triplets were left unharmed. After 48 h of VOC exposure, we collected the VOCs from a subset of the emitter plants (for 2 h), and one receiver from each cage was removed to measure extrafloral nectar (EFN) production and to collect leaves for total phenolic analyses. The remaining receivers were subjected to herbivory to assess signaling effects on defense induction. Emitter seedlings released larger quantities of VOCs in response to caterpillar damage than juveniles, and ontogenetic stages also differed in the composition of the emitted VOC blend. Accordingly, we found trends for ontogenetic variation in signaling effects: seedling receivers exposed to damaged emitters tended to produce more EFN both prior to and following damage compared to those exposed to undamaged emitters, whereas juvenile receivers showed no EFN response to emitter damage. Similarly, seedling receivers exposed to damaged emitters exhibited higher phenolic concentrations, whereas no such signaling effect was observed in juveniles. These findings indicate that VOC-mediated signaling of defenses is strong in young cotton plants but weakens during development in pre-reproductive juvenile plants, and that this is reflected in both direct and indirect defense responses.

items.title: Volatile Insensitivity and Localized Alkaloids Support Commensalism in the Oxytropis sericea-Alternaria oxytropis Association.
items.abstract: The endophytic fungus Alternaria oxytropis is vertically transmitted through silky crazyweed (Oxytropis sericea Nutt.) and produces the neurotoxin swainsonine, yet its influence on host chemical signaling remains unclear. Here we characterize the floral and foliar volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles of endophyte-infected (E+) and endophyte-free (E-) O. sericea using dynamic headspace GC-MS on greenhouse- and field-grown plants - the first characterization of volatile profiles in this species. Endophyte infection had a negligible effect on VOC composition, explaining less than 1% of compositional variance in both greenhouse and field settings, with no compound differing consistently by infection status. Seven volatiles were reliably detected across both environments. The dominant axes of variation (PCA) instead reflected differences among individuals and between size-matched E+/E- plant across years. These accounted for most compositional variance (72.6% greenhouse, 64.9% field), and VOC profiles differed markedly between collection years, likely reflecting fine-scale environmental and physiological variation. Ancillary nectar assays and pollinator observations revealed no consistent differences between E + and E- plants, and seed set was unaffected regardless of endophyte status. Swainsonine in floral organs was roughly an order of magnitude lower than in leaves and near-trace in nectar, indicating that any localized chemical defense is likely decoupled from scent chemistry. Together, these findings position the Oxytropis-Alternaria association toward the commensal end of the symbiotic continuum: the fungus maintains vertical transmission while the host shows no detectable effect on volatile signaling, pollinator attraction, or reproductive output, despite the resources required to sustain fungal alkaloid biosynthesis. This system offers a tractable model for understanding how endophyte associations persist in the absence of measurable host benefit.

items.title: An integrated chemical and biomarker approach using Ucides cordatus (Crustacea; Decapoda) to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two Amazonian estuaries.
items.abstract: In this study, an integrated chemical and biomarker approach was applied using the mangrove crab Ucides cordatus to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two distinct Amazonian estuaries. Crabs were collected from São José Bay (A1-minimally impacted) and São Marcos Bay (A2-impacted by port activities) on the Amazon coast of Brazil. Simultaneously with crab sampling, physicochemical parameters and trace element levels in sediment and water samples were assessed. Biometric measurements included cephalothorax length and width, cheliped propodus length and width, movable finger length and width, and total weight. Two biomarkers, genotoxic responses (micronuclei) and histopathological lesions (gills and liver hepatopancreas), were measured. Abiotic parameters, such as pH, dissolved oxygen, and salinity, were similar between the two study areas (A1 and A2). However, the concentrations of trace elements (Zn, Fe, Al, and Mn) in the water were increased in A2. Biometric data revealed that crabs from A2 were significantly smaller and lighter (p < 0.05) than those from A1. Gill lesions (marginal canal deformation, pillar cell rupture, and necrosis) were frequently observed in crabs from both sites, with a higher prevalence in A2. Hepatopancreas histological alterations (e.g., necrosis) were significantly more common in crabs from A2 (p < 0.05). Genotoxic responses, such as pycnotic nuclei, were also significantly more frequent in A2 (p < 0.05). The results demonstrate that Ucides cordatus effectively reflects environmental contamination through measurable histological and genotoxic biomarkers, which is consistent with the chemical evidence of trace element pollution in estuarine environments.

items.title: Robustness of oxygen metrics to sampling frequency in a stratified lake.
items.abstract: Long-term lake monitoring often relies on monthly dissolved oxygen profiles, but the robustness of derived oxygen metrics to this temporal resolution is uncertain. We compared three years (2022-2024) of hourly sensor observations (high-frequency (HF)) with approximately monthly discrete profiles (low-frequency (LF)) from a small, dimictic subalpine lake. We evaluated volume-weighted oxygen concentrations, hypolimnetic oxygen depletion rates (ODR) and depth-specific counts of days with oxygen < 2 mg L⁻1. To isolate temporal sampling effects on ODR, we subsampled the HF daily record at 7-, 14-, 30- and 60-day intervals across all starting-day offsets within fixed annual fitting periods. LF profiles interpolated to daily resolution reproduced broad seasonal oxygen trajectories, but concentration differences persisted on matched sampling dates, particularly at 9 and 12 m. The mean within-year range width of signed ODR deviations from the full-HF reference was 8.0 percentage points at 7-day sampling, 20.5 at 14 days, 47.5 at 30 days and 48.6 at 60 days. Depth-specific low-oxygen-day counts were strongly correlated between datasets (Pearson's r = 0.933-0.977), but unequal observation coverage precluded unbiased estimates of annual duration. The results indicate that approximately monthly profiles can describe broad seasonal oxygen dynamics in this lake, whereas more frequent sampling reduces the sensitivity of ODR estimates to sampling timing.

items.title: Fungicide co-exposure influences ibuprofen accumulation, distribution and phytotoxicological responses in zucchini (Cucurbita pepo).
items.abstract: Pharmaceuticals introduced into agricultural soils through wastewater reuse and biosolids application may coexist with crop-protection products, yet the influence of fungicides on pharmaceutical uptake and phytotoxicity in crops remains poorly understood. This study investigated how benomyl, chlorothalonil, validamycin A, and probenazole affect ibuprofen (IBU) accumulation, translocation, and physiological responses in zucchini ( Cucurbita pepo cv. Soraya). IBU accumulated mainly in roots, and its distribution depended on fungicide identity. Compared with IBU alone, root accumulation was numerically higher under benomyl and significantly higher under validamycin A. Root-to-leaf translocation factors varied among treatments, but these differences were not statistically significant. These findings indicate treatment-dependent effects of fungicide co-exposure on IBU accumulation, particularly in roots, while evidence for differential root-to-leaf translocation remains inconclusive. Ibuprofen alone caused only minor physiological changes, whereas co-exposure, particularly with benomyl and chlorothalonil, reduced biomass and photosynthetic pigment concentrations and altered antioxidant and detoxification responses. The IBU+B treatment was associated with the highest lipid peroxidation. Molecular docking predicted a computationally plausible interaction between IBU and CpMLP-SY1, with AutoDock Vina scores ranging from -6.8 to -6.6 kcal mol -1 . Metabolic disturbances were strongest in roots and were dominated by amino acid biosynthesis and metabolism, particularly pathways involving branched-chain, aromatic and sulfur-containing amino acids, with additional alterations in secondary metabolism. These results indicate that fungicide co-exposure can influence IBU accumulation and plant responses in a treatment-dependent manner.

items.title: Multilayered network analysis reveals the centrality of newly discovered Nucleocytoviricota in wastewater treatment plant communities.
items.abstract: Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. Previous research has leveraged computational approaches to map their extensive diversity. Experimental work has, in parallel, begun to elucidate their intricate interactions with hosts, bacterial symbionts, co-infecting virophages, and other mobile genetic elements.Although unlikely to replicate all simultaneously within the same host cell, the convergence of these entities within a single environment creates a dense hub of potential interactions that calls for a holistic, topology-based analysis. Here, we recovered high-quality genomes of 61 Nucleocytoviruses, 15 virophages and 14 polinton-like viruses from deeply sequenced metagenomes of 23 Danish wastewater treatment plants, and integrated them into a multilayered interaction network together with microbial contigs. This network recovered putative interactions across multiple levels, including Nucleocytoviruses co-occurring with hyperparasitic elements, associations with abundant activated sludge bacteria, and read-level signals of integration events. We show that the giants among viruses act as centrality-inducing entities, elevating others into highly central positions within the community and therefore are key players shaping the microbial community structure, ecology and evolution in wastewater treatment plants.

items.title: Functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover across coral-associated microbiomes.
items.abstract: Coral-associated microbiomes are fundamental to holobiont health and resilience, yet their community structures often demonstrate high taxonomic variability across host species. Whether such variability results in functional instability or reflects pervasive metabolic redundancy remains unclear. Here, we investigated microbial taxonomic structure, functional potential, and community assembly mechanisms across 15 coral species using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. These communities exhibited extreme taxonomic heterogeneity, high beta-diversity, and the absence of a universally shared core genus, indicating strong host-specific filtering that dictates microbial membership. In contrast, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway-based functional profiles exhibited striking convergence across hosts, revealing a conserved metabolic landscape despite extensive taxonomic turnover. Mantel and Procrustes analyses identified a weak but significant correspondence between taxonomic composition and functional potential, a pattern consistent with functional redundancy across coral-associated microbiomes. Null model-based assembly analyses further revealed a decoupling between taxonomic and functional organization. Taxonomic structure was shaped by a host-dependent balance of stochastic and deterministic processes, whereas functional profiles were predominantly assembled through stochastic processes, maintaining consistently high functional redundancy across hosts. Metagenomic profiling uncovered a two-tier functional architecture underlying this stability: a conserved, high-abundance metabolic core enriched in carbon and phosphorus cycling and stress response functions that support microbial persistence in the coral microenvironment, together with lower-abundance host-specific metabolic modules involved in nitrogen and sulfur transformations that enable niche adaptation. Thus, functional requirements primarily govern the coral-associated microbiome rather than taxonomic identity. This synergy between conserved survival traits and flexible metabolic capacities maintains holobiont homeostasis despite extensive taxonomic turnover.IMPORTANCECoral reefs rely on complex partnerships between corals and their associated microorganisms to maintain health and withstand environmental stress. However, it remains unclear whether changes in microbial communities across different coral species lead to loss of important functions. In this study, we examined microorganisms associated with 15 coral species from the South China Sea and found that coral species hosted highly different microbial communities, while maintaining similar microbial functions. Our findings reveal that different microbial groups can perform similar ecological roles, allowing coral-associated communities to remain functionally stable despite changes in microbial membership. This functional flexibility may help corals maintain biological balance under changing environmental conditions and provides new insights into how coral holobionts preserve resilience in the face of ecological disturbances.

items.title: Competition-dominated microbial interactions and adaptive mutations enhance synthetic denitrifying community functions.
items.abstract: Understanding how interspecific interactions shape ecosystem functioning is a fundamental and longstanding question in ecology, especially along an evolutionary trajectory. Here, we used experimental evolution to evaluate how microbial interactions and adaptive mutations shaped community-level functions in synthetic denitrifying communities (SDCs) along a species richness gradient (one, two, and six species). Our results showed that competitive microbial interactions were observed and significantly (P < 0.05) enhanced denitrification rates in the six-species SDCs during experimental evolution. Genome and metagenome re-sequencing analysis revealed the highest fixed non-synonymous and frameshift mutations within the six-species SDCs, among genes involved in nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion pathways. AlphaFold2 protein structure prediction, molecular docking, and Evo 2 host fitness prediction indicated that the fixed mutations could improve host strain fitness, and partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed that interspecific competition accelerated adaptive mutations, thereby reinforcing community-level functions, indicating potential Red Queen dynamics. This study offers novel insights into our understanding of eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive mutations, and community functions, with important implications for active nitrogen removal and greenhouse gas mitigation in diverse ecosystems. Microbial diversity is widely recognized as a key driver of ecosystem functioning, yet how species interactions shape ecosystem functions through evolutionary processes remains poorly understood. Using synthetic denitrifying communities with different levels of species richness, we show that interspecific competition can accelerate adaptive mutations and enhance community-level denitrification over evolutionary timescales. Communities with higher species richness accumulated more adaptive mutations, particularly in genes associated with nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion systems, ultimately improving microbial fitness and denitrification performance. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that microbial competition can promote functional adaptation, consistent with the Red Queen hypothesis. This study advances our understanding of the eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive evolution, and ecosystem functioning.

items.title: Unilateral cross-feeding constrains adaptive evolution, even in the producer without direct fitness effects.
items.abstract: Cross-feeding interactions are pervasive in microbial communities and profoundly shape community structure, stability, and function. While previous studies have explored how cross-feeding affects evolvability, this work has predominantly focused on bidirectional mutualistic interactions in engineered auxotrophic systems where both partners reciprocally exchange essential metabolites. However, most metabolic interactions in natural microbial communities are unidirectional, with organisms feeding on the metabolic waste products of other species. Our study addresses this gap by examining how a unidirectional cross-feeding interaction affects the evolutionary dynamics of both the producer (Acinetobacter johnsonii) and consumer (Pseudomonas putida) over 800 generations of experimental evolution. We found that co-culture constrained adaptive evolution in both species. Co-cultures exhibited lower πN/πS ratios (0.75 for P. putida; 1.04 for A. johnsonii) than monocultures (1.44 and 2.02, respectively), indicating stronger purifying selection against nonsynonymous mutations in the community context. Lineage tracking through whole genome sequencing of populations and clones revealed greater lineage diversity and complexity in monocultures, with more mutations showing significant parallelism across replicate populations. Additionally, P. putida evolved increased dependence on its partner; co-culture-evolved P. putida grew significantly worse than its ancestor when A. johnsonii was removed. These findings indicate that ecological interactions can reshape fitness landscapes and constrain adaptive evolution even when fitness benefits are unidirectional, with implications for understanding microbial community stability and predicting evolutionary dynamics in complex communities.

items.title: Heatwave-Resilient Cuticular Microbiota Protect the Leaf Beetle Plagiodera versicolora From Fungal Infection.
items.abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves-extreme thermal events characterized by prolonged supra-optimal temperatures-exert profound impacts on global ecosystem stability and species interactions. While the disruptive effects of thermal stress on host physiology and gut microbiota are well documented, the role of cuticular microbiota in host defense under heatwaves remains poorly characterized. Here, we show that the cuticular microbiota of the willow leaf beetle Plagiodera versicolora may serve as a thermostable protective barrier against the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana. Using microbiota-manipulated larval models, we found that cuticular microbiota significantly bolstered host survival under both control (27°C) and simulated heatwave (32°C) regimes. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing revealed a dramatic microbial regime shift: Pantoea dominated at control temperatures, whereas Enterobacter proliferated and became predominant during simulated heatwaves. Both genera exhibited potent antifungal activity that markedly increased with rising temperature, suggesting a potential functional compensation property whereby thermally adaptive taxa may maintain host defensive capacity under climatic perturbations. Recolonization experiments confirmed that cuticle-isolated Enterobacter gergoviae and Pantoea anthophila are sufficient to reduce the increased fungal susceptibility of germ-free larvae. Mechanistically, these symbionts appear to inhibit fungal germination through direct antagonism and modulate host immune responses by upregulating antimicrobial peptide effectors while potentially reducing excessive immune recognition signaling. These findings highlight the resilience of cuticular defensive symbioses in the face of climate change and provide new insights into the adaptive mechanisms that sustain host-microbe-pathogen dynamics in a warming world.

items.title: Benzoic Acid Secreted From the Chickpea Root Promotes Persistent Colonisation by Specific Soil Microbes.
items.abstract: The plant root tip is highly sensitive to environmental cues and exerts sensory, chemical and movement responses. However, the microbial diversification at the root tip, and the nature of root-selection for microbes, are poorly understood. This study investigated root exudation and microbiome colonisation in the chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) root tip and root base, in diverse soils. For the endosphere microbiome, deterministic effects were more important than stochastic processes in shaping the root tip microbiome, indicated by the stable endophyte composition independent of the soil microbiota background. A genotype with high secretion of benzoic acid (BA), was consistently colonised by 3 core ASV (Amplicon Sequence Variant) from the Burkholderia clade. Two of 98 isolated strains were confirmed as the culturable candidates of the core ASV, both of which were characterised by superior BA tolerance and the ability to utilise BA as a sole carbon source, demonstrated through high expression of BA degradation genes. Additionally, one IAA-producing coloniser specifically promoted the growth of its original host genotype across different soils, but provided no consistent benefits for other genotypes. Our results reveal the mechanisms by which soil microbes interact with root exudates of a host genotype to establish colonisation.

items.title: The characterization of municipal solid waste in a Ukrainian region during the war period: Reference values and a methodological review.
items.abstract: Ukraine's sustainable post-war transition toward resilient, resource-oriented waste management (WM) systems relies mainly on accurate data on municipal solid waste (MSW) generation and composition. This paper reviews methodologies and reference values for MSW composition in the Poltava region during the war period (2023-2024), combining (1) a systematic analysis of pre-war and wartime data from several Ukrainian regions and (2) four seasonal sorting analyses conducted in the Kotelva settlement, complemented by a simplified socio-demographic stratification approach using Austrian MSW data as analogies. The four seasonal sorting analyses applied two successive Ukrainian methodological frameworks, the latter supplemented by the Austrian and European waste classification approach. Existing Ukrainian data from different regions show wide ranges for key waste fractions, reflecting strong methodological heterogeneity-from purely normative, regulation-based estimates to seasonally stratified field campaigns. Wartime MSW in Kotelva was dominated by kitchen waste (mean 37.4 wt%), along with organic (other than food) waste (6.0 wt%), followed by inert construction waste (7.6 wt%), hygiene products (7.3 wt%), and textiles (5.9 wt%). Compared with 2020 pre-war data, a shift from glass to plastic packaging in the residual waste was observed. The study demonstrates that the current Ukrainian methodology only partially aligns with European practice, underscoring the need for a harmonized national framework. Moreover, a simplified comparative approach based on socio-demographic stratification was developed to pre-assess the MSW composition of Ukrainian settlements lacking basic WM data. The proposed approach may serve as offer a pragmatic interim tool for WM planning in data-poor Ukrainian regions to promptly support post-war circular-economy-oriented decision-making.

items.title: Natural recovery and gaming disorder: a case series.
items.abstract: Conceptualizations of recovery in gaming disorder (GD) remain relatively underdeveloped. While remission without formal treatment appears common in longitudinal data, the mechanisms through which it occurs have received little systematic attention. In contrast, natural recovery-the resolution of addictive problems without formal treatment-is well documented in substance and gambling research, where it has prompted broader reconceptualizations of how and where recovery unfolds. Using longitudinal qualitative data from Finland, Slovakia and South Korea, this case series examines how individuals who had previously experienced self-identified gaming-related problems reached recovery without successful intervention explicitly targeting their gaming behaviour. Six recurring recovery pathways were identified: axiological shift, social enforcement, gradual regulation, reflexive transformation, healing comorbidity and environmental transformation. Rather than centring on abstinence or direct symptom elimination, recovery emerged through reconfigurations of life structure, social roles and personal value hierarchies. In most cases, gaming did not disappear but was repositioned within a broader ecology of responsibilities and relationships. These findings suggest that natural recovery in GD may be better understood as a contextual and relational reconfiguration rather than solely as symptom reduction. The pathways identified here provide a conceptual stepping stone towards more comprehensive frameworks for understanding the recovery process in GD.

items.title: Experience-dependent shifts in behavioural decision-making following repeated captures in a wild mammal.
items.abstract: Live trapping is central to behavioural ecology, yet whether post-capture behaviour reflects consistent among-individual differences and how it is modified by repeated captures remain poorly understood. Here, we repeatedly captured wild individuals of the rodent Apodemus mystacinus and temporarily held them in a standardised wooden experimental box. We then allowed them to voluntarily exit the box near the capture location and continuously recorded their behaviour for 5 minutes. Using multilevel, multivariate and continuous-time multi-state models, we characterise the sequence of behavioural states from confinement to escape. We also test whether capture experience reorganises individual behavioural trajectories and whether individual characteristics, such as body mass and sex, mediate behavioural transitions across capture-recapture events. We show that there is among-individual variation in the measured post-capture behaviours and that repeated captures reorganise the structure and sequential organisation of behavioural responses after individuals exit a trap. Importantly, we also show that recapture experience and body mass are associated with an increased tendency towards rapid escape. In contrast, we find that sex has no detectable effects. Our findings highlight that behaviours expressed immediately after trap release do not represent individuals' undisturbed ecological baseline, but instead experience-dependent responses shaped by individuals' cumulative history of interactions with their environment.

items.title: Soil moisture enhances the vibrations induced by moving earthworms, especially of detritivores.
items.abstract: Earthworms (Lumbricidae) are moisture-loving soil-dwellers that can be categorized into two feeding guilds with distinct behaviours: detritivores and geophages. Detritivores feed on litter fragments and geophages on smaller litter particles mixed with soil. When earthworms move within and across soil layers to forage, soil characteristics might influence the scale of these movements and their detectability to predators. To investigate the extent to which the detection of earthworm movements and the vibrations they thereby generate is affected by soil moisture, we used an innovative method to detect and quantify vibrations of moving earthworms emitted through the soil. We designed a mesocosm experiment in which we recorded, with a geophone, the movement-induced vibrations of detritivores and geophages in drier and wetter soils. Earthworm vibrations were detected best at 200 Hz and were detected significantly more in wetter than in drier soils. Moreover, in wetter soils, vibrations induced by detritivores were detected more frequently and at higher intensities than those of geophages. These findings suggest differences in activity levels between detritivores and geophages, as a function of soil moisture content. The observed activity patterns are likely to have food web consequences because earthworm consumers relying on mechanoreceptors to detect prey might detect detritivores more often, specifically in wetter soils.

items.title: Modularity without convergence: integrated evolution of the salamander autopodium.
items.abstract: Morphological modularity is known to favour evolutionary diversification by enabling different body regions to vary in response to functional and ecological demands. Despite their remarkable diversity in limb morphology and ecology, amphibians-and salamanders in particular-remain significantly under-represented in empirical tests of modularity. Using geometric morphometrics and phylogenetic comparative methods, we investigate patterns of shape variation, integration and modularity in the salamander autopodium. We first validated a landmark-based method to outline foot shape, demonstrating that image orientation does not affect shape analyses and that species can be reliably distinguished. We then applied this approach to a larger comparative dataset encompassing 149 salamander taxa across major lineages and ecological strategies. Our findings demonstrate that the salamander autopodium is functionally modular: the distal region (digits and interdigital region) shows more evolutionary lability than the proximal pes, while remaining integrated within a coordinated evolutionary system. Furthermore, the combinations of allometric, ecological and life-history factors account for a small but significant percentage of shape variation, with a low evolutionary signal in foot shape. Our results suggest that modular organization of the salamander foot may allow for morphological variation while still being limited by a common evolutionary and developmental history. By focusing on an understudied group and morphological system, this study provides new insight on how modularity influences limb evolution in tetrapods.

items.title: A climate action intervention increases four psychological motivators, as well as climate advocacy, activism and civic participation.
items.abstract: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. As part of a broader Registered Report series, this study examined whether a longitudinal intervention designed to strengthen psychological correlates of pro-environmental behaviour could motivate n = 31 university students in The Netherlands to take climate action. The intervention was delivered over six weeks through interactive lessons and activities informed by psychological theories and interventions. The goal was to increase pro-climate behaviours by targeting 12 psychological factors. Participants completed surveys assessing these correlates, as well as ecological momentary assessments of individual and collective pro-climate behaviours before and after the intervention, and after three months (14 days each). A control group was included ( n = 27). Results showed that 4 of the 12 psychological correlates increased significantly: emotional engagement, collective efficacy, the bottom-up theory of change (the belief that change can start from grassroots action and spread systemically) and climate appraisal. Three (except appraisal) remained elevated at the three-month follow-up. Civic engagement, advocacy and activism increased after the intervention in the experimental group relative to control group. The increase in activist behaviour was predicted by the development of a bottom-up theory of change.

items.title: Can consumers accurately identify loot boxes and loot box receipts?
items.abstract: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children's, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.

items.title: Psychological and behavioral correlates of food addiction symptoms in university students: the role of hedonic eating and food label attitudes.
items.abstract: Food addiction (FA) involves addictive-like eating and impaired control over palatable food consumption. This cross-sectional study examined FA correlates among 404 university students, focusing on palatable eating motives and food label reading attitudes. Sixty-six participants (16.3%) met the original Yale Food Addiction Scale (YFAS 1.0) threshold of at least three of seven DSM-IV-TR criteria plus clinically significant impairment or distress. Female sex, smoking, obesity, and a higher T-PEMS mean were associated with higher odds of meeting the threshold; the obesity estimate was imprecise because that subgroup was small. Model discrimination was acceptable in-sample (AUC = 0.746). The T-PEMS mean had a weak inverse correlation with label attitudes ( r = -0.143) that was not significant after adjustment (β = -0.10, p = 0.060; R 2 = 0.057). Findings support an association between palatable eating motives and FA but limited evidence for an independent label-attitude relationship. Longitudinal and multicenter studies are needed.

items.title: Boosting or Blocking Breastfeeding Confidence? The Role of Online Breastfeeding Content in Relation to Mothers' Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy.
items.abstract: Mothers increasingly go online to find answers to their breastfeeding concerns, read personal experiences, or connect with breastfeeding "mommy influencers." This study analyzes how the consultation of online platforms and breastfeeding-related posts is linked to mothers' breastfeeding self-efficacy, and whether this relationship is moderated by mothers' different motives (i.e., information-seeking, entertainment, or community building) for consuming such content online within a Dutch-speaking context. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory and the Uses and Gratifications framework, an online survey (N = 354; M age = 31, 22) was conducted among Dutch-speaking mothers. Participants reported their exposure to online breastfeeding content from various resources (social media, "Mommy influencers," parenting community groups), their motives for consulting these different resources, and their breastfeeding self-efficacy. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) reveals that online breastfeeding content consumption is not directly related to breastfeeding self-efficacy. However, an interaction effect was found with the information-seeking motive: mothers using online parenting platforms for informational purposes show a more negative association between online exposure to breastfeeding content and breastfeeding self-efficacy compared to mothers not using these platforms for informational reasons. These findings highlight the complex role of online breastfeeding content, suggesting that informational motives may shape mothers' self-efficacy differently.
