items.title: Level of educational attainment and school dropout rates of people with disability in Denmark.
items.abstract: Aims Education is linked to health outcomes, and health selection processes may shape educational trajectories among people with disabilities. This study examines educational attainment and school dropout patterns among people with physical and mental disabilities. Methods This cross-sectional study used data from a nationally representative survey of Danish adults ( N =18,749). Participants included individuals with physical disability only ( n =4047), mental disability only ( n =888), and both physical and mental disabilities ( n =745). Results Compared with individuals without disabilities, those with disabilities had significantly lower levels of educational attainment and were less likely to participate in higher education. Participants with only physical disability (odds ratio (OR) 0.71, confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.77), only mental disability (OR 0.64, CI 0.54-0.76), and both physical and mental disabilities (OR 0.46, CI 0.39-0.54) had lower odds of completing higher education compared with individuals without disabilities. A similar pattern was observed for dropout. Participants with physical (OR 1.47, CI 1.35-1.61), mental (OR 2.61, CI 2.22-3.07), and both physical and mental disabilities (OR 3.26, CI 2.78-3.84) had higher odds of dropping out. Moreover, early-onset disability (before age 25 years) was associated with lower odds of higher education completion compared with adult-onset disability (OR 1.16, CI 1.00-1.35). Conclusions Disability remains a major barrier to accessing and completing higher education, particularly when disability occurs early in life. Although higher education is free in Denmark and students with disabilities receive financial support, further measures are needed to close the educational gap .

items.title: EXPRESS: The Dynamics of Cue Integration in Metacognitive Judgments.
items.abstract: Learners form judgments of learning (JOLs) by integrating multiple cues. However, little is known about how cue integration might change over time. To examine this, we introduced a modified cue-integration paradigm in which one cue (the context cue) remained constant across sequences of trials varying in length, while another cue (the target cue) varied randomly. This design allowed us to examine how the consistency and variability of a cue affect its use for JOLs and that of other available cues. In three experiments, participants studied nouns with two cues manipulated per experiment (e.g., emotionality, concreteness). In all experiments, both cues influenced JOLs, and the target cue's influence remained stable across conditions, suggesting that learners used the two cues independently. In Experiment 1, the context cue's effect declined when its level was constant across multiple consecutive trials. This adaptation effect did not replicate in Experiments 2 and 3. Exploratory cross-experimental analyses showed stronger context cue effects immediately after than immediately before context cue levels switched. This hints at a transient increase in cue salience following a switch. Together, our findings show that learners flexibly respond to changes in cue consistency and variability while maintaining their overall cue integration strategy.

items.title: Psychological distress among nurses before and after COVID-19 vaccines: A repeated cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundExtensive research conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic has consistently found significant levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among healthcare workers, particularly among nurses. Nevertheless, the effect of COVID-19 vaccine availability on the psychological distress of healthcare workforce remains unexplored.ObjectiveTo compare levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among Spanish nurses immediately before and after the full COVID-19 vaccination protocol which was conducted in Spain throughout 2021.MethodsWe employed a repeated cross-sectional design recruiting 439 and 410 Spanish registered nurses at the first (pre-vaccination) and second (post-vaccination) timepoints respectively. Data on psychological distress were collected via online surveys using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).ResultsAfter vaccination nurses showed lower perceived stress and depression with a small effect size, but anxiety was not reduced. The magnitude of these effects was very small. Although in both timepoints psychological distress was higher in women, the initial differences between frontline and non-frontline professionals tended to disappear. Over the period studied, the proportion of nurses receiving psychiatric or psychological care increased from 7.7% to 20.4%, and half of those using psychotropic drugs had started treatment in the preceding year.ConclusionsThe psychological distress of nurses continued being a relevant problem even after COVID-19 vaccines became available. Policymakers and health systems must ensure adequate psychological support for nurses and a supportive work environment to improve their long-term resilience and well-being, regardless of the existence of effective vaccines.

items.title: Effectiveness of a continuous ergonomic program on workplace health and cognitive strain in university employees.
items.abstract: BackgroundUniversity staff are at high risk of musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and mental workload due to prolonged static postures, poor ergonomic conditions, and high cognitive demands. These issues lead to significant health and productivity challenges, particularly in developing countries.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the impact of a participatory ergonomic intervention program on reducing MSDs and mental workload among university staff, and to enhance their awareness of ergonomic principles.MethodsA quasi-experimental design with pre- and post-tests was used, involving 60 participants divided into control and intervention groups. The intervention included 8 weekly training sessions on ergonomics, workstation adjustments, and the introduction of ergonomic equipment. Data were collected using the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ) and NASA-TLX workload index, analyzed via paired t-tests and covariance analysis.ResultsThe intervention significantly reduced mental workload by 24.17% (p = 0.008), with the highest reductions in physical (46.58%) and mental (35.84%) dimensions. MSDs prevalence decreased notably in the back (50%), neck (39%), and wrists (39-61.6%). The control group showed no significant changes.ConclusionsBased on these results, continuous training and ergonomic adjustments are recommended, as they may help sustain the observed benefits over the long term. This approach has the potential to promote healthier work environments and could lead to enhanced productivity, although further longitudinal research is needed to directly confirm these broader implications.

items.title: Understanding the Complex Linkages Between Climate Change and Gender-Based Violence Globally.
items.abstract: Many determinants of gender-based violence (GBV) are sensitive to climate change. In this theoretical article, we offer a conceptual framework for analyzing how climate change can shape the incidence of GBV through five mechanisms: human physiology and psychology, economic insecurity and job loss, scarcity of natural resources, changes in migration patterns, and disruption of infrastructure and essential services. We argue that significant empirical gaps in the literature stem from over-reliance on household surveys using narrow measures of domestic violence in a non-representative set of contexts, and provide methodological recommendations for achieving a more expansive understanding of climate effects on GBV.

items.title: Perceived satisfaction with care, service atmosphere and mood fluctuations among patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder in Italian mental health supported accommodations: a multicenter study.
items.abstract: Background Supported Accommodations (SA) are central to Italy's community-based mental health care for individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), offering structured, recovery-oriented environments. While symptom severity remains important, care environment and satisfaction strongly influence well-being. Mood fluctuations, a key aspect of daily functioning, have been underexplored in SA. Using the Experience Sampling Method (ESM), this study aims to examine the associations between perceived ward atmosphere, care satisfaction, and momentary mood in SA residents with SSD. Methods As part of the DiAPAson project, 68 residents with SSD were assessed also using ESM. Additional measures included psychopathology (BPRS, BNSS), functioning (SLOF, WHODAS 2.0), perceived ward atmosphere (WAS-P) and service satisfaction (VSSS-32). Descriptive analyses were conducted, and a structural equation model examined mood in relation to clinical, demographic, and environmental factors. Results Residents with SSD (29.4% female; mean age = 42.8 years) were mostly single (80.9%) and unemployed (79.4%), with a mean disorder duration of 19.2 years. Clinical assessments indicated moderate symptom severity and functioning. Structural equation modelling showed excellent fit (CFI = 1.000; RMSEA = 0.000; SRMR = 0.060). The latent variable Env-Perc, combining service satisfaction (VSSS-32) and perceived ward atmosphere (WAS-P), was the only significant predictor of momentary mood (β = 0.344, 95%CI: [0.084;0954], p = 0.033). Conclusions Perceived satisfaction with care and service atmosphere in SA contribute to promoting positive mood among individuals with SSD. Trial registration ISRCTN registry ID ISRCTN21141466, registration date 17 February 2020.

items.title: Webcams can be used to study eye movements during reading.
items.abstract: Eye movements have revealed a wealth of information about how readers process written language. Modern eye trackers can record eye movements in the lab with high accuracy. However, such equipment is expensive, and participant testing is labour-intensive. Kaduk et al. (Behav Res Methods 56(5):5002-5022, 2023) recently reported that webcam eye tracking may be a viable alternative, showing that webcams achieved correlations with laboratory eye trackers of ~0.83 during a free-viewing task. We conducted three experiments to test whether webcams can be used to study eye movements during reading. Participants read short sentences with a target word frequency manipulation while their eye movements were recorded with both an EyeLink system and a webcam in the laboratory (co-registration, Experiments 1 and 2) or online with their own webcam (online study, Experiment 3). In the lab, the webcam-based system recorded raw gaze positions that were highly correlated with the EyeLink (median r = 0.805), replicating Kaduk et al.'s results. We also found evidence for word frequency effects in the webcam data, but there was more noise than in the EyeLink data. In the online study, data quality was much poorer, but we still found reliable effects that were consistent with those observed in the laboratory. In summary, webcam-based eye tracking may be viable for studying reading, especially under laboratory conditions. However, obtaining useful data may require collecting many more observations when using webcams than with high-accuracy eye trackers.

items.title: Self-Care as a Self-Regulatory Process Linking Loneliness and Humor to Mental and Physical Health in Older Adults.
items.abstract: Psychosocial experiences such as loneliness and humor are associated with health in later life, but less is known about their relationship with everyday self-care. This study examined whether self-care was associated with mental and physical health beyond emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor and whether self-care statistically accounted for indirect associations between these psychosocial factors and health-related quality of life in older adults. A cross-sectional community-based sample of 675 adults aged 60-99 years completed measures of emotional loneliness, self-enhancing humor, self-care, and health-related quality of life. Meaning and Life Purpose was examined separately as an exploratory predictor. Hierarchical regression models adjusted for age and sex were followed by bootstrapped indirect-effect analyses with 5000 resamples. Sensitivity analyses used overlap-reduced self-care scores to address potential conceptual and item-level overlap among measures. The self-care composite was strongly positively associated with both mental (r = 0.692) and physical health (r = 0.700; both p < 0.001). In hierarchical models, self-care added 13.7% and 15.3% of explained variance in mental and physical health, respectively, yielding final R2 values of 0.529 and 0.526. In the final models, self-care remained positively associated with mental (β = 0.515, p < 0.001) and physical health (β = 0.545, p < 0.001), while emotional loneliness remained negatively associated with both outcomes. Bootstrapped analyses showed significant indirect associations through self-care for emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor in relation to both health outcomes. These associations remained statistically supported in conservative overlap-reduced sensitivity analyses. Exploratory indirect associations involving Meaning and Life Purpose were not robust to sensitivity analyses. Self-care was strongly associated with perceived mental and physical health and accounted for statistically supported indirect associations linking emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor with health outcomes. The findings identify self-care as a potentially important behavioral intermediary in later life, while the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about temporal or causal mechanisms. Longitudinal research is needed to determine the direction and developmental course of these relationships.

items.title: Evaluating methods for testing publication bias in meta-analyses with confounding covariates: A simulation study.
items.abstract: Selective publication of favorable results can bias meta-analytic estimates and threaten the validity of meta-analyses. Many methods that detect and adjust for publication bias perform poorly under substantial between-study heterogeneity. Heterogeneity complicates publication bias assessment because study characteristics may be associated with both effect size estimates and standard errors. These characteristics can induce an effect-precision association that regression-based diagnostics may misattribute to selective publication when such characteristics are omitted. However, it remains unclear how best to incorporate these confounding characteristics across methods and how their performance varies with confounding level, selective publication, residual heterogeneity, and the number of studies. To address this gap, I conduct an extensive Monte Carlo simulation evaluating Egger-type regression tests, residual-based tests, and a likelihood-ratio test of the three-parameter selection model (3PSM) under the one-step p value selection mechanism. Results show that when confounding covariates were ignored, Egger-type regression tests and residual analyses exhibited inflated Type I error rates, whereas the 3PSM likelihood-ratio test maintained near-nominal, albeit slightly inflated, Type I error rates across conditions. When confounding covariates were incorporated, Egger-type tests had well-calibrated Type I error rates, residual analyses based on residualizing effect sizes alone tended to be conservative, and the 3PSM test showed slight inflation. Nevertheless, 3PSM consistently yielded higher power than other methods. Overall, the findings suggest that Egger-type regression tests and 3PSM can be used as complementary analyses for assessing selective publication when confounding covariates are present.

items.title: Public responses to biodiversity loss terminology and crisis framing.
items.abstract: To avoid the technical term "biodiversity loss", public communications often refer to "nature loss" or "extinction of plants and animals" or apply crisis framing by stating "biodiversity crisis," "nature crisis," or "extinction crisis." To assess public responses to these terms, we conducted a randomized survey experiment with 7338 U.S. adults. Participants were randomly assigned to one term (biodiversity loss, nature loss, extinction of plants and animals, biodiversity crisis, nature crisis, or extinction crisis), either alone or in the context of an explanation and photos of plants and animals. With and without context, "biodiversity loss" and "biodiversity crisis" received the lowest ratings of familiarity, concern, perceived urgency, and conservation support. "Extinction of plants and animals" generally received the highest ratings. "Nature loss" performed similarly to this term when context was provided. Crisis framing had little to no effect. Terminology effects were strongest for political Independents. We discuss implications for public communications.

items.title: Altered language network microstructure links with impaired language function and development in very preterm/very low birth weight born adults.
items.abstract: Premature birth is associated with impaired language function. In premature-born children, language function has been linked with microstructural alterations of the language network.Whether these brain-language associations persist into adulthood remains unclear. We investigated the microstructural properties of major dorsal and ventral language pathways in very preterm/very low birth weight (VPT/VLBW) adults and their associations with language performance in adulthood and childhood. Sixty-three VPT/VLBW and eighty full-term-born adults (mean age 26.8 years) underwent diffusion-weighted imaging and language assessment. The arcuate fasciculus, superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus were reconstructed using probabilistic tractography from which fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) measures were extracted. Adult language function was assessed via the Regensburg word fluency test, rapid automatized naming and verbal IQ; childhood language was assessed at the mean age of 8 using the Kaufman Assessment Battery for children. We observed altered language network microstructure in VPT/VLBW participants, illustrated by lower FA and higher MD in the SLF and UF. These microstructural alterations were associated with language function in adulthood, but also with language development in childhood. We found that the association between tract microstructure and language abilities differed between groups. Our results demonstrate altered language network microstructure in premature born adults, which links with impaired language function and development. These findings extend previous work by comprehensively characterizing the adult dorsal and ventral language network and relating its microstructural properties to language function across development. The selective follow-up sample may limit generalizability to the broader VPT/VLBW population.

items.title: Statistical Learning of Feature-Spatial Mappings and Its Modulation by Cue-Induced Expectation.
items.abstract: Visual statistical learning enables individuals to extract regularities from the environment, thereby optimizing attentional allocation. Previous research has mainly focused on unidimensional location or feature probability learning, leaving unclear whether individuals can acquire multidimensional mappings between target features and high-probability spatial locations, and how cue-induced expectations modulate the neural expression of such mappings. We employed a location probability paradigm combined with multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) and recorded EEG. Reaction times showed a significant gradient from the feature-matched high-probability location to the low-probability location, indicating successful acquisition of feature-spatial mappings under both cue conditions. The N2pc did not reliably differentiate the two high-probability location conditions, providing no detectable evidence of feature-dependent modulation of early lateralized selection. Predictive cues elicited brief pretarget alpha lateralization toward the cue-associated HPTL. Search-array-locked MVPA discriminated feature-matched from feature-mismatched HPTL trials under both cue conditions, with stronger decoding under predictive cueing. These findings show that learned feature-spatial regularities were expressed behaviorally and in distributed neural activity, and that predictive cues modulated their neural expression before and after search-array onset.

items.title: Co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences among adolescents: The predictive role of sleep disturbance.
items.abstract: Background Internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are common among adolescents. However, few studies have explored the longitudinal co-development of internalizing symptoms and PLEs in this age group. Methods A total of 7529 adolescents (M age at baseline = 13.89 years, SD = 1.34; 50% girls) participated in this three-wave longitudinal study. A parallel-process latent class growth analysis identified joint trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs, and multinomial logistic regression examined the effect of sleep disturbance. Results Three distinct trajectories were identified: a low-risk group (74.0%), a pure-internalizing symptoms group (13.5%), and a chronic co-occurring group (12.5%). After controlling for sample characteristics, negative life events during follow-up, and sleep duration, baseline sleep disturbance was significantly associated with both the pure-internalizing symptoms trajectory (OR = 3.41, 95% CI = 2.84-4.08) and the chronic co-occurring trajectory (OR = 3.69, 95% CI = 3.06-4.46). Conclusions These findings indicate that sleep disturbance independently associated with the heterogeneous co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs. Early assessment and treatment of sleep disturbance may be an important strategy for the prevention and intervention of psychopathology development.

items.title: Emotion regulation diversity and depressive symptoms in mid- to older adulthood: A longitudinal investigation.
items.abstract: Depression is associated with emotion regulation (ER) impairments. ER diversity has been proposed as novel measure of the diversity of the ER repertoire and has been linked to clinical depression status cross sectionally. A more diverse ER repertoire, particularly under stressful circumstances, may protect against depressive symptom elevation longitudinally. This study used a longitudinal design to examine the within- and between-person associations between ER diversity, stress, and depression in mid- to later life adults. ER strategy use, perceived stress, and depressive symptoms were assessed. A series of linear mixed effects models were fit. As expected, ER diversity did not systematically change over the course of 10 years. Importantly, perceived stress moderated the ER diversity - depression association between individuals. Specifically, for individuals experiencing moderate to high levels of perceived stress, higher ER diversity was associated with lower depressive symptom levels. This moderation effect was observed consistently across baseline age and was not influenced by aging longitudinally. Thus, a diverse ER repertoire under stress may protect against depressive symptom elevation in mid- to later-life adults.

items.title: Towards semantic brain-computer interfacing: The graded inventory of semantic triggers (GIST) paradigm.
items.abstract: Objective Semantic Brain-Computer Interfaces (sBCIs) aim to decode conceptual information directly from neural activity, enabling more efficient and natural communication for individuals with severe motor impairments. However, existing approaches are often confounded by stimulus-driven perceptual processes and lack a reliable means of tagging the moment of concept formation. We introduce the Graded Inventory of Semantic Triggers (GIST), a novel electroencephalography (EEG) paradigm designed to elicit semantic retrieval from graded verbal clues with precise temporal alignment. Approach: EEG data were recorded from 14 participants performing the GIST task across three semantic categories (food, musical instruments, and body parts). Target neural activity was aligned to each participant's self-reported moment of semantic retrieval (spacebar press), enabling response-locked analysis. Here, we propose a staged framework where the first comprises a Conformer-based encoder trained on pooled data using a hybrid contrastive objective that combines instance-level consistency and cross-participant class alignment with domain-adversarial learning to reduce participant-specific information. In the second stage, the frozen encoder is transferred to a held-out participant whose data played no part in Stage 1, and a support vector machine is calibrated on that participant's own labelled items under a nested leave-one-item-out protocol. Results: Above-chance semantic decoding was achieved in all three pairwise tasks. Mean accuracies were 73.4% (Body vs. Food), 70.7% (Body vs. Music), and 68.2% (Food vs. Music). Participant-level permutation tests were significant in 9/11 participants for Body vs. Food and 8/11 for each of the other tasks (p < 0.05). The pre-response interval at [-1.5s, -0.5s] was the most discriminative. Significance: The GIST paradigm enables controlled elicitation and temporal alignment of semantic processing while reducing perceptual confounds. Combined with cross-participant representation pretraining and participant-specific calibration, the results demonstrate above-chance decoding of semantic categories from EEG in individuals excluded from representation learning, supporting the feasibility of sBCIs.

items.title: Barriers and facilitators to informal caregiving in Rhode Island: A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Informal caregivers are instrumental in supporting the activities of older adults; however, caregiving can negatively impact caregivers' health. This qualitative study explored the experiences, support, and unmet needs of informal caregivers of older adults (n = 12) in Rhode Island. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed and analyzed through a thematic analysis approach. Identified themes were categorized into three domains: 1) Health Services Challenges for Care Recipients, 2) Negative Impact on Caregivers, and 3) Caregiver Coping Strategies and Challenges. Results indicate that informal caregivers often struggled to access health services and experienced significant disruptions in their lives, ultimately taking a toll on their health and well-being. Finding meaning through caregiving for loved ones and home self-care practices, such as yoga, helped caregivers cope with personal challenges. Findings suggest the need for tailored interventions to better support caregivers throughout the caregiving process.

items.title: Pointing at communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor skills in preterm and full-term infants at 18 months.
items.abstract: Preterm birth represents a risk for vulnerability across neurodevelopmental domains. However, its impact on early communication and cross-domain associations remains underexplored. This study compared preterm and full-term infants at 18 months on communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor abilities, and examined associations between pointing and these skills. Thirty-nine preterm and 28 full-term infants participated. Pointing (hand, index), vocal productions (vocalizations, babbling, words), and expression modalities (unimodal gestural, unimodal vocal, bimodal gestural-vocal) were elicited using the "decorated room" task and coded with ELAN. Cognitive, language (receptive, expressive), and motor (fine, gross) abilities were assessed with the BSID-III. Preterm infants produced fewer index points, babbling, and bimodal expressions, and showed lower scores across all BSID-III scales. Only in preterm infants, index pointing significantly correlated with developmental scores, particularly cognitive and fine-motor ones. Findings highlight interconnected cross-domain developmental trajectories in the preterm population, with index pointing as a key developmental marker at 18 months.

items.title: Exploring pathways between childhood parental abuse and adulthood generalized anxiety disorder: The roles of neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness.
items.abstract: Childhood parental abuse is an established risk factor for adulthood generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), but the personality mechanisms explaining this pathway are underinvestigated. Based on developmental psychopathology and triple vulnerability models, this study evaluated whether neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness mediated the 18-year prospective paths from maternal and paternal abuse to adulthood GAD severity. Each abuse source was tested independently. Community adults (N = 3293) (M age = 45.61 years, standard deviation [SD] = 11.41, range = 20-86; 54.95% women; 89.7% non-Hispanic White) participated in three Midlife Development in the United States (MIDUS) study waves. A parallel latent variable mediation analysis estimated all three personality traits as mediators. Covariate-adjusted analyses controlled for age, sex, race, education, and body mass index (BMI). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) and residualized-change models differentiated trait-level from within-person effects. Greater maternal, but not paternal, abuse significantly predicted higher neuroticism, which, in turn, significantly mediated the path to GAD symptoms (B = 0.051, p = .008). This effect remained significant after covariate adjustment and in unadjusted and covariate-adjusted RI-CLPMs (Bs = 0.074 and 0.060, ps < .001), though paternal abuse showed a smaller effect. Change-based mediation was attenuated (B = 0.007, p = .014). Conscientiousness and extraversion did not mediate any path. Neuroticism mediated the 18-year path from childhood maternal abuse to GAD symptoms, mainly via trait-level differences, but pre-existing personality differences are still potential confounders. Neuroticism-focused prevention approaches, possibly optimized via transdiagnostic strategies, require assessment.

items.title: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Driving is a cognitively demanding task that involves the continuous integration of attention, executive control, visual processing, and motor coordination. Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may disrupt these functions and affect driving performance during recovery. Driving simulation is increasingly used to examine post-mTBI driving performance, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in simulator platforms, task designs, and outcome selection. This scoping review characterized driving simulation methodologies used to assess post-mTBI driving performance and examined patterns of mTBI-related findings across reported outcomes. A systematic search of seven electronic databases identified 12 eligible publications between 2017 and 2026. Publications were synthesized by participant characteristics, time since injury, simulator platform, task demands, and outcomes. Across publications, mTBI-related findings were most frequently reported for vehicle control metrics, particularly lane position variability and speed regulation. mTBI-related differences were most often condition-specific, including differences during curves, hazard events, and manipulated cognitive load or dual-task conditions. Cognitive measures also demonstrated mTBI-related differences and associations to driving performance, particularly those assessing executive functioning and processing speed domains. Differences were observed across all post-injury intervals, including ≥ 15 days, with a small number of related publications reporting performance differences after symptom resolution. However, the predominantly cross-sectional evidence does not establish whether these differences persist over time within the same individuals. Findings suggest that driving simulation can provide a useful controlled method for examining functional driving performance following mTBI across varying road environments and task demands. Future work should prioritize standardizing simulator outcomes and validating simulator performance against on-road, naturalistic-driving, and crash-related outcomes.

items.title: Creating safer social media environments for body image: Evidence and research priorities for multilevel interventions.
items.abstract: Public, policy, and research interest is growing in interventions that create safer social media environments for body image. Although intervention efforts have primarily focused on helping individuals critically evaluate or manage social media, users' experiences are also shaped by parents, peers, influencers, advertisers, social norms, platform systems, and government regulation. This paper applies a social ecological framework to review emerging approaches across intrapersonal, interpersonal, organisational, community, and public-policy levels. At the intrapersonal level, media literacy, temporary reductions in use, and feed curation have produced mixed, though sometimes promising, effects. Evidence for interventions involving parents, educators, peers, and influencers remains limited, despite their potential to shape young people's social media practices and the content they encounter. Similarly, advertising labels have generally failed to protect body image, while more substantive changes to advertising content, platform design, recommendation systems, and social norms have rarely been evaluated. The effects of rapidly emerging policies and regulations on body image are also largely unknown. We identify priorities for developing and evaluating interventions at each level, including stakeholder co-design, ecologically valid trials, longer follow-ups, objective assessment of content exposure and engagement, and careful monitoring of unintended effects. Individual-level strategies remain important but cannot address the broader systems that produce and reinforce appearance pressures. Coordinated interventions across multiple ecological levels are needed to create meaningful and sustained improvements in social media environments.

items.title: Awareness of anchoring: Intentional processes contribute to anchoring effects.
items.abstract: Judgments and decisions are highly susceptible to influence from reference points. Anchoring effects arise when a benchmark is provided prior to estimation of a target quantity, and are observed even when the anchor is ostensibly shown to be randomly generated. It is commonly assumed that anchoring is automatic and unavoidable, but very little research has directly investigated this assumption. We report five studies aiming to characterize individuals' awareness of anchors and their effects. High proportions of participants indicated that knowing an anchor would improve their estimates (Studies 1 and 3), and desired to view an ostensibly random anchor - indicating that they would use it to inform their own absolute estimates (Study 2). Anchoring was stronger for participants who indicated that they intended to use (Studies 2 and 3) or reported having used (Study 5) the anchor value to inform their estimate. We also replicated and extended a previous demonstration that anchors have a reduced effect when they are judged to be poor estimates of the target quantity (Studies 1, 3, 4). Although anchoring was not eliminated in participants who reported that they did not intend to use the anchor, or judged it to be a poor estimate, the results overall suggest a substantial explanatory role for intention and awareness in the generation of anchoring effects.

items.title: The unique contributions of negative emotionality and sleep problems to toddlers' physiological stress response.
items.abstract: Previous research has examined temperament and sleep separately with respect to their relationship to young children's physiological stress response; however, little research has jointly investigated these two constructs in relation to children's physiological stress response. Previous research also has not considered the potential contributions of individual components of children's negative emotionality to their stress response. In the present study, mothers reported on children's negative emotionality and sleep problems when children were 18 and 24 months old respectively. When children were 30 months old, saliva samples were collected prior to and after the stranger approach task to assess physiological stress response as measured by total cortisol secretion (AUCg) and cortisol reactivity (AUCi). Results showed that frustration was positively associated with AUCg. Frustration and sleep problems were also both positively associated with AUCi, and shyness was negatively associated with AUCi. No other dimensions of negative emotionality were related to AUCg or AUCi. These results highlight the unique contributions of toddlers' temperament and sleep difficulties to their stress physiology. Furthermore, these results highlight the importance of parsing out the individual components of negative emotionality when conducting temperament research on children's stress response.

items.title: Sleep in the first three years of life: Age-related patterns and predictors in a South African sample.
items.abstract: Sleep is integral to early neurodevelopment and health, yet most normative data derive from high-income, global North populations. Context-specific data from sub-Saharan Africa, and South Africa in particular, remain scarce. This study describes sleep patterns across the first three years of life in a South African sample and examines caregiver and child characteristics associated with variation in sleep outcomes. A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 340 South African caregivers of children aged 0-36 months. Sleep was assessed using items from the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised. Several sleep outcomes were examined across six age bands. One-way ANOVAs examined age-related differences, and multiple linear regression analyses identified caregiver and child correlates of sleep. Significant age-related differences were observed for total sleep duration, nighttime consolidation, and daytime sleep, with large effect sizes for daytime sleep. Bedtime, bedtime consistency, and sleep onset latency remained similar across the six age groups (0-3-25-36 months). Child age was the most consistent predictor of sleep outcomes. Caregiver unemployment was associated with shorter and less consolidated nighttime sleep. Second-born or later children showed more frequent night wakings and greater daytime napping. Intermediate temperament was associated with longer sleep onset latency. Age-related differences in sleep patterns during the first three years are broadly consistent with international findings, though aspects of sleep timing appear more contextually shaped. Findings provide preliminary data for South Africa and highlight the need for age-stratified, culturally sensitive sleep guidance and interventions.

items.title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Processes in Transgender and Gender Diverse Adults with Chronic Physical Illnesses: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) adults experience high rates of chronic physical illnesses (CPIs) and mental health difficulties, yet little is known about the psychosocial processes underlying this relationship. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the literature examining psychosocial factors associated with mental health among TGD adults living with CPIs. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Eligible qualitative and quantitative studies that investigated psychosocial processes and mental health outcomes among TGD adults with CPIs were included. Twenty-five studies met the eligibility criteria. Most were cross-sectional and focused on transgender women living with HIV. Minority stress-related experiences, including stigma, discrimination, trauma, and violence, were consistently associated with depression, anxiety, psychological distress, poorer quality of life, and reduced healthcare engagement. In contrast, social support, community connectedness, resilience, coping, mindfulness, and spirituality emerged as important protective factors. Few studies examined CPIs beyond HIV or biophysiological processes. Overall, the evidence highlights the central role of minority stress in shaping mental health among TGD adults with CPIs while revealing substantial gaps regarding diverse TGD populations, non-HIV chronic illnesses, and transdiagnostic and biopsychosocial mechanisms that should be prioritized in future research.

items.title: Parental Smartphone Use and Children's Emotional Well-Being in Everyday Family Life: Experience Sampling Study.
items.abstract: Over the past decade, smartphones have become an integral part of family life, shaping both daily routines and parent-child interactions. Although parental smartphone use in the presence of children is frequently framed as harmful through concepts such as phubbing and technoference, these constructs emphasize disruptive smartphone use and may bias interpretations toward negative effects. Moreover, most previous research has relied on cross-sectional self-report data, limiting insight into how parental smartphone use relates to children's well-being in everyday life. This study examined the associations between parental smartphone use in the presence of the child and children's affective well-being, as well as perceived threats to children's fundamental needs, using both self-reported and device-logged measures of smartphone use. Individual parents (N=131) participated in a 10-day daily diary study. Each evening, parents reported their smartphone use in the presence of a selected target child, their child's positive and negative affect, and perceived threats to their child's fundamental psychological needs. In addition, Android users who provided consent installed a mobile sensing app that continuously recorded objective smartphone use throughout the study period. Multilevel models were used to examine both within-person (day-to-day fluctuations) and between-person associations separately for mothers and fathers while controlling for day of study, weekday vs weekend, and daily working hours. Higher parental smartphone use was largely unrelated to children's affective well-being. However, mothers who, on average, reported greater overall smartphone use perceived greater threat to their child's fundamental needs. Similarly, on days when fathers reported using their smartphones more than usual, they also perceived greater threats to their child's fundamental needs. In regard to positive affect, no significant associations were found for children's positive affect perceived by their parents, indicating that parents who, on average, used their smartphones more frequently around their child did not report lower child positive affect. Regarding negative affect, fathers who reported higher overall smartphone use also reported higher child negative affect. Additionally, on days when mothers used their smartphone more than usual, they perceived their child as displaying more negative affect. None of these associations emerged when parental smartphone use was assessed using device-logged data. Taken together, these findings suggest that perceived child need threat may be linked to parents' subjective perceptions and interpretations of their smartphone use rather than to their digitally traced smartphone behavior. This discrepancy underscores the importance of distinguishing between subjective and objective assessments of parental smartphone use and highlights the need for future research that integrates children's perspectives and interactional context to clarify when and how parental smartphone use may impact children's well-being.

items.title: Multiple Sessions of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Combined With Squat Training Improve Lower-Limb Maximum Strength in Healthy Adult Men.
items.abstract: Yan, X, Zuo, Z, Nitsche, MA, Zhang, X, and Qi, F. Multiple sessions of transcranial direct current stimulation combined with squat training improve lower-limb maximum strength in healthy adult men. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to investigate the effects of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with Squat training (ST) on lower-limb maximum strength in healthy adult men. Sixty men (age: 21.6 ± 2.1 years, height: 177.5 ± 5.3 cm, body mass: 73.1 ± 7.4 kg) were randomly assigned to 4 groups (tDCS + ST group, sham tDCS + ST group, tDCS + rest group, sham tDCS + rest group). The 6-week intervention program was implemented with biweekly sessions, totaling 12 treatment sessions, each separated by a minimum 48-hour interval. After the tDCS intervention, the ST groups performed squat exercises while the tDCS + rest and sham tDCS + rest groups sat quietly for 30 minutes. Lower-limb maximal muscle strength was measured at 4 distinct time points: preintervention (T0), 24 hours post-third week intervention (T1), 24 hours post-sixth week final session (T2), and 1 week post-entire intervention completion (T3). Key evaluation metrics were measured, including 1 repetition maximum (1RM) squat, knee extensor and flexor peak torque, and rectus femoris cross-sectional area (CSA). Significant improvements in 1RM, knee extensor strength, and nondominant rectus femoris CSA were observed in both tDCS + ST and sham tDCS + ST groups compared with the sham tDCS-only group (p < 0.05). No differences in knee strength, 1RM, or rectus femoris CSA were observed between the tDCS + rest and sham tDCS + rest groups. The results indicate that anodal tDCS combined with ST does not yield additional training benefits on lower-limb maximal strength in healthy adults when compared with ST alone.

items.title: Network Analysis of Depressive Symptoms Among Chinese Older Adults Across Different Intergenerational Support Patterns.
items.abstract: BackgroundIntergenerational support plays a crucial role in mental health in later life, yet both the heterogeneity of support patterns and the symptom-level interplay among depressive symptoms remain underexplored.MethodsUsing data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS 2020, N = 7,444), Latent Class Analysis (LCA) identified intergenerational support patterns. Network analysis and the Network Comparison Test (NCT) were utilized to estimate and compare depressive symptom networks (CESD-10) across subgroups.ResultsThree patterns emerged: Distant-Supportive (55.9%), Proximate-Interactive (24.2%), and Traditional Co-resident (19.9%). While "sadness" and "being bothered" were universal core symptoms, NCT revealed distinct structural disparities. The Proximate-Interactive group exhibited a uniquely strong "bothered-fearful" connection. The Distant-Supportive group showed pronounced "effort-cannot get going" pathways, whereas the Traditional Co-resident group displayed a stronger "bothered-trouble focusing" link.ConclusionsIntergenerational support patterns are not only associated with overall depression severity but also with differences in the network topology of depressive symptoms. Differentiated interventions tailored to specific family structures are essential for geriatric mental health.

items.title: An interpretable machine learning model integrating mucosal and cellular immunity to predict SARS-CoV-2 reinfection: a multicenter cohort study.
items.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4+ central memory T cells (TCM) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4+ TCM cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.

items.title: Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine Use Among U.S. Children: National Health Interview Survey 2012 and 2022.
items.abstract: A recent report of traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM) utilization by U.S. children found increased usage across 2007, 2012, and 2022 by age, sex, and race/ethnicity. Here, we examine cross-sectional changes between 2012 and 2022 in detail by TCIM approach and sociodemographic and health characteristics, including reports of asthma, depression, diabetes, and pain, in U.S. children aged 4-17 years. We examined overall TCIM use, use of practitioner-based TCIMs (TCIM directly provided by practitioners) and use of nonpractitioner TCIMs (TCIM not directly provided by practitioners). National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) in 2007, 2012, 2017, and 2022 asked questions on TCIM, but analyses were limited to 2012 and 2022 as they had the most comparable wording. Prevalence and variance estimates were calculated using Proc Survey Procedures in SAS software version 9.4 to account for NHIS's complex sample design. When using the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, we found that utilization among U.S. children increased from 6.4% in 2012 to 17.8% in 2022, largely driven by use of nonpractitioner-based TCIMs, which rose from 3.2% to 14.0%. Among those using practitioner-based TCIM, use specifically for pain management increased from 28.7% to 47.6%. In both years, children who were non-Hispanic, White, Female, from families with at least one college-educated adult, and reporting current depression or asthma were more likely to utilize any TCIM. Based on the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, U.S. children are increasingly utilizing TCIMs, particularly nonpractitioner approaches, mirroring similar increases in TCIM use by U.S. adults. Given the fast pace of TCIM adoption by children in the United States, future research examining the downstream impacts of these changes is warranted.

items.title: Disease-specific body composition patterns in children with cerebral palsy and spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cerebral palsy (CP) are severe neurological conditions characterized by neurodegeneration and non-progressive brain injury, respectively, both profoundly affecting the nutritional status in children. This observational study aimed to comprehensively assess and compare anthropometry and body composition across groups of children with SMA, CP, and healthy controls (HCs). We enrolled three age- and sex-matched groups of 40 children each: CP (Gross Motor Function Classification System IV-V), SMA (Types I-II), and HC. Anthropometry, skinfolds, and circumferences were collected, and relative z-score was calculated. Body fat percentage (BF%) was estimated using the Slaughter equation; fat mass index (FMI), fat-free mass (FFM), and FFM Index (FFMI) were calculated. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and robust linear regression were performed adjusting for sex, age, body mass index z-score (BMIz), epilepsy, feeding via, ventilation, and pharmacological treatment. BMIz was significantly lower in children with neurological impairment than in HC, with no difference between CP and SMA (HC: 0.04 [-0.5; 0.6]; CP: -1.8 [-4.3; -0.6]; SMA: -3.0 [-4.7; -1.2], p < 0.0001). After adjustments, SMA group showed 17.02% higher BF% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 8.27-25.78; p = 0.0003) and higher FMI (+1.37; 95% CI: 0.98-3.75; p = 0.001), compared to CP. When referenced to HC, FMI was higher in SMA and lower in CP. Lastly, SMA showed lower FFMI compared to both CP and HC. SMA is characterized by higher BF% and a marked deficit in FFM compared to CP, independently of BMIz, epilepsy, feeding via, and pharmacological treatment. Neurological impairments are associated with distinct body composition patterns, highlighting the need for personalized nutritional assessment.

items.title: Cumulative work duration and multisystem health burdens among informal sandstone workers in Thailand.
items.abstract: BackgroundInformal sandstone workers are exposed to multiple occupational hazards, yet evidence on their combined multisystem health effects remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine associations of cumulative work duration, occupational factors, and health behaviors with musculoskeletal, respiratory, dermatologic, and auditory symptoms among informal sandstone workers.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 92 informal sandstone workers in Northeastern Thailand. Data were collected using structured interviews covering demographic, behavioral, occupational, and health characteristics. Cumulative work duration was calculated from years of employment, months worked per year, and daily working hours. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with system-specific symptoms.ResultsMusculoskeletal symptoms were the most prevalent (89.1%), followed by respiratory (60.9%), auditory (47.8%), and dermatologic symptoms (41.3%). High cumulative work duration was significantly associated with musculoskeletal symptoms (aOR = 6.21, 95% CI = 1.02-37.76). Male workers had lower odds of respiratory symptoms compared with female workers (aOR = 0.20, 95% CI = 0.06-0.68). Higher noise sensitivity scores were significantly associated with auditory symptoms (aOR = 3.65, 95% CI = 1.73-7.70).ConclusionsCumulative occupational workload, sex differences, and noise sensitivity were associated with multisystem health symptoms among informal sandstone workers. Integrated occupational health interventions are needed to reduce long-term health risks in informal quarry settings.

items.title: Perception and satisfaction of injured workers toward rehabilitation services: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundWork-related injuries pose significant physical, psychological, and economic burdens on workers, their families, and society. Rehabilitation and return-to-work (RTW) programs are essential for recovery and reintegration into the workforce. However, little is known about injured workers' perceptions of and satisfaction with rehabilitation services in Jordan.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore and compare the perceptions and satisfaction of injured employees with rehabilitation services offered by the Social Security Corporation (SSC) and evaluate their outcomes of returning to work (RTW).MethodsThis cross-sectional survey evaluated perceptions and outcomes of return-to-work and satisfaction of a random sample of injured employees in Jordan in 2022. Phone interviews were conducted by trained interviewers using a five-part questionnaire on injury and rehabilitation experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential tests, including independent t-tests, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.ResultsA total of 400 injured workers were surveyed. The mean age of the respondents was 36.1 ± 10.3 years, with the majority being males (92.5%) and married (70.3%). Less than half (46.8%) received rehabilitative services. The type and cause of injury were strongly correlated with receiving rehabilitation (p < 0.001). The mean perception rating was 3.89 ± 0.49 (out of 5), and the mean satisfaction rating among those who underwent rehabilitation was 4.52 ± 0.53. Perception was significantly higher among higher-income workers and workers who had rehabilitation services. There was a positive correlation between perception and satisfaction (r = 0.328, p < 0.001). In general, 87.5% of those who were injured returned to work.ConclusionMost injured workers successfully returned to work and expressed generally positive perceptions of SSC rehabilitation services. Enhancing awareness among employers and employees about the value and benefits of rehabilitation could further improve understanding, engagement, and utilization of these services among injured workers.

items.title: Phenology drives rice-fall armyworm interactions and arthropod community dynamics through foliar volatile signaling.
items.abstract: Background Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are one of the key mediators of plant-insect interactions. Although several studies have examined the factors affecting volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions, the role of phenology in determining the effects of volatile emission is less understood, especially in rice. Currently, fall armyworm (FAW, Spodoptera frugiperda) is considered a minor pest in rice; however, changes in climatic conditions and the rapid emergence of pesticide resistance can quickly alter this status. To address this, we examined how plant phenology and FAW herbivory affect foliar volatile emissions and the associated arthropod community dynamics in rice. Results Among the phenological stages (n = 6 per treatment), the vegetative stage emitted significantly more day volatiles than the reproductive stage. FAW herbivory also induced volatile emission in rice. Furthermore, in the Y-tube olfactometer choice assays, FAW larvae preferred volatiles from the vegetative stage and undamaged plants. After normalizing volatile emissions by plant biomass, the most common volatile compounds emitted included diketone alcohol, ethylhexyl benzoate, and ethylhexanol. In the common garden experiment, more arthropods, regardless of their taxonomic status, were attracted to the vegetative stage, although they were not significantly attracted to FAW-damaged plants. In addition, Diptera was the most predominant order observed, irrespective of the treatments. Conclusion Our findings collectively show that phenology is the key driver in mediating volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions in rice. The observed phenology-driven changes in VOC emissions influence differences in arthropod attraction, suggesting ecological consequences in rice-FAW interactions and highlighting the importance of incorporating phenology into sustainable pest management strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Novel but stable endosymbionts have contrasting effects on aphid dispersal and plant feeding damage in the cereal pest Diuraphis noxia.
items.abstract: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid ( Diuraphis noxia ), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. Endosymbiont-mediated changes in feeding damage did not involve the main plant immune response pathways: transinfected and wild type aphids induced similar levels of jasmonic acid, jasmonic acid-isoleucine, and salicylic acid in plant tissues, even though these plant defenses were strongly activated during aphid feeding. Novel endosymbionts can therefore modulate the severity of plant feeding damage by aphids as well as influencing aphid dispersal. Potential applications in controlling pest D. noxia populations are discussed.

items.title: Differential impacts of early, extended-spectrum, and last-resort β-lactams on manure-derived microbiomes and resistomes in an in vitro model.
items.abstract: Understanding the environmental dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is crucial for mitigating its spread and reducing the clinical burden of resistant infections. In a previous study, we demonstrated that copiotrophic enrichment in a medium that stimulates the growth of gut-associated bacteria can reveal clinically associated bacterial populations and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) that are not detected through direct environmental sampling. In the present study, we applied this enrichment approach to poultry manure to examine how β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics (cefotaxime and meropenem) shape the composition and resistance profiles of copiotrophic, gut-like microbial community relative to an earlier β-lactam (ampicillin) and to antibiotic-free controls. Our results show that extended-spectrum and last-resort β-lactams induced more pronounced shifts in microbial diversity, resistome, and mobilome profiles compared to ampicillin. When focusing on specific taxa, such as clinically relevant enteric bacteria and both susceptible and β-lactam-resistant coliforms, differential responses were observed correlating to the antimicrobial range of action. Moreover, cefotaxime and meropenem exerted different effects on the relative abundance of enteric bacteria and plasmids harboring multiple ARGs. Together, these findings underline how the diversity of pathogen and AMR indicators in gut microbiomes may be shaped by different selective pressures imposed by β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics.IMPORTANCEThis study explores how different generations of β-lactam antibiotics shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance in a gut-like in vitro system. Using a metabolically driven synthetic community derived from manure, we found that advanced β-lactams such as cefotaxime and meropenem led to stronger and more specific shifts in both community composition and resistance gene profiles compared to ampicillin. These results emphasize that the ecological impact of antibiotics depends not only on whether bacteria are inhibited but also on the spectrum of activity of each compound. In addition, the system we used provides a simple and controllable way to study interactions among antibiotics, microbial communities, and the resistome. Overall, this work offers a clearer ecological view of how clinically important antibiotics may influence microbiomes and the spread of antibiotic resistance genes.

items.title: Adolescent Digital Engagement and Well-being Patterns Among Spanish Youth: A Data Note on Social Media Use, Mental Health Perceptions, and Digital Well-being (SMARS, 2024)
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of social media platforms among adolescents has generated significant concern about its implications for mental health and digital well-being. In Spain, where social network use is near-universal among minors, this intersection is especially acute given the country’s high rates of psychological disorders among young people. This article describes a dataset generated within the National R&D&i Project “Adolescent Recipients and Creators of Mental Health Content on Social Media” (SMARS, ref. PID2022-141454OB-I00). The dataset provides a comprehensive, multidimensional quantitative record of the digital lives of 1,043 Spanish adolescents aged 12 to 18, collected through a structured online survey administered between April 24 and May 6, 2024. It captures detailed information on platform usage patterns (TikTok and Instagram), content consumption preferences across 20 categories, social perceptions of digital technology impact, and validated digital well-being self-assessments. The instrument incorporates an adapted Social Perception Scale (α = 0.89) and a three-factor Digital Well-being on TikTok Scale (α = 0.79–0.83), validated through Exploratory Factor Analysis. This dataset offers a reusable, platform-specific resource for interdisciplinary research in communication, psychology, sociology, and digital health, enabling comparative studies, gender-differentiated analyses, and evidence-based digital literacy program development.

items.title: Hydrological Conditions Drive Colonial Waterbird Breeding Dynamics in Monsoon-Dependent Wetlands of Southern India.
items.abstract: Wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to environmental variability, but the relative importance of hydrological and climatic drivers of colonial waterbird breeding is poorly understood in landscapes that depend on the tropical monsoon. We investigated the influence of wetland inundation and climatic conditions on the occurrence of nesting, colony abundance and species richness of colonial nesting waterbirds across nine wetlands in Tamil Nadu, India, over three breeding seasons (2022-2023 to 2024-2025). Breeding responses were quantified through systematic field surveys and related to wetland water extent derived from Sentinel-2 imagery and climatic variables obtained from the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. We measured the effects of water extent, temperature, precipitation and wind speed with generalised linear mixed models. A total of 16 colonial nesting waterbird species were recorded. Environmental conditions during the 30-day period preceding surveys consistently provided the strongest explanation of breeding responses. Water extent emerged as the dominant predictor of nesting occurrence, colony abundance and species richness. The nesting probability increased significantly with water extent (β = 1.732, p < 0.001), whereas colony abundance (β = 0.612, p < 0.001) and species richness (β = 0.275, p < 0.001) increased with greater inundation. Maximum temperature negatively affected colony abundance and species richness, whereas precipitation had weaker negative effects and wind speed had no significant effect. Our findings indicate that the main driver of colonial waterbird breeding dynamics in monsoon-dependent wetlands is wetland inundation, while climatic factors exert secondary effects on colony performance and diversity. Securing suitable hydrological conditions will be essential to the conservation of colonial waterbird populations in the face of increasing climatic variability.

items.title: Long-Term Population Dynamics of the Spotted Stem Borer ( Chilo partellus ) in Contrasting Maize Farming Systems Under Variable Climatic Conditions in East Africa.
items.abstract: The spotted stem borer (Chilo partellus) is one of the most destructive pests of maize in sub-Saharan Africa, causing substantial yield losses and threatening food security among smallholder farming communities. This study investigated the long-term relationships between climatic variability and C. partellus incidence across contrasting organic and conventional farming systems in two agroecological zones. Biweekly monitoring observations of C. partellus incidence were summarized quarterly for temporal analyses across four long-term farming systems at Chuka and Thika: conventional high-, organic high-, conventional low-, and organic low-input. The resulting analytical series represented 32 and 28 quarterly positions at Chuka and Thika, respectively. Climatic variables (temperature, rainfall, and relative humidity) were obtained from on-site weather stations. Spearman's rank correlation, cross-correlation, ARIMA/SARIMA time-series models with exogenous climatic predictors (ARIMAX/SARIMAX), and Bayesian generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate climatic associations and farming systems effects. Temperature emerged as the climatic variable most consistently associated with C. partellus incidence, showing significant negative relationships across all farming systems at Chuka and within the organic farming systems at Thika, whereas rainfall and relative humidity exhibited comparatively weak associations. Cross-correlation analyses indicated predominantly contemporaneous and short lag associations (0-2 quarters) between climatic variables and pest incidence. Time-series models were evaluated using descriptive measures of in-sample agreement between observed and fitted values. Across farming systems, R2 values ranged from 0.039 to 0.650, indicating substantial variation in the degree to which the fitted models represented the observed temporal patterns. These measures describe in-sample model fit and should not be interpreted as evidence of out-of-sample predictive or forecasting performance. Bayesian analyses further indicated that C. partellus incidence was higher in the organic than in the conventional high-input systems after accounting for climatic variability, whereas the 95% credible intervals for farming system effects in the low-input systems overlapped zero. Overall, these findings suggest that climatic variability and farming system management are associated with long-term variation in C. partellus incidence. The findings may inform the development of climate-informed pest-monitoring and integrated pest management strategies, while independently validated models would be required before application for pest forecasting under sustainable maize production in East Africa.

items.title: Does (co-)variation between boldness and growth differ between sexes? A nuanced and powerful evaluation of the pace of life hypothesis.
items.abstract: A major goal of behavioral ecology is identifying sources of among-individual variation in behavior. Theory suggests that life history traits and personality should be correlated at the individual level, but despite much attention, it has little support. A potentially crucial aspect influencing life history and personality associations that has been overlooked is sex. Males and females of many species differ in energy requirements, energy allocation, and behavior, suggesting that sex may affect correlations between life history and personality differently; if so, not accounting for sex differences may obscure relationships. We address this possibility by intensive longitudinal sampling of boldness and growth in 66 male and 92 female pillbugs (Armadillidium vulgare) (total N = 158) using novel statistical methods to estimate sex-specific (co-)variances in a single parsimonious model. We found that females and males had similar mean boldness, similar among-individual variation in boldness and in growth rate, but females grew faster than males. We found support for a positive correlation between boldness and growth in males but no correlation in females. Differences in personality-life-history correlations between females and males may be linked to sex-specific reproductive strategies. Given the ubiquity of sex differences in life history and behavior, this sex-specific approach to studying trait integration is likely to provide novel insights in many systems that may have gone unnoticed.

items.title: Empowerment of Islamic Religious Education Teachers through Generative AI Training for the Development of Islamic Value-Based Learning Media at SMP Negeri 35 Medan
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, particularly Generative AI, has created new opportunities for developing innovative, interactive, and contextual learning media. However, many Islamic Religious Education (IRE) teachers still have limited competencies in utilizing this technology as a learning medium while maintaining Islamic values. This Community Service Program (PKM) aimed to improve the competence of IRE teachers at SMP Negeri 35 Medan in utilizing Generative AI to develop creative, effective, and Islamic value-based learning media. The program employed a Participatory Action Learning approach consisting of needs identification, educational sessions, practical training, mentoring, and evaluation. The training involved demonstrations and hands-on practice using various Generative AI platforms, including ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma AI, and Microsoft Copilot, to develop teaching materials, presentations, assessment questions, and visual learning media based on Islamic values. The results indicated an improvement in participants' understanding of Generative AI, enhanced skills in developing digital learning media, and increased awareness of the ethical use of AI from an Islamic perspective. The teachers were able to produce learning media that were more engaging, interactive, contextual, and supportive of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. This program contributed positively to improving teachers' digital literacy while strengthening the integration of technology and Islamic values in the IRE learning process.

items.title: MEASURING CONSCIOUS LEADERSHIP: DEVELOPMENT OF THE TOTAL LEADERSHIP INDEX AS A 100-POINT EXECUTIVE MATURITY ARCHITECTURE
items.abstract: Leadership assessment often oscillates between subjective reputation, outcome-based appraisal and broad competency or style measures. These approaches are valuable, but they do not consistently reveal how senior leaders regulate pressure before decision, sequencing, reflection and institutional speech. This conceptual paper develops the Total Leadership Index (TLI) as a 100-point executive maturity architecture comprising four equally weighted pillars: Decision Stillness and Pressure Containment; Timing and Sequence Discipline; Structured Reflection and Root-Cause Honesty; and Governed Speech and Institutional Consequence. Each pillar contains five behaviorally anchored indicators scored from 0 to 5, producing twenty indicators and a total score from 0 to 100. The model complements personality inventories, transformational, ethical, authentic and servant-leadership scales, competency frameworks, 360-degree feedback and performance scorecards by adding a pre-decisional, evidence-governed maturity lens. Distinctive design features include evidence-before-number scoring, a pillar-profile interpretation rule, an evidence-confidence overlay, multi-source moderation, maturity bands, a provisional balance rule and red-flag safeguards. The paper proposes six testable propositions and a staged validation agenda involving expert content review, item development, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, reliability, criterion and incremental validity, measurement invariance and longitudinal intervention studies. Practical illustrations show how TLI may support executive coaching, succession, crisis review, board oversight and public-sector governance. No empirical findings are claimed; the framework is advanced as a falsifiable research architecture whose weights, thresholds and predictive utility require cross-sector and cross-cultural testing.

items.title: Digital Mental Health Supports for Young People
items.abstract: Young people across the island of Ireland are navigating rising levels of psychological distress in a context marked by long waiting lists, fragmented services, and persistent inequities. Digital mental health supports offer a promising way to expand access, but international and local evidence shows that these tools are often underused when they are not co-produced with young people or tailored to diverse cultural and social realities. As part of the larger Atlantic Futures project, this all-island research study set out to address that gap by engaging young people—particularly those experiencing marginalisation—and the staff who support them to identify needs, evaluate digital tools, and generate evidence to guide implementation. Drawing on scoping reviews, surveys, creative workshops, a co-designed Google Site, and an acceptability and implementation study with a combined number of approximately 150 marginalised young people in the ROI and NI, the project found low awareness of existing digital supports among young people but interest in accessible, relatable, and youth-centred tools. Young people emphasised anonymity, immediacy, and autonomy as key advantages of digital supports but stressed that credibility, cultural relevance, and simplicity are essential for sustained engagement. Tools backed by trusted institutions (e.g., HSE, Action Mental Health) and those reviewed by peers were perceived as most reliable. Youth participants consistently rejected overly clinical, complex, or “school-like” designs, favouring platforms that are intuitive, strengths-based, and personalised. Across methods, young people described mental health challenges rooted in structural pressures—academic stress, financial strain, stigma, discrimination, and rural isolation. Marginalised groups, including Traveller youth, migrants, LGBTQ+ young people, and those with disabilities, reported additional barriers to help-seeking. Digital tools were seen as valuable complements to traditional services, particularly where waiting lists, geography, or stigma limit access. However, young people were clear that digital supports cannot replace human connection; instead, they should form part of blended, flexible pathways that integrate online and offline care. Consultation with service providers echoed these insights, highlighting the need for evidence-based tools, strong data protection, simple navigation, and organisational training to support implementation. They also identified literacy, digital skills, and privacy concerns as barriers for young people, reinforcing the importance of low-threshold, anonymous, and accessible design. The findings from an all-island policy dialogue with key policymakers, service providers and young people underscored the absence of a unified all-island governance framework for youth digital mental health and called for coordinated, youth-led approaches to accreditation, implementation, and participation. Overall, the project demonstrates that co-produced, equity-orientated digital mental health supports can meaningfully enhance access and engagement for young people across Ireland. To maximise impact, future efforts should prioritise youth participation, cultural competence, implementation planning, and cross-sector collaboration. Digital supports must be embedded within broader mental health systems—not treated as standalone solutions—to ensure that all young people can access timely, relevant, and trustworthy care.
