items.title: Beyond Complexity: Evaluating Simple vs. Complex Deep Learning Architectures for Urban Density Mapping
items.abstract: The spatial distribution of population density and land use is a fundamental metric for targeting spatial planning policies under the Sustainable Development Goals. This study presents a comparative evaluation of deep learning architectures for urban density estimation, with an emphasis on spatial generalization. The study was conducted in Jakarta and its surrounding cities (Jabodetabek), a highly heterogeneous region that provides a rigorous setting for evaluating model generalization. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and European Space Agency WorldCover 2020 data were acquired through Google Earth Engine, together with the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and the Normalized Difference Built-up Index to explicitly represent vegetation and built-up characteristics. Quantitative evaluation showed that all deep learning models performed well, with R² exceeding 0.94 in all experiments. The U-Net architecture achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with the lowest mean squared error (MSE = 0.0006954). Notably, the lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) proved to be a highly competitive alternative (MSE = 0.0006998), requiring approximately four times fewer parameters and delivering roughly twice the inference speed of the deeper U-Net and ResNet models. In contrast, complex models such as EfficientNet and ResNet showed diminishing returns in accuracy relative to their design complexity, while classical machine learning baselines (Random Forest and XGBoost) failed to capture spatial configurations robustly. These findings demonstrate that increasing network depth does not necessarily improve performance in spatial fractional regression. Therefore, model selection should balance predictive accuracy against computational and environmental costs. items.title: Decolonized and resistant ecologies: An examination of John Still’s The Jungle Tide
items.abstract: This article focuses on John Still’s ([1930] 1955) novel, The Jungle Tide that describes the impact of the European colonial enterprise on the ecologies of South Asia, specifically on their post-independence predicaments. It examines how even a loyal imperialist like Still was deeply disturbed by the ways in which colonialism initiated the ruinous intersection of racial-capitalism and plantation-monoculture, resulting in the large-scale movement of people for labour, and extensive deforestation programmes that led to the destruction of rainforests, species depletion, and biodiversity loss. The novel provides insights into the ways in which the Sri Lankan forests were destroyed to make way for plantation monoculture while also challenging the prevailing colonial assumptions that legitimized this conversion. This article explores Still’s interrogation of the ideologies of colonial, postcolonial, and neocolonial governance, structural racism, global capitalism, and environmental degradation and how these interconnected forces become imbricated in Sri Lankan and South Asian histories.

items.title: Species composition and assemblages of ichthyoplankton during winter and summer around the Korean Peninsula
items.abstract: Background Understanding the spatial distribution of ichthyoplankton is fundamental for identifying spawning habitats, evaluating recruitment processes, and monitoring changes in marine fish populations. However, previous studies in Korean waters have largely focused on individual coastal regions, limiting nationwide comparisons of assemblage structure. Methods We conducted standardized surveys in February and July 2017 across the Yellow Sea, Korea Strait, East Sea, and Jeju waters. Ichthyoplankton was sampled at 133 stations, with valid samples from 130 stations in February and 133 in July. Species were identified morphologically, with DNA barcoding used for selected specimens requiring confirmation. Results We identified 30 egg taxa and 61 larval taxa in February, and 53 egg taxa and 154 larval taxa in July. Species richness increased markedly in July, and larval assemblages consistently contained more taxa than egg assemblages. Ammodytes japonicus dominated larval abundance in February, whereas Engraulis japonicus dominated both egg and larval abundance in July. Regional differentiation was more apparent in July. Surface temperature and salinity also differed among the four regions. Discussion Differences between February and July were consistent with species-specific spawning periods. Regional differentiation previously reported for fish assemblages in Korean waters was also evident in ichthyoplankton. Because the surveys covered only February and July of a single year, the results do not represent the full seasonal variability of ichthyoplankton assemblages.

items.title: Overcoming insect pest challenges for sustainable rice production in the Americas
items.abstract: Rice production in the Americas has expanded to meet a rising demand, but insect pests continue to threaten yields, grain quality, and farmer incomes. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the major insect pests affecting rice systems across the Americas and evaluates the performance, trade-offs, and complementarities of existing and emerging controls. It describes regional pest complexes, such as rice water weevil in the United States, Hoja Blanca vectors and stem borers in tropical areas, and late-season stink bugs across the continent. It examines how climate change, land use, and trade change invasion risk and pest activity timing. The review examines integrated pest management components: surveillance that blends field/edge scouting with decision-support tools and predictive modeling; cultural and agronomic practices that reduce baseline risk; biological control via parasitoids, predators, and entomopathogens using classical, augmentative, and conservation strategies; and threshold-based chemical control emphasizing resistance management, and residue stewardship. Innovative approaches, including AI-enabled forecasting, genomics-assisted resistance, and RNA interference technologies (RNAi) are also examined, alongside socioeconomic conditions that governing their adoption. Ultimately, the review develops adaptable, research-supported strategies that protect crop yields, preserve natural predators, increase farmers’ incomes, and bolster local food security, while tackling escalating environmental and climate issues through ecological, technological, and socioeconomic dimensions.

items.title: Eco-Environmental, Health and Socio-Economic Perspectives on Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins
items.abstract: Cyanobacteria, or blue-green algae, the first oxygenic photosynthetic organisms on Earth, play indispensable ecological roles as primary producers and drivers of biogeochemical cycles, and are also sources of human food, nutraceuticals, and biotechnological products. However, cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs), intensified by eutrophication and global climate change, threaten water quality, biodiversity, and human health due to their production of diverse secondary metabolites, i.e., taste and odor (T&O) compounds and cyanotoxins. This Special Issue, “Ecology and Toxicology of Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins”, compiles 13 papers from 9 countries that collectively advance our understanding of these issues across multiple scales. Cyanotoxins, including microcystins, cylindrospermopsins, anatoxins, and saxitoxins, can cause various hazards to animals and humans, including systemic toxicity, hepatotoxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, reproductive/developmental toxicity, neurotoxicity, immunotoxicity, and endocrine disruption. CyanoHABs are governed by complex bottom-up and top-down regulation, and blooms and cyanotoxin production are closely linked, but not always consistent/synonymous. Environmental stressors, e.g., phosphorus limitation, cold shock, and grazing pressure, selectively favor toxigenic genotypes, or can increase the cellular cyanotoxin quota, although overall population growth is suppressed. This can be explained by the fact that cyanotoxins can help cyanobacteria to better adapt to environmental stressors. When blooms disperse, demise, or are disrupted by certain interventions, the reduced biomass may increase exposure to dissolved, extra-cellular cyanotoxins if intra-cellular toxins are released faster than they are degraded or removed. We term the uncoupling of biomass and toxicity as the “cyanobacterial biomass–toxicity paradox”. We propose a “3P framework”, i.e., prediction, prevention, and prioritization, for the evidence-based risk management of CyanoHABs and cyanotoxins. We also advocate for more studies using multi-omics and artificial intelligence, as well as multi-disciplinary, multi-sectoral, and multi-stakeholder collaboration under the “One Health” umbrella to translate science into actionable solutions for sustainable development.

items.title: Cascading effects of soil water content on leaf chemistry and damage: implications for plant susceptibility to pests and pathogens in a drier world
items.abstract: Climate change is causing major alterations in precipitation regimes and soil water availability, with far-reaching effects on plant traits. Changes in plant chemistry under drought scenarios are particularly relevant, as they can modulate plant interactions with antagonistic organisms. However, how such changes in plant chemistry affect plant susceptibility to biotic damage remains poorly understood. Here we integrated results from a systematic literature review and a field study in Mediterranean mixed forests to advance our understanding of the cascading effects of reduced soil water content on leaf reserves, defences and damage caused by herbivores and pathogens. The literature review revealed that studies linking soil water content with leaf chemistry and damage remain scarce and reported a variety of direct and indirect relationships between the three components. Nevertheless, most studies found higher leaf damage under drier conditions. Results from our field study also supported that leaf damage increased with decreasing soil water content, a relationship largely mediated by changes in leaf phenolic compounds. In Mediterranean forests, phenolics play a major role in protection against desiccation and UV radiation due to their antioxidant properties, yet certain phenolic compounds can also benefit antagonists. Overall, our findings suggest that leaf damage can increase in a drier climate, forcing tree species to face fundamental trade-offs when protecting themselves from the combined stress imposed by abiotic (drought) and biotic (pests and pathogens) components of global change.

items.title: Parasites as environmental bioindicators and climate-sensitive sentinels in arid ecosystems: a one health synthesis with a focus on Saudi Arabia
items.abstract: Parasites integrate environmental conditions across trophic levels and may therefore provide sensitive, mechanistically interpretable signals of ecosystem change. This narrative synthesis evaluates the potential of parasites and parasite communities as environmental bioindicators and climate-sensitive sentinels, with particular emphasis on arid ecosystems and Saudi Arabia. We integrate evidence from terrestrial, aquatic, marine, and zoonotic systems to examine how warming, drought, hydrological change, salinity, pollution, land-use transformation, and host-mediated vector movement influence parasite occurrence, transmission, phenology, community composition, and contaminant accumulation. The evidence supports two complementary bioindicator functions: accumulation indicators, in which parasites concentrate environmental contaminants, and effect indicators, in which parasite prevalence, phenology, richness, or community structure responds to environmental disturbance. Saudi marine systems provide particularly strong examples, including trace-metal accumulation by acanthocephalans and nematodes, community-level changes associated with habitat degradation, and seasonal transmission of Kudoa sp. in Priacanthus tayenus . Terrestrial and waterborne systems provide additional candidate signals through tick phenology and the distribution of Cryptosporidium and Giardia. However, the current evidence base is dominated by cross-sectional studies, heterogeneous diagnostic methods, and geographically fragmented datasets; consequently, parasites should be regarded as promising candidate sentinels rather than validated early-warning indicators. We identify priority research needs and propose a One Health surveillance architecture integrating standardised parasitological sampling, environmental and meteorological measurements, molecular identification, remote sensing, livestock-movement data, and multivariate community analysis. Long-term, coupled datasets will be essential to distinguish climate-driven signals from concurrent anthropogenic pressures and to translate parasite bioindication from an ecological concept into an operational monitoring tool for arid and peri-arid regions.

items.title: Construction of an agricultural green development indicator system and trend projection for the 15th five-year plan period in Jiangxi Province
items.abstract: Introduction As a central pillar of high-quality agricultural advancement, agricultural green development (AGD) is essential for promoting agricultural and rural modernization and building a strong agricultural province. Methods Focusing on Jiangxi Province—a key traditional agricultural province and a national ecological civilization pilot zone—this study establishes a comprehensive AGD evaluation indicator system covering 18 secondary indicators across five dimensions: resource conservation and efficient utilization, environmental governance of production sites, agricultural ecological restoration, green industrial development, and green technological support. The entropy weight method measures Jiangxi’s AGD level from 2010 to 2025, while the GM(1,1) grey model forecasts its trajectory during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Results The results show that: (1) Jiangxi’s comprehensive AGD index grew steadily from 11.37 to 80.51, with agricultural ecological restoration carrying the largest weight (29.42); (2) the index is projected to reach 86.97 by 2030; all fitted GM(1,1) models have MAPE below 10%, meeting the Grade I accuracy standard. Discussion Although constraints remain, including inadequate hilly mechanization, limited smallholder green production capacity, and difficult non-point source pollution control, future work should strengthen green resource utilization, deepen production-site governance, improve technological support, and optimize incentives to drive the green transition of smallholders.

items.title: Newly planted woodlands improve connectivity for woodland fauna, flora and fungi
items.abstract: Abstract Context Young planted woodlands may only support a small proportion of the biodiversity found in mature woodlands but may play an important role in promoting species movements and enhancing biodiversity due to their emerging structural similarities. Objectives We assessed whether recently planted woodlands increase connectivity between mature woodland patches relative to agricultural fields, and whether responses vary across active (small mammals, ground invertebrates) and passive (plants, fungi) dispersers. Methods We used a multi-taxa natural experiment across paired sites where mature woodlands were either connected by planted woodland or separated by farmland. Movement was quantified using PIT-tagging of small mammals and beetles, pitfall trapping, vegetation surveys, airborne spore traps and soil eDNA metabarcoding. A Bayesian beta-binomial model estimated taxon-specific habitat preferences for dispersal. Results Although we did not detect inter-patch movements, we detected higher movement of wood mice, ground active invertebrates, plants, and fungi into new woodlands relative to agricultural fields, whereas, field voles exhibited minimal movement, and some airborne fungal groups showed reduced movement within planted woodlands. Young woodlands generally supported higher woodland specialist richness, abundance or occurrence than fields but did not support the full complement of species associated with mature woodlands. Conclusions Newly planted woodlands can enhance functional connectivity for multiple woodland associated taxa, but the benefits are taxon specific and shaped by differences in mobility, dispersal mode and establishment requirements. Strategic placement of planted woodland adjacent to existing woodland can improve landscape scale connectivity, further improved by additional habitat development to support more specialised species.

items.title: Enns Entomology Museum Collection (EEM)
items.abstract: The Enns Entomology Museum (EEM) is the insect collection of the University of Missouri, Columbia, Missouri, USA, holding more than 7 million specimens. It preserves pinned, papered, slide-mounted and fluid-preserved insects and other arthropods as a permanent record of biodiversity supporting taxonomy, ecology, agriculture and conservation. Founded in 1874 with Charles V. Riley as its first curator, the collection was renamed in 1980 for entomologist Wilbur R. Enns. Donations totaling nearly five million specimens since 1941, including the Missouri Department of Conservation's statewide aquatic invertebrate samples, have made it the reference collection for the insects of the Ozark Plateau, from which 80–90% of the material originates. Holdings also include type material, papered Odonata, insect galls, fossils, about 35,000 microscope slides, and a wet collection of about 4.5 million aquatic insects.

items.title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

items.title: Quantum-enhanced phase sensitivity in an all-fiber Mach–Zehnder interferometer
items.abstract: Abstract Recent advances in quantum photonics have enabled increasingly robust protocols in optical phase estimation, achieving precisions beyond the standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit. While intrinsic losses hinder the realization of unconditional super-sensitivity, reaching quantum advantage, defined as sensitivity surpassing that of any classical counterpart with identical resources, remains achievable. Here we experimentally demonstrate such an advantage using a fully fibered Mach–Zehnder–type interferometer operating at telecom wavelengths, free of post-selection. The scheme relies on the conversion of polarization-entangled photon pairs, a degree of freedom commonly favored for experimental convenience, into energy–time entanglement, which is particularly well suited for scalable fiber-based sensors. All system imperfections, including asymmetric losses and detector inefficiencies, are accounted for in the Fisher information analysis, yielding a measured quantum advantage of 10%. This result highlights the practicality of compact, alignment-free quantum interferometers for real-world sensing applications.

items.title: The Metallicity Distribution of the Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxy Segue 1
items.abstract: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs; stellar masses M * < 10 5 M ⊙ ) offer unique insights into early chemical evolution in low-mass systems. However, interpreting their metallicity distribution functions (MDFs) has been challenging due to limited spectroscopic samples, especially beyond the red giant branch. We present metallicities from the Ca II K absorption feature, measured from low-resolution ( R ∼ 1000 ) Keck/LRIS spectroscopy of 40 stars in the UFD Segue~1 ( M * ≈ 500 M ⊙ ), including both red giant branch and main-sequence turnoff stars, resulting in a metallicity sample more than six times larger than previously published data for Segue~1. The resulting MDF has an average [Fe/H] = − 2.52 ± 0.10 dex and a dispersion of σ = 0.59 ± 0.06 dex, and is best described by a single Gaussian, with no evidence for multimodal substructure. This is consistent with a continuous, short-duration ($$1~Gyr) episode of star formation and chemical enrichment prior to reionization. The nonzero metallicity spread reaffirms its classification as a galaxy. Segue~1 highlights the rich chemical enrichment histories present even in the least massive galaxies, and underscores the importance of deep spectroscopic follow-up to fully characterize these ancient stellar systems.

items.title: Ultraviolet diversity of Little Red Dots as a probe for direct-collapse black hole ages
items.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) uncovered by the James Webb Space Telescope have been proposed as candidate galaxies hosting embedded accreting direct-collapse black holes (DCBHs), yet the relative ultraviolet (UV) emission of their host galaxy remains highly uncertain and diverse across the population. Using a large-scale cosmological hydrodynamical simulation from the MELI ⊙ RA suite, we investigate the contribution of PopIII stars and accreting DCBHs in LRD candidates at z > 8.5 , in the rest-frame 0.2 − 0.6 μ m band. We find that the UV emission from the host galaxy evolves rapidly over the first ∼ 30 M y r following DCBH formation, reflecting the build-up of stellar mass and metal enrichment. This evolution consists of a rapid transition from initially BH-dominated systems, with negligible stellar mass, low metallicity, and high accretion rates, to progressively more developed hosts in which rapid star formation enhances the UV output and metallicity increases. After ∼ 30 M y r , the stellar continuum typically overwhelms the accreting DCBH contribution, producing bluer colours and more extended stellar distributions. As a result, UV-bright LRDs are predicted to host older DCBHs, have higher gas-phase metallicities, lower BH-to-stellar mass ratios, and lower Eddington ratios. The short-lived nature of the LRD phase places strong constraints on their emergence over cosmic time. Overall, our results suggest that DCBH ages can be constrained from the host galaxy contribution to the UV-optical spectrum of LRDs, relative to that of the accreting DCBH, and support the picture in which a DCBH evolutionary sequence is systematically encoded in emission line properties, gas-phase metallicities, and accretion states.

items.title: Deconfined quantum critical point in a dissipative spin-1/2 chain
items.abstract: Open quantum spin systems offer a previously unexplored route to realizing deconfined quantum criticality. We consider a spin-1/2 $J$-$Q_3$ chain, consisting of an antiferromagnetic (AFM) Heisenberg exchange and a competing multi-spin interaction favoring a valence-bond solid (VBS) state, with each spin component coupled to a bosonic bath. Using non-Abelian bosonization and renormalization-group (RG) analysis, combined with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, we determine the phase diagram and the associated phase transitions of the model. We show that strong dissipation stabilizes an AFM phase for sub-Ohmic, Ohmic, and super-Ohmic baths. Continuous AFM-VBS transitions at finite dissipation are found upon increasing the multi-spin interaction in both the sub-Ohmic and Ohmic regimes. Critical properties are obtained through perturbative RG analysis and QMC simulations. In the Ohmic case, the critical point features spinon deconfinement and emergent O(4) symmetry. In the sub-Ohmic regime, the transition may also involve spinon deconfinement, provided that spinons remain deconfined in the dissipative VBS phase. In addition, in the super-Ohmic regime, we propose a transition from AFM phase to a quasi-long-range ordered phase.

items.title: Multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: Angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
items.abstract: The angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated M1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses, and mass ratios. The angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. Following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. The dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. The degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. Superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. Fourier analysis reveals a characteristic frequency of $\sim 0.6$--$0.7$ kHz, consistent with differential rotation in the remnant and inner disk layers, indicating a dynamical coupling between rotational structure and neutrino emission variability. Finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. The polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron-rich and below equilibrium.

items.title: Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft observations
items.abstract: Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is linked to Mars’ extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar wind, this finding bears on solar–wind interactions at comets and other small bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind–planet coupling at unmagnetized worlds.

items.title: Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) Approach to Physics Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Physics learning in the 21st century requires instructional approaches that develop students’ conceptual understanding while fostering their ability to analyze and make informed decisions regarding complex real-world issues. The Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) approach has emerged as a promising strategy for connecting physics concepts with social and environmental contexts. This study aims to systematically examine the application of the Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) approach in physics learning during the period 2015–2025. Specifically, this study identifies topic trends, learning models, the implementation of the SSI approach, and its impact on the physics learning process. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Data were collected from the ScienceDirect and Google Scholar databases using the keywords "Learning Outcomes", "Physics Learning", and "Socio-Scientific Issues". A total of 22 articles met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final synthesis. The results indicate that climate change is the most frequently addressed topic in implementing the SSI approach in physics learning, with junior high school being the dominant educational level represented in the reviewed studies. Furthermore, the SSI approach has proven effective in improving students' scientific argumentation skills and strengthening their understanding of physics concepts in real-life contexts. These findings suggest that integrating socio-scientific issues into physics learning provides a meaningful and contextual strategy for enhancing science education.

items.title: Identity, individuality and naming
items.abstract: Abstract The philosophical theorem “identity of the indiscernibles” (Leibniz’s law) is inspected from the standpoint of objects of our physical world. Although logically stringent, it suffers from a naïve use of terms such as objects and properties. A modified formulation that takes account of the coupling between objects and state and so matches reality, is proposed. The transition from indiscernibility to eventually individuality can be followed along increasing complexity, which leads to irreversible features and finally to irreproducibilty. This path is also mirrored by the issue of naming and the transition from physical, chemical nomenclature to biological nomenclature and finally personal naming. Personal names, in order for them to be adequate, require individuality and lack of reproducibility.

items.title: Journal of Communication and Information Systems
items.abstract: With the increasing tendency of incorporating technology into environments and activities in everyday life, new methods are being proposed to better integrate devices and mankind.Networks designed for monitoring areas through video and image systems are being implemented in several applications.Recent studies have shown interest from both the academy and industry to integrate wireless surveillance networks with lowcost and long range transmission technologies, such as LoRa (Long Range).With the intention to explore this topic, this work presents the development of a system prototype for intelligent monitoring as a basis to future implementation of low-cost LoRabased Wireless Image Sensor Networks (WISN).The developed system consists of a processing unit, a data routing interface and multiple sensor nodes.Its operation is autonomous and initiated through the detection of human presence, by the sensor node, capturing an image of the individuals present at each detection.The data is transmitted through LoRa devices to the central hub, where python-based methods of facial detection and recognition are employed.Several tests were performed to both adjust the system and to verify its efficiency.The results achieved indicate the viability of the proposed low-cost LoRa-based WISN.

items.title: Are cortical microcircuits optimized for information flux?—A simulation-based reverse engineering study
items.abstract: Introduction A sufficiently large information flux in recurrent neural networks, quantified by the mutual information between successive network states, has been proposed as a marker of rich information-processing capabilities. This raises the question of whether biological neural networks, such as cortical microcircuits, may be structurally organized to enhance information flux. Methods To investigate this possibility, we study a simplified model of the cortical layer 5 architecture, in which a densely and strongly interconnected core population is embedded within a larger supporting network. Results Surprisingly, we find that the embedding network exerts a pronounced flux-enhancing effect on the core dynamics. Systematic reverse-engineering analyses reveal that the embedding network primarily generates heterogeneous negative mean inputs that shift the core neurons into a higher-flux operating regime. Replacing the full time-dependent embedding signals by corresponding constant biases preserves this flux-enhancing effect, indicating that the detailed signal dynamics are not essential under the tested conditions. We further show that the information flux can be increased even beyond the biologically embedded case by applying optimized uniform or neuron-specific biases to the core neurons, and that similarly high values can emerge from a simple local adaptive-bias rule. Additional controls show that adaptive regulation and independently tuned inhibitory targeting further improve the embedded network, whereas removing the privileged strong-weight organization of the core abolishes the embedding advantage. Discussion These results suggest that the surrounding network acts as a distributed regulator that prevents a strongly recurrent core from becoming trapped in saturated, low-flux states, rather than as an optimizer of information flux. Our findings are relevant both for the functional interpretation of biological neural circuits and for the design of artificial recurrent systems such as reservoir computers.

items.title: Visual Trend Analysis of E-Commerce Thumbnails Using Parallel Computing for Image Big Data
items.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce platforms has led to the massive accumulation of product thumbnail images, making manual visual analysis inefficient and conventional sequential processing methods insufficient to handle such data volumes in a timely manner. Given the crucial role of thumbnails in influencing consumer purchasing decisions, computational strategies are required to accelerate the analysis process without compromising classification accuracy. This study applies a parallel computing approach combined with deep learning to improve the efficiency of visual trend analysis using two primary datasets: 2,608 images for model training and validation, and 40,254 images for large-scale inference. The proposed framework integrates parallel image preprocessing on multi-core CPUs, the development of a Convolutional Neural Network based on MobileNetV2 using a transfer learning approach, and batch-based parallel inference on GPUs. The developed model demonstrates stable and convergent performance, achieving a training accuracy of 0.85 and a validation accuracy of 0.83. Efficiency testing during the preprocessing stage shows that the parallel approach is more effective under large data workloads, providing a speed improvement of up to 1.58×. During the inference stage, predictions for 500 images can be completed in 1.84 seconds compared to 41.76 seconds using the sequential method, resulting in a significant computational speedup of 22.8×. Big data analysis reveals a polarization of visual strategies, where technology product categories are dominated by infographic-style thumbnails, fashion categories rely heavily on human model representations, and household product categories emphasize clean product visuals supported by promotional elements. This study concludes that the application of parallel computing significantly enhances the efficiency and scalability of visual big data analysis in e-commerce and supports more operational and strategic mapping of visual trends.

items.title: Self-Control and Social Media Addiction: A Review Among Generation Z University Students
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the relationship between self-control and social media addiction among Generation Z university students. The rapid development of digital technology has made social media an inseparable part of daily life, especially for Generation Z who are considered digital natives. However, excessive use of social media may lead to addictive behaviors that negatively affect psychological well-being, academic performance, and social functioning. This research employed a quantitative correlational design with 354 undergraduate students as participants. Sampling was conducted using a convenience sampling technique. Self-control was measured using the Brief Self-Control Scale (BSCS), while social media addiction was measured using a Social Media Addiction Scale adapted from previous studies. Data were analyzed using Spearman’s rho correlation test due to non-normal data distribution. The results revealed a significant negative correlation between self-control and social media addiction (r = -0.109 ; p = 0.041). This indicates that higher levels of self-control are associated with lower levels of social media addiction. The findings emphasize the importance of strengthening self-regulation skills among university students to prevent problematic social media use. Future research is recommended to explore mediating or moderating variables such as social support and psychological well-being.

items.title: Jointly predicting courses and grades using a transformer-based model
items.abstract: Existing predictive models in learning analytics often treat student academic history as a simple sequence, overlooking the concurrent nature of courses taken within a semester. This simplification can lead to inaccurate performance predictions, particularly for students with heavy or challenging course loads. This paper introduces a TRansformer for Academic Course-grade Estimation (TRACE) that addresses this limitation by jointly predicting both the set of courses a student will take and their corresponding grades for an upcoming semester. Our approach encodes courses on a per-semester basis to capture the effects of course concurrency and utilizes a novel loss function combining course-set prediction with grade prediction. We demonstrate that predicting courses taken in addition to the grades in those courses leads to significant improvements in prediction quality. Trained on ten years of institutional data, our joint prediction model reduces mean absolute error by nearly 50% compared to an identical architecture that predicts grades alone. The model also outperforms traditional LSTM-based sequential models, as well as graph neural network-based approaches, and offers natural ways to incorporate student attribute data. This work demonstrates the utility of modern neural architectures for creating interpretable models that can be adapted to new institutions via retraining and recalibration, as well as the importance of key techniques, such as predicting courses taken during training. We discuss how this model could be incorporated into early detection systems at institutions of higher education.

items.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
items.abstract: We present a systems-security case study of a two-node split-LLM training system whose privacy evaluation passed while leaving an observable channel untested. The Trusted Local Node (TLN) sends protected activations to the Untrusted Cloud Node (UCN), the UCN returns its output, and TLN, holding the private loss, returns the output gradient. The frame the UCN receives mixes real rows with decoys, and the loss ignores the decoys. Their gradients are exactly zero, so the pattern of zeros reveals which rows were real. We measure it with a protocol fixed in advance: a leak injected at known strength to prove the instrument can see one, a shuffled-label control to prove it does not report absent leaks, and a threshold set before the runs. Across nine seeds, the zeros identified the real rows on every frame, 4,096 of 4,096 per run. An attack on the frame contents recovered about one extra token per hundred over a constant-guess baseline (+0.65 to +1.50 percentage points); the shuffled controls recovered nothing. A second set of runs repeated this on a configuration that keeps model quality within budget, so the finding is not confined to a setting nobody would deploy. On both datasets, every such run passed the forward-channel privacy check and the quality check, yet failed that same check once the returned gradient was included. Clipping and noising each row of the gradient closed the leak for about 0.01 nats of held-out cross-entropy. The system is not thereby safe: five classes of attack, including those accumulating observations across training steps, were never measured.

items.title: Conservation and Development of the Thai Children’s Folk Play Wisdom in Andaman Coastal Provinces
items.abstract: The objectives of this research are to: 1) examine the value of traditional folk play on physical, emotional, mental, social, and cognitive development of Thai children in the Andaman coastal provinces; 2) examine factors affecting the conservation of folk play wisdom in the Andaman coastal provinces; and 3) propose guidelines to develop Thai children folk plays in Andaman provinces. The sample consisted of 400 primary school students and 50 key informants including school administrators, primary school homeroom teachers, physical education teachers, local leaders, folk philosophers, and parents. Research instruments comprised: 1) a handbook of traditional folk play for Thai children in the Andaman coastal provinces; 2) an observation form for assessing the value of traditional folk play; and 3) interview protocols regarding conservation factors and development guidelines for traditional folk play. The content validity of the instruments was determined by calculating the Index of Item-Objective Congruence (IOC) with values ranging from 0.67-1.00. The reliability coefficients were 0.87 for the observation form and 0.85 for the interview protocols. Data were analyzed using mean, standard deviation, and content analysis. The findings revealed that: 1) traditional folk play significantly contributed to children's development across all aspects (physical, emotional, mental, social, and cognitive) at high levels; 2) conservation of folk play wisdom was influenced by personal factors, family and social factors, economic factors, and technological factors; and 3) effective guidelines for developing folk play wisdom included implementing supportive local policies, establishing educational institution policies, adapting play formats and equipment, and implementing targeted projects. The research findings provide valuable direction for developing local curricula and activities that promote the conservation of indigenous wisdom in educational institutions.

items.title: The Schematic Brain: The Neurophysiology of Behavioral Schemas.
items.abstract: How does prior experience shape the way we interpret new situations, learn faster, and adapt when the world changes? These capacities depend on schemas: structured representations of relational knowledge that the brain builds through experience and reuses flexibly across contexts. Although schemas have long been central to theories of memory and cognition, their neural implementation is only now becoming accessible through advances in large-scale neural recordings, population-level analysis methods, and precise causal circuit tools. Here we review the emerging systems neuroscience of schemas, focusing on animal models where mechanistic dissection is feasible. We argue that schema formation, use, and updating are not discrete processes but reflect a continuous adaptive interplay between the strength of prior knowledge and the degree to which new information aligns with it. At the neural level, schemas appear to be encoded as structured low-dimensional population geometries distributed across hippocampal-prefrontal circuits, with distinct but interacting contributions from orbitofrontal cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and hippocampus. These representations actively shape perception, guide behavior, and reorganize when the environment demands it.

items.title: Using 360-video to investigate visual exploratory activity in 7v7 and 9v9 sided games in women's soccer.
items.abstract: Immersive technology such as 360-video offers opportunities to analyse visual exploratory activity (VEA) under varying task constraints in controlled experimental settings. The study aimed to investigate the effect of pitch location and sided‑game format on VEA and verbal action responses in 360-video. Nineteen sub-elite female soccer players (21 ± 4 years) viewed 40 soccer videos in a head-mounted display. Footage was recorded using a stationary GoPro 360 Max camera at eye height in defensive and attacking central midfield locations. VEA was measured as the number of "scans" away from the ball across 32 analysed trials. Upon receiving a pass in 360-video, participants simulated and verbalised an action to continue play. A 2 × 2 repeated‑measures ANOVA showed a significant main effect of pitch location ( p = 0.016), with higher scan frequencies in defensive (0.31 ± 0.15 scans/s) than attacking midfield (0.29 ± 0.15 scans/s), with no significant effect of sided‑game or interaction effect ( p > 0.05). Findings demonstrate players had significantly higher scan frequencies in defensive central midfield compared with attacking central midfield, with the most verbal actions per trial in the 9v9 attacking midfield condition. Future research should assess agreement between VEA measured in 360-video and on-field activities.

items.title: Maternal Factors Modifying the Link Between Genetic Risk for Autism and Developmental Milestones.
items.abstract: Although common genetic liability-quantified through polygenic risk scores (PRS)-accounts for substantial variance in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) liability, how prenatal environmental exposures interact with genetic predisposition to shape developmental outcomes remains poorly understood. Using the data from Autism Genetic Resource Exchange (AGRE), we examined whether maternal prenatal factors moderate the association between ASD PRS and developmental outcomes, including language delay, motor delay, and core ASD traits. In exploratory gene-environment interaction analyses, amniocentesis was a candidate positive moderator of the association between PRS and both language and motor delay, such that higher polygenic liability was associated with a greater likelihood of these delays among prenatally exposed children. First-trimester vaginal bleeding showed a similar positive interaction estimate for motor delay. Maternal use of over-the-counter (OTC) medications during pregnancy-predominantly acetaminophen, reported by 59.9% of OTC users-was associated with an inverse interaction estimate, corresponding to a decreased association between polygenic liability and language delay among exposed children. These observations suggest that several prenatal factors may modify the association between common genetic liability and developmental outcomes among autistic children and should be considered hypothesis-generating until replicated in larger, population-based cohorts. Replication in independent samples, together with analyses that address selection and confounding, will be required before these candidate gene-environment interactions can be interpreted as reflecting specific developmental mechanisms.

items.title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms.
items.abstract: Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding within this population and task context.

items.title: Sex Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Responses to Adolescents' Questions on Romantic Relationships and Sexuality.
items.abstract: Large language model chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have garnered increasing attention in the field of education, due to its versatility, processing speed, and widespread accessibility. However, its application to sexual education remains understudied, highlighting the need for more research into its potential to support informed decision-making among youth. The current study aimed to document ChatGPT-3.5 responses to adolescents' questions about romantic relationships and sexuality, using a more-than-human netnography approach. To obtain these responses, 393 anonymized emails written in French and English from adolescents aged 14 to 16 were collected from a recognized youth support organization. Data were obtained through ChatGPT-3.5 from January 14 to 31, 2024. The analyses focused on identifying content violations and describing the response formats, followed by a conventional content analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 recommendations. Overall, 17.8% of the emails were flagged as potentially violating ChatGPT-3.5's content policy. Responses were provided in two formats: (1) structured text or (2) continuous text that both included an introduction clarifying the question, normalizing the experience, and/or validating emotions; a list of recommendations; and a conclusion promoting support seeking, and/or a positive outlook. The recommendations aimed to encourage adolescents to embrace authenticity and personal agency, practice self-care and build self-confidence, engage in open communication, develop meaningful relationships, and seek support when needed. The findings highlight ChatGPT's potential to contribute to comprehensive sex education for adolescents seeking information.

items.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.
items.abstract: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

items.title: Neural mechanisms underlying metacognitive processes in sequential decision-making.
items.abstract: Self-monitoring in decision-making is a hallmark of self-improvement in cognitive processes. To enhance outcomes in future decisions, individuals must accurately assess the correctness of prior choices and apply the information to control subsequent decisions. Although metacognition encompasses monitoring and control functions, the neural mechanisms underlying these processes and their relationships remain unclear. Furthermore, while the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in both functions, their distinct neural substrates and interrelations require further elucidation. In this study, we employed a sequential perceptual decision-making task with confidence ratings to examine how initial confidence influences subsequent decisions while recording neural activity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Subjects (female and male) performed a visual discrimination of two different-sized stimuli and subsequently rated their decision confidence. Behavioral results showed that subjects were more likely to change their choices between initial and subsequent decisions according to confidence levels. A signature of confidence (confidence magnitude) in initial decisions was observed primarily in the anterior medial PFC (amPFC). In contrast, the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) exhibited higher neural activity related to changes of their initial choice at subsequent decisions. Furthermore, the pregenual ACC (pgACC) was associated with both processes, and it exhibited effective connectivity with the amPFC and dACC. These findings suggest that the medial PFC plays a role in integrating metacognitive monitoring and subsequent control in the sequential decision-making processes. Significance Statement Metacognition, encompassing monitoring and control, is fundamental to self-regulation and sequential decision-making. Despite their distinct roles, the neural mechanisms of how monitoring connects to subsequent control remain unclear. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), we reveal distinct yet interconnected medial prefrontal regions that support metacognitive processes. Specifically, the anterior medial prefrontal cortex encodes confidence in initial decisions, while the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex supports changes of mind. Effective connectivity analysis indicates that the pregenual anterior cingulate cortex integrates these processes. These findings advance our understanding of medial prefrontal mechanisms underlying adaptive self-regulation, with implications for addressing disorders characterized by impaired behavioral control.

items.title: Tumor innervation in non-central nervous system tumors: origins, mechanisms, and phenotypic plasticity.
items.abstract: The peripheral nervous system has emerged as an important regulator of solid tumor biology. We synthesize recent advances in cancer neuroscience, focusing on three interconnected themes: the cellular origins of tumor-associated nerves, the molecular mechanisms that govern neural recruitment and remodeling, and the resulting phenotypic plasticity within the tumor microenvironment. Tumor innervation arises through axon extension from pre-existing nerves, recruitment of neural precursors, and neuron-like transdifferentiation of non-neuronal cells. These processes are driven by neurotrophic factors, axon guidance cues, extracellular vesicles, and stress-associated pathways. The functional consequences of innervation are context-dependent, with sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory inputs exerting distinct effects across tumor types and stages. We conclude by outlining key challenges and future directions for therapeutic translation.

items.title: Obesity-induced oxidative stress and cGMP depletion suppress cerebellar α2,3-Na<sup>+</sup>,K<sup>+</sup>-ATPase activity in female mice.
items.abstract: Obesity is a major metabolic disorder linked to neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. Beyond hypothalamic alterations, emerging evidence indicates that extra-hypothalamic regions, including the cerebellum, are vulnerable to obesity-induced neurotoxicity. This study investigated whether high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity causes cerebellar oxidative stress, impairs Na + ,K + -ATPase (NKA) activity, and triggers molecular features resembling brain aging in female Balb/C mice. Chronic 10-week HFD intake established a marked obese phenotype, characterized by increased adiposity, fasting hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and elevated serum TNF-α. In the cerebellum, obesity induced a selective, expression-independent reduction in α2,3-NKA isoform activity, accompanied by a marked depletion of tissue cGMP levels. This functional impairment was driven by an oxidative microenvironment, evidenced by elevated H 2 O 2 and TBARS levels and increased 4-HNE accumulation. Concomitantly, obese animals mounted an adaptive antioxidant response characterized by increased GST, GR, and GPx activities, reduced glutathione (GSH) consumption, and ERK1/2-mediated nuclear translocation of Nrf2, alongside structural membrane lipid remodeling (elevated cholesterol and reduced phospholipids). In summary, chronic obesity induces robust lipoxidative stress and suppresses cerebellar cGMP signaling and α2,3-NKA activity in female mice, recapitulating key molecular hallmarks of natural brain aging.

items.title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

items.title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
items.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

items.title: Interpersonal neural synchrony and parent-child behaviors during naturalistic interactions: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Interpersonal neural synchrony (INS), defined as the temporal alignment of neural activity between socially interacting individuals, has been proposed as an index of parent-child interaction quality. However, its relationship with moment-to-moment adjustment of parent-child behavior remains insufficiently understood. This systematic review examined associations between INS and observable behavior during naturalistic parent-child interactions, the factors influencing these associations, and the methods used to investigate them. Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 15 peer-reviewed empirical studies involving children from preschool age to early adolescence. INS-behavior associations were heterogeneous across studies. Higher INS was most consistently associated with mutual engagement, shared positive affect, and supportive parenting, whereas findings concerning reciprocity, responsiveness, and child agency were more context-dependent. Time-resolved analyses further indicated that INS fluctuated in relation to specific behavioral events and revealed temporally asymmetric patterns in which parent or child neural activity preceded that of the interaction partner. However, these patterns do not establish causal directionality and may partly reflect shared exposure to task-related or interactional inputs. Task structure and the availability of direct social cues appeared to shape INS-behavior associations, while parental stress and child social functioning emerged as potential sources of variability in INS. Methodologically, the findings highlight the value of combining micro- and macro-level behavioral coding with time-resolved and directionality-sensitive analyses, alongside stronger controls for spurious synchrony and common inputs. Given the limited number and methodological heterogeneity of available studies, the findings should be regarded as preliminary and primarily hypothesis-generating.

items.title: From Blue Dye to Multimodal-Guided Surgery: The Evolution of Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Vulvar Cancer - A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Future progress should focus on standardized fluorescence protocols, rigorously sequenced ICG-first validation, hybrid radioactive-fluorescent strategies, and integration of imaging-derived and artificial intelligence-based tools into individualized groin management.

items.title: Repeated ketamine administration induces cross-tolerance to sodium salicylate but not to morphine in male rats.
items.abstract: Cross-tolerance profiles provide critical insights into shared neurobiological substrates among analgesics. This study evaluated whether repeated sub-anesthetic ketamine administration induces cross-tolerance to morphine or sodium salicylate. Thirty-six adults male Wistar rats (180-200 g, n = 6/group) received either normal saline or ketamine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) once daily for 8 consecutive days. Antinociceptive thresholds were assessed daily using the hot-plate test (52 ± 0.5 °C) at 45 min post-injection and expressed as the percentage of maximum possible effect (MPE%). On day 9, acute cross-tolerance challenges were conducted using morphine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) or sodium salicylate (300 mg/kg, i.p.). Serum malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity was measured on day 8 to evaluate systemic oxidative status. Repeated ketamine administration produced a progressive decline in MPE%, demonstrating marked antinociceptive tolerance by day 8. On day 9, morphine maintained full antinociceptive efficacy in ketamine-pretreated rats, indicating no cross-tolerance. Conversely, sodium salicylate-induced antinociception was significantly blunted, confirming cross-tolerance. Biochemically, ketamine pre-treatment did not elevate serum MDA and preserved SOD activity substantially better than morphine. In conclusion, repeated sub-anesthetic ketamine administration induces antinociceptive tolerance and selective cross-tolerance to sodium salicylate, while sparing morphine responsiveness. These behavioral adaptations parallel a favorable redox balance, highlighting distinct pharmacodynamic mechanisms governing ketamine interactions with opioid versus non-opioid regimens.

items.title: Maternal high-fat diet and metformin treatment affect palatable diet preference and central reward system gene expression in rat offspring in a sex-specific manner.
items.abstract: Maternal metformin (MT) treatment improves the metabolic phenotype of high-fat (HF) diet-exposed offspring, but its effect on offspring's palatable food preference remains unclear. We assessed HF diet and sucrose preferences in adult offspring from Sprague-Dawley rat dams fed a control diet, an HF diet with or without MT treatment. Additionally, we measured the mRNA expression of sweet taste perception-related genes in taste buds and dopamine- and opioid-related genes in the central reward system. In adult males, maternal HF diet increased HF food preference and decreased dopamine-related gene expression in the reward system. Furthermore, maternal MT treatment decreased low-concentration sucrose preference, and reduced opioid-related gene expression in the reward system. Maternal HF diet elevated sweet taste perception-related gene expression in taste buds, while maternal MT treatment reversed these changes. In adult females, neither maternal HF diet nor MT treatment affected HF food preference. However, maternal HF diet decreased low-concentration sucrose preference and reduced the expression of sweet taste perception-related genes, while maternal MT treatment did not reverse it. At weaning, maternal MT treatment generally decreased dopamine- and opioid-related gene expression in the central reward system across both sexes. Notably, this early-life central reward transcriptional suppression persisted into adulthood in males but not in females. Our results indicate that maternal HF diet and MT treatment influence HF diet and low-concentration sucrose preferences in adult offspring in a sex-specific manner, which may be associated with altered gene expression in the central reward system and the peripheral taste perception pathways.

items.title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
items.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.

items.title: Meta-Analytic Evidence of Clinical, Cognitive, Biological and Treatment Characteristics of Bipolar Spectrum Disorder in Children and Adolescents: Results From an Umbrella Review.
items.abstract: Objective To comprehensively synthesize the meta-analytic evidence regarding bipolar spectrum disorder (BSD) in children and adolescents. Method PRISMA-compliant umbrella review (PROSPERO:CRD420250651065) across multiple databases to identify meta-analyses involving children and adolescents with BSD. Literature search, screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (via AMSTAR-2) were performed independently. Findings were synthesized and grouped according to key clinical, cognitive, biological and treatment domains. Results Fifty-two meta-analyses were included (k=754, N=59,967, age=13.0 years, 44.8% female participants). Most reported symptoms were increased energy (79%, 95% confidence interval (CI)=61-93%), irritability (77%, 95%CI=64-88%), and mood lability (76%, 95%CI=55-92%). Psychiatric comorbidities were common, with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder being most frequent (53%, 95%CI=36-70%). Treatment delay was longer in children and adolescents than in adults with BSD (SMD=0.39, 95%CI=0.15-0.64). 26.2% (95%CI=24.4-28.0) of children and adolescents with BSD attempted suicide at least once, with higher risk vs. children and adolescents with depression (OR=1.59; 95%CI=1.24-2.05) and adult-BSD (OR=1.68, 95%CI=1.29-2.18). Compared to healthy controls (HCs), children and adolescents with BSD showed neurocognitive impairments. Abnormalities in neuroimaging markers were significant in children and adolescents with BSD vs. HCs, children and adolescents with depression and adult-BSD. Second-generation antipsychotics (SMD=0.68, 95%CI=0.51-0.86) and mood stabilizers (SMD=0.61, 95%CI=0.40-0.82) were superior for mania vs. placebo. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) was associated with improvements in manic and depressive symptoms. Conclusion BSD in children and adolescents is linked to illness severity, cognitive deficits, and neuroimaging abnormalities, requiring integrated pharmacological and psychosocial interventions (e.g. CBT). SGAs effectively treat mania, but options for depression remain limited. More prognostic and long-term studies are needed.

items.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
items.abstract: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches to effectively guide clinical management. To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile. Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were investigated using logistic regression models. A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 [95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]). These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are warranted.

items.title: CX3CL1 (fractalkine)-CX3CR1 interface drives CD8⁺ T cell-induced neurodegeneration in human brain organoids.
items.abstract: Immune-neuron interactions play a critical role in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how CD8⁺ T cells contribute to brain pathology remains poorly understood. Amyloid-β (Aβ), a hallmark of AD, is known to trigger neuronal stress and inflammation. Here, we established a human cortical organoid (hCO) model to investigate CD8⁺ T cell responses to Aβ-induced neurodegenerative stress. Aβ exposure increased neuronal expression of CX3CL1 (fractalkine), which engages its receptor CX3CR1 on CD8⁺ T cells. Transwell migration assays showed enhanced recruitment of CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells toward Aβ-treated hCOs. In parallel, Aβ upregulated IL-15 expression, a cytokine that supports CD8⁺ T cell activation. The infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells led to neuronal injury, marked by MAP2 loss and cleaved Caspase-3 activation, accompanied by an increase in gene signatures for cell death and inflammation. Exposure to the conditioned medium of activated CX3CR1 high CD8⁺ T cell recapitulated this damage, and the neutralization of CD8 + T cell cytokines and cytotoxic molecules rescued the phenotype. These findings identify the CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis and CD8⁺ T cell effector programs as drivers of neurotoxicity and establish brain organoids as a platform to study immune-driven neurodegeneration.
