items.title: Multiple sources contribute to predictive tactile attenuation in the mouse whisker system.
items.abstract: The brain predicts action outcomes using interacting neuronal systems that integrate sensory feedback, movement, and rewards. In the mouse whisker system, we investigated whether two presumed predictive mechanisms jointly attenuate ascending tactile signals during movement. To this end, we employed an open-loop whisker-reach task that monitored facial nucleus motor activity and presented experimental tactile consequences while measuring tactile attenuation in the barrel cortex. Experimentally manipulating sensory consequences revealed two distinct systems. Sensory gating, a previously documented but functionally unclear mechanism of tactile attenuation, appeared graded but persisted during and after movement. In contrast, a second system was found to be temporally precise, generate suppression when stimuli are omitted, and capable of being learned within hundreds of trials. We label it state estimation as its characteristics-active suppression of expected tactile input-aligns well with the classical reafference principle, previously overlooked in the whisker system.

items.title: Improving optogenetic control over G<sub>i/o</sub>-coupled receptor signaling by optimized GIRK channel expression.
items.abstract: Stimulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that couple to G i/o leads to the activation of G protein-activated inward rectifier K + (GIRK) channels and membrane hyperpolarization in excitable cells. GIRK channel availability can determine the success of optogenetic silencing strategies based on G i/o -coupled GPCRs. To selectively enhance G i/o -mediated GIRK currents, we created expression cassettes that coupled the activity of a GIRK subunit to the light-activated G i/o -coupled GPCRs Opn4L (an opsin also known as melanopsin), longwave-sensitive opsin Opn1, parapinopsin, or Opn7b. We used the GIRK1 F137S mutant because of its fast activation, generation of large currents, and formation of homomeric channels, which reduced the size of the expression cassette. We demonstrated that light-mediated activation of GIRK1 F137S through the opsins induced robust GIRK currents in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes, and cerebellar Purkinje neurons. Moreover, coupling GIRK1 F137S activation to the promiscuous Opn4L changed the net effect of G protein signaling from G q/11 -mediated excitation to G i/o -mediated inhibition in cerebellar Purkinje neurons and cardiomyocytes. Thus, our tools optimize the use of GIRK activity in the optogenetic control of the G i/o pathway in excitable cells.

items.title: Endothelial neo-antigen expression initiates CD8⁺ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis amplified by peripheral immune challenge.
items.abstract: Primary central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and devastating inflammatory cerebrovascular disease for which pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly defined, largely due to limited access to human tissue and the absence of validated experimental models. Here, we present a mouse model of CNS-restricted vasculitis based on inducible, endothelial-biased neoantigen expression, termed brain endothelial ovalbumin (BrEndO). In BrEndO mice, tamoxifen-induced ovalbumin (OVA) expression in cerebral endothelial cells (ECs) elicited a controlled endogenous CD8+ T cell response at the blood-brain barrier that remained clinically restrained. In contrast, peripheral immune activation through infection with OVA-expressing Listeria monocytogenes or systemic PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade converted this regulated response into severe, CD8+ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis with vascular injury and parenchymal infiltration. Transcriptomic profiling of inflamed cerebral microvessels and spatial transcriptomic analyses demonstrated shared inflammatory and immune activation signatures between BrEndO mice and human primary CNS vasculitis brain biopsies. These findings identify antigen-specific endothelial immune recognition as a regulated process whose breakdown precipitates CNS-restricted vasculitis and establish BrEndO as an experimentally tractable platform to investigate mechanisms and modifiers of immune-mediated cerebrovascular inflammation.

items.title: A biopsychosocial perspective on obesity and eating disorders: A narrative overview and exploratory study of ghrelin, LEAP2, trait impulsivity, and eating psychopathology.
items.abstract: Dysregulated eating in obesity and eating disorders (ED) is associated with complex relationships between peripheral hormonal signals and neurobehavioral characteristics. Ghrelin and its endogenous antagonist liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide-2 (LEAP2) have been implicated in the regulation of energy homeostasis and food intake, while trait impulsivity has been proposed as a transdiagnostic characteristic associated with dysregulated eating. This study aimed to integrate narrative evidence with exploratory empirical data to examine associations between ghrelin, LEAP2, and trait impulsivity in women with obesity, with and without ED, and to explore their associations with food addiction (FA) and eating psychopathology. A total of 164 adult women (67 with obesity, 35 with obesity + ED, 62 healthy controls) completed anthropometric assessments, fasting ghrelin and LEAP2 determinations, and psychometric measures of trait impulsivity, FA, and eating psychopathology. Group comparisons and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to explore associations between endocrine and behavioral variables. Women with obesity (with or without ED) showed significantly lower ghrelin levels than controls, while LEAP2 concentrations did not differ between groups. Trait impulsivity and FA scores were higher in the obesity + ED group. Within this subgroup, SEM analyses identified positive associations of trait impulsivity and FA with eating psychopathology, while LEAP2 was positively associated with trait impulsivity and FA scores. Previous research has pointed to potential associations of ghrelin and LEAP2 with obesity and ED, as well as with behavioral characteristics related to dysregulated eating, although the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. In our study, ghrelin was lower in women with obesity, whereas LEAP2 did not differ between groups. The observed associations involving LEAP2 emerged only in the exploratory SEM analysis and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not provide evidence of mechanistic or causal relationships. Further research in larger and longitudinal samples is needed to replicate these findings and clarify the relationships among endocrine and behavioral factors.

items.title: Therapeutic potential of varenicline in neuropsychiatric disorders: insights into its molecular mechanisms.
items.abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders pose significant health challenges. Current drug therapies are often inadequate, highlighting the urgent need for new and effective treatments. The α4β2 nicotinic receptor has been implicated in the pathophysiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders. In this context, varenicline, its selective agonist, has garnered increasing attention for its potential therapeutic effects across a range of neuropsychiatric conditions. Emerging preclinical evidence suggests that varenicline may exert neuroprotective effects through modulation of pathways that include synaptic plasticity and synaptic proteins, neuroinflammation, microglial activation, apoptosis, and autophagy. However, direct target engagement for many of these pathways has not yet been established. In this review, we provide a comprehensive review of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which varenicline might be expected to exert therapeutic effects in a range of neuropsychiatric disorders. Most previous reviews of varenicline have concentrated on its use as a smoking cessation aid or on its potential to treat individual diseases. The current review takes a different approach, focusing at the molecular level on the various pathways that are affected in different diseases, and discussing within each section the evidence that currently exists in relation to each of these in studies conducted in rodent models and in clinical trials. The review seeks to provide insight into the potential benefits and drawbacks of using a single compound to treat a variety of disorders, and to highlight areas for future research.

items.title: Embedding team-based learning in graduate anatomy: The impact on student performance.
items.abstract: Team-based learning (TBL) is widely used in health professions education; however, its role within integrated curriculum redesigns serving increasingly heterogeneous student populations remains less well understood. Grounded in a conceptual framework emphasizing preparation, individual accountability, collaborative knowledge construction, immediate feedback, and application, this study evaluated TBL within a redesigned graduate-level gross anatomy course. Four cohorts (2022-2025) were analyzed: Two completed the original lecture-based curriculum and two completed a redesigned curriculum incorporating TBL, required human donor dissection laboratories, formative assessments, and team-based examinations. A standardized Individual Performance Score (IPS) enabled comparison across cohorts. Grade distributions, item-level psychometric indices, early assessment predictive value, and student perceptions were also evaluated. Overall IPS differences were not significant (H = 6.50, p = 0.089); however, the redesigned curriculum was associated with a higher proportion of A grades (+11.7%, p = 0.012) and differences in performance distribution (U = 16,143.5, p = 0.043). TBL-aligned items demonstrated stronger discrimination and point-biserial correlations, while early practical performance strongly predicted overall outcomes. Student perceptions were favorable, with 90.8% endorsing TBL activities and 94.1% reporting that team-based examinations supported understanding. Embedding TBL within an integrated graduate anatomy curriculum may support high achievement, assessment quality, and collaborative learning. However, the historical cohort design, concurrent admissions changes, and multifaceted curricular redesign limit causal attribution to TBL alone. These findings support positioning TBL as one component of a broader curricular framework rather than an isolated intervention.

items.title: Therapeutic potential analysis of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
items.abstract: Abstract Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is a core pathological process underlying further neurological deterioration after reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Developing more effective neuroprotective agents is therefore a current priority in neuroscience research. Sertoli cells possess unique immunoprivileged and nutritional support functions within the testes and secrete exosomes that serve as important mediators of intercellular communication, with substantial potential for neuroprotection. This review addresses the protective mechanisms of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Through a comprehensive literature review, we systematically summarize their neuroprotective effects, including the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inhibition of cellular apoptosis, promotion of neurovascular repair, regulation of autophagy, and influence on epigenetic modifications and related signaling pathways. By synthesizing the latest findings in this field, we aim to provide insights into the development and translation of novel neuroprotective strategies based on Sertoli cell-derived exosomes.

items.title: Dynamic Changes in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein Levels Predicts Early Neurological Deterioration After Intravenous Thrombolysis in Minor Stroke.
items.abstract: Minor strokes may be associated with early neurological deterioration (END) and disabilities. The objective was to investigate the role of serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in predicting END. Data originated from a multicenter cohort study conducted prospectively. ΔGFAP was calculated as the ratio of post-thrombolysis GFAP at 24 h to baseline GFAP. Univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between ∆GFAP and END, and a nomogram was established to illustrate its predictive value. END occurred in 20 (7.35%) of the 272 patients with minor stroke who underwent intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). Elevated ∆GFAP was independently associated with END (OR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.67 to 7.31; p < 0.001), even after adjusting for confounders (adjusted OR, 4.64; 95% CI, 1.86 to 11.54; p < 0.001). Furthermore, a model combining ∆GFAP, age, and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission demonstrated a good predictive value for END (AUC = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.89). ∆GFAP is a strong, independent predictor of END in patients with minor strokes. Integrating ∆GFAP, age, and NIHSS score into a prognostic model results in a good discriminative ability for predicting END.

items.title: Adolescent Chronic Sleep Restriction Induces a Mesolimbic Hypodopaminergic State Associated with Addiction Vulnerability.
items.abstract: Adolescent sleep insufficiency is increasingly prevalent, but whether repeated insufficient sleep during this developmental period promotes addiction vulnerability remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of chronic sleep restriction (CSR) imposed during adolescence, from 4 to 7 weeks of age, on the mesocorticolimbic dopamine (DA) system and addiction-related behaviors in mice. Behavioral and neuronal responses in the mesolimbic pathway to the psychostimulant Amphetamine (Amph) were examined. Also, DA-related molecular and structural components, including DA receptors, DA turnover, and developmental regulators such as Netrin-1/deleted in colorectal cancer (DCC), were assessed. Our results identified that adolescent CSR induces a hypodopaminergic profile characterized by reduced neuronal activity in the core regions of the mesolimbic DA circuit at baseline and upon acute Amph stimulation, downregulated striatal DA receptors, and reduced DA axon innervation in the ventral striatum. Altered Netrin-1/DCC signaling and mesocortical DA synthesis further suggest that sleep loss during adolescence disrupts ongoing maturation of DA circuitry. Furthermore, these neurobiological profiles were accompanied by enhanced Amph-induced conditioned place preference (CPP). Together, these findings indicate that chronic adolescent sleep insufficiency induces a constellation of behavioral and neurobiological adaptations relevant to addiction susceptibility. In contrast to prior acute sleep-loss paradigms that mainly capture transient DA activation, our data support a model in which repeated sleep restriction imposes cumulative allostatic load and promotes longer-term maladaptive remodeling of reward circuitry. These results identify insufficient sleep during adolescence as a potential risk factor for addiction vulnerability.

items.title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
items.abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

items.title: Research Trends in Suicide Bereavement and Postvention - A Global Bibliometric and Content Analysis.
items.abstract: Background: Suicide bereavement refers to the grief experienced by individuals who have lost a close contact to suicide. It is often characterized by intense emotional distress, feelings of guilt, stigma, and social isolation, and may increase the risk of mental health problems and suicidal behavior. As research on suicide bereavement and postvention continues to expand globally, there is a growing need to map its development systematically and identify key trends. Aims: This study aimed to describe patterns in published literature on suicide bereavement and postvention through a global bibliometric analysis. Method: Systematic searches in eight databases (Web of Science; Scopus; CINAHL; PsycINFO; MEDLINE; Embase; Emcare; APA PsycArticles) yielded 49,386 references. After deduplication and screening, 1,072 articles published between 1953 and 2025 were included. Eligible peer-reviewed publications included empirical research, evidence syntheses (systematic reviews, scoping reviews, meta-analyses) and nonempirical publications (such as opinion pieces, and personal experiences). There were no restrictions on language, location, or year of publication. Results: The 1,072 eligible publications demonstrated a steady increase in suicide bereavement/postvention publications annually. 95% of publications were by first authors from high-income countries, while 1.3% of first authors were from lower-middle-income and low-income countries. Most studies were empirical and followed a quantitative or qualitative design, primarily cross-sectional, increasing over the years, while nonempirical publications declined. We identified few longitudinal or interventional studies. Populations sampled most frequently were working-age adults, with few studies focused on older adults. Limitations: The results provide little information about the methodological quality of the included studies. Some full texts could not be found and were unavailable for data extraction. Conclusion: The research gaps identified suggest that future studies should focus on underrepresented populations as well as on high-quality intervention studies to address adverse outcomes among suicide loss survivors.

items.title: Sex differences in dietary leucine utilization revealed by <sup>13</sup>C tracing in the cockroach Blaptica dubia.
items.abstract: Sex differences in amino acid acquisition and allocation are fundamental determinants of insect life-history strategies, yet the fate of assimilated amino acids after ingestion remains largely unknown. Here, we used 13 C stable isotope tracing to investigate sex-specific patterns of dietary leucine utilization in the cockroach Blaptica dubia. Adult males and females were fed artificial diets containing either 13 C-labeled or unlabeled leucine for 14 days, after which food consumption; body, gut, and fecal mass; gut length; fecal isotope enrichment; and tissue-specific 13 C incorporation were measured. 13 C enrichment of CO₂ was also measured. Females consumed less food than males but had substantially greater fresh and dry body mass, longer alimentary canals, and larger gut mass. Despite consuming more food and having significantly lower body mass (almost half that of females), males did not show greater 13 C enrichment in somatic tissues; no significant sex differences were detected in the brain, fat body, muscle, or respired CO₂. In contrast, male reproductive tissues showed significantly higher isotope enrichment than female oothecae, suggesting differences in the timing and dynamics of nutrient allocation to reproduction. Male feces showed significantly greater 13 C enrichment than female feces. In males, fecal 13 C enrichment did not differ between days 7 and 14, whereas females showed greater enrichment on day 14, consistent with slower food transit. Together, the larger, longer alimentary canal and lower fecal 13 C enrichment in females, combined with their lower food intake, are consistent with greater leucine retention and utilization and may indicate more efficient nutrient assimilation in females.

items.title: Novel strategy for advanced treatment of municipal wastewater with low carbon footprint: biological nitrogen removal and potent greenhouse gas mitigation in anaerobic-anoxic biofilter reactor by introducing raw wastewater.
items.abstract: To address the high carbon footprint of wastewater treatment plants, this study developed an anaerobic-anoxic biofilter reactor (A 2 -BFR) with a large ratio of height to diameter through two-point inlet. Raw wastewater was fed at bottom inlet to produce methane anaerobically. Meanwhile, the secondary effluent containing NO 3 - -N was fed at middle inlet to produce NO 2 - -N, which could be further removed through nitrite-dependent anaerobic methane oxidation (n-DAMO) and anaerobic ammonium oxidation (AMX). The results demonstrated that the effluent concentrations of TN and NH 4 + -N in A 2 -BFR remained 12.22 and 1.95 mg N/L, when the flow ratio of raw wastewater to secondary effluent was 1: 5. The apparent dissolved CH 4 attenuation rate was approximately 7.60 g CH 4 /(m 3 ·d), leading the effluent dissolved CH 4 concentration remained around 0.98 mg/L. Microbial community analysis revealed that DAMO bacteria (Candidatus Methylomirabilis) and anammox bacteria (Candidatus Brocadia) acted as the core consortium for nitrogen removal, jointly responsible for NO 2 - -N removal. Typical denitrifier bacteria Denitratisoma and sulfur autotrophic denitrifying bacteria Thiobacillus could reduce NO 3 - -N to NO 2 - -N, and ammonia oxidizing archaea such as Candidatus Nitrosocosmicus and norank_f_Nitrososphaeraceae could also oxidize NH 4 + -N to NO 2 - -N, which stably supplied substrates for the core microbes of nitrogen removal and promoted their enrichment and functional expression. Without external aeration and additional carbon sources, only feeding 16.67% raw wastewater to A 2 -BFR could ensure the secondary effluent of higher nitrate discharge in compliance with standards. This study provides a novel strategy for the advanced treatment of municipal wastewater with low carbon footprint.

items.title: Deep phylogeny, a candidate ancestral whole-genome duplication, and gene-family evolution in Delphinieae.
items.abstract: Delphinieae is a species-rich group in the buttercup family (Ranunculaceae) and its only lineage with complex, bilaterally symmetrical flowers, yet its early evolutionary relationships remain unresolved. To address this, we analyzed nuclear gene sequences from 54 transcriptomes, representing 40 species and two infraspecific taxa that cover all four genera of Delphinieae. Coalescent analyses consistently recovered Staphisagria as the earliest-diverging genus, followed by Gymnaconitum, with Delphinium and Aconitum as sister genera. These main intergeneric divergences occurred rapidly between 29.6 and 27.5 million years ago. Deep gene-tree conflict was concentrated around these early divergences and was best explained by incomplete lineage sorting; no clear signal of ancient hybridization was detected. Furthermore, analyses of duplicated genes and their chromosomal positions jointly supported a candidate whole-genome duplication on the Delphinieae stem lineage, with duplication ages concentrated near 52 million years ago. Two gene families involved in floral development also duplicated near this interval. For one family, corresponding copies occur in duplicated chromosome segments, and two related copies are adjacent, a pattern consistent with a large-scale duplication followed by a later local duplication. For the second family, one copy is incompletely represented in the chromosome-scale assembly, preventing a conclusive structural comparison. The candidate whole-genome duplication predates crown diversification of the living genera by more than 20 million years, indicating a prolonged interval between genome duplication and subsequent radiation.

items.title: Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester (DINCH) and its metabolites in body fluids of rats and humans after single oral doses of DINCH.
items.abstract: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has established a tolerable daily intake (TDI) of 1mg/kg bw/d for the plasticizer DINCH (Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester). To characterize the maximum internal doses resulting from a single dosing and to assess species differences relevant for extrapolating rat toxicokinetics to humans, concentration-time profiles of DINCH and its metabolites (specific monoesters: MINCH, OH-MINCH, oxo-MINCH, cx-MINCH; non-specific metabolite: CHDA) were quantified in the blood of male Wistar rats and male human volunteers. Urinary excretion of metabolites was additionally evaluated for humans. Single oral doses of ring-deuterated DINCH were administered (rats: 1 or 40mg/kg bw; humans: 1mg/kg bw). In rats, gastrointestinal absorption exhibited saturation, as a 40-fold increase in administered dose resulted in only ~25-fold increases in C max and AUC. Across species, the hierarchy of C max in blood was consistent: DINCH > CHDA > cx-MINCH > MINCH > OH-MINCH > oxo-MINCH. Notably, C max values for DINCH and MINCH in blood after a 1mg/kg bw (1.74µM and 0.10µM) dose in humans were like those observed in rats following a 40-fold higher dose (4.4µM and 0.11µM). Corresponding AUC∞ values showed the same pattern, indicating greater systemic availability of DINCH in humans, although this is partly counter balanced by plasma protein binding. In humans, approximately 50% of MINCH and 70-80% of the other monoester metabolites were glucuronidated, whereas these metabolites remained unconjugated in rats. CHDA was unconjugated in both species. Overall, the data highlight both shared and species-specific features of DINCH metabolism in rats and humans.

items.title: Interbacterial competition triggers stress-induced CRISPR immunity against bacteriophages.
items.abstract: Bacteria-phage interactions are often studied in relatively simple experimental systems involving a single bacterial strain infected by a single phage. 1 In natural environments, however, bacteria typically inhabit complex multispecies communities where species compete for limited resources and ecological niches. 2 , 3 , 4 Recent studies show that the microbial community context can have profound effects on the evolution of phage resistance. 5 For example, Pseudomonas aeruginosa evolves phage resistance primarily through receptor loss when grown in isolation but switches to CRISPR-based immunity in the presence of bacterial competitors. 6 , 7 Previous work showed that interspecies competition can favor CRISPR-immune bacteria over surface mutants after phage resistance has evolved. 6 However, it remains unknown whether competition also alters the initial generation of CRISPR immunity by changing CRISPR-Cas expression and spacer acquisition before selection among resistance phenotypes occurs. Here, we show that interbacterial competition can trigger CRISPR-Cas activation and adaptation in P. aeruginosa. When co-cultured with Acinetobacter baumannii, P. aeruginosa exhibited markedly increased expression of CRISPR-Cas genes and a higher frequency of new spacer acquisition, whereas no such induction occurred in monoculture or mixed communities lacking A. baumannii. This upregulation was associated with markers of DNA damage and stress signaling, indicating that competition-induced stress primes the bacterial adaptive immune response. These findings identify interbacterial antagonism as an ecological and physiological trigger for CRISPR activation, linking competitive interactions to enhanced antiphage defense. More broadly, our results suggest that bacteria sense and respond to competitive stress in complex microbial communities by increasing the generation of more adapted genotypes.

items.title: Vertical migration of short- and medium-chain chlorinated paraffins in the marine water column and sediments of the Northern Yellow Sea, China.
items.abstract: Short- and medium-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs and MCCPs) are high-production-volume persistent organic pollutants, attracting increasing global concerns. Coastal zones are suffering severe adverse impacts from SCCPs and MCCPs derived from both terrestrial discharge and marine anthropogenic activities. However, data on their occurrence, and vertical transport mechanisms within marginal sea systems remain sparse and their sources and ecological risks in marine ecosystem are poorly understood. Herein, the spatial distribution and vertical migration of MCCPs and SCCPs in surface, bottom seawater, and sediments of the Northern Yellow Sea (NYS) were systematically investigated. Results identify maritime discharge from shipping lanes and inputs from aquaculture as the primary contamination sources. Both MCCPs and SCCPs were ubiquitously found across all samples, with higher levels of SCCPs than MCCPs in sediments. Bottom seawater exhibited higher CP concentrations than surface seawater, attributing to the hydrophobicity-driven sorption to suspended particles and subsequent settling/resuspension processes. Sediment-water partitioning and fugacity fraction (ff) analyses indicated congener-specific behavior played a key role in the vertical migration of CPs. Most CP congeners showed low ff values (<0.2), confirming sediments as a primary sink, whereas congeners with shorter carbon chain and lower chlorine substitution (e.g., C10Cl5) displayed a potential for remobilization, with a mean ff value of 0.897. Ecological risk assessments revealed a medium risk in seawater, and a low but persistent risk in sediments. These findings highlight the critical roles of hydrodynamics, organic matter, and marine anthropogenic emissions in governing CP fate in the NYS coastal zones.

items.title: Assessment of trace metal concentrations in the giant mud crab Scylla olivacea and sediments from the coast of Pakistan.
items.abstract: The Pakistani coast holds economic potential through its rich marine resources, including a thriving mud crab fishery. However, it faces increasing trace metal contamination from both anthropogenic and natural sources. Coastal sediments act as reservoirs for these pollutants, facilitating their spread and endangering marine ecosystems, marine life, and human health. Hence, effective and continuous monitoring is essential to detect potential problems and ensure the safety of mud crab (Scylla olivacea) consumption. In order to provide baseline data, concentrations of 14 trace metals were measured in 24 sediment samples from eight sites and 50 mud crab claws from five sites at the Pakistani coast using Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). The Metal Pollution Index (MPI) was highest in Sandspit (75) and Keti Bandar (60). The Ecological Risk Index (RI) highlights elevated risks in Khor Kalmat, Sandspit, and Gwadar, with values exceeding 60. The Biota Sediment Accumulation Factor (BSAF) indicates bioaccumulation, with Zn (10.5) and As (5.5) in Ibrahim Hyderi and Sonmiani exceeding the threshold of 1, signalling ecological concerns. Total Hazard Index (THI) values were below 1 for all trace metals but were close to 1 for Hg (0.7) and Cu (0.7). A THI value >1 indicates potential hazard to health from trace metal ingestion through consumption of mud crabs. Lifetime cancer risk (CR) exceeded the 10 -5 threshold for As at all sites and for Cd at Ibrahim Hyderi, indicating non-negligible lifetime cancer risk.

items.title: Stress-induced maternal effects on offspring: linking multivariate egg investment to environmental quality.
items.abstract: Hormone-mediated maternal effects can shape offspring development in variable environmental conditions resulting in adaptive behavioral phenotypes. Numerous hormones can vary with environmental conditions and lead to different adaptive offspring responses. However, most of what we know about hormone-mediated maternal effects comes from studies on individual hormones even though the endocrine response to the environment is multifaceted and complex. Physiological stress responses in mothers may lead to greater offspring exposure to glucocorticoids or influence the allocation of other classes of maternal steroids (e.g. androgens, estrogens, progestogens) and any of these hormones may induce adaptive responses in offspring. Examining how the multivariate suite of yolk hormones responds to ecologically relevant environmental variation in natural systems is critical for assessing their role as potential cues of environmental conditions. Female western bluebirds (Sialia mexicana) in challenging environmental conditions have increased circulating glucocorticoids and produce better adapted offspring that are more aggressive and are more likely to disperse. We used this well-characterized adaptive maternal effect to test the functional importance of multiple classes of steroids using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS-MS). We found that in more challenging environments - fewer nest sites, smaller territories - the multivariate yolk steroid profile shifted, with the strongest change in glucocorticoid metabolites, suggesting that maternal glucocorticoid processing varies with ecological context. We also found that estrone and etiocholanolone, but not other androgens, covaried with maternal environment. Overall, our results advance our understanding of the mechanisms underlying adaptive maternal effects in nature and highlight novel steroid pathways that may influence offspring phenotypes.

items.title: Uranium retention and possible redox transformation by Sphingomonas metalli-silicate mixtures in simulated mining environments.
items.abstract: While the speciation and transport of uranium (U) in binary mineral-only or microbe-only systems have been well characterized, the coupled regulation of U(VI) retention and valence transformation at coexisting mineral-microbe interfaces remain poorly constrained. Therefore, this study investigated how Sphingomonas metalli (S. metalli), a prevalent bacterium in U mining areas, influences U(VI) sorption and redox behavior during its interaction with three representative silicate minerals with contrasting surface properties (chlorite, albite, and muscovite). Batch experiments conducted across a pH range of 5 - 10 show that a slight decrease in U sorption (up to 22%) was observed in the presence of bacteria, except for the chlorite under near-neutral conditions, with this effect becoming less pronounced under alkaline conditions (pH 8 - 10). This decrease could be due to bacteria-induced modification of mineral surfaces, e.g., mineral surface charge screening and site-blocking effects driven by EPS, and possible sorption competition between U and bacterial extracellular metabolites. Infrared spectroscopy analyses support such surface modification, showing that bacterial attachment perturbs Si-O and Al-O functional groups on mineral surfaces. In addition to sorption processes, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy suggests that a minor reduced U (as U(IV)) component may form in bacterial and mineral-bacteria systems even under aerobic conditions. Collectively, these results highlight that S. metalli acts as an interfacial regulator in microbe-mineral-U systems, suppressing mineral surface retention and inducing limited U(VI) reduction. These findings improve understanding of U partitioning in microbially active mining environments and provide a basis for more realistic assessment of uranium mobility and environmental risk.

items.title: Reed-straw configuration density in Suaeda salsa restoration: Context-dependent biological responses under controlled flooding.
items.abstract: Locally sourced reed straw may provide a biodegradable, near-natural aid for re-establishing Suaeda salsa on hydrologically variable salt-marsh surfaces. We screened no mulch and 1-, 2-, and 3-cm anchored, cross-woven configurations across three flooding depths and three daily inundation durations. The split-plot experiment comprised 36 independently operated tanks and 144 separate pots. The implemented configurations differed in standing seedling proportion, plant height, root biomass, and total biomass, and several configuration contrasts changed with hydrological treatment. A quasi-binomial mixed-model sensitivity analysis supported the early seedling result, while per-pot analyses supported the biomass result. No configuration was consistently superior, and none of the 27 hydrology-specific day-9 or day-90 treatment-versus-control contrasts remained significant after Holm adjustment. The descriptive pattern supports carrying the 2- and 3-cm configurations forward for direct comparison in a subsequent validation study; it does not establish an optimum. The experiment is therefore a controlled screen of a composite reed-straw configuration, not a test of spacing geometry alone or a field-ready restoration prescription.

items.title: Reduced Crude Protein Nutrition in Poultry: Mechanistic Links Between Nitrogen Metabolism, Gut Microbial Ecology, and Intestinal Physiology.
items.abstract: Reducing dietary crude protein (CP) has emerged as an effective nutritional strategy to improve nitrogen utilisation efficiency and reduce environmental nitrogen losses in poultry production. Beyond these practical benefits, dietary protein concentration and digestibility influence nitrogen flow, microbial substrate availability, and metabolic interactions within the gastrointestinal tract, thereby shaping host-microbiota function. This review synthesises current evidence on the mechanistic links between reduced crude protein nutrition, nitrogen metabolism, gut microbial ecology, and intestinal physiology in poultry. Quantitative evidence indicates that responses depend strongly on the magnitude of CP reduction and dietary formulation. For example, a 2-percentage-point CP reduction with balanced lysine, methionine, and threonine improved growth and intestinal morphology, whereas a 3-percentage-point reduction has been associated with decreased duodenal and ileal villus height; in contrast, a 1.5-percentage-point reduction produced no significant morphological impairment. Recent evidence further shows that a 2% lower-protein diet can increase ileal microbial richness and diversity, while bacteriophage supplementation significantly improves nitrogen digestibility (p = 0.045), and dietary protein level itself affects nitrogen digestibility (p = 0.017). Collectively, moderate CP reduction supported by adequate digestible amino acids and highly digestible ingredients can decrease undigested nitrogen flow and proteolytic fermentation while maintaining intestinal function. However, excessive protein restriction, poor amino acid balance, or reduced ingredient digestibility may disrupt microbial metabolism and compromise intestinal integrity. These findings position reduced crude protein nutrition as a precision nutritional strategy in which the magnitude of protein reduction, amino acid adequacy, digestibility, and microbial substrate availability collectively determine productive, intestinal, and environmental outcomes.

items.title: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate.
items.abstract: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

items.title: Ecological, physiological, and evolutionary drivers of stoichiometry in insects.
items.abstract: The elemental composition of organisms links physiology to biogeochemical cycles, yet the relative contributions of evolutionary divergence, ecology, and allometry to stoichiometric variation remain incompletely resolved. Here, we integrate a global insect stoichiometric database spanning 223 species with a comprehensive phylogenetic backbone to evaluate the relative importance of hypothesized ecophysiological drivers of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry within a multivariate framework. We found a strong phylogenetic signal in stoichiometric ratios and in P and N content, with evolutionary divergence (phylogenetic structure) accounting for approximately half of the explained variation in P-based ratios, exceeding the contribution of any individual ecological predictor. Phylogenetically corrected models recover trophic enrichment across successive trophic levels, consistent with previously documented patterns, and positive scaling between body mass and both C:P and N:P, in line with the general predictions of the Growth Rate Hypothesis. Temperature was the strongest ecological predictor of insect stoichiometry, with positive effects on C:P and N:P ratios and a negative effect on C:N, highlighting the thermal underpinnings of previously observed geographic patterns. Finally, our models recover higher P and lower C in terrestrial insects relative to their aquatic counterparts, contrary to classic expectations that invoke differences in structural constraints and autotrophic composition across habitats. Together, our work shows that variation in insect stoichiometry emerges from the interacting influences of evolutionary divergence and ecological and physiological variation, which can be disentangled through appropriately scaled, phylogenetically informed analyses.

items.title: A cost-effective data assimilation system for improving ROMS simulations in the Southwest Atlantic.
items.abstract: This study presents for the first time the integration of the low-cost REMO Ocean Data Assimilation System (RODAS) into the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) for assimilating Sea Surface Temperature (SST) observations. RODAS is an Ensemble Optimal Interpolation (EnOI)-based data assimilation system originally developed for use with the HYCOM model. Here, it is adapted to ROMS and applied to the Southwest Atlantic, with a focus on evaluating its impact on short-term ocean hindcasts. We conducted 4-years simulations with and without SST assimilation, referred to as RODAS_SST and Free, respectively. The RODAS_SST experiment showed a 70% reduction in SST root mean square deviation (RMSD) relative to the Free run, and a 55% reduction compared to 72-hour hindcasts generated from previous analysis cycles. When compared with the GLORYS reanalysis, SST RMSD was reduced by 64%. Ocean heat content estimates also improved, with reductions in mean absolute error of 15% during summer and 25% in winter. While assimilation improved surface and subsurface thermal structure in general, comparisons with Argo profiles revealed occasional degradations near the thermocline, highlighting the need for better multivariate covariance representation in the EnOI scheme. The successful implementation of RODAS in ROMS provides a cost-effective tool for enhancing model initial conditions and regional ocean simulations. Future developments will include the assimilation of Argo temperature and salinity profiles, sea level anomaly (SLA) data, and observations from the SWOT satellite. The code will be openly released, aiming to broaden access to ocean data assimilation by enabling robust performance even on limited computational resources.

items.title: Transparency, accountability, and scholarly integrity: A systematic narrative review of artificial intelligence governance frameworks in healthcare publication.
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare research and scholarly publication has produced a rapidly expanding but fragmented ecosystem of reporting guidelines, governance frameworks, editorial policies, and regulatory instruments, imposing significant burdens on researchers, reviewers, and editors. This systematic narrative review identified, stratified, and synthesized governance frameworks and reporting standards addressing transparent and ethical AI use in healthcare publications, and characterized the governance trajectory from predictive model standards to generative AI oversight. Fourteen Boolean search strings were executed in PubMed (MEDLINE) covering 1 January 2018-19 May 2026, supplemented by manual searching of the EQUATOR Network guideline library. Records were deduplicated and prioritized using a relevance-scoring algorithm. Of 30,276 deduplicated records, 888 progressed to human screening; 100 publications were included, comprising 69 governance instruments and policies classified across four evidence tiers and 31 contextual evidence sources. Included sources spanned six thematic groups: predictive and diagnostic AI frameworks (G1); sociotechnical and lifecycle governance (G2); generative AI and LLM-specific standards (G3); specialty-specific extensions (G4); surgical reporting updates (G5); and editorial and publication policy (G6). Analysis identified four consecutive phases of governance development from 2018 to 2026, characterized by a shift from model performance transparency toward comprehensive sociotechnical accountability. Three governance tensions emerged: the trade-off between framework specificity and universal applicability; the gap between disclosure-focused standards and lifecycle governance; and the risk of epistemic conflation, whereby heterogeneous instruments are perceived as carrying equivalent authority when treated as interchangeable. AI governance in healthcare publications remains fragmented and epistemically uneven. Advancing the field requires harmonization across evidence tiers, adaptive updating mechanisms, and lifecycle-oriented governance frameworks.

items.title: Small waterways in boreal forests: How artificial waterways influence benthic macroinvertebrate communities.
items.abstract: Across the boreal biome, extensive ditching and stream modification have created widespread networks of artificial waterways. These channels now form a major part of Sweden's aquatic landscape but remain poorly studied despite their potential ecological role. We surveyed 32 reaches representing natural streams, modified waterways, and ditches on peat and till soils to assess how habitat conditions and benthic macroinvertebrate communities vary across this gradient of naturalness. Natural streams supported higher taxa richness than ditches, while overall diversity and abundance were similar across waterway types. Peat ditches were distinguished by low pH and high organic substrates, whereas till ditches and modified waterways closely resembled natural streams, suggesting ecological convergence over time. Similar to studies done in purely natural systems, catchment area and pH were key predictors of taxa richness in our gradient of naturalness. Our results indicate that modified waterways contain similar biodiversity to natural streams and that soil type is more important for biodiversity than waterway origin, providing a baseline for conservation and restoration planning in managed forest landscapes.

items.title: Effects of a three-year maize-soybean rotation on soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing Fusarium spp. inoculum potential.
items.abstract: Maize-soybean succession dominates grain production in tropical Brazil, and rotation is often recommended to improve soil health. However, few field studies have followed both soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing pathogens over several seasons in tropical no-till systems. We compared continuous maize, continuous soybean and maize-soybean rotation for three seasons (2016-2017 to 2018-2019). In a fourth season (2019-2020), maize was grown in all plots to test legacy effects. Bacterial communities were profiled by 16 S rRNA (V3-V4) amplicon sequencing. The fum1 gene of fumonisin-producing Fusarium spp. was quantified by qPCR in soil and in maize stalks left on the soil surface. In the first three seasons, rotation did not detectably increase bacterial diversity, although statistical power was low (n = 4 plots; post-hoc power 12-61%). Community composition differed among seasons and was associated with antecedent precipitation as Actinobacteria were most abundant in the driest season. In the fourth season, a continuous-soybean history was associated with higher bacterial richness and Shannon diversity in the maize rhizosphere at tasselling than a rotation history, whereas bulk-soil diversity did not differ among land uses. A rotation history was associated with lower fum1 abundance in bulk soil. In contrast, continuous maize was associated with lower fum1 in stalks (third season), less stalk rot and fewer infected grains. Soil and crop residues therefore responded differently to rotation. Given the single site and limited plot-level replication, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

items.title: Mercury dynamics in surface-active soil invertebrates from an ecological reserve in the Brazilian savanna.
items.abstract: This study evaluated total mercury (THg) distribution and accumulation in soil, litter, and surface-active soil invertebrates at the Águas Emendadas Ecological Station (ESECAE), a savanna reserve in central Brazil. We assessed whether THg differed between soil and litter; whether soil pH and organic matter influenced soil THg, the degree of THg accumulation in invertebrates relative to soil and litter; whether feeding habits structured epigeic soil fauna according to THg concentrations; and whether biomagnification could be inferred within the local trophic network. THg concentrations were significantly higher in litter (51.7 ± 5.6 ng g⁻ 1 ) than in soil (34.9 ± 13.5 ng g⁻ 1 ; t = 4.402, df = 7, p = 0.0032). Soil organic matter was positively associated with soil THg (R 2 = 0.455, p = 0.039), whereas pH showed no significant relationship. Invertebrate THg concentrations ranged from 0.095 to 970.70 ng g⁻ 1 , reaching values approximately 15 times higher than those in soil or litter. Overall, 83.75% of samples showed bioaccumulation potential, and macroaccumulation predominated relative to both soil (80.38%) and litter (68.53%). Grouping by feeding habits revealed consistent accumulation patterns, indicating trophic-level biomagnification. Predator frequency increased from 9.1% in the lowest THg group to 45.5% in the highest, while phytophagous organisms decreased from 26.1% to 2.3%. Our results underscore the complexity of mercury cycling in terrestrial food webs and highlight the role of ecological traits and environmental parameters in modulating mercury bioavailability and transfer.

items.title: Genome-wide characterization of DUB genes in Betula platyphylla and BpUBP3 function in pollen tube growth.
items.abstract: The ubiquitination/deubiquitination system is a key regulatory mechanism for maintaining proteome homeostasis in eukaryotic cells. Deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs), which remove ubiquitin from substrate proteins, regulate plant development, stress responses, and other physiological processes. Although DUBs have emerged as important regulators of plant growth and stress responses, their systematic genomic characterization in white birch (Betula platyphylla) remains limited, restricting our understanding of their potential roles in the reproduction of woody plants. In this study, 56 BpDUB genes were identified in white birch (Betula platyphylla) and classified into six conserved subfamilies (UBP, OTU, UCH, MJD, JAMM, and MINDY). Comparative and synteny analyses revealed that DUB genes are evolutionarily conserved while exhibiting lineage-specific divergence across angiosperms. Promoter analysis showed that BpDUBs harbor diverse cis-acting elements associated with growth and development, stress responses, hormone signaling, and transcription factor binding. Treatment with the broad-spectrum DUB inhibitor PR-619 markedly impaired both pollen germination and pollen tube elongation, supporting the involvement of DUB activity in pollen development. RNA-seq analysis showed that BpUBP3 exhibited stage-specific induction during pollen germination, and AS-ODN-mediated downregulation of BpUBP3 reduced pollen germination and pollen tube growth. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting a role for BpUBP3 in pollen germination and pollen tube growth and provide a basis for further investigation of DUB functions in reproductive development in white birch.

items.title: The missing metric in ecological studies: Land tenure system of territorial carnivores.
items.abstract: Land tenure is a fundamental ecological process in territorial animals; it reflects how individuals establish and maintain access to space and resources. First conceptualised by Hornocker in 1969, it provides an early understanding of population dynamics. However, this critical aspect for interpreting the stability, predictability and exclusivity of a population is rarely evaluated. To date, there has been no clear ecological definition of the land tenure system. To understand this concept, we review more than 50 years of research on territorial carnivores and synthesise how land tenure has been quantified across taxa. We examine how this aspect links population and demographic processes that lead to species conservation in various landscape scenarios. The goal is to develop a standardised approach across species and landscapes to evaluate land tenure by providing a framework and testable hypotheses. As land tenure provides critical insights into the spatial stability of populations and informs conservation planning, its limited integration into ecological studies remains concerning despite advances in population ecology and monitoring technologies. We attempted to build a foundation for future research that aims to measure population stability and species persistence.

items.title: Environmental and human-related gradients shape the community structure of medium and large terrestrial mammals in a central Amazonian white-sand Forest.
items.abstract: Medium- and large-sized terrestrial mammals play key ecological roles in tropical forests; however, the relative importance of environmental filters and anthropogenic disturbances in structuring their assemblages in Amazonian campinarana (white-sand) ecosystems remains poorly understood. In this study, we evaluated the influence of these factors on species composition and habitat use by medium- and large-sized terrestrial mammals, as well as by the frugivore-herbivore guild in Amazonian campinarana ecosystems. We used camera traps and structural equation modelling. We recorded 22 species over 4721 camera-trap days, with assemblages dominated by frugivore-herbivores and by dietary and habitat generalists, such as the common opossum (Didelphis marsupialis). Habitat use by the overall mammal assemblage was higher in areas with lower vegetation height, whereas terrain elevation relative to the nearest drainage (HAND index) had an indirect effect mediated by vegetation structure. In contrast, frugivore-herbivore species showed more selective responses, with higher habitat-use intensity in areas farther from human influence. Mammal assemblages were predominantly influenced by distance to houses, whereas the composition of the frugivore-herbivore guild was associated with distance to houses and tree height. Our results demonstrate that even low levels of human presence are sufficient to structure mammal assemblages, reinforcing the need for spatially explicit management strategies aimed at conserving the functional integrity of these unique and highly sensitive ecosystems.

items.title: Megafaunal engineering in the tropical rainforest: African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) reduce avian species richness but elevate functional diversity.
items.abstract: African forest elephants (Loxodonta cyclotis) are critically endangered ecosystem engineers of African tropical forests. Despite their rapidly declining population trend, little is known of how forest elephants interact with other vertebrate assemblages. To explore this, we studied avian communities within a continuous tropical rainforest on the slopes of Mt. Cameroon. The area's topography allowed us to survey birds in elephant-grazed primary forest and in adjacent portions that elephants avoid, isolating the effect of megafaunal grazing within an otherwise intact system. We additionally surveyed nearby secondary forests fragmented by human activity, contrasting the disappearance of a single ecosystem engineer against the reshaping of forest by anthropogenic disturbance. We assessed the taxonomic diversity (species richness, Shannon index), functional diversity (Rao's quadratic entropy), functional redundancy (species overlap in functional space), and composition of functional traits (abundance-weighted trait averages). Previous research suggested that loss of forest elephants would negatively impact avian assemblages through reduced habitat heterogeneity. In contrast, we show that elephant grazing itself significantly reduced species richness, to levels comparable with heavily disturbed secondary forests. Functional diversity nevertheless increased in both the grazed and secondary forest, but at the cost of functional redundancy: in both of these habitats, the avian assemblages were taxonomically impoverished, yet functionally more dispersed, with some foraging niches negatively affected. The elephant-grazed forest was dominated by understory and terrestrial invertivores, whereas the ungrazed forest supported frugivores and larger birds. The secondary forest, in turn, harboured a functionally distinct assemblage of open-habitat species with high dispersal ability and divergent foraging strategies. Together these patterns show that although elephant grazing reduces taxonomic diversity to a degree comparable with anthropogenic disturbance, it reshapes functional composition in fundamentally different ways. The presence of forest elephants facilitates stable populations of forest specialist birds, such as terrestrial invertivores. Conversely, the adverse effects of elephant grazing on frugivores and large birds could be minimized by establishing larger reserves of lightly grazed forest, possibly alongside ungrazed refuges. Overall, our results show that loss of keystone megaherbivores has widespread consequences for other rainforest vertebrates, potentially resulting in a cascading restructuring of key ecosystem functions.

items.title: Human hunters-still poorly understood-likely cannot mimic the roles of disappearing top predators.
items.abstract: Research Highlight: Geng, Y., Mammides, C., He, R.-C., Wang, L., Luo, K., Zhang, Z.-Y., Wang, B., & Quan, R.-C. (2026). Human hunters are no substitute for vanishing apex predators. Journal of Animal Ecology, 1-13. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2656.70306. As large carnivores decline and humans rise to become the planet's most influential predator, scant consideration has been given to the functional roles of hunters (and fishers) in ecological communities. In novel, landscape-scale work, Geng et al. (2026) ask whether hunters can serve similar roles as the predators they are replacing. Camera-trap records from 400 sites characterized as apex predator-dominated, hunter-dominated and predator-absent were analysed across multiple ecological measures. Apex predator-dominated sites hosted ~30% more species and nearly 50% greater abundances of mammals. Network measures of prey populations were most robust at apex predator sites and weakest at hunter-dominated sites. Finally, prey showed up to 2.6 times longer avoidance times following hunter presence. These striking patterns suggest that hunters do not replicate the ecological influence of the area's vanishing predators. Work like this can benefit from much more data about human predators. Specifically, ecologists can confront in careful ways the conceptual, methodological and ethical constraints of studying our own species as predators. Outcomes could include greater knowledge about the ecological influence of the planet's 'super predator', the underlying mechanisms, and related insight to apply to mitigation.

items.title: Nanoscale pesticide delivery suppresses pathogens and enriches beneficial microbiomes for safer crop protection.
items.abstract: Nanocarrier-based pesticide delivery platforms substantially boost agrochemical utilization efficiency, yet their cascading ecological repercussions for rhizosphere and soil microbial ecology remain insufficiently understood. Here, a star polycation (SPc) nanocarrier was employed to construct a matrine nano-formulation (MT@SPc) with typical nano-pesticide characteristics. MT@SPc and commercial matrine formulation (MT SL) were employed as representative systems to further evaluate their impacts on rhizosphere and soil microbial ecosystems. Compared with MT SL, MT@SPc reshaped rhizosphere microbial communities by suppressing phytopathogens and promoting the enrichment of beneficial bacteria. Further validation using four representative bacterial isolates obtained from soil demonstrated that MT@SPc significantly inhibited the growth of the phytopathogen Pectobacterium carotovorum, whereas enriched beneficial bacteria exhibited lower susceptibility to MT@SPc. Multi-scale mechanistic analyses revealed that MT@SPc could interact with bacterial cell surfaces through physicochemical interactions, resulting in pronounced surface deformation and structural damage in P. carotovorum. Multi-omics analyses associated with physiological and biochemical assays further demonstrated that MT@SPc disrupted cell wall and membrane integrity, leading to ionic imbalance, metabolite leakage and oxidative stress. However, beneficial bacteria maintained higher stability, and their enrichment was associated with microbial community shifts following pathogen suppression. Overall, this study reveals that nano-pesticides drive rhizosphere community restructuring through differential microbial responses, providing mechanistic insights into nano-pesticide-microbiome interactions in complex ecological systems.

items.title: Live biotherapeutics in the post-antibiotic era: exploring the potential of probiotics to counter multidrug resistance.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat that compromises the effectiveness of existing antibiotics and highlights the urgent need for alternative and adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Probiotics have emerged as potential adjunctive strategies because of their ability to modulate host-microbe interactions and influence microbial ecology without promoting resistance. This review examines the current evidence on the potential role of probiotics in combating multidrug-resistant organisms, based on findings from in vitro studies, animal models, and clinical investigations. The review is based on a narrative literature search of the PubMed database, covering studies published between 2020 and 2025, with earlier landmark studies. The mechanisms discussed include competitive exclusion of pathogens, the production of antimicrobial compounds, the enhancement of intestinal barrier function, and the modulation of host immune responses. In addition, probiotics are evaluated for their capacity to interfere with quorum sensing and inhibit biofilm formation, thereby reducing pathogen virulence and colonization. The review also addresses key limitations, including strain-specific variability, safety concerns in vulnerable populations, and the lack of standardized clinical protocols. Current evidence suggests that probiotics may represent a useful adjunct to existing AMR management strategies. However, their broader clinical application requires larger research to establish their efficacy and safety.

items.title: "A Minefield for the Novice": Australian Women's Experiences Seeking Health Information Online About Perimenopause.
items.abstract: During perimenopause, many women experience psychological and physiological symptoms that can seriously impact quality of life and future health. However, they report challenges accessing appropriate information and medical support, likely exacerbated by clinician knowledge gaps, stigma, and a persistent lack of research, consistent with a documented pattern of structural sexism in health systems. Consequently, women increasingly turn to alternative sources, particularly online, for support. Although scholarship exists on online health-information seeking and women's digital health engagement, limited research examines how women navigate online health information under clinical and structural invalidation. This study gathered responses from 58 perimenopausal women through an online qualitative survey and constructed three themes using reflexive thematic analysis: (a) the search for validation; (b) trust erosion and the support gap; and (c) self-efficacy, agency and kinship. Interpreted through an epistemic injustice lens, the findings indicated that participants used digital literacy strategies to reassert epistemic standing and compensate for structural lack of support, yet were left to navigate variable-quality health information. Therefore, health information providers and policymakers should acknowledge perimenopausal complexity, model knowledge-appraisal strategies rather than present information as resolved, and mandate training to address the support gap. Health professionals should also validate women's epistemic standing before clinically interpreting symptoms.

items.title: EXPRESS: Cardio‑Glymphatic Association: Left‑Heart Dysfunction in CSVD and Its Association With Glymphatic‑Related Cognitive Impairment.
items.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a leading cause of vascular cognitive impairment. The glymphatic system, a brain-wide waste clearance pathway, may be impaired in CSVD, but its upstream drivers and role linking systemic factors to cognitive impairment remain unclear. This study explored whether glymphatic dysfunction statistically mediates the association between left-heart dysfunction and cognitive impairment in CSVD. We enrolled 80 CSVD-VCI, 80 CSVD-NCI, and 80 normal controls aged 50-80 years. All participants underwent neuropsychological assessment, cardiac ultrasound (measuring left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF], left ventricular end-diastolic diameter [LVEDD], and left atrial diameter [LAD]), and brain MRI to measure the DTI-ALPS index of glymphatic activity. The DTI-ALPS index was progressively reduced: NC > CSVD-NCI > CSVD-VCI. It correlated positively with LVEF and negatively with LAD, and was associated with multiple cognitive domains. Mediation analysis suggests that DTI-ALPS statistically significantly mediated the effects of LVEF and LAD on cognitive performance. These cross-sectional findings suggest that glymphatic dysfunction is a key feature of CSVD and may represent a potential correlative link connecting left-heart dysfunction to cognitive impairment, consistent with a potential cardio-glymphatic pathway in CSVD pathophysiology.

items.title: Shared variance across FrACT visual tasks: Robust positive associations but inconclusive latent structure.
items.abstract: A long-standing question in vision science is whether individual differences in visual performance reflect a general visual ability or a set of largely task-specific processes. Previous studies have often reported weak associations across heterogeneous perceptual tasks, challenging the idea of a common visual factor. Here, we asked whether shared variance becomes more evident when visual tasks are conceptually and procedurally similar. One hundred fifty-eight adults completed eight low-level acuity and hyperacuity paradigms implemented in FrACT 10 : single letter, Landolt C, tumbling E, row of optotypes, flanking rings, frame ring, Vernier two-line, and Vernier three-line tasks. After outlier exclusion, analyses were conducted on 132 participants. Within-session test-retest reliability was moderate for most tasks. Pairwise correlations revealed a broad positive manifold: all correlations were positive, 27 of 28 survived false-discovery-rate correction, and Bayesian analyses provided strong evidence for nonzero associations in most task pairs. However, association strength depended strongly on task similarity, with robust correlations among optotype-based tasks and weaker links between optotype and Vernier paradigms. Exploratory factor analyses indicated substantial shared covariance but failed to support a stable latent structure: A one-factor model fit poorly, whereas two-factor and three-factor solutions produced improper estimates. These findings support an intermediate account of visual individual differences. Visual performance is neither fully independent across tasks nor reducible to a strong general visual factor; instead, commonality appears partial, task-dependent, and shaped by the composition of the task battery. The study materials are described in the Method section and are based on FrACT 10 . This study was not preregistered.

items.title: Self-Harm Ideation in Perinatal Mothers in Home Visiting Programs.
items.abstract: Objectives To examine the prevalence and predictors of self-harm ideation during the perinatal period among mothers (N = 9638) enrolled in a home visiting program. Methods Subjects were all mothers enrolled in a home visiting program in the United States between 2006 and 2023 who completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS; Cox et al., 1987) prenatally and/or at up to 6 months postpartum. Item 10 of the EPDS, reflecting thoughts of self-harm, was used to operationalize self-harm ideation and severity. Demographic and clinical variables were examined as predictors of self-harm ideation and change over the two time points. Results 6.8% of the sample reported self-harm ideation prenatally, with 33.8% of these mothers endorsing the two highest levels of severity. 4.0% of the sample reported self-harm ideation postnatally. Of those who reported self-harm ideation prenatally, 77.9% no longer reported it postnatally. Reporting of self-harm ideation was associated with mean EPDS scores above the established clinical cutoff (≥ 13). Younger mothers reported higher levels of ideation compared with older mothers. Conclusions for practice A large proportion of mothers reported self-harm ideation prenatally, and younger mothers reported higher levels of ideation compared with older mothers. Given the dangers of unrecognized and untreated suicide risk in perinatal mothers, home visitors are in a unique and important position to support and link mothers to mental health services.

items.title: Effect sizes for brain-based predictive models of cognition across the lifespan.
items.abstract: Brain-based predictive models offer a promising approach to understanding individual differences in cognitive functioning across the lifespan. This review synthesizes current literature on brain-based cognitive predictions using large-scale datasets, examining how methodological choices and data-related factors impact model performance. We find that brain-based predictive models demonstrate relatively consistent, albeit wide ranging performance across the lifespan, explaining approximately 10-40% of variance in cognitive abilities. Key findings include: (1) models perform better when predicting general cognitive ability compared to specific functions; (2) crystallized abilities are more predictable than fluid abilities; (3) task-based functional connectivity generally outperforms resting-state approaches in younger populations, while structural measures become superior predictors in older adults; (4) multimodal approaches using hierarchical stacked models optimize prediction accuracy; and (5) elastic net and ridge regression provide optimal balance between predictive performance and computational efficiency. In summary, we propose methodological advances to improve the precision and utility of brain-based cognitive predictions.

items.title: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: This study examined age-related differences in behavior and brain dynamics underlying cognitive-motor interference (CMI) during motor dual-tasks (DT) with increasing motor task complexity. Behavioral performance and electrocortical activity were assessed in 19 younger adults (11 males, 8 females; 25.5 ± 2.3 years) and 11 older adults (6 males, 5 females; 72.6 ± 4.6 years) using mobile electroencephalography (EEG). Participants performed an oddball choice-reaction task under three conditions: sitting, standing, and treadmill walking. Event-related potential (ERPs; P1, N1, P3) amplitudes and latencies, response times, postural sway, and gait parameters were recorded to evaluate CMI. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVAs with within-subject factors of motor condition and stimulus type and age group as a between-subject factor. Older adults exhibited reduced step length compared to younger adults, but no DT-related changes in gait or postural sway were observed. Response times were generally slower in older adults and increased from sitting to standing and walking whereas younger adults showed slowing only from sitting to standing. Early sensory ERP components (P1, N1) demonstrated increased amplitudes with higher motor demands. The P3 component was reduced in amplitude in both groups during walking, with delayed latencies in older adults. For both groups, P3 latencies were associated with prolonged response times. Our findings suggest that this slowing during walking reflects altered cognitive resource allocation, characterized by delayed central information processing and enhanced early visual processing, rather than impaired peripheral motor coordination.

items.title: The effects of an online mindfulness-based intervention for parents of children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
items.abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have been identified as a complementary treatment for children with ADHD. While there is a growing interest in developing MBIs in online formats, its application in parents is largely based on healthy populations. A two-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) was designed to investigate the effectiveness of an online MBI (arm 1) compared with an online psychoeducation (PSY) program (arm 2). Outcomes were measured before the intervention, after the intervention, and at 3-month follow-up. A total of 248 parents whose children with ADHD symptoms aged 6 to 12 years old participated in the study, with 131 parents assigned to the online MBI group and 117 to the PSY group. Both groups indicated significant and lasting improvements in their children's ADHD symptoms, executive functioning, and parental well-being. In addition, parental stress levels and two dimensions of expressed emotion, including critical comments and initial statements, decreased significantly in both groups. Notably, a specific benefit of the online MBI was identified for insomnia. A small-magnitude improvement in parent-child relationship quality, as a dimension of expressed emotion, was observed in the repeated measures ANOVA but was not consistently supported by the sensitivity analysis. Future studies should verify the specific and sustainable treatment effects of MBIs, strengthening parental engagement and support.

items.title: Motor planning in Colombian spider monkeys (Ateles fusciceps rufiventris).
items.abstract: The morphological constraint hypothesis suggests that primates with less dexterity show more consistent motor planning because there is less flexibility to compensate for inefficient actions. Spiders monkeys offer a unique opportunity to test this hypothesis because they do not have a functional thumb. Colombian spider monkeys (Ateles fusciceps rufiventris, n=8) housed at a wildlife park were tested on a standard motor planning task. A trial began when a dowel baited on one end was placed on an elevated apparatus and ended when a monkey grasped the dowel with the hands. Grip use was coded from video as radial (pronated overhand grip with the radius bone towards food) or non-radial. The percentage of radial grips was used in analyses for comparison to other platyrrhines. As a group, spider monkeys used a radial grip significantly more than chance (M ± SD=73.38% ± 18.91), indicating spider monkeys engage in second-order motor planning. Spider monkeys differed in radial grip use from captive cotton-top tamarins (Saguinus oedipus) but not captive (Sapajus spp) or wild capuchins (Sapajus libidinosus) tested on the elevated dowel task in prior work by other investigators. Together, these findings have mixed implications for the morphological constraint hypothesis that merit further study.

items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of emotion regulation-based therapy on emotion regulation, cognitive flexibility, and symptom severity in patients with irritable bowel syndrome. Method In this randomized controlled trial, 40 patients with irritable bowel syndrome (diagnosed according to Rome IV criteria) referred to Hospital (2025) were randomly assigned to experimental and control groups (20 per group); 36 participants completed the study (18 per group). The control group received usual medical care. Data were collected using the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ), Cognitive Flexibility Inventory (CFI), and Functional Bowel Disorder Symptom Severity Scale (FS-BSS) at pretest, posttest, and three-month follow-up, and analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA in SPSS 26.
