items.title: Health starts with the skin! Risk and protective psychological processes linking distress to quality of life in chronic dermatological conditions.
items.abstract: Background Chronic dermatological conditions, particularly psoriasis, are associated with substantial psychological burden and impaired quality of life. However, the psychosocial factors accounting for the relationship between psychological distress, dermatology-specific quality of life, and overall life satisfaction remain insufficiently understood. Objective This study examined key risk and protective psychological factors associated with the relationship between distress and well-being among individuals with psoriasis and other chronic dermatological conditions. Methods A total of 108 adults diagnosed with psoriasis or other chronic skin diseases (mean age = 48.32 years; 67.6% women) completed validated self-report measures assessing psychological distress, affect, acceptance of living with the disease, perceived stigma, social anxiety, perceived social support, self-compassion, mindfulness, dermatology-related quality of life, and satisfaction with life. Parallel mediation analyses were conducted while controlling for age and sex. Results Higher psychological distress was statistically associated with greater impairment in dermatology-related quality of life both directly and indirectly through several psychosocial processes. Negative affect and perceived stigma were associated with greater distress-related impairment in dermatological quality of life, whereas acceptance of living with the disease emerged as a protective factor associated with lower impairment. In contrast, the indirect association between distress and lower life satisfaction was statistically accounted for by maladaptive self-compassion components, specifically isolation and over-identification. Dispositional mindfulness and perceived social support did not show significant mediating effects. Conclusions The findings highlight distinct psychological factors associated with distress and reduced well-being in individuals with chronic dermatological conditions. Acceptance-related processes may protect against dermatology-specific quality of life impairment, whereas stigma and negative affect are associated with greater vulnerability. In addition, self-critical and isolating responses to distress appear particularly relevant for diminished life satisfaction. These results support the integration of acceptance-based, compassion-focused, and stigma-reduction approaches within psycho-dermatological care.

items.title: Changes in students' self-reported psychological flexibility scores and teacher-rated behavioral difficulties during a year-long, teacher-delivered social-emotional learning curriculum based on acceptance and commitment therapy.
items.abstract: This study examined longitudinal changes and social validity during implementation of a culturally adapted, teacher-delivered social-emotional learning curriculum grounded in acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) and applied behavior analysis (ABA) in Czech public primary schools. Participants were 448 children in Grades 2-5 from 23 classrooms across 10 schools. The year-long program was implemented as part of routine classroom practice, with assessments at baseline, midyear, and post-implementation. Students completed a shortened Czech adaptation of the Children's Psychological Flexibility Questionnaire (CPFQ), and teachers completed the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) and rated program social validity. Psychometric evaluation indicated substantial limitations in the CPFQ, including suboptimal factorial fit and low reliability of some subscales; the Present Moment subscale was excluded from longitudinal analyses, and changes in the remaining subscale scores were treated as exploratory. Linear mixed-effects models showed small increases in Acceptance and Defusion subscale scores, no clear linear change in Self-as-Context or Values scores, and a small decrease in Committed Action scores. Teacher-rated SDQ outcomes showed consistent changes in a favorable direction, including teacher-perceived reductions in emotional symptoms, conduct problems, hyperactivity, peer problems, and total difficulties, alongside increased prosocial behavior. Because the same teachers delivered the curriculum and rated children's behavior, with no parent, independent, or blinded assessments, these findings reflect teacher-perceived change. Teachers generally evaluated the program favorably while identifying time demands as the main constraint on implementation. Overall, the findings document favorable changes during implementation, particularly in teacher-rated functioning, while highlighting limitations in the measurement of psychological flexibility and the need for controlled evaluation.

items.title: Family History of Eating Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesise the available literature on the prevalence of a family history of eating disorders (ED) among individuals with EDs. Method A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and APA PsycInfo. Studies were included if they reported prevalence estimates of a family history of EDs. PRISMA guidelines were followed. Study selection was conducted through independent, blinded screening by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist. Results were synthesised narratively and pooled using meta-analysis of prevalence estimates. Results A total of 45 studies (N = 47,045) were included in the review, of which 32 were eligible for meta-analysis. The meta-analysis estimated that 18.1% of individuals with an ED had one or more relatives with a current or past ED. Considerable between-study heterogeneity was observed, although there was no evidence of publication bias. Conclusions This systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrates that EDs aggregate within families, particularly among first-degree relatives, supporting familial liability to EDs. These findings underscore the importance of considering family history in both clinical assessment and future research. Further studies are needed to address evidence gaps and to place greater emphasis on underrepresented populations.

items.title: Clinical Hypnosis for Osteoarthritis and Arthritis-Related Pain: A Systematic Review and Critical Synthesis.
items.abstract: Osteoarthritis and arthritis related pain can lead to functional limitation, reduced mobility, and poorer quality of life. This systematic review examined the potential role of clinical hypnosis as an adjunctive intervention for adults with osteoarthritis or arthritis related pain in routine care and perioperative settings. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria, including five randomized controlled trials and three nonrandomized single group studies, with 281 participants overall. Across included studies, clinical hypnosis was associated with improvement in pain related distress, anxiety, catastrophizing, pain interference, and in some studies reduced medication use. Findings support the potential value of clinical hypnosis as an adjunctive approach for symptom management and perioperative support in osteoarthritis and arthritis related pain, while further well designed trials are needed.

items.title: Clinical Hypnosis for Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Chronic non-cancer pain requires multimodal management, and clinical hypnosis has been examined as a complementary intervention. This PRISMA ScR scoping review mapped the extent and characteristics of the evidence base, intervention features, and research gaps for clinical hypnosis in chronic non-cancer pain. We included 48 intervention studies involving 3,166 participants, encompassing randomized controlled trials and other study designs. Hypnosis was applied to nociceptive, neuropathic, nociplastic, and mixed pain presentations using diverse techniques and delivery formats. Outcomes most frequently included pain intensity and pain related distress, with additional measures of coping, sleep, and daily functioning. The mapped literature commonly involved small samples, frequent use of passive comparators, limited demographic reporting and diversity, and variable intervention reporting. This review extends prior syntheses by detailing how clinical hypnosis has been operationalized for chronic non-cancer pain and by identifying methodological and reporting gaps to guide future research.

items.title: Development and validation of the anxious behaviors questionnaire (ABQ) in older adults.
items.abstract: Objectives Research on GAD in older adults-and the overt behaviors that may contribute to it-remains limited. Evaluating behaviors with age-appropriate tools may improve GAD diagnosis in older adults. This paper describes the development and psychometric evaluation of a self-report measure of behaviors associated with GAD: the Anxious Behaviors Questionnaire (ABQ). Study 1 explored the factor structure using exploratory factor analysis (EFA). Study 2 evaluated the resulting structure using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and examined additional psychometric properties. Methods In Study 1, the ABQ was administered to 303 French-Canadian older adults. In Study 2, it was administered to 361 older adults, who also completed measures of GAD symptoms and avoidant and safety behaviors associated with GAD to assess convergent validity. The ABQ was re-administered three weeks later to assess test-retest reliability. Results EFAs and CFAs supported the five-factor model (Overpreparation, Avoidance, Control, Reassurance-seeking, and Procrastination). The 23-item ABQ demonstrated adequate model fit, with results supporting its internal consistency, convergent validity, and temporal stability. Conclusion The ABQ is the first questionnaire to measure behaviors associated with GAD specifically among older adults. It has several advantages for researchers and clinicians: it measures distinct behaviors briefly, making it suitable for aging populations.

items.title: Ethnic identity commitment, exploration, and alcohol use among students at a historically black college/university.
items.abstract: Objective To examine whether ethnic identity commitment and exploration are associated with alcohol use among historically black college and university (HBCU) students; experiential avoidance was examined as a coping-related correlate. Participants Participants were 230 undergraduates at a large southeastern HBCU; 95.7% were ages 18-24, 74% were women, and 90.4% identified as Black. Methods Students completed self-report measures of alcohol use, ethnic identity dimensions, experiential avoidance, and demographics. Hierarchical regressions tested direct associations; exploratory bootstrap models tested indirect effects. Results Stronger commitment was associated with lower alcohol use, whereas exploration was not significantly associated with alcohol use. Experiential avoidance was not directly associated with alcohol use but was associated with lower commitment and exploration. Exploratory indirect associations between experiential avoidance and alcohol use through commitment and exploration were nonsignificant after correction for multiple testing. Conclusions Findings extend prior ethnic identity and alcohol research by examining commitment and exploration separately in an HBCU sample. Commitment may be the more alcohol-relevant ethnic identity dimension, whereas experiential avoidance may be more closely related to identity processes than drinking.

items.title: Searching for the Pattern: Understanding, Assessing, and Transforming Social Settings.
items.abstract: A historical analysis of systems theory ideas from the biological and physical sciences reveals their infusion into sociology and action-oriented subfields of psychology, including social, organizational, developmental, and community psychology. Constructs and processes are identified that are useful for creating a framework to understand, assess, and transform social settings. The central theoretical concept that surfaces is the emergent pattern of dynamic transactions that communicates critical information and meaning, referred to as "social regularity." This is followed by an examination of the varying definitions and frameworks of proximal social settings (e.g., classrooms, community-based organizations, workplaces) in which individuals derive the bulk of their experiences in forming their character, identity, learning, and well-being. Social regularity is at the core of an evolving social-setting model that communicates meaning through several channels-control and power, modes of expressing communication, and the flow of information-that result in corresponding distributional equity outcomes. From these communication channels, an action model for transforming social settings to create more equitable aggregate-level individual outcomes and improved setting outcomes is explicated. Corresponding methods of measurement are described. Various strategies and tactics are suggested to directly target social regularities. Relational-, norm-, and structural-focused examples are provided.

items.title: Ask the experts: a practitioner-centred approach to resilience in emergency medical services.
items.abstract: Background: Resilience in high-stress occupations is commonly framed as a trait, an outcome, or the absence of psychopathology. None of these framings captures what practitioners in emergency medical services actually do, and interventions built on trait-based models have produced weak or inconsistent effects. Objective: This study argues that frontline resilience in emergency medical services is better understood as a domain-specific expert skill, and that work mode - a deliberately entered state, akin to an athlete's game face, in which the demands of the task rather than the emotional force of the scene govern functioning - is its central empirical signature. The aims were to identify factors that intensify traumatic impact, characterise the strategies practitioners use to maintain functioning, and explore systemic and relational barriers that constrain coping. Method: Twenty Queensland Ambulance Service paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2-38 years) participated in semi-structured interviews, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Three intensifiers of traumatic impact (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) defined the operational demands against which resilience was enacted. Three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode , social scaffolding) described the architecture of sustained functioning. Work mode exhibited the defining features of skilled performance: domain specificity, a phased temporal structure (preparation, containment, recovery), and a developmental trajectory from effortful to automatic execution. Two further themes (organisational distrust, the outsider gap) described the systemic and relational conditions that constrain coping. Conclusions: Treating resilience as expertise shifts the field from descriptive stressor-outcome accounts towards assessable, trainable capacities, and exposes the limitations of trait-based self-report measures that cannot distinguish genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism.

items.title: Complex post-traumatic stress disorder in refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced people: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background: Forcibly displaced populations, including refugees, asylum seekers, and internally displaced persons, are frequently exposed to severe, prolonged and repeated trauma from which escape is difficult or impossible. Such exposures increase the risk for complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD), defined by core PTSD symptoms alongside disturbances in self-organisation (DSO), including affective dysregulation, negative self-concept, and relational difficulties. However, the prevalence of CPTSD in forcibly displaced populations has not yet been quantitatively synthesised, and the added value of the CPTSD construct over PTSD in this population has not been examined. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis searched five databases from inception to January 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate pooled CPTSD prevalence, with pre-specified subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Results: Twenty studies met inclusion criteria, representing 17 independent samples ( n = 12,504). Reported CPTSD prevalence varied from 3.0% to 74.6%. The random-effects pooled prevalence, retained as a descriptive summary of the included studies, was 20.9% (95% CI [12.6%, 32.6%]), the 95% prediction interval was [1.7%, 80.3%]. Between-study heterogeneity was very high ( I² = 98.3%). Recruitment context was strongly associated with prevalence: estimates averaged 10.6% in community-based samples and 55.2% in treatment-seeking samples. Asylum seekers exhibited markedly higher prevalence than refugees. Across four studies, post-migration living difficulties, including legal insecurity, poverty, and marginalisation, were more strongly associated with DSO symptoms than with core PTSD symptoms, suggesting that ongoing structural adversity actively perpetuates complex trauma psychopathology beyond pre-migration trauma alone. Conclusion: Available evidence indicates marked variation in CPTSD prevalence across forcibly displaced populations rather than a single generalisable prevalence rate. Recruitment context accounts for part of this variation, but the limited and geographically uneven evidence base prevents global population-level inference. Future studies should use representative sampling and consistently report displacement, trauma, and post-migration characteristics to permit more informative explanations of between-population variation.

items.title: Investigating the relationship between childhood interpersonal traumatic experiences and appraisals, belonging, shame, and dissociation.
items.abstract: Background: The association between childhood trauma and an array of psychosocial outcomes, including shame, dissociation and social connection, has attracted increasing empirical attention. Efforts are now being made to understand how these variables may be interrelated. Objective: This study aims to further expand on previous work by examining over two studies the relationship between childhood betrayal trauma, markers of belonging in social connections, shame and dissociation. Method: Both studies recruited a general population representative age and gender sample via Prolific and used path analysis. Study 1 ( N = 247; Mage = 46.66 ( SD = 15.57), 52.6% female) assessed whether the need to belong moderated the relationship between childhood betrayal trauma and fear of belonging, with this latter variable influencing both shame and dissociation. Results: Results ultimately showed the best model fit being childhood betrayal trauma directly influencing shame and dissociation with these latter two variables significantly impacting fear of belonging. Study 2 ( N = 289; Mage = 46.48 ( SD = 16.26), 52.2% female) sought to replicate and expand Study 1, with the best model fit showing that perceived impact of childhood betrayal trauma mediated the relationship between childhood betrayal trauma and both shame and dissociation, with these latter two variables directly impacting fear of belonging. Conclusion: Dissociation and shame are supported as important variables in the aftermath of childhood betrayal trauma and its subjective impact, while also having a potential impact on the fear a person has of connecting with other people.

items.title: An intervention mapping study to adapt trauma-focused social adjustment therapy for adolescents with trauma-related interpersonal difficulties.
items.abstract: Background: Interventions that effectively reduce posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms are not necessarily effective in improving interpersonal functioning among adolescents with complex trauma histories. Despite the developmental significance of interpersonal functioning during adolescence, there remains a lack of interventions specifically targeting trauma-related interpersonal difficulties in this population. Objective: This study aimed to adapt the Trauma-Focused Social Adjustment Therapy (TF-SAT) protocol for adolescents. The original protocol was developed for young adults with trauma histories, and the adaptation focuses on adolescents with complex trauma histories and trauma-related interpersonal difficulties . Method: The TF-SAT intervention protocol was systematically adapted using the Intervention Mapping Protocol (IMP), informed by two meta-analyses, a quantitative study, and relevant theoretical literature. Results: The intervention development process resulted in an adapted TF-SAT protocol targeting trauma-related cognitive (i.e. cognitive avoidance), emotional (i.e. dissociation and alexithymia), and interpersonal (i.e. social problem-solving) processes hypothesised to underlie interpersonal difficulties. The original TF-SAT framework was extended to propose differential cognitive and emotional pathways across different trauma symptom patterns. Intervention implementation and evaluation procedures were also developed to guide future feasibility and effectiveness testing, as well as ongoing protocol refinement. Conclusions: This study provides a theory- and evidence-informed intervention protocol designed to address trauma-related interpersonal difficulties among adolescents with complex trauma histories. The adapted TF-SAT protocol provides a foundation for future feasibility testing and the development of more targeted, developmentally appropriate trauma interventions tailored to different trauma response patterns.

items.title: Fatigue in head and neck cancer survivors after radiotherapy - prevalence, risk factors, and radiation dose correlates.
items.abstract: To determine the prevalence of fatigue in head and neck cancer survivors and identify associated factors, including potential associations with radiation dose to cerebral organs at risk (OAR). This cross-sectional observational study included survivors treated with curative radiotherapy between 2005 and 2023 at a tertiary cancer center. Fatigue and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) were assessed with the EORTC QLQ-C30. Dosimetric analyses evaluated associations between fatigue and radiation dose to intracranial OAR (brainstem, cerebellum, posterior fossa, medulla, pituitary gland, basal ganglia, hippocampus), including voxel-based analysis (VBA). One hundred fifty-eight patients were included. The most common tumor site was the oropharynx (38.6%). Median time from radiotherapy completion to study participation was 41 (IQR, 22-61) months. The mean fatigue score was 44.7 (SD, 28.0), exceeding the fatigue levels in the age- and sex-adjusted German general population (29.7); 51.3% of patients showed clinically relevant fatigue (≥ 39 points). Fatigue was inversely associated with HRQoL (ρ = - 0.59, p < 0.001), and positively with distress (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001) and fear of cancer recurrence (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). Higher fatigue was found in patients with impaired performance status and in those with laryngeal and hypopharyngeal cancers. Neither cerebral OAR radiation doses nor skeletal muscle mass index was associated with fatigue, and VBA revealed no relevant subregions. Clinically relevant fatigue affects about half of head and neck cancer survivors. The absence of a correlation with cerebral OAR doses suggests that other, probably multifactorial somatic, psychological and lifestyle-related factors play a more central role in the genesis of fatigue than the radiation-related brain exposures investigated.

items.title: The Effects of Extreme Climate Events on Healthcare Access, Mental Health, and Economic Stability Among PLHIV in Brazil.
items.abstract: Climate change and HIV are intersecting crises, yet their combined impact on Latin America's HIV care continuum remains understudied. Using a descriptive cross-sectional design with data from the 2024 Brazilian HIV Stigma Index, we examined the consequences of extreme climate events-primarily the May 2024 floods in Porto Alegre-on healthcare access, mental health, and socioeconomic stability among 156 people living with HIV. These events were associated with substantial care disruptions, with many participants reporting rescheduled or canceled medical appointments and laboratory monitoring. Furthermore, 60.5% reported negative mental health impacts and 37.3% suffered household income reductions. Institutional support reached a minority, leaving many reliant on civil society for survival needs. These findings highlight an urgent need for climate-resilient HIV policies integrating mental health care and social protection to sustain treatment adherence during public calamities.

items.title: Young adults' understanding of, and reaction to, those with uncertain genetic results.
items.abstract: Background Genetic advances increase the likelihood that children may receive uncertain diagnoses such as cystic fibrosis screen positive inconclusive diagnosis (CFSPID) from newborn screening. Research suggests a profound impact on parents. Research is needed to understand the impact on the child, especially at key developmental points such as young adulthood, when identity forms. As young adults (YA) are influenced by peer reactions, this novel study explored YAs' sensemaking of CFSPID, and their hypothetical reactions to peers or romantic partners with CFSPID. Methods Four focus groups were conducted and analysed using thematic analysis across three sections: understanding, peer and romantic relationships. Results Understanding: Without knowledge about CFSPID, participants used cystic fibrosis, genetic and contagious illness knowledge to form assumptions. Peer and romantic relationships: In both sections, YAs wanted to support their friend/partner; however, their responses revealed assumptions that a person with CFSPID would need more physical and psychological support and would be seen differently by some. Most wanted to learn more but were unsure whether it was appropriate to ask the person with CFPSID. Although rare, some reported they would avoid romantic relationships with YAs with CFSPID. All data suggesting people with CFPSID would be treated differently was based on erroneous assumptions due to a lack of CFSPID knowledge. Providing information about how CFPSID is different from CF did not appear sufficient to stop a reliance on CF knowledge when making sense of CFSPID. Conclusion Further research should explore whether it's possible to change assumptions when YAs disclose uncertain results.

items.title: Psychometric Evaluation of the Turkish Prolonged Grief Assessment-Child Version.
items.abstract: The inclusion of prolonged grief disorder (PGD) in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, Text Revision (DSM-5-TR) has highlighted the need for developmentally appropriate, validated measures. Many measures for bereaved youth predate the DSM-5-TR criteria and do not fully align with them. We evaluated the psychometric properties of the Turkish Prolonged Grief Assessment-Child Version (PGA-C) in 436 participants aged 8-17 years, 6-36 months after parental loss. The PGA-C had α = .92 and a two-week intraclass correlation coefficient of .735. A one-factor model with two residual covariances showed acceptable fit, and associations with depression, anxiety, posttraumatic stress, and quality of life supported convergent validity. A cutoff of 50 showed concordance with the algorithm-based probable PGD (area under the curve = .941). These findings support the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the PGA-C for parentally bereaved Turkish youth.

items.title: Lifestyle factors associated with hot flash frequency and daily interference: highlighting the role of sleep quality, diet quality and physical activity.
items.abstract: To examine associations of lifestyle and demographic factors with hot flash frequency (HFF) and hot flash-related daily interference (HFRDI) in a multicultural Australian convenience sample. The study fills an evidence gap by investigating how lifestyle factors interact with ethnicity and self-reported menopausal status in Australia's diverse population, an area with limited prior research. A cross-sectional online survey conducted in 2024-2025 included a convenience sample of women who self-identified as being in perimenopause and postmenopause (mean age: 56.1±6.6 y). All demographic, menopause, lifestyle, medication-use, and symptom information was self-reported through the online questionnaire. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, menopause status, and symptom outcomes were self-reported. Diet quality, physical activity, and sleep were assessed using an adapted Global Diet Quality Score, an International Physical Activity Questionnaire-based measure, and a modified Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, respectively. Menopause status was self-reported, and duration in that status was recorded; Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop (STRAW) +10 informed the terminology but was not used to assign specific reproductive-aging substages. Outcomes included HFF and HFRDI. Ordinal logistic models estimated adjusted associations controlling for age, menopause status/duration, and ethnicity. Sleep quality was the strongest correlate of HFF and HFRDI. For HFF, each one-category worsening in sleep quality was associated with higher odds of being in a higher frequency category (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=2.44; P=0.001); older age was inversely associated (aOR=0.42; P=0.002). For HFRDI, poorer sleep was strongly associated with greater interference (aOR=4.93; P<0.001). Ethnicity was not associated with frequency (P=0.687) but was associated with daily interference (aOR=2.66; P=0.037). Diet quality showed a nonsignificant inverse association for daily interference (P=0.077). Physical activity showed a small, nonsignificant tendency toward higher frequency (P=0.135). Findings suggest the importance of routine sleep quality for symptom burden and may inform lifestyle-focused approaches to symptom management.

items.title: Educational Outcomes at 7, 11 and 16 Years of Age for Children Born Small for Gestational Age: Results From the Auckland Birthweight Collaborative Study.
items.abstract: Aim Small for gestational age (SGA) has been linked to lower school achievement in childhood. However, this association has only been shown consistently in preterm-SGA cohorts. This paper aims to determine whether being born SGA at term is associated with school performance at 7, 11 and 16 years of age. Methods n = 871 children born at term (n = 433 small-for-gestational-age [SGA] and n = 438 appropriate for gestational age [AGA]) had education outcomes analysed at age 7 (n = 265 SGA, n = 304 AGA), 11 (n = 200 SGA, n = 218 AGA) and 16 (n = 152 SGA, n = 185 AGA). The outcomes studied were the risk of below-average achievement in oral comprehension, written comprehension and mathematics at 7 and 11 years of age, and the risk of not achieving final secondary school qualifications at 16. Binary and multinomial logistic regression were performed. Results SGA children score below-average in written comprehension at 7 (OR 1.71, CI 1.04-2.80) and oral comprehension at 11 (OR 2.10, CI 1.22-3.62). These associations were not statistically significant once adjusted for confounders (written comprehension at 7 aOR 1.54, CI 0.89-2.69; oral comprehension at 11 aOR 1.79, CI 0.99-3.25). There was no statistically significant difference in secondary school achievement (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.45-1.42) between SGA and AGA children. Conclusions Our results show that being born SGA at term does not independently increase the risk of below-average performance at ages 7, 11 or 16 after adjusting for known social and environmental confounders. However, clinicians should maintain active surveillance for term SGA infants, particularly when co-occurring environmental or maternal risk factors are present.

items.title: Bereavement, Psychological Distress, and Inflammation: Findings From the MIDUS Refresher Cohort.
items.abstract: Bereavement can adversely affect psychological and physical health. Using MIDUS Refresher 1 data, we examined psychological and inflammatory differences between bereaved (n = 373) and non-bereaved (n = 490) adults and tested whether depression, anxiety, and stress moderated associations between bereavement and inflammation. Participants completed measures of depressive symptoms, anxiety, and perceived stress and provided blood samples for interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Adjusting for key covariates, bereaved participants reported significantly greater depressive symptoms, anxiety, and perceived stress (ps < .001) and had higher IL-6 (p = .001) and TNF-α (p < .001) than non-bereaved participants. Psychological symptoms did not moderate associations between bereavement and inflammatory markers. Findings suggest that bereavement is associated with concurrent psychological distress and elevated inflammation, but these effects may be partly independent. Identifying other psychological and contextual factors may clarify individual differences in inflammatory responses following loss.

items.title: Mental health experiences and barriers: Black adolescents presenting for suicide risk and their caregivers.
items.abstract: Background Health disparities in suicidal behaviors exist for Black youth. There are many barriers that Black adolescents and their caregivers encounter when attempting to access mental health (MH) care. However, there is limited information available concerning their experiences, barriers, and facilitators of MH services. Methods Qualitative interviews were conducted with Black adolescents (ages 10-18) presenting in a pediatric emergency department with past-year suicidal ideation and/or behaviors and/or their caregivers. The sample consisted of 9 adolescents and 11 caregivers. Qualitative analysis was conducted by structured annotation and thematic analysis. Results Adolescent and caregiver interviews identified seven themes: (1) emotional and behavioral experiences; (2) impact of previous MH treatment; (3) MH barriers; (4) facilitators for future treatment; (5) MH communication; (6) support; and (7) community resources. Conclusion Themes highlighted by both adolescents and caregivers were the impact of previous treatment, MH barriers, facilitators for future treatment, MH communication, and support. Although the interviews are consistent with research literature documenting the negative experiences and barriers to care for Black adolescents, MH experiences can be positive and helpful if provided in a culturally responsive manner.

items.title: Significant others' perspectives on formal supports at 3- and 12-months post-discharge from specialist rehabilitation units following acquired brain injury and spinal cord injury.
items.abstract: Purpose To explore from significant others' perspective the experiences of and barriers to accessing formal supports in the first year post-discharge after acquired brain injury (ABI) and spinal cord injury (SCI). Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with significant others (family members/friends) of individuals with newly acquired ABI and SCI at 3- ( n = 24) and 12-months post-discharge ( n = 19) from inpatient rehabilitation in Queensland, Australia. Data were thematically analysed using the Framework method. Results Four themes emerged. Theme 1 ( Journeying along new and complex pathways ) describes participants' experience forging a path through an unknown landscape. Theme 2 ( Being on the same page through open and active communication ) highlights the impact of communication on the experience of formal supports. Theme 3 ( Getting the support right: prioritising the who and how ) stresses the importance of formal supports understanding the person with the injury, their interests and needs. Theme 4 ( Becoming the safety net ) describes the impact on significant others who had to fill the gaps in formal support. Conclusion The findings underscore the need to proactively involve significant others as well as people with an injury in the rehabilitation and decision-making process to support the needs and well-being of both parties.

items.title: The Event-Level Association Between Alcohol Use and Intimate Partner Violence Perpetration: A Systematic Narrative Review of the Literature.
items.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) perpetration is a significant public health concern, with up to 90% of individuals in intimate relationships experiencing some form of physical, psychological, or sexual IPV from their partner throughout their lifetime. Over 30 years of research have concluded that alcohol use results in greater risk for IPV perpetration. Despite this known association, only recently has alcohol use been examined as a proximal predictor of IPV perpetration in daily diary-type studies. The present study aimed to provide a systematic narrative review of current research on the event-level association between alcohol use and psychological, physical, and sexual IPV perpetration. Relevant studies were obtained by searching PsycInfo, PubMed, and CINAHL. Full-text peer-reviewed studies published in English that quantitatively assessed the event-level association between alcohol use and physical, psychological, and/or sexual IPV perpetration ( N = 24) were retained. Results provide support for the event-level association between alcohol use and IPV perpetration across college student, couple, community, clinical, and adjudicated samples. Future research is needed to distinguish whether certain patterns of alcohol use, quantity, or level of intoxication are associated with greater IPV risk. Similarly, future studies should aim to examine psychological, physical, and sexual IPV perpetration separately, and to identify how other known risk factors may interact with alcohol use to predict event-level IPV perpetration. These findings highlight the usefulness of clinical intervention efforts that provide skills to target urges to drink or to aggress in the moment when they are needed, with the ultimate goal of reducing alcohol-related IPV perpetration.

items.title: Environmental and economic drivers of persistent open defecation in the rural state of Osun, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Open defecation remains a major environmental health challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa, with Nigeria bearing one of the highest global burdens despite increasing access to improved water sources and widespread awareness of sanitation-related health risks in rural areas. Community-led total sanitation (CLTS) emphasizes behavioural change, prompting families to build their own latrines using local materials. CLTS drives community mobilization to stop open defecation collectively; the widespread prevalence of the practice in rural areas reveals a significant gap between sanitation knowledge and actual practice. Furthermore, very few empirical studies integrate the roles of environmental constraints, household financial choices, and sanitation behaviour gaps in under-resourced settings. This study addresses this gap by investigating the environmental and socioeconomic determinants of open defecation persistence through a baseline assessment conducted during CLTS in the rural state of Osun, Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 200 respondents across four rural villages in Osun between March and May 2023. Data on sanitation infrastructure, defecation practices, water access, hygiene behaviours, and household economic priorities were collected using semi-structured questionnaires. Associations were examined using χ2 tests, ANOVA, and multiple regression analyses. A total of 91.5% of households practised open defecation, with only 5.5% owning improved toilet facilities, despite 89.5% having access to improved water sources. A pronounced knowledge-practice gap was observed: 51.5% of households practising handwashing before meals were still disposing of faeces in open spaces (χ²=36.4, p<0.01). Household income significantly influenced prioritization of mobile phone purchases over latrine construction (χ²=19.34, p=0.04), while education level correlated with toilet quality perceptions (χ²=41.36, p<0.01). Soil type significantly influenced flooding risk and latrine siting feasibility (χ²=8.51, p=0.004). Regression analysis revealed that household size, gender, and perceived importance of handwashing significantly predicted water storage expenditure (F=7.44, p<0.001, R²=0.188). This study shows that awareness campaigns alone cannot stop open defecation in rural Nigeria, as knowledge and water access cannot overcome the structural barriers of extreme poverty and environmental constraints. Therefore, securing a nationwide open defecation-free status by 2030 requires a paradigm shift beyond behavioural interventions. In rural settings, sustainable progress depends on integrating subsidized financing mechanisms, conducting environmental feasibility assessments, and embedding sanitation initiatives within national poverty reduction frameworks. This comprehensive approach is necessary because current non-subsidized CLTS approaches are insufficient for rural communities facing extreme resource constraints.

items.title: Dual-Targeting Nanomicelles Co-Loading Sorafenib and Artesunate Combats Hepatocellular Carcinoma via the Synergistically Enhanced Ferroptosis Strategy.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a formidable malignancy with limited response to conventional monotherapies, largely due to its complicated pathogenesis and useful cellular defense systems. In this study, we constructed a dual-targeting polymeric micelle (S&A@TPD/HG PMs), co-delivering sorafenib (SOR), and artesunate (ART) to achieve synergistic ferroptosis-based therapy against HCC. The micelle features a hyaluronic acid (HA) shell functionalized with glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) for active dual targeting to CD44 and GA receptors overexpressed on HCC cells; while its triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-decorated inner core facilitates mitochondrial anchoring and co-conveys the drugs, enabling stepwise subcellular targeting. Compared with free drugs or single-drug-loaded micelles, S&A@TPD/HG PMs effectively induced mitochondrial damage by depleting glutathione (GSH), and downregulating GSH peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression to disrupt the mitochondrial antioxidant defense system, elevating intracellular Fe 2+ to increase reactive oxygen species (ROS) and lipid peroxidation (LPO) production, thereby compromising mitochondrial redox homeostasis and potentiating ferroptosis jointly. This ferroptosis-inducing activity yielded potent in vivo antitumor efficacy in Huh-7 tumor-bearing nude mice, with a tumor inhibition rate of 74.23% and minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, the organelle-specific targeting combined with co-delivery of synergistic drug pairs represents a promising strategy for combating malignancies and provides a blueprint for the rational design of multifunctional nanosystems.

items.title: Beyond Technical Tasks: Making Nursing Care Visible in Nurse Anaesthesia Practice-A Focused Ethnography.
items.abstract: Aim To explore how nursing care is enacted in daily nurse anaesthesia practice when caring for patients requiring anaesthesia services. Design A focused ethnography. Methods The study involved non-participant observation of nine nurse anaesthetists totalling 63 h, along with nine semi-structured individual interviews at a Norwegian university hospital. Data were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Findings The overarching theme, Striving to provide holistic nursing care, captured how NAs integrate clinical, technological, relational and organisational competencies in complex, high-risk environments while navigating tensions between efficiency demands and person-centred care principles. Conclusion Nursing care in nurse anaesthesia practice is enacted through the continuous integration of clinical, technological, relational and organisational competencies. While nurse anaesthetists strive to provide holistic, person-centred care, practice is shaped by tensions between efficiency demands, organisational constraints and patient-centred priorities. Despite these challenges, nurse anaesthetists play a key role in maintaining patient safety, continuity of care and high-quality anaesthesia services. Implications for the profession and patient care This study sheds light on the often-overlooked relational, holistic, and coordinative dimensions of nurse anaesthesia practice. By making these contributions more visible, the findings may support service development, enhance collaborative models of care, and strengthen the utilisation of nursing expertise in anaesthesia services. The findings also highlight the broad scope of nurse anaesthesia practice and may inform future professional, organisational, educational, and workforce-related discussions. Impact This study contributes to a broader reconceptualisation of nurse anaesthesia practice, with relevance for education, leadership and quality of care, and may inform countries seeking to integrate nurse anaesthetists to improve access to safe anaesthesia care. Reporting method The Standard for Reporting Qualitative Research (SRQR) checklist was used to enhance trustworthiness and transparency. items.title: Ensuring equitable emergency, critical and operative care.
items.abstract: Conditions requiring emergency, critical and operative (ECO) care account for a substantial proportion of preventable mortality and disability worldwide, yet ECO systems remain fragmented and underdeveloped in many settings. Recent global policy advances, including the adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Strategy and Action Plan for Integrated ECO Care by the World Health Assembly, provide an important opportunity to strengthen these systems. However, implementation must prioritise equity. ECO care spans a wide spectrum of complexity and cost, from basic triage, oxygen therapy and essential operations to advanced intensive care and specialised surgery. Given finite resources, health systems should first ensure universal access to foundational ECO care: early recognition of illness, basic airway and oxygen support, essential medications, monitoring, infection prevention, and timely referral. Approaches such as Essential Emergency and Critical Care (EECC) offer a feasible, highly cost-effective minimum standard of care, and prioritising such foundational ECO care is both an ethical imperative and the most effective pathway to achieving equitable population-level health gains.

items.title: The L.I.F.T. Project-the 6 Intervention Mapping Steps to Create a Faith-Based HIV Health Education Intervention in the U.S. South.
items.abstract: Memphis, TN ranks first in the U.S. for HIV incidence and is designated as a high priority geographic area by the U.S. Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) Initiative. National EHE goals call for active engagement of all community sectors, including faith-based organizations, to promote HIV testing and prevention. Given Memphis' high density of predominately Black Churches and faith-centric culture, these institutions serve as a strategic platform for culturally tailored behavioral interventions. This study details the 6 behavioral intervention mapping (IM) steps used to plan, implement, and evaluate Leading by Igniting Faith and Education to Tackle Stigma (L.I.F.T.)-a faith-based HIV health education curriculum addressing HIV testing and prevention discrepancies in high HIV-incidence areas. IM is a systematic approach, useful for involving faith communities by providing a theory-informed scaffolding to address HIV disparities via community education programming.

items.title: Age-specific survival after breast conservation versus mastectomy for ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast.
items.abstract: Breast conservation for invasive breast cancer is associated with better survival and fewer complications than mastectomy, which is especially relevant for older patients. It is unclear whether this can be extrapolated to ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). This population-based cohort study used data from the Breast Cancer Database Sweden (BCBaSe 3.0) to compare overall survival (OS), breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) and local recurrence (LR) probabilities in three different age groups (< 60, 60-69, 70 + years) of women with primary DCIS undergoing breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy (BCS + RT), mastectomy without radiotherapy (Mx-RT), or breast-conserving surgery without radiotherapy (BCS-RT) during 2008-2019. Complete cases (CC) and multiple imputation (MI) analyses were applied. In 7165 women, treatment was BCS + RT (53.3%), BCS-RT (13.4%), or Mx-RT (33.2%). Estimated 10-year OS was 90.4% (95% CI 89.3-91.5) and BCSS 98.8% (98.3-99.2). After adjustments for patient and tumour factors, including socioeconomic status and comorbidity, Mx-RT was associated with a higher overall mortality than BCS + RT in CC (HR 2.10; 95% CI 1.20-3.67) but not in MI analyses (HR 1.29; 0.95-1.76). In age 70 + years, however, the overall mortality was consistently increased (CC: HR 2.48; 1.09-5.62, MI: HR 1.89; 1.23-2.90). Also BCS-RT was associated with a higher overall mortality than BCS + RT (CC: HR 2.68; 1.34-5.34, and MI: HR 1.72; 1.23-2.39). The 10-year LR probability was low (7.2%, 95% CI 6.3-8.0). Compared to BCS + RT, Mx-RT was associated with a lower (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.11-0.28) and BCS-RT with a higher LR risk (HR 1.79; 1.31-2.46), especially among ages 70+. BCS + RT in DCIS appears safe. Acknowledging potential selection bias, BCS + RT may be associated with favourable overall survival outcomes in older women despite a higher risk of local recurrence.

items.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China's food chain: projections to 2050.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China's food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance (gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes (qnrB17, qnrS1) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes (bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

items.title: The content and reporting completeness of physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Objectives This study synthesised the content and reporting completeness of published physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA). Methods This systematic review undertook electronic database searches in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, CINAHL and PEDro (until June 2025) for any peer-reviewed articles/studies describing physical therapist-led interventions across non-surgical and perioperative settings for adults aged 45 years and over with GHOA. The content and reporting completeness were synthesized using the 22-item Template for Intervention Description and Replication for rehabilitation interventions (TIDIeR_Rehab). Results Overall, 134 articles/studies describing 156 physical therapist-led interventions were included, comprising mostly case series designs (n=47, 35.1%) or narrative reviews (n=38, 28.4%). Of the remaining 49 articles/studies, only 11 were studies reporting RCT results and three were protocols of RCTs in progress. Intervention content varied considerably, and the overall completeness of intervention item reporting was poor (only 18%). Interventions in non-surgical contexts commonly included strengthening exercises (n=33, 53.2%), range of motion (ROM) exercises (n=23, 37.1%), and electrotherapy modalities (n=16, 25.8%). Sling immobilisation was most reported in postoperative interventions (n=64, 72.7%). Many different proposed mechanisms of action were reported (n=49, 31.4%); but all were biomechanically orientated. Conclusion Very few high-quality empirical studies evaluating physical therapist-led interventions for GHOA have been published. We found substantial heterogeneity in the content of published physical therapist-led interventions, and the reporting completeness was generally poor. This suggests considerable uncertainty regarding best practice physical therapy for GHOA in terms of intervention content. Future high-quality empirical research is needed, preferably using RCT designs that include clear descriptions of interventions.

items.title: Barriers and enablers to engagement with green social prescribing in primary care: a scoping review using the socio-ecological model.
items.abstract: Background Green social prescribing (GSP) connects individuals with nature-based interventions (NBIs) through healthcare providers, link workers, and social and community networks. While evidence supports the health benefits of NBIs, further research is needed to understand the factors that influence engagement. Aim To explore barriers and enablers to GSP and NBIs for prescribers, service users and community providers. Design & setting A scoping review in primary care and community settings. Method We systematically searched Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and SCOPUS from 2019. We assessed quality using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. We mapped data to the socioecological framework during synthesis. Results Out of 4864 screened records, 45 studies from 11 countries were included. GSP and NBIs face micro-level barriers such as knowledge gaps, cultural and social issues, time and cost constraints and perceptions of adverse weather; meso-level and macro-level challenges include unequal access, underfunded NBIs, an emphasis on biomedical models, safety concerns, limited training, and insufficient policy support and leadership. Engagement was enabled by flexible, person-centred approaches, tailored NBIs with clear pathways, including link workers, strong cross-sector partnerships, community co-design, and public health campaigns. Conclusion Promoting engagement with GSP and NBIs requires a multi-level approach that addresses systemic barriers through collaboration between prescribers, third-sector organisations and policymakers. Investment in workforce training and sustainable funding models is critical to support long-term success in primary care and community settings. Addressing health inequalities by improving access for people in areas of high socioeconomic deprivation remains a priority.

items.title: Efficacy and Feasibility of Just-in-Time Nudging in Reducing Evening Snacking Measured by Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Micro-Randomized Study.
items.abstract: Aims This study aimed to determine whether in people with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a digital nudge delivered by a smartphone app soon after dinner reduces subsequent snacking events as measured by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Methods Participants: Adults with T2DM, managed with diet or stable oral antidiabetic medication for at least 3 months, and who habitually snacked after dinner on ≥ 3 nights/week. Design Pictographic nudges were co-designed with consumers. After-dinner snacking behaviours were confirmed during a 2-week Lead-In phase by CGM. Thereafter, eligible participants were micro-randomized daily (1:1, MRT phase) to either a pictographic nudge delivered-in-time (Intui Research) or no nudge for a second 2-week period. The primary outcome was the difference in incremental area under the CGM curve (net-iAUC) between nudging days and non-nudging days during the period 90-min post-dinner until 4 AM. Results Sixty-six participants completed the Lead-In phase and 56 completed the MRT phase with available CGM data. CGM data were collected over 911 nights during the Lead-In phase and 780 nights during the MRT phase, with a total of 410 digital nudges sent. Over the entire 2-week period there was no effect of nudging on the primary outcome (net-iAUC). However, secondary analyses showed that there was an initial nudge effect that faded over time. Similar results were observed for snacking behaviour and CGM time-in-range. Conclusion This study provides preliminary feasibility of delivering just-in-time nudges in adults with T2DM, with no overall glycaemic benefit. Exploratory early effects warrant confirmation and investigation of strategies to sustain efficacy. Trial registration ACTRN12622000531718.

items.title: Next-Generation CRISPR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Veterinary Parasitology: From Laboratory Innovation to One Health Surveillance.
items.abstract: Veterinary parasitic diseases remain a major threat to livestock production, companion animal health, wildlife conservation, and public health worldwide. Conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy, serology, and culture-based techniques, often suffer from limited sensitivity, poor specificity, prolonged turnaround time, and dependence on specialized laboratory facilities. Recent advances in Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based diagnostics have introduced highly sensitive, rapid, and field-deployable platforms for parasite detection. This review critically summarizes the principles and recent applications of CRISPR/Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14-based diagnostic approaches in veterinary parasitology, covering protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites. It further compares CRISPR platforms and discusses their integration with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to improve diagnostic performance. Moreover, current challenges, including sample preparation, assay standardization, multiplex detection, regulatory approval, and commercialization, are highlighted. Finally, future perspectives on amplification-free CRISPR assays, artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, and point-of-care platforms are discussed. By providing a translational perspective from laboratory innovation to field application, this review highlights the potential of CRISPR-based diagnostics to transform veterinary parasite surveillance and disease control.

items.title: Reinforcement learning-driven optimal capital allocation for intelligent finance.
items.abstract: Optimal capital allocation in financial markets has long been a challenging task due to the dynamic nature of market conditions, risk factors, and the complexity of financial data. Traditional methods of portfolio management often fail to adapt to market shifts and do not fully leverage potential of modern machine learning techniques. To develop a model that dynamically optimizes capital allocation, leveraging reinforcement learning (RL), with focus on risk management, stability, and adaptability. Proposed model, Dynamic Actor-Critic (DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model for portfolio optimization. A Dynamic Actor-Critic (DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model is developed for portfolio optimization. The Dynamic Actor-Critic module learns optimal portfolio policies by evaluating actions and maximizing long-term returns, while the CPPO mechanism ensures stable policy updates and risk-controlled portfolio optimization. The Intelligent Finance Assets dataset contains 7,000 records with 32 features, whereas the Massive Yahoo Finance dataset includes 603k records with 9 features, collected from publicly available Kaggle sources for financial analysis. Normalization and data cleaning techniques for smooth data integration and model readiness, and LDA extracts discriminative financial features to improve portfolio allocation prediction performance. Experimental settings are implemented using Python. Proposed DAC-CPPO model, achieving 97.6% accuracy, 0.074 MAE, 0.081 RMSE, 1.91 Sharpe ratio, 1.12 Cumulative return, and 0.14 Volatility, demonstrates superior risk-adjusted performance, offering higher returns while managing market risks effectively compared to other existing models. The DAC-CPPO model offers a robust solution for practical capital allocation by combining advanced RL techniques, ensuring effective decision-making while managing risks in dynamic financial environments.

items.title: Multiplexed CRISPRi reveals a transcriptional switch between KLF activators and repressors in the maturing neocortex.
items.abstract: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional 'switch' to first activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.

items.title: Depth-dependent soil water-salt relationships in the Hetao Irrigation District, arid Northwest China: Implications for sustainable management.
items.abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil water and salt content remain poorly characterized. We monitored soil moisture and electrical conductivity (EC) at six depths (0-100 cm) across 15 sites in the Hetao Irrigation District, China, during the 2025 growing season. Our results indicate a depth-dependent divergence in water-salt associations. The EC-derived salinity index varied from 0.08 to 42.91 g/kg, exhibiting extreme spatial heterogeneity (coefficient of variation (CV) = 185.2%) across the salinity gradient. However, moisture-salinity relationships showed marked depth dependency. Surface soils (0-20 cm) exhibited non-statistically significant correlations (r = 0.07), whereas deep layers (60-100 cm) showed a statistically significant but weak positive correlation (r = 0.25, p < 0.01, R2 = 0.06), indicating limited explanatory power. This pattern is consistent with a subtle tendency of downward salt redistribution. The EC-derived salinity index showed a 42% increase in deep layers (from 1.59 to 2.26 g/kg) over the season, compared to a 136% fluctuation in surface layers. These results highlight limitations of surface-focused monitoring approaches and indicate patterns consistent with subsurface salt redistribution. Compared with previous studies, this work provides a depth-resolved, multi-site observational dataset combined with a stratified analytical approach, offering additional evidence for interpreting soil salinity dynamics under heterogeneous field conditions.

items.title: Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation and supporting sustainable urban planning. This study integrates machine learning and geospatial technologies to analyze spatio-temporal land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and urban expansion in Gambella Town, Ethiopia. Multi-temporal Landsat satellite images from 2005, 2015, and 2025 were processed using remote sensing techniques and a supervised machine learning approach based on the Random Forest (RF) classifier. Six major LULC classes were identified: Agricultural Land, Bush with Grass, Built-Up Area, Bare Land, Forest Land, and Water Bodies. The classification achieved overall accuracies of 90%, 90%, and 89% for 2005, 2015, and 2025, respectively. The results revealed substantial land transformation and rapid physical urban expansion, with the built-up area increasing from 93 ha (2.0%) in 2005-1,956 ha (41.3%) in 2025. This expansion was accompanied by major transformations of surrounding land resources, particularly the conversion of Bush with Grass and other open areas to built-up land. Agricultural land increased from 634 ha (13.4%) to 1,750 ha (36.9%), whereas Bush with Grass declined from 3,375 ha (71.1%) to 652 ha (13.7%). Socio-economic information collected from 277 respondents indicated that population growth, rural-urban migration, housing demand, employment opportunities, and infrastructure development were major drivers of urban expansion. The study distinguishes urban expansion, represented by the increase in built-up land, from urban sprawl, which refers to the spatial pattern and form of outward urban development. The integration of Random Forest classification and GIS-based spatial analysis provides valuable evidence of land transformation, vegetation loss, and increasing pressure on urban services, supporting more sustainable urban planning and land management in Gambella Town.

items.title: A Reverse-Gold Theorem: Positive-Data Identification by Substrate-Bounded Contrastive Learners
items.abstract: Gold's theorem shows that no learner can identify an arbitrary language in a superfinite class from positive presentations alone. We prove a positive result of a different shape. Fix an innate \emph{recursive contrast operator} $R$ mapping any string to a finite set of structurally bounded perturbations of it, and a discriminative scorer of bounded capacity trained by InfoNCE-style contrastive estimation \citep{vandenoord2018,macollins2018} on self-generated perturbations. Under a faithfulness condition relating operator, scorer, and target, the trained scorer achieves \emph{PAC conditional identification} from positive data alone: with high probability it ranks all but an $\varepsilon$-fraction of positives above every out-of-language perturbation in their own orbit, with sample complexity polynomial in the capacity, the orbit size, the score bound, and $1/\varepsilon$. The negatives are constructed by the learner, not supplied by an oracle, and no global normalizing constant over strings is ever computed. The misranking bound follows from the geometry of the contrastive loss---per-example loss floors plus a definite loss increment under misranking---yielding an $\varepsilon^{-2}$ rate, together with an explicit approximation gap that quantifies the cost of in-language (``colliding'') perturbations and vanishes for orbit-pure operators. The ranking guarantee lifts to a global membership classifier under a margin condition, and the same operator composed with the learned scorer is a normalization-free Metropolis--Hastings generator. We instantiate the hypotheses for substitutable context-free languages \citep{clarkeyraud2007} and the subregular classes \citep{heinz2010,hayashikamigaito2025}, and state an open conjecture locating the construction in the mildly context-sensitive hierarchy.

items.title: System-evolutionary view of RNA presence in living cells
items.abstract: Our guiding question for this article was: How did RNA adjust its life when the RNA world era came to an end? RNA has its practical execution side in the whole-cell systems setup serving critical functions in metabolism, compartmentalization, and in the RNA-DNA-Protein network, coupling information handling and different events of macromolecule production into a self-sustaining loop. Aligning with current views of cooperation we find that RNA life is distributed across a population of information-bearing entities persisting by compatibility, with DNA serving as a long-term memory and proteins offering the catalytic reach. We suggest that the reproduction-survival axis, relevant to higher organisms, is also manifested by RNA in many forms, including RNA-primers, mRNAs, tRNAs, and rRNAs. Each of these have contrasting, highly adapted molecular phenotypes. Ultimately, we wish to emphasize the evolutionary narrative where RNA did not lose in exchange for DNA genes or otherwise. Ultimately, RNA just changed strategy and in its various forms has an active and critically important presence in all cells at all times.

items.title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries I: the effects of stellar evolution
items.abstract: Context. Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essential to understand the interplay between stellar evolution and binary perturbations. Aims. We investigate how uncertainties in stellar mass-loss histories affect the dynamical evolution of remnant planetary systems in wide binaries, and assess their relative importance compared with binary perturbations in driving the accretion of rocky material onto white dwarfs. Methods. We perform REBOUND N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar parameters interpolated from MESA evolutionary tracks and tidal interactions, following the dynamical evolution up to the white dwarf stage. We explore two stellar-evolution models with distinct mass-loss histories for wide binary systems hosting a Jupiter-mass planet and a planetesimal disc, spanning a range of binary architectures. Results. The adopted stellar-evolution model has only a minor effect on the survival of the planet, mainly affecting the timing and efficiency of planetesimal delivery during the white dwarf stage. Instead, the architecture of the binary primarily controls the pollution outcome: wider binaries produce the highest rates of accretion onto the white dwarf, consistent with the observed prevalence of polluted white dwarfs in wide binaries. Moreover, planetesimal reservoirs remain long-lived, with survival times increasing with binary separation, enabling Gyr-long metal pollution. Conclusions. Our results suggest that the architecture of wide binaries, rather than uncertainties in stellar evolution, is the dominant factor controlling the dynamical delivery of rocky material onto white dwarfs.

items.title: FAUST XXXII. Chemically layered structures and ionisation in the disk and envelope of NGC 1333 IRAS 4C
items.abstract: Recent molecular line observations with high spatial resolutions have revealed vertical chemical stratification in Class I/II disks (i.e. chemical composition changing with height in the vertical direction of the disk), as well as a radial variation of ionisation rates. However, such chemical layered structures in Class 0 disk and envelope systems have been investigated only for limited objects, such as L1527. In the context of the ALMA Large Program FAUST, we report the results of molecular line observations toward the disk and envelope around the low-mass Class 0 protostar NGC 1333 IRAS 4C in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. Previous observations have shown that the disk rotation axis of this object is largely tilted to the line of sight, making it suitable for studying the molecular abundance distribution as a function of disk height. We found that the molecules known as gas density tracers such as C18O and H2CO are distributed around the disk midplane. In addition, molecules known as tracers of photochemical reactions such as CCH and c-C3H2 are distributed in the low-density upper layers of the disk, unlike the distribution in L1527. Moreover, the column density ratio of HCO+/CO derived from the H13CO+ and C18O line emission suggests that the ionisation degree and the ionisation rate vary with the disk radius and they are larger in the outer region of the disk and envelope.

items.title: Systematic Uncertainties in Rocky Exoplanet Reflected Light from Incomplete Laboratory BRDF Measurements
items.abstract: The first observations of short-period rocky exoplanets have initiated the era of terrestrial exoplanet characterization. The interpretation of these observations relies on forward models used in atmospheric and surface retrieval frameworks. While atmospheric modeling is supported by extensive laboratory datasets of molecular opacities, the experimental basis for rocky surface characterization remains limited. Most reflectance libraries of planetary analog materials provide spectra measured at a single illumination and viewing geometry, constraining the spectral behavior but not its full angular scattering properties. We show that incomplete angular coverage in laboratory bidirectional reflectance measurements introduces an intrinsic systematic uncertainty in the interpretation of rocky exoplanet observations. We demonstrate that multiple combinations of photometric parameters can reproduce the same laboratory reflectance spectrum while predicting different angular scattering behaviors and disk-integrated observables. We propagate this non-uniqueness to reflected-light phase curves, geometric albedos, and planet-star contrast ratios between $0.5$--$1.7\,μ$m, representative of the spectral range targeted by future direct-imaging missions such as the HWO. We find that single-geometry laboratory spectra produce large uncertainties in predicted signals, particularly at small phase angles. Simplified assumptions adopted in exoplanet studies, such as isotropic scattering can additionally introduce systematic biases. Using multi-angular laboratory measurements from the Bloomsburg University Goniometer dataset, we show that the uncertainty in predicted observables collapses once angular scattering behavior is directly constrained. Our results demonstrate that multi-angular measurements are required to construct physically predictive reflected-light models of rocky exoplanets.

items.title: Saturation Level of the Streaming Instability
items.abstract: In proto-planetary disks, gas turbulence can cluster dust grains and catalyze the formation of planetesimals. This process depends on the strength of the turbulence. Here, we evaluate the turbulence strength that is induced by the streaming instability. Based on the amount of free energy available, we estimate the viscous parameter to be alpha ~ St Pi^2 f(epsilon), where St (< 1) is the Stokes number of the streaming grains, Pi is the dimensionless pressure gradient, and f (epsilon) is an explicit function of epsilon, the local dust-to-gas density ratio. This estimate explains the results of many previous studies, and is also supported by our additional tailor-made simulations. We discuss two easy applications of our result, one is a self-consistent dust scale height, one is the astrophysical relevance of a pressure bump. Lastly, while this work allows one to characterize the streaming turbulence, we emphasize our current inability to connect the strength of turbulence to the formation of planetesimals.

items.title: A Solar Optical Clock
items.abstract: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.
