items.title: Pairwise assessment correlations predict cooperation of the Leading Eight under private assessment
items.abstract: Indirect reciprocity can sustain cooperation when individuals use reputations to decide whom to help. The Leading Eight norms sustain such cooperation under public assessment, where all individuals share the same assessments. Under private assessment, however, observers may disagree, yet their assessments remain correlated. Two quantities, the average fraction of good assessments $h$ and the conditional probability $h_{\mathrm G}$ that one observer assesses a player as good given that another does, are known to determine the stability of cooperation, but how $h_{\mathrm G}$ itself is determined has remained open. Within a pairwise approximation, we derive a closed equation for $h_{\mathrm G}$ that, together with that for $h$, determines both quantities for all eight norms, including third-order ones. This description substantially improves agreement with simulations over a mean-field approximation that neglects correlations, and recovers the known classification of the Leading Eight into three classes. The remaining discrepancies are largest for L2 and L5 at low error rates and decrease as assessment error increases. Relating $h_{\mathrm G}$ to the variance of individual goodness suggests that these discrepancies reflect information beyond the first two moments of the goodness distribution. Our framework provides a concise and analytically tractable tool for evaluating social norms under private assessment.

items.title: Connectivism as an Innovative Didactic Experience in Preservice Physics Teacher Education
items.abstract: This chapter examines the use of connectivism as a pedagogical approach in preservice physics teacher education through a classroom experience conducted in a Contemporary Physics course at the Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia (UPTC). The study involved 21 preservice teachers organized into four collaborative groups. Using a qualitative approach, students selected and discussed digital learning resources, interacted through WhatsApp, and prepared collaborative reports connecting contemporary physics concepts with scientific and technological applications. The analysis considered conceptual understanding, argumentation, questioning, critical thinking, relationships among concepts, and the use of digital resources. Students' reports and feedback indicated favorable perceptions of the collaborative activities and provided examples of conceptual connections, evidence-based explanations, and reflection on future teaching practices. The chapter discusses the possibilities of connectivist learning networks for physics teacher education, drawing on the findings of this particular classroom experience.

items.title: How Can Consciousness Propagate Through Chemical Synapses? Conscious Ontogenetic Development Through Phasic Release and Synaptic Density, Within Subconscious Priors of Tonic Stimulation
items.abstract: The transmission of consciousness through a chemical synapses is an under-specified probable occurrence. Chemical transmission is essential for neuronal propagation and neural propagation is essential within many existing measurements of consciousness. The development and plasticity of consciousness throughout an animal's lifetime requires grounded chemical distinctions, executive and non-executive processing and discrete neurotransmission should be neurobiologically consistent with existing accounts of consciousness. These hypotheses propose chemical-conscious correlates between neurons and are attached through evolution to established cognitive and environmental mechanisms. These hypotheses suggest consciousness may be chemically affected at global scales and developed ontogenetically during continuous environmental rationalization and all subsequent propagation. Single-synaptic phasic transmitter transients are positioned as executive signals within neural propagation, selecting synaptic and possibly epigenetic reconsolidation while directing attention towards significance within tonic stimulation. This framing is consistent with phasic and tonic dynamics, with each transmitter being differentiated by their established functions. Phasic transients are further suggested to direct cortical spreading (an established signature of consciousness) under tonic, epigenetic, and synaptic allowance. Because phasic release fundamentally affects synaptic plasticity, while synapses determine the threshold and magnitude of phasic response, this framing allows a developmental and individually variable model of consciousness. Existing theories may be extended under this hypothetical developmental framing, such as Predictive Processing, Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT), Integrated Information Theory (IIT), and Affective Neuroscience; extending each framework by approaching phasic response as a significance signal at the synaptic scale, providing mechanisms through which present conscious experience updates future conscious experience. Because each hypothesis is falsifiable, provided predictions and experimental directions can largely determine the accuracy of each claim; given hypotheses are precise enough to fail and many of their correlating experiments are practical enough to proceed. If this account holds, it points toward practical improvements in consciousness research, chemical synaptic mechanisms, depression treatments, therapeutic approaches, memory rehabilitation, learning environment refinement strategies, and early developmental interventions.

items.title: On Motivating the Choice of Link Function in Binomial Regression Through A Latent Abundance Process
items.abstract: Ecologists commonly apply binomial regression to study binary data. Often, the link function in binomial regression is not purposefully chosen, but instead selected on the grounds of interpretation or computation efficiency. However, if the binary response is the result of a latent abundance process, then the link function implies assumptions for this underlying process. The most well-known example of this is the complementary log-log (cloglog) link, which has direct connections with the probability of a positive count under a latent Poisson distribution. If the binary response can be assumed to represent a truncated latent count, the cloglog link can be a better choice than the logit link. On the other hand, counts in ecology are often overdispersed, meaning the assumption of an underlying Poisson abundance process is unrealistic. In this article, we provide a framework for consideration of the link choice in binomial regression, in terms of the latent abundance process that binary responses can represent. Aside from the Poisson case mentioned above, we show that the cloglog link is the right choice if the latent abundance process represents the biomass of individuals, or if the latent abundance process comes from an overdispersed count distribution with a linear mean-variance relationship. For the case where the latent count follows a negative binomial distribution with a quadratic mean-variance relationship, we derive a new generalized complementary log-log (gcloglog) link function, which includes the case of the cloglog link as well as that of the logit link, where the latter implies assuming moderate overdispersion in the form of a geometric distribution. Two simulation studies demonstrate that cloglog and logit link binomial regression can exhibit bias and undercoverage when the latent count is more overdispersed than assumed, while gcloglog link models overcome this issue but in practice require replication in the binomial response for reliable estimation. Two real ecological datasets further illustrate how to use the gcloglog link binomial regression in practice including as a means of sensitivity analysis. We encourage ecologists to give more thought to the choice of link function in binomial regression, based on considering the latent abundance process and its properties.

items.title: Private forest reserves in Brazils agricultural landscapes effectively sustain the occupancy and abundance of multiple threatened large vertebrate
items.abstract: 1. Understanding the factors that shape wildlife abundance and distributions is at the core of applied ecology and wildlife management. Accurate predictions on the population level outcomes of land management are especially urgent in biodiversity hotspots around the world that are undergoing rapid transformation. In South America, both the Cerrado and Amazon are increasingly being converted to agricultural land-uses to produce soybean and corn and raise cattle. Over the last several decades Brazil has become one of the leading global producers of these products. At the same time, Brazil has some of the strongest federal regulations focused on protecting native habitat. The Native Vegetation Protection Law (or the Forest Code) requires private properties retain native vegetation as Legal Reserves, and as a result more than half of the countrys remaining native habitat now lies on private lands. Whether retained habitat under this ambitious policy sustains populations of large, wide-ranging vertebrates across entire agricultural production landscapes remains untested. 2. Here, we conducted a landscape scale survey using camera-trap stations across ~606,000 km2 of Mato Grosso, Brazils largest producer of cattle, soybean and corn. We sampled 115 independent sites between November 2024 and September 2025, spanning both crop seasons. We estimated occupancy of jaguars and expected abundance of white-lipped peccary and lowland tapir, using a combination of occupancy and Royle Nichols models. We fit an abundance-mediated interaction model to formally test the role of prey abundance in driving jaguar occupancy across the landscape. 3. We found high occurrence and expected abundance of all three species. Forest cover was the only covariate common to all top models for every species: predicted jaguar occupancy probability rose as forest cover increased and expected peccary and tapir abundance also increased as a function of forest cover. 4. Our empirical estimates from abundance-mediated interaction models were consistent with jaguar occupancy being a function of both habitat availability and prey (peccary) abundance. 5. Synthesis and applications. Native forest retained on private land under Brazil's Forest Code is associated with the persistence and local abundance of an apex predator, a megaherbivore and a keystone ungulate across one of the world's most intensively farmed regions. Jaguar occupancy rose from 0.33 to 0.87 as forest cover increased from 15% to 65%, indicating that maintaining Legal Reserve requirements is central to retaining large vertebrates in production landscapes. Private reserves should be managed as complements to, not substitutes for, protected areas and Indigenous territories, and habitat-retention policy should be paired with mitigation of crop damage and livestock depredation to prevent retained forests from becoming ecological traps. Our framework provides a transferable approach for evaluating habitat-retention policies for wide-ranging species elsewhere.

items.title: Educational games for teaching science in middle school: an integrative review
items.abstract: Given the contemporary challenges of science education, active learning methodologies present themselves as a teaching strategy aimed at promoting greater student engagement, thereby making the teaching-learning process more meaningful. Within this context, play-based games emerge as didactic strategies that combine playfulness, interaction, and the collective construction of knowledge. Accordingly, the present study aimed to conduct a survey of the main play-based games applicable to middle school (Ensino Fundamental Anos Finais) for teaching Biology content. The research is characterized as an integrative review, developed through searches in the Portal Periódicos CAPES and Google Scholar databases, covering publications from 2019 to 2026. A total of 1,669 articles were identified, of which, after the screening stages and application of inclusion and exclusion criteria, only 13 composed the final sample for analysis. The results evidenced the use of physical games, such as board and card games, dice, and dominoes, addressing content in Zoology, Ecology, Cell Biology, Botany, Physiology, and Genetics. The analyzed studies indicate that games foster engagement, active participation, and the consolidation of scientific concepts, in addition to enabling diagnostic assessment when developed under teacher mediation. In times of unmotivated students and screens competing with the blackboard, playfulness presents itself not as an alternative, but as a necessity. The results of this study prove it: when students play, they do not just learn Biology, they live Biology. And what is lived is not forgotten. Investing in educational games is, therefore, investing in a more humane, active, meaningful, and innovative science education.

items.title: Negentropic Value Currency: From Scarcity to Order—Monetary Value Anchored in Net Order Creation
items.abstract: What anchors the value of money? Metallism answers with commodity scarcity, chartalism with sovereign power, free-banking theory with issuer reputation, and cryptocurrency with algorithmic scarcity. Despite their differences, these traditions share one premise: monetary value must rest on some form of scarcity. This paper argues that the premise, not any particular answer, is the problem. As the marginal cost of basic material provision falls toward zero and value creation migrates into knowledge, ecology, and care, a scarcity-based unit of account systematically misprices the activities on which civilizational survival depends. Drawing on the entropy economics of Georgescu-Roegen and the energy-money proposals of Soddy and the technocracy movement, we develop a candidate anchor that replaces scarcity with net order creation: value as the net increment of systemic order, measured by exergy input net of ecological entropy debt, directed non-equilibrium maintenance time, and structural information gain against a no-intervention counterfactual. Four screening criteria select the Cobb-Douglas power family as the unique twice-differentiable functional form, and the symmetric benchmark minimizes both error transmission and single-factor manipulation leverage. We supply microfoundations (existence, uniqueness, and conditional decentralization of the planner's optimum by means of consensus coefficients), a general equilibrium with endogenous calibration, mechanism-design defenses, component-level consistency checks in which R&D intensity explains 68.5% of the cross-country variance in knowledge-output density and survives country and year fixed effects in an innovation panel covering 90 economies, and an engineering blueprint for a recomputable measurement infrastructure. A first end-to-end measurement of the information factor on public bibliometric data (52,690 citing works across three anchor contributions) demonstrates computability, returns an intuitively valid ordering orthogonal to citation volume, and — by falsifying the original normalization of the information-gain formula — motivates the bounded Jensen–Shannon form adopted in the text. The macrostability of the anchor is deliberately left to companion work; this paper establishes the theory of value and the conditions under which it can be operationalized.

items.title: Revelation and Prophetic Cognition in the Philosophy of Avicenna
items.abstract: Revelation occupies a significant position at the intersection of metaphysics, psychology, and political philosophy in Avicenna’s account of prophecy. Building upon questions developed by al-Fārābī, Avicenna explains prophetic knowledge through the exceptional perfection of human cognitive faculties and their relationship with the intelligible order. Although God remains the ultimate source of revelation, its reception is understood within a hierarchy of intellectual and celestial mediation. Prophecy thus represents a distinctive realization of human capacities rather than a phenomenon wholly external to human nature. This article examines the relationship between emanation, the rational soul, intellectual perfection, and the imaginative reception of revealed knowledge. Particular attention is given to the distinction between intellectual apprehension and the representation of intelligible content through images, whether during sleep or in waking experience. The discussion also considers the practical significance of prophecy: the prophet communicates knowledge in forms capable of guiding collective life and shaping moral and political conduct. Avicenna’s account consequently presents revelation as both an exceptional mode of cognition and a foundation for the public responsibilities of prophetic leadership. At the same time, the possibility of related experiences among spiritually disciplined individuals requires a distinction between extraordinary cognition and the full capacities associated with the prophetic mission.

items.title: Compound climate extremes predict dengue risk at operational lead times across Brazil
items.abstract: Brazil has one of the highest dengue burdens globally, with transmission influenced by climate events. Yet, the effects of compound climate extremes on dengue risk and prediction have not been quantified to date. Using a Bayesian spatiotemporal model of monthly dengue cases across 435 health regions from 2010 to 2025, we estimated relative risk associated with interacting long-lag and short-lag drought indicators and temperature anomalies across nine Köppen-Geiger climatic zones, adjusting for absolute temperature and El Niño-Southern Oscillation. Long-lag dry, mid-lag warm and short-lag wet conditions were associated with the highest relative risk in five climatic zones, with temperature anomalies modifying hydrometeorological dynamics more strongly in temperate than tropical areas. Climate covariates improved the prediction of case counts and outbreaks compared to baseline models at lead times of 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, and for the upcoming season 5 months ahead. Improvements were greatest in the Northeast, Southeast, and Midwest. Recent dengue incidence provided the greatest improvement at the 1-month lead, whereas combining incidence with climate information performed best at 3- and 6-month leads. We extended our framework to weekly state-level predictions of the season ahead to align with national public health planning. We proposed a multi-staged dengue forecasting approach to enhance early warning and response across Brazil.

items.title: Beyond biological threats: A global ecological study of International Health Regulations (2005) core capacities and multi-hazard disaster outcomes, 2015–2023
items.abstract: Abstract The International Health Regulations (IHR, 2005) apply an all-hazards approach to public health risks irrespective of origin. This study examined whether IHR core capacities, previously studied mainly in relation to infectious diseases, were associated with multi-hazard disaster outcomes. Across 196 States Parties from 2015 to 2023, an ecological panel linked nine cross-cutting IHR capacities and a study-specific IHR average score to Sendai Framework Monitor (SFM) and Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) mortality and morbidity. Associations were estimated with Poisson regression models adjusted for country and year fixed effects, population size, and socioeconomic factors. Analyses were repeated for 2020–2023. A 10-point increase in IHR average score corresponded to 39.1% and 40.7% lower SFM and EM-DAT mortality rates during 2020–2023, but not across 2015–2023. Laboratory was associated with lower mortality in both datasets. For disaster morbidity, a 10-point increase in IHR average score was associated with 44.7% lower SFM morbidity rates across 2015–2023, but not during 2020–2023 or in EM-DAT. Higher IHR Coordination , Surveillance , and Risk communication scores were associated with lower SFM morbidity across 2015–2023. Linking harmonized IHR self-assessment scores with two global disaster datasets indicates the relevance of IHR (2005) core capacities beyond biological threats.

items.title: Five-Year Longitudinal Changes and Determinants of Serum PFAS Exposure Profiles in a Community-Based Cohort from Southern China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants widely detected in human populations. Although regulatory actions have restricted several legacy PFAS, longitudinal evidence on changes in human PFAS exposure and their determinants remains limited, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. This study aimed to characterize five-year changes in serum legacy PFAS concentrations and identify demographic and geographic determinants of longitudinal exposure among community residents in Guangzhou, southern China. Methods We conducted a prospective community-based cohort study of 958 residents from three communities representing distinct residential environments: an urban commercial area, an industrial/livestock/fishery area, and an ecological conservation area. Participants were examined at baseline (2018–2019) and follow-up (2023–2024). Serum legacy PFAS concentrations were measured using ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Temporal changes were assessed using paired analyses, and longitudinal determinants were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction. Results Six legacy PFAS with detection frequencies approaching 100% were included in longitudinal analyses. Over five years, total PFOS, PFNA, PFDA, and total PFHxS concentrations decreased from 14.129 to 11.262, 0.998 to 0.871, 0.692 to 0.532, and 0.771 to 0.598 ng/mL, respectively, whereas PFOA increased from 5.534 to 9.789 ng/mL and PFHpA from 0.024 to 0.034 ng/mL. Older age was consistently associated with higher concentrations of all six PFAS. Residential location was also an important determinant, with higher PFAS concentrations observed among residents of the urban commercial and industrial/livestock/fishery communities than among those in the ecological conservation community. Conclusions Serum legacy PFAS exposure showed heterogeneous five-year trajectories in this community-based population in Guangzhou, with divergent temporal patterns across individual PFAS. The contrasting trends and persistent demographic and geographic differences highlight the complexity of human PFAS exposure following regulatory changes. Continued biomonitoring and identification of populations with elevated exposure are warranted to support targeted exposure reduction and public health surveillance.

items.title: From Hippocrates to UTCI: Twenty-Five Centuries of Human Biometeorology
items.abstract: Abstract Human biometeorology, which describes how the atmosphere and the wider environment affect human health, well - being, and performance, was initially organized and presented as a 20th-century discipline, formalized by Tromp and Landsberg and later by physiological thermal indices such as the Physiologically Equivalent Temperature (PET) and the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI). This paper takes a longer view. It traces a continuous, if uneven, tradition of linking atmospheric conditions to human health across more than two millennia: religious and mythological ideas, the weather knowledge of indigenous societies, biblical and ancient Near Eastern sources, the medical systems of Egypt, China and India, Presocratic natural philosophy, the Hippocratic Corpus, Aristotle and the Peripatetic school, and Hellenistic and Roman scholarship. It also argues that the thermal environment is not only something scholarship later described, but a force that helped shape culture itself - visible in the thermal picture of paradise and hell across unrelated traditions and in the open - air institutions of Greek public life. On the modern side, we place the decisive physical step earlier than usual: Konrad Büttner formulated the energy balance of the human body in the 1930s, three decades before Fanger and six before PET, and Wolf H. Weihe stated in 1976 the problem that still governs the field: especially the atmosphere acts through many factors, and their ranking depends on the question asked. Modern rational indices quantify a long-standing insight rather than inventing it: human health depends on several atmospheric factors acting together, not on air temperature alone.

items.title: Disparity in the Prevalence of Pit and Fissure Sealants Among 12-Year-Old Children in Puerto Rico: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Pit and fissure sealants (PFS) are an important tool in preventing and managing caries development on primary and permanent posterior teeth in children and adolescents. Among children living in Puerto Rico, particularly those of low socioeconomic status, this preventive measure has historically been underutilized. The completion of the Government Health Insurance (GHI) reform in 2000 marked a pivotal moment, expanding access to PFS across the entire island. In this study, we compared oral health data from 12-year-old school-attending children in Puerto Rico in 1997 and 2011 to evaluate changes in PFS prevalence and socioeconomic disparities, using school type as a proxy for socioeconomic status. Methods This cross-sectional study used two probabilistic samples (n = 1,587 in 2011 and n = 1,435 in 1997) of 12-year-olds enrolled in school, stratified by GHI region, school type, and sex. Calibrated examiners evaluated the presence of PFS on at least one permanent first molar. Logistic regression models compared PFS prevalence by school type in 1997 and 2011, adjusting for sex and region. A P -value ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Sex distribution and school type were similar in 1997 (49% female; 18% private schools) and 2011 (53% female; 23% private schools). Between 1997 and 2011, PFS prevalence increased among all children (4.3% vs. 18.1%), as well as among children attending private (11.1% vs. 25.8%), public rural (3.4% vs. 16.3%), and public urban schools (2.5% vs. 16.9%). Participants attending public-rural and public-urban schools were less likely to have sealants, both in 1997 ( OR public−rural =0.19; 95% CI: 0.07–0.46; OR public−urban =0.17; 95% CI: 0.06–0.48) and in 2011 ( OR public−rural =0.57; 95% CI: 0.33–0.99; OR public−urban =0.60; 95% CI: 0.39–0.93), versus those from private schools. Conclusions PFS prevalence increased among 12-year-old school-attending children in Puerto Rico across all school types between 1997 and 2011, a period that coincided with island-wide GHI implementation. However, disparities between children attending public and private schools persisted. These findings suggest that expanded insurance coverage alone may be insufficient to eliminate disparities in preventive dental care and that socioeconomic background may influence PFS utilization.

items.title: Guaraci: A Reproducible Orchestrator for Direct Extraction of Brazilian Public-Health and Environmental Data
items.abstract: Brazilian public data relevant to health and the environment are dispersed across heterogeneous official systems - FTP servers (DATASUS), REST APIs (OpenDataSUS/DEMAS), and web portals (gov.br) - and published in legacy, often compressed formats (e.g., DBC/DBF) with schemas that change across years and topics, which makes integrated, reproducible reuse costly. Guaraci is an open-source (MIT), Docker-first orchestrator that acquires such data directly from the primary official sources, decodes legacy formats, harmonizes heterogeneous schemas, records full provenance, and delivers the result to a downstream data lake. It integrates 90+ sources spanning public health (DATASUS microdata such as hospital and mortality information system; OpenDataSUS arbovirus and immunization data; gov.br sanitation indicators) and the environment (NASA POWER climate series, FIRMS active-fire detections and GPM IMERG precipitation), behind a single asynchronous job engine exposed through a command-line interface and a REST API. Data are decoded to records with pyreaddbc/dbfread, harmonized by taking the union of all historical columns (null-padding missing fields) and exported to CSV, Parquet and SQLite with a machine-readable file capturing source, request filters and output paths. By abstracting unstable FTP servers, paginated APIs and legacy encodings behind one reproducible mechanism, Guaraci lowers the technical barrier to Brazilian public data and continuously supplies analysis-ready inputs for spatio-temporal epidemiological modelling, machine-learning applications and cross-source studies.

items.title: Association Between Neighbourhood-level Antibiotic Utilization and the Rate of Community-Associated C. difficile (CA-CDI) Infection: An Ecological Study.
items.abstract: Despite reductions in hospital-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) incidence in Canada and the United States, the incidence of community-associated CDI (CA-CDI) has remained high. We sought to investigate whether neighbourhood-level variation in antibiotic utilization is associated with CA-CDI. We conducted a neighbourhood-level ecological study across 1,520 neighbourhoods in Ontario, Canada. Residents aged ≥66 without hospitalization in the prior 30 days were eligible for inclusion from 2017 to 2023. Antibiotic utilization, CDI cases, and population were identified for each neighbourhood using comprehensive province-wide databases. CA-CDI rate was the outcome (incident cases of CA-CDI/10,000 person-years). Rate of antibiotic utilization (DOT per 1000 person-days) was the primary exposure. The rate-ratio (RR) of CA-CDI associated with increased antibiotic utilization was estimated using negative-binomial regression, adjusting for 8 demographic and health care covariates. We also evaluated risk based on low-, moderate-, and high-risk antibiotic strata based on published literature. We identified 19,757 CA-CDI cases. We observed substantial variation in antibiotic utilization across neighbourhoods (Median=21.1 DOT/1000 person-days; interquartile range [IQR], 16.7-25.6). After adjustments, we observed an association between overall antibiotic utilization (RR=1.13 per 10-point increase in DOT; 95% confidence interval [95%CI], 1.09-1.18). A gradient wherein higher risk antibiotic agents were more strongly associated with CA-CDI was apparent (Low-risk: RR=1.08; 95%CI, 1.01-1.15; Moderate-risk: RR=1.27; 95%CI, 1.15-1.39; High-risk: RR=1.73; 95%CI, 1.13-2.66). Neighbourhoods with higher antibiotic utilization, especially for moderate and high-risk antibiotics, have higher CA-CDI incidence. Reducing variability in neighbourhood antibiotic utilization could help reduce the burden of CDI.

items.title: Addressing the weight of the issue: gaps in obesity education among US osteopathic medical students.
items.abstract: Context Obesity is a significant public health concern, with the United States experiencing some of the highest obesity rates worldwide. Despite the widespread prevalence and negative impacts on patient health, obesity education in medical school curricula remains insufficient. This training deficit contributes to a lack of preparedness among medical students in the management of obesity, leading to healthcare provider bias and inadequate patient care. Objectives This study aims to identify potential gaps in obesity education within US osteopathic medical schools by assessing current osteopathic medical students' knowledge, confidence, and perceptions of medical school obesity education. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was distributed to osteopathic medical students across all 42 US osteopathic medical schools through the Student Osteopathic Medical Association (SOMA) weekly emails, SOMA internal chapter emails, and SOMA social media accounts from October 2024 to December 2024. The inclusion criteria were that participants had to be currently enrolled first-, second-, third-, and fourth-year osteopathic medical students and provide informed consent. The responses were summarized utilizing descriptive analysis. Each survey question was analyzed independently, considering the varying number of responses received per question. Results A total of 208 students participated in the survey. Out of the 208 respondents, most students felt somewhat prepared (38.5 %) or unprepared/very unprepared (32.7 %) to manage obesity and provide nutrition education in the clinical setting. Due to the number of participants, the responses are considered in aggregate and not grouped by cohort year. In addition, there was nearly an even split among students regarding comfort in discussing obesity and weight management with patients, with 30.6 % stating that they are uncomfortable or very uncomfortable, 37.4 % reporting being somewhat comfortable, and 32.0 % feeling comfortable or very comfortable. Only 14.1 % of students reported having standardized patient encounters regarding obesity counseling, with most of these encounters (55.2 %) lasting less than 30 min. Regarding comfort discussing weight bias and stigma, 59.8 % of the students reported feeling somewhat comfortable, comfortable, or very comfortable discussing weight bias and stigma, while 40.2 % were slightly uncomfortable or not comfortable addressing the topic with patients. Given the limited sample size and response rate, these findings are exploratory and limited by a low response rate and potential response bias. Conclusions These findings suggest potential gaps in obesity education among the responding osteopathic medical students. While limited by sample size and possible response bias, the results highlight opportunities for strengthening obesity-related curricula, particularly in experiential learning and weight bias training.

items.title: Learners do not readily form abstract category representations across sensory modalities.
items.abstract: A long-standing debate in cognitive science centers around whether our internal representations of the external world are abstract and amodal or whether they are grounded by sensory modality. Perceptual category learning presents a unique test bed of this debate as categories exist within all sensory modalities, but there is mixed evidence about whether people form abstract representations that can be analogized across modalities. In the present study, we examine whether learners form such abstract representations of auditory and visual categories that share the same rule-based structure. Across three experiments, we examine whether learners spontaneously or explicitly form abstract representations across sensory modalities. Overall, we found no evidence of shared abstract representations even in the conditions that would theoretically most strongly encourage it-when information across modalities was conceptually aligned (rather than misaligned), when information across modalities was encountered within the same task (rather than separate tasks), and when participants were explicitly instructed to analogize across modalities (rather than doing so spontaneously). These results suggest that even when abstract representation across auditory and visual modalities is encouraged, the knowledge formed during perceptual category learning is modality-specific. These results highlight the importance of considering the role of modality in category learning and cognition more broadly. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: On bias in detecting bias: A signal detection analysis of attributions to gender discrimination.
items.abstract: Discrimination is the unjust treatment of people based on their group membership, and detecting discrimination is a necessary first step in countering it. Attributions to discrimination have often been conceptualized in terms of signal detection theory, with researchers speculating about the role of sensitivity (i.e., observers' ability to recognize discrimination) and response bias (i.e., their tendency to judge that discrimination is present) in observers' judgments. Here, we take a first step toward moving beyond conceptual applications to empirical signal detection theory analyses of attributions to discrimination across five studies examining judgments about gender discrimination in corporate pay raise decisions. We find that prototypes (Studies 1-3) and their alignment with the actual pattern of decisions (Studies 2-4) inform observers' response bias, reflecting differences in their attribution of unfair outcomes to discrimination (Study 5). In contrast, the extent of harm caused by discriminatory outcomes exerts a small effect on sensitivity and a large effect on response bias (Studies 1-3), which reflects observers' determination of a fair standard for decisions (Study 5). Theoretically, the present work contributes to the causal analysis of central factors shaping attributions to discrimination. Specifically, we shed light on whether effects of these factors are mediated by response bias or sensitivity, and assess their causal origin in either the application of a merit standard or attributional processing. items.title: Examining cognitive correlates of motivated memory in older adults using standard and naturalistic paradigms
items.abstract: Background: Learning and retaining information is essential for daily function. Research within several sectors of psychology (e.g., educational, cognitive, behavioral neuroscience) suggests that motivation and the reward system interact with memory structures, thus potentially influencing memory performance. This has been termed motivated memory. Motivated memory has been studied in adults across the lifespan but has yet to be thoroughly explored using established and novel, naturalistic paradigms in older adults. Studying the effect of motivation on memory in older adults is particularly important because a decline in cognitive function (i.e., memory) over time can lead to decreased independence and quality of life and an increase of caregiver burden. Motivated memory mechanisms may offer unique opportunities for intervention for those with cognitive decline. As such, greater understanding regarding the extent to which motivation can impact cognition, especially for memory for naturalistic, ecologically valid information, is needed. The aim of the current study is to gain a more thorough understanding of how motivation impacts memory. Specifically, we aimed to address important gaps in the literature regarding 1) the cognitive correlates of the motivated memory effect (i.e., episodic memory, executive function), 2) the type of information and learning processes that are most influenced by motivation (i.e., item memory, semantic memory, associative memory; free recall, recognition), 3) the effect of motivation on memory, specifically in a population of older adults, and 4) using a paradigm that simulates naturalistic information. Methods: This study recruited 53 participants to complete two cognitive tasks: an established task called the Selectivity Task (ST) and a novel task called the Motivated Memory Task (MMT). Both tasks assessed recall of higher value information compared to lower value information (e.g., motivated memory). Participants also completed questionnaires assessing their current mood, cognitive function, and motivation. The ST utilized an arbitrary point value system, and the MMT was designed to present naturalistic, health-related information that is of higher value (dementia risk factors and prevention facts) and lower value (polio risk factors and prevention facts). Participants also completed a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment, from which we derived composite scores of cognitive domains to examine cognitive correlates of motivated memory. Regressions examined the cognitive correlates of motivated memory on the ST, using the selectivity index (ST-SI; Aim 1). A series of ANCOVAs were performed to evaluate the effect of motivation on recalling higher versus lower value items on the novel MMT (Aim 2). Results: Results suggest that the ST-SI was not associated with either episodic memory, executive function, or motivation score. Contrary to our hypotheses, on the MMT, participants recalled more semantic details about the prevention facts for polio overall, across all time points. However, consistent with hypotheses, participants recognized dementia risk factors with greater accuracy than polio risk factors on a test of delayed recognition. Conclusion: Motivation to learn health information may influence item recognition memory but not free recall and not semantic or associative memory, possibly providing support for the dual-process theory of memory and aging. These results suggest that healthcare providers should encourage patients to use cue-based recognition for their care rather than relying on free recall.

items.title: An exploratory study of relationships between the executive functions and spatiotemporal control in a complex motor task: the spatial tapping task
items.abstract: Executive functions (EFs) are cognitive processes enabling planning, control, and regulation of behavior. A variety of tasks have been developed to evaluate EFs, from complex reasoning to simpler inhibition tasks, reflecting the diversity of symptoms observed in patients with executive deficits. Recent research has emphasized their unity , proposing three core functions, working memory, inhibition, and switching, that share resources and combine to enable complex tasks. Yet, no single task captures both the unity and diversity of EFs, limiting the development of a unified framework and a balanced assessment. To address this gap, we designed the spatial tapping task, a timing paradigm combining finger tapping and circle drawing. Finger tapping requires working memory for explicit timing control, whereas circle drawing requires anticipatory control akin to switching to control movement trajectory, enabling implicit timing control. Participants produce taps along a circular trajectory with the tempo increasing progressively. A slow tempo favors discrete movements with long pauses between taps, whereas a fast tempo promotes continuous motion. Previous analyses supported a change in timing control mode with increasing tempo. Here, we explored the hypothesis that EFs are engaged accordingly: working memory in the slow/discrete phase, switching in the fast/continuous phase, and inhibition in the intermediate phase, where demands for continuous motion increase. In two studies combined into a single dataset, we compared scores with those from neuropsychological tests using correlations. We found that timing accuracy in the slow/discrete phase was associated with working memory, spatial accuracy in the fast/continuous phase with switching, and longer contact time in the intermediate phase with inhibition. We also explored whether performance was consistent with the EF deficits described in the literature, and the potential contribution of motor output, reporting scores obtained across populations with executive deficits (aging and dementia), combined executive and motor impairments (schizophrenia), and motor expertise (biscriptual writers), along with matched controls. Findings were consistent, although often more specific, and highlighted an important contribution of motor output. Altogether, our results provide initial evidence that the task can be used to investigate EFs, although cognitive, motor, and sensory contributions need to be disentangled to improve its specificity.

items.title: The construction of professionals' perception of emotional intelligence competence and the symbolic association of performance and project success in the UK construction industry
items.abstract: Research Gap - The UK construction industry faces challenges such as disputes, low productivity, and poor project delivery, partly due to the lack of soft skills, including communication, motivation, negotiation, ethics, and Emotional Intelligence (EI). The impact of EI remains unclear. This study argues that addressing industry issues requires both technical and soft skills, with EI being crucial. A gap exists in understanding EI awareness, perceptions, and use, especially its effect on performance and projects. Purpose - This thesis explores the link between EI competence and construction professionals' perceived performance, evaluating whether EI is vital for project success in the UK. Methodology - Using semi-structured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis via NVivo 14, the study maps EI to Goleman’s models to examine understanding and application of EI, recommending ways to foster an EI-aware workforce. Findings: Few participants received EI training; however, those who did showed improved engagement with stakeholders. Most lacked EI training, indicating unawareness. The holistic EI skills included stakeholder engagement, trust, communication, teambuilding, resilience, social awareness, relationship management, and humour, all of which are essential for conflict resolution, teamwork, and psychological safety. A lack of EI led to conflicts, delays, operational issues, and increased costs. Professionals see a broad industry need for EI awareness, recommending integration into competency frameworks by industry bodies such as RICS, CIOB, CIAT, ICE, and APM and academic curricula. Originality - The study highlights a critical lack of EI knowledge in the UK construction sector, advocating for EI to be part of mandatory training, standards, and education.

items.title: When digital literacy meets negative bias: Understanding the adoption of online information and sentiment on X
items.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly mediate how citizens engage with public policy, shaping not only access to information but also the formation of collective interpretations and sentiments. In the context of Indonesia’s Free Nutritious Meal (Makan Bergizi Gratis: MBG) program, this study examines the relationship between individual digital literacy and online information adoption, while simultaneously mapping public sentiment and discourse dynamics on X. Employing a concurrent mixed-methods design, the study combines an online survey of 385 social media users drawing on the DigComp 2.2 framework and the Information Adoption Model with large-scale social media analysis of 87,589 MBG-related mentions on X collected between April and August 2025 using Drone Emprit. Regression analysis revealed that digital literacy significantly predicts information adoption regarding the MBG program (β = 0.581, R² = 0.549, p < 0.001), indicating that digital literacy explains 54.9% of the variance in information adoption and substantially enhances individuals’ capacity to evaluate and accept policy-related information. While digital literacy supports information adoption at the individual level, the overall online discourse surrounding MBG remained predominantly negative, suggesting a disconnect between individual informational competence and collective sentiment formation. Sentiment analysis further revealed that public discourse was predominantly negative (56%), compared with positive (43%) and neutral (1%) expressions, with significant surges observed in May and July 2025. Network analysis additionally revealed that negative sentiment is concentrated around accounts with high centrality and influence, thereby amplifying critical narratives through networked interactions. These findings highlight a structural tension between individual informational competence and collective sentiment formation in digital communication environments. This research contributes to the existing body of work on digital communication and public policy by illustrating that initiatives aimed at improving digital literacy should be complemented by network-aware communication strategies, such as influencer engagement and real-time discourse monitoring, to bolster public trust and legitimacy in extensive policy interventions.

items.title: Doray the Catbaloganon Explorer on Probability: Validation of a Mathematics Strategic Intervention Material (SIM)
items.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to develop and validate Doray the Catbaloganon Explorer on Probability, a culturally contextualized and gamified Strategic Intervention Material (SIM) for teaching probability to Grade 8 learners. Methodology:The study employed a descriptive-evaluative research design.Five experts and Grade 8 students evaluated the developed SIM in terms of content validity, clarity and readability, engagement and motivation, practicality and usefulness, design and visual appeal, and usability.Results: All 14 indicators obtained an Item-Level Content Validity Index (I-CVI) of 1.00, resulting in a Scale-Level Content Validity Index (S-CVI) of 1.00, indicating excellent content validity.The SIM received Very High/Excellent ratings across all evaluation dimensions, with mean scores ranging from 4.89 to 4.98 and standard deviations ranging from 0.02 to 0.08.Reliability received the highest rating among both experts (M = 4.97, SD = 0.03) and students (M = 4.98, SD = 0.02). Conclusion:The developed SIM demonstrated excellent content validity and very high ratings for instructional quality, usability, and acceptability.It may therefore be used as a supplementary instructional resource for teaching probability to Grade 8 learners.

items.title: Development of Communication Styles Scale (CSS) for University Students: Qualitative Item Generation and Content Validation
items.abstract: University life is one of the most challenging phases of a student's life because of the interplay of social and academic demands, resulting in anxiety and stress (Yan, 2025; Zhang et al., 2022; SAMFIRA, 2020). One of the challenges is maintaining good interpersonal relationships and communication is imperative to this (Horan et al., 2021, Griggio et al., 2019; Chandra, Mohammadnezhad, & Ward, 2018). However, as people vary both in verbal and non-verbal communication due to cultural differences (Mascarenhas et al., 2015); it is important to know more about this area to develop effective communication skills accordingly. The current study aimed to develop a scale to measure communication styles among university students. Following a rigorous literature review, which identified gaps in existing measures, two focus groups and three semi-structured interviews with clinical psychologists were conducted. After thematic analysis, a final pool of items was generated for expert review. For this, Content Validity Index was established by clinical psychologists through rating the relevance of the items to the construct (N=7) and 40 items were retained.

items.title: Monitoring AI-generated English research texts: lexical-semantic accuracy, source fidelity, and revision performance
items.abstract: Introduction Linguistically fluent AI-generated English texts can conceal lexical-semantic shifts, altered concept boundaries, source omissions, and unsupported causal formulations. This study compared English paragraphs generated under general and source-constrained conditions and examined how learners' global judgments and localized problem marking were associated with subsequent written revision. Methods Seventy-three agricultural and forestry students evaluated two English paragraphs generated from Chinese source materials under a fixed sequence of general and source-constrained prompts, then selected and revised one paragraph. The linked corpus comprised 146 AI-generated texts, 73 revised texts, 146 global judgment records, 657 expert rating records, 562 coded terminology units, and 511 participant-marked problems. Expert assessments covered lexical-semantic accuracy, source fidelity, and global discourse organization, while revision analyses examined global judgment discrepancy, localized problem marking, and individual-difference variables. Results Source-constrained texts received higher lexical-semantic accuracy scores (mean difference = 0.846, t = 10.634, p < 0.001, d z = 1.245) and source-fidelity scores (mean difference = 0.855, t = 8.819, p < 0.001, d z = 1.032), while global discourse organization differed little between conditions. Lexical-semantic accuracy was strongly associated with source fidelity ( b = 0.522, p < 0.001), whereas the 5,000-resample bootstrap interval for the product of the adjusted coefficients linking these measures to discourse organization spanned zero. After controlling for selected source-text quality, localized problem marking and domain knowledge were positively associated with revised quality, trust in AI-generated language output was negatively associated, and global judgment discrepancy showed no unique association. Discussion Source comparison and localized problem identification were more closely associated with successful written revision than agreement with expert global judgments. These findings highlight the importance of attending to linguistic form, semantic boundaries, and source information when evaluating and revising AI-generated English research texts.

items.title: Managing at the Margin: A Conceptual Framework of Nano-Enterprise Management, Collective Support, Survival and Real Graduation in Nigeria
items.abstract: Most Nigerian enterprises are very small, and since 2021, national policy has treated the smallest of them, those with turnover below ₦3 million and one or two workers, as a separate nano tier. Management research and support programmes often treat these ventures as miniature versions of larger firms, although their owners work under acute scarcity of capital, time and attention. This conceptual, theory-building paper integrates scarcity theory, evidence on management practices and business training in small firms, entrepreneurial bricolage and collective-action theory, and draws on the authors’ studies of cooperative membership and savings. Its specific contribution is a scarcity-based framework of nano-enterprise management that separates survival and income stability from real graduation to the micro tier, which is measured on turnover deflated to 2021 naira. Nine propositions, each with falsification criteria and boundary conditions, state that scarcity lowers the quality of management practices; those simple practices matter at least as much as conventional training for survival, and personal-initiative capability matters more for graduation; that bricolage protects survival but does not by itself produce growth; and that cooperative support helps where governance is sound and complements capability building. The paper concludes that short, simple support delivered through well-governed collectives is the most promising route to survival and graduation, although no proposition has yet been tested. It recommends that SMEDAN and development partners pilot and evaluate simple-rule and personal-initiative modules against conventional training and track graduation on deflated turnover.

items.title: Doing development differently: reframing academic development in the shadow of performance and scarcity
items.abstract: This study investigates how academic development (AD) is enacted in resource-constrained, performance-driven university contexts where formal structures are weak or absent. Drawing on qualitative data from a large private university in southwest China, the research introduces the concept of compressed institutional contexts to explain how academic work is reorganised under simultaneous demands for accountability, market responsiveness, and student outcomes. Rather than disappearing, AD is redistributed across overlapping roles and embedded within daily practices such as teaching, student support, and administrative coordination. The findings show that academic development persists in such contexts not through formalised centres or structured programmes, but as embedded and improvised practices woven into everyday academic work. Faculty development is increasingly shaped by institutional performance logics, including employability outcomes and evaluative targets, rather than by pedagogical ideals or reflective enhancement alone. Professional growth occurs primarily through multi-role enactment and real-time adaptation, as academics learn by integrating teaching, administration, and coordination responsibilities under conditions of institutional urgency. By reframing academic development as an organisationally situated and practice-based process, this paper contributes to a more inclusive understanding of AD that accounts for non-elite, market-facing, and resource-constrained institutions.

items.title: The Consistency of Subjective and Objective Factors Influencing Walking Path Choice Around Rail Transit Stations
items.abstract: The station–city integration development strategy, guided by the Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) model, has enhanced the coupling relationship between rail transit stations and urban areas. Walking, as a core mode of low-carbon urban transport, plays a significant role in the connectivity between stations and urban areas and in the rate of passenger flow dispersal. During peak periods, large volumes of passengers flood the streets, forming complex and diverse walking paths that penetrate urban neighborhoods. Route choice is a complex decision-making process influenced by both subjective and objective factors. Previous studies on pathfinding activities have often focused on either subjective or objective factors in isolation, with limited research on their interaction. This paper establishes a comparative analysis framework based on the translation of subjective and objective information and behavioral feedback mechanisms. Using Lvcuo Station, a transit station on Xiamen’s Metro Line 1 in Fujian Province, China, as a case study, we collected walking data from 410 passengers through field surveys. We used the Kappa consistency coefficient test method to analyze the performance of the interaction between the objective environment and subjective environmental cognitive factors when pedestrians exit the rail transit station and walk to their destinations. The results revealed the following: (1) Overall, there is a significant deviation effect of subjective and objective factors on passengers’ pathfinding behavior, with some spatial correlation with the built environment of the streets. (2) The consistency of influences on walking activities varies significantly across different travel periods, distances, and purposes.

items.title: Research on Visual Comfort of Color Matching in Space Station Experiment Module
items.abstract: When astronauts conduct long-term space missions in a closed space station, they may experience physiological and psychological discomfort due to complex space environments. Considering the living environment, appropriate color adjustment has a positive effect on improving astronauts’ visual comfort, promoting their physical and mental health, and improving operational efficiency. Some scholars have also proposed ideas for the internal color of space stations, but most lack clear and complete evaluations that are suitable for human needs. This study aims to compare the differences in the impact of nine different color matching schemes on human visual comfort through a simulation experiment that combines physiological signals with subjective evaluation. The results showed that using 2–3 colors to match people had the highest comfort level, and people were more willing to choose cool, white, or cool, warm, and white color combinations. Among them, spaces using blue, green, and white colors to match could help alleviate visual fatigue, while spaces using yellow, green, and white colors to match could help people maintain or form a good psychological state. Finally, based on the experimental results, corresponding color matching suggestions were proposed, and prospects for the future development and construction of space stations were discussed.

items.title: Perceived Ability and Influencing Factors of the Signage System for Color Vision Deficiency Groups: A Case Study of Metro Travel Processes
items.abstract: In the process of wayfinding, people with color vision deficiency (CVD) find it difficult to search and understand the relevant signage and guidance information, which reduces the efficiency of wayfinding decision-making of travellers. The current research on CVD mainly focuses on the digital media interface, and there is a lack of exploration of the signage perception ability of CVD groups in complex environments. In this study, we selected metro travel as the type of behaviour to be studied, chose Xiamen Metro Lvcuo Station and four nodes in the surrounding urban area as the research scope, considered the two pairs of influencing factors of the environment and color vision, and used 360° panoramic view and simulation of CVD to implement the information search experiment, and made a comparative analysis of the relevant eye-movement and visual indexes. The experimental results show that subjects with simulated CVD have a significantly weaker ability to perceive the current signage system than normal color vision (NCV) subjects, and have the ability to be less easily disturbed by the colorful visual environment; changes in the outdoor light environment also significantly affect the ability of the experimental subjects to perceive the signage system. The study explores travel environment enhancement strategies that are friendly to the CVD group based on their unique visual recognition needs. It advocates the analysis of the key points of urban public space design with the concept of inclusiveness, and provides a theoretical basis for the subsequent inclusive construction and optimisation of cities.

items.title: Impact of Patient Mistreatment on Psychological Wellbeing of Nurses in Tertiary Health Care Unit through Mediating Role of Emotional Exhaustion and Moderating Role of Servant Leadership
items.abstract: Purpose: This study investigates how patient mistreatment impacts the psychological well-being of nurses in tertiary healthcare units, focusing on the mediating role of emotional exhaustion and the moderating role of servant leadership. Methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted with a sample size of at least 205 respondents for 41 questionnaire items. The participants were selected from tertiary health sectors using non-probability convenience sampling. Exclusion criteria included unwillingness to participate and less than one year of institutional experience. A validated questionnaire with five sections covering four variables was used. Findings: The results show a positive association between patient mistreatment and emotional exhaustion. Emotional exhaustion, in turn, is negatively associated with psychological well-being and mediates the relationship between patient mistreatment and psychological well-being. Interestingly, unlike previous studies, this study found no significant direct impact of patient mistreatment on the psychological well-being of nurses. Significance: The study addresses a gap in the existing literature on the impact of patient mistreatment on the psychological well-being of nurses in Pakistan’s tertiary healthcare units, particularly through the roles of emotional exhaustion and servant leadership. It offers new insights and a conceptual model, tested for the first time in Pak-Army institutions, on improving nurses' psychological well-being. The findings have practical implications for nursing managers in healthcare organizations, suggesting that addressing emotional exhaustion and promoting servant leadership can mitigate the negative effects of patient mistreatment on nurses' psychological well-being.

items.title: Reconsidering Antisocial Personality Disorder: A Trauma-Informed Framework for Clinical Assessment in Correctional Settings
items.abstract: Antisocial Personality Disorder (ASPD) is disproportionately represented within correctional populations, with prevalence estimates ranging from 40% to 70% among incarcerated individuals (Fazel & Danesh, 2002). In many institutional contexts, ASPD is conceptualized primarily through observable conduct—impulsivity, aggression, deceitfulness, and disregard for the rights of others—often reinforcing the belief that the disorder is static and largely untreatable (American Psychiatric Association [APA], 2022). A common refrain in correctional settings when individuals present as disruptive yet non-psychotic is: “That isn’t mental health—that is behavioral.” Such statements reflect a behavior-only framework that risks obscuring developmental and trauma-related contributors to antisocial presentations. Research consistently demonstrates high rates of childhood maltreatment, attachment disruption, and exposure to chronic violence among incarcerated individuals (Ford & Courtois, 2014). Trauma exposure frequently precedes conduct disorder and may shape neurodevelopmental, affect-regulation, and relational patterns that later meet criteria for ASPD. This paper argues for a trauma-informed reconceptualization of ASPD that integrates developmental history, attachment disruption, and adverse childhood experiences into clinical assessment and documentation practices. A structured framework is proposed to support differential diagnosis, reduce diagnostic overshadowing, and enhance ethical precision in forensic mental health settings. By contextualizing antisocial behaviors without minimizing accountability, forensic counselors can advance more clinically nuanced, trauma-responsive, and professionally responsible interventions.

items.title: Psychometric validation of the NIH Toolbox for use with individuals with phenylketonuria: Evidence from the PHEFREE consortium longitudinal study
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recent advancements in the development of novel therapies to treat phenylketonuria (PKU) have fueled a call for new assessment tools that are sensitive to PKU-related neurocognitive disruptions. The present study evaluated the NIH Toolbox, a computer-administered battery of neurobehavioral measures, for assessing cognitive function in children and adults with early-treated PKU. METHODS: Data were examined from 91 individuals with PKU (aged 8-55 years) enrolled in an ongoing NIH-funded longitudinal study of hyperphenylalaninemia. Participants completed the NIH Toolbox as well as several validation instruments including the Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence-Second Edition, Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery (CANTAB), and Conners' Continuous Performance Test. RESULTS: Consistent with prior research, crystallized cognition was intact in both children and adults. In contrast, fluid cognition deficits were observed primarily in younger children while older children and adults generally performed within expectations. NIH Toolbox composite scores demonstrated strong concurrent validity with Wechsler indices and moderate correlations with other established measures. CONCLUSIONS: The NIH Toolbox shows promise as a valid and practical measure of neurocognitive function in PKU, supporting its potential integration into clinical trials and research protocols. Future research should prioritize longitudinal designs to assess test-retest reliability, sensitivity to change, and subgroup differences related to treatment modalities. Ongoing efforts, such as the PHEFREE consortium, will be critical for establishing the NIH Toolbox as a robust outcome measure for PKU intervention studies.

items.title: Detecting long-term canopy change and vegetation shifts in northern peatlands using LAI and climate data
items.abstract: Abstract. Peatlands store vast amounts of carbon, yet their canopies are changing under northern warming. We assessed recent vegetation trajectories by analysing greening and browning across northern peatlands using a gap-filled, sensor-independent climate data record of leaf area index (LAI) for 2001–2023. To our knowledge, this provides the first multi-decadal, peatland-specific assessment of canopy trends based strictly on mapped peatlands. Although greening was widespread at the pixel level (77 % of peatlands; greening-to-browning ratio 3.5:1), the area-weighted LAI trend at the map scale was not significant. LAI anomalies were weakly positively correlated with temperature and weakly negatively correlated with precipitation. Higher tree cover was associated with less greening, with a smaller effect observed in areas with deciduous needleleaf forests and under higher precipitation. Decadal variability left a regional, non-linear imprint: most pixels showed no breakpoints, but where present they often were temporally aligned with phase shifts in the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). Cup-shaped trends were concentrated in West Siberia, whereas hat-shaped trends were widespread across Europe, northeastern Asia, and Canada. Protected peatlands did not show different LAI trends when differences in climate and canopy were taken into account. Overall, recent peatland canopy change was not a uniform increase in greenness but reflected moisture-sensitive, composition-dependent responses modulated by decadal climate variability. Together, these results provide a circumpolar, peatland-specific baseline that clarifies where and why LAI is changing and enables evaluation of how moisture conditions, decadal variability, canopy composition, and protection status relate to recent canopy trajectories in northern peatlands.

items.title: Water quality data from the Paute and Jubones river systems of Ecuador
items.abstract: Abstract In Ecuador, the Paute river basin supports the generation of approximately 40% of the national electricity demand, yet studies on its ecological quality tend to be spatially or temporally limited. Moreover, the underlying raw data often remains unpublished and stored in personal or institutional databases. To counter this situation, we collected data from the Paute and Jubones river systems every three months over a two-year period (July 2023 – April 2025), amounting to a total of eight time points. The data record covers 67 unique stations and includes information on the aquatic habitat, the abiotic water quality status, the prevailing macroinvertebrate communities, and the presence of both dissolved and emitted greenhouse gases. Climate conditions varied considerably during this two-year period, as Ecuador experienced two severe droughts that affected the overall water supply and the associated energy production. Hence, the provided data can be useful for local water managers, scholars, and academics interested in the Andean headwater system under normal and exceptional circumstances.

items.title: Microplastic contamination in surface water and sediments of Lake Canaçari, Central Amazon, during the dry season
items.abstract: Abstract Contamination by microplastics is an emerging environmental problem that is widely distributed across continental aquatic environments and may cause ecological impacts. This study evaluated the occurrence, concentration, and chemical and morphological characteristics of microplastics in surface waters and sediments from Lake Canaçari, comparing two areas with different land-use patterns within a floodplain system in the Central Amazon. Microplastics were detected in all sampled areas. In surface water, concentrations ranged from 0 (no microplastic particles detected in one sample) to 1,000 microplastics·m⁻ 3 (405 ± 298 microplastics·m⁻ 3 ), while in sediments, they ranged from 7 to 307 microplastics·kg⁻ 1 (77 ± 104 microplastics·kg⁻ 1 ). No significant differences in microplastic concentrations were observed between fishing and human-settlement areas. The particles were predominantly blue fibers (< 1,000 μm). Among the spectroscopically analyzed particles, polyethylene was the most frequently identified polymer, while copper phthalocyanine pigments, including Pigment Blue 15 and Pigment Green 7, were also detected by FTIR and/or Raman spectroscopy. Overall, the results suggest that Lake Canaçari may act as a transport pathway, redistribution zone, and retention compartment for microplastics; however, seasonal sampling is needed to confirm how these processes vary throughout the hydrological cycle. These results reinforce the role of Amazonian floodplain systems in the regional dynamics of microplastics and highlight the need for monitoring and management strategies that incorporate seasonal hydrological connectivity at the basin scale.

items.title: Quantitative horizon scanning to identify species with the potential to become plant pests in new regions
items.abstract: The international spread of emerging and novel plant pests is increasing rapidly due to the expansion of global trade and poses substantial economic, socio-cultural, and environmental risks across ecosystems worldwide. Horizon scanning offers a proactive means of identifying emerging pests before they establish in new regions, creating valuable opportunities for prevention and risk mitigation. However, current horizon scanning approaches are largely qualitative, relying on extensive literature reviews and expert consultation that are both time-consuming and resource intensive. The Euphresco project presented here aims to strengthen and accelerate traditional horizon scanning by introducing a quantitative, highly automated modelling framework capable of screening large numbers of potential plant pests and identifying and prioritising those posing the greatest risk. The approach integrates multiple analytical components, including automated data retrieval from databases and web sources, high-throughput climate-suitability and ecological modelling, machine learning-assisted screening and analysis for informing and quantifying risk criteria, quantitative prioritisation of species according to risk, and sensitivity analysis to test the robustness of the ranking. The new approach will support evidence-based triage, enabling the most concerning pests to be rapidly identified for formal pest risk assessment and targeted surveillance. Ultimately, the project seeks to develop an open-source, robust, and maintainable toolkit that enables efficient, scalable, and automated horizon scanning for any country or region, supporting more effective integration of quantitative risk intelligence into phytosanitary decision-making.

items.title: Ontogenetic allometry of the first gonopod in the land crab Johngarthia lagostoma (H. Milne Edwards, 1837) (Crustacea: Brachyura: Gecarcinidae): delayed development of the corneous unguis suggests morphofunctional specialization
items.abstract: Abstract In Brachyura, reproduction involves a range of behavioral, morphological, and physiological mechanisms that contribute to reproductive success. The land crab Johngarthia lagostoma , endemic to four oceanic islands in the South Atlantic, shows no clear pre- or post-copulatory guarding behavior, and the mechanisms involved in sexual selection remain uncertain. This study investigated the ontogenetic development of the first gonopod using relative growth analyses and high-resolution imaging techniques, with special emphasis on the corneous unguis, a distal non-calcified structure of unknown function. Morphometric analyses were performed using carapace width as the independent variable and measurements from different gonopod regions, including the corneous unguis, as dependent variables. Relative growth was evaluated using power function, and growth shifts were estimated from the intersection between juvenile and adult growth phases. Nano-computed tomography and X-ray analyses were used to describe the overall morphology of the gonopod and provided detailed visualization of its distal region, including the horny claw and associated setae field. Most biometric relationships showed growth shifts at similar sizes (50–55 mm CW ). In contrast, the corneous unguis showed a delayed ontogenetic transition (64.9 mm CW ), indicating a developmental trajectory distinct from that of the other gonopod regions. The coordinated maturation of most gonopod regions, together with the delayed development of the corneous unguis, indicates differential developmental timing among components of the copulatory apparatus. Although the functional role of the corneous unguis remains uncertain, its distinct ontogenetic pattern supports the hypothesis that it may be involved in post-copulatory reproductive processes associated with sperm transfer and/or ejaculate processing.

items.title: Deconstructing raptor species richness global pattern: shared evolutionary but divergent ecological drivers across orders
items.abstract: The latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG) is one of the most widespread biodiversity patterns, yet its shape and drivers differ among taxa. Such differences reflect the distinct evolutionary histories, biogeographic origins, physiological limits and ecological requirements of taxa. Analyses of geographic gradients of species richness in major taxa can mask lineage-specific patterns as well as the effects of evolutionary and ecological drivers. Whether this also applies to groups of unrelated clades with similar ecologies remains to be determined. Using a deconstructive approach, we evaluated the evolutionary and ecological drivers that generate the global species richness pattern of the polyphyletic group of raptors, analysing each order (Accipitriformes, Cathartiformes, Falconiformes and Strigiformes) separately. We compiled geographic range maps for 557 of the 558 extant raptor species (99.82%) to describe their global species richness pattern. We tested eight hypotheses related to evolutionary and ecological drivers, using piecewise structural equation models applied independently to each raptor order. We found that evolutionary time was the strongest and most consistent positive driver of species richness across all four raptor orders (total effects 0.27–0.75), followed by topographic heterogeneity (0.04–0.09). Speciation rate had positive effects on Cathartiformes, Falconiformes, and Strigiformes, but a weak negative effect on Accipitriformes. Past temperature stability increased richness in Accipitriformes but decreased it in Strigiformes, with no detectable effect in the other two orders. The other ecological drivers varied in magnitude among orders. The geographic gradient of raptor species richness follows the LDG, but each raptor order exhibits a distinct spatial configuration. Evolutionary time acts as a shared evolutionary driver across all orders, whereas ecological drivers shape species richness differently among orders. Our study highlights that deconstructing a polyphyletic, ecologically similar group into its composing lineages is essential to uncover the processes underlying its global biodiversity pattern.
